### 3.3 New Image Selected

Selecting an image calls MW::fileSelectionChange, which:

- selects the first image in the folder if the program is starting;
- records the current DataModel row and its key;
- updates the thumbView and gridView delegates;
- synchronises the thumb, grid and table views, and loads the current image in loupe mode;
- updates the window title, status bar, info panel and classification badges;
- updates the metadata and image caching, and the cursor position on the image cache progress bar;
- loads the thumbnail if the selected image's metadata has not been read yet (usually the first image in a new folder).

A selection change may also scroll the views. IconView signals MW::thumbHasScrolled / gridHasScrolled / tableHasScrolled for the current view, which updates the visible icon range (firstVisible / lastVisible); see [3.6.2 Tracking Icon Parameters](#362-tracking-icon-parameters).

### 3.4 Go to Folder (Path Entry)

Go > Go to Folder... (Ctrl+Shift+G, MW::gotoFolder in `Main/mainwindow.cpp`) is the type-a-path route into the pipeline, as opposed to File > Open Folder..., which has to be navigated. It is a small modal dialog: a path field with a folder-only QCompleter, a Browse... button that hands off to QFileDialog, and an "Include subfolders" checkbox. It ends in fsTree->select(path, recurse ? "Recurse" : "None"), the same call the Recent Folders and Bookmarks entry points make, so the selection lands in the Folders dock and everything downstream is unchanged.

- The field accepts what a path usually arrives as: leading/trailing whitespace, surrounding quotes, a file:// URL, and a leading \~. MW::gotoFolder's expand() lambda normalises those before validating.
- Validation runs on every keystroke and gates the Go button rather than reporting after the fact. A file rather than a folder, or a non-existent path, disables Go and says which inline beneath the field. An empty field disables Go silently, because the field's own label already says what belongs there.
- The Folders dock is shown if hidden, since that is where the result appears.
- This is deliberately the ONE Go menu item never gated by enableSelectionDependentMenus: it is how the user gets a folder in the first place.
- Its default shortcut is set where the action is built, not in loadShortcuts' default block, because that block only runs for a profile with no saved Shortcuts group and an existing user would otherwise never receive it.

#### 3.4.1 In the Library, Opening a Folder Filters

In the Library, opening a folder never leaves the Library; only the Folders button in the Module dock switches Library -> Folders. Go to Folder, File > Open Folder and File > Recent folders all route through MW::filterLibraryToFolder(path, recurse) while G::scope == Catalog. It does what a Bookmarks click does there (MW::bookmarkClicked):

- BookMarks::libraryFolders turns the path into the Library folder filter: the folder itself, or the Library's include folders beneath it when the path sits above them.
- MW::requestLibraryFolderFilter(inc, exc, clearOthers=true) checks it in the Filters panel's Folders category, clearing every other filter first ("show me this folder").
- recurse false excludes each Library folder directly inside the target (BookMarks::libraryChildFolders), the same "this folder only" that LibTree's Alt-click asks for. Go to Folder passes its "Include subfolders" box; Open Folder and Recent Folders pass true, as a bookmark does.

Where the reason a folder is unavailable can be shown before the action, it is:

- Go to Folder (titled "Go to Folder in the Library") greys Go with "Not in the Library. Use Folders in the Source panel to open it."
- Recent folders greys such entries with that reason as the tooltip (MW::updateRecentFoldersEnabled on aboutToShow).
- The native Open Folder dialog cannot grey folders, so there the reason is a popup after the choice.

A Library folder whose volume is not mounted still counts, because the Library check runs before any disk check. The Library's folders arrive from MW::updateLibraryTree's background read; until they have (BookMarks::isLibraryKnown), nothing is greyed and the popup says the folders are still being read.

### 3.5 Un-Ingested Picks Block a Model Reset or a Quit

Picks live only in the DataModel. The pick flag is a column (G::PickColumn), not something written to the file or the sidecar. The settings pickLog is a crash-recovery record, not a store, and the catalog does not hold picks at all (see [17.1 The Catalog (Cross-Folder Search)](#171-the-catalog-cross-folder-search)). So the moment the model's rows go away, a cull that has not been ingested is gone with no way back.

MW::okToDiscardPicks(action, proceedLabel) (`Main/mainwindow.cpp`) is the guard. It returns true when it is safe to proceed, and it must be asked BEFORE anything is torn down, because a "Cancel" answer has to leave the session exactly as it was: still loaded, still cached, still picked. It has three callers, the three ways the rows are thrown away:

- MW::folderSelectionChange, when resetDataModel is true. That flag means exactly "clear the model and load this folder instead". A Cmd-click that ADDS a folder, a Cmd-click that removes one, and a Shift range each pass false, and none of them lose a pick. The call is the first statement in the function, ahead of setScope and resetDevelopCachesForNewFolder.
- MW::loadCatalogScope, when the request is not an append. A replacing result set clears the model as thoroughly as a folder change does; an append keeps every loaded row, and therefore every pick, so it never asks.
- MW::closeEvent, ahead of every teardown step including the "Closing Winnow ..." message. Everything below that point is one-way, so an answer taken later could not be honoured; a refusal is event->ignore() and the session carries on untouched. The background-ingest wait just below it is not a case this catches: MW::ingest marks those rows "Ingested" as soon as the copy starts, so there is nothing left to warn about.

DataModel::pickCount counts the UNFILTERED model, like isAnyPick: a pick hidden by the current filter is still a pick, and still lost.

#### 3.5.1 The Dialog

- Two buttons, and the first names the action: "Select another folder" / "Load search results" / "Close", then Cancel. A button that says what clicking it does needs no reading back up to the text, which is why proceedLabel is a separate argument from action (action is the same phrase as a gerund, for the sentence "Selecting another folder will discard the picks.").
- Cancel is the default and the escape button. Losing a cull cannot be undone, unlike the delete warning next door, which defaults to Yes because the files land in the trash.
- The buttons are widened to their text after setStyleSheet(G::css). The app stylesheet gives QPushButton 5 px of horizontal padding and a min-width, and a min-width is not a fit: "Select another folder" is wider than the style's own sizeHint and it clipped. Each button gets max(sizeHint, textWidth + 40) from the STYLED font's metrics, with '&' removed first (a mnemonic, not a glyph).

#### 3.5.2 Exemptions

Three cases where the picks are not really being abandoned, or nobody can answer:

- The preference. Preferences > General > "Warn if picks have not been ingested" (MW::pickLossWarning, settings key "pickLossWarning", default on) turns it off for picking that is not a prelude to an ingest. Same shape as deleteWarning.
- MW::ingest navigating to the ingest destination. On the gotoIngestFolder path MW::ingest returns before MW::setIngested runs, so the rows still say "Picked" even though the files have just been copied. ignorePickLossWarning is set around that fsTree->select call: the folder change IS the ingest finishing.
- QStandardPaths::isTestModeEnabled(). --selftest, --soaktest and --devtest change folders on a timer with nothing to answer a modal dialog. The crash-recovery prompt takes the same exemption for the same reason.

#### 3.5.3 A Cancelled Folder Change Must Leave the Panels Agreeing

After a cancel the panels must still agree with the DataModel. That takes more than putting the highlight back, because FSTree moves it on BOTH sides of the emit:

- FSTree::mousePressEvent chains to QTreeView::mousePressEvent (which selects) BEFORE emitting, so the highlight has already moved and has to be REPAIRED.
- FSTree::select emits FIRST and then calls setCurrentIndex + selectionModel()->select, so a repair made during the signal is immediately overwritten; that path has to be STOPPED instead. This is the one that matters in practice: Bookmarks, Go to Folder, Recent Folders, the USB entry point and MW::folderAndFileSelectionChange all go through select().

So MW answers the signal rather than only returning from it:

- MW::folderSelectionChange calls FSTree::refuseFolderChange(loadedFolders), which restores the selection AND sets a flag.
- EVERY emitter in FSTree goes through the private FSTree::emitFolderSelectionChange, which clears the flag, emits, and returns whether MW accepted. The connection is direct (same thread, no queue), so the answer is in by the time emit returns.
- A refused select() returns false without touching the highlight; a refused mouse press returns without advancing prevIdx (the Shift-range anchor).
- Restoring is safe because FSTree::selectionChanged only reschedules the folder watch; nothing there re-selects, re-loads or re-emits.

syncSelectionToFolders is passed an EMPTY list outside the Folders scope: after a catalog load folderList holds every parent folder of the results, which is why the Folders panel deliberately does not follow a search.

The same rule applies to the Filter panel's Here/Everywhere selector (the scopeChanged lambda in MW::createFilterDock). Switching back to Here re-selects from folderList only when the DataModel holds a FOLDER load (dm->scopeRequest().scope == Folders); otherwise it clears the tree. That lambda also runs as the echo of a folder click: MW::folderSelectionChange -> MW::setScope(Folders) -> FilterPanel::setScope emits scopeChanged while the catalog rows are still loaded. Syncing on that echo selected every catalog folder and hid the folder just clicked. The lambda reads G::scope before calling setScope and syncs only when the flip started in the catalog, which means the user pressed the selector.

Two more things would undo the repair:

- The release. QAbstractItemView defers a selection to mouseReleaseEvent when the press landed on an already-selected item (so a drag can start). FSTree::mousePressEvent records pressWasRefused, and mouseReleaseEvent swallows that release rather than chaining to QTreeView.
- The view state. The dialog is modal and opens from inside mousePressEvent, so the view may never see the matching release, and QTreeView entered DragSelectingState on the press, where it rubber-band selects on the next mouse move. refuseFolderChange calls setState(NoState) rather than relying on a release arriving.

Bookmarks is the same choice in another widget, and Qt highlighted the clicked item before MW::bookmarkClicked ran, so the refusal path also calls bookmarks->select(dm->primaryFolderPath()). That only moves the current item (and clears it when the folder is not bookmarked), so it restores without starting anything. MW::bookmarkClicked also stops scrolling the tree to a folder it is no longer highlighting, and MW::folderAndFileSelectionChange asks fsTree->lastFolderChangeRefused() so a refusal is not logged as "fsTree failed to select folder": it is the user's answer, not a failure.

MW::folderAndFileChangePath is cleared on a cancel for the same reason. MW::folderAndFileSelectionChange (a Finder double-click, an external app) parks the image to select there and then calls fsTree->select. MW::folderChanged consumes it on the NEXT folder load, whenever that is, where a path from the folder that was never opened would resolve to row -1.

### 3.6 Icons

Icons (thumbnails) are 256 px on the long side and stored in the DataModel in column 0 under Qt::DecorationRole (the QPixmap); the icon's QRect is kept on the same cell under G::IconRectRole.

The number of icons to hold is dm->iconChunkSize, set per folder in DataModel::resolveIconChunkSize:

- Brute force (G::useJitIconCache == false): it equals the row count (all icons).
- JIT: the memory budget (iconBudgetCount), clamped to the row count and to the 3x-visible floor (iconChunkFloor).

See [5.3 Icon Caching](#53-icon-caching) for the full brute-force vs JIT model (Layers 1-3). As the user moves through the images, by selection or scrolling, the icon range is recalculated around the middle visible icon, and MW::updateIconRange holds iconChunkSize at the floor. The current image is centred in the visible views (thumbView, gridView and tableView) using the midVisibleCell.

#### 3.6.2 Tracking Icon Parameters

The number of visible icons (visibleCellCount) changes whenever the size of the view or the size of the icons changes. Then:

- IconView::updateVisible is called. A number of IconView operations use the parameters it defines.
- MW::updateIconRange updates the DataModel iconChunkSize based on which view has the most visible icons and the current iconChunkSize.

The first, middle and last visible icons change on every scroll event, whether from the user scrolling or selecting another image (see also [6 Scrolling](#6-scrolling)):

- MW::thumbHasScrolled, MW::gridHasScrolled or MW::tableHasScrolled is triggered.
- MW::updateIconRange calls IconView::updateVisible.
- The other visible views are scrolled to sync.

#### 3.6.3 Thumbnail (Icon) Decoding

Thumb::loadThumb (Image/thumb.cpp), called by Reader::readIcon, decodes the icon for column 0. It prefers a small embedded preview over decoding the full image:

```
video                          -> loadFromVideo
isEmbeddedThumb (offset+len)   -> loadFromJpgData
cr3 (if loadFromJpgData fails) -> loadFromImageIO   (CR3 HDR PQ, see below)
heic                           -> loadFromHeic
tif (G::useMyTiff)             -> loadFromTiff
else                           -> loadFromEntireFile (Qt, scaled)
```

Embedded thumbnail format by file type (verified against ExifTool's documentation, the DNG spec, and lclevy/canon_cr3):

- JPEG and the raw formats NEF, CR2, ARW, SR2, RAF, ORF, RW2: the embedded thumb is JPEG (TIFF tags 513/514 or makernote payloads).
- CR3: standard CR3 stores JPEG in the THMB (thumbnail) and PRVW (preview) boxes. A CR3 shot in HDR PQ mode encodes BOTH as HEVC (hvc1), a headerless HEIF bitstream, not JPEG (see below).
- DNG: the spec allows preview/thumbnail IFDs to be uncompressed RGB, JPEG or JPEG XL. Winnow's DNG parser scans for JPEG streams and selects the smallest, so m.offsetThumb/lengthThumb always point at a JPEG. It deliberately does NOT scan the Photoshop IRB (tag 34377) for a thumbnail the way Tiff::parse does: DNG stores its previews in subIFDs (tag 330), which the parser already handles. An IRB thumb only exists if the DNG was round-tripped through Photoshop. ifdPhotoshopOffset is still read in dng.cpp, so IRB::readThumb() could be added there as a !m.lengthThumb-gated fallback if ever needed.
- TIFF: IRB (Photoshop) thumbs are JPEG (m.thumbFormat = Jpg); chained-IFD and subIFD thumbs are TIFF (m.thumbFormat = Tif). The TIFF-format thumbs leave m.lengthThumb == 0, so isEmbeddedThumb is false and they go to loadFromTiff rather than loadFromJpgData.
- HEIC / HIF (including Canon HEIF stills): decoded natively by loadFromHeic (libheif on Windows, ImageIO on macOS).
- The remaining types (bmp, png, gif, webp, jp2, tga, svg, etc.) have no embedded thumbnail and are decoded whole by loadFromEntireFile.

loadFromJpgData reads m.offsetThumb/m.lengthThumb and decodes with the fast "JPEG" hint, then falls back to Qt content-sniffing (loadFromData with no format hint). The fallback makes the path tolerant of any Qt-decodable self-contained embedded thumbnail; undecodable buffers return false and fall through to the next loader.

##### 3.6.3.1 CR3 HDR PQ

The THMB payload is a bare HEVC bitstream (no HEIF file header), so neither the "JPEG" decode nor the content-sniff fallback can read it, and loadFromJpgData fails. loadThumb has a failure-driven fallback: when ext == "cr3" and the embedded path did not succeed (and is not retrying a locked file), it calls loadFromImageIO before the loadFromEntireFile catch-all.

- macOS: loadFromImageIO -> macImageIOThumbnail. ImageIO supports CR3 natively and returns the embedded preview, or a downscaled decode of the raw. This is the supported, tested platform.
- Windows: loadFromImageIO returns Fail (no safe path: libheif rejects CR3 and Heic::decodeThumbnail does not guard read failures), so loadThumb falls through to loadFromEntireFile. A full Windows fix would need WIC plus the Canon raw codec.

Being failure-driven is deliberate: standard CR3 files decode in loadFromJpgData and never reach loadFromImageIO, so their behaviour is unchanged, and it does not depend on the CR3 parser detecting the hvc1 codec.

### 3.8 Investigations and Fixes

#### 3.8.1 Pick Counts Are Maintained, Not Counted (2026-09-24)

isAnyPick, pickCount and the status bar's MW::getPicked each walked every row through DataModel::data, and the selection path asks for them several times per keypress: enableSelectionDependentMenus twice (once directly and once from loupeDisplay), and MW::updateStatus from the selection change, loupeDisplay and ImageView::scale. Sampled while arrowing through a 148,567-row library, getPicked was 51% of the GUI thread and isAnyPick 14%.

- RowStore now keeps an exact picked count, adjusted in setValue(PickColumn) and in every splice (insertRows, removeRows, compact, resize, clear), so isAnyPick and pickCount are O(1). Pinned by tst_imagerow::pickedCountStaysExact.
- getPicked counts the FILTERED rows. With no filter the proxy holds every row and the model count is the answer. With a filter it still walks, but caches the result against RowStore::pickGeneration (moves on any pick or row-set change), dm->instance (MW::filterChange always bumps it) and the proxy row count.

The same sample found MW::isPreviewCacheFolderLoaded at 22%: isCachePath per entry of dm->folderList (8,400 folders in a catalog), each building two QFileInfos under a mutex. DevPreviewCache::containsCachePath now resolves the cache directory once for the whole list. Since even that cleaned 8,400 paths (\~4 ms a keypress), MW::isPreviewCacheFolderLoaded also caches its answer against dm->folderListGen, an atomic counter bumped at every folderList mutation (clear, the three appends, removeAll). A new site that mutates folderList must bump it too, or the read-only gating of the cache folder goes stale.

#### 3.8.2 loupeDisplay Is Not a Mode Switch per Image (2026-09-24)

MW::fileSelectionChange calls loupeDisplay for every selection made in Loupe, and it ran the full mode switch each time:

- filters->enable (a filter-tree walk);
- sel->save/recover (a ClearAndSelect that re-emits the selection just made);
- thumbView->setThumbParameters, whose setSpacing(0) makes QListView schedule a relayout that the following scrollToRow's visualRect then forces over EVERY row (\~12 ms at 148,567 rows);
- enableSelectionDependentMenus a second time.

Sampled while arrowing at that size, it was \~20 ms of a \~30 ms selection.

Fix: loupeDisplay takes a fast path when src is "MW::fileSelectionChange", G::mode and prevMode are both Loupe, and the central layout is already on LoupeTab. It updates the status bar, the classification badge, the thumb strip's scroll (dm->scrollToIcon, as before) and the no-images message, and returns. Measured after: \~9 ms per arrow keypress at 148,567 rows (36 presses, 325 ms of GUI time), down from \~30 ms.

Every real mode switch (asLoupeAction, keyPressEvent, the double-click and Enter paths, setOperationMode, the Embellish paths, opening the app) passes its own src and still runs the whole thing. Nothing in the skipped part changes without a mode switch: the filter tree is disabled only by compareDisplay, and thumb parameters change only through a mode switch, a workspace or a preference.

#### 3.8.3 Load Performance on a 9,000-Image Recursive Tree

Measured on a \~9,000-image / 1,333-folder recursive tree, cold cache, with the [PERF] Phase1 / Phase2 lines (see [22.1 Probe Switches](#221-probe-switches)). Instrumentation overturned the assumption that the proxy/view insert dominated.

Phase 1 (build the DataModel, GUI thread): wall 2,408 ms -> 542 ms (4.4x) after three fixes.

- msg \~1,299 ms (58%): a centralMsg per folder, each a synchronous repaint() in MW::setCentralMessage. Fixed by G::throttleFolderLoadMsg.
- enum \~580 ms, cold about equal to warm (not I/O-bound): QDir recompiled \~50 wildcard name-filter regexes per folder. Fixed by entryList(QDir::Files, NoSort) + a QSet&lt;QString> suffix check (DataModel::supportedExtSet); \~230 ms after.
- insert \~370 -> \~250 ms: the batched per-folder insert (G::useBatchedFolderInsert).
- sort \~9 ms: negligible (a per-folder std::sort of \~7 files).

To compare runs, clear the OS file cache between them (`sudo purge`) and flip the flag under test.

Phase 2 (read metadata and icons, worker threads): wall \~9.6 s, I/O- and decode-bound in the Reader pool. The metaReadThread is \~1% busy (dispatch \~87 ms, needToRead \~10 ms), thumbRetries = 0 (the 100 ms loadThumb contention loop never fires), and the Reader::readIcon double-scale that was removed was redundant (loadThumb already scales to thumbMax). The only real Phase 2 levers are reducing decode volume (icon windowing) or reader-pool tuning. (This measurement once concluded that the worker-thread proxy access was not worth a snapshot rewrite for SPEED, at \~0.1% of the load; it was later moved off the proxy anyway, for correctness: see [4.4 Worker Threads and the Model](#44-worker-threads-and-the-model).)

## 4 The DataModel

This part covers the DataModel (Datamodel/datamodel.h, a QAbstractTableModel over the RowStore), its sort/filter proxy (SortFilter, dm->sf), and how the model changes after a load: filtering, sorting, on-the-fly inserts and deletes, and the worker threads that read it. The load itself is in [3 Folder Loading](#3-folder-loading).

The legacy Folder Change and Image Change call sequences (the MetadataCache architecture in Cache/mdcache.cpp, no longer compiled) have been removed; the current sequences are [3.2 New Folder Selected (Call Sequence)](#32-new-folder-selected-call-sequence) and [3.3 New Image Selected](#33-new-image-selected).

### 4.1 Filter Change

```
MW::filterChange
DataModel::newInstance
ImageCache::stop
SortFilter::filterChange                // invalidate(): one layoutChanged
BuildFilters::update
IconView::refreshThumbs
MetaRead::initialize                    // QUEUED to metaReadThread
ImageCache::filterChange
thumbView->selectThumb
MW::scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible
```

#### 4.1.1 One Invalidate per Change

SortFilter::filterChange calls invalidate(), which clears the proxy's mapping and emits ONE layoutAboutToBeChanged / layoutChanged pair; the mapping is rebuilt lazily and once. The incremental invalidateRowsFilter() emits one begin/endInsertRows per CONTIGUOUS RUN of rows changing visibility, and a filter over a photo library is scattered by nature: 348 signal pairs for one action, each splicing the proxy's mapping vectors and reaching three views.

The price is persistent indexes. layoutChanged carries no remapping, so the selection model and any open editor are invalidated rather than moved. That is acceptable only because of what surrounds it: MW::filterChange saves the selection before and restores it after (Selection::recoverVisible, or a fresh select when the current row was filtered out), as it has always done around a sort. Nothing else in the app listens to the proxy's rowsInserted, and the snapshot rebuild is wired to layoutChanged as well, so the workers are still told. A QModelIndex held across a filter change is a dangling pointer (see [2.13.1.1 A Proxy Index Does Not Survive a Filter Change](#21311-a-proxy-index-does-not-survive-a-filter-change)).

#### 4.1.2 No Re-Sort Unless the Sort Is Wrong

Filtering does not disturb the sort. The proxy runs with dynamicSortFilter TRUE in steady state (off only for the duration of a batched folder load, restored by restoreProxySortAfterLoad), so the rows the filter brings back are inserted in sorted position.

MW::filterChange therefore calls sortChange only when the proxy does not already hold the requested sort (sf->sortColumn() / sf->sortOrder() against sortColumn / isReverseSort). QSortFilterProxyModel::sort does NOT early-out on the column and order it is already sorted by: the old unconditional call re-sorted all 43,070 rows, emitted layoutChanged to three views, then saved and recovered the selection and refreshed the icons, at 0.6 to 3.9 s per filter change. A sort that genuinely is not in place (after a load, a workspace or a menu sort) still goes through sortChange. Only currentSfRow is kept by hand in the skip path, because the phases after it read it.

#### 4.1.3 The Proxy Snapshot Is Coalesced

DataModel::rebuildProxySnapshot walks every proxy row (mapToSource, a path string through data(), two hash inserts): 6.5 ms at 43,070 rows. It used to be connected DIRECTLY to the proxy's rowsInserted / rowsRemoved / layoutChanged / modelReset, so it ran once per signal block.

DataModel::scheduleProxySnapshotRebuild sets a flag and posts a zero timer, the same shape as SortFilter::scheduleCompileFilters and DataModel::scheduleVisibleEmit. The snapshot is read ONLY by MetaRead and ImageCache, never by GUI code in the middle of a mutation, so it need only be whole by the time the event loop turns.

The exception: a caller about to QUEUE work to those threads does not return to the event loop first, so it must flush. DataModel::flushProxySnapshot is called at the four sites that hand the workers something: MW::filterChange before MetaRead::initialize, and the three setStartRow invokes (reloadIconChunk, folderAndFileSelectionChange, updateChange). A direct rebuildProxySnapshot also clears the pending flag, so paths that already rebuild explicitly do not pay for a second walk.

#### 4.1.4 MetaRead::initialize Is Queued, Not Called

MetaRead::initialize CLEARS rowsReading, videoRowsReading and readSuccessThisCycle, the sets MetaRead::needToRead reads on metaReadThread. MW::filterChange used to call it directly on the GUI thread while that thread was running; a QSet cleared under a concurrent contains() is a freed hash pointer, and the crash was a null dereference inside needToRead, reached from nextRowToRead / dispatch. It needed a busy loader to show up, which is why it surfaced when Shift+click began changing a whole range of items at once.

Every caller of initialize now queues it (see MW::folderAndFileSelectionChange and the insert path). Nothing in filterChange needs it to have run before the function returns: the setStartRow that acts on the re-initialised state is itself queued, and arrives behind it.

#### 4.1.5 Selection Recovery and the Central View

When the current row survives the filter, MW::filterChange restores the prior selection via Selection::recoverVisible() (2026-10-19: it was Selection::recover() and only when NO rows were filtered out, so any active filter collapsed a multi-image selection on every filterChange -- including the one a keyword drop on the Keywords panel triggers through rebuildKeywordFilters; the selected rows the filter still shows are now kept, the hidden ones dropped, and only a filtered-out current falls back to selecting a single new current). Like recover() it sets the current index with QItemSelectionModel::NoUpdate and therefore does NOT re-emit fileSelectionChange. The central view is not re-rendered for the current item. A still image keeps showing because imageView retains its decoded pixmap, but a video's first frame (rendered by videoView on the VideoTab) must be re-asserted. MW::refresh does this at its tail: for a video current item in Loupe mode it re-selects the VideoTab and reloads the first frame (guarded so a clip already shown paused is not reloaded).

#### 4.1.6 A Press That Settles a Filter Must Swallow the Release

QAbstractItemView emits itemClicked from the RELEASE, against the index it still holds pressed, and Filters::itemClickedSignal reads a click that did not toggle the box as a click on the item's TEXT and toggles it itself. So every early return in Filters::mousePressEvent (Opt+click to exclude, a plain click clearing an exclusion, and the Shift+click range) used to be followed by a second, contradictory change. On a range that had just been cleared it put the clicked item back on (the range's own anchor, checked again the instant it was unchecked), and on all three it ran MW::filterChange a SECOND time over the whole model, which on a large folder is seconds of filtering to arrive where the user already was.

Filters::swallowNextRelease drops that release, the same device as hdrJustClicked beside it.

#### 4.1.7 Phase Timing

MW::filterChange is phase-timed under G::isPerfProbe (--perfprobe, or WINNOW_PERF_PROBE=1). The phases are sfFilter, buildFilters, sort, status, refreshIcons, snapshot, imageCache, selection and scroll; each number is the time since the previous phase, so they add up to the total beside them. The line also reports the snapshot count (snapshots = N (M ms)), because the snapshot defect above was invisible as a total.

### 4.2 Adding a Folder Rebuilds the Filters (Keeping the Checks)

A Cmd-click (or Shift-click) in the Folders tree adds to what is loaded without resetting the model. The non-reset branch of MW::folderSelectionChange used to only abort the running build ("stop building but do not clear filters"). When the load finished, buildFiltersWhenModelReady called BuildFilters::build, which returns at once while filters->filtersBuilt is set, and then recount(), which updates the counts of items that already exist and CREATES NONE. So an added folder never appeared under Folders, and neither did any camera, lens, year or keyword only it held. Removing a folder left its items behind the same way. (Reported against the Folders category after it became a path tree, but the defect was in the build gate, not the category.)

The fix rebuilds and puts the checks back:

- The non-reset branch calls Filters::save and BuildFilters::reset(false), so the build after the load is a full one.
- MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange, connected to BuildFilters::finishedBuildFilters AHEAD of the LibTree handlers, calls Filters::restore (keyed on category and value, so it survives the rebuild) and re-applies with filterChange.
- It re-applies whenever anything HAD been checked, not only when something still is: the proxy's compiled predicate holds the old checks until filterChange recompiles it, so a check whose value left with a removed folder would otherwise go on filtering.
- It saves once per burst. A Shift-select arrives as one folderSelectionChange per folder; saving on the second would save the tree the first had already cleared, losing the user's checks. restoreFiltersPending gates it, and MW::reset clears it, because a full reset throws away the set those checks belonged to.

### 4.3 On-the-Fly Insert and Delete (One Pipeline)

Every change to the LOADED model goes through ONE pipeline, MW::applyModelChange (`Main/fileoperations.cpp`): a focus stack, embellish or export result appearing in the folder, a file rewritten in place, Winnow deleting files, or the menu Refresh finding changes made outside. MW::insertFiles, MW::refresh (reconcileDisk) and MW::refreshAfterRemoval are thin callers; generateMeanStack and the test helpers use insertFiles. Nothing outside DataModel calls dm->insert or dm->refresh directly.

Why one pipeline: it broke four times in four ways in 2026. A new row landed at the END of the proxy (twice). The second of two focus stacks was DELETED by refresh(), because DataModel::insert rebuilt fPathRow before the new row had its path, leaving an empty key that sourceModified reported as a file gone from disk. And the Filters were rebuilt per file before the rows had metadata, then never again. Each was a step run in the wrong order by one of several callers that each did its own subset.

#### 4.3.1 The Order

The order is the fix:

1. dm->newInstance BEFORE any row moves. MetaRead and ImageCache write by ROW NUMBER stamped with their instance, so a write in flight would land on a shifted row. The model drops stale-instance writes, and refreshViews -> MW::filterChange re-initialises the readers.
2. Mutate through DataModel's batch calls only.
3. Load the new/changed rows' metadata and thumbnails synchronously, so they end MetaLoaded with a current icon. The async re-read does not reliably complete here, and ImageCache decodes only MetaLoaded rows.
4. refreshViews: proxy re-assert in source order (after the metadata, whose dataChanged would otherwise kick rows to the end again), ImageCache, selection, icons, video, Develop panel; image counts.
5. Filters LAST: Filters::save, BuildFilters::rebuild, and MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange puts the checks back on finishedBuildFilters. This is the same route a folder add uses, so an active filter survives an insert or a delete.
6. DataModel::verifyIntegrity.

#### 4.3.2 Rules That Keep It Correct

Step 1 protects only a read stamped with the instance its row came from (2026-10-03). MetaRead picks a reader's path and row from the proxy snapshot but stamps the reader with dm->instance, and the snapshot is rebuilt on the GUI thread a turn of the event loop AFTER the model changes. At the end of a revisited folder's load, applyModelChange bumped the instance and inserted a version row at row 1; MetaRead dispatched at once from the old 14-row snapshot into the 15-row model under the NEW instance, so every result passed the instance guard and landed one row above its own image. Each thumbnail and EXIF block shifted one place, and a video row was handed a PNG, so its thumbnail never rendered. MetaRead::dispatch now waits (10 ms, before a row is chosen, so nothing is marked in flight) while the snapshot's instance or source row count differs from the model's, and DataModel::newInstance schedules a snapshot rebuild so a bump with no structural change still ends the wait.

The worker mirror is spliced, not copied (2026-09-28). RowSync holds the lock-free per-row flags (MetaAttempted, MetaLoaded, IconLoaded, IsVideo, CacheMB) that ImageCache and MetaRead read off the GUI thread. It used to be rebuilt on rowsInserted/rowsRemoved/modelReset by copying the old array POSITION FOR POSITION, which is right only for rows appended or removed at the END. An insert in the middle (a focus stack placed in sort order, a version row after its master) left every later row reading its neighbour's flags: ImageCache skipped real images as "Video" and waited on metadata that had loaded, MetaRead never fetched some icons, the loupe stopped following the selection and thumbnails went missing. It hid until versions made a mid-model insert happen on every load.

- rowsInserted/rowsRemoved now splice at the rows that moved (DataModel::spliceRowSync, RowSyncArray::copySpliced), and a reset rebuilds from the row store (rebuildRowSync).
- verifyIntegrity checks every row's RowSync flags against its own columns, so a regression is a MODELINTEGRITY line after the first mutation (A/B: the old copy fails model_mutation at its first insert).

A discarded decode is not an attempt. ImageCache counted every dispatch against maxAttemptsToCacheImage, including decodes thrown away for an instance clash because the model changed under them. A burst of model changes while the cache was filling (the load, then the version-row insert and the filter restore) retried every row into the cap, after which okToDecode said "Max attempts reached" for all of them forever. okToCache now undoes the count on an instance clash (unbumpStateAttempts), against the key the decoder worked on (the sfRow is the old instance's).

Deleting every filtered image keeps the filter (2026-10-06). It used to clear the filters and show the whole folder, two ways:

- MW::refreshViews ran BuildFilters::rebuild whenever the proxy came up empty (exactly what deleting the whole filtered set does), and the rebuild's reset removed the checked items BEFORE step 5 saved them, so there was nothing to restore. That rebuild is gone; step 5 is the only one.
- Every category the build fills is rebuilt from the rows, so a check whose value left with the deleted images (every 5-star image, every image from one camera) had no item to come back on, and Filters::restore dropped it. applyModelChange now sets MW::restoreKeepsMissing when it arms the restore, and MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange passes it to Filters::restore(keepMissing), which puts such a check back on a zero-count item (Filters::emptyItemFor, row-filled and session categories only). The filter stays on and shows nothing until the user clears it. A folder change, MW::reset and the Library/Folders state restores clear the flag: there, a value not in the new set should go.

The predicate is held while the restore is pending (2026-10-15). Step 5's rebuild UNCHECKS the whole tree (Filters::reset -> clearAll), and the checks only come back when the async build finishes. Any filterChange in between compiled that empty tree and showed every row. New Version hit it every time: MW::rereadVersionMasters runs applyModelChange twice (re-read the master, then reconcileVersionRows inserts the version row), and the second one's refreshViews -> filterChange landed in the first one's window, so viewing a collection the grid flashed the whole Library and then snapped back. applyModelChange now calls SortFilter::holdPredicate(true) before the rebuild: compileFilters keeps the predicate it has, so a re-filter in the window still re-tests every row (new rows appear) against the checks the user actually has. It is released, with a recompile, at the top of MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange (on finishedBuildFilters) and in MW::reset, where a new set has no restore to wait for.

#### 4.3.3 The DataModel Side

- DataModel::insertFiles inserts every path not already present at its DataModel::sortKey position INSIDE ITS FOLDER'S BLOCK (the model is sorted per folder, folders in load order; a file whose folder has no rows falls back to the first row sorting after it). It then rebuilds fPathRow ONCE after every row has its path, recounts the load flags and re-derives the current index.
- sortKey is the single definition of the load order (lower-cased path; with combineRawJpg the jpg of a pair sorts after its raw), shared with the catalog fill. The old insert ignored combineRawJpg.
- removeFolder goes through removeFiles. It used to wrap each removeRows in its own begin/endRemoveRows, i.e. NESTED removal notifications.
- DataModel::refresh returns the paths needing (re)load, batches its inserts and removals, guards a missing row, and walks a locked snapshot of fPathRow. rebuildRowFromPathHash skips empty paths.
- Catalog scope: refresh takes MODIFICATIONS ONLY. The rows are a query result, so a file the query excluded is not "added", and a row on an unplugged drive is not "removed" (Catalog::Availability keeps those on purpose). Diffing the folder listings would pull in the one and drop the other.

#### 4.3.4 Integrity Checks and Tests

DataModel::verifyIntegrity runs after every mutation: fPathRow has one entry per row, no empty key, every row's path maps back to its row, the five running load counts equal a recount, and each row's RowSync flags match its columns. A failure prints MODELINTEGRITY lines and raises a G::issue, so the model names the defect when it happens instead of a thumbnail going missing later.

ctest model_mutation (WINNOW_SELFTEST_MUTATION=1, Main/selftestmutation.cpp) works on a temporary copy of the fixture folder. It inserts one file, then two at once, replaces one in place, removes scattered rows, finds an outside add and delete through Refresh, removes everything and inserts into the empty model, checking integrity, presence, sort order, MetaLoaded and proxy order after each, with the model-contract tester attached. Its "click after versions" step checks navigation right after a mid-model insert. Not yet covered: an active filter or a Catalog scope during the mutation, and a mutation racing a folder load (the TSan harness).

The click-through probe, WINNOW_SELFTEST_NAV=1 (MW::selfTestNavigate, Main/selftestnav.cpp; ctest selftest_nav), selects rows one at a time after the load and checks each reaches the ImageCache and the loupe, dumping the ImageCache health checks, decoders and item list on the first failure. That is how the RowSync and attempt-count faults above were found. WINNOW_SELFTEST_CLICK_MS sets the wait per click (default 6000, long enough for a raw). It is not WINNOW_SELFTEST_NAV_MS: that name already drives the generic self-test's own navigation ticker, and reusing it made the two fight over the selection.

### 4.4 Worker Threads and the Model

No worker thread reads the model. For BuildFilters, ImageCache and MetaRead, every dm-> reference on a worker thread is either one of the published-view accessors below, an atomic, or inside a report function that MW calls directly on the GUI thread. That audit is mechanical and worth re-running after any change here.

The model (DataModel and the QSortFilterProxyModel over it) is not thread-safe, and the GUI thread writes into it continuously during a load (addMetadataForItem, setIcon1). Worker reads of it used to be real data races that happened to be quiet, so each worker now reads a published copy:

```
Worker        Reads                                    Built by
BuildFilters  FilterSnapshot (Datamodel/filtersnapshot.h)  makeSnapshot, GUI thread
ImageCache    ProxySnapshot + RowSyncArray (modelsync.h)   proxy signals, GUI thread
MetaRead      ProxySnapshot + RowSyncArray                 proxy signals, GUI thread
ImageDecoder  RowStore directly (locked, thread-safe)      -
```

Three reads were left alone because they were already safe: SortFilter::isSuspended (a std::atomic&lt;bool>), DataModel::metaReadHadFailure (two atomic counters) and dm->instance. dm->iconChunkSize was not safe (written by the GUI thread's chunk-sizing logic, read in setStartRow), so it is now a std::atomic&lt;int> beside startIconRange and endIconRange.

#### 4.4.1 BuildFilters Reads a Snapshot

BuildFilters is a QThread, and it used to read the model directly: around seventy calls of the shape dm->index(row, G::PickColumn).data() and dm->sf->index(row, ...).data() over three pass groups. Now makeSnapshot() copies every column the counting needs into plain data ON THE GUI THREAD, and the worker reads nothing but that snapshot. Every entry point that starts the thread (build, update, updateAllCounts, updateCategory) calls publishSnapshot() first.

- A snapshot is immutable and per-run, handed round as a shared_ptr&lt;const>. It was a plain member first, and ThreadSanitizer found the hole within one folder load: MW::buildFiltersWhenModelReady calls build(), which STARTS the thread, then recount() on the next line, and recount's own snapshot cleared the QVector out from under appendUniqueItems() reading it on the worker. run() now takes its own reference at entry and holds it for the whole run, and recount() uses its own without touching pendingSnap. The general lesson: moving a race off the model does not remove it if the thing you moved it to is still one shared mutable object.
- The strings are cheap, which is what makes a whole-model copy affordable. QString is implicitly shared and QVariant::toString() hands back a reference to the same buffer, so a row of fourteen values is fourteen pointer copies.
- inProxy is captured, not recomputed. The filtered counts need "which rows survive the current filter", a proxy question, and asking the proxy per row from the worker is the race being removed. makeSnapshot walks the proxy ONCE and marks the DataModel rows it maps to. As a bonus the filtered and unfiltered counts now describe the SAME INSTANT; before, they were two walks of two models the GUI thread could change in between.

The snapshot reads the store, not the model (2026-09-24). makeSnapshot used to read nineteen cells a row (the seventeen slots, KeywordsAll and DupHideRawRole) through dm->index(row, col).data(): an index, DataModel::data and three RowStore lock acquisitions per cell, about nine million at 148,567 rows, on the GUI thread, on every filter change and every rating/label edit (173-264 ms). Every one of those columns is a RowStore column, so makeSnapshot now takes them in one pass under ONE read lock with RowStore::forEachRow(cells, fn), which hands fn exactly the QVariants value() would (pinned by tst_imagerow::forEachRowMatchesValue). fn must not call back into the store; the lock is not recursive. A new filter category adds its column to the same cells list.

The values table is reused while nothing it holds has changed. A pure filter change alters which rows the proxy admits and nothing else, yet each one used to copy the nineteen cells of every row and free the previous copy on the GUI thread (about half of a 300-900 ms toggle at 148,567 rows). FilterSnapshot is now split: an immutable shared table of row values (FilterValuesPtr) and a per-snapshot inProxy vector.

- makeSnapshot keeps the last table and reuses it while RowStore::watchedGeneration() holds still, along with the row count and combineRawJpg (which hiddenRaw folds in).
- RowStore bumps that generation for a write to any cell named by setWatchedCells (makeSnapshot registers its nineteen) and for every insert, removal, compact, resize or clear, and for nothing else, so the icon, cache and verify bookkeeping that never stops while browsing does not defeat it.
- The generation is read BEFORE the pass, so a write landing mid-pass forces the next rebuild rather than being missed. A write that stores the same value still bumps it; a spurious rebuild is the safe failure. Pinned by tst_imagerow::watchedGenerationMovesOnlyForWatchedCells.
- When it does change, the table is patched, not rebuilt. FilterValues is chunks of 1,024 rows behind shared_ptr&lt;const>, and RowStore::takeWatchedChanges names the rows written in watched cells since the last snapshot (or says "structural": rows renumbered, the watched set changed, or more than 4,096 rows). makeSnapshot re-reads those rows (RowStore::readRow), copying only their chunks, so a snapshot a worker still holds is never modified. Pinned by tst_imagerow::watchedChangesNameTheRowsUntilTheyCannot.
- The worker only ever reads the table, so sharing it across snapshots and threads needs no lock.

#### 4.4.2 The Worker Records, the GUI Thread Applies

Counting off the model was only half the problem. run() also called filters->addCategoryItems(), updateFilteredCountPerItem(), updateCategoryItems(), update(), setEachCatTextColor() and setEnabled() DIRECTLY, mutating a QTreeWidget from a worker under a QMutex that the GUI thread does not take when it paints the tree or the user clicks it.

Now the counting passes append a FilterOp (a kind, a map, the target category item) to a batch, and BuildFilters::applyOps performs them on the GUI thread. run() touches nothing on Filters at all, not even a debug print. applyOps guards on G::isGuiThread() so a future caller cannot quietly reintroduce it.

- Dispatch is inline or queued, never blocking. updateCategory(runSync) calls run() directly on the GUI thread precisely so the tree is updated BEFORE the caller goes on to MW::filterChange (deferring it would reintroduce the use-after-free runSync exists to prevent), so dispatchOps applies inline when it is already on the GUI thread. Otherwise the batch is stashed and posted with a queued invokeMethod. It must NOT be a BlockingQueuedConnection: abortProcessing() calls wait() from the GUI thread, so a worker blocking on the GUI thread would deadlock against it.
- Nothing is dropped; abortProcessing DRAINS. A posted batch could land on a tree the caller had since reset, and the obvious guard (stamp the batch, discard a stale one) is wrong here: a discarded batch also discards its Done op, so Filters::buildingFilters would stay true and BuildFilters::build() early-returns on it, wedging the panel. Instead abortProcessing() calls flushOps() after wait(), applying whatever the worker stashed before the next build can start. flushOps swaps the batch out under the mutex, so calling it twice is harmless. A partial batch from an aborted build applies partially.
- A drained Done does not finish the build that replaces it (2026-10-06). When build() was the caller, the drained Done ran done() from INSIDE build(): it emitted finishedBuildFilters (so MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange ran, possibly filterChange -> update(), which started the thread), reset isReset and consumed the afterAction build() had just set. build()'s own start() then found the thread running and did nothing, so the Reset never ran. The visible case was a focus stack whose Green label never reached the Labels count. build() now sets BuildFilters::superseding around its abortProcessing(), and done() returns at once while it is set. Only build() sets it: update(), updateAllCounts() and updateCategory() may start nothing (their load gate), and a Reset they drain must still finish or Filters::buildingFilters stays latched.
- The category pointers in a batch are stable. A FilterOp carries a QTreeWidgetItem\* recorded on the worker and used later on the GUI thread, which would dangle if the tree were rebuilt in between. It cannot be: Filters::reset() calls removeChildrenDynamicFilters(), which is takeChildren() on the TOP-LEVEL category items, and those live for the life of the widget. Reading those member pointers is the only thing the worker still touches on Filters.
- done() runs last, on the GUI thread, as the final op of the batch. It used to run at the end of run(), before the GUI had seen any of the work, so finishedBuildFilters could reach MW while the panel still held the previous folder's items. setIdle() and stopped() deliberately stay in run(): they mean "the thread has finished", which is how abortProcessing's wait() and MW's shutdown check read them.

#### 4.4.3 Faceted Filter Counts

The Filters panel's Avail column (item column 2, headed "Filter" until 2026-10-12; tooltip "Images available for this item, based on the current filtration.") counts each category over the rows every OTHER category admits, not over the proxy (2026-10-12). Checks within a category are OR-ed, so checking Rating 5 must leave Rating 4 showing what checking it would add, while Picks, Types, Keywords and the rest narrow.

- BuildFilters::addFacets (GUI thread, end of makeSnapshot) evaluates the compiled predicate once per row OUTSIDE the proxy with FilterPredicate::soleRejectorColumn, and records snap.rescue[row] = the column of the one category that rejects it (-2 / none when two or more do).
- countSlot / countKeywords count category C over FilterSnapshot::countsFor(row, C's column): in the proxy, or rescued by C.
- The category's column comes from its header's ColumnRole (snap.facetColumn), not the snapshot slot; Folders compares G::FolderPathsAllColumn.
- Setting a category aside sets aside ALL its checks (includes, excludes, query expressions), as SortFilter::acceptsRowIgnoring does for the Map.
- Not set aside: Keywords in ALL mode (matchAll AND-s its checks, so the plain filtered count is right) and categories with no column (Queries).
- Never rescued: the hidden raw half of a raw+jpg pair, and a version in a collapsed group (SortFilter's "unless its master is filtered out" refinement is skipped).
- Nothing is rescued while a load runs or when nothing is filtering, so those counts are unchanged.

Cost: one RowStore::forEachRow over the predicate's columns (EditRole) plus one predicate evaluation per rejected row; columns the store does not cover are read through the model for rejected rows only. A visible consequence: unchecked siblings in the category being filtered no longer grey out (the greying means "filtered count == 0"). Pinned by tst_filterpredicate::soleRejectorDrivesFacetedCounts.

#### 4.4.4 One Table of Categories

appendUniqueItems, updateUnfilteredCounts and updateFilteredCounts used to be the same fifteen categories written out three times (511 lines kept in step by hand), differing only in which Filters sink they called and which rows they counted. A category is now one row of BuildFilters::sinks() (a snapshot slot, a tree item, a name) plus one column in makeSnapshot's table, so a category cannot reach two of the three passes and miss the third. Keywords stay outside the table because a row carries a LIST of them; they are counted by countKeywords and appended by each caller after the loop.

Two behaviours were deliberately preserved:

- updateUnfilteredCounts does NOT count the Search category. It used to build that map and throw it away (its sink was commented out), because search's unfiltered count goes through updateUnfilteredSearchCount and updateSearchCategoryCount.
- Focal length is right-justified to four characters at snapshot time, as all three passes did; that is what makes "50" and "400" sort as numbers.

One behaviour changed, for the better: updateCategoryItems (the edited-category path) read the model WITHOUT trimming while every other pass trimmed, so a value with stray whitespace could appear as a second, near-identical item. It reads the trimmed snapshot now.

##### 4.4.4.1 Adding a Filter Category

A category is declared in five places:

1. The Slot in Datamodel/filtersnapshot.h.
2. The column in BuildFilters::makeSnapshot's col[] table (and the RowStore cells list).
3. The row in BuildFilters::sinks().
4. The tree item and category name in Filters: member, catXxx string, filterCategoryToDmColumn, createDynamicFilters, setCategoryBackground, removeChildrenDynamicFilters, collapseAllFiltersExceptSearch, and the two {item, column} tables that serve Catalog scope.
5. If the catalog can answer it, a case in Catalog::categorySql.

A NESTED category (one whose items form a tree keyed on a path in data(1), as Keywords and Folders are) must also be added to Filters::isNestedCategory, which makes itemMapKey return the path rather than the label, and needs its own add/update builders in the Filters::addCategoryItems and updateCategoryItems dispatch; the flat builders are one level deep.

What one costs, measured at -O2 on an M4:

- In makeSnapshot on the GUI thread, one value read and trim per row: 1.0 ms at 43,000 rows, 5.9 ms at 250,000 (now mostly the toString/trim, since the lookup moved to forEachRow).
- On the worker, one countSlot pass per row per counting pass (two passes on a build, three on updateAllCounts): 1.5 ms/pass at 43,000 rows and 8.5 ms at 250,000 for a low-cardinality category; 2.7 and 15.8 ms for one with sixty distinct values.
- About 24 bytes per row per slot in the snapshot (QString headers; the buffers are shared with the model).
- Nothing for filtering: FilterPredicate::accepts skips a category that is not filtering with one inline isFiltering() test and never reads its column.

The real variable is CARDINALITY, not category count. Filters::addCategoryItems creates a QTreeWidgetItem per DISTINCT VALUE on the GUI thread, the shape that produced the 56-second stall applyOps is timed for (see [17.19.3 The Filter Tree Recompiled Once per Item (56 Seconds of Dead GUI)](#17193-the-filter-tree-recompiled-once-per-item-56-seconds-of-dead-gui)). Twelve months and sixty ISOs are nothing; a category over a continuous value should be bucketed rather than listed raw.

##### 4.4.4.2 Category Values That Are Not Just Their Column's Text

- Month (G::MonthColumn) is a DERIVED column beside Year and Day (Datamodel/rowfields.h), written from Catalog::monthLabel as the month NUMBER, "1".."12", unpadded like the day (2026-09-29; it was the English abbreviation "Jan".."Dec"). A number because a query must be able to compare it (month:>5, Utilities/queryexpr.h) and because a number is not a language (createdDT.toString("MMM") would follow the system locale). Catalog::categorySql produces the same text (CAST(CAST(strftime('%m') AS INTEGER) AS TEXT)), so the same June is one filter item in both scopes; pinned by tst_catalog. A saved Library filter that checked a month by its old NAME no longer restores. As text "1".."12" would read 1, 10, 11, 12, 2 ..., so Filters::addCategoryItems inserts months in Catalog::monthLabels() order with the blank (no capture date) last.
- Day is the day of the month, "1".."31" (2026-09-26), not the date. It used to be "yyyy-MM-dd", which made Days a list of every date shot and duplicated Year and Month. Now Year, Month and Day are three independent categories that AND together: "the 15th of every month" is a filter, and one date is its three items checked together. DataModel::addMetadataForItem writes QString::number(day) and Catalog::categorySql writes CAST(CAST(strftime('%d', ...) AS INTEGER) AS TEXT). Days are inserted in NUMERIC order, blank last.
- "Most Recent Day" (Filters menu, Shift+D) used to check the last Days item, the newest date; with day-of-month items that would be "the 31st of every month". MW::filterLastDay now finds the newest capture date (Catalog::mostRecentCaptureDate, MAX(captured) read back as the camera's wall clock, in Catalog scope; the newest valid Year/Month/Day triple in the DataModel in Folder scope), and Filters::setMostRecentDay checks (or unchecks) its Year, Month and Day items. Filters::isOnlyMostRecentDayChecked, which syncs the menu tick, is true when exactly one item is checked in each of the three and they are that date.
- ISO follows focal length: the model holds an int, the snapshot right-justifies it to six characters (409600 is the widest a camera reports) so "800" sorts after "1600" rather than between "100" and "8000", and the padded text is what the filter item carries. That works because a QVariant int compares EQUAL to its padded string form (measured, not assumed), so the item can show padded text and still match a row holding the number. The catalog pads identically with printf('%6d', i.iso).

#### 4.4.5 ImageCache Owns Its Own Bookkeeping

isCaching, isCached, attempts, decoderId, decoder status and error message used to live in the DATAMODEL: ImageCache wrote them through queued setValSf signals to the GUI thread and then read them back off the cache thread. Every read raced the GUI thread's write, and the value read was whatever had been APPLIED so far rather than what the cache thread had just decided. A snapshot cannot fix that, because these change continuously while the cache runs. They are state, and state belongs to whoever makes the decision.

- ImageCache::RowCache is that state, KEYED BY FILE PATH rather than by row: proxy rows shift under filtering and sorting, and icd->imCache is already keyed by path, so the two can never disagree.
- The model still carries the columns, updated through the same queued signals (the icon delegate draws its cached badge from G::IsCachedColumn and the table shows the rest), but only as a one-way MIRROR for display. Writes go to RowCache FIRST and the model after.
- The mirror is keyed by path too: ImageCache::setCached carries fPath, and DataModel::setCached resolves it through fPathRow to the SOURCE row. It used to address the proxy by the snapshot's sfRow, which a filter or sort landing before the queued slot ran had renumbered, producing hundreds of "Invalid sfIdx. Src: DataModel::setCached" issues a day, or a cache badge on the WRONG image. Evictions of filter-hidden images were sent with sfRow = -1 and always failed, so their IsCachedColumn stayed true until the filter was cleared. A path no longer in the model is dropped silently.
- State is dropped on an instance change (initialize, updateInstance) and per path on removal (removeCachedImage, removeFromCache, which MW's delete/replace path already calls). A path reappearing in the next folder must not inherit its retry count, and one that had failed terminally would otherwise never be decoded again. In initialize() the ORDER matters: resetStaleIsCaching() reads RowCache to find rows left marked caching and mirrors isCaching=false to the DataModel for each, so clearing first would make it a no-op.

Everything else ImageCache reads comes through six accessors (pathAt, sfRowOf, rowCountSf, isVideoAt, metaLoadedAt, cacheMBAt), the only places the cache thread touches dm. Each takes its own reference to a published view (Datamodel/modelsync.h):

- ProxySnapshot answers the STRUCTURAL questions: what is at proxy row N, which proxy row holds this path, how many rows.
- RowSyncArray answers the LIVE ones: is the metadata loaded, how big will this decode be, is it a video.

The split is not cosmetic. ImageCache::waitForMetaRead POLLS metadata status in a condition-wait loop, so a copy would never see it change, while the paths and row order must NOT change under a pass or the cache trims the wrong rows.

The snapshot is rebuilt from the proxy's own signals (rowsInserted, rowsRemoved, modelReset, layoutChanged), not from a list of call sites; there is no correct list to maintain, since SortFilter::invalidate() is reached from MW, the Filters tree and combineRawJpg alike. Those four are sufficient because the VIEWS rely on exactly the same signals; a change that emitted none of them would leave the grid stale too. It is ALSO rebuilt explicitly in DataModel::endLoad and at the end of the batched insert, because the batch calls setRowCount BEFORE it writes any cell, so the snapshot built from that rowsInserted has the right number of rows and no paths. Rebuilds are coalesced (see [4.1.3 The Proxy Snapshot Is Coalesced](#413-the-proxy-snapshot-is-coalesced)), and ProxyPaths (every row's path by DataModel row and the reverse hash) is shared between rebuilds until RowStore::fieldGeneration(PathColumn, PathRole) moves; only dmRowOf and sfRowOfDm (a vector) are rebuilt per proxy change. RowSyncArray is grown from the SOURCE row count, not the proxy's: it is indexed by DataModel row, and a filtered-out row still needs its slot.

#### 4.4.6 MetaRead's Reads

MetaRead uses the same arrangement (rowCountSf, rowCountDm, dmRowOf, pathAt, iconLoadedAt, metaAttemptedAt, isVideoAt) in needToRead, the icon re-arm scan in setStartRow and the nextA walk. ProxySnapshot carries sourceRows (the DATAMODEL row count; progress and the completion checks count model rows, and a filtered row still exists in the model) and sfRowOfDmRow, the reverse of dmRowOf, because a Reader reports a DataModel row and MetaRead works in proxy rows. The reverse map is a hash, since the lookup runs once per returning reader.

MetaRead no longer writes to the proxy. needToRead used to mark a dispatched VIDEO row in flight with dm->sf->setData(..., G::MetadataReadingColumn, true), a proxy mutation from metaReadThread. Non-video rows had already moved to the worker-local rowsReading set; video could not follow, because a video's decode outlives its Reader (processReturningReader must not clear the marker, or dispatch re-picks the file and spawns a second QMediaPlayer on it, which corrupts AVFoundation), and only the GUI thread learns when the frame lands.

A queued write would not do: the guard has to read true IMMEDIATELY, or the same video is dispatched twice before the queued setValSf lands. So the guard is a second worker-local set, videoRowsReading, and the GUI thread REPORTS the outcome back:

- DataModel::videoReadingCleared(sfRow, instance) is emitted by both resolution paths, setIconFromVideoFrame (success) and clearVideoReadingFlag (failure), and MetaRead::onVideoReadingCleared drops the row.
- The signal carries the PROXY row because that is how MetaRead keys the set and only the GUI thread may map a DataModel row to one.
- A stale instance is ignored: the sets are cleared wholesale on setStartRow and initialize, and a late signal from the previous folder must not clear a row the current one just dispatched.
- The success emit is unconditional. If the icon was already set the row is done just the same, and leaving the marker would stop the dispatcher ever revisiting it.
- G::MetadataReadingColumn is still maintained through the queued setValSf so the table and the diagnostics report show it; it is no longer what the guard reads.

A QModelIndex must not cross a queued connection. processReturningReader used to build one with dm->sf->index(r->dmRow, 0) on metaReadThread and emit it to Selection::setCurrentIndex, so the index was built from a wrong-thread proxy read AND delivered later, when it might name a different row or nothing. The signal now carries the proxy ROW (MetaRead::selectRow), and the connect site in MW::createDataModel builds a fresh index on the GUI thread when it is used. emitFileSelectionChangeWithDelay, which held a QModelIndex across a QTimer for the same purpose, had no callers and was deleted. MetaRead::initialize also logged dm->primaryFolderPath(), which walks folderList on the wrong thread; it logs the row count instead.

A suspended proxy is a wait, never a drop (fixed 2026-10-15). MetaRead::dispatch used to return at once on abort OR dm->sf->isSuspended(); for a returning reader that skipped processReturningReader, leaving the reader cycling forever. The suspended case now WAITS like the backpressure, navigation and snapshot gates; see [4.14.4 A Suspended Proxy Retired MetaRead's Readers One by One](#4144-a-suspended-proxy-retired-metareads-readers-one-by-one).

#### 4.4.7 ImageDecoder Reads the Store

ImageDecoder::decode resolves sfRow to its DATAMODEL row and path from dm->proxySnapshot() once, and every column read (path, orientation, rotation, offsets, type, ICC, ISO, model, devPreview key) goes through ImageDecoder::dmVal(col, role) -> dm->index(dmRow, col), which is RowStore: locked and thread-safe. No proxy call is left on the decoder thread. See [4.14.2 ImageDecoder on the Proxy Hung a Filter for 20 s](#4142-imagedecoder-on-the-proxy-hung-a-filter-for-20-s) for why.

The remaining worker-side dm->sf reads in metaread.cpp and imagecache.cpp are all in on-demand REPORT functions (reportHealthChecks, reportCacheItemList, the MetaRead diagnostics), not the decode or read path.

#### 4.4.8 Every Worker Thread Is Stopped in closeEvent

Any worker thread that can be running at quit must be stopped AND WAITED FOR in MW::closeEvent; destructors are not a shutdown path on macOS. A quit through -[NSApplication terminate:] (the Dock, logout, shutdown) calls exit() directly: main() never returns, MW is never destroyed, and static destructors run while threads are still alive. CatalogScanner::shutdown() (stop, quit the thread, wait, bounded at 5 s) is the model. See [4.14.11 Crash on Quit From the Dock, at Logout or at Shutdown](#41411-crash-on-quit-from-the-dock-at-logout-or-at-shutdown).

### 4.5 Row Storage

DataModel is a hand-written QAbstractTableModel. It holds no QStandardItems: every value comes from one of three stores, and data() / setData() are the only seam, so no view, delegate, proxy or saved column-width setting knows what is behind it. They all address the model by G::dataModelColumns and read it through data().

```
Store                               Holds                                   Keyed by
RowStore (Datamodel/imagerow.h)     resident fields: every row needs them   row (spliced)
ScratchStore (Datamodel/rowscratch.h)  decode-time fields                   row (hash)
IconStore (Datamodel/iconstore.h)   thumbnails                              path (row key)
```

#### 4.5.1 The Field Table (rowfields.h)

Datamodel/rowfields.h is the field table: one SCHEMA and one loader for the DataModel and the catalog index, not one storage engine. The same facts about an image used to be written out four times by hand (G::dataModelColumns, the DataModel cells, the catalog's image table, and Catalog::categorySql), and that they agreed was a matter of vigilance (tst_catalog::categoryItemsMatchWhatTheDatamodelWrites exists only to pin two of them against the other two). The table is an X-macro so a field declared once can generate all four.

It also draws the RESIDENT / SCRATCH / DERIVED line:

- Resident fields are what every row needs to be listed, sorted, filtered and drawn.
- Scratch fields (segment offsets, ICC buffers, decoder id/status/error, decode timings) are needed only while a decoder or cache is working on that image. They are roughly a quarter of the columns and belong in a side table populated for the rows in flight.
- Derived fields (Year/Month/Day, ShootingInfo, ...) are computed from others.

tst_rowfields makes the table binding rather than documentary. It asks the real schema (PRAGMA table_info) rather than a pasted copy, and checks that every field naming a SQL column has one, that no scratch field is ever persisted, and that the resident/scratch/derived partition covers every field. It was verified to FAIL: a field pointing at a non-existent column was added deliberately, the test caught it by name, and it was removed. A drift test that has never been seen to fail is not evidence of anything.

#### 4.5.2 RowStore

ImageRow is a packed struct per row with the repeated strings interned (folder, type, make, model, lens, year, day, creator, copyright, keywords), since those are the same handful of values across a whole shoot. The full path is stored (\~190 bytes of a row) even though it could be composed: it is the identity key that icd, fPathRow and the proxy snapshot all use, and composing it per access would trade \~45 MB at 250k rows for an allocation on every hot path.

- Coverage is per (COLUMN, ROLE), not per column. Column 0 alone is six fields, none of them the cell's value: G::IconRectRole and the four raw+jpg pairing roles (DupHideRaw, DupIsJpg, DupRawType, DupOtherIdx). The path lives on PathColumn under G::PathRole, where EditRole is never set.
- RowStore::covers(column, role) is the single authority, asked on both the read and write sides with nothing in front of it. It is derived from fieldBit(), which is also the set-mask position, so "is this column held here" and "has this row's copy been written" are answered from the same table. (Two lists that must agree is one list too many; see [4.14.12 Building the Row Store (the Migration Record)](#41412-building-the-row-store-the-migration-record).)
- Unset is not zero. An unset cell must return an INVALID QVariant, because callers branch on isValid(): Duration is set only for video, IconAspectRatio only once an icon is decoded, Err only on a row whose metadata failed, and dupOtherIdx is an int row whose callers test isValid() to mean "not paired". ImageRow carries a two-word set mask and value() returns invalid until the bit is set. An EXPLICITLY empty string is a value, even though it interns to the same id as never-written.
- Return exactly what the model always returned, not a tidier version of it. A column that looks numeric but is stored as text stays text: Rating is a QString (empty = unrated, which is a different filter item from 0) and MPix is QString::number(mp, 'f', 2). A column that is numeric stays numeric: exposureTimeNum, aperture, focal length and ISO are doubles/ints, and ExposureTimeItemDelegate guards with "value == 0" before computing 1/value, which does not fire for a QString.
- One type per column. Width, Height and Orientation are int; Search and Ingested are bool throughout (in the model and in searchTrue's filter value). A column whose type depends on which code path wrote it last makes sorting and branching depend on load order: "1000" sorted before "999" for rows the metadata path filled (QString) and after it for rows the thumb path filled (int).
- Alignment is a property of the COLUMN: a static table in datamodel.cpp, served by data() for Qt::TextAlignmentRole. There is no `align` parameter on setValueDm/setValueSF any more; it used to stamp whatever column a worker wrote with AlignLeft, so seven columns rendered differently depending on how far a background load had got. RawRenderColumn is deliberately not in the table.
- Tooltips are derived in data(), not stored: the fifteen per-row ToolTipRole writes were the cell's own text written back into a second role (the keyword columns are joined with Utilities::stringListToString).
- The issue list on ErrColumn (Qt::UserRole, a QList&lt;QSharedPointer&lt;Issue>>) has a named home. A role that is neither in a store nor handled explicitly is DROPPED, deliberately; a general "any role" hash would silently absorb the next role somebody adds.
- RowStore keeps running counts (metadataAttempted, metadataLoaded, iconLoaded, videoRow, picked) so isMetaReadFinished(), the icon-chunk check and the pick counts need not rescan. setData reads the OLD value through data() to count transitions.
- RowStore::forEachRow(cells, fn) reads many cells of every row under ONE read lock; fn must not call back into the store (the lock is not recursive). fieldGeneration(column, role) and watchedGeneration() let caches (sort ranks, the filter snapshot, ProxyPaths) know when a column has changed.

Both RowStore and ScratchStore take a QReadWriteLock. Off-thread readers (decoders, readers, cache bookkeeping) read cells while a load is writing them, and both stores move memory as they are written: the scratch table rehashes on a new entry and the row store's interner reallocates on a new string, so an unlocked reader mid-lookup walks freed memory. ThreadSanitizer reported both on the first run after the QStandardItem writes went (ScratchStore::setValue racing ImageDecoder::decode, and the interner on the proxy run).

#### 4.5.3 ScratchStore

A hash keyed by row, not part of ImageRow. A row nothing has touched has NO ENTRY; an entry that exists is a few dozen packed bytes. data() answers a covered scratch column UNCONDITIONALLY, with no contains() guard: "no entry" is the store's real answer for a row nothing has decoded.

- Unset is a value here too: every field carries a bit in RowScratch::setMask. Without it an unwritten segment offset reads back as 0, which is a legal offset, so a decoder would simply read from the front of the file, on some formats only.
- iccBuf (a real ICC profile, commonly 500 bytes to 4 KB, of which a shoot shares ONE) and iccSpace (a handful of distinct strings across a library) are interned and referenced by a qint32. Measured on the mixed 50-file \_ThumbTest folder: 4 distinct ICC profiles and 3 space names; uninterned, the ICC column alone would be \~500 MB across a 250,000-row catalog. decoderErrMsg is deliberately NOT interned: it is written only on a failure and can embed a row number.
- ifdOffsets is held as quint32s; the QList&lt;QVariant> is rebuilt on the way out.
- RowStore::covers and ScratchStore::covers never claim the same column.
- Not yet done: eviction. Evicting a segment offset means being able to get it back (a re-read of the file's metadata), which belongs with a gap-filling loader. addMetadataForItem currently writes the segment offsets for every row it reads.

#### 4.5.4 IconStore

Thumbnails are held by path (the row's key), not on Qt::DecorationRole of a row. A thumbnail belongs to an IMAGE: rows shift under sorting and filtering and are rebuilt on every folder change, while an icon held by path is simply still there. icd->imCache is keyed by path too, and the catalog's chain "memory store, then index, then decode" only reads as one lookup if the memory layer is keyed the same way.

- The seam is data() and setData() on DecorationRole, so no view or delegate changed. setData with an empty QVariant removes from the store. That removal is not gated on any base-class acceptance.
- The policy of what gets loaded and dropped did not move with the storage: the icon chunk range (resolveIconChunkSize, applyIconCachePressure, clearIconsOutsideChunkRange). See [5.3 Icon Caching](#53-icon-caching).
- A re-key must carry the icon. DataModel::setData moves the IconStore entry whenever a row's G::KeyRole changes (a rename in RenameFileDlg::renameDatamodel, a version re-key in rekeyVersions). Before that, a renamed image showed a blank cell for good: the icon sat under the old path and IconLoadedColumn still said loaded, so MetaRead never fetched it again. Pinned by the model_mutation self-test (V13, "rename master").

#### 4.5.5 The Model Itself

- rowCount() is the row store's size, so the count cannot disagree with what is held. columnCount is a constant. headerData serves a table of name plus geek flag.
- insertRows / removeRows splice both stores (and RowSync, see [4.3.2 Rules That Keep It Correct](#432-rules-that-keep-it-correct)) and are the ONLY way the row count moves. A plain resize() could never be right: inserts and removals take rows from the MIDDLE (insertFiles, remove, removeFolder), and a resize appends or truncates at the END, so every row past the splice would point at a different image.
- clear() keeps the contract QStandardItemModel::clear() had, discarding the headers too, so its callers still pair it with setModelProperties().
- flags() returns 47 (Selectable | Editable | DragEnabled | DropEnabled | Enabled), fingerprinted from the old base class and reproduced verbatim. Editable looks wrong and is harmless (both views are NoEditTriggers); dropping it would be a behaviour change hiding inside a storage change. The vertical header still numbers rows from 1 for the same reason, although TableView hides it.

The model contract is a ctest gate. Because DataModel is hand-written, index and parent consistency, the begin/end pairing around every insertion and removal, headerData, flags and the counts are this code's responsibility. QAbstractItemModelTester is attached to both the DataModel and the proxy for a whole fixture load under WINNOW_SELFTEST_MODELTEST=1, in Fatal mode, as the model_contract test. It removes a row from the MIDDLE before exiting: loading a folder only ever appends, so without that the removal pairing went unchecked (an injected beginRemoveRows off-by-one passed until the removal was added).

Unit tests pin what the old shadow comparisons used to prove:

- tst_imagerow: unset is not zero, text is not number (the ExposureTime case and its reverse, Rating and MPix), row splicing, picked count, forEachRow, field and watched generations, and variantComparisonIsTypeTolerant.
- tst_rowscratch: unwritten fields read back invalid while an explicit zero does not; reading a row nobody wrote does not create an entry; the two stores never claim the same column; each column returns the type the delegates branch on; 500 rows sharing one ICC profile intern to one copy.
- tst_rowfields: the field table against the real schema.

#### 4.5.6 What a Row Costs

The decision to hold a whole catalog in memory rests on one number, measured on a prototype BEFORE any of DataModel was rewritten (5,000 and 20,000 rows, agreeing within 0.5%):

```
  QStandardItemModel, 92 columns      19,900 bytes/row      4.6 GB at 250k
  packed struct + interned repeats       573 bytes/row      137 MB at 250k
                                                            (34x)
```

Each populated QStandardItem cell is an item plus its role list plus a pointer slot; \~110 cells a row is roughly 20 KB before a single thumbnail, worse than the 15-18 KB estimated from the type sizes (the ordinary reason for measuring rather than deriving). The 573 is the pessimistic end (every row given a title and five keywords); a sparse row measured 413.
