QStandardItemModel also held a QList&lt;QStandardItem\*> of rowCount x 93, 744 bytes of mostly null pointers per row (186 MB at 250,000 rows), which the base-class swap removed.

RowStore::approxBytes() and tst_imagerow::prefixExpansionStaysInBudget re-measure it. Measured 2026-09-06 over 20,000 populated rows: \~1,050 bytes/row including spare capacity, \~600 bytes/row of content, and sizeof(ImageRow) is 472 of that on its own. About 366 bytes a row of the first figure is the row VECTOR's unused capacity (resize(20,000) reserves about 35,500), genuinely allocated but a property of QVector's growth rather than of a row. Even at that reading a row is an order of magnitude under the QStandardItems' cost.

The test gates a DELTA, not an absolute. The absolute is dominated by sizeof(ImageRow) and allocator spare capacity, neither of which a change under test controls. The first delta it gated: making G::KeywordsAllColumn hold every ancestor PREFIX of every keyword path cost SIX bytes a row against an estimate of thirty-two, because siblings share ancestors (five assigned paths expand to about eleven distinct prefixes, not fifteen) and the ids landed inside a QVector block the row had already rounded up.

### 4.6 The Compiled Filter Predicate

SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow does not read the Filters tree. The tree is compiled once per change, on the GUI thread, into the plain data in Datamodel/filterpredicate.h, published as a shared_ptr&lt;const> (the same shape as ProxySnapshot), so a row test holds its own reference alive while the GUI thread swaps in a rebuilt one. The compile is coalesced (SortFilter::scheduleCompileFilters).

It used to walk the widget once per row with a QTreeWidgetItemIterator, comparing QVariants as it went:

- O(rows x items). The tree holds one item per DISTINCT VALUE (every keyword, camera model, lens), so a few hundred items is ordinary (the 50-file \_ThumbTest folder builds 201), walked for every row on every filter change, sort and insert, fetching the row's cell once per ITEM.
- It read a widget another pass was writing. BuildFilters adds and removes items as metadata arrives, and filterAcceptsRow read (\*filter)->checkState(0) while it did; there was a `// crash` comment on that line.

Recompilation is driven by the tree's own signals (itemChanged for a check state, the model's structural signals for BuildFilters adding items), not by a list of call sites, so a path that mutates the tree cannot forget to say so.

The semantics:

- `includes` being empty IS the category not narrowing anything (what isCategoryUnchecked used to mean).
- Excludes live in their own list, so an exclusion cannot make its category count as filtering. A category holding only exclusions subtracts rather than narrows; if it counted as filtering, every row lacking any of its items would be rejected, which is the whole set.
- Order of rejection does not matter: every path either returns false or continues and the function is pure, so evaluating one category completely before the next is equivalent to the old interleaved walk.
- Two comparisons are kept deliberately different, because the old code made them differently. An INCLUDE on a QStringList column does .contains(filterValue) with filterValue still a QVariant (compared as variants); an EXCLUDE does .contains(filterValue.toString()). Every filter value on a keyword category is a QString, so they agree today; kept apart, a future change behaves where it always would have.
- FilterCategory::isFiltering() does not count includeAll (the Search category's armed-but-empty state) unless the category also has an exclude, so acceptsEverything() can take its fast path.
- A category that is not filtering is skipped with one inline isFiltering() test and its column is never read.
- SortFilter::holdPredicate(true) keeps the current predicate through a pending filter restore (see [4.3.2 Rules That Keep It Correct](#432-rules-that-keep-it-correct)).

The evaluation is a template taking a callable rather than a model, so tst_filterpredicate tests the whole decision without one, including that a category is read once per row and not once per item. Measured over the 50-row folder with a 200-item tree and three items checked: 228-467 microseconds walking the tree, 36-40 compiled. The shape matters more than the ratio: the compiled cost is proportional to the CHECKED items, the old cost to the whole tree.

### 4.7 Contracts Around Edits and Loads

#### 4.7.1 updateCategory Before filterChange: Pass runSync

BuildFilters::updateCategory suspends proxy filtering, then rebuilds the edited category: inline on the GUI thread when runSync is true, otherwise on the BuildFilters worker. A caller that follows it with MW::filterChange MUST pass runSync = true. Without it the counts are applied a turn of the event loop after the filter change that was supposed to use them, so the category shows the previous keypress's numbers (and, before the compiled predicate and GUI-thread tree ops, it was a use-after-free; see [4.14.13 A Classification Key Rebuilt the Filter Tree on Another Thread (the 1-5 Crash)](#41413-a-classification-key-rebuilt-the-filter-tree-on-another-thread-the-1-5-crash)). MW::togglePick, MW::setRating, MW::setColorClass, MW::setColorClassForRow, MW::findDuplicates and InfoView::dataChanged (Title, Creator) all pass it.

#### 4.7.2 Whoever Suspends the Proxy Must See It Lifted

BuildFilters::updateCategory suspends proxy filtering unconditionally. The things that lift it are MW::filterChange (on both of its paths), the G::isModifyingDatamodel branch inside updateCategory, DataModel::endLoad, InfoView::dataChanged, and updateCategory itself on its deferred path. BuildFilters::done()'s own lift is commented out.

A caller that runs updateCategory and then SKIPS filterChange must lift it explicitly: dm->sf->suspend(false, "&lt;caller>: no filter change"). Otherwise suspendFiltering stays TRUE and SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow accepts every row until something else calls filterChange ("filtering that works once and then stops"). MW::togglePick, togglePickUnlessRejected and toggleReject all had it on their picks-not-filtered branch, masked because clicking anything in the Filters panel calls filterChange. Anything that copies togglePick's skip-the-filter-change pattern has to copy that line with it. MW::editNeedsRefilter decides when a rating/label edit can skip the filter change (see [4.14.9 Rating and Label Edits](#4149-rating-and-label-edits)).

While the proxy is suspended, workers wait rather than fail: see [4.14.3 A Suspended Proxy Blacklisted a Wave of Rows](#4143-a-suspended-proxy-blacklisted-a-wave-of-rows) and [4.14.4 A Suspended Proxy Retired MetaRead's Readers One by One](#4144-a-suspended-proxy-retired-metareads-readers-one-by-one).

#### 4.7.3 "Is a Load Running" Is Not "Has Every Row Been Read"

Three flags answer three different questions:

```
G::allMetadataAttempted   every row has had a metadata read attempted. Republished
                          on EVERY read as isMetaReadFinished(); FLAPS false during
                          ordinary scrolling, because MW::refreshStaleRows (the
                          scroll-in verification) clears stale rows back to
                          MetaNotAttempted. Never use it to mean "model ready".
G::isLoadRunning          the model is being built. Set by MW::folderSelectionChange
                          and MW::loadCatalogScope AFTER their stop(); cleared at
                          the TOP of MW::metadataComplete or by MW::stop.
G::isModifyingDatamodel   teardown in progress; the click gate. FSTree and Bookmarks
                          refuse clicks while it is set ("Busy, try new folder in a
                          sec."). A replacing load's stop() clears it at once.
```

Readers that mean "the model is not complete yet" test G::isLoadRunning: SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow, BuildFilters::update / updateAllCounts / updateCategory (with Filters' context menu and LibTree's folder click), DataModel's versionsChanged post, MW::reconcileVersionRows and MW::newVersion, the catalog scanner's pause, the scroll-in whole-set sweep, and the aborted-filter-build retry.

The auto-scan kicks in MW (the one-shot after a selection and the resume timer) stay on the teardown flag: each gives up after a bounded wait, and a whole load would outlast it.

isModifyingDatamodel was never simply held through a replacing load, because holding the click gate through a 155,000-image Library load would make it impossible to interrupt by clicking a folder. The two meanings were split instead (2026-09-28).

A model fully populated while a handful of its rows are re-read is well defined to filter: a row whose metadata has not landed does not match an active filter, and BuildFilters re-runs when it does. With no filter set nothing changes either way, because the compiled predicate acceptsEverything(). SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow's load gate sits BELOW the raw+jpg and collapsed-version tests, because those are the model's shape, not a question about metadata; only the user's predicate is suspended while loading.

#### 4.7.4 The Visible Range Is Measured After Every Selection

dm->firstVisibleIcon / lastVisibleIcon / visibleIcons (what the user can SEE) are written only by MW::updateIconRange. They are a different pair from startIconRange / endIconRange (the loader's chunk, set by dm->setIconRange(sfRow)). DataModel::iconRowVisible answers "is this row on screen" from the visible range, and setIcon1 / setValDm / setValSf skip the dataChanged for any row it says is off screen, so a stale visible range means suppressed repaints.

MW::updateChange calls scheduleIconRangeSettle AFTER fileSelectionChange returns (the scrolls happen inside it, so measuring first would measure where the view WAS). See [4.14.14 The Visible Range the Keyboard Never Updated (and the Latch That Leaked)](#41414-the-visible-range-the-keyboard-never-updated-and-the-latch-that-leaked).

G::ScrollSignalGuard (Main/global.h) is how code suppresses the views' scroll handlers while it scrolls them itself. It is RAII, beside G::A11ySuspend, and restores what it found rather than forcing false, so a handler's own sync scrolls nest correctly inside an outer guard. Never set G::ignoreScrollSignal by hand.

### 4.8 Model Notifications

Per-row model signals are the dominant cost of a large load, not the work they announce: the proxy and three views (four, counting TableView's frozen column) each act on every dataChanged, and on macOS the accessibility bridge used to rebuild the whole table on each one.

#### 4.8.1 Visible Rows Only, Coalesced

Every per-row write path writes under a QSignalBlocker and emits dataChanged for VISIBLE rows only, coalesced per turn of the event loop: DataModel::setValDm, setValSf (the one the Reader and Thumb threads use), setIcon1, setIcon, and setIconFromVideoFrame.

- DataModel::iconRowVisible answers "does this row need repainting at all", from the visible range MW::updateIconRange maintains (see [4.7.4 The Visible Range Is Measured After Every Selection](#474-the-visible-range-is-measured-after-every-selection)). A row nobody can see needs no repaint: the value lands in the model either way and the view reads it when it scrolls in.
- DataModel::scheduleVisibleEmit answers "how often". It collects dirty rows and flushes after kVisibleEmitDeferMs (20 ms, about a frame), emitting one dataChanged per CONTIGUOUS RUN (runs rather than one span, so a scattered set does not repaint everything between two distant rows). A row being filled takes a burst of writes (decoration, icon-loaded, status, reading flag, aspect ratio), and without coalescing each was its own notification. The flush is a 20 ms timer, NOT a zero timer: Qt gives a zero timer the lowest priority, so it fires only when the queue is empty, and during a scroll the queue is full of the very icon events being coalesced; the repaint for the forty visible rows waited behind all 2,000 of the chunk (see [5.10.5 Why a Catalog Scope Would Not Scroll (Nine Defects, One Policy, and Where It Ends)](#5105-why-a-catalog-scope-would-not-scroll-nine-defects-one-policy-and-where-it-ends)).
- In setIconFromVideoFrame the blocker ends before videoReadingCleared, because QSignalBlocker blocks every signal the object emits and MetaRead needs that one to drop its in-flight marker.
- Per-row view work must stay per row. IconView::refreshIcon (reached from refreshViewsOnCacheChange for every image entering or leaving the image cache) drops that row's delegate cache entry and calls update(idx) only when the row is on screen; it never relayouts the view (see [5.10.8 Selecting an Image Rebuilt Two Views, per Cached Image (the Click That Stalled)](#5108-selecting-an-image-rebuilt-two-views-per-cached-image-the-click-that-stalled)). DataModel::setCached follows the blocked, coalesced rule too.
- A new write path must follow the same rule. Under --perfprobe the scroll line carries an "emit gate" row (notified / suppressed against the visible window) and "[PERF] emit flush" names the DataModel row runs each coalesced flush emitted: the first read for any future "loads but does not paint".

#### 4.8.2 Whatever Changes the Visible Set Asks for What It Needs

A load that depends on a side effect of selection is a load with no owner. MW::filterChange dispatches for itself: one queued MetaRead::setStartRow at the current row, after scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible (which establishes the icon range the dispatch reads) and after DataModel::flushProxySnapshot. Selection::recover deliberately emits no fileSelectionChange (QItemSelectionModel::NoUpdate), and Selection::select is a no-op when the row is already current, so relying on the selection to tell the loader leaves every row under the visible window unread. It is one call per user action, and needToRead skips rows that already have what they need. See [4.14.17 Filter the Catalog and Nothing Paints (an Invalid Fallback Index)](#41417-filter-the-catalog-and-nothing-paints-an-invalid-fallback-index).

#### 4.8.3 Item Views Offer No Table to Accessibility (macOS)

main.cpp installs a QAccessible factory (winnowItemViewAccessible) that gives IconView, TableView and TableView's FrozenTableView a plain QAccessibleWidget with role List. Qt consults factories against the MOST-DERIVED class name first (QAccessible::queryAccessibleInterface), so it pre-empts the built-in QListView/QTableView interface. With no tableInterface(), QAccessible::updateAccessibility skips modelChange, and QCocoaAccessibility's TableModelChanged -> updateTableModel (which rebuilt an Obj-C element per cell for EVERY row on each notification) does nothing. The cost goes away for every write path at once, including hidden views.

- The trade, chosen deliberately: VoiceOver still reaches the views and the rest of the UI but cannot step through individual thumbnails or table rows; at catalog scale that navigation froze the app on every change anyway.
- macOS only (Q_OS_MAC). The O(rows) rebuild is the Cocoa bridge's; Windows UIA has not been measured to need it.
- The bridge cannot be held off. Qt activates accessibility on the FIRST system accessibility query to any Winnow window (qnsview_accessibility.mm, activateQtAccessibility); window managers, clipboard and text-expander utilities send them, and it stays on for the session. The same mechanism re-enables it under WINNOW_NO_A11Y=1 (QAccessible::setActive(false), kept as a diagnostic) or a G::A11ySuspend, so neither is a dependable fix on its own.
- The per-item events had to go with it. QListView/QTableView::selectionChanged and ::currentChanged post SelectionAdd/SelectionRemove/Focus events addressed to a numbered CHILD, and the list interface has none, so every selection printed "Cannot create accessible child interface", "Invalid child in QAccessibleEvent" and Cocoa's "invalid element". IconView, TableView and FrozenTableView override both and, on macOS, call QAbstractItemView's version directly; in Qt 6.11 those overrides do nothing else. Recheck them on a Qt upgrade.
- A new view on dm->sf must join all three places: the factory's class list, and the two overrides.
- The visible-only and coalesced emits above STAY: they also save the proxy and view work, which is not accessibility.

Probe lines: "[PERF] setScope(Catalog) START" (rows loaded, trigger, a11yActive), "[PERF] catalog switch click-to-loaded", "[PERF] loadCatalogScope teardown" and "[PERF] MW::stop" (busy subsystems, wait, reset).

### 4.9 One Way In (setScope and the Reconcile Write-Back)

A folder scope and a catalog scope are the same thing: a predicate over the catalogue of images. A FOLDER SCOPE IS THE QUERY WITH A FOLDER/SUBTREE PREDICATE PLUS A FILESYSTEM RECONCILE; a CATALOG SCOPE IS THE SAME QUERY WITHOUT IT. ScopeRequest (Datamodel/datamodel.h) is that description, and DataModel::setScope is the one entry point; addFolder and addPaths are its private implementation details.

- reconcile is the only difference, and it is real. A folder scope walks the filesystem because the directory listing IS the set; the index is at best a cache of it. A catalog scope cannot: its results come from a hundred folders, so there is no directory to enumerate.
- The request is remembered. folderList cannot distinguish "these folders" from "a search that happened to match images in these folders", and a reload, a refresh and the write-back below all need to know which. An APPEND leaves the previous request in place (what is loaded is then the union of two searches, and neither alone describes it).
- The query travels with the result: FilterPanel and CatalogView emit loadResults(paths, append, query), so the ScopeRequest records what the user ASKED for, not only what it resolved to.
- setScope does not queue internally, deliberately. Both callers already defer the load onto the event loop (it must not run inside the signal that asked for it, because MW::stop has just torn down the reader threads), and the catalog caller has work to do immediately after the fill (the availability pass); queueing here as well would put that work before the fill.

#### 4.9.1 The Reconcile Write-Back

MW::folderChangeCompleted commits the loaded rows to the catalog, which says what IS there. Catalog::reconcileFolder(folder, present) says what is NOT: a file deleted outside Winnow used to stay live in the index and keep turning up in searches until the global sweep happened to stat it. It costs NO STAT: the load has just listed the directory, so whatever the index still calls live and the listing did not find is gone. That is cheap enough to run on every folder load, where sweep() (one stat per row over the whole catalog) can only be a rare one-shot.

It DEMOTES, never deletes, as sweep does: a row that comes back is promoted again by the next commit that sees the file, so a briefly unreadable folder costs a rescan rather than its catalogued keywords.

Three preconditions, each of which is a way to delete a library by accident:

- Only a scope that enumerated. A catalog scope's paths are a search result, not a listing of any one folder; treating them as one would demote most of the library. dm->scopeRequest().reconcile is the check.
- Only a load that finished. An aborted (Esc) or memory-capped load is a partial listing, and a partial listing demotes everything it did not reach.
- An empty folder must be told apart from an unreadable one. Delete every image in a catalogued folder and no row survives to name it, so DataModel::folderPathSets seeds an empty entry from folderList. But folderList is appended BEFORE the listing is attempted, so a folder that is gone, unmounted or unreadable arrives looking exactly like an empty one. One stat per EMPTY folder settles it; folders that produced rows need none.

folderPathSets uses EVERY row, not only the read ones (unlike catalogRows(), which skips anything not yet MetaLoaded): the question is "was this file there", and a row exists because the enumeration found it. Raw+JPG pairing is safe for the same reason: combineRawJpg hides one of a pair in the PROXY, and both members always have a DataModel row.

### 4.10 The Instance

dm->instance identifies one population of the DataModel. DataModel::newInstance increments it whenever rows move or the set changes: a new primary folder, a folder added or removed, a filter change (MW::filterChange always bumps it), and the start of every on-the-fly model change (see [4.3 On-the-Fly Insert and Delete (One Pipeline)](#43-on-the-fly-insert-and-delete-one-pipeline)). A sort keeps the instance.

- Worker signals carry the instance they were issued under, and DataModel slots drop any whose instance no longer matches.
- MetaRead must be re-initialised (queued) and filtering re-applied when it changes.
- Anything a worker keeps across calls must be keyed by something that survives what the instance does NOT cover. MetaRead's sets are keyed by DataModel row because a sort keeps the instance but renumbers the proxy (see [4.14.18 Sort the Catalog and Every Other Cell Is Blank (a Position Is Not an Image)](#41418-sort-the-catalog-and-every-other-cell-is-blank-a-position-is-not-an-image)).

### 4.11 Sort Change

```
MW::sortChange
sel->save
thumbView->sortThumbs                   // SortFilter::sort, inside a SortKeyScope
sel->recover / sel->select
refreshIcons
scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible
resyncIconLoaderAfterReorder            // queued: re-measure, refetch the chunk
```

A user sort asked for while metadata is loading is deferred, not dropped (MW::applyDeferredSort). How the proxy compares rows is in [4.14.7 The Proxy Re-sort Compares Stored Keys](#4147-the-proxy-re-sort-compares-stored-keys).

### 4.12 Combine Raw+JPG

When a folder holds raw+jpg pairs (same base name), the "Combine Raw+JPG" toggle decides whether each pair is shown as a single row (raw primary, the jpg folded into it) or as two rows. The state lives in combineRawJpg, mirrored to G::combineRawJpg, dm->sf, fsTree and bookmarks (the folder and bookmark panels show image counts that depend on it).

Entry points (both route to MW::setCombineRawJpg):

- combineRawJpgAction: File menu item, shortcut Opt/Alt + J. Being checkable, the action flips its own checked state before triggered fires.
- rawJpgStatusBtn: status-bar button. Its lambda calls combineRawJpgAction->toggle() (which does not re-emit triggered), then calls setCombineRawJpg directly.

combineRawJpgAction->isChecked() is the source of truth; setCombineRawJpg reads it into combineRawJpg. Because the trigger has already flipped the action, any early return must restore it with setChecked(combineRawJpg); otherwise the action and flag desync and a later click is spent re-aligning them instead of toggling.

Three load states:

- Folder loaded (rows exist and G::allMetadataAttempted): full apply. Persist to QSettings, rewrite the Type column for jpg duplicates ("JPG" vs "JPG+&lt;raw>"), dm->rebuildTypeFilter, filterChange (re-pairs / splits the proxy) and buildFilters->updateAllCounts (the proxy baseline changed without a Filters-tree change, so unfiltered counts must be recomputed too).
- No folder loaded (dm->rowCount() == 0): allowed. setCombineRawJpg records the setting and refreshes the folder/bookmark counts, then returns before the DataModel/proxy rebuild.
- Folder loading: blocked. rawJpgStatusBtn and combineRawJpgAction are disabled in MW::folderChanged at load start and re-enabled in MW::folderChangeCompleted, and updateStatusBar enforces it too. setCombineRawJpg also guards the case (restores the action and shows a "folder is still loading" popup) so a queued shortcut cannot slip through.

Key files: Main/setandupdate.cpp (setCombineRawJpg), Main/status.cpp (updateStatusBar: button icon/tooltip/enabled state), Main/initialize.cpp (rawJpgStatusBtn wiring), Main/menusandactions.cpp (combineRawJpgAction), Main/mainwindow.cpp (folderChanged / folderChangeCompleted enable/disable).

#### 4.12.1 The Pairing Roles

DataModel::rawJpgPairing records the pairing on COLUMN 0 of both halves: the raw row gets G::DupHideRawRole, the jpg row gets G::DupIsJpgRole plus G::DupRawTypeRole ("NEF", "ORF"), and BOTH get G::DupOtherIdxRole pointing at the other.

Read them through DataModel::isDupJpg / isDupHiddenRaw / dupOtherRow / dupRawType, never through data(G::Dup...Role) directly. The roles live on column 0 alone, so reading one off any other column, or off the proxy, returns an INVALID QVariant, which reads as "not a pair" rather than as an error. That had already happened twice: MW::setTagValue tested the role on the tag's own column, so tag edits never propagated to the hidden raw file; and MW::setColorClass looked the paired row up through dm->sf when the row it held was a DATAMODEL row, and a hidden raw is filtered OUT of the proxy, so the colour-class log named a different image. The accessors range-check as well, which is why they return -1 or false rather than an index.

G::DupOtherIdxRole holds a plain int row, not a QModelIndex: a QModelIndex is a reference into a model that is cleared and rebuilt on every folder change, and it cannot be range-checked once stale. The bulk-load tracker beside it (prevRawRow) is an int for the same reason and is reset by clearDataModel.

### 4.13 Cropped Dimensions and Cropped Aspect

Width, Height, Dimensions, MPix and Aspect Ratio are the FILE's, written once from its metadata (DataModel::addMetadataForItem); a version copies its master's (fillVersionRow), so a crop never moves them. That is correct for their readers: the loupe zoom frame (IconView, beside WidthOrigPreview/HeightOrigPreview) and IconViewDelegate::blackBorderOffset treat Aspect Ratio as the source geometry. Icon Aspect Ratio did follow a crop, only because setDevelopIcon measures the rendered thumbnail, and it is blank until a thumbnail loads, so no use for filtering. (Reported against a version with a new crop, 2026-09-28; the decision was new columns rather than repurposing the old.)

G::CroppedDimensionsColumn and G::CroppedAspectRatioColumn ("Cropped Dimensions", "Cropped Aspect") are the image AS DISPLAYED: oriented by EXIF, then cropped, straightened and warped by the develop geometry. For an image with no geometry they equal the oriented file values. RowStore holds both as interned strings.

- Factors, not pixels. Metadata::developCropFactors decodes the recipe (EditStack::fromBase64), asks CropTransform::geometryTransform for the geometry stage's output size on the oriented frame (the same straighten -> warp -> crop sizing the render uses) and keeps output/source per axis in ImageMetadata::cropFx/cropFy (VersionSummary::cropFx/cropFy for each version). Factors survive a later correction of the dimensions. A recipe with Transform Preview off (Geometry::show false) counts as identity, because the render bypasses the stage. parseSidecar computes them after the format parse, for the image and every version it lists.
- Written by DataModel::setCroppedGeometry, from: addMetadataForItem (every file read, and fillVersionRow with the version's own factors); MW::devPreviewUpdated when a recipe is saved (and noteVersionDevelop keeps the version summary in step, so a later refill does not revert it); setValDm when the thumb path supplies dimensions the metadata could not (undeveloped rows only, since the row does not hold its factors); and setIcon1's video branch. devPreviewUpdated also refills any "Filter on..." category over a cropped column, since a new crop can be a value it has not listed.
- Blank means unknown. A developed row served from the catalog index (ImageMetadata::fromIndex) has not had its recipe read, so both columns stay blank rather than claim the file's size; they fill when the sidecar is read or the recipe is saved. The catalog does not persist them.

### 4.14 Investigations and Fixes

#### 4.14.1 What a Filter Change Costs (9.5 s to 261 ms)

Measured at 43,070 rows with the range gesture clearing the last filter. It began at 9,547 ms and ended at 261 ms (36x) in four steps, none of them in the filtering itself:

```
  9,547   as found          sfFilter 5,205  sort 3,942(worst)  selection 2,033
  8,695   duplicate filterChange and the redundant re-sort gone
  4,565   accessibility suspended across the operation (G::A11ySuspend)
  3,216   proxy-snapshot rebuild coalesced (348 walks of the model -> 1)
    261   invalidate() instead of 348 incremental block signals
```

The final phase line: sfFilter 30, buildFilters 47, sort 0, status 11, refreshIcons 47, snapshot 0, select 0, scroll 123.

The predicate was never in it: 10 ms across 43,070 rows, 0.2% of the invalidate it was assumed to be. Every one of the four was a notification cost: telling the accessibility bridge, telling the worker snapshot, telling the views. The load path got faster too, unasked: the Phase 2 MetaRead wall time fell from 3,663-4,694 ms to 1,559 ms, because the reader pool was no longer competing with a GUI thread busy for seconds.

The 348 blocks cost twice, and the first half was ours. Rebuilding the proxy snapshot per BLOCK meant hundreds of walks of the model to answer a question whose answer changes once per user action, worth 1.35 s of the 4.3 s. (An earlier draft claimed it was the WHOLE 4.3 s, on an estimate of 12.4 ms per rebuild that the probe then measured at 6.5 ms, and the early blocks walk a proxy that is still small. The arithmetic fit because the estimate had been fitted to it.) The second half was the incremental invalidate itself. See [4.1.3 The Proxy Snapshot Is Coalesced](#413-the-proxy-snapshot-is-coalesced) and [4.1.1 One Invalidate per Change](#411-one-invalidate-per-change) for the fixes, and [4.14.16 The Accessibility Bridge Rebuilds the Whole Table, per Write](#41416-the-accessibility-bridge-rebuilds-the-whole-table-per-write) for G::A11ySuspend.

The "scroll" phase was not scrolling. MW::scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible opened with G::wait(100), which is not a sleep: it runs a NESTED EVENT LOOP, so its cost is whatever is queued when it is reached. Probed: wait(100) = 3,710 ms, scrollToRow = 0 ms, updateIconRange = 0 ms; with the accessibility guard in place, 123 ms, still the largest phase of a filter change and a re-entrancy hazard in the middle of one. The wait has since been removed (see [6.4.1 Removing the G::wait Pumps](#641-removing-the-gwait-pumps)).

#### 4.14.2 ImageDecoder on the Proxy Hung a Filter for 20 s

Fixed 2026-09-24. The ImageCache chose rows from the snapshot, but each ImageDecoder then read its row's columns (13 reads a decode) through dm->sf->index(sfRow, ...) on its own thread. QSortFilterProxyModel builds its mapping LAZILY, so when MW::filterChange had just invalidated it, the first index() on each decoder thread rebuilt it: a stable_sort of every accepted row. Sampled while clearing a one-item filter at 148,567 rows: the GUI thread and \~18 decoder threads each sorting all the rows at once, 95% of their time in QReadWriteLock contention on RowStore, the GUI still in its sort after 20 s. It was also an unsynchronised write to the proxy's private mapping from many threads, the race the thread-safety notes had deferred until it showed up. The fix is [4.4.7 ImageDecoder Reads the Store](#447-imagedecoder-reads-the-store).

#### 4.14.3 A Suspended Proxy Blacklisted a Wave of Rows

Fixed 2026-10-06. ImageDecoder::decode still refused to run while dm->sf->isSuspended(), a guard from when it read the live proxy that the snapshot had made pointless, and it reported Status::Failed, which okToDecode treats as TERMINAL. A filter edit or a BuildFilters category rebuild suspends the proxy for a moment; every decode in flight then failed "Proxy suspended." and those rows were never decoded again for the rest of the folder. Seen navigating an OM-1 card: 95 rows of the target range, the current image among them, Failed with attempts = 1, every decoder idle and cacheUpToDate false, the loupe blank and staying blank.

- The guard is gone. A row missing from the snapshot (the model changed under the request) now reports Abort, which is transient.
- ImageCache::setCurrentPosition clears a terminal status on the CURRENT row, so whatever latches a row in future, the image the user is looking at always gets another try (the attempts cap still bounds an unreadable file).

Diagnose it from Help > Diagnostics > ImageCache diagnostics: the Cache Item List's Status and Error message columns name the latch.

#### 4.14.4 A Suspended Proxy Retired MetaRead's Readers One by One

Fixed 2026-10-15. The same guard lived in MetaRead::dispatch: on abort OR dm->sf->isSuspended() it returned at once. dispatchReaders sets cycling[id] = true before calling dispatch, and for a RETURNING reader that early return skipped processReturningReader, so the row stayed in rowsReading, cycling[id] was never cleared, and dispatchReaders never dispatched that reader again. Picking, rating and labelling suspend the proxy for a moment (MW::togglePick, setRating, setColorClass), so every pick that landed on a returning reader retired one reader for the rest of the folder.

Seen culling a 1,670-image OM-1 card with a Days filter on: icons stopped at the current row, 1,054 rows had none and drew no cell at all, MetaRead diagnostics showed all 18 readers Cycling = true, Pending = false, Status Ready, and Log/blank_rows.txt read suspendedReturns = 18 = readerCount.

The suspended case now WAITS like the backpressure, navigation and snapshot gates (QTimer::singleShot(20) and retry, keeping isReturning so the result is still processed); only abort drops a return. Diagnose it from Help > Diagnostics > MetadataCache diagnostics (Reader status: every row Cycling true, none Pending) and the Blank thumbnail report (cycling = all 1s, suspendedReturns).

#### 4.14.5 The Terminal-Failure Check That Never Fired

Found while moving ImageCache's state into RowCache. ImageCache::okToDecode skips a row whose previous decode failed terminally, and it read G::DecoderReturnStatusColumn with .toString() to compare against status NAMES ("Invalid", "Failed", ...). The column is written as the enum's INT, so .toString() produced "3" and the list never matched. The check had never once fired, and a terminally failed image was retried maxAttemptsToCacheImage times on every pass. Reading the int from RowCache makes it work. The terminal set is unchanged, and still excludes Undefined, Abort and InstanceClash, which are transient and must stay retry-eligible.

#### 4.14.6 Verified by Measurement, Not by Inspection

ThreadSanitizer only proves the races are gone; it says nothing about whether the caches still work, and every published-view accessor fails SILENTLY (an empty path, a zero size, a false metaLoaded) by simply loading nothing. --selftest would still exit 0 because rows exist.

- ImageCache: a temporary probe printing the imCache count, the DataModel's isCached count and icd MB at the end of --selftest gave byte-identical numbers before and after the change (50-row folder: 13 images, 752.2 MB, DataModel agreeing with the cache on all 13). That is what establishes that pathAt, cacheMBAt and metaLoadedAt resolve.
- MetaRead: a probe at the selftest exit reported metaAttempted, metaLoaded, iconLoaded and the cache figures. On a 50-row folder, 50/50/50 with 13 images cached at 752.2 MB, identical to the baseline. 50 of 50 is complete by definition, which establishes that iconLoadedAt, metaAttemptedAt and pathAt resolve.

#### 4.14.7 The Proxy Re-sort Compares Stored Keys

2026-09-24, revised 2026-09-25. After a load, restoreProxySortAfterLoad puts the proxy in source order (sort(-1)), so the first MW::filterChange finds the sort column wrong and runs sortChange, and from then on every filter change re-sorts every admitted row (invalidate() rebuilds the mapping with a full stable_sort). Each comparison was QSortFilterProxyModel::lessThan fetching BOTH values through DataModel::data: an index, a covers check and three RowStore lock acquisitions per side. Clearing a filter at 148,567 rows is about 2.5 million comparisons, 350-518 ms of a 700-900 ms toggle.

SortFilter now overrides lessThan:

- Inside a SortKeyScope, opened around the invalidate() in SortFilter::filterChange (which also calls rowCount() so the lazy rebuild happens inside the scope) and around SortFilter::sort, the sort column is read for every row in one RowStore::forEachRow pass.
- lessThan compares those keys with a copy of Qt 6.11's QAbstractItemModelPrivate::isVariantLessThan (private API, so copied, from qtbase/src/corelib/itemmodels/qabstractitemmodel.cpp; if Qt changes it, change the copy), honouring sortCaseSensitivity and isSortLocaleAware.
- Then it compares RANKS (2026-09-25). winnowSortRanks (Datamodel/variantless.h) sorts the column's keys once and gives equal keys equal ranks, so rank[a] &lt; rank[b] exactly when the key comparison says a &lt; b, and any stable sort gives the same order comparing two ints. SortFilter caches the ranks per (column, sort role, case sensitivity, locale awareness) until RowStore::fieldGeneration for that column moves, and falls back to comparing keys when the valid keys are not all one type (isVariantLessThan is only a strict weak ordering within a type). Pinned by tst_variantless::ranksGiveTheSameOrderAsQt / ranksRefuseMixedTypes. RowStore::fieldGeneration is per field bit plus a splice counter, pinned by tst_imagerow::fieldGenerationMovesForItsFieldAndSplicesOnly.
- Outside a scope, off the GUI thread, for a column RowStore does not hold, or for a row past the keys, it is Qt's lessThan unchanged. The dynamic re-sort of a single edited row behaves exactly as before, and a stray worker-thread proxy access can never read keys the GUI thread is freeing.

Two guards on the copy:

- tests/unit/tst_variantless checks it against Qt pairwise over every value pair and end to end: a stock proxy and a keyed one driven through the same sort history must hold the same order. Qt's sort is stable relative to the proxy's CURRENT order, so a hand-written stable_sort from source order is NOT a valid reference; the first draft of that test made exactly that mistake.
- Under --perfprobe, SortFilter::verifySortOrder walks the proxy after every keyed sort and prints "[PERF] sort check ... out of order = N" using Qt's base lessThan. 0 is the only correct answer.

#### 4.14.8 Clearing a Filter, a Load's Snapshots, Hidden Thumbnails, a Dropped Sort

Four follow-ups (2026-09-25), each measured first.

1. Clearing a filter at 148,567 rows was 273-382 ms: \~58 ms in Qt's stable sort (fixed by the ranks above), \~20 ms in filterAcceptsRow, and 55-72 ms rebuilding the proxy snapshot (fixed by sharing ProxyPaths, see [4.4.5 ImageCache Owns Its Own Bookkeeping](#445-imagecache-owns-its-own-bookkeeping)). The predicate: FilterCategory::isFiltering() no longer counts includeAll (the Search category's armed-but-empty state, which accepts every row) unless the category also has an exclude. That item is checked by default, so every filter pass had been reading and comparing every row's Search cell, and acceptsEverything() never took its fast path. tst_filterpredicate::includeAllMatchesWithoutComparing asserts the column is not read.
2. DataModel::scheduleProxySnapshotRebuild no longer rebuilds between CATALOG FILL batches (pendingCatalogRows non-empty): \~75 rebuilds over a growing model, \~1 s of a Library load, for readers MW::stop has halted. The pending flag is left set and endLoad's explicit rebuild makes the snapshot current. Folder loads are untouched; they rebuild explicitly per batch because readers do run during them.
3. DataModel::evictHiddenIcons, called by MW::filterChange after the snapshot flush. clearIconsOutsideChunkRange walks PROXY rows only, so a filtered-out row's thumbnail was never evicted (18,090 held against a 10,000 bound after one filter). It runs in bounded mode only (the chunk smaller than the model) and only past the retention bound (maxIconChunkOrAll); MetaRead re-reads them when a filter change brings them back, because filterChange's MetaRead::initialize clears readSuccessThisCycle. "[PERF] evictHiddenIcons" under --perfprobe.
4. MW::sortChange no longer drops a USER sort (menu, direction button, table header, workspace) asked for while metadata is still loading. It records the column and direction, logs a Comment to the issue log, and MW::applyDeferredSort runs it from metadataComplete after that function resets the menu to File Name. Internal callers keep the silent skip. Measured: the sort menu and the direction button are DISABLED while a load runs, so in practice this catches a table-header click or a workspace switch during a load; the menu path is normally unreachable.

#### 4.14.9 Rating and Label Edits

2026-09-24. A rating or colour-label keypress cost \~250 ms at 148,567 rows: \~145 ms in a full MW::filterChange, \~110 ms rebuilding the whole filter-count table for one changed row, \~23 ms in a thumbnail refresh with a relayout. Three changes:

1. MW::editNeedsRefilter(column): the edit runs filterChange only when the proxy is SORTED by the edited column (setValDm writes under a QSignalBlocker, so the proxy would not re-sort by itself) or an ACTIVE filter category reads it (SortFilter::filterReadsColumn -> FilterPredicate::readsColumn, pinned by tst_filterpredicate::readsColumnOnlyForActiveCategories). Otherwise it only lifts the proxy suspension. The edited cell repaints through setValDm's visible-row notification, and the edited category's counts come from the updateCategory that runs first. Side effect: the first edit after opening the Library no longer re-sorts the grid into the sort-menu order; the first real filter change still does.
2. The filter-count table is patched, not rebuilt (see [4.4.1 BuildFilters Reads a Snapshot](#441-buildfilters-reads-a-snapshot)).
3. MW::repaintIconViews: a viewport update on thumbView and gridView instead of refreshIcons, whose rejustify is for a change of thumbnail size, not of a badge.

Under --perfprobe each edit prints "[PERF] MW::setRating N ms ... refilter = yes/no" (and MW::setColorClass) for the WHOLE keypress, sidecar write included.

#### 4.14.10 The Two Post-Load Stalls

2026-09-24. Opening a 148,567-image Library produced two GUI stalls every time, \~1.1-1.5 s as the load completed and \~1.5-2.2 s a few seconds later, because the work queued behind the last fill batch runs back to back and starves the watchdog timer. The pieces:

1. MW::buildFiltersWhenModelReady called build() and then recount(), and recount() ran BOTH counting passes over every row on the GUI thread (\~250-430 ms) to supply what build()'s Reset did not: unfiltered counts for items AddItems skips (Filters::addCategoryItems drops a value that is already an item: the predefined Picks/Ratings/Labels items, and anything a non-reset build kept). The Reset run in BuildFilters::run now does updateUnfilteredCounts itself, on the worker after AddItems, and buildFiltersWhenModelReady calls recount() only when build() will return early (filters already built or building), which is the case recount exists for.
2. MW::checkForUpdate's first QNetworkAccessManager::get initialised Qt's TLS backend and loaded the system certificates on the GUI thread, 4 s in, mid-load. showEvent now warms QSslConfiguration::defaultConfiguration() on a pool thread when it schedules the check; both TLS backends guard that initialisation with a mutex.
3. finishCatalogFill's "Sorting ..." message was a synchronous repaint for a 3-7 ms step. Removed ("Collating folders ..." stays).
4. BuildFilters::applyOps took 542 ms (115 ms after the fix): Filters::addFolderItems created each of 8,400 folder items ATTACHED, so each cost an insert and every setter a dataChanged through the tree model, \~50,000 signals. addFolderItems, addKeywordItems and addCategoryItems now build new items detached (a node under a NEW parent is simply built under it) and hand each already-attached parent its new children in one addChildren; order is unchanged. Detached items are styled with Filters::applyItemStyle (styleFilterItem without its category-header test, since a detached top-level node has no parent yet). Detached setup also no longer sets itemCheckStateHasChanged via Filters::dataChanged; that flag interprets user clicks, and a build setting it was spurious. Pinned by tst_filters (tree shape under anchors, roll-up, state surviving a second build, keyword tree).
5. The second stall was the automatic catalog scan, which survived 1-4 (\~1.4 s). Sampled at 10 ms intervals (1 ms sampling perturbs the load enough to move or merge the stalls): a single-shot timer -> MW::startCatalogScan -> FilterPanel::setScanning(true) -> refresh() -> runSearch -> Catalog::searchRows fetching all 148,567 rows on the GUI thread (\~1.1 s), after which runSearch found the result unchanged and loaded nothing. setScanning(true) now only calls updateStatus. setScanning(false), at the end of a scan, still refreshes, because that is how newly catalogued rows reach the panel.

Then the search left the GUI thread entirely: FilterPanel::runSearch runs Catalog::searchRows on a pool thread and applies the result in FilterPanel::applySearchResult on the GUI thread.

- searchGen numbers the searches and only the newest is applied, so a slow result cannot land over a later scope switch or query; leaving Catalog scope voids one in flight.
- forcePending carries a scope entry's `force` across searches that superseded it.
- The run-to-run path comparison is built on the worker.
- updateStatus holds back "Nothing catalogued yet" while a search is in flight (totalMatches is 0 until the first one lands).
- Catalog::searchRows releases Catalog::mutex once the query is BUILT (the SQL runs on the calling thread's own CacheDb connection). Held, a pool-thread query would have blocked every GUI-thread Catalog call (isAvailable, a rating's updateCatalogForRow) for its 1.1-1.5 s, moving the stall rather than removing it.
- Under --perfprobe: "[PERF] catalog search N ms (pool thread) rows = ... changed = ... forced = ...".

Not changed: QListView's one full layout of the filmstrip after a load (\~100-170 ms), and DataModel::rebuildProxySnapshot firing between folder-load batches (\~0.6-1 s of load time, spread across batches, so not a stall).

#### 4.14.11 Crash on Quit From the Dock, at Logout or at Shutdown

Fixed 2026-09-24. Three layers, found in order.

1. The SQLite connection registry. Those quits go through -[NSApplication terminate:], which calls exit() directly: main() never returns, so the QApplication on its stack still exists while static destructors run. QtSql's connection registry (a Q_GLOBAL_STATIC) is destroyed among them, and the main thread's QThreadStorage&lt;Conn\*> (Cache/cachedb.cpp, one SQLite connection per thread) is cleaned up AFTER it. So Conn::release's guard, !QCoreApplication::instance(), passed, it called QSqlDatabase::database and read the destroyed registry: SIGSEGV in QtSqlGlobals::connection. Five crash reports in one day, all from that path; a quit through Qt Creator's stop, which returns from main normally, did not crash. Conn::release now also returns early on gProcessExiting, set by an atexit handler registered just after the first addDatabase. That is after the registry exists, so (atexit handlers and static destructors run in reverse registration order) it runs before the registry is destroyed.
2. The catalog scanner thread, still mid-file while exit() destroyed the globals it uses (one report in Jpeg::parse -> G::issueDedup's static hash, one in Catalog::staleOf -> CacheDb::db -> the QtSql registry). MW::closeEvent called CatalogScanner::stop(), which only raises the abort flag; the destructor's quit()+wait() never runs, because MW is not destroyed before exit() on this path. closeEvent now calls CatalogScanner::shutdown(): stop, quit the thread and wait for it, bounded at 5 s (every scanner loop checks abort between files, so it normally returns in milliseconds). The destructor calls the same function.
3. The root cause: closeEvent was not running on these quits AT ALL (no "MW::stop src = MW::closeEvent" in the log). Since 2024-11 main() had called Mac::initializeAppDelegate(), which did [NSApp setDelegate:] with a Winnow AppDelegate whose only method was applicationSupportsSecureRestorableState. That REPLACED Qt's QCocoaApplicationDelegate (confirmed in the running app with lldb: NSApp.delegate was &lt;AppDelegate>). AppKit asked that delegate whether to terminate, it had no applicationShouldTerminate, so -[NSApplication \_handleAEQuit] went straight to terminate: -> exit(). No picks prompt, no Develop-edit flush (developProperties->flushAll), no DevPreviewCache/ThumbCache saves, and every worker thread left running into static destruction. Qt's delegate also carries openFiles, Dock-icon reopen and the Dock menu, all bypassed with it. Qt 6.11's own delegate already returns YES for applicationSupportsSecureRestorableState, so the call and the class are gone (Utilities/mac.mm explains; a future delegate must be set BEFORE QApplication so Qt keeps it as its reflectionDelegate).

The Conn and CatalogScanner guards stay: they are correct on any path that reaches exit() with threads alive.

#### 4.14.12 Building the Row Store (the Migration Record)

DataModel went from a QStandardItemModel (93 QStandardItems per row) to a QAbstractTableModel over RowStore / ScratchStore / IconStore in a sequence of passes, each verified before the next. The record is kept for its lessons; the result is [4.5 Row Storage](#45-row-storage).

##### 4.14.12.1 The Sequence

1. Shadow, not swap. A model cannot be half-swapped: change the base class and nothing works until everything works, so there is no point where a test can say whether it is still correct. The store was written BESIDE the items by the same DataModel::setData, and DataModel::verifyRowStore() walked every row and covered column and asked the two to agree. Nothing read the store; it was the thing under test. It covered 37 columns, listed explicitly rather than inferred as "everything not scratch", because a column silently assumed covered is a column the verification quietly stopped checking.
2. data() served the covered columns from the store, with G::useRowStore = false falling straight back. Proof was an A/B fingerprint: a SHA-1 over what data() returns for every covered column of every row, store on and off.
3. Thumbnails moved to the path-keyed IconStore. Five sites bypassed the data()/setData() seam and had to be converted: two idempotency guards in setIcon/setIcon1 (itemFromIndex(dmIdx)->icon().isNull()), setIconFromVideoFrame's item->setIcon, two clipboard/drag paths in IconView (dm->item(row)->icon()), and the thumbnail ROTATION in MW, which also leaked a QStandardItem it allocated and immediately overwrote. Verified over four folders including videos: icons through data() matched the store's count every time (4/4, 13/13, 50/50, 51/51).
4. The ScratchStore took the 24 decode-time columns, under the same shadow verification (0 mismatches out of 7,800 values over five folders).
5. The item writes were deleted for every covered column, both stores together, retiring verifyRowStore and G::useRowStore with them (a fallback to the items is not a fallback once they are empty). Items per row: 93 -> 31.4.
6. The second batch covered 31 more columns (four decode facts to scratch: NS Thumb, NS Image, Msec/Mp, Raw Render; 27 image properties to ImageRow) and introduced the set mask. Items per row: 31.4 -> 3.1.
7. The compiled filter predicate replaced the tree walk (verified by keeping the old implementation as filterAcceptsRowLegacy and comparing row by row over 1,600 randomised trials on the REAL Filters tree, 0 mismatches).
8. Search and Ingested were settled on bool. Items per row: 3.1 -> 1.08.
9. The remaining roles (column 0's icon rect and pairing roles, the ErrColumn issue list) moved, and the base class was swapped, verified by an A/B fingerprint at ELEVEN roles plus flags(), headerData() at four roles and the counts, byte-identical on all four folders, and by the model_contract gate.

##### 4.14.12.2 Bugs the Verification Found

- Rating is a QString, not a number. Stored as an int, an unrated image read back as "0", which would have put it in a rating category it does not belong to.
- MPix is a formatted string. A float in the store returned 24.15999984741211 where the model said 24.16: one filter item per image instead of one per sensor size.
- Neither would have crashed anything; both would have quietly changed what the Filters panel offered. The rule both broke: return exactly what the model returned.
- The text comparison missed a type change, and the app aborted on the first run with reads enabled: ExposureTimeItemDelegate::displayText(value=+Inf) -> qRound(+Inf) -> ASSERT. exposureTimeNum is a double and the delegate guards with "value == 0"; the store had interned it as text, the digits matched, but the guard does not fire for a QString. Aperture, focal length and ISO had the same fault. verifyRowStore then compared the variant's KIND as well as its text, grouping the numeric types together (the model itself was loose there), because text-vs-number is what a delegate branches on.
- With the type check, three columns turned out to hold a different type depending on which path wrote them last (a defect in the MODEL): Search ("false" QString at creation, bool once metadata arrived), Width and Height (QString::number from addMetadataForItem, int from Thumb::setImageDimensions via setValDm). Width and Height were settled on int, which also made the sort consistently numeric. A dead QString write of Orientation in addMetadataForItem was removed, settling that column as int.
- A role-aware coverage change broke every path. Coverage became per (column, role) (PathColumn at G::PathRole), but the WRITE side kept an older "EditRole or DisplayRole" guard in front of covers(), so PathRole writes were dropped while data() served PathRole from the store. The app came up with no thumbnails and no loupe image. Neither check caught it, because verifyRowStore and the fingerprint both looped at Qt::EditRole ONLY, so the one column covered at another role was the one neither looked at. "0 mismatches over 1,750 values" was true and useless. Both then iterated every role the store claimed, and the re-broken build reported it plainly (PATHS: empty=4 of 4, icons=0, loupeImage=NO).
- The scratch comparison would have compared "" with "". QVariant::toString() is EMPTY for a QByteArray and a QVariantList, so the ICC buffer and IFD offsets, the two columns least likely to be right, would have reported clean. Both got a real rendering (hex for the blob, joined elements for the list) before the store was trusted.
- The running counts drifted after the item writes went. setData counted transitions by reading the OLD value with QStandardItemModel::data; once the items were empty every write looked like a change and the counts drifted past rowCount(). Reading the old value through data() fixed it, verified against a full scan on five runs and proven to fail by re-injecting the item read (56/50 attempted, 55/50 loaded).
- itemFromIndex creates what it cannot find. iconCount(), the loaded-icon range report and the row report all asked itemFromIndex(...)->icon(), which had returned null since thumbnails left the items, and in Qt 6 itemFromIndex LAZILY CREATES a missing item, so each call allocated a QStandardItem per row to read a guaranteed null. The same trap invalidated the first attempt to measure the work: a probe walking itemFromIndex reported 93 items per row, having created every one of them.
- The icon was still being written to the item as well as to IconStore and never read back. That one wasted write was why column 0 still had a QStandardItem on every row after the value columns had gone.
- In passing: DataModel::imMetadata read m.iccSpace from G::ICCSegmentOffsetColumn rather than G::ICCSpaceColumn, so the colour-space NAME came back as an offset. It was left for a separate behaviour change and has since been fixed (datamodel.cpp reads ICCSpaceColumn).
- ThreadSanitizer found what the fingerprints could not: the store locks (see [4.5.2 RowStore](#452-rowstore)). Both races were confirmed NEW by stashing the work and re-running: the unmodified tree passed. With the locks, run_tsan.sh passed and run_tsan_proxy.sh reported no race on three consecutive runs against the 50-file folder.

##### 4.14.12.3 A Fact That Was Wrong

Search and Ingested were held back through three passes on a claim, written down twice, that QVariant(QString("false")).toBool() is TRUE ("a non-empty string"), making the row-creation value a live matching bug only the filter could settle. Measured:

```
  QVariant(QString("false")).toBool()             false   (Qt 6 special-cases it)
  QVariant(QString("true")).toBool()              true
  QVariant(QString("false")) == QVariant(false)   true    (both directions)
  QVariant(QString("true"))  == QVariant(true)    true
```

So the mixed types cost nothing at runtime: every toBool() reader was right, and the filter's QVariant comparison converted between the two forms. Settling them was tidying, not a fix. The lesson is not about QVariant: a plausible claim about a library was carried through three passes and steered a decision because nobody spent the two minutes it took to run it. tst_imagerow::variantComparisonIsTypeTolerant pins the measured behaviour, because the wrong version was persuasive and because anything reading an older catalog row still relies on the conversion. The change was verified by fingerprinting WHICH ROWS each of 400 randomised filter trials accepts, per folder, before and after: byte-identical on all four.

##### 4.14.12.4 Rules That Came Out of It

- A check that does not cover the same ground as the code it checks proves nothing about the part it skips. Iterate every role, every type, every path.
- A comparison is only evidence if it is stable when nothing changed. Three runs of the UNCHANGED binary produced three different fingerprints; six columns vary run to run. NS Thumb, NS Image and DecoderId legitimately (nanosecond timings, and which decoder thread took the row). XmpSegmentLength, IsXMP and ICCSpace did NOT legitimately: a pre-existing metadata-read defect that reproduces on the unmodified binary and does not converge at a 25-second settle. Noted, not fixed.
- Prove a check fails before trusting it: every new check here was re-run with the bug deliberately re-injected, and seen to fail by name, before it was believed.
- The Filters build has a load-timing dependency of its own: the same folder yields 17 or 50 leaf items (74 vs 75 items) on different runs. A comparison that included it would have blamed the store. Still unexplained.
- Two guards (or two lists) that must agree is one too many. Make one the authority and derive the other.

#### 4.14.13 A Classification Key Rebuilt the Filter Tree on Another Thread (the 1-5 Crash)

The report was "setting a colour (keys 1-5) can cause a crash" during a cull of a card. The crash report said exactly where: SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow, EXC_BAD_ACCESS on a null pointer, reached from QSortFilterProxyModel::invalidateRowsFilter &lt;- SortFilter::filterChange &lt;- MW::filterChange &lt;- MW::setColorClass (against the installed 2.05 build).

BuildFilters::updateCategory's own comment states the rule: a caller that follows it with MW::filterChange MUST pass runSync, because filterChange un-suspends the proxy and re-runs filterAcceptsRow over category items the worker is still adding and removing. MW::togglePick had been fixed for this; MW::setRating, MW::setColorClass, MW::setColorClassForRow, MW::findDuplicates and InfoView::dataChanged (Title, Creator) had not, and each called filterChange on the very next line. All now pass runSync = true.

Two later changes narrowed the window without closing the contract: filterAcceptsRow evaluates a compiled FilterPredicate held by shared_ptr rather than walking the tree, and BuildFilters::dispatchOps applies every tree mutation on the GUI thread. Between them the use-after-free is gone from the current code, which is why it is a 2.05 crash. The ordering is what remains (stale counts), and passing runSync fixes both.

Why only in a cull: one colour key is one rebuild and one filter change, so nothing overlaps. A cull is a key every second or two for an hour, over a folder large enough that the rebuild is still running when filterChange starts.

The other half of the same contract is who lifts the suspension; see [4.7.2 Whoever Suspends the Proxy Must See It Lifted](#472-whoever-suspends-the-proxy-must-see-it-lifted).

#### 4.14.14 The Visible Range the Keyboard Never Updated (and the Latch That Leaked)

MW::updateIconRange's only navigation-reachable callers were MW::thumbHasScrolled / gridHasScrolled / tableHasScrolled, all gated on G::ignoreScrollSignal being false. MW::fileSelectionChange calls scrollToCurrent on all three views, and each of those set that flag TRUE immediately before its own scrollTo. So every handler in the sequence saw true and skipped: arrow-key navigation never measured the visible window.

The cost was suppressed repaints, not a stale number. Measured over 20 seconds of held arrow key on a 3,404-row card folder: the visible range frozen at 0-10, emits(suppressed) 11,307 against emits(visible) 149. Every icon arriving for the rows the user was actually looking at was stored without telling the views. It was largely invisible because scrolling repaints the strip anyway.

Fix: updateChange calls scheduleIconRangeSettle after fileSelectionChange returns. That helper already existed for the deferred-layout case: one pending settle, a zero timer, and a re-dispatch to MetaRead only if the chunk moved. A held arrow key pays for one measurement per turn of the event loop rather than one per keypress. A/B over 600 selections at 45 ms: GUI time per selection p50 2 ms and p90 5 ms in both, gap p50 44 ms in both, GUI stalls 6 in both; the 3 ms updateIconRange costs lands on the settle timer rather than on the keypress.

The flag itself leaked. G::ignoreScrollSignal was set by hand at six sites and cleared at the TAIL of the three handlers, so the clearing belonged to a different function from the setting, and any path that set it without producing a scroll signal left it on. That was the ordinary case: in Loupe, gridView and tableView are hidden, so the last two scrollToCurrent calls moved no scrollbar, no handler ran, and the flag stayed TRUE, swallowing the user's NEXT genuine scroll. It is now G::ScrollSignalGuard.

#### 4.14.15 A Filter That Turned Itself Off (Keyword Added in a Filtered Catalog)

Reported from a catalog filtered on 2026: double-clicking a keyword in the Keyword list wrote the tag, and the grid and status bar then showed all 43,000 images while the Filters panel still showed 2026 checked. The keyword itself was written correctly (the sidecar carried dc:subject Squirrel and lr:hierarchicalSubject Fauna|Animal|Squirrel). What failed was the filter.

The cause was G::allMetadataAttempted used as though it meant "the model is ready". In a catalog scope it flaps false constantly, because every filter change moves the visible window and the scroll-in verifier then finds more stale rows. MW::filterChange and Filters::itemClickedSignal had been fixed for this, and the fix stopped there. Four more places still read the flag:

- SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow began "if (!G::allMetadataAttempted) return true", so the PROXY accepted every row. The panel's checkboxes were untouched, nothing errored, and the scope silently widened.
- BuildFilters::update, updateAllCounts and updateCategory each skipped their rebuild on the same flag. updateCategory suspends the proxy on entry and, on that path, returned WITHOUT lifting the suspension and without rebuilding, so the category the edit had just changed was never updated.

All four were moved to G::isModifyingDatamodel, and then (2026-09-28) to G::isLoadRunning when it turned out that a replacing load's MW::stop() clears isModifyingDatamodel at once, so the gates had been off for the whole fill and metadata read of every replacing load. See [4.7.3 "Is a Load Running" Is Not "Has Every Row Been Read"](#473-is-a-load-running-is-not-has-every-row-been-read).

#### 4.14.16 The Accessibility Bridge Rebuilds the Whole Table, per Write

What froze a catalog scope for 42 seconds was found by sampling the stalled process rather than by reasoning about it: 2,666 of 2,838 main-thread samples, 94%:

```
  DataModel::setValSf -> QSortFilterProxyModel::setData -> DataModel::setData
    -> dataChanged -> _q_sourceDataChanged -> dataChanged
      -> QAbstractItemView::dataChanged
        -> -[QMacAccessibilityElement updateTableModel]
          -> -[QMacAccessibilityElement populateTableArray:count:]
            -> _objc_rootAllocWithZone -> malloc
```

Every per-row write reached the view; the view notified the Cocoa accessibility bridge; the bridge rebuilt its element array for EVERY ROW IN THE MODEL, an Obj-C object per cell, once per write, over 42,979 rows. Confirmed by turning it off: WINNOW_NO_A11Y=1 made the stall vanish with every other number unchanged.

Why six earlier hypotheses missed it:

- It is per WRITE, not per icon, so lowering the thumbnail ceiling from 10,000 to 2,000 cut the icons 12x and left the stall at 41 s.
- It happens inside queued setValSf events, so every timed stage of the load (applyScope 585 ms, the 22-batch fill 757 ms, folders+setCurrent 12 ms, endLoad 8 ms, restoreSort 26 ms, folderChanged 0 ms, availabilityOf 297 ms off-thread, applyOps 78 ms) was small and none contained it.
- The offscreen platform plugin has no Cocoa accessibility bridge, so --catalogload reported healthy numbers throughout.

The fixes, in order:

1. setValSf now writes under a blocker and emits for visible rows only, as setValDm already had since the earlier load-responsiveness work. 41.8 s -> 14.6 s, and one stall instead of two.
2. DataModel::setIcon made three bare setData calls (decoration, IconLoadedColumn, MetadataReadingColumn) where setIcon1 beside it batched; it now batches too. The counters then said the throttle was working (emits(visible) = 225 against emits(suppressed) = 7,999, visible range 0-10) and that the remaining stall was not notifying.
3. A second sample named the fourth write path: DataModel::setIconFromVideoFrame, which never consulted iconRowVisible and made FIVE bare setData calls, with an empty brace block where the QSignalBlocker belonged. It was not even counted, which is why emits(visible) sat frozen while the stalls continued. A catalog holds videos (201 in the icon range on this library), and a video frame decodes slowly, so they arrived spread across the whole load, one 42,979-element rebuild each.
4. A third sample, during the 5.6 s that survived, landed in setValSf's OWN emit, the one the visible-row guard allows. The guard was right (eleven rows on screen), but 209 notifications went to those eleven rows, because a row being filled takes a burst of writes. At \~27 ms per rebuild that is the 5.6 s exactly. scheduleVisibleEmit coalesces them.
5. The end state removes the table: everything above reduced the NUMBER of notifications, but a fill still inserts in 21 batches, and a folder -> Catalog switch measured 7.9-8.3 s against 1.6 s for the same load at startup (the per-batch notification climbed with the model, 0.3 -> 5 ms, and 550 icons took 4,206 ms to set against 0.2 ms for 126 at startup). The only difference was whether the bridge was on. The QAccessible factory (see [4.8.3 Item Views Offer No Table to Accessibility (macOS)](#483-item-views-offer-no-table-to-accessibility-macos)) took IconView and TableView off the table interface: 8.2 s -> 3.1 s. The per-batch notification still climbed 0.12 -> 1.43 ms, a quarter of the old cost: one view of four. TableView's frozenView, a plain QTableView overlay on the same model and selection model, is now a FrozenTableView matched by the factory as well.

The same shape appeared three times in one investigation: SortFilter recompiling the whole predicate per tree item, MetaRead re-dispatching every row per redo, and the accessibility bridge rebuilding every row per write. Each was invisible at folder scale and quadratic at catalog scale.

#### 4.14.17 Filter the Catalog and Nothing Paints (an Invalid Fallback Index)

Catalog scope, click a filter, and the thumbnails do not appear at all. Click anywhere in thumbView, or switch to gridView and back, and they appear.

It was one invalid QModelIndex. MW::filterChange asks whether the current image survived the filter, and falls back when it did not:

```
  QModelIndex newSfIdx = dm->sf->mapFromSource(dm->currentDmIdx);
  int oldSfRow = dm->currentSfIdx.row();
  if (!newSfIdx.isValid()) {
      if (oldSfRow < sfRows) newSfIdx = dm->sf->index(oldSfRow, 0);
      else newSfIdx = dm->sf->index(sfRows-1, 0);
  }
```

mapFromSource is invalid whenever the filter removed the current image, the ordinary case. The fallback read dm->currentSfIdx, a PERSISTENT index into the proxy, and since SortFilter::filterChange calls invalidate() rather than re-mapping, after the filter it read back as row -1. -1 is less than sfRows, so the first branch was taken, and sf->index(-1, 0) is INVALID. Selection::select rejects one: it warns, beeps, raises a popup and returns WITHOUT SELECTING. Nothing then emitted fileSelectionChange, so nothing dispatched MetaRead for the new visible window, so no icons were read for the rows on screen. A click selects a row and dispatches a read; a view switch calls updateIconRange and dispatches a read; hence "it paints if I touch it".

Fix 1, a clamp: try dm->currentSfRow (the maintained plain int) first, then the persistent index, then row 0, bounded by sfRows-1. A filtration with no rows has already returned through nullFiltration.

The same hole had a second door: UNCHECKING the filter. With the clamp in, filtering ISO 80 painted correctly, and removing that filter painted three thumbnails (the current row and its two neighbours, the only ones that already had icons). Nothing was invalid this time. The dispatch to MetaRead had never been MW::filterChange's own act; it was a side effect of the selection, and both branches can be silent (Selection::recover on purpose, Selection::select when the row is already current).

Fix 2: filterChange dispatches for itself (see [4.8.2 Whatever Changes the Visible Set Asks for What It Needs](#482-whatever-changes-the-visible-set-asks-for-what-it-needs)). The phase timer gained a "dispatch" phase so the cost is visible.

Read the warnings in the paste before instrumenting what is not warning. "Selection::select(QModelIndex) sfIdx = QModelIndex(-1,-1,0x0,QObject(0x0)) invalid." sat in the middle of every pasted probe, one line above the filterChange summary, through three rounds of investigation that went to the deferred layout, the nested event loop and the visible-emit gate first. Two wrong suspects were ruled out by measurement and one by revert: removing the G::wait(100) did not cause it (the symptom stayed with the wait restored), and the emit gate did not (notified = 209, suppressed = 2,855, every suppressed row genuinely off-screen, 11 of 355 visible).

Not kept: a mechanism to remember and repay suppressed notifications. It was written against the gate theory, and the data says the gate behaves as designed; an off-screen row repaints from the model when it is scrolled to. It would have been a permanent cost on the hot path for a hypothesis already overtaken.

#### 4.14.18 Sort the Catalog and Every Other Cell Is Blank (a Position Is Not an Image)

A 155,098-row Library load, Grid view, saved Library sort File Name: every other cell blank on screen (the frame, label and number missing, the delegate's early return for a row with no icon). A scroll brought them back.

The cause: a catalog fills in PATH order, and MetaRead loads the icon chunk (rows 0-10,000) in that order. At load completion MW::applyRestoredLibrarySort re-sorted by file NAME. MetaRead's worker-local sets (readSuccessThisCycle, rowsReading, videoRowsReading) and its icon range were all PROXY rows (positions), and a sort keeps the instance, so nothing reset them and nothing restarted the loader. By name, the duplicates in a second folder (dm row \~103,000) interleave with the first (dm rows 0-15): the first set was loaded, the second never asked for, hence the alternating pattern. A filter change never had this problem because it bumps the instance and re-initialises MetaRead.

How it was found: MetaRead::rowStateReport (probe) names, per row, whether the loader thinks it is in flight, returned or out of range. Driven by the headless --catalogload with WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_SORTNAME=1 (sort after the load settles), it reproduced the screenshot image for image. WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_RESTORESORT=1 arms the restored sort where a launch runs it (mid-cycle); WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_JUMP=&lt;row> selects a row and reports again; WINNOW_ROWREPORT_ALL=1 lists loaded rows too.

The fixes:

1. The three MetaRead sets are keyed by DATAMODEL row. DataModel rows only move under a new instance (MW::applyModelChange bumps it first), which clears them. DataModel::videoReadingCleared and MetaRead's column write (setValDm, was setValSf) carry the DataModel row for the same reason.
2. MW::resyncIconLoaderAfterReorder, called at the end of MW::sortChange: queued, it re-measures the visible window (updateIconRange -> setIconRange recounts the chunk), and if the chunk is missing icons runs the index prefetch (hydrated catalog) and reloadIconChunk.
3. A proxy layoutChanged resets the eviction delta (lastEvictStart/End), so the next clearIconsOutsideChunkRange is a full sweep.
4. The pending first selection is a DataModel row (pendingSelectionDmRow). As a position it stayed armed when the index prefetch served the row, and after a re-sort the first reader returning ANY image at that position selected it; the A/B run with the old code showed the selection jumping to row 0.

Open: "Loading the library" was reported blanking mid-load. MW::updateIconRange no longer switches to GridTab while G::isLoadRunning and the message is showing, but the suspected route (the hidden grid resized by the status bar) was DISPROVED: Qt does not deliver resize events to hidden widgets (WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_RESIZE=1 A/B, no flip either way). Under --perfprobe every central page change during a load prints with its call stack ("[PERF] CENTRAL page ->"), to name the real caller from one session.

#### 4.14.19 The Phantom Sort Column and the Header Click That Ran Before the Sort

A persisted sortColumn could be out of range (== G::TotalColumns) and reach the proxy via QTableView::setSortingEnabled, which calls sort() directly, bypassing MW::sortChange / IconView::sortThumbs. Sorting by an invalid column reverses the model under DescendingOrder (Z-A). SortFilter::sort() now clamps any out-of-range column to -1 (no sort / source order), the single chokepoint covering every path, and the workspace load also sanitises a stale persisted sortColumn.

A header-click sort ran MW's handling before the sort. MW::sortIndicatorChanged is connected to the same QHeaderView::sortIndicatorChanged signal that QTableView sorts from, and MW::reset toggles setSortingEnabled off and on, which RE-REGISTERS QTableView's slot behind MW's. So from the first folder load onwards MW's ran FIRST, against the pre-sort order. Qt remaps the selection model correctly across a proxy sort (measured: selection and current index both follow the items), but everything MW did afterwards (dm->currentSfIdx/currentSfRow, the delegates' currentRow, the scroll and the image cache resort) kept the OLD row, so the current image jumped while the menu sort held it.

- The tail now runs QUEUED (so connection order cannot matter) and goes through MW::sortChange, the same function the sort menu uses; the re-sort there is a no-op because the proxy already holds the column and order.
- MW::sortColumn / isReverseSort are synced here too. Checking a menu action does not emit triggered, so sortChangeFromAction never ran and MW's idea of the sort stayed on whatever the MENU last chose, which MW::filterChange reads to decide whether the sort needs recovering.

## 5 Caching

Three caches keep Winnow from decoding or reading the same thing twice:

- Metadata and icons: MetaRead (Cache/metaread.cpp) dispatches a pool of Reader workers (Cache/reader.cpp) that read each row's metadata and its 256 px icon into the DataModel. Icons are also cached on disk in the index (see [5.8 Thumbnails in the Index (ThumbCache)](#58-thumbnails-in-the-index-thumbcache)).
- Full-size images: ImageCache (Cache/imagecache.cpp) decodes ahead of and behind the current image with a pool of ImageDecoder workers.
- Developed previews: DevPreviewCache (see [12.1 Original and Developed Previews](#121-original-and-developed-previews)).

The earlier MetadataCache / metadataCacheThread system (Cache/mdcache.cpp, mdcacher.cpp, mdcachemgr.cpp) is no longer compiled; the files are retained on disk for reference only.

### 5.1 Overview

- When a new folder or a new file is selected, or a scroll event occurs in IconView, MetaRead is started. It dispatches Reader workers outward from the start row to load metadata and icons.
- Once the start row has been read, MetaRead emits select, which (via MW::fileSelectionChange) starts the ImageCache around the current row; from then on the two run concurrently.
- If a new image is selected, MW::fileSelectionChange repositions MetaRead and the ImageCache around the new current row.
- If the user scrolls the thumbView or gridView, scroll events reach MW::thumbHasScrolled / MW::gridHasScrolled. Rapid scrolling coalesces (the next scroll event supersedes the prior), so MetaRead is only re-dispatched when scrolling pauses or is slow. ImageCache is not restarted, because no new image has been selected.

See the top-of-file comments in Cache/metaread.cpp and Cache/reader.cpp for more detail.

### 5.2 Cache Status

Two status lights on the right of the status bar (metadataThreadRunningLabel and imageThreadRunningLabel) show metadata and image caching; a small light on the lower right of each thumbnail shows that its image is cached. The lights are shown in Preview mode only: Develop works on the single current image with read-ahead trimmed to it, so folder caching progress means nothing there. MW::updateStatusBar owns their visibility (from G::operationMode), and MW::setOperationMode calls it on every mode change.

The metadata light (MW::updateMetadataThreadRunStatus) is colour-coded so the active icon-cache mode is visible at a glance:

```
red     metadata thread running
green   idle, brute force (G::useJitIconCache == false)
blue    idle, JIT caching active (G::useJitIconCache == true)
orange  idle, forced pressure (G::iconPressureTestLevel >= 2)  [precedence: orange > blue]
yellow  idle, load failed
```

The image cache progress bar shows every image in the folder: the target range, which are cached, and the cursor position.

Functions:

```
MW::createStatusBar                      status labels, right of status bar
MW::refreshAfterImageCacheSizeChange     a preference change updates cache status
MW::setThreadRunStatusInactive           caching lights grey
MW::updateImageCachingThreadRunStatus    image caching light green/red
MW::updateMetadataThreadRunStatus        metadata light (colours above)
MW::setCacheStatusVisibility             updateState toggles the progress display
MW::updateImageCacheStatus               ImageCache updates cache status
MW::setCacheProgressEnabled              applies "Hide caching progress"
```
