A mouse wheel only ever reports a vertical delta, and a thumbView docked top or bottom is a single non-wrapping row with a horizontal scrollbar and no vertical one (MW::setThumbDockFeatures), so a vertical-only delta would move nothing. IconView::wheelEvent therefore remaps a vertical-only delta onto the x axis when !isWrapping(). That remap is the ONLY place horizontal thumbnail wheel scrolling is decided; there is no wheel handling in MW::eventFilter or in the scroll-sync path.

- isWrapping() is the axis test used throughout IconView (scrollPosition, scrollUp/Down, scrollPageUp/Down, both engines). Wrapping follows the thumbDock position: false when docked top or bottom (horizontal row), true when docked left, right or floating, and always true for gridView. Gestures that already carry an x component (two-finger horizontal, a tilt wheel, Shift+wheel on macOS) are untouched.
- The remap covers a trackpad vertical two-finger swipe as well as a mouse wheel, matching how a single-row list behaves elsewhere on macOS. To limit it to a physical mouse, add event->source() == Qt::MouseEventNotSynthesized to the remap condition; the comment at the remap site says the same.

### 6.3 Resizing Icons or the Viewport

When the IconView viewport is resized or the icon size changes, the result is a scroll event. To keep the view centred on what it showed, the middle icon is tracked as dm->scrollToIcon: G::resizingIcons is set for the resize, the scroll event that follows does not reset dm->scrollToIcon, and MW::thumbHasScrolled / gridHasScrolled reset G::resizingIcons to false. That lets the three views sync on dm->scrollToIcon. A window resize burst (e.g. maximise) anchors on one row for the whole burst (see [6.4.2 A Window Resize Keeps the Grid on the Same Image (2026-10-01)](#642-a-window-resize-keeps-the-grid-on-the-same-image-2026-10-01)).

#### 6.3.1 Persisted Icon Size

IconView::assignedIconWidth is the reference width rejustify() uses to compute thumbs-per-row and then justify the cell width to exactly fill the row. The justified result lands in iconWidth, which can differ from assignedIconWidth, and iconWidth is viewport-dependent: a rejustify() at a narrow width shrinks it toward ICON_MIN while assignedIconWidth is unchanged.

- Save assignedIconWidth, not iconWidth. At startup the hidden gridView receives resize events at a narrow width, each scheduling a rejustify() that justified iconWidth down to e.g. 62; saving iconWidth persisted that transient size, so the grid reverted to \~62 on the next launch. (thumbView has an extra guard: rejustify() skips "Thumbnails" while G::isInitializing, and MW::showEvent applies its size via setThumbSize().)
- On restore, set assignedIconWidth = iconWidth BEFORE calling rejustify(). rejustify() justifies from assignedIconWidth, so restoring only iconWidth discards the saved size.
- rejustify clamps assignedIconWidth to [ICON_MIN, G::maxIconSize] and applies justify()'s cell ceiling (see [6.4.3 Rejustify Obeys the Enlarge Ceiling (2026-10-16)](#643-rejustify-obeys-the-enlarge-ceiling-2026-10-16)).

Where the rules are applied:

- MW::writeSettings / MW::createGridView: between-session save/restore. writeSettings saves gridView->assignedIconWidth as thumbWidthGrid; createGridView loads it into iconWidth, then copies it to assignedIconWidth.
- MW::snapshotWorkspace / MW::invokeWorkspace: per-workspace save/restore for thumbView and gridView (Main/workspaces.cpp).
- MW::builtInDefaultWorkspace sets assignedIconWidth = iconWidth before rejustify(), so the hard-coded defaults (thumb 100, grid 160) are honoured.

### 6.4 Investigations and Fixes

#### 6.4.1 Removing the G::wait Pumps

G::wait is NOT a sleep. It runs a nested event loop, so it costs whatever happens to be queued, it can paint a half-finished state, and it lets a second key press re-enter the code that called it. Treat every remaining call as a re-entrancy point.

##### 6.4.1.1 The Wait in scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible

The deferred layout was never what it waited for. Every reader in that function forces the posted layout itself: QListView::visualRect goes through rectForIndex and indexAt through intersectingSet, both of which call executePostedLayout(); QHeaderView does the same in its section lookups, which TableView::updateVisible reads through rowAt(). The one exception is TableView::isRowVisible, which tests a cached firstVisibleRow/lastVisibleRow window refreshed from resize and scroll events, so the wait is replaced by a direct tableView->updateVisible() when the table is visible. That much was verified against the Qt 6 sources rather than assumed.

What the pump also did is the part worth keeping. It let the queued tail of the caller run BEFORE updateIconRange measured the visible window: the deferred layouts, and the resize and rejustify that showing or hiding a scrollbar triggers, each of which calls updateIconRange. Measuring before those have run can leave the icon chunk centred on where the view WAS, and the chunk is what the loader reads.

MW::scheduleIconRangeSettle asks the same question on the other side of the queue instead: one pending settle at a time, a zero timer (lowest priority in Qt, so it lands after the posted layouts and resizes), and a re-dispatch through reloadIconChunk ONLY if the range actually moved. In the ordinary case the second measurement agrees with the first and it costs one updateIconRange. It is the same coalesced shape as scheduleVisibleEmit and scheduleCompileFilters, without the re-entrancy of a nested loop.

The first attempt at this was reverted, and why is the useful part. Removing the wait coincided with "filter the catalog and no thumbnails paint", so it was put back, correctly on the evidence available. The symptom then survived with the wait restored, which cleared it: the real defects were an invalid fallback index and a dispatch that rode on a side effect of the selection (see [4.14.17 Filter the Catalog and Nothing Paints (an Invalid Fallback Index)](#41417-filter-the-catalog-and-nothing-paints-an-invalid-fallback-index)). Only with those fixed did removing the wait mean anything, because until then any test of it was reading a broken load path.

##### 6.4.1.2 The View Switches' Waits (2026-10-01)

MW::gridDisplay and MW::tableDisplay each ran G::wait(100) before scrolling the newly shown view, on every view switch, and twice on G from Develop. Measured with WFPROBE, it was the largest remaining cost of leaving Develop. Inside it, a repaint painted a half-applied workspace (the full-window grid flash), the deferred keyword count refresh ran mid-switch, and a second key press could re-enter the switch.

What it was really waiting for was the new page's SIZE. QStackedLayout::setGeometry sizes only the CURRENT widget, and a page made current is resized by a posted LayoutRequest, so scrolling before that centred the row in the size the page had when last shown. Both functions now make that synchronous:

1. Activate the main window's layout (the thumb dock was just hidden or shown).
2. Re-apply the stack's rect, centralLayout->setGeometry(centralLayout->geometry()), which sizes the new page and sends its resize at once. Guarded for the first show, when the stack has no rect yet.
3. The QListView's deferred item layout needs nothing, because scrollTo forces it through visualRect. tableDisplay refreshes TableView's cached visible-row window with updateVisible.
4. Both then call scheduleIconRangeSettle, as scrollToCurrentRowIfNotVisible does.

The dead wait loop after the return in SortFilter::filterChange (whose while (!finished || timeIsUp) could never have exited) was deleted.

The table's first show was off-centre. TableView set its row height (verticalHeader()->setDefaultSectionSize, from the font size), icon size and header height ONLY in paintEvent, so the first tableDisplay centred the row with Qt's default row height and the first paint then resized every row under that pixel scroll position. It was right every time after, a latent bug the old wait may have hidden. Those settings are now TableView::applyRowMetrics. paintEvent still calls it (that is how a font change reaches the table), each setter is skipped when the value has not changed, and tableDisplay calls it before scrolling.

##### 6.4.1.3 Other Waits Removed (2026-10-01)

- Thumb's file-busy retry (Thumb::loadThumb) is now QThread::msleep(100). It runs on a Reader's own thread inside a queued Reader::read, where G::wait's nested loop could run MetaRead's BlockingQueued Reader::stop (readerThread->quit()) in the middle of the load. Abort is unaffected: abortProcessing sets the flag directly and it is tested on both sides of the wait.
- DockWidget::restore's 10 ms pause, which let the platform place the newly floating native window before the saved geometry was applied, is now a 10 ms deferred setGeometry. Same ordering, without pumping every queued event inside the double-click handler; it is skipped if the dock has been docked again in between.
- Quitting during a background ingest no longer waits inside MW::closeEvent. It used to run while (G::isRunningBackgroundIngest) G::wait(100), a nested event loop inside a half-closed window for as long as the copy took. Now closeEvent DECLINES the close (event->ignore()), sets quitWhenIngestDone and shows the popup. The check comes first, ahead of the picks question, so that question is asked once. MW::ingestFinished queues MW::close when the copy is done, and that close runs the normal teardown. The app stays usable while the ingest finishes, and an OS-level quit (Dock, logout) is cancelled rather than held, with Winnow quitting by itself afterwards. Ingest::run's early return when no filename template matched now emits ingestFinished as well; it used to leave the flag set forever, which would have hung the old loop on quit.

##### 6.4.1.4 Embellish Export Runs From the Event Loop (2026-10-18)

EmbelExport::exportImages used to be one loop on the GUI thread with a G::wait(50) per image, and renderDeveloped pumped G::wait(20) until each develop render landed. That pump was how Esc reached the abort, but it also delivered every other key, click, wheel, drop and window close mid-export, so ExportInputGuard, an application event filter, swallowed all user input except Esc for the whole export. The UI was frozen for as long as the batch took.

Both the pump and the guard are gone. The export is now a chain of steps run from the event loop, the same shape as ImageExporter:

- startNext asks pixelSource (MW::developPixelSource) for the develop render. Its GUI-thread steps (the recipe, the metadata, the mask prerequisites) run as ordinary events between the worker steps, as that function was written to. `done` is delivered through qApp and checked against a QPointer, so a render that lands after a quit is dropped.
- onPixels puts the render on the scene, or falls back to the image cache, else the file (loadImage).
- compose builds the embellishment and renders the scene to a QImage. This is the one step left on the GUI thread, because the scene is a QGraphicsScene of QPixmap items.
- EmbelWriter, on its own thread, encodes the file and the thumbnail and runs the ExifTool tag, ICC and thumbnail copies. ExifTool is a stay-open QProcess driven with blocking waits, so it is created on that thread and lives for the batch. The render runs ahead of the writer by at most two images, since each one queued is a full-size image held.

With the UI live, the export depends on nothing the user can change:

- The template: MW::beginEmbelExport greys the Embellish editor, its run button and the Embellish export menu (reason "an Embellish export is running"), and the editor's title reads "Embellish Editor (exporting...)". One export at a time; a winnet that arrives during one waits for it, then runs.
- The datamodel: MW::setEmbelPixelSource snapshots every image's metadata and orientation at the start, as the focus stacker does, so a folder change part way through does not leave the later images with nothing to render from. loadImage skips the datamodel for an image no longer in it.
- The view mode: Embel's gates on G::mode == "Loupe" (Embel::isActive) do not apply to the export's instance, which would otherwise have written every image after a switch to Grid without its embellishments.
- Destinations: names are decided before the writer has saved the earlier images, so the batch reserves its own names as well as checking the disk. Overwrite replaces an old file, never another image of the same batch.

G::isProcessingExportedImages, which makes ImageView::loadImage refuse to load, is now set only for a remote (winnet) export, which runs at startup before any folder is shown. A local export leaves the user free to browse. Esc aborts while MW::embelExporter is set. A quit deletes the export after the image being written, so no file is left half done.

Two bugs fixed on the way, both in what an export of several local images wrote:

- Text items with a metadata template read the LOUPE's current image (EmbelProperties::metaString), so every image in a multi-image export got the same title, date and exposure. The export's instance now uses EmbelProperties::metaStringOf, the exported image's row, and the file when the row has left the view.
- Embel::addImageToScene and updateImage replaced the image EmbelExport had put on the scene with the image cache's copy whenever there was one, which for a raw while browsing is the embedded preview. That undid the develop render of [14.2.3 Embellish Export](#1423-embellish-export) for every cached image. The export's instance now keeps the image it was given.

Still to do: a QImage-only render path so compose can leave the GUI thread too (notes/_ToDo.txt).

Also fixed: exportImages' three early returns (no images, "Do not Embellish", folder dialog cancelled) left G::isProcessingExportedImages set. ImageView::loadImage refuses to load while it is set and MW::exportEmbel never cleared it, so after one of those returns the loupe stopped loading images.

#### 6.4.2 A Window Resize Keeps the Grid on the Same Image (2026-10-01)

Maximising in Grid view showed an empty central area until a scroll, and restoring landed about 5,600 images away from where the user had been. A wrapping IconView's scroll position is a PIXEL offset, and a maximise animates through about ten widths; cells per row go from 6 to 13, so the same offset lands on a different image at every step. Measured with WFPROBE, the centre row drifted from 33,537 to 72,689, far outside the loaded icon chunk, so nothing was drawn. rejustify, which read its anchor off the viewport centre AFTER the drift, then locked the view there. Restoring drifted back to 27,945.

Fix:

- IconView::resizeEvent captures the anchor ONCE, at the first event of a burst, from the last settled layout (midVisibleCell; resizeAnchorRow / resizeAnchorAtTop).
- Every event of the burst re-centres on that row under a ScrollSignalGuard, which also keeps it inside the loaded chunk.
- rejustify takes the anchor before any early return, so a skipped rejustify cannot leave a stale one, then uses and clears it. A view at the top stays at the top.

Two defects in the same code were also fixed. Each resize event had queued its own singleShot rejustify (ten re-layouts per maximise); it is now one restartable rejustifyTimer per view. The previous width was a function static shared by thumbView and gridView; it is now per view (prevResizeWidth).

#### 6.4.3 Rejustify Obeys the Enlarge Ceiling (2026-10-16)

Switching Browse -> Develop/Keywords/Map -> Browse gave oversized grid thumbnails (3 per row, \~345 px, on a 1080 px grid), although [ ] stops at 5 per row. The workflow switch re-applies the Browse workspace, which sets iconWidth = assignedIconWidth = the stored thumbWidthGrid and calls rejustify.

- justify() (the [ ] path) caps the CELL at G::maxIconSize (wCell > max -> one more per row). rejustify had no cap, so justification widened a near-max cell by up to 2x.
- Its bounds check reset an out-of-range assignedIconWidth to iconWidth, which is the same stored value, so widths saved above the max (old settings hold 263 / 290) survived.

rejustify now clamps assignedIconWidth to [ICON_MIN, G::maxIconSize] and applies justify's cell ceiling after justifying. Still true: a workflow switch restores the workspace's stored grid size, not the size the user last set in Browse.

## 7 Actions and Shortcuts

Shortcut changes also update Help/shortcutsform.ui (Help > Shortcuts); the real bindings are in Main/menusandactions.cpp.

### 7.1 Enable/Disable Rules

Menu and toolbar actions that act on the loaded folder, the current selection or the picked images are enabled and disabled centrally in MW::enableSelectionDependentMenus() (`Main/menusandactions.cpp`). Pick-dependent actions are also kept in sync by MW::updatePickDependentActions() (`Main/mainwindow.cpp`), called from the pick-toggle paths.

Always valid, never gated here: app/window/help/about, dock-visibility toggles, workspaces (including the view keys E / G / T, see [7.5.7 The View Keys Are the Way Out of Develop Mode](#757-the-view-keys-are-the-way-out-of-develop-mode)), preferences, open folder, colour manage, combine raw+jpg, diagnostics, folder-tree/USB context actions handled by the rename\* slots, "Manage External Applications" and File > Manage Catalog.... File > Open Library is gated too, but from MW::updateLibraryTree, because it depends on whether the index will open, not on the selection; it writes the same "disabledReason" property.

#### 7.1.1 Conditions and Triggers

Four state conditions drive enabling. Each must have a trigger that re-runs the update when the condition can change, or actions get stuck disabled:

- dmHasRows (dm->rowCount() > 0, a folder is loaded). Triggers: fileSelectionChange (auto-select after load), selectionChanged (on clear), and view-mode switches, all of which call enableSelectionDependentMenus().
- hasSelection / selection count (sel->count()). Trigger: the selection model's selectionChanged signal, connected directly to enableSelectionDependentMenus() in MW::createSelection() (`Main/initialize.cpp`). Essential: extending or shrinking a selection with Shift/Ctrl does NOT change the current index, so fileSelectionChange alone would never re-evaluate count-dependent actions (focusStack stuck disabled after growing the selection to two).
- isAnyPick (dm->isAnyPick(), O(1)). Triggers: updatePickDependentActions(), called from every pick-toggle path in `Main/pick.cpp` (togglePick, togglePickUnlessRejected, togglePickMouseOverItem, toggleReject, updatePickFromHistory, recoverPickLog) and after ingest in MW::setIngested() (`Main/setandupdate.cpp`). enableSelectionDependentMenus() also calls it.
- isUpDown (gridView or tableView visible). Trigger: view-mode switches.

#### 7.1.2 Rules by Action

Requires dmHasRows (folder loaded):

- File: revealFile (+context), reportMetadata, copyFolderPathFromContext, copyImagePathFromContext, rename, saveAsFile, refreshCurrent (needed to pick up files added externally).
- Edit: selectAll, invertSelection, shareFiles, copyFiles, copyImage, deleteImages, pick, pickMouseOver, reject, pickUnlessRejected, popPickHistory, tokenTemplateEditor, rotateRight/Left, ratingsMenu + rate0..5, labelsMenu + label0..5, utilitiesMenu (mediaReadSpeed, visCmpImages).
- Go: jump, random, and all horizontal/home/end/page navigation (+AddToSelection), and the scroll family except up/down.
- Filter: filterMenu + all filter\* children.
- Sort: sortMenu + all sort\* children.
- Embellish: embelExportMenu + children, embelNew/Read/SaveTemplate.
- View: copyInfoTextToClipboard, slideShow, zoomTo/In/Out/Toggle, thumbsEnlarge/Shrink. (asLoupe, asGrid and asTable are NOT gated on a folder; see below.)

Requires Develop mode (syncDevelopMenuEnabled, not the gate() table): every action in the Develop-mode table below, plus the developExportPresetMenu submenu, which also requires at least one saved export preset.

Requires selection count >= 2: asCompare (compare view), meanStack, focusStack.

Requires isAnyPick: ingest, nextPick, prevPick.

Requires a view that scrolls vertically (isUpDown): keyUp/Down (+AddToSelection), keyScrollUp/Down.

Other:

- Open With per-app actions require a selection; manageAppAction is always enabled.
- pasteFiles is enabled when the clipboard holds file URLs (Utilities::clipboardHasUrls()).
- Go > Go to Folder... is never gated: it is how the user gets a folder in the first place.

#### 7.1.3 The Menu vs Shortcut Pitfall

Disabling a QMenu (menu->setEnabled(false)) only greys its entry in the menu bar. It does NOT disable the window-level shortcuts of its child actions, because each child is added to MW via addAction() with its own shortcut (rate "1", label "6", filter "Shift+6"), and those keep firing with no folder loaded.

- Menus whose children carry shortcuts are gated with the local setMenuEnabled() helper, which disables the menu AND every child action: ratingsMenu, labelsMenu, sortMenu, filterMenu, utilitiesMenu, embelExportMenu.
- developExportPresetMenu needs none of this: its items are built on aboutToShow and carry no shortcuts, so disabling the menu is enough.
- The Open With submenu is iterated the same way but stays enabled so manageAppAction remains reachable; only its per-app actions are gated.
- The Go menu itself is never disabled, because "Go to Folder..." must be reachable with nothing loaded. Every other Go item (jump, arrow/page/home/end navigation, the add-to-selection variants, the scroll keys, next/prev pick, random image) is gated individually, so with no folder loaded the menu opens with one live item and the rest greyed with their reason.

### 7.2 Disabled Shortcut Feedback

A disabled QAction does not fire and Qt does not consume its shortcut, so the key falls through as a normal KeyPress. To say why nothing happened, the qApp event filter (MW::eventFilter, `Main/mainwindow.cpp`) intercepts KeyPress events:

- MW::disabledActionForShortcut(seq) scans MW::actions() for an action whose shortcut matches the key sequence, and returns it only if it is disabled AND no enabled action owns the same shortcut (an enabled one would already have handled the key).
- MW::actionDisabledReason(a) reads the action's "disabledReason" dynamic property and formats it as "&lt;action name> — &lt;reason>." The reason is recorded where the action is gated: enableSelectionDependentMenus() uses a gate() helper (and setMenuEnabled() for menu children) that sets both the enabled state and the property, and updatePickDependentActions() does the same for ingest / nextPick / prevPick. Because the reason lives next to the gating, the two never drift. A disabled action with no property falls back to "not available right now".
- On a match the reason is shown via G::popup and the key is consumed.

Guards: skipped during initialisation, for auto-repeat, for modifier-only presses, when focus is in a text-entry widget (QLineEdit / QTextEdit / QPlainTextEdit), and when focus is in another top-level window (fw->window() != MW), so typing is never hijacked.

#### 7.2.1 Modeless Dialog Shortcut Guard

MW's single-key shortcuts use the default Qt::WindowShortcut context, which Qt activates whenever the action's window is anywhere in the parent chain of the active window. A modeless dialog parented to MW (e.g. Preferences) therefore does NOT shield them: a digit typed into a Preferences spin box would fire rate "1". The enabled-action case fires via Qt's shortcut map (QEvent::ShortcutOverride) before the KeyPress handler runs, so the eventFilter also intercepts ShortcutOverride: when focus is in another window and the key matches an MW-owned shortcut (MW::ownsShortcut(seq)), it accepts the override and consumes the event, delivering the key to the focused widget as normal input. This scopes suppression to MW's own shortcuts, leaving the dialog's own (typically Ctrl-modified) shortcuts free.

### 7.3 Return and Enter

Return and Enter are the SAME command key in Winnow: every operation bound to one must also fire on the other. Never test the key codes by hand; use the helpers in `Main/global.h`:

- G::isEnterKey(int) / G::isEnterKey(const QKeyEvent\*): true for Qt::Key_Return and Qt::Key_Enter.
- G::bareModifiers(const QKeyEvent\*): the event's modifiers with Qt::KeypadModifier removed. Use it for every "bare key" gate: write `if (G::bareModifiers(e) == Qt::NoModifier)`, NOT `e->modifiers() == Qt::NoModifier`.

Two traps:

1. The Enter key (numeric keypad Enter, or Fn+Return on a MacBook) reports Qt::Key_Enter, not Qt::Key_Return. A handler testing only Key_Return ignores it.
2. That same press ALSO sets Qt::KeypadModifier, so a gate written as `modifiers() == Qt::NoModifier` rejects keypad Enter even when the handler inside it tests Key_Enter. This silently broke the Develop Transform commit and the spot-tool fill commit.

QAction shortcuts cannot use the helpers, so bind all three sequences (QShortcutMap does not reliably strip KeypadModifier on macOS, hence the third):

```
act->setShortcuts({QKeySequence(Qt::Key_Return),
                   QKeySequence(Qt::Key_Enter),
                   QKeySequence(Qt::KeypadModifier | Qt::Key_Enter)});
```

ZoomDlg (`Dialogs/zoomdlg.cpp`) is the only Return/Enter QAction shortcut in the app. Qt already treats the two keys identically in QLineEdit (returnPressed), QDialog (default-button activation) and QAbstractItemView (activated), so connections to those signals need nothing; only hand-rolled keyPressEvent / eventFilter / event() handlers do.

Known gap, deliberately not fixed: Qt::KeypadModifier is handled nowhere else. MW::ownsShortcut and MW::disabledActionForShortcut build a QKeySequence from e->keyCombination(), which keeps the modifier, so no keypad key can match a stored sequence and the numeric keypad is inert for every other shortcut. Stripping the modifier there would newly make keypad 1-5 set ratings and keypad 6-0 set colour labels. Recorded so it stays a decision rather than a rediscovery.

### 7.4 Escape (the Cancel Chain, and the Way Back to the Grid)

Escape owns no QAction; it is handled in MW::keyReleaseEvent (`Main/mainwindow.cpp`) as ONE else-if chain, and the ORDER is the design: Esc cancels the most specific thing that is running, and only the LAST branch changes the view.

1. Reset the popup (always, before the chain).
2. End a stress test.
3. Stop a folder load.
4. Stop a file copy.
5. Cancel the slideshow.
6. Abort an Embellish export / colour analysis / focus stack.
7. Exit full screen.
8. Re-enable a disabled FSTree or Bookmarks.
9. With nothing left to cancel, fall back to the GRID from whichever other view is up: loupe, table or compare.

The grid branch has the same destination as G but calls MW::gridDisplay directly rather than triggering asGridAction. gridDisplay ticks asGridAction itself, so the exclusive view group stays in sync, and going through the action would also reassert the Browse layout; Esc is a way out of the image, not a request to rebuild the user's panels. It does not leave Keywords. Three guards:

- Preview mode only. In Develop, Esc belongs to the active tool (see [7.5 Develop Mode Local Shortcuts](#75-develop-mode-local-shortcuts)), and a bare Esc must not throw the user out of the image.
- G::mode is "Loupe", "Table" or "Compare" (in the grid there is nowhere to go).
- asGridAction->isEnabled().

A playing video is paused first: the video's own Esc handler sits AFTER the chain and is keyed off the central view being the video tab, so once gridDisplay has run it no longer fires, and the audio would keep playing over the grid. Full screen is tested BEFORE the grid branch, so in full screen the first Esc restores the window and a second goes to the grid.

### 7.5 Develop Mode Local Shortcuts

Ten keys mean something different in Develop mode than in Preview mode:

```
R   Crop / Transform panel      developTransformAction   (Preview: enters Develop + opens it)
N   New Mask                    developNewScopeAction    (Preview: unbound)
M   Tweak Mask                  developAddToMaskAction   (Preview: unbound)
O   Mask overlay tint on/off    toggleMaskOverlayAction  (Preview: Open folder)
S   Spot removal tool           developSpotAction        (Preview: Slideshow)
W   White balance sampler       developWbSamplerAction   (Preview: New workspace)
X   Export developed images     developExportAction      (Preview: Reject)
H   History panel               historyDockVisibleAction (Preview: unbound)
P   History panel, Presets open presetsDockVisibleAction (Preview: Pick)
\   Before / After              developBeforeAfterAction (Browse: compare the current image)
```

- H and P are not Develop-menu local: they are the View menu's "History Panel" / "Develop Presets" items, enabled in both modes, while the KEYS are Develop-only because the dock exists only alongside the Develop dock. Both address the SAME dock: H opens it with its History section expanded, P with its Presets section expanded.
- W is doubly contextual: an ACTIVE Transform session claims it for Warp (arbiter rule 1a, before this table), so W reaches the white balance dropper only when no Transform is up.
- "\\" is the only non-letter in the table, which is why the arbiter's value-editor guard tests MEMBERSHIP OF THE TABLE rather than the A-Z range (see Guards).

Three more keys apply only while a SUBMASK is being defined (still PENDING), handled in MW::eventFilter rather than by an action:

```
Return      Commit the submask into the mask (same as the panel's button)
Opt/Alt     (held) preview + commit that submask as a SUBTRACT
Shift+Opt   (held) preview + commit that submask as an INTERSECT
```

Return also closes a submask RE-OPENED from the Submasks list ("Done"); its edits are already part of the mask, so there is nothing to commit and the modifiers are inert there (its op is changed on its own row). The modifiers are MOMENTARY: read live (press AND release are tracked, so the veil follows the key with the mouse stationary) and never latched until commit. Opt is skipped while a Brush/Object stroke is in flight, where it means "erase from this stroke": Opt takes away from the STROKE while painting and from the MASK otherwise. See [11.15 Scope and Mask Model](#1115-scope-and-mask-model).

#### 7.5.1 Why Not Just Give These Actions a Shortcut

Qt allows exactly ONE QAction per key sequence. Bind "S" to both slideShowAction and developSpotAction and QShortcutMap reports an ambiguous overload and fires NEITHER, so a mode-local key cannot be a second QAction. Nor can the keys be swapped on and off the actions at mode change: that fights the user's customisations in the "Shortcuts" settings group, and any desync leaves keys bound to the wrong mode.

#### 7.5.2 Mechanism

The Develop actions are created with NO QKeySequence. MW::loadDevelopShortcuts, called at the end of MW::loadShortcuts, fills developShortcuts, a QHash&lt;int, QAction\*> of bare Qt::Key -> action. MW::eventFilter routes QEvent::ShortcutOverride and QEvent::KeyPress to MW::developShortcutIntercept while G::operationMode == Develop:

- ShortcutOverride is accepted, which cancels the global QAction (Qt sends the override to the focus widget before the shortcut system runs).
- The KeyPress that follows triggers the Develop action. The work is done here, not on the override, because the override is only sent for keys a global action owns (R/N/M/H own none), and because consuming the KeyPress is what makes the selection rule below a real "ignore".

In Preview mode the arbiter is never called. This is the same two-step pattern ReplacePanel::eventFilter uses.

Tool-local keys outrank mode-local ones: a key an armed tool owns ([ / ] brush size, A auto-mask, Cmd+Z undo stroke, Enter and Esc) is deliberately NOT in developShortcuts. ImageView::event claims those from their global actions while its tool is live, so the table need not know tools exist. Conversely the spot tool must NOT claim S, or S could arm the tool but never disarm it.

#### 7.5.3 Contextual Keys (Active Only While a Panel or Tool Is Up)

Some Develop keys are valid only while a specific tool is active, so they cannot live in the static table (that would steal them mode-wide). They are a guarded branch INSIDE developShortcutIntercept, ahead of rule 1, keyed off the tool's "active" flag. Today the only case is the Transform panel: while developCropEditing is true,

- C/L/W/A beat their window-level shortcuts (A Run Droplet, C Compare) and call TransformPanel::handleTransformShortcut(key);
- Esc calls MW::cancelDevelopTransform (discard the session and hide the panel);
- Enter/Return calls toggleDevelopTransform (commit and hide, i.e. R again), EXCEPT while a warp quad is traced (imageView->cropIsWarp()), where the branch falls through so ImageView commits the quad (rectify) via its own Enter path.

Doing it in the arbiter rather than in ImageView::event is deliberate: the crop overlay usually does NOT hold keyboard focus, so an ImageView ShortcutOverride claim never fires (the first, wrong, fix). The arbiter is a qApp filter, so it works regardless of focus. Add future panel/tool-scoped letter keys here the same way (guard on the tool's active flag), NOT to developShortcuts and NOT to ImageView::event.

#### 7.5.4 Space: Temporary Zoom and Pan Over a Develop Tool

A mask, spot or crop tool owns the mouse (brush, lasso, eyedropper, spot pins, crop handles), so the loupe's click-to-zoom and drag-to-pan are unavailable while editing. HOLDING Space borrows them back: the tool's mouse branches are skipped and the base loupe gesture runs (click toggles zoom, drag pans a zoomed image); releasing Space resumes the tool with no state lost. It applies to every tool, including Crop.

- The wheel zooms too: in Develop, ImageView::wheelEvent zooms the image under the cursor (ImageView::wheelZoom, cursor-anchored) instead of Preview's prev/next navigation. While a Spot or Brush/Object tool is armed the wheel resizes that tool; a plain wheel inside a Radial Gradient's core ellipse resizes it proportionally; Shift + wheel over a Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient or Brush submask changes its FEATHER. Hold Space (spacePanOverride) to zoom with the wheel there. macOS swaps the scroll axes while Shift is held, so the shared helper (wheelDelta) takes whichever axis reported.
- Space is bound to zoomToggleAction globally, and ImageView usually lacks keyboard focus in Develop, so this is driven from MW::eventFilter (which sees KeyPress AND KeyRelease), NOT developShortcutIntercept (which never sees KeyRelease). The ShortcutOverride pass is accepted to free the key from zoomToggleAction; KeyPress/KeyRelease call ImageView::setSpacePanOverride, which flips the flag every ImageView mouse handler is gated on.
- A value editor keeps Space as a literal character (same guard as the arbiter), auto-repeat is ignored, and ApplicationDeactivate clears the flag so a Space released in another app cannot leave it stuck. A change that arrives mid-stroke is deferred (ImageView::applyDeferredSpacePan) and applied on the next mouse release, so a partly painted stroke is not corrupted.

#### 7.5.5 Guards (MW::developShortcutIntercept, in Order)

1. Focus in a QDialog: bail. This mirrors the modeless dialog guard, which cannot cover these keys because it matches via MW::ownsShortcut() and a Develop action has no sequence. Without it a bare S typed into a Preferences field would arm the spot tool. Floating QDockWidgets are separate top-level windows too but belong to the MW workspace, hence the QDialog test.
2. Esc while a submask is open: discard it if still PENDING, else just close it (escapeMaskTool), and consume. Placed BEFORE the value-editor bail so it fires even when focus is on a mask slider (Hue/Sat) or the Color Range wheel; it falls through while the WB dropper or Transform is up, whose Esc handlers run later.
3. Focus in a value editor (QAbstractSlider / QAbstractSpinBox / QLineEdit / QComboBox): bail, so arrows still nudge a Develop slider and letters still type. EXCEPTION: a key that is in developShortcuts is still arbitrated over a slider or spin box (including a spin box's internal QLineEdit; see isTextEntryWidget()). Focus sits on a dock slider for most of a Develop session, and bailing there passed the key to its GLOBAL action: O opened the folder dialog instead of toggling the overlay (likewise S = Slideshow, X = Reject). Only real text entry (the search field, an EDITABLE QComboBox) keeps its letters. A read-only combo is not text entry: isTextEntryWidget() once treated every QComboBox as text entry, and since the Develop dock's rows are read-only combos (View transform, WB preset) that keep focus after a pick, R/S/O/N/M/W/X/H/P went dead after choosing a View (fixed 2026-08-29). A read-only combo now only loses its type-to-select search.
4. Auto-repeat: bail. Every Develop key is a toggle or pops a dialog.

#### 7.5.6 Selection Keys Are Ignored in Develop Mode

Arrows, PgUp/PgDn and Home/End (bare or Shift'd, plus the Ctrl+Shift+Alt pick-nav and Shift+Ctrl+Right random-image combos) are swallowed in Develop unless thumbView has the focus (MW::thumbViewHasFocus()), so the keyboard cannot navigate off the image being developed. Alt+key is EXCLUDED (Alt+arrow / Alt+Home scroll and pan within the image), but Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Left/Right IS pick navigation, hence the Ctrl test in isSelectionKey().

The bare Left/Right navigation intercept further down MW::eventFilter bypasses the shortcut system entirely (faster than a menu shortcut). It needs no mode guard of its own only because the arbiter runs first and consumes the arrow; keep that ordering.

#### 7.5.7 The View Keys Are the Way Out of Develop Mode

Develop edits a single image, so it always runs in Loupe: MW::setOperationMode forces Loupe on entry. Compare (C) is the one view unavailable in Develop: MW::enableSelectionDependentMenus disables asCompareAction there, which greys its menu item AND stops its C shortcut; the reason ("not available in Develop mode") surfaces via Disabled Shortcut Feedback.

Loupe (E), Grid (G) and Table (T) stay enabled in Develop, because they are the way OUT: D only enters Develop, and each view key leaves it (setOperationMode(Preview)), applies the Browse layout and shows that view. None of the three is arbitrated in developShortcutIntercept, so they mean the same thing in both modes.

They are not gated on a loaded folder either. D enters the Develop layout with no folder loaded (it is gated on the read-only cache folder, not on rows), so gating E / G / T on dmHasRows stranded the user in the Develop layout at startup with no way back. With nothing to show, each view function calls MW::showCentralMessageIfNoImages, which puts "Select from the Source or Bookmarks panels." (or the matching empty-folder / empty-filtration wording, as MW::nullFiltration uses) back over the empty view.

#### 7.5.8 Discoverability

A key-less QAction renders no shortcut column, so each Develop action embeds its hint in its text after a tab ("New Mask\\tN"), the idiom pickAction and jumpAction use for their multi-key hints. The keys appear in three places: the Utilities > Develop submenu (built in MW::createUtilMenu; MW::syncDevelopMenuEnabled greys the mode-local items outside Develop so they never advertise a key that does something else), the Develop action-row button tooltips, and Help > Shortcuts.

syncDevelopMenuEnabled must run on the MODE CHANGE, not only on the menu's aboutToShow. The arbiter dispatches the keys by calling QAction::trigger(), which is a no-op on a disabled action, so opening the Develop menu once in Preview (which greys those items) left R/S/O/N/M/W/X dead for the whole next Develop session. MW::setOperationMode calls it too.

Save Develop Preset (Cmd+Shift+N) is the exception: a modified combo owned by no other action, so it is a normal QAction with a real QKeySequence, kept Develop-only by its enabled state (setOperationMode enables it only in Develop; syncDevelopMenuEnabled greys it in Preview). See [11.33 Develop Presets](#1133-develop-presets).

Develop > Export with preset is a QMenu rebuilt on aboutToShow from the export preset store (MW::buildDevelopExportPresetMenu), as embelExportMenu is rebuilt from the embellish templates. It has no action and no shortcut; syncDevelopMenuEnabled disables the MENU outside Develop and when no export preset has been saved. See [14 Export](#14-export).

## 8 Map and Geotagging

### 8.1 The Map Module

The Map module (Module dock > Map, View > Map Mode, MW::invokeMapWorkflow) shows a world map with a pin for every image the filters show that carries a GPS location, as Lightroom Classic's Map module does. Version 1 is VIEW AND BROWSE: pins, clusters, a hover preview, click a pin to filter to its images, and the map following the selection. Lightroom's Saved Locations are here as Places, and thumbnails dragged onto the map are geotagged. GPX tracklogs and reverse geocoding are later phases. Built; largely untested in-app.

Files: `Views/Map/mapview.*` (the page), `Views/Map/maptilesource.*` (tiles), `Utilities/geo.*` (the pure maths, tested by `tests/unit/tst_geo.cpp`), `Selection::selectRows`, `MW::applyMapPinFilter` (Main/sortandfilter.cpp) and the Filters "Map pin" category.

#### 8.1.1 Why Not Google, Apple or Qt Location

- Google and Apple Maps: licensing and billing, not technology. Google's terms allow Google's map only through Google's own APIs (not as tiles in Winnow's own map), require an API key with billing attached (which a desktop app must ship where anyone can extract it), and restrict storing geocoding results, which rules out reverse geocoding writing City / Country into metadata. Lightroom does it under a commercial agreement. Apple's MapKit is free but native only on Apple platforms, which breaks the cross-platform rule; MapKit JS in a web view on Windows is a grey area in Apple's terms. OpenStreetMap data (ODbL) is free with attribution, and storing place names derived from it is allowed.
- Qt Location is QML-only in Qt 6: it would bring a QML runtime, a QQuickWidget and QML plugins into the bundle for one page, it is not in the installed Qt kit, and pins, clusters and the preview would be written in QML beside a widgets app. The map is a tile grid, a projection and a paintEvent, so MapView is a plain QWidget, with no new Qt module (Qt6::Network was already linked).

#### 8.1.2 Tile Providers

The default is OpenStreetMap's own tiles, with no key. With the Preferences > Map fields empty the map uses tile.openstreetmap.org (MapTileSource::Provider::openStreetMap, applied by MW::applyMapProvider). An earlier version shipped NO provider on the belief that OSM's tile policy forbids apps; that was wrong, and it left the map blank until the user signed up somewhere. The policy allows an application on conditions Winnow meets, and none may be relaxed, because OSM blocks an app that abuses the service:

- a User-Agent naming the app and a contact URL: "Winnow/&lt;version> (+https://winnow.ca)" (OSM blocks generic library defaults);
- the "© OpenStreetMap contributors" attribution drawn on the map;
- tiles cached locally (the 500 MB disk cache, PreferCache);
- AT MOST 2 CONNECTIONS (Provider::maxConnections; 6 for other providers);
- no bulk or ahead-of-view downloading (only tiles a paint asks for are fetched; nothing is prefetched).

The Style menu (the first of the map's corner controls; MW::mapStyle, QSettings "mapStyle") picks the tiles. Three built-ins, all keyless, all on volunteer-run servers, all held to 2 connections:

```
Style         Provider                                    Max zoom   Policy
Standard      openStreetMap   tile.openstreetmap.org         19      OSMF tile policy: apps allowed; UA with
                                                                     contact URL; attribution; cache; no
                                                                     bulk/prefetch/offline
Cycle         cyclOsm   {s}.tile-cyclosm.openstreetmap.fr    19      OSMF fair-use terms (cyclosm.org)
Topographic   openTopoMap   {s}.tile.opentopomap.org         17      opentopomap.org/about: third-party use
                                                                     welcome if it does not overload the
                                                                     server; no uptime guarantee
```

- The "Cycle Map" layer on openstreetmap.org is a DIFFERENT map (OpenCycleMap, served by Thunderforest) and needs a key; CyclOSM is the keyless cycling map.
- {s} in a template is an a/b/c subdomain chosen from the tile (not rotated per request), so a tile always has one URL and the disk cache finds it.
- The fourth item, Custom, is the URL template in Preferences > Map ({z} {x} {y}, {s}, and {key} for an API key), with the key, the attribution text and the provider's maximum zoom (MW::mapTileUrl / mapTileKey / mapAttribution / mapMaxZoom, QSettings keys of the same names). It is greyed, with the reason in its tooltip, until a URL is entered; entering one switches the map to Custom, and clearing it goes back to Standard. A custom URL that points at an OpenStreetMap server (it contains "openstreetmap.", so a local chapter's such as openstreetmap.fr counts) keeps the 2-connection limit and the attribution. The key sits unencrypted in the settings file, and the preference tooltip says so. Many commercial providers' free tiers are non-commercial only; that is the user's account and the user's terms. The menu's last item opens Preferences > Map.

When tiles fail, a banner at the top of the map says why, with a "Map Preferences ..." button: a provider that refuses requests (HTTP 401/403, a bad key), rate-limits (429), sends something that is not an image, or a custom URL that is not a valid template (MapTileSource::lastError). Pins, clusters and selection work without tiles, on a plain background.

#### 8.1.3 Tiles (MapTileSource)

- Two caches: a QNetworkDiskCache in QStandardPaths::CacheLocation/maptiles (500 MB, honouring the provider's cache headers, so a place seen before draws offline) and a QCache of decoded pixmaps (64 MB).
- MapView asks for every tile it needs each paint (beginFrame / tile / endFrame). A missing tile is queued, not fetched; endFrame orders the queue nearest the centre first, current zoom first, and drops any tile the frame no longer wants, so a fast zoom does not download every level it passed through.
- At most Provider::maxConnections requests are in flight. A failed tile is not retried for a minute.
- While a tile is missing, the nearest cached ancestor tile (up to 5 levels up) is drawn scaled up in its place.

Projection and zoom: Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), world pixels at a fractional zoom (Geo::lonLatToWorld / worldToLonLat). Tiles are drawn from the nearest integer zoom, scaled by the difference. The world wraps east-west (Geo::wrapTileX; pins are drawn at their three nearest world copies); latitudes beyond +-85.0511 are clamped.

#### 8.1.4 Points and Clusters

MapView::rebuildPoints walks the DATAMODEL's rows on the GUI thread, keeps those SortFilter::acceptsRowIgnoring(row, G::MapPinColumn) admits (every filter EXCEPT the Map pin, so the map shows what the filters show but a pin click does not empty the map), and parses G::GPSCoordColumn with Geo::parseCoord.

- Winnow holds a location as the DMS string GPS::decode builds (49°13'13.477" N 123°57'22.220" W), not as numbers. parseCoord also takes a decimal "lat,lon" pair, and rejects "Error", out-of-range values and exactly 0,0 (a camera without a fix writes zeros, and a pin in the Gulf of Guinea for each such image is noise).
- The count at the bottom left ("n of m images have a location") says why pins are missing.
- MapView's point ids are DATAMODEL rows; the proxy row is looked up (sfRowsOf) only to select, and the selection is mapped back to source rows to highlight.
- Clusters: pins within \~44 screen pixels are drawn as one pin with a count (Geo::cluster, a hash of cells in world pixels at the current zoom, so a cluster is the same size on screen at any zoom). Rebuilt only when the zoom or the points change, never on a pan. Selected images' pins are drawn in the Module dock's selected yellow, on top; the current image gets a white ring.

#### 8.1.5 Interaction

- Drag pans. A mouse wheel zooms half a level about the cursor; a trackpad scroll pans; a pinch zooms. Only QWheelEvent::phase() tells a wheel from a trackpad (see [6.2 Wheel and Trackpad Scrolling](#62-wheel-and-trackpad-scrolling)).
- Double-click zooms in, or on a pin filters to it and opens Browse Loupe.
- Hovering a pin opens a preview (the thumbnail from the DataModel icon, name, date, and "n of m" with arrows for a cluster) and a tooltip saying what a click does. Clicking the thumbnail selects that image through Selection::selectRows (Cmd/Ctrl-click adds it), first filtering to its pin if the Map pin filter is leaving it out.
- The corner controls are the Style menu, Fit All, Fit Selection, Follow (pan to the current image when it goes off screen; on by default), and zoom - / slider / +.

#### 8.1.6 Clicking a Pin Filters

A click on a pin (one image or a cluster) shows only its images: MapView emits filterToPin with the pin's DataModel rows, and MW::applyMapPinFilter REPLACES every filter (categories, search text, the pick / rating / colour actions) with the Filters panel's "Map pin" category (Metadata group, after GPS), in one filterChange, exactly as a Collection, Query, Bookmark or keyword click does. Those clicks, and Clear All, override it in turn, because they all start with MW::uncheckAllFilters.

- Cmd/Ctrl- or Shift-click toggles a pin IN an existing Map pin filter without touching the other filters: added if any of its images is out, taken out if all are in; taking out the last unchecks the category.
- Clicking the pin that is already the whole filter does nothing (it is also the second release of a double-click).
- Refused, with a popup, while a load is running, as MW::applySetFilter is.
- G::MapPinColumn is virtual, like G::CollectionsColumn: DataModel::data answers it as a bool from a side table of row KEYS (DataModel::setMapPinKeys; G::KeyRole, so a version is its own row), held under its own read/write lock. Keys rather than rows, so a sort or an insert cannot move the pin onto other images.
- The category has one item, "Images in the pin", whose value is true, made and counted by MW (Filters::setMapPinItem), not by BuildFilters. It is ALWAYS SHOWN, greyed and empty until a pin is clicked, with a tooltip saying where it comes from (a category that comes and goes is one nobody learns is there). Unchecking it shows everything again; the item stays so the pin can be re-checked; Opt+click excludes the pin's images instead. It is a session choice: Filters::persistableState never saves it, and Filters::reset (a new folder or Library load) removes the item.
- The map keeps every pin: points are the rows every OTHER filter admits (FilterPredicate::accepts takes an ignoreColumn, and SortFilter::acceptsRowIgnoring wraps filterAcceptsRow's decision, raw+jpg and collapsed versions included, without its side effects). Pins the Map pin filter leaves out are drawn at 45% opacity, and the count says "Showing the n images in the clicked pin".
- Tested: tst_filterpredicate::mapPinIsBoolAndCanBeIgnored.

#### 8.1.7 The View Is Persisted

MW::writeSettings saves the map's centre and zoom (QSettings mapLat, mapLon, mapZoom), only once the map has been shown that session, so a session that never opened Map leaves the last real view alone. MW::setupCentralWidget restores them with MapView::setView after applyMapProvider (so the zoom is clamped to the style's maximum). A restored view stands in for the first load's automatic fit (MapView::viewRestored), so the map reopens where it was left; every later new folder or Library load still fits once.

The automatic fit is keyed on the DATASET, the key of DataModel row 0 (MapView::fittedDataset), NOT on G::dmInstance. MW::filterChange bumps the instance, so keying on it re-fitted the map on every filter change, which threw the restored view away at startup (the saved filters are restored with a filterChange) and undid a Places click's fit to the place. A load replaces row 0; a filter, a sort or a progressive load's appended rows never do.

#### 8.1.8 Signals Only While Showing

MapView connects in showEvent, and disconnects in hideEvent, to the proxy and the DataModel (reset, layout, rows; the DataModel too, because its points are DataModel rows and a row the proxy hides still moves the rows after it), the DataModel's dataChanged on the GPS column, and the selection model, and rebuilds through a 150 ms debounce. The model's signals already fan out to three views, and a hidden map has no business adding to that.

#### 8.1.9 The Page, and Keeping It

The map is central page MapTab (8). MW::invokeWorkflowWorkspace puts it up after applying the Map layout (so Reset Layout and a resumed session get it too), because a workspace carries a Browse view and invokeWorkspace has just shown that.

G::mode is deliberately NOT given a "Map" value: it is compared in some fifty places as Loupe / Grid / Table / Compare. Instead MW::inMapModule() (currentWorkflow == WfMap; the WORKFLOW, not the page, because the page is the message page while a folder loads) guards the paths that would otherwise take the page back: MW::fileSelectionChange (which also puts the map back up after a folder load), MW::refreshViewsOnCacheChange, MW::sortChange, the Table re-assert on folder change and the video re-assert after a filter. The four display functions (loupeDisplay, gridDisplay, tableDisplay, compareDisplay) and IconView's double-click route through MW::requestView when called from Map, so Enter, Esc, a double-click or a view key leave for Browse with the workflow, the layout and the lit Module button all changing together. Without that, the loupe came up with the workflow still Map and the next selection change put the map back.

The Map workflow has no shipped default layout until one is captured into Workspaces/defaults.json (Window > Workspace > Default, developer only); until then MW::builtInDefaultWorkspace is used and the Default menu item is greyed with its reason.

### 8.2 Places (Saved Map Areas)

Places are areas the user draws on the map, an ELLIPSE or a POLYGON, each with a name, and filters to the images taken inside: Lightroom Classic's Saved Locations. The Places panel (Window > Places Panel; shown by the shipped Map layout) lists them, one row each with its name and the number of loaded images inside it. Places may overlap: an image is in every place its GPS location falls inside.

Files: `Main/mwplaces.cpp` (the dock, membership, the filter, the dialog flow), `Views/Map/placelist.*` (the list), `Dialogs/placedlg.*` (New / Edit), `Views/Map/mapview.*` (drawing and edit mode), `Utilities/geo.*` (Geo::Place, contains, toJson / fromJson; tests in `tests/unit/tst_geo.cpp`).

Why "Places", not "Locations": the keyword tree already has a Location branch (Location|Canada|BC|...), and Filters shows Keywords. A panel and a category also called Locations, with nothing to do with those keywords, would read as a view of them.

#### 8.2.1 Storage

userdata.db, as CollectionStore::Kind::Place (= 2; the enum is a published integer, appended, never renumbered). A place is a top-level node; its shape is the node's definition, Geo::toJson, A PUBLISHED FORMAT (keys may be added, never renamed or rescaled):

```
{"v":1,"shape":"ellipse","lat":49.28,"lon":-123.12,"rx":0.3,"ry":0.125,"angle":33}
{"v":1,"shape":"polygon","points":[[49,-123],[49,-122],[50,-122.5]]}     [lat, lon] pairs
```

No members are stored: an image is in a place because of where it was taken, worked out when the images load. Places are the user's own work, which is what userdata.db exists to keep (never index.db, which is rebuilt from the images). Unlike Collections and Queries, places are NOT the Library's: they are pure geometry over whatever is loaded, so the panel and the filter work in Folders too.

#### 8.2.2 What You See Is What Filters

The map draws in Web Mercator, so Geo::contains tests in Web Mercator too, in world pixels at zoom 0 (the world is 256 px square). An ellipse is a true ellipse ON THE MAP (semi-axes rx/ry in zoom-0 world pixels, not metres, plus an angle, clockwise on screen), and a polygon's edges are the straight lines drawn between its corners (even-odd ray casting on the projected corners). Geo::outlineWorld0 gives the same outline to MapView, so the drawn boundary is exactly the filter's.

The antimeridian: every longitude (corners and the point tested) is unwrapped to within 180 degrees of the place's anchor (its centre, or its first corner) before it is projected, so a place drawn across 180 degrees is one shape. A place may therefore span at most 180 degrees of longitude, which no real one does.

#### 8.2.3 The Column and the Category

The Filters "Places" category (Metadata group, beside GPS and Map pin) filters on G::PlacesColumn, the ids of the places a row was taken inside. Like G::CollectionsColumn it is virtual: DataModel::data answers it from a side table, source path -> ids (DataModel::setPlaceMembership, under a read-write lock), so a version is in its master's places.

- MW::refreshPlaceMembership builds the table in one pass over the loaded rows (Geo::parseCoord on G::GPSCoordColumn, then Geo::contains against every place) and sets the counts. It runs after every filter build (so after every load), when the places change (CollectionStore::nodesChanged for Kind::Place), and, debounced 400 ms, when rows are inserted or removed or a GPS coordinate changes.
- A refilter follows only when the membership CHANGED and a place is filtering, so the repeated runs cost the grid nothing. Its cost is logged under the perf probe ("[PERF] refreshPlaceMembership"); it is unmeasured at 43k rows.
- The category is filled, counted and checked through the same Filters calls as Collections and Queries (setSetNodes, setSetCounts, setSetFilter, setFilterState; Filters::isSetCategory), but is left alone by setLibrarySetsAvailable (Filters::isLibrarySetCategory is the Library's two only). Items are keyed by id (isNestedCategory), so a saved Library filter restores a renamed place.
- Tested: tst_filterpredicate::overlappingPlacesAreOrAndExcludable.

#### 8.2.4 The Panel Is a Second View of the Category

Its SELECTION is the filter (PlaceList, ExtendedSelection): a click shows only that place's images, Cmd+click adds or removes a place, Shift+click takes a range, a click on empty space stops filtering by place.

- Each change goes to MW::applyPlaceFilter, which, like a Collection or Bookmark click, clears EVERY filter and checks those places in one filterChange (refused while a load runs, with a popup; it first loads every row's metadata so membership is complete), then fits the map to them.
- MW::syncPlaceListFromFilters, called from syncLibTreeFromFilters after every filter change and build, pushes the category's checks back into the selection (signals blocked), enables Cancel, and has the map draw the checked places (MapView::setShownPlaces).
- The title bar has + (New Place), Cancel (stop filtering by place, keep the other filters), collapse and close. The context menu (contextMenuEvent; not Qt::ActionsContextMenu, which never delivers it) has New Place..., Zoom Map to, Rename..., Edit Shape... and Delete...; a double-click zooms the map to the place.
- If userdata.db cannot be used, the list and + are greyed with the store's reason above them.

#### 8.2.5 Drawing a Place

+ opens PlaceDlg, a NON-MODAL tool window (the map behind it must keep taking clicks), with the name, the type (Ellipse / Polygon), a directions caption for the chosen type, a line saying what is still missing, Remove Last Corner (polygons), Cancel and Done.

- Done is greyed until there is a name and a finished shape, and the status line and its tooltip say which is missing, never a popup after the click.
- + enters the Map module first if it is not up (and keeps the Places panel shown, since a Map layout saved before v11 does not list it).
- MapView::beginPlaceEdit puts the map into EDIT MODE; MW::finishPlaceDlg saves (CollectionStore::create, or rename + setDefinition for Edit Shape) and ends it. A NEW place is then applied as the filter, so it shows what it found.
- The type last used is remembered (QSettings "placeDlgShape").

Edit mode (MapView): clicks belong to the shape. Pins neither filter nor preview, and a double-click neither zooms nor opens the loupe; a drag on empty map still pans and the wheel still zooms. The map takes keyboard focus and claims Esc, Delete and Backspace through ShortcutOverride (Delete and Backspace are otherwise global delete-image actions).

- Ellipse: starts centred in the view at a quarter of its size. The handles are the Develop radial mask's (ImageView::maskRadialAxisHandles, maskRadialRotateHandleVp, maskHitTest): the centre (white) moves it; four axis ends (blue) set a semi-axis from the cursor's distance along that axis, Shift scales both to keep the shape; the knob (green) 24 px past +x turns it. 11 px pick radius, centre first. The maths is in screen pixels; sizes are stored in zoom-0 world pixels, so they hold at every zoom.
- Polygon: a click (press and release without a drag) adds a corner, with a dashed rubber band from the last corner to the cursor. The shape closes on a double-click, or on a click on the first corner (drawn larger and green once there are three). The double-click's first click has already added its corner, so its second release is ignored. Delete / Backspace (or Remove Last Corner) takes the last corner away and reopens the shape. Once closed, any corner can be dragged.
- Esc on the map cancels the dialog. Hiding the map page (another workflow, a load's message page, but not a minimised window) cancels too: a shape cannot be drawn on a page that has gone.

#### 8.2.6 Registered as a Dock

At every checklist site in [2.5.3 Every Tabbable Dock Needs a Glyph](#253-every-tabbable-dock-needs-a-glyph): places_white.png (a map marker), graphicFor / dockFor, dockForTabText, dockTextNames, dockTabToolTip (no F-key), dockVisibleAction, placeDocksAddedSince (v11, tabbed with queriesDock), winnowStateVersion 11, workspaces (isPlacesDockVisible; absent = off; the shipped Map layout has it on), full screen (Preferences "Show places"), collapse state ("PlacesDock"), diagnostics.

v1 gaps: no folders of places (the store supports nesting; the panel is flat), no "place:" field in the query grammar, no reverse geocoding to name a place, and the counts are of the loaded images only.

### 8.3 Drag to Geotag

Drag thumbnails from the grid or filmstrip onto the map and drop them where they were taken: each image gets that location. While the drag is over the map, a yellow pin marks the drop point with "Drop to set the location of N images".

Files: `Views/Map/mapview.*` (the drop target), `Main/mwgeotag.cpp` (MW::geotagRows), `Metadata/metadata.cpp` (Metadata::writeGpsToSidecar, and the read in parseSidecar), `Metadata/xmp.cpp` (the exif:GPS\* properties), `Utilities/geo.*` (formatCoord, toXmpCoord / fromXmpCoord; tests in tst_geo, and the sidecar round trip in tst_xmpkeywords).

The drop is a COPY. MapView sets Qt::CopyAction on dragEnter, dragMove AND drop, before doing anything: IconView::startDrag trashes the originals when a target takes the default Move. Only urls that name LOADED images count (DataModel::rowFromKey); companions (sidecars, with G::includeSidecars) and files from elsewhere are ignored, and a drag naming no loaded image is refused. The drop location is the map point under the cursor (MapView::screenToLonLat). The geotag runs QUEUED after the drop, because it may ask a question and a modal dialog must not run inside the drag's own event loop.

#### 8.3.1 Where the Location Goes

The library and the sidecar, NEVER the image file:

- The sidecar (Metadata::writeGpsToSidecar): exif:GPSLatitude, exif:GPSLongitude and exif:GPSVersionID ("2.2.0.0"), as Lightroom writes them, in the XMP GPSCoordinate form "DDD,MM.mmmmmmK" (49,13.224618N). A narrow in-place edit like writeKeywordsToSidecar: every other property is left as it was. Never embedded, whatever "Permit image file modification" says: the camera's own GPS block stays in the file, and deleting the two sidecar properties restores it. A sidecar flagged metadataembedded keeps the flag.
- The read back (Metadata::parseSidecar): the sidecar's GPS, when both axes parse and are not 0,0, WINS over the file's, and is read BEFORE the metadataembedded early return. It is turned into the string GPS::decode builds (Geo::formatCoord), so a location set in Winnow, or in Lightroom for a raw file, reads exactly like a camera's.
- The DataModel: G::GPSCoordColumn on every row of each file (a version is its file; with combineRawJpg the other half of a pair is included), in that same string. HasGPS follows (it is derived).
- The catalog: MW::updateCatalogForRow per row (the sidecar's new mtime moves the freshness stamp, so the commit is not skipped).

A file's rows change only when its sidecar write succeeded; failures are listed in a warning. A drop onto images that ALREADY HAVE A LOCATION asks first ("N of the M images already have a location. Replace it?"), so a drop a few pixels off never silently moves a camera's coordinates. Refused while a load runs.

Afterwards: BuildFilters::recount (the GPS category's counts); a filterChange if a filter or sort reads GPS (editNeedsRefilter); MW::refreshPlaceMembership (which refilters itself if a Places check is affected); MapView::activate, because setValDm notifies only the rows on screen; and InfoView::updateInfo for the current image, because the Metadata panel re-reads the model only on a selection change.

A geotagged image may leave the grid, by decision. With a filter that reads the location (GPS = False, a Place), the refilter takes the image out at once (the way to work through a "no location yet" list), and the current image moves to the next one, so the Metadata panel shows THAT image (with no location), not the one just tagged. The popup carries the coordinate set.

Not yet: undo, removing a location, geotagging images that are not loaded, and GPX tracklogs.

## 9 File Operations

### 9.1 The FileOps Choke Point (Images and Their Companions)

An image in Winnow is not one file. It is the image plus its companions: the XMP sidecar, holding ratings, labels, orientation and the ENTIRE develop recipe (and its versions), plus a .txt sidecar when present. The catalog index is derived and rebuildable; THE SIDECAR IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the image, so losing one loses every edit ever made to it.

Why this exists: companion handling used to be implemented four different ways (a .xmp+.txt helper used by four call sites, a .xmp-only helper used by one, a directory basename scan used by rename, and a hardcoded baseName + ".xmp" in ingest and the metadata writers). They disagreed about .txt files, about case, and about whether an externally dropped file had a sidecar at all. Adding devPreviews, a second piece of per-image state that has to track the first exactly, made one definition mandatory. Utilities/fileops.h is it.

What it provides:

- companions(): the one definition of "the sidecars belonging to this image".
- flushPendingEdits().
- copyFile / moveFile / trashFile(s), which do the whole job: image, companions, devPreview cache, catalog rows.
- onCopied / onMoved / onDeleted for callers that must move the bytes themselves: the rename dialog and ingest both rename companions to a NEW base name, which the generic helpers cannot express.

Routed operations: delete / trash (MW::deleteFiles), rename (all four paths in RenameFileDlg), both drop handlers (FSTree and BookMarks), the icon-view drag source, copy / paste, both ingest implementations, and Utilities::backup.

#### 9.1.1 The Flush Is Not Optional

Develop edits are written on a 2 s debounce. Before FileOps only copy and export flushed first, so deleting, renaming, moving or ingesting an image inside that window let the pending write land AFTERWARDS, recreating a sidecar at the old path after a rename, or resurrecting one that had just been deleted. Every entry point now flushes first. This was a live data-loss bug for the recipe, independent of previews.

#### 9.1.2 companions() Is Narrower Than the Rename Scan

It matches only sidecar suffixes (.xmp, .txt), case-insensitively, and only the sidecars that are THIS image's under the [9.2 Sidecar Naming](#92-sidecar-naming) rule. Every file sharing the base name would sweep in the paired JPG of a raw+jpg pair, and trashing a NEF must not trash its JPG, nor may trashing the JPG take the NEF's IMG_1.xmp (which it did until full-name sidecars). Rename is the one operation that genuinely wants the wider net and keeps its own scan; it notifies FileOps per file so the devPreview cache follows.

Copy does NOT duplicate the devPreview. A copied image carries its sidecar, so the 256 px thumbnail travels; the devPreview simply misses at the destination and is re-rendered on the next edit. Duplicating it would double the cache for every copy to buy back one decode.

#### 9.1.3 Bulk Trash Is Linear, With Progress and Cancel

Trashing 7,000 images once beachballed for minutes and was force-quit part way through, because every per-file step cost the size of the folder: companions() listed and statted the WHOLE folder for each image, the Develop flush and three cache-index transactions ran per file, and the model then rediscovered the deletions by re-listing every folder and removing rows one at a time, rebuilding the path hash and recounting the load flags after each (plus a spurious ROWLOSS warning per row).

- FileOps::trashFiles is the batch form: the Develop flush runs once, each folder's SIDECARS are listed once (name-filtered to \*.xmp / \*.txt, case-insensitive) and looked up by base name, and the DevPreviewCache / ThumbCache / Catalog rows go in one transaction per 100-file chunk. trashFile is a one-path trashFiles.
- MW::deleteFiles shows a window-modal progress dialog with Cancel for more than 20 files. It pumps once per chunk, and a cancel stops between chunks.
- The model drops exactly what left through DataModel::removeFiles: a few contiguous runs go out as removeRows, and a scattered selection is one reset over a single-pass compaction of the row stores. Nothing re-scans the disk (MW::refreshAfterRemoval, not MW::refresh).
- The result separates trashed, missing (already gone, e.g. after a drag-move out, and still removed from the model) and failed (locked or protected); one popup summarises a cancel or any failures.
- FileOps::setTrashHook lets tst_fileops run the batch against a temp folder instead of the real Trash.

#### 9.1.4 Defects Fixed While Routing

- External drops from Finder / Explorer now carry sidecars (the block used to be gated on isInternal, so a dropped raw arrived without its ratings or recipe).
- Folder counts refresh after ANY drop, not only a CopyAction.
- Ingest no longer reports a spurious integrity failure for every image that simply has no sidecar, no longer files a failed backup copy under "integrity failure" against the wrong pair of paths, and no longer runs a second uniquifying rename that could desynchronise an image from its sidecar.
- Utilities::backup carries the sidecars, so restoring a backup no longer loses the image's edits.

Move drops still delete from the DRAG SOURCE. Both drop handlers always copy; the source deletion comes from IconView::startDrag after drag->exec() reports a MoveAction. This looks split but is correct: it is also what makes dragging OUT of Winnow to Finder behave as a move. Do not "fix" it by deleting in the drop handler; an internal move would then delete twice. (The flip side: a no-modifier drag of thumbnails onto any target that accepts a MoveAction makes IconView trash the files.)

The preview cache folder refuses every write ([12.8 The Preview Cache Folder Is Read-Only](#128-the-preview-cache-folder-is-read-only)), and a version key is refused by every entry point ([13.1 The Row Key](#131-the-row-key)).

### 9.2 Sidecar Naming

Full-name sidecars for JPEG, TIFF, PNG and DNG. The rule is in Utilities/fileops.h (FileOps::sidecarPath and friends), and nowhere else:

```
Raw and HEIC              IMG_1.NEF  ->  IMG_1.xmp       Lightroom's name
JPEG, TIFF, PNG, DNG      IMG_1.JPG  ->  IMG_1.JPG.xmp   full-name sidecar
```

Why: Lightroom Classic writes XMP INTO JPEG, TIFF, PNG, PSD and DNG files and IGNORES any .xmp beside them; only proprietary raw (and HEIC) get a sidecar, named by replacing the extension. So in a raw+JPEG pair IMG_1.xmp is the RAW's, and Winnow, which used to write IMG_1.xmp for every format, was writing a JPEG's title, rating, keywords and Develop recipe into the raw's Lightroom sidecar; Lightroom then showed them on the raw and never on the JPEG. The full-name sidecar cannot collide. It is Winnow-private: the Develop recipe always lives there, and so do the standard fields while "Permit image file modification" (G::modifySourceFiles, default OFF) forbids writing into the image. When that preference is on, the standard fields go INTO the file instead ([9.4 Writing Metadata Into Image Files](#94-writing-metadata-into-image-files)).

Read priority is unchanged: the image's own embedded XMP first, then the sidecar by newer-wins on xmp:ModifyDate (Metadata::parseSidecar). That is correct for the full-name formats too: if Lightroom later rewrites the file's embedded XMP, its newer ModifyDate beats a stale Winnow sidecar.

#### 9.2.1 Legacy Sidecars

A full-name image with no IMG_1.JPG.xmp still READS an old IMG_1.xmp (FileOps::existingSidecar), unless a file of any other format shares the base name, in which case it is that file's (a raw's Lightroom sidecar) and is left alone. The first write adopts it (FileOps::prepareSidecarForWrite): MOVED to the new name when the image is the only file with that base name, COPIED when another full-name image may still read it (the DNG of a DNG+JPG pair). Every sidecar writer calls prepareSidecarForWrite; every reader calls existingSidecar. A JPEG in a raw+JPEG pair therefore loses sight of anything an older Winnow wrote to the shared IMG_1.xmp for it: that data could not be told apart from the raw's.

The ownership test needs the folder's file names. existingSidecar is on the folder-load path (DataModel's Sidecar column, parseSidecar on the MetaRead workers), and in a raw+JPEG folder every JPEG asks. So FileOps keeps one names-only listing per folder, keyed on the folder's mtime and guarded by a mutex; trashFiles builds its own once per folder, because every trash moves the mtime.

#### 9.2.2 Everything That Builds a Sidecar Name Goes Through It

The Metadata writers and readers (writeXMP, writeOrientation, writeDevelopSidecar, writeKeywordsToSidecar, readDevelopSidecar, readDevThumb, parseSidecar, the metadata report), the catalog freshness stamps (catalogscanner, catalogenumerate, IndexMetadata::candidate, catalogRowFor, the keyword write-backs), the focus-stack output label, and FileOps::companionDest for anything that renames a companion (move, copy, ingest, Utilities::backup): DSC_1.JPG.xmp becomes &lt;new>.JPG.xmp, never &lt;new>.xmp. The rename dialog keeps its own base-name scan but rebuilds names with completeSuffix, so it preserves everything after the base name. Metadata::sidecarPath is gone. Base names use the LAST dot, as Lightroom does: a.b.NEF -> a.b.xmp (older Winnow wrote a.xmp). Pinned by tst_fileops.

Sidecar writes are atomic (QSaveFile) and serialised per image (FileOps::sidecarLock); see [11.40.4 Winnow No Longer Creates One](#11404-winnow-no-longer-creates-one) and [13.2 Storage](#132-storage).

### 9.3 Renaming Images

File > Rename (MW::renameSelectedFiles, Main/fileoperations.cpp) renames the selected or picked images with a {TOKEN} filename template, or, for one image, a typed name. RenameFileDlg (Utilities/renamefile.cpp) carries every file sharing an image's base name along with it (sidecars, the other half of a raw+JPEG pair), and first moves aside any existing file whose base name the new name would take. The dialog's Help button opens Docs/renamehelp.html, which explains both rename modes and the sidecar ownership rules for users; keep it in step with this section.

#### 9.3.1 Across Folders

A selection may span folders: in Library and Catalog mode, and in a recursive folder load, the selection comes from many folders. The old gate compared every image with dm->folderList.at(0), the LOADED folder, so in Library mode every rename was refused with "You can only rename images from a single folder". The gate is gone.

- RenameFileDlg groups the selection by folder (in selection order) and runs renameInFolder once per folder, because the base-name, sidecar and conflict scans are all folder scans. The Finder-lock pre-check in MW::renameSelectedFiles is per folder too.
- One sequence across folders: with an {XX..} token the counter runs on from folder to folder rather than restarting, and its suggested start is one past the highest existing number in ANY selected folder, so two folders never get the same numbered name from one rename.
- Paths are resolved BEFORE anything is renamed: the selection list (source paths, from DataModel::getSelectionOrPicks) is grouped up front, and nothing reads paths back from proxy rows mid-rename, because a renamed row can re-sort in the proxy.

#### 9.3.2 Only the Selected File

By default simple rename takes the whole base-name group, so selecting x.tif renames x.jpg, x.arw and x.xmp too. The "Only rename the selected file" checkbox (off by default; RenameFileDlg::renameOnlySelected) renames the image plus FileOps::companions(image) instead, each to FileOps::companionDest: the ownership rule above, which move, copy, ingest and trash already use. So in x.arw / x.jpg / x.tif / x.xmp / x.tif.xmp, renaming x.tif takes only x.tif.xmp; x.xmp is the raw's.

- FileOps::prepareSidecarForWrite runs first, so a full-name image still reading a legacy x.xmp adopts it as x.tif.xmp (moved when alone, copied when shared) before the rename. Without it the rename would carry x.xmp to y.xmp, where a y.arw would claim it.
- The conflict test checks only the destinations actually written (the image and its companions), not every file with the new base name; a y.arw no longer blocks x.tif -> y.tif. A case-only change is not a conflict.
- It renames with std::rename, NOT FileOps::moveFile: moveFile removes an existing destination first, and in a case-only rename on a case-insensitive volume the destination is the source.
- The checkbox is disabled, with the reason in its text and tooltip, when Combine Raw+Jpg is on and the image is a combined pair (G::DupOtherIdxRole valid): renaming one half would orphan the hidden other half.

The base-name-group manual path (renameSingleManual) calls FileOps::onMoved per file; it was the one rename path that did not, so a manual rename left the devPreview behind. Versions follow their master ([13.8 File Operations With Versions](#138-file-operations-with-versions)).

### 9.4 Writing Metadata Into Image Files

"Permit image file modification" (G::modifySourceFiles; Preferences > General or the status-bar delta button; default OFF). With it on, Metadata::writeXMP and Metadata::writeKeywordsToSidecar write rating, label, title, creator, rights, email, url and keywords into the XMP packet INSIDE a JPEG, TIFF, PNG or DNG, where Lightroom Classic reads them, since it ignores sidecars for those formats.
