Raw and HEIC keep the .xmp sidecar in every case. Develop recipes and their previews are never embedded; they stay in the full-name sidecar. Orientation goes into the file too (below). Every write into an original gates on this one flag; anything else falls back to the sidecar.

#### 9.4.1 The Containers

Metadata/xmpembed.{h,cpp} (namespace XmpEmbed), pure Qt Core so tst_xmpembed drives it on real bytes:

- JPEG: the APP1 "http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/" segment is replaced, or inserted after the leading JFIF / Exif segments (Exif has to stay first). Extended XMP segments are left alone. Rebuilt in memory and replaced atomically with QSaveFile. A packet over 65,502 bytes is TooLarge (padding is dropped first).
- PNG: the iTXt "XML:com.adobe.xmp" chunk (uncompressed) is replaced, or inserted before the first IDAT, with a fresh CRC. Rebuilt and replaced atomically.
- TIFF (and DNG): IFD0 tag 700, and NOTHING EXISTING IS MOVED OR OVERWRITTEN. The packet is appended at the end of the file; then either the 700 entry is repointed (8 bytes) or, when IFD0 has none, a copy of IFD0 with the entry added in tag order is appended and the header's 4-byte IFD0 pointer is repointed. Each step is fsync'd before the pointer that makes it reachable is written, so a crash at any point leaves the old file plus unreferenced bytes at the end. Rewriting was ruled out because a TIFF can be hundreds of MB and writeXMP runs on the GUI thread per image; measured on a 209 MB TIFF, the whole read-modify-write took a quarter of a second. The price is that each edit leaves the previous packet behind (a few KB). BigTIFF is refused.

#### 9.4.2 A Packet Winnow Cannot Read Is Never Replaced

XmpEmbed::read reports Malformed for a packet it found but could not lift an &lt;x:xmpmeta> out of (a compressed PNG iTXt, an x:xapmeta packet), and Metadata::embedXmp refuses a packet rapidxml cannot parse, allowing only the repair that adds a missing rdf:about. Xmp::fix() would otherwise start from an empty skeleton and silently delete another application's data (Lightroom's develop settings, for one). Every refusal is reported with G::issue, and the edit is written to the sidecar instead, so nothing the user typed is lost, only not where they asked. The backup (G::backupBeforeModifying, Utilities::backup) is taken before any write.

The sidecar is stripped and MARKED after a successful embed (Metadata::markSidecarEmbedded): the standard fields come out and winnow:MetadataEmbedded="True" goes in. Without that the stale copy would win later: a Develop edit bumps the sidecar's xmp:ModifyDate, newer-wins then prefers the sidecar, and its dc:subject (read unguarded, so that a removal syncs) would clear every keyword. Metadata::parseSidecar reads only orientation from a marked sidecar. A later sidecar write (permission turned off again) removes the marker, and writeXMP then writes EVERY field so the sidecar can speak for the image again.

#### 9.4.3 XMP Shapes and Read Precedence

Fixed while here, because Lightroom reads the embedded packet with a real XMP toolkit:

- dc:title and dc:rights are written as a language alternative (rdf:Alt, xml:lang="x-default") and dc:creator as a sequence (rdf:Seq) (Xmp::ElementType LangAlt and Seq), where Winnow used to write plain attributes.
- Values are UTF-8; writeXMP used to pass them through toLatin1(), which turned anything outside Latin-1 into '?'.
- Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo (email, url) is created INSIDE rdf:Description when first needed (Xmp::ensureParent); the skeleton used to carry it as a sibling of rdf:Description, which is not valid RDF.
- The reader already handled all three shapes, so existing sidecars read as before.

A non-empty XMP creator now wins on read. Metadata/xmpapply.h took the XMP dc:creator only when the parser had found no EXIF Artist, and Png::parse did the same for title, creator and rights against its tEXt / eXIf values. Harmless while edits lived in a sidecar, but with the edit embedded that guard made a creator typed in Winnow read back as the camera's Artist. XMP is where Winnow and Lightroom write an edit, so a non-empty XMP value wins (the MWG rule), and an empty one still never clears the EXIF value.

#### 9.4.4 Orientation

The EXIF Orientation entry (tag 274) in IFD0 (in the Exif APP1 segment of a JPEG, or IFD0 of a TIFF / DNG), because that is what viewers read; tiff:Orientation in XMP is not. Its value lives inside the 12-byte IFD entry, so XmpEmbed::writeOrientation patches those 2 bytes in place: nothing moves and there is no half-written state (verified on real little- and big-endian files: one byte changes, exiftool -validate unchanged). Metadata::writeOrientation used to run ExifTool, and wrote into RAW files too; raw and HEIC now always use the sidecar, and so does any file with no Orientation entry to patch (every PNG, JPEGs without Exif), since adding an entry would mean rewriting the IFD. After a successful patch the sidecar's tiff:Orientation is removed, since parseSidecar would otherwise apply the stale value over the file's.

#### 9.4.5 Limits

- Extended XMP is not written. A JPEG's main packet is limited to one APP1 segment (65,502 bytes); a document that does not fit even without padding is TooLarge, and the edit goes to the sidecar with a warning. Extended XMP segments already in a file (Lightroom writes them for very large develop settings) are left untouched, and the main packet's xmpNote:HasExtendedXMP survives the round trip, so the two stay paired.
- IPTC-IIM is not updated. A JPEG or TIFF whose APP13 / IPTC block also carries a title or keywords keeps the old values there. Winnow's own readers apply XMP over IIM, and MWG-compliant readers (Lightroom included) prefer XMP while the IIM digest still matches, which it does since the IIM is untouched.
- Macintosh extended attributes (Finder tags) are lost when a JPEG or PNG is replaced, as with any write-and-rename.

#### 9.4.6 Every Caller Now Writes a File the User Can Lose

A caller that names the WRONG image is no longer a stray sidecar but a changed original. The first in-app test found one: InfoView::dataChanged built a list of datamodel rows and then indexed the model with selection.at(i).row(), a PROXY row, so in a multi-folder set a title typed for one JPEG was embedded into an unrelated image in another library (repaired by hand). It uses the datamodel rows now. MW::setRating, MW::setColorClass and the keyword paths were audited and map proxy to datamodel correctly. ANY NEW WRITER MUST DO THE SAME.

Where edits go is shown while editing: InfoView::updateSaveNote puts it on the Tags header ("saved in the image file", "saved to a Winnow sidecar" with a tooltip saying Lightroom will not see it and how to turn the permission on, or "saved to sidecar" for raw), refreshed on selection and when the permission is toggled (MW::toggleModifyImages).

Verified on real files (two Lightroom-edited JPEGs, a PNG, a DNG, a 209 MB TIFF): every existing XMP property survived as ExifTool reports it, the added one appeared, and exiftool -validate gave the same warnings before and after. Pinned by tst_xmpembed.

### 9.5 Folder Tree Auto-Refresh

The Folders tree (FSTree) updates itself when subfolders are added or removed on disk outside Winnow (in Finder or Explorer); no manual Refresh is needed.

- Mechanism: a cross-platform QFileSystemWatcher (FSTree::folderWatcher), wired in FSTree::setupFolderWatcher(). Qt maps it onto the native facility (FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows, inotify on Linux), so one code path serves both platforms.
- Scope: QFileSystemWatcher reports only paths explicitly registered, so Winnow watches only the folders currently visible in the viewport. updateWatchedFolders() diffs the visible set against the watched set and applies the delta; scheduleWatchResync() re-runs it (debounced 150 ms) on scroll, expand, collapse, selection, resize and refresh.
- On directoryChanged, onWatchedDirectoryChanged() debounces (300 ms), then calls FSFilter::refresh(), which uses invalidate() so the view re-queries the live FSModel::hasChildren() and the expand decoration appears or disappears, and re-syncs the watch set so a newly created subfolder is itself watched.
- Drive/volume mount and unmount is a separate path (Windows WM_DEVICECHANGE via WinNativeEventFilter); this covers folder content changes only.

Key files: File/fstree.cpp, File/fstree.h.

### 9.6 Creating a Folder (Folders Context Menu)

Right-clicking a folder in the Folders panel offers "Create folder in "&lt;folder>"", directly above "Reveal in Finder" / "Open in Explorer". The parent is the folder under the right-click (MW::mouseOverFolderPath, set in MW::eventFilter as the context menu opens), not the selected folder.

Flow: createFolderFromContextAction -> MW::createFolderFromContext (Main/fileoperations.cpp) -> FSTree::createFolder(parentFolder).

- createFolder asks for the name with a QInputDialog (default "untitled folder"). An empty name, "." / "..", a name containing any of / \\ : \* ? " &lt; > | (illegal on Windows, and / is illegal on macOS, so one rule serves both platforms), or a name that already exists re-opens the dialog with the problem stated above the prompt, keeping what was typed.
- The folder is made with QDir::mkdir, then refreshModel() runs, the parent is expanded and the new folder is scrolled into view.
- The new folder is deliberately NOT selected: selecting it would load an empty folder and throw away the current DataModel.

Disabled with a reason: as the menu is built, MW::eventFilter greys the item and appends the reason to its label when the create cannot succeed: "(read-only)" when the folder is not writable, "(preview cache folder)" for the Develop preview cache (DevPreviewCache::isCachePath). MW::createFolderFromContext also calls refuseCacheFolder, and FSTree::createFolder re-checks that the parent exists and is writable, so a caller that skips the menu gate is still refused. The item is not in the Bookmarks context menu.

Key files: File/fstree.cpp (FSTree::createFolder), Main/fileoperations.cpp (MW::createFolderFromContext), Main/menusandactions.cpp (createFolderFromContextAction, fsTreeActions order, MW::renameCreateFolderAction), Main/mainwindow.cpp (eventFilter enable/rename).

### 9.7 Memory Card Eject

Ejecting a removable card (USB drive / memory card) safely unmounts it. The platform-specific work is in UsbUtil (`Utilities/usbutil.cpp`):

- UsbUtil::eject(rootPath). Windows: DISMOUNT_VOLUME then STORAGE_EJECT_MEDIA via DeviceIoControl. macOS: "diskutil eject &lt;mount point>". Returns true only on a real success (the Windows path reports failure if either ioctl fails).
- UsbUtil::isEjectable(rootPath): true only when rootPath is a mounted volume that is valid (ready, writable) AND removable (DRIVE_REMOVABLE / DRIVE_CDROM on Windows; under /Volumes/ on macOS). Both functions require the volume's mount root, not a subfolder.

MW::ejectUsb(path) (`Main/mainwindow.cpp`) wraps them: if the drive is currently loaded in the DataModel, it first calls stop() and clears the FSTree selection (reading files from a drive after ejection would crash), then ejects and shows a confirmation or failure popup.

#### 9.7.1 Entry Points

Eject is reachable ONLY from the context menus of the Folders (FSTree) and Bookmarks panels; there is no main-menu eject action. The context action (ejectActionFromContextMenu -> MW::ejectUsbFromContextMenu) ejects the drive of the moused-over folder (mouseOverFolderPath). MW::renameEjectUsbMenu() sets the action's label ("Eject Memory Card &lt;drive>") and enabled state from that folder as the context menu is built.

The moused-over (or ingest source) path is usually a subfolder, such as a DCIM folder, so MW::ejectUsb() and MW::renameEjectUsbMenu() both normalise with QStorageInfo(path).rootPath() before calling UsbUtil. Eject works, and the menu item enables, for any folder on the card.

#### 9.7.2 Auto-Eject After Ingest

The ingest dialog's "eject" checkbox is bound to the persisted setting autoEjectUsb ("autoEjectUSB"). When set, MW::ingest() ejects the source card after a successful FOREGROUND ingest, on both the gotoIngestFolder early-return path and the normal path, after the copy has finished (IngestDlg runs the foreground copy synchronously during exec()). The eject targets dm->primaryFolderPath(), normalised to the drive root by ejectUsb().

Auto-eject is foreground-only by design. The ingest dialog disables AND clears the checkbox whenever background ingest is selected (IngestDlg::on_backgroundIngestChk_stateChanged, `Dialogs/ingestdlg.cpp`), and the checkbox is initialised after the background checkbox, so a persisted autoEjectUsb=true is reconciled to false at construction. MW::ingest() also guards the eject with !isBackgroundIngest: ejecting mid-copy would fail or corrupt the transfer.

### 9.8 Find Duplicates

FindDuplicatesDlg (`Dialogs/findduplicatesdlg.*`) finds duplicates of a set of candidate images among a set of target images. MW::findDuplicates launches it as a modeless window, and on accept it rebuilds the Compare filter so the flagged duplicates can be shown.

Two lists drive everything:

- The candidate "A" list: the images being checked. A snapshot (aItems) of the selected dm->sf rows, taken when the window opens.
- The target "B" list: bItems, built from the include/exclude folders dragged into the dialog. Each entry caches name, type, createdDate, aspect, duration and a thumbnail (im) for pixel comparison.

Layout: findduplicatesdlg.ui lays the upper area out as leftFrame then rightFrame inside horizontalLayout_13. leftFrame (left) holds the candidate table (tv); rightFrame (right) holds the target folder lists and the comparison controls.

#### 9.8.1 Modeless Window

The window is modeless (show(), not exec()) so folders can be dragged into the include/exclude lists from Winnow's own Folders panel as well as from Finder/Explorer. It is parented to MW with Qt::Window, so it is an independent, movable window that stays ABOVE MW (a parentless window drops behind MW the moment a drag starts in FSTree). WA_DeleteOnClose; MW holds it in a QPointer (MW::findDuplicatesDlg) so a second request raises the open window. MW connects QDialog::accepted to the Compare-filter rebuild.

Consequences of being modeless:

- Pressing a folder in FSTree to drag it LOADS that folder, so the DataModel can change under the window at any time. Hence the candidate snapshot and path-based output.
- The window owns its own Metadata instance (not MW's), because MW may be using its Metadata for a folder load while a search runs here.
- DragToList always takes a drop as a CopyAction. FSTree is InternalMove, so it proposes MoveAction, and a view whose drag is accepted as a Move removes what was dragged (compare the IconView drag that deleted files: a no-modifier drag is a MoveAction, and a target that accepts it makes the source remove what was dragged).
- The search loops pump the event loop, so closeEvent can arrive mid-run. It sets abort + closePending and ignores the close; on_compareBtn_clicked closes once the run unwinds.

#### 9.8.2 Candidates (the A List)

Candidates are the SELECTED images in dm->sf, not all filtered images; if nothing is selected it falls back to all filtered rows, so the dialog is never empty. setupModel() copies everything the comparison needs into aItems (struct A: path, name, created, aspect, video, duration, and the DecorationRole icon as a QImage). The candidate index a is the row in the dialog's QStandardItemModel and keys results[a] / matches[a] / aItems[a]. Nothing in the search reads dm->sf for a candidate, so a folder change in Winnow cannot shift or invalidate the candidates.

#### 9.8.3 Target Folder Lists (DragToList)

The include and exclude lists (ui->includeSubfolders / excludeSubfolders) are DragToList, a QListWidget in which every item is an editable folder path with a checkbox (Qt::ItemIsUserCheckable, default unchecked) meaning "and its subfolders"; a grey "\*checked includes subfolders" note (subfoldersNoteLbl) sits under the lists, beside Clear Folders. Every item is made by DragToList::newPathItem, so the flags cannot drift between routes. Toggling the checkbox fires itemChanged like an edit, so it also raises pathsChanged and clears stale results; the context menu has a matching Include subfolders toggle.

Paths get in by drop (FSTree, Finder, Explorer), the Add buttons (addFolders), editing an item (double-click; F2 on Windows, Return on macOS), or appending one (double-click empty space, or right-click > Add folder path). Right-click also has Edit path / Remove path; Delete or Backspace removes the selected paths. The list tooltip says all of this.

- Every entry route goes through DragToList::addPath or the edit commit (onItemChanged), which normalise: trim, expand a leading \~, fromNativeSeparators, cleanPath (drops a trailing slash). Normalising first is what makes the duplicate test reliable.
- The editor is the default line edit plus a QCompleter over a QFileSystemModel of folders (PathEditDelegate, local to the .cpp).
- A path that is not an existing folder is kept but drawn red with a "Folder not found" tooltip (a typo, or an unmounted drive); buildBList skips it.
- Empty and duplicate rows are removed in the closeEditor override, i.e. AFTER the editor is gone. Removing a row from inside itemChanged would delete the item the view is still committing to. This also cleans up an append abandoned with Escape.
- pathsChanged() fires on any drop or edit; the dialog connects it to clear() so stale results are dropped, but not while isRunning, because clear() empties bItems under the running search.

#### 9.8.4 Targets (the B List)

buildBList() expands the include folders, subtracts the exclude folders, then appends a bItem per supported file found. Recursion is PER ROW (DragToList::includesSubfolders(row), the item checkbox) on both sides: an include row checked adds its whole subfolder tree, an exclude row checked removes its whole tree, unchecked means that folder alone. It replaced a single global "Include subfolders" checkbox (the same move the Manage Catalog roots made).

If no candidate is a video (candidatesHaveVideo() is false, tested via G::VideoColumn), videos are excluded from the targets too. getMetadataBItems() then fills each bItem's metadata and thumbnail.

#### 9.8.5 Comparison

on_compareBtn_clicked() runs the search: clear -> buildBList -> getMetadataBItems -> pixelCompare() (when "same pixels" is checked) or findMatches() (criteria: name / type / date / aspect / duration). Matched candidates are checked in the dialog table.

- Both paths skip a target whose path IS the candidate (sameFilePath), so a candidate folder that is also a target does not report every image as its own duplicate. findMatches once had this test inverted (if (!sameFilePath) continue), which skipped every target EXCEPT the candidate itself, so criteria searches found nothing in other folders.
- File name matching compares the full lower-cased file name, extension included.
- Pixel comparison only makes sense if the two thumbnails share dimensions, so both the candidate (from the decoration-role icon) and target thumbnails go through normalizeBThumb(): scaled to 256 px on the long side (aspect preserved) and converted to QImage::Format_RGB32. For matching-aspect images that yields identical dimensions.
- compareRGB() sums the per-channel absolute differences over the overlapping rectangle, reading pixels directly from constScanLine() as QRgb (both inputs are RGB32). QImage::pixelColor() per pixel was \~50x slower and, over every A x B combination, was the original cause of the long main-thread stall.

Video target thumbnails come from FrameDecoder asynchronously: getMetadataBItems() queues each video (addToQueue) and increments pendingVideoFrames; the first frame arrives later at setImageFromVideoFrame(), which stores the normalised thumbnail and decrements the counter. getMetadataBItems() WAITS for pendingVideoFrames to reach 0 before returning (pumping the event loop, with a 30 s timeout and an abort check), so pixelCompare() never runs against null video thumbnails. pendingVideoFrames is reset in clear().

Responsiveness: the whole search runs synchronously on the GUI thread. Its progress/abort hooks were originally gated on G::useProcessEvents, which is globally false, so the GUI froze for the entire run. The compute loops (getMetadataBItems, pixelCompare, findMatches) now pump the event loop unconditionally; pixelCompare throttles to one update per percent. on_compareBtn_clicked guards re-entry (if (isRunning) return), disables compareBtn during the run, and resets isRunning / re-enables the button on every exit path.

#### 9.8.6 Output

on_updateDupsAndQuitBtn_clicked() writes the result back to the DataModel. It first clears G::CompareColumn on ALL dm->sf rows (candidates are only a subset, so a candidate-only pass would leave stale flags), then sets it for each checked candidate, found by PATH (dm->proxyRowFromPath), because Winnow may have changed folders since the snapshot; candidates no longer loaded are skipped. It then accepts the dialog and MW's accepted handler refreshes the Compare filter.

When NONE of the candidates are loaded any more, updateApplyState() greys the button and puts the reason ("Candidate folder is no longer open in Winnow...") in progressLbl and the tooltip. It is re-checked when the window is activated (changeEvent ActivationChange) and after each search.

## 10 Raw Decoding

Full-sensor raw decoding (demosaic), modelled on LibRaw and validated against it. It is separate from the embedded-JPG preview path: a raw file still shows its embedded JPG when no sensor decoder exists for its format (or the decode fails), and whenever G::useRaw is off. Which engine renders a raw (Winnow or Apple Core Image) is in [10.9 Raw Renderers (Winnow and Apple)](#109-raw-renderers-winnow-and-apple).

### 10.1 Pipeline

ImageFormats/Raw/:

```
ImageDecoder::load()
  -> RawFormat::Create(ext)          factory (rawFactories(): one ext -> decoder table);
                                     nullptr = no sensor decoder (embedded JPG)
  -> RawFormat::Decode()             shared, camera-agnostic pipeline:
```

1. UnpackCfa(): PER-FORMAT virtual, THE override point. Vendor packed/compressed bitstream -> normalised CFA mosaic (RawImage). Lives in the vendor .cpp (canon.cpp, nikon.cpp, ...) as a class SEPARATE from that file's metadata parser.
2. SubtractBlack(): shared per-2x2-position black subtraction + clip.
3. Demosaic::Run(): shared, camera-agnostic. Bilinear3x3 for Bayer, XTransWindow (5x5) for Fuji X-Trans; AHD/DCB later. It operates only on the CFA mosaic + pattern (Bayer) or raw.xtrans (the 6x6 map), so it is unit-testable.
4. RawColor::ToCameraNative(): shared. CHARACTERISES the image (builds the camera -> working matrix and the as-shot multipliers into WorkingImage::cam) but does NOT apply them. Pixels stay in the sensor's own primaries, tagged ColorSpace::CameraNative, unclamped.
5. Develop::Apply(): stage 0 is the INPUT PROFILE (camera-native -> working space), then the parametric edits in linear space.
6. OutputTransform::ToImage(): baseline tone curve (raw only) + primaries + gamma -> QImage.

Demosaic is deliberately NOT the override point: the algorithm is shared across cameras, and only the unpack/decompress step is vendor-specific (LibRaw's real structure). An earlier (2025) unused scaffold (ImageFormats/Base/rawbase.\* + ImageFormats/Tiff/tiffdecoder.\*) used the rejected demosaic()-as-override axis and has been removed.

Threading: one RawFormat instance is constructed per decode (per decoder thread). Unlike the Metadata-owned parser singletons, RawFormat instances are never shared, so per-decode scratch carries no cross-thread races.

#### 10.1.1 Why the Decode Stops at Camera-Native

The buffer RawColor produces is what WorkingImageCache stores, so anything baked in there can only be undone by decoding the raw again. Applying the white balance and the colour matrix downstream of the cache, in Develop, makes a white-balance or camera-profile change a RE-RENDER rather than a re-decode. The old code also clamped negatives to zero here, destroying every out-of-gamut sensor colour before the user had touched the image; that clamp is gone, and out-of-gamut values survive to the output stage, the only stage that knows what gamut it renders into.

It costs nothing per pixel: Develop::buildPointCoeffs folds the input profile, the white balance, exposure, the Colour RGB sliders and the Calibrate matrix into a SINGLE 3x3 (PointCoeffs::preMat). Develop::ToWorkingSpace is the standalone version, used only when the point pass cannot carry it: an identity edit (no point pass at all) and an active Denoise (op #1, which runs BEFORE the point pass and must see working-space pixels).

### 10.2 Metadata Plumbing (RawSensorInfo)

The per-file facts UnpackCfa needs (CFA strip offset/length, geometry, bitsPerSample, compression, CFA pattern, levels, sample byte order, and the colour: xyzToCam, camMul, hasColorMatrix) live in struct RawSensorInfo (Metadata/rawsensorinfo.h, dependency-free), carried on ImageMetadata::rawInfo.

- Sony::parse fills it once during the normal metadata read (from the SubIFD0 it already parses; no second walk). Other formats self-walk at decode time.
- DataModel keeps a lock-guarded QHash&lt;fPath, RawSensorInfo> (fPathRawInfo\*), written in addMetadataForItem and cleared on folder reload. ImageDecoder fetches it via dm->fPathRawInfoGet() in cache mode (indMeta carries it directly in independent mode) and hands it to RawFormat::Decode.
- Gated on G::useRaw: when raw decoding is OFF, both the parse-time fill and the store are skipped, so the MetaRead path pays nothing. If useRaw is toggled on after a folder is read, rawInfo is absent and UnpackCfa falls back to its self-walk; the store repopulates on the next folder read.
- The self-walk fills the SAME fields as the parse path, geometry AND colour (model -> matrix via tag 272, the DNG-tag black/WB fallbacks). If it filled only geometry, a toggle-on after a useRaw-off load would render with an identity matrix and no WB (a green tint). The CFAPattern -> enum mapping is shared via cfaPatternFromPlaneColor() in rawimage.h.

### 10.3 Colour: the Camera Matrix

RawColor::ToCameraNative follows dcraw/libraw cam_xyz_coeff. The input is the model's XYZ(D65) -> camera matrix (DNG ColorMatrix / adobe_coeff convention), looked up in ImageFormats/Raw/cameramatrix.cpp, a FULL port of libraw's adobe_coeff for the mainstream still-camera makers (776 models; phone/action/cinema/bare-sensor and 4-colour CMYG/RGBE entries omitted).

- Each row also carries adobe_coeff t_black / t_maximum, read via cameraLevelsForModel() as a fallback black/white where a decoder would otherwise guess (e.g. Canon, whose saturation is below the bit-depth max: a 7D Mark II clips at 13584, not 16383).
- Lookup is a case-insensitive LONGEST-PREFIX match, so one "Nikon D800" row covers D800/D800E and "Sony ILCE-9" covers ILCE-9/9M2, while the most specific key wins (a short "Nikon D3" never shadows "D300").
- Regenerate from a newer libraw colordata.cpp with tools/gen_cameramatrix.py when bodies are added. A wrong matrix is a hue shift, not a crash, so verify visually.
- From it RawColor builds camRgb = xyzToCam . rgbToXyz, row-normalises so neutral maps to neutral, derives the neutral white balance preMul = 1/rowSum, and inverts to camera -> linear RGB (rgbCam). It STORES the white balance (as-shot raw.camMul when the parser filled it, else preMul; normalised to green) and the matrix in WorkingImage::cam.
- An unknown model gives an identity xyzToCam: an sRGB-assumed pass-through that renders approximately, with a colour cast.

#### 10.3.1 Canonical Camera Model

ImageFormats/Raw/cameramodel.h, canonicalCameraModel: the ONE string a body is identified by, and the key to TWO independent tables: the matrix table above and a DCP's UniqueCameraModel (CameraProfileStore). Both want the same shape, MAKER-PREFIXED and spaced: "Olympus E-M1 Mark III", "Fujifilm GFX 100", "Panasonic DC-GX9".

EXIF does not supply it. Nikon and Canon put the maker in tag 272 themselves ("NIKON D850", "Canon EOS R5"); Olympus, Fujifilm and Panasonic do NOT ("E-M1", "X-T2", "DC-GX9"), and also glue words the tables space out ("OM-1MarkII" vs "OM-1 Mark II", "GFX50S II" vs "GFX 50S II"). Every parser runs make/model through canonicalCameraModel before storing ImageMetadata::model, and that string reaches the model column, the matrix table and the profile store alike. (Until 2026-09-14 those three parsers stored tag 272 unchanged, so ORF, RAF and RW2 missed BOTH lookups: an empty Profile dropdown and an identity matrix, a plausible-looking cast rather than a visible failure. Sony's parser had always compensated with a hard-coded "Sony " prefix, which this helper generalises.)

Three spacing rules, all deliberately narrow and idempotent:

- "Mark" is spaced out only when a roman numeral or digit follows it.
- The "GFX" split is anchored at the start AND Fujifilm-only. The obvious general form ("letters then digits get a space") destroys the X100 family.
- Canon's "mN" suffix becomes " Mark N" (Canon-only, anchored at the END, N in 2..4). Canon writes "Canon EOS R6m2" and the table carries "Canon EOS R6 Mark II"; without the rule (added 2026-09-16) the longest-prefix match fell through to "Canon EOS R6", a DIFFERENT sensor, so the image rendered through the wrong matrix, silently and plausibly.

Not bugs: "Sony ILCE-9M2" -> "Sony ILCE-9" and "Fujifilm X-T50" -> "Fujifilm X-T5" are what libraw master does (neither body has its own adobe_coeff row), and "Nikon D800E" -> "Nikon D800" is the same matrix by design.

One maker disagrees: libraw files the OM bodies under "Olympus OM-1", while Adobe ships their profiles as "OM Digital Solutions OM-1". The canonical form follows libraw (cameramatrix.cpp is generated from it and is the render-critical lookup); CameraProfileStore::lookupLocked retries over cameraModelAliases(), trying every candidate for an EXACT match before any for a prefix match, so an alias's exact hit beats the canonical spelling's partial one.

Pinned by tests/unit/tst_cameramodel.cpp, which resolves each sample body end to end against the compiled-in matrix table and the installed profiles, and asserts the BARE EXIF model still finds nothing (otherwise the case has quietly stopped guarding anything). The catalog stores the model per image, so ORF/RAF/RW2 rows indexed before the change carry the bare model until the folder is browsed again. Measured 2026-09-14 with the app's own store (profiles per body): E-M1 6, OM-1 Mark II 11, DC-GX9 12, D7200 13, X-T2 / X-T50 / GFX 50S II 1 each; the Fuji count is low for a different reason (see [10.8 Adobe Look Profiles (.xmp): Declined](#108-adobe-look-profiles-xmp-declined)).

### 10.4 As-Shot White Balance

RawFormat::ReadAsShotColor(file, m, RawSensorInfo&) is the colour half of a decode on its own: the model matrix and the as-shot multipliers, no sensor unpack and no pixels. Each vendor's UnpackCfa calls the SAME function for its own camMul, so there is ONE definition per format of "where this format keeps its white balance". Overridden by all seven:

```
Nikon      MakerNote 0x0C, else the older 0x97 ColorBalance block
Canon      CR2 and CR3: ColorData 0x4001, the record LENGTH selecting the layout
Olympus    MakerNote -> ImageProcessing 0x2040 -> WB_RBLevels 0x0100
Panasonic  IFD0 tags 0x24 / 0x25 / 0x26
Fuji       the CFA directory's 0x2FF0, else the repeated-triple scan of the 0xC000 blob
DNG        ColorMatrix + AsShotNeutral
Sony       the ENCRYPTED SR2Private block (readSr2Levels); the plaintext SubIFD copy
           Sony::parse picks up is only a seed
```

Each override re-walks the file HEADER only, nothing beside a Core Image decode; the CR3 and RAF ones read a bounded prefix rather than the whole file.

#### 10.4.1 Under the Apple Engine

Fixed 2026-09-16. AppleRawDecode::Decode returns pixels with Core Image's own profile and white balance applied, and deliberately leaves WorkingImage::cam INVALID, and an invalid cam made WhiteBalance::resolve return its literal 6500 K / 0 default. So the Develop Temp/Tint row showed 6500 / 0 on EVERY raw file under the Apple engine; the makernote WB lived inside UnpackCfa, which that engine never calls. Decode() now calls ReadAsShotColor after a successful Core Image decode and hands the result to RawColor::Characterise.

Safe for the render: the Apple engine's pixels stay tagged kWorking, and Develop's stage-0 preMat fold is gated on CameraNative, so the input matrix is not applied twice. cam is used for the WB READOUT and for relativeGains, which is exactly right, because Core Image's output already carries the as-shot balance cam describes. For the same reason attachProfile (workingimagecache.cpp) ALSO requires CameraNative: cam.valid alone no longer distinguishes the two engines, and attaching a DCP to a Core Image result would layer a second input profile on an image that already has one (reachable via a pasted preset or a sidecar written under the Winnow engine).

#### 10.4.2 Re-read When the Decode Lands

The second cause of the same 6500 / 0 symptom. MW::fileSelectionChange points the dock at the new image AT SELECTION, a second or so before the raw decode finishes, and DevelopProperties::currentCam() is a cache PEEK (WorkingImageCache::get, no build), so refreshWbRow resolved against an invalid cam and nothing re-read it when the WorkingImage arrived. MW::renderDevelopPreview now calls DevelopProperties::onWorkingImageReady once the WorkingImage is in hand. It is EDGE-TRIGGERED on the resolved as-shot Kelvin CHANGING, so calling it on every render costs nothing and cannot overwrite a slider being dragged. It is keyed on the value rather than a seen flag deliberately: switching the renderer re-decodes, and the two engines need not agree to the kelvin. The Profile combo has the same dependency and is refreshed alongside; a future dock row keyed on cam must join them, because buildTree alone is too early.

#### 10.4.3 As Shot Is Profile-Dependent

asShotK / asShotTint are solved at decode against the BUILT-IN per-model matrix, because a profile is an edit attached only at render time. A DCP REPLACES that matrix, so the same file is balanced for a measurably different temperature under it. attachProfile therefore re-solves (CameraProfile::resolveAsShot) via the DNG specification's NeutralToXY, a fixed-point iteration because the matrix to invert depends on the temperature being solved for: start at D50, invert the ColorMatrix resolved there onto the camera neutral (1/asShotMul), read the temperature off the chromaticity with WhiteBalance::tempTintFromXY, resolve again, repeat. Without it, picking a profile moved the rendering without moving the Temp number, and since relativeGains anchors on asShotK/asShotTint, "as shot" would stop being an exact no-op. See [11.27 White Balance (Absolute, Kelvin)](#1127-white-balance-absolute-kelvin).

### 10.5 Format Decoders

Every decoder below was validated against the libraw/rawpy oracle (a throwaway Python reference in scratch, since the bit-level schemes are too subtle to guess). A format with no decoder, or a variant a decoder does not handle, returns false from Decode() and ImageDecoder falls back to the embedded JPG.

#### 10.5.1 Sony ARW

SonyRaw::UnpackCfa (ImageFormats/Sony/sony.cpp) handles:

- UNCOMPRESSED ARW (Compression 1, e.g. A9 II: 14-bit LE uint16, Bayer RGGB). Reads StripOffsets/Counts, ImageWidth/Length, BitsPerSample, CFAPattern (33422), WhiteLevel (50717) via the plumbed RawSensorInfo or a self-walk (readSonyTiffSensorInfo).
- ARW2 "Compressed" (Compression 32767; decodeSonyArw2, tried first). Each 16-byte group encodes 16 photosites of one Bayer colour across 32 columns: an 11-bit max and min, the indices holding them, then 7-bit deltas shifted to fit (max - min). The 11-bit values expand through a Sony tone curve from tag 0x7010 (4 control points; breakpoints at point>>2, slope starts at 4 and doubles each segment; sample = curve[pix&lt;&lt;1]>>2). Columns are de-interleaved even-then-odd within each 32-column group. Ported from dcraw's sony_arw2_load_raw; byte-identical to libraw on an A9 ARW.
- Not handled: the NEWER "Lossless Compressed RAW" (Compression JPEG, e.g. A1/A7R5), which is lossless JPEG and could reuse LosslessJpeg.

Levels and white balance come from the ENCRYPTED SR2Private block on both paths. An ARW does NOT carry BlackLevel or the as-shot WB in any plaintext IFD: WB_RGGBLevels (0x7313, R G1 G2 B), BlackLevel (0x7310) and WhiteLevel (0x787f) live in an SR2SubIFD obfuscated with Sony's LFSR stream cipher, reached from IFD0's DNGPrivateData (0xC634) -> a small plaintext IFD carrying 0x7200 (SR2SubIFD offset), 0x7201 (length) and 0x7221 (key).

- readSr2Levels decrypts that block (sonyDecrypt, dcraw's pad generator; the generator index starts at 127, where dcraw's init loop leaves it, not 0) and walks the plaintext IFD, rebasing value offsets by -0x7200offset because they are still absolute file offsets.
- applySr2Levels then overwrites raw.black / raw.camMul on the freshly unpacked mosaic; both unpack paths call it, so it is the single source of Sony levels.
- Winnow used to look these tags up in the plaintext raw SubIFD, silently find nothing, and fall back to a hard-coded black of 512 with camMul 1,1,1,1. Bodies whose real pedestal IS 512 (most E-mount) rendered correctly by luck; a DSC-RX100 (pedestal 800) came out washed out, its blacks lifted \~1.8% of full scale. Validated tag-for-tag against ExifTool on nine bodies (RX100, A7R2/4/5, A9/A9II/A9III, A1II).
- raw.white is deliberately NOT taken from 0x787f: Sony declares 15360, but the ARW tone curve expands sensor values past it and libraw saturates at 16383; adopting 15360 would brighten every Sony render \~7% away from the reference.
- Limitation: clipped highlights can show a slight tint until highlight recovery lands.

#### 10.5.2 Adobe DNG

DngRaw (ImageFormats/Dng/dng.cpp) is self-contained: UnpackCfa walks the TIFF/EP IFDs (via TiffWalk), finds the CFA image (Photometric == CFA 32803, full-res, most pixels), and decodes UNCOMPRESSED (Compression 1) and LOSSLESS-JPEG (Compression 7), in STRIP or TILE layout (tiles placed left-to-right, top-to-bottom, edge-cropped).

- DNG carries its OWN colour: xyzToCam = ColorMatrix2 (D65; else ColorMatrix1), camMul = 1 / AsShotNeutral, plus BlackLevel (50714), WhiteLevel (50717) and CFAPattern (33422). No per-model table and nothing plumbed at parse time; it always self-walks.
- Verified byte-identical to the reference on a single-strip lossless DNG (Leica M10) and a 726-tile lossless DNG (Nikon D850 / Lightroom).
- Limitations: assumes ColorMatrix2's illuminant is D65 (no chromatic adaptation yet); packed sub-16-bit uncompressed storage is not handled.

#### 10.5.3 Fujifilm RAF

FujiRaw (ImageFormats/Fuji/fuji.cpp). RAF is a Fuji container ("FUJIFILMCCD-RAW "): a big-endian header with offsets (92 = CFA metadata dir, 100/104 = CFA data offset/length) to an embedded JPEG; a CFA directory (tag 0x100 = raw H/W; 0x131 = the X-Trans 6x6 colour map, 36 bytes REVERSED -> [yy][xx], 0=R 1=G 2=B; 0xC000 = the RAFData block with the WB); and the CFA data. The FujiIFD that prefixes the CFA block (cfaOff -> little-endian TIFF -> 0xf000 -> FujiIFD) carries BitsPerSample (0xf003 -> white), per-CFA BlackLevel (0xf00a) and the compressed-strip offset (0xf007).

Two CFA encodings, routed on the 16-byte header at cfaOff + 0xf007 (signature 0x4953 = compressed):

- Uncompressed: rawW\*rawH\*2 bytes plus a small leading header (size = cfaLen - rawW\*rawH\*2, e.g. 2048), little-endian 16-bit samples.
- Compressed (lossless/lossy, most current bodies): FujiCompressed::decode (ImageFormats/Fuji/fujicompressed.cpp), a faithful port of libraw's fuji_compressed.cpp with all decoder state in a per-call Ctx struct (no globals, so concurrent cache-thread decodes are safe). The 16-byte BE header gives the lossless flag, raw_type (16 = X-Trans, 0 = Bayer), bits, geometry, block_size (0x300) / blocks_in_row / total_lines; each vertical block is a gradient-predicted, adaptive Golomb-Rice bitstream. Fuji Bayer bodies (GFX) are RGGB; X-Trans uses the 0x131 map.

- Active-area crop: the decoded mosaic is the FULL sensor (with optical-black margins, \~190 black columns on the right of a GFX). Crop to RawImageCropTopLeft (0x0110 = top,left) + RawImageCroppedSize (0x0111 = H,W), or they show as a black edge. Bayer keeps an even origin (RGGB phase); X-Trans rolls the 6x6 map by (top%6, left%6) so the demosaicer, which tiles from (0,0), still gets the right colours.
- WB: the 0x2FF0 tag when present, else the as-shot WB_GRBLevels [G,R,B] in the 0xC000 block. That block ALSO holds WB presets (daylight, tungsten, ...) that look identical to a WB triple, so a first-match scan can grab the tungsten preset and badly over-saturate; the as-shot WB is written as THREE identical consecutive triples, so a 3x repeat is required (G = green reference, smallest). Robust across bodies without libraw's per-model wb_section table; within \~1% of libraw on GFX, \~3% on X-T2 (libraw also averages two records by CCT, visually negligible).
- Matrix by model (RAF header camera id at 0x1C -> "Fujifilm X-T50"). X-Trans is demosaiced by Demosaic::XTransWindow (5x5 same-colour average over the tiled 6x6 map; the native channel exact).
- Verified byte-identical to libraw on the uncompressed X-T50 and the compressed X-Trans (X-T2) and Bayer (GFX 50S II) RAFs.
- Limitations: the lossy compressed path is ported but unexercised (no lossy test file); white level is the FujiIFD BitsPerSample max (e.g. 16383 at 14-bit), not libraw's tighter per-body saturation (GFX 15872), so highlights clip slightly late.

#### 10.5.4 Panasonic RW2

PanasonicRaw (ImageFormats/Panasonic/panasonic.cpp). RW2 is TIFF-like (magic 0x55); IFD0 carries the raw tags: SensorWidth/Height (0x02/0x03), RawFormat version (0x2D), RawDataOffset (0x118), CFA (0x09: 1=RGGB 2=GRBG 3=GBRG 4=BGGR), per-channel WB (0x24/0x25/0x26 = R/G/B, green == 256) and black (0x1C..0x1E, stored 15 below true).

It decodes the classic RawFormat-4 compression (dcraw panasonic_load_raw): a 14-column group code with a per-pair nibble predictor, bits pulled from Panasonic's reversed 16 KB "pana_bits" buffer (refilled rotated by loadFlags = 0x2008; byte index vbits>>3 ^ 0x3FF0). Validated byte-identical to libraw on a DC-GX9 RW2. Matrix from the per-model table. Limitation: RawFormat 5/6/7 (newer cameras) use different loadFlags or a different codec and return false.

#### 10.5.5 Olympus and OM System ORF

OlympusRaw (ImageFormats/Olympus/olympus.cpp). The ORF TIFF LIES: it tags the raw strip Compression 1 / 16-bit, but the strip is Olympus's proprietary 12-bit compression: a Huffman magnitude code (a direct 4096-entry 12-bit-prefix table) + an adaptive bit length per sample + a median predictor (w, n, nw) with a 2-column running carry; the bitstream starts 7 bytes into the strip. Ported from dcraw's olympus_load_raw; byte-identical to libraw on an E-M1 ORF.

- As-shot WB is read from the Olympus MakerNote (header "OLYMPUS\\0II\\3\\0" -> TiffWalk::initEmbedded with base = MakerNote start, IFD at +12; ImageProcessing 0x2040 -> WB_RBLevels 0x0100, two SHORTs R,B with green == 256). It is essential: a matrix-neutral render is badly green for Olympus.
- OM System bodies use a second header (fixed 2026-10-11): an OM-1's MakerNote opens "OM SYSTEM\\0\\0\\0II\\4\\0", 16 bytes, IFD at +16, offsets still relative to the MakerNote start, the same 0x2040 -> 0x0100 path below it. ReadAsShotColor accepted only "OLYMPUS", so every OM System raw fell back to the matrix-derived neutral: an OM-1 frame with as-shot WB_RBLevels 584/520 (Lightroom: As Shot 5050 K / +20) rendered as 6500 K, with pixels Lightroom renders neutral at blue/green 0.45-0.77 in linear light, a strong yellow-green cast that read as highlight "blooming". OlympusRaw::parse already scanned for either header; the colour reader now accepts both.
- First cut: white 4095 (12-bit), the E-M1-validated black 255 and BGGR pattern (ORF has no CFAPattern tag). Per-model black/pattern/bit-depth is a refinement (the OM-1 may differ).

TiffWalk::init accepts non-42 TIFF magics (ORF 0x4F52, RW2 0x55, CR2 0x4352), since the endian marker plus a sane first-IFD offset is enough; standard TIFF (magic 42) still validates.

#### 10.5.6 Nikon NEF

NikonRaw (ImageFormats/Nikon/nikon.cpp) is self-contained. It walks the NEF IFDs (via TiffWalk) to the CFA SubIFD (Compression 34713 = Nikon NEF Compressed), then reads the linearisation/Huffman metadata from the Nikon type-3 MakerNote (tag 0x96).

- Some bodies (Z9) expose SEVERAL such SubIFDs (the full-res frame plus smaller/0x0 placeholders), so the largest valid-geometry candidate is chosen, not the last seen (otherwise the 0x0 IFD fails the geometry check and the decode falls back to the embedded preview).
- The MakerNote is an EMBEDDED TIFF ("Nikon\\0" + 2 version bytes + "\\0\\0" + its own header at base = mnOffset+10, offsets relative to base); TiffWalk::init(file, base) handles it.
- Nikon's compression is NOT lossless JPEG: each sample is a Huffman-coded difference (one of dcraw's 6 trees, chosen by version byte + bit depth) against DUAL predictors (a vertical predictor for the first two columns per row parity, then a running horizontal predictor per column parity), mapped through a linearisation curve (identity for the 0x46 lossless mode; interpolated with a tree "split" row for the 0x44 lossy mode). Ported from dcraw's nikon_load_raw; byte-identical to libraw on 14-bit (D810) and 12-bit (D7200) lossless NEF. The 0x44 lossy path is ported but not exercised by a test file.
- Colour matrix from the shared per-model table (an unknown model falls back to identity, a colour cast; seen on the Z9 before its row was added). White = (1&lt;&lt;bps)-1.
- Black from MakerNote tag 0x3d (4 SHORTs, per-channel pedestal: D850 400, D810 600, Z9 1008, matching libraw), falling back to the decoded minimum only on older bodies that omit it (D2H/D100/D800E, \~0 pedestal). The minimum alone is fragile: one sub-pedestal hot pixel drags it below the true black, so SubtractBlack under-subtracts and the frame renders washed out (D850: darkest pixel 78 vs true 400).
- Bit-depth scaling of 0x3d is essential: the tag is always in the body's NATIVE 14-bit units, even for a 12-bit NEF, whose samples are the 14-bit readout shifted down two stops, so it is applied as blackTag >> (14 - bps). Taken at face value on a 12-bit file it subtracts 4x the pedestal: nearly black with a heavy green cast (green photosites sit \~40% above red/blue and are the only ones surviving the clamp). Seen on a 12-bit D7200 (tag 600 vs a measured pedestal of \~150).
- CFA phase from the raw SubIFD's CFAPattern (0x828E) via cfaPatternFromPlaneColor(). Most bodies are RGGB, but older sensors differ (D100 GRBG, D2H GBRG), and decoding those as RGGB rendered greens as magenta. Falls back to RGGB when the tag is absent.
- Active-area crop: some bodies pad the active area with non-image columns that fringe the edges magenta when demosaiced (the pad sits at or below black, and the WB gains amplify the remainder). A per-model crop (libraw margins; D2H: left 6, width 2482; D800/D800E: 7424 -> width 7378, libraw's 46-column right trim) removes them. Margins are even so the CFA phase is unchanged; add a row per affected model. The pad is not always optical black: on the D800E the 46-column tail measured as 14 columns of a constant 600, then 2 saturated (16382) columns, then 30 columns of literal 1, right edge only. Because a pad can read BELOW the pedestal, the crop runs BEFORE the black-level step and the self-calibrated minimum is re-measured over the cropped area.
- As-shot WB from the UNENCRYPTED MakerNote tag 0x0C (WhiteBalanceRBLevels, 4 RATIONALs R, B, G1, G2), matching libraw's cam_mul on D810/D7200/D100. Some bodies (D100) store only R/B and leave green 0, meaning green = 1; substitute 1.0 rather than rejecting the tag. Old bodies without 0x0C (D2H) carry WB in the ColorBalance block 0x97, whose early pre-encryption versions ("0100".."0103") store RGGB levels as 16-bit ints at a version-dependent offset (layout from dcraw's parse_makernote; reproduces libraw's D2H cam_mul 611,256,397,256). The version-0223+ cipher is unbroken, but those bodies all expose 0x0C.

##### 10.5.6.1 Nikon Lens Names

A lens with no EXIF LensModel (every F-mount body) is named in Nikon::parse from nikonLensHash, keyed by 7 bytes of MakerNote LensData (0x98) plus LensType (0x83), exiftool's Composite LensID. Where those 7 bytes sit depends on the LensData VERSION (its first 4 bytes):

```
0100        plain at 0x06       (D100, D1X)
0101        plain at 0x0b       (D70)
0201-0203   encrypted at 0x0b   (D2X, D700, D3)
0204        encrypted at 0x0c   (D90, D800, D850)
0800-0802   encrypted at 0x0d   (Z6/Z7/Z9 with an adapted lens)
```

Encryption starts at byte 4, keyed by ShutterCount (0xa7) and SerialNumber (0x1d); a non-numeric serial keys as 0x22 on a D50 and 0x60 otherwise (exiftool SerialKey). Validated against exiftool's LensID on 40 NEFs across versions 0100/0201/0203/0204/0801. An unknown lens stays blank.

There is deliberately NO exiftool fallback. A metadata parser runs for every thumbnail load on twenty threads, and a process launch there is never cheap enough: add a missing lens to nikonLensHash from exiftool's %nikonLensIDs (ReleaseExtras/ExifTool/lib/Image/ExifTool/Nikon.pm). See [10.10.1 A Fork Storm Behind the Nikon Lens Name](#10101-a-fork-storm-behind-the-nikon-lens-name).

#### 10.5.7 Canon CR2

CanonRaw (ImageFormats/Canon/canon.cpp) is self-contained. It walks the CR2 IFD chain (via TiffWalk), finds the raw IFD (the one with Canon slice tag 0xC640), decodes its lossless-JPEG strip (Compression 6), then reassembles Canon's vertical SLICES: 0xC640 = [nFullSlices, sliceWidth, lastSliceWidth], and the component-interleaved JPEG raster maps back to sensor (row, col) by dcraw's formula.

- From the Canon MakerNote (IFD0 -> ExifIFD 0x8769 -> MakerNote 0x927C): SensorInfo (0xE0 -> active-area crop L/T/R/B) and ColorData (0x4001 -> WB_RGGBLevelsAsShot; offset 63 for modern ColorData, 25/24/142 for older lengths).
- Black is self-calibrated from the masked optical-black columns (x &lt; left) before cropping; white = (1&lt;&lt;precision)-1; matrix from the per-model table; pattern RGGB; crop origin forced even to keep the Bayer phase.
- Verified byte-identical on a 7D Mark II CR2.
- Limitations: lossless-JPEG CR2 only (sRAW/mRAW and very old layouts not handled); black is a masked-column average, not per-channel; the ColorData WB offset table covers the common versions.

#### 10.5.8 Canon CR3 (CRX)

CanonCR3Raw (ImageFormats/Canon/crx.cpp + crxcodec.cpp; CanonCR3 handles the CR3 metadata). It walks the ISO-BMFF box tree for the full-resolution CRAW track and reads its CMP1 geometry (fW/fH, tile, nBits, planes, cfaLayout), the IAD1 active-area crop, and the CRX bitstream location (stbl co64 offset + stsz length).

Canon writes TWO different CRX streams behind the same extension, selected by the camera's RAW / C-RAW setting and distinguishable only from CMP1 byte 26 (encType&lt;&lt;4 | imageLevels). crx.cpp routes on imageLevels: 0 -> the clean-room level-0 decoder, 1-3 -> CrxCodec::Decode. Everything after the mosaic (IAD1 crop, per-channel black, white, WB, matrix) is shared.

- "RAW", level 0 (clean-room): adaptive Golomb-Rice (escape 41 / 21 bits / kMax 15) + JPEG-LS-style MED prediction + T.87 run mode. Re-derived by byte-level instrumentation against the libraw/rawpy oracle: (a) the tile's four Bayer planes share ONE CONTINUOUS bitstream: do NOT re-seek per plane to the byte offsets (only R5 and R6 II even planes land byte-aligned; odd planes start mid-byte); the reader runs continuously, and only k and the run s_param reset at each plane's first line. (b) The non-top line adapts k from a LOOK-AHEAD-adjusted code bit_code = (bit_code + |2\*(d-b)|) >> 1 (the sample itself is decoded with adaptation OFF); the top line uses ordinary per-symbol adaptation. (c) Run entry when coeff a == b == d; predictor med(a, b, c); s_param persists plane-wide. The four planes interleave ROW-MAJOR into the RGGB mosaic (plane 0/1/2/3 -> quad (0,0)(0,1)(1,0)(1,1)), then crop to IAD1. Byte-identical (0 diffs) to the oracle on EOS R5 (46.65M px) and R6 II (25.49M px).
- "C-RAW", the wavelet levels (a LibRaw port, NOT clean-room): each plane is wavelet-transformed (imageLevels 3), so the stream carries 3\*levels+1 = 10 quantised subbands per plane behind a DIFFERENT TLV marker set (0xff11/12/13 rather than 0xff01/02/03; tile/plane/subband records of 16/8/16 bytes), plus a Golomb-coded per-tile QP table that builds the inverse-quantisation step table. crxcodec.cpp is a faithful port of LibRaw's src/decoders/crx.cpp (LGPL 2.1 / CDDL 1.0, attributed in the file header): the inverse 5/3 lifting DWT, per-subband inverse quantisation and three extra line-decoder variants. Changes from upstream are limited to the input layer (CrxBitstream reads by memcpy from the resident file buffer; curBufOffset is still an absolute file offset), an alignment-safe 32-bit load, a local sgetn/exception shim, and a serial per-plane loop in place of OpenMP (Winnow already decodes images concurrently). Keep the distinction when editing: crx.cpp's clean-room claim covers the container walk and LEVEL 0 ONLY. Bit-exact (0 diffs) against the oracle on 43 EOS R5 files (41 C-RAW, 2 RAW); the IAD1 crop reproduces libraw's visible geometry (8191x5463, margins 144/112).
- Black is self-calibrated PER-CHANNEL from the masked columns; white = (1&lt;&lt;nBits)-1 refined by the per-model table; WB from the CMT3 makernote ColorData (0x4001, the same offset table as CR2); matrix from the per-model table; pattern RGGB.
- CrxCodec also decodes level 0 correctly, so consolidating onto it is possible; the clean-room path is kept because it is byte-validated and carries no LGPL lineage.
- Pinned by tests/unit/tst_crx.cpp, which checksums the mosaic against oracle-derived CRC32s. It needs sample files, so it SKIPS unless WINNOW_TEST_CR3_DIR points at a directory of .cr3 files.
- Limitations: single-tile only (tileWidth/Height == fW/fH), which is what current full-frame bodies write; multi-tile or non-4-plane CRAW returns false. encType 1 is rejected rather than guessed at (signed output, no sample to validate). CR3 HDR-PQ thumbnail handling is separate (see [3.6.3.1 CR3 HDR PQ](#3631-cr3-hdr-pq)).

C-RAW is the DEFAULT on current bodies: of 499 CR3s in the local test corpus, 497 are C-RAW. Before the wavelet port (2026-09-20) the great majority of real CR3 files never decoded, and the failure was silent and worse than it looked: UnpackCfa returned false, ImageDecoder::load fell back to the embedded JPEG, and that preview is tagged kWorking, not CameraNative. Both camera-profile application sites (Develop::ToWorkingSpace and the preMat fold in develop.cpp) are gated on CameraNative, so the image looked fine while the Profile dropdown and every other raw-only control quietly did nothing; currentIsRaw() tests the file EXTENSION, so nothing in the UI was greyed to say so. (The Apple engine decodes C-RAW but returns kWorking too, so it was never a workaround for profiles.)

### 10.6 Shared Readers

- TiffWalk (ImageFormats/Raw/tiffwalk.\*): a small shared TIFF/EP IFD reader (header, IFDs + SubIFDs, tag value accessors: scalar / u32 array / real array / bytes / ascii, handling the inline-vs-offset rule and endianness, and embedded MakerNote TIFFs via a base offset). Used by DNG, Nikon, Canon, Olympus and Panasonic; SonyRaw still has its own inline walk.
- LosslessJpeg (ImageFormats/Raw/losslessjpeg.\*): the compression behind Canon CR2, most compressed DNG, and lossless NEF/ARW variants. NOT DCT JPEG: the lossless mode (SOF3), where each sample is Huffman-coded as the difference from a spatial predictor of its neighbours. LosslessJpeg::Decode(bytes) -> Image{width, height, components, precision, samples}, samples interleaved by component (samples[(y\*width+x)\*comps + c]). Camera-agnostic; each vendor decoder extracts the bytestream from its container and reassembles components/tiles/slices into the CFA. Scope: single scan, Huffman, predictors 1-7, point transform; NO restart intervals yet (returns false on DRI > 0). Byte-identical to a reference decoder validated end to end on a lossless-JPEG DNG (Leica M10: 14-bit, 2 components, predictor 1).

### 10.7 Status

```
Done        scaffold; Sony ARW (uncompressed + ARW2); real colour (per-model matrix,
            matrix-derived WB, as-shot WB/black for every format); shared
            lossless-JPEG; DNG; CR2; CR3 (level 0 + C-RAW); NEF; RAF; RW2; ORF
Next        a better demosaic (AHD); Sony lossless-compressed (Compression JPEG);
            RW2 RawFormat 5/6/7; DNG chromatic adaptation for ColorMatrix1-only files
```

### 10.8 Adobe Look Profiles (.xmp): Declined

A design record, so the investigation is not repeated. CameraProfileStore sweeps CameraRaw/CameraProfiles for \*.dcp and reads .dcp only. Adobe has a SECOND profile tree: /Library/Application Support/Adobe/CameraRaw/Settings/Adobe/Profiles/ (mirrored inside the Lightroom Classic app bundle at Contents/Resources/Settings/Adobe/Profiles/), holding 577 \*.xmp profiles under Camera/&lt;Maker>/ (Fujifilm 89, Nikon 340, Panasonic 38, Sigma 45, Ricoh 7) plus creative sets (Adaptive, Artistic, B&W, Modern, Vintage) that are not camera-restricted. This is why a Fuji body shows one profile row: its film simulations were never .dcp files.

A Look is not a DCP. It is an XMP preset (crs:PresetType="Look") carrying crs:CameraModelRestriction (spelled EXACTLY as canonicalCameraModel spells it, e.g. "Fujifilm GFX 50S II"), crs:CameraProfile (the BASE profile the look sits on, e.g. "Camera PROVIA/Standard"), and crs:RGBTable + crs:Table\_&lt;uuid>: a 3-D RGB LUT, \~30 KB in a proprietary printable-ASCII encoding. Supporting them would be a new render stage (base profile, then a 3-D LUT). For the GFX 50S II it would add 4 rows (CLASSIC Neg, NOSTALGIC Neg, BLEACH BYPASS, Sepia), not the 19 Lightroom offers: the older 15 (PROVIA, VELVIA, ASTIA, CLASSIC CHROME, Pro Neg Hi/Std, ETERNA, ACROS x4, Monochrome x4) are not on disk in any form (their names appear only as strings inside Camera Raw.plugin's Mach-O). Nikon is the bigger prize (340 looks).

The encoding spike (2026-09-14) concluded NOT FEASIBLE from the files alone:

- Solved: the container is base85, 5 chars -> 4 bytes, with the MOST significant digit LAST in each group. The alphabet is the 85 printable ASCII characters minus nine XML- and shell-awkward ones (" & , ; &lt; > \\ \_ \~). Three ranks were pinned by frequency analysis at the most-significant position over 8.14 million groups: '%' is rank 82 (it appears at 49% of the uniform rate, the signature of a digit whose range is partly reachable under a 2^32 ceiling), and '#' and '\$' are ranks 83/84 (they NEVER appear there).
- Not solved: the other 82 ranks. The order is not ASCII ascending or descending, and not any of the 170 affine (a\*i+b mod 85, both digit orders) mappings; every one still overflows 32 bits.
- The usual tricks fail. The payload is NOT zlib or deflate: all 514 tables share the top TWO digits of their first group, confining the first four bytes to a 614,125-wide window, and no choice of rank('0') puts the zlib signature 78 9C inside it; group 1 is not constant either. There is no smoothness to exploit for seriation: symbol entropy is 6.4085 bits against a 6.4094 maximum, and the top-digit autocorrelation is 0.0142 against 0.0118 for random. Structurally, group 0's top digits are constant, groups 1-2 partly constrained (34 and 37 distinct leading digits across 514 files) and group 3 onward \~random (73-74): a header of roughly 12-20 bytes, then opaque data, already compressed or encrypted by something that is not deflate.
- Two unknowns stacked (an arbitrary 85-symbol permutation AND an unidentified codec) are not worth further effort without an oracle (a file whose decoded contents are known independently).

The index-only option (list Looks without rendering them) was DROPPED too: a Look's base profile is one of the 15 inside Camera Raw.plugin, so the rows could be honoured neither by LUT nor by base, a dropdown of entries that quietly do nothing, exactly what the greyed-with-a-reason rule exists to prevent.

### 10.9 Raw Renderers (Winnow and Apple)

Two engines decode a raw to a WorkingImage (demosaic + global colour/baseline luma NR + start WB/black/white):

- Winnow (winnowDecodeRawEngine): the in-house decoder. Portable, the only engine on Windows, and the canonical focus-stacking engine (deterministic, CFA-level control).
- Apple (appleDecodeRawEngine): macOS Core Image (CIRAWFilter), GPU demosaic + NR, macOS ONLY; callers fall back to Winnow off-mac.

Both converge on WorkingImage, so Develop, local luma NR and the OutputTransform are engine-agnostic.

#### 10.9.1 The Default and the Per-Image Choice

"Render using" is part of each image's recipe (2026-10-14), a Global-scope tri-state like denoiseRaw: EditParams::rawEngine (-1 unset = follow the default, 0 Winnow, 1 Apple) plus appleRawVersion (with Apple: 0 newest, N = Apple Raw N). It used to be one global switch, so choosing Apple Raw 9 on a version (virtual copy) changed its master, and every other raw, too.

- Written to the sidecar only when SET, so an untouched raw keeps its recipe and devPreview key. isIdentity counts it (a renderer choice alone is an edit).
- The DEFAULT, what an unset image renders with, is G::decodeRawEngine + AppleRawDecode::VersionPin, set in Preferences > Developed previews > "Default raw renderer" (Preferences::rawRendererChoices: Winnow, Apple Raw (newest), Apple Raw N per version this Mac has). G::decodeRawEngine is persisted in QSettings as "decodeRawEngine" (beside "useRaw"); the compiled-in default is currently appleDecodeRawEngine (Main/global.cpp), and off-mac an Apple value is normalised to Winnow on load. The version pin is persisted as "appleRawDecoderVersion".
- Never read G::decodeRawEngine directly to decide how an image renders.

One resolver: Develop/rawrender.h.

- RawRender::Choice {apple, applePin}; defaultChoice(); resolve(globalParams); fromBlob(recipe base64; it probes for "rawEngine" before parsing, since it runs per edited image as sidecars are read); apply(params, choice); tag() ("w" / "a0" / "a9"); label().
- MW::rawRenderFor(fPath) / DevelopProperties::rawRenderFor(fPath) answer it for an image on the GUI thread (the session recipe in stackCache, else the sidecar). A worker resolves on the GUI thread and captures the Choice.

Where the choice is used:

- RawFormat::Decode takes the Choice (null = default): the engine, the Apple version (AppleRawDecode::Decode's pin argument), the Winnow-only PMRID gate, and the TAG on every base it hands back (WorkingImage::rawRenderTag; copyMetadata carries it). decodeRawWorking (PMRID) always passes Winnow.
- ImageDecoder::rawRender is set by decodeIndependent's argument (MW::ensureDevelopWork, MW::developPixelSource: the Develop image, export and the devPreview builder, the callers that know the recipe) and reset per cache decode(). An ImageCache decode knows no recipe and uses the default; its display image is replaced by the Develop render or the recipe's devPreview wherever the recipe matters.
- WorkingImageCache is keyed by SOURCE + TAG. put() files a base under its rawRenderTag; get(key, tag) / contains(key, tag) ask for the recipe's renderer and fall back to the UNTAGGED entry (non-raw images, raws built from the embedded preview); remove() drops every renderer's entry for the file; the Develop pin keeps all of them. A master on Winnow and its version on Apple Raw 9 hold separate bases, and NOTHING IS CLEARED on a switch: the render that follows asks for the new tag, misses, and MW::ensureDevelopWork decodes. Undo/redo, presets and Paste Settings land the same way, because the choice is just recipe state. The Denoise-raw paths (ensureRawDenoise) ask for the Winnow tag.
- The develop PROXY is rebuilt when its base changes under the same path (MW::developProxySrc, a weak_ptr). It used to be kept by path alone, so a renderer switch went on showing the old decoder's pixels.
- Render keys: Metadata::devPreviewKey hashes the recipe's EFFECTIVE renderer (RawRender::engineKey + appleKeyPart of fromBlob(blob)); defaultRenderKey the default's. For a recipe that never chose, the strings are exactly what the global setting produced, so no existing preview was re-keyed.
- Raw panel: DevelopProperties::setRawRenderer writes the choice into scope 0 (noteScopeEdit "Render using" -> History; multi-image propagation via kIntFields rawEngine/appleRawVersion), reflects the engine, rebuilds the tree deferred (camera profiles and the denoise rows are Winnow-only), emits rawRendererChanged (MW warms PMRID) and paramsChanged. reflectEngine / syncRawPanel / the camera-profile row / the Raw demosaic menu read currentRawRender().
- Presets: the published "demosaicEngine" token ("apple" / "winnow") lands in the recipe (mergePreset) instead of switching a global; "appleRawVersion" (int) travels beside it under Apple. Captured as the image's EFFECTIVE renderer.
- A new version copies its origin's recipe, so it starts with the origin's renderer (or none, following the default).

#### 10.9.2 Apple Decoder Version

AppleRawDecode::Decode ALWAYS sets CIRAWFilter.decoderVersion (2026-10-13); it never leaves it to Core Image, whose default is NOT the newest whatever its header says (on macOS 27, CR3, D850 NEF and X-T50 RAF list 7, 8, 9 but default to 8, and version 9 decodes them to different pixels).

- The pin is per image (EditParams::appleRawVersion); AppleRawDecode::VersionPin() is only the DEFAULT for images that have not chosen. 0 = the newest version each file supports; N = the newest version &lt;= N the file supports, or the file's oldest if N is older than all of them (PickVersion).
- If the chosen version gives no output image (version 9 can need on-demand resources), the decode falls back to Core Image's default and, on macOS 27+, requests the download in the background. A decode never waits on the network.

Which versions an image supports can only be known reliably by opening the file with Core Image (50-200 ms). Not from the camera: CIRAWFilter.supportedCameraModelsWithVersion (macOS 27) lists ILCE-9M2 under 8 while the A9 II sample file offers only 7, Apple's model names do not match EXIF ("Nikon Z9" vs "NIKON Z 9"), and the list can differ between files from one camera (compression).

- So the decode records {supported versions, version used} per path (AppleRawDecode::DecodedVersions) and posts a queued callback; MW routes it to DevelopProperties::syncAppleDecoderVersions, which fills the Raw panel's "Render using" list: one "Apple Raw N" entry per version the image supports, newest first, then Winnow, with the image's choice selected.
- The list does not wait for an Apple decode (which never happens while Winnow is the engine). When syncAppleDecoderVersions finds no record it calls AppleRawDecode::RequestVersions, which opens the file with CIRAWFilter on the global QThreadPool (no decode), records the supported list plus the version the current pin WOULD use, and posts the same callback; one request per path, de-duplicated while in flight, and a real decode later overwrites the record. The unnumbered "Apple Raw" shows only for that moment.
- Choosing the TOP entry sets pin 0 (newest; follows OS updates); a lower entry pins N, for THIS image. The selected entry is what the image's own choice picks from its list (PickVersion's rule), not the version the file's last decode used, which may have been another version of it on another renderer.

Render keys fold in the Apple state, under the Apple engine only: "|appleRaw=c3:&lt;pin>:&lt;fp>".

- &lt;pin> is the pin, or LatestDecoderVersion() for "newest" (the highest CIRAWDecoderVersionN symbol the running macOS exports, found with dlsym), so an OS update adding a version misses the old previews.
- &lt;fp> is AppleRawDecode::SupportFingerprint: the pin does not say which version a FILE decodes with (under "newest", a camera Apple adds to decoder 9 moves from 8 to 9 with the pin unchanged, and its version-8 previews were served beside a version-9 loupe). The per-file version can only change when Apple's support does, so the fingerprint hashes (8 hex) the macOS build (sysctl kern.osversion), RawCamera.bundle's CFBundleVersion (RAW compatibility updates) and the sorted names of the downloaded camera assets in AssetsV2/com_apple_MobileAsset_RawCamera_Camera (macOS 27 on-demand support; also checked under /private/var/MobileAsset). \~7 ms once per launch, cached, re-read after a downloadResources this process requested completes. Any change misses every Apple preview once (they re-render lazily); Winnow keys are untouched.
- "c3" marks the colour fix below, so every preview built before it misses.

View cameras supported: RawPanel's appleBlock (a rule and a transparent "View cameras supported" button, shown only while an Apple decoder renders; RawPanel::setEngine; the mirror of the Winnow-only denoiseBlock) opens Dialogs/applecamerasdlg (AppleCamerasDlg). It has an "Apple Raw N" dropdown (AppleRawDecode::AvailableVersions, the dlsym'd symbols), a filter box with a live "x of y cameras" count, and the list from AppleRawDecode::SupportedCameraModels: CIRAWFilter supportedCameraModelsWithVersion (macOS 27+, \~0.2 s, cached per version), or before macOS 27 the single all-versions supportedCameraModels with the dropdown disabled and saying so. It opens on the version the current image renders with. A note says it is Apple's per-model list in Apple's spelling and that a file can offer fewer versions; the Render using list remains the per-file truth.

#### 10.9.3 Apple Engine Output: Colour Space and Look

Fixed 2026-10-13. Two bugs made Apple renders oversaturated, cyan-shifted and brighter than Winnow:

1. Core Image rendered linear sRGB while the WorkingImage was tagged kWorking, which is linear Rec.2020. The CIContext OUTPUT space is now kCGColorSpaceExtendedLinearITUR_2020 (static_assert against kWorking). Its WORKING space deliberately stays extended linear sRGB: decoder 9 with a Rec.2020 working space renders wrong colour (D850 centre blue 0.245 -> 0.162, red negative) and decoder 8 does not; sRGB working + Rec.2020 output matches the BT.2087 matrix to 4 places on both.
2. Apple's tone boost was on (the lines turning it off had been commented out on 2026-07-06), so its tone curve stacked under the OutputTransform's. boostAmount, boostShadowAmount, localToneMapAmount, contrastAmount, sharpnessAmount and detailAmount are now 0, verified linear: +1 EV doubles every sample on D850, CR3, X-T50 and A1 II.

Apple's luminance/colour NOISE REDUCTION stays at Core Image's per-image defaults, by the user's choice (it is the point of decoder 9). Sharpening is Develop's Detail section's job.

### 10.10 Investigations and Fixes

#### 10.10.1 A Fork Storm Behind the Nikon Lens Name

The worst stall in a large catalog (2026-09-24). The Nikon parser always decrypted LensData and always read offset 0x0c, so only version-0204 bodies ever matched nikonLensHash, and every other NEF fell through to an exiftool PROCESS LAUNCH asking for LensModel. Those bodies do not write LensModel, so it returned nothing, and the next read of the same file (every thumbnail load re-parses) launched it again. With twenty reader threads that is a fork storm, and fork() takes every malloc zone lock and the objc runtime locks for its duration: the GUI thread sampled 97% blocked in \_\_ulock_wait2 behind it, reported as GUI STALLs of 1-19 s while selecting, filtering and scrolling a 148k-row library.

The fix reads the LensData version and its offset (see [10.5.6.1 Nikon Lens Names](#10561-nikon-lens-names)) and removes the exiftool fallback entirely. The general tell: a main thread that samples almost entirely in \_\_ulock_wait2 means some thread is fork()ing (a QProcess, exiftool).

## 11 Develop

Lightroom-style non-destructive adjustments (denoise, white balance, exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, texture, dehaze ...). They apply to ALL image types (JPEG / TIFF / HEIC / raw), so they are a shared stage AFTER decode and BEFORE the display tone / gamma / ICC transform, not part of RawFormat. Adjustments run on a FLOAT LINEAR working buffer, because exposure, tone and dehaze need headroom.

Adding or changing an adjustment touches about twelve files; follow [11.38 Adding or Changing a Develop Adjustment (Checklist)](#1138-adding-or-changing-a-develop-adjustment-checklist). Preset and sidecar keys are a published format: add freely, never rename or rescale in place (see [11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)](#1139-stale-presets-and-history-schema-drift)).

### 11.1 The Pipeline

The unifying representation is WorkingImage: float linear scene-referred RGB, a colour-space tag and a white reference. Both decode paths converge on it:

```
RAW:      ... -> Demosaic -> camera RGB          (RawColor stops CAMERA-NATIVE)
NON-RAW:  QImage decode -> un-gamma to linear -> working space   (InputTransform)
```

and one consumer:

```
WorkingImage -> Develop(EditParams) -> OutputTransform(view transform + primaries + transfer + ICC) -> QImage
```

- WorkingImage::space (ColorSpaceMath::ColorSpace) says which primaries the pixels are in RIGHT NOW, so no stage has to assume. The raw path arrives CameraNative and Develop's stage 0 converts; the non-raw path arrives already in the working space. It is orthogonal to sceneReferred (scene vs display referred); both are needed and neither implies the other.
- The working space is named once, ColorSpaceMath::kWorking (Develop/colorspace.h): LINEAR REC.2020, D65. Every op derives its luma weights from it via lumaWeights() instead of hard-coding Rec.709. That was \~15 sites writing 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722, plus rangemask.h using the Rec.601 triple (an inconsistency, not a decision: a Luminance Range mask selected on a different luma from every other op). Widening the working space is one line plus re-blessed goldens (see [11.4.1 Widening the Working Space (Rec.709 to Rec.2020)](#1141-widening-the-working-space-rec709-to-rec2020)).
- EditParams is one versioned struct with identity defaults (absent = no-op = no behaviour change): the single source of truth for every adjustment value. It is persisted per image (sidecar; see [11.14 Develop Persistence](#1114-develop-persistence)) and the slider UI binds to it.
- Develop is a stateless, re-entrant processor constructed per decode (the same discipline as Demosaic / RawFormat), with a FIXED operation order.

#### 11.1.1 Operation Order

```
Stage  Operation            What it does
0      Input profile        camera-native -> working space (raw); see below
1      Denoise              luma / chroma; earliest. For raw, ideally on the CFA mosaic
2      White balance        linear channel scale (raw: camMul, from temp/tint)
2b     Calibration          3x3 primary re-point (R/G/B hue + sat), in LINEAR light,
                            rows sum to 1 so neutrals are fixed (Calibrate panel)
3      Exposure             linear gain 2^EV
3b     Colour RGB           per-channel linear gain (red / green / blue), folded into 2
4      Contrast             S-curve about mid-grey
5      Highlights/Shadows,  region-weighted tone lifts; Whites/Blacks as endpoint
       Whites/Blacks        (white-point / black-point) moves (see [[The Tone Controls]])
5a     Tone curve           the Curves panel's point curves, composed into the SAME
                            perceptual LUT right after 4/5 (Lightroom's order): the
                            RGB composite first, then the per-channel R/G/B curve
5c     Colour HSL           hue rotation + saturation + vibrance + luminance
5c2    Point color          up to 8 sampled colours, each shifting hue/sat/lum of the
                            pixels near it in OKLab of the DISPLAY value
5d     Colour grading       tonal-range tinting per shadows / midtones / highlights,
                            plus a global range (Color Grade panel)
6      Texture              fine local contrast (~13 px)
6.5    Clarity              MID-radius local contrast (~60 px), midtone-weighted,
                            halo-guarded
7      Dehaze               local contrast + black point (~170 px), haze estimate
8      Vignette             radial corner exposure falloff (exposure / feather)
8.5    Sharpen              capture sharpening: an unsharp mask on luminance, edge-gated
                            (amount / radius / detail / masking); the ONE op with an
                            ABSOLUTE pixel radius
9      Grain                monochromatic film grain (amount / size / roughness)
```

Stages 0, 2, 2b, 3 and 3b fold into ONE 3x3 (PointCoeffs::preMat), and 4 through 5d are one fused point-op pass (see [11.12 Develop Performance](#1112-develop-performance)). The local-contrast ladder is 1 px (Sharpen) / 13 px (Texture) / 60 px (Clarity) / 170 px (Dehaze).

Two ops give better results inside the raw pipeline: white balance (at the camera-RGB stage) and denoise (on the CFA mosaic). EditParams is shared, so RawFormat::Decode() takes an optional const EditParams\* and can consume those fields at the right stages while Develop handles the rest; denoise-raw (PMRID) is the CFA-stage case (see [11.17 Raw Denoise](#1117-raw-denoise)).

#### 11.1.2 The Input Profile Is Not an Edit

Stage 0 is never skipped by a "nothing to adjust" fast path. A camera-native buffer that reaches OutputTransform is not caught: ColorSpaceMath::matrix returns the IDENTITY for CameraNative (it has no tabulated primaries), so the sensor values are written out unconverted and UNBALANCED, which looks like a heavily GREEN image (a Bayer sensor's green response dominates). Rule for any new render path: CONVERT FIRST, then decide whether there is anything else to do.

Four paths skipped it and were fixed (2026-08):

- WorkingImageCache::render's identity fast path now converts a COPY (the cache entry stays camera-native for the develop path).
- WorkingImageCache::renderStack's `if (!base.isIdentity()) Apply` now calls Develop::Apply unconditionally, whose OWN identity early-out still runs stage 0.
- RawFormat::Decode's no-edit tail converts a copy of \*work.
- ImageDecoder::load's cached-base shortcut (reusing an already-decoded WorkingImage instead of re-demosaicing) went through OutputTransform::ToImage directly, skipping stage 0 AND the saved recipe (it sets developApplied, so applyDevelop would not put the recipe back). It now goes through WorkingImageCache::render, which does both, plus the recipe's view transform.

Symptoms that found them: double-clicking a Develop caption resets that adjustment, and on an otherwise unedited image that makes the params identity, so the next render went green; and selecting a second edited image sometimes came back green and un-edited ("sometimes" being exactly when a base happened to be cached for it).

The recipe's VIEW TRANSFORM travels the same way. OutputTransform::ToImage defaults to None (the identity), so any call site that renders a recipe must pass OutputTransform::ViewFromInt(edit.viewTransform), or a Filmic / AgX image renders un-tone-mapped whenever it comes through that path.
