The tone LUT therefore depends on EditParams::viewTransform, which promotes an existing rule from cosmetic to load-bearing: a render site that builds the LUT for one view transform and renders with another puts the regions in the wrong place. tst_toneregions caught exactly that (its render used None while EditParams defaulted to Filmic), so the test sets both. Two test targets that linked develop.cpp without outputtransform.cpp had to gain it.

#### 11.8.2 The Operators

The fit: one raw (ILCE-1) exported from Lightroom Classic 15.5.1 at 17 settings (each of blacks / shadows / highlights / whites at -100, -50, +50, +100, plus all-zero) and from Winnow at the same 17, full resolution, 8-bit sRGB, no resampling. Histogram-matching the two ZERO renders recovers the baseline difference as a per-pixel curve and divides it out (0.70 levels residual); histogram-matching each slider render against its own zero render recovers THAT SLIDER'S OPERATOR as an explicit curve. The constants in develop.cpp fit those 16 curves at 2.45 levels of 255 RMS overall (worst operator 4.7, worst point 11; 24.1 before).

- The model families are not uniform, and that is the finding. Lightroom's endpoint controls are endpoint moves in the direction that CLIPS and gentle band lifts in the direction that cannot: Blacks - is a black-point raise (crushes, clips at 0) while Blacks + is a band lift (opens the shadows); Whites + is a white-point lower (brightens, clips at white) while Whites - is a band pull. Shadows and Highlights are bands in both directions (Shadows has since become a gain; below). An operator symmetric in sign cannot reproduce a control whose two directions do different things: Blacks +100 lifts by at most 26 levels; Blacks -100 crushes everything below level 48 to black. (kBlackPointRange 0.220 / kBlackPointExpo 1.6, kWhitePointRange 0.310 / kWhitePointExpo 1.8.)
- The response is not linear in the slider, so each operator carries an exponent: the ratio between Lightroom's +100 and +50 curves runs from 1.8 (highlights) to 3.2 (whites) where linear would be 2.0.
- The bands OVERLAP: Shadows reaches to level 160 and Highlights starts at 48, so a midtone takes a share of each and their shifts add. tst_toneregions asserts what IS true (two controls never COMPOUND: the pair never exceeds the sum of the two alone), replacing the old "they do not overlap" assertion.
- The region handles SLIDE the bands rather than setting their peaks (a handle that overwrote a peak would throw the fit away). The defaults (0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75) remain an EXACT no-op, so every older sidecar keeps rendering from the same three numbers.
- The lifts are applied on the DISPLAY axis. The value goes out through the view transform and transfer (OutputTransform::DisplayPosition), is moved there, and comes back (PerceptualFromDisplay, by bisection: the transforms have no tractable inverse, and this runs 1024 times per render, not per pixel). That is the axis Lightroom's operators were measured on and the handles are drawn on. Converting the shift into a working-value shift via the view transform's local slope fails near the shoulder, where the slope is small enough that the conversion explodes.
- Contrast stays in the working domain (a slope about mid-grey, where "about mid-grey" means something physical). applyToneShape carries TWO positions: d0, taken BEFORE the contrast slope (where a handle points), and d, taken after (the value being moved). Collapsing them reintroduces the contrast bug, and did once during this work.
- The endpoint move scales the headroom rather than flattening it. The LUT spans \~3 stops above white (kToneLutMaxN = 8), and because the remap is affine and unclamped at the top, a value above white stays above white and SEPARATED from its neighbours; clamping there would collapse every specular highlight the moment Whites moved.
- The monotonicity clamp is in buildPointCoeffs, not applyToneShape, because that is the one place the whole composed curve exists (the parametric shape, the RGB composite curve and the per-channel curve, in render order); clamping any one alone still lets the composition invert. Proven load-bearing: with the other changes in, disabling it still inverts the ramp at sample 13.
- Develop::ParametricCurve does NOT see the clamp: it draws the parametric shape alone, which is what the Curves panel's Parametric view is a view of, so where the clamp fires the plot shows a dip the render does not have. Accepted: the alternative is a plot that stops responding to a slider still being dragged.
- The Curves panel's Parametric bands write two kinds of control: bands 0 and 3 (blacks, whites) drag endpoint moves while bands 1 and 2 drag region lifts, exactly as Lightroom's histogram zones behave, and each band label names the Basic slider it writes.
- Existing sidecars with non-zero blacks / shadows / highlights / whites re-rendered when the operators changed kind (whites and blacks a lot). Accepted: the alternative is keeping an operator that is measurably the wrong shape. No EditParams field changed, so every sidecar still LOADS.

#### 11.8.3 Shadows Is a Gain

Refit 2026-10-05. The 2026-09-17 band was the wrong KIND of operator even though its histogram fit was good: Lightroom's Shadows "retains contrast" while Winnow's "shifted the black point". The band was an additive display-space lift peaking at level 5, and adding a constant to the deepest tones IS a black-point raise (at +100 the darkest 1% of one ILCE-1 frame went from level 5 to 35; Lightroom 1 to 8). Histogram matching recovers a curve's average placement, and an offset and a gain can agree on a histogram while disagreeing on what happens BETWEEN neighbouring dark tones, which is what the eye reads as contrast.

How it was measured: Lightroom and Winnow exports of one raw (2022-04-12_0002, ILCE-1) at Shadows -100/-50/0/+50/+100, full resolution, 16-bit sRGB, in \~/Pictures/\_LRref (2022-04-12_0002_LR_Shadows\_&lt;n>.tif and 2022-04-12_0002Shadows\_&lt;n>.tif). Each app is compared only against its own zero render, so the framing and base rendering do not enter. Per display-level bin of the zero render, the gain is log2 of the mean display-linear luminance of the slider render over the zero render's. Findings:

1. Lightroom's change is a GAIN: -100 mirrors +100 in stops, and +-50 is half of +-100 (fitted exponent 1.03, taken as 1).
2. It is \~1-D: the pixel's own value explains 78% of the gain's variance, an 8 px neighbourhood 82%, larger radii less, so Lightroom's Shadows is NOT a large-radius local tone mapper and no spatial pass was added.
3. Detail inside shadow regions GROWS 43% at +100, where the band left it unchanged: a gain scales dark tones apart instead of shifting them together.

The operator (applyToneShape + shadowGainWeight): d -> sRGB(sRGB^-1(d) \* 2^(amount \* 2.34 \* w(d0))), with w(x) = (0.942 e^(-x/0.089) + 0.058) \* (1 - smoothstep(x / 0.874)), x = max(0, d0 - shadow-handle shift). Lightroom's measured gain at +100: +2.6 stops at level 2, +1.2 at 18, +0.5 at 42, +0.15 at 74, +0.04 at 146, 0 by \~190. Fit: 0.31 levels RMS across all four settings, worst point 1.35 (the band: 3.9 / 5.5 / 7.8 / 14.3 RMS, worst 23). Monotone at both slider ends (minimum composed slope 0.79 of the input's at +100, 0.20 at -100). Shadows runs FIRST among the region moves (after the endpoint moves): it scales light, so the additive moves shift the scaled value. The shadow handle slides the start of the decay; the crossover stretches the tail; the defaults are an exact no-op.

- Tested by tst_toneregions::shadowsIsAGainNotAnOffset: Shadows +100 leaves black at black and keeps at least 45% of the light ratio between levels \~5 and \~20 (the band kept \~37%; Lightroom 56%). The first version asserted that the RISE in levels between 10 and 40 grows, and failed against the new operator, because a gain that fades with brightness shrinks that rise, and Lightroom's curve does too: ratio, not rise, separates a gain from an offset. regionsDoNotSlideWithContrast moved from the Shadows lift to the Highlights lift for a related reason: a gain's peak lift in LEVELS moves with Contrast because the value it scales moves, even though its weight does not.
- Existing sidecars with a non-zero Shadows re-render, noticeably at large values: at +100 a level-10 tone now lifts about half as far (\~+17 levels instead of +35).

#### 11.8.4 Highlights

Highlights + keeps its fixed band (no data to refit). Highlights - is image-adaptive and local, and it also recovers what a positive Exposure pushed past white. It runs as four parts:

1. The fitted band (as for the other regions), at a per-frame STRENGTH.
2. A scene-linear RECOVERY stage when Exposure is positive.
3. A LOCAL LAPLACIAN field that moves bright regions as regions.
4. A FRAME-RELATIVE gain that compresses bright regions relative to the frame's log-mean, scaled by the frame's range.

##### 11.8.4.1 The Strength Is a Budget

A second Lightroom series (an E-M1 snow raw, 2017-01-10_0025.ORF, at Exposure 0 and +1.5, Highlights 0 / -50 / -100) showed the 2026-09-17 fixed band was right only for the frame it was fitted on. Lightroom's -100 pulls the same display level very differently per frame (max pull 53 levels on the dark ILCE-1 frame, 24 on the snow, 12 on the snow at +1.5), where Winnow's fixed band pulled the pushed snow's median down 52 levels to Lightroom's 11. All five Lightroom curves are ONE band shape (up from display 0.05, peak 0.92, down to white) times a per-frame strength (1.84 levels RMS with the strength fitted per frame), linear in the slider.

Strength x the band's mean weight over the frame's histogram came out at 8.0 / 11.5 / 9.3 levels on the three frames: Lightroom spreads a roughly fixed average pull over whatever is bright. So strength = kHighsDownBudget / mean weight, capped at kHighsDownAmpMax for near-black frames, and raised by a positive Exposure: budget x (1 + kHighsDownBudgetPerEV x max(0, Exposure)). Current constants: budget 0.017 of the display range, per-EV 0.3, cap 0.60 (see the record below for how each moved).

Measured on the frame, not the buffer. The mean weight comes from the frame's statistics sample: WorkingImage::statSlot, a slot shared by every copy, proxy and crop through copyMetadata, holding a \~128 px INTER_AREA downscale of the whole frame (Develop::StatSample, filled once, lazily, under the slot's mutex). Develop::Apply develops that sample FIRST with the same params (so it is in exactly the state the image is in), takes the weight from it, REUSES its point coefficients (they depend on params, metadata and the weight, never otherwise on pixels), and hands the image a NEW slot holding the developed sample, so a mask scope developing from the Global result measures that result. The Detail 1:1 patch is a crop: cutDetailRoi calls Develop::StatSample(full) before copyMetadata, so the shared slot is filled from the full frame, never from the crop. The weight is binned on the perceptual axis (2048 bins), so the band is evaluated per bin, not per pixel: \~1 ms net per Apply. The Curves panel's Parametric plot has no frame and draws Highlights - at kHighsDown.amp (0.117, the strength for a mean weight of 0.30). Tested by tst_toneregions::highlightsAdaptsToTheFrame (the same ramp level takes at least twice the pull in a dark frame as in a bright one) and highlightsStatisticIsTheFrameNotTheCrop.

##### 11.8.4.2 Recovering a Push Past White

With a positive Exposure, Highlights -100 brings back everything the push blew (2026-10-10). The band cannot: it is placed on the DISPLAY axis, which clamps at white, so values pushed past the view's clip sit at d0 = 1, where its weight is zero (Exposure +3 on a ramp left the top 3 stops at 255 under Highlights -100, with the data intact in the point pass).

Highlights - with a positive Exposure therefore ALSO runs a scene-linear stage at the very start of applyToneShape: in x = log2(n), identity below a knee, then x' = knee + L(1 - exp(-(x - knee)/L)) (slope 1 at the knee, monotone). L is solved so the brightest value the push CAN have created (the view's clip point, display 0.998, times 2^Exposure) lands on display 0.98 (level 250) at -100, and halfway in stops at -50; a barely positive Exposure lands barely under the clip, so it is continuous. The knee sits at most 1 stop below the landing point (kRecoverKneeMax), so the stage only reshapes the shoulder and the band does the rest. Positions are carried back through the contrast slope, and the tone LUT's domain scales by 2^Exposure. It is params-only, so every render (proxy, full res, Detail patch, mask scope) draws the same curve, and so does the Parametric plot.

- Measured on the ramp (None view): Exposure +3 / Highlights -100 brings every blown sample back, ordered and distinct, top at 244; at +1.5 every tone up to level 235 renders at or above the unedited ramp (255 renders 244, under the landing point by design). The cost is a compressed top on big pushes: three stops land in roughly levels 220..244. Not fitted to Lightroom.
- Tested by tst_toneregions::highlightsRecoverAPushPastWhite and highlightsRecoveryDoesNotCompound.
- Limits: it reads THIS scope's Exposure, so a mask scope cannot recover the Global scope's push; it is per channel like the rest of the tone LUT; it assumes the original's top was at most the view's clip; sensor-clipped raw pixels come back in whatever colour the white balance made them (no highlight reconstruction).
- Two versions were rejected, both in-app on one ORF (Standard roll-off, Exposure +1.5). (1) MEASURING the frame's brightest value and compressing it under the clip: under Standard roll-off the visible blowout is the shoulder, the measured top was only 0.4 stops past the clip, and it differed by render (a Detail patch is a crop, a mask scope develops from the accumulator), giving different curves per render. (2) UNDOING THE PUSH in the highlights outright: the band then pulled the same tones again, the snow came out darker than the unedited frame (90th percentile 126 vs 162), its interquartile range fell from 44 to 9 and the frame went flat grey. Recovery must stop at "no longer blown", not "unexposed". (For reference, the band alone at Exposure +1.5 / Highlights -100 already took that frame from 5.5% of pixels at level 250+ to 0.16% and restored snow texture.)

##### 11.8.4.3 Local: the Highlights Field

A third Lightroom series (an OM-1 forest frame: a sunlit fern pool in dark woods, 2022-09-07_0019.orf) showed Lightroom pulling the pool MUCH harder than Winnow, and pulling it as a REGION (at Exposure +2.5 / -100 its 90th percentile fell 165 -> 92, Winnow's 168 -> 129). A map of Lightroom's per-pixel gain is one smooth, edge-aware blob covering the sunlit area, 1-1.5 stops deep, taking the dark gaps between fronds down with the bright fronds and stopping cleanly at the trunks, with no halo. The pixel's own level explained 41% of Lightroom's log gain there, and a guided filter on log luminance plus the pixel 85%. ("Close to 1-D within a frame" still holds for the high-key snow frame, which is why a per-pixel band matched it, and does not hold for a small bright region in a dark frame.)

The operator is a LOCAL LAPLACIAN FILTER (Paris, Hasinoff & Kautz 2011, in the fast form of Aubry et al. 2014; the method Lightroom's 2012 process tone controls are widely reported to rest on). It matches what was measured: regions compressed as wholes, fine contrast inside them kept or raised (Lightroom's -100 raised the sunlit area's fine-scale log contrast 0.26 -> 0.30), no halo at edges.

- The fitted band rides in its remapping function: at each pyramid level, a tone within kHighsLocalSigma (0.07 on the d0 axis) of the local reference g takes the band's shift AT g, so a region moves as a region and its texture rides along; a tone further from g takes its OWN shift, so an edge is per pixel and cannot halo.
- Develop::buildHiField runs it for luminance on the band's own axis (d0: after recovery, before contrast and the endpoint moves) over the frame's LocalSample, a \~1024 px INTER_AREA downscale held in the same per-frame slot as the StatSample (StatSampleSlot::local, Develop::LocalSample; cutDetailRoi fills it from the full image before cutting the patch), with kHighsLocalLevels = 12 reference tones in parallel (QtConcurrent) and each remap tabulated per reference. The filter is factored into localLaplacian() and guidedCoefficients().
- What it adds beyond the per-pixel band, correction = (result - I) - shift(I), is guided-upsampled (guide d0, radius 2 sample px): correction \~ a \* d0 + b locally, and the a, b grids go to applyPointOps as the HiField. Per pixel the fused pass reads a, b bilinearly (through WorkingImage::frameX.., so a crop reads the field in place), evaluates them on the pixel's own d0, and per channel adds that correction to the channel's own per-pixel shift (capped at 0: Highlights - never brightens), on the display axis: band-free display value (hiDispLut, by s) + own shift (hiShiftLut, by s) + correction, back through hiBackLut[ch] (display -> linear, Curves included).
- With no field (the StatSample's own develop, a crop whose slot has no LocalSample, a mask scope's patch), toneLut, which always holds the full per-pixel curve, is used.
- The filter runs on the 1024 px sample and is upsampled rather than run at the render's resolution, so the proxy and the settle render agree (pyramid levels are resolution-relative). That cost \~0.8 levels at half resolution and kept the halo term at -0.6.
- The band stays per channel. Lightroom's pull on the backlit moss is one equal display shift for all three channels (192/182/147 -> 108/98/63), and the per-channel band's unequal shifts tint that moss orange, but weighting the shift by luminance or by the max channel was worse on levels everywhere and no better on chroma overall.

Why not the guided filter (v4, built and pulled 2026-10-11): the first local version read a guided-filter base of log luminance on the 128 px StatSample grid and carried each channel's band position by region minus pixel. In-app it HALOED: bright fronds beside dark trunks were judged to sit in a darker region and left unpulled, a milky glow beside every trunk, which the RMS fit could not see. The prototype harness was given a HALO term (the mean pull on bright pixels 2-10 px at 1/4 resolution from dark objects, minus Lightroom's, against the same for bright pixels far from them) and scored: guided at 128 px +12.8 levels short near edges (far +3.8), at 512 px +10.2, at full resolution +9.1; local Laplacian -1.5 / -2.0 (sigma 0.10), +0.8 / +5.0 (sigma 0.07). Score halos, not just RMS. Two domain mistakes on the way: measuring the region in scene light carried pushed highlights below the band's peak (the brightest tones pulled least), and measuring it on the finished display value let Whites + flatten every clipped tone into one region.

##### 11.8.4.4 Frame-Relative and Range-Scaled

At Exposure 0 the forest frame is 81% near black, and Lightroom's -100 takes \~70% of the brightness off everything above level \~50, where the ILCE frame's same levels take far less: Lightroom compresses bright REGIONS RELATIVE TO THE FRAME, not display levels. Measured in log luminance against the frame's log-mean, -100 removes a fraction of each tone's distance above it (0.57 forest 0, 0.45 forest +2.5, 0.32 ILCE 0, 0.36 snow 0, 0.25 ILCE +1.5, 0.23 snow +1.5), tapering toward white.

Ten more Lightroom pairs at Exposure 0 (Highlights 0 / -100: a seascape, two portraits, a beach, a backyard sunset, two forests, two lagoon birds, a frame with the sun in it) gave the system identification: one shared shape times a per-frame strength still fits, but the strength runs 0.4 (snow +1.5) to 3.2 (the sunset band over a dark field), and its best single predictor is the frame's RANGE, p99 minus log-mean in stops (R2 0.72 of log strength; log-mean alone 0.67, p99 0.17). Lightroom also darkens a high-range frame AS A WHOLE: at the anchor itself -1.2 stops on the forest at 0 and -2.6 on the sunset, \~-0.2 on snow and portraits. Normalising the tone axis by the range did not collapse the curves any better than scaling the strength.

What ships: a gain 2^-(term) in display-linear light, with term = amount^1.5 \* e^(0.35 \* (range - 4.5)) \* (0.16 \* (L - anchor)^1.125 + 0.30), the 0.30 being the whole-frame part; L = log2 display-linear luminance of the band-free DISPLAY value; anchor = the frame's log-mean of it and range = p99 - anchor, both read from the StatSample's lumBins histogram (kHighsAnchorO / kHighsAnchorRangeB / kHighsAnchorRange0); tapered to nothing between display 0.93 and white. It is carried by region through a second local Laplacian on L (region split 1.9 stops; Develop::buildHiField's second pass, HiField::ga/gb, PointCoeffs::hiLogLumLut / hiDropByL), with the per-pixel table hiGainByS as the no-field fallback.

Cost (debug, 3000 x 2000, Exposure +1, Highlights -100): the first field \~40 ms (the LocalSample is filled once per frame; the filter re-runs per Apply because it depends on the params), the fused pass \~70 ms against \~2 ms for a gain-only pass (one extra pow per pixel plus four table reads per channel); the second local Laplacian adds \~0.14 s to a 20 MP debug render. Release should be several times faster; not yet measured in-app.

##### 11.8.4.5 Status and Open Questions

Through the real pipeline, nineteen Lightroom pairs: mean RMS 4.76 levels of 255 (forest 0 3.4 with its bright bands within +3 levels; forest +2.5 8.3; snow 0 5.2; snow +1.5 3.2; sunset 7.2), at a cost on a few low-range frames (ILCE +1.5 7.1, the seascape 3.5: it over-pulls flat low-range frames a little). All tst_toneregions cases pass; a region split of 2.2+ scored \~0.03 better but haloed a pool edge by 2 levels (highlightsPullsTheRegion).

Still open, the user's case: the forest at +2.5. Lightroom compresses that frame almost evenly (baseline 75 -> 63, 150 -> 92, 200 -> 114, 225 -> 133); Winnow pulls 75 -> 58 but 200 -> 127 and 225 -> 150, so the sunlit ferns stay visibly brighter. Ruled out: the taper (starting it at 0.99 moved the frame 8.33 -> 8.10) and the per-EV budget (0.6 fixed the top bands but over-pulled the mids elsewhere). Measured against an existing test: Lightroom's push + -100 renders the forest's bright tones 30-50 levels DARKER than its unpushed, unedited render (68% of level 100-235 pixels), while on snow it never does, so tst_toneregions::highlightsRecoveryDoesNotCompound holds for low-range frames only; it is what fails first when the taper starts later than 0.93. The next data that would pin the push dependence: the forest at Exposure +1 and +2 with Highlights 0 / -100.

##### 11.8.4.6 Calibration Record

- 2026-09-17: the fixed band, fitted on one ILCE-1 frame.
- 2026-10-10: the budget-based strength (kHighsDownBudget 0.035, cap 0.35); one shared budget predicted all five snow/ILCE curves at 0.75-3.3 levels RMS (fixed band 2.0-35.3), 1.5-4.8 with each frame held out.
- 2026-10-11 (v5): the local Laplacian. Numbers (levels RMS; forest +2.5/-100, forest -50, snow +1.5/-100, snow 0/-100, ILCE -100): per-pixel band with a 0.2 push term 15.3 / 5.5 / 3.5 / 5.4 / 4.3; local Laplacian sigma 0.07, 12 levels, push term 0.1: 11.2 / 4.7 / 3.2 / 5.2 / 4.0. The v4 guided-filter numbers recorded at the time are superseded.
- 2026-10-11, the strength refit through the real pipeline (eight Lightroom-matched renders scored with developrender, each app's pull against its OWN Highlights 0 render, plus the halo term): only 0.65% of the forest is past white at +2.5, so the gap was mostly the band's strength on tones just below white, not recovery. Lightroom's mean pull at -100 is 8.3 / 9.9 / 11.8 / 9.9 levels on ILCE 0 / ILCE +1.5 / snow 0 / snow +1.5 and 18.9 on the forest, the outlier, and since ILCE +1.5 is pushed too, the push does not explain it: it is the only very high-contrast scene. A plateau above the band's peak and a steeper slider exponent together bought 0.04 and were not kept. Push 0.3 / cap 0.60 shipped: mean RMS 5.85 (v5 6.26).
- 2026-10-11, the frame-relative term: the real pipeline had scored the band 12.2 on forest 0 where the Python model scored 7.9, because the local field was SUBTRACTING \~10 levels everywhere (in a sparse pool of bright fronds on dark ground the local reference sits low). Shipped the band (budget 0.035 -> 0.020) plus a frame-relative gain with exponent 1.5 and split 1.0 stop: mean RMS 6.56 -> 6.26. Tried and dropped: the anchor curve only for what a region adds beyond the pixel (6.82); the term per pixel (6.31, but it compressed texture by a third and inverted the Whites +100 ramp by a level, caught by tst_toneregions); pull left at white or a taper from 0.8 (up to 0.2 better on RMS, but -50 then cleared every pushed sample where Lightroom leaves part blown, and the white and no-compounding tests failed).
- 2026-10-11, the range scaling (the formula above; split 1.0 -> 1.9; budget 0.020 -> 0.017): 6.02 -> 4.76 on the re-registered baseline. The harness had to be fixed FIRST: Lightroom applies the lens profile's distortion correction, which integer-offset alignment cannot match (edge correlation \~0 on seven of nineteen pairs, so every earlier score on them carried registration error). lrcompare.py now registers by ECC homography plus a Gaussian-smoothed DIS optical flow (edge correlation 0.64-0.97 on all pairs), cached per pair in .lrcompare_cache.

#### 11.8.5 The Calibration Loop

Pixels Exposure pushes past white cannot be studied from any 8/16-bit export, since both apps' renders clip them. So a Develop export can also write the image it develops as unclipped scene-linear float:

- WINNOW_DUMP_WORKING=&lt;folder>, then export: dumpWorkingForCalibration (mainwindow.cpp, file-local) writes &lt;folder>/&lt;base>.wkg, the working-space image with its white balance applied, before exposure and every edit, plus white, sceneReferred and the orientation in degrees (format in the function's comment).
- `Winnow --dumpworking <raw> <out.wkg>` (main.cpp, runDumpWorking) does the same headlessly: offscreen, no catalog or settings, before the single-instance check so it runs beside an open Winnow, with the in-house raw decoder (RawFormat::Decode, as decodeRawWorking), converting with the as-shot white balance.
- tests/unit/developrender.cpp (target developrender, built with the tests) renders a .wkg through Develop::Apply + OutputTransform::ToImage16 with any recipe (a Winnow sidecar / EditStack JSON, global scope only, masks, geometry and fills ignored with a warning; or a bare params object), plus key=value overrides by the PUBLISHED sidecar keys (EditStack::paramsToJson), and writes a rotated 16-bit TIFF. Exact for a profile with no look (Winnow Standard); a camera profile's OutputLook is not carried. It reproduced the app's own exports exactly (Highlights 0 identical, -100 within 0.1 level mean).
- tests/calibration/lrcompare.py drives cases from tests/calibration/cases.json (raw, Winnow baseline/target recipes, the Lightroom pair): makes missing dumps, renders, registers, and scores each app's pull against its own baseline, with optional halo / bright-band terms and a crop sheet.
- The format lives in one header, Develop/workingdump.h, shared by the export hook, the headless mode and developrender.
- What the user still owns: the Lightroom exports (in \~/Pictures/\_LRref), and the final in-app look (the tool skips lens correction, masks, geometry, spot fills and raw denoise).

#### 11.8.6 Tests

tst_toneregions (16 cases), including:

- highlightsPullsTheRegion: on a dark frame holding a bright pool of low-contrast checker, the checker keeps at least a level more contrast than under the per-pixel band (the same frame rendered as a crop of an unfilled local slot, which is the per-pixel fallback); a pool pixel 2 px inside the edge is pulled within a level of the pool's centre; dark background 3 px outside within a level of background far away. (Its v4 form demanded that a single-pixel 0.6 dot inside a 0.85 pool be pulled like the pool; a local Laplacian rightly treats that contrast as an edge, so that test pinned the guided filter's behaviour, not Lightroom's.)
- highlightsAdaptsToTheFrame: the same ramp level takes at least twice the pull in a dark frame as in a bright one.
- highlightsStatisticIsTheFrameNotTheCrop: a crop sharing the frame's sample renders within 1 level of the full frame; the control crop measuring itself differs, so the test can see the bug. It fills the LocalSample before cutting its crop, as cutDetailRoi does.
- highlightsDoNotDragTheWhitePoint measures white in a flat white tail after the ramp.
- highlightsDevelopsOnAPoolThread develops the local-Highlights path on the global pool (see [11.41.1 A Stack Overflow on a Pool Thread](#11411-a-stack-overflow-on-a-pool-thread)).
- shadowsIsAGainNotAnOffset, highlightsRecoverAPushPastWhite, highlightsRecoveryDoesNotCompound, regionsDoNotSlideWithContrast.

### 11.9 Panel Focus and Slider Arrow-Nudge

The Develop dock is a PropertyEditor (QTreeView) whose value cells are persistent editor widgets (SliderEditor -> Slider). Global image navigation (Left/Right = previous/next image) is handled in MW::eventFilter. What disambiguates "navigate images" from "nudge this slider" is Qt keyboard focus:

- Slider has StrongFocus and takes focus on click (Slider::mousePressEvent). SliderEditor sets setFocusProxy(slider), so a click or Tab into the row lands focus on the slider.
- Slider::keyPressEvent nudges on Left/Right (and Up/Down; PageUp/PageDown take the larger step) and ACCEPTS the key. Accepting matters: MW's arrow handler is an APPLICATION event filter, and application filters run once per object as an UNconsumed key propagates up the parent chain, so an arrow the slider did not accept reaches MW::eventFilter with obj == "MWWindow" and moves the selection. (QAbstractSlider's own stepping was not enough in practice, hence the explicit override.)
- Belt and braces: MW::eventFilter's Left/Right navigation is a no-op when QApplication::focusWidget() is a value editor (QAbstractSlider / QAbstractSpinBox / QLineEdit / QComboBox). When focus leaves the panel, arrows navigate images again.

The focus cue (which slider owns the arrows): SliderEditor::paintEvent fills the VALUE cell with a subtle translucent blue when slider->hasFocus(), and the delegate fills the CAPTION cell with the same blue (when the value sibling is DT_Slider and SliderEditor::sliderHasFocus()), so the focused row reads as one blue band. Slider::focusInEvent / focusOutEvent -> syncFocusRepaint() repaints the SliderEditor AND its parent viewport (so the delegate re-tints the caption). Generic to every PropertyEditor slider (Develop, Embellish, Preferences).

Caption click (Develop): clicking a slider row's CAPTION (column 0) is intercepted in DevelopProperties::mousePressEvent. It:

1. focuses that slider via SliderEditor::focusSlider, so the arrow keys nudge it without first clicking the track;
2. hides the mask overlay (maskTintHideRequested) so the effect shows, EXCEPT for a mask-setting slider (a child of a mask tool, e.g. Feather/Hue), which keeps the overlay since you are editing the mask;
3. FLASHES the caption white, fading to 0 over \~0.45 s. The flash is a generic PropertyEditor mechanism: DevelopProperties::flashCaption animates the caption's UR_FlashLevel role (0..1) with a QVariantAnimation, and PropertyDelegate blends the caption text toward white by that amount.

A caption DOUBLE-click resets the slider to its default (base PropertyEditor) and then re-focuses the slider (DevelopProperties::mouseDoubleClickEvent); otherwise Qt's click focus moves to the tree and the row loses its blue cue.

Not done: a panel-LEVEL active-border cue across all docks (DockWidget has not solved drawing a border around a QDockWidget); the control-level cue already shows where slider keys land.

### 11.10 Develop Diagnostics

Help > Diagnostics > Develop diagnostics (MW::developDiagnostics, wired in menusandactions.cpp as diagnosticsDevelopAction via MW::diagnosticsDevelop) dumps, in one read-only snapshot, everything the Develop pipeline depends on for the selected image:

- the operation-mode / raw-engine globals (G::operationMode, G::useRaw, G::decodeRawEngine) and the image's resolved raw renderer;
- the current file (raw?, video?, ISO, camera model, and the devPreview cache payload for it);
- the cached scene-linear WorkingImage base (dims, sceneReferred, white, MB). This is the first thing to check: a sceneReferred=false base, or dims that differ from the sensor active area, means Develop is editing the display-referred embedded JPG, not the sensor image;
- the rawInfo (active area, bits, compression, CFA, black/white, matrix);
- the effective EditParams for the Global scope and each enabled non-Global scope (+ mask counts), and the crop/warp Geometry;
- the interactive develop caches (the PMRID "Denoise raw" base and keys, developWorkTriedPath / in-flight guards, proxy and full-res render state, mask reference caches).

The DENOISE section reports the PMRID (k,b) noise-model resolution FOR THE CURRENT IMAGE: the tier that fired (DNG NoiseProfile / model table / blind / generic), the resolved k,b, and whether the file carried a DNG NoiseProfile. It is the first thing to check if a file denoises wrong (source=generic on a Nikon means its modelMatch missed). The snapshot (developPmridResSource/K/B/HadNP) is captured in ensureRawDenoise on a PMRID decode and keyed to developPmridKey, so it is never stale: it shows only while developPmridFull is this image's base, else "(no current PMRID base)". PMRID::LastResolution() is the worker-side hand-off it is captured from.

The DENOISE section ends with two TIMING lines for the most recent denoise of the session (any image; the file name is in the line):

- RawFormat::LastDenoiseTiming(): unpack, black, clean demosaic/colour, mosaic copy, PMRID, denoised demosaic/colour, blend, total ("interactive" = the full-strength ensureRawDenoise pass; "saved edit" = a display/export decode carrying a Denoise raw recipe).
- That decode's own PMRID::Timing, passed out of PMRID::Apply per call, NOT read from PMRID::LastTiming() (a Develop denoise and an ImageCache saved-edit decode can run PMRID at the same time and would overwrite each other): backend, kb resolve, pack, per-tile input build / model Run / merge sums, first/min/max/mean Run, tile count and padded tile shape, unpack, and the one-time session load.

They are NOT printed to the console (the per-decode qInfo lines, ensureRawDenoise's "Denoise raw job" line and the PMRID warm-up line were removed 2026-10-13), so this dump is the one place to read them. It is the probe for making denoised renders faster: read it before changing the model export or the tiler.

The report ENDS with "Folders with cached devPreviews": the cache dir, the total preview count / bytes against the LRU cap, and one row per folder holding on-disk devPreviews (count, live count, MB), from DevPreviewCache::folderStats(). It describes the cache rather than the image, so it is appended even when nothing is selected. live &lt; count means those sources were missing at the last sweep (deleted, or on an unmounted volume; the sweep cannot tell the two apart, so it demotes rather than deletes).

#### 11.10.1 Render Verification

Two axes, so the two failure modes seen (an edit silently dropped; the demosaic not triggered) are each caught. Both are sub-millisecond and stored on MW (developVerify\* / developVerifyVsPreview\*):

- [A] The Develop DISPLAY vs the Preview (embedded) image. The Preview image is captured (downscaled) on entering Develop (MW::setOperationMode, before the re-decode); each develop display, edited or not, is grid-sampled against it in MW::updateDevelopScopes. maxAbs > 0 confirms the decode change (demosaic) and/or edits took effect; maxAbs == 0 on a raw in Edit=Raw means the demosaic did NOT apply (the display is still the embedded preview). Populates for an unedited image on mode entry.
- [B] The recipe vs the un-developed base. On each full-res settle the worker renders the CLEAN base with identity params vs the actual base (including raw denoise) with the recipe at \~256 px (geometry suppressed so sizes match). maxAbs == 0 with a non-identity recipe is a dropped edit (the "denoise does nothing" class). Populates only on edited settle renders.

#### 11.10.2 Entering Develop Must Re-decode

ImageDecoder::load() picks the decode by (G::operationMode == Develop && G::useRaw): Preview shows the embedded preview, Develop demosaics the raw, so switching mode changes the decode even when useRaw does not flip. setOperationMode drives the re-decode via toggleUseRaw WHEN useRaw changes; if useRaw already matched the target (left true from a prior session), toggleUseRaw was skipped and NOTHING re-decoded, so the loupe kept showing the embedded image until the user toggled the Edit-source selector. The useRaw-unchanged branch now also sets imageView->currentImageHasChanged and emits imageCacheColorManageChange() (-> reloadImageCache -> refreshViewsOnCacheChange -> loupe), matching the toggleUseRaw refresh.

### 11.11 The Adjustments

How each op is implemented; the tone controls have their own section ([11.8 The Tone Controls](#118-the-tone-controls)), and so do white balance, curves, calibrate, colour grade and point colour.

#### 11.11.1 Point Ops

All per-pixel, fused into one pass (Develop::buildPointCoeffs + applyPointOps):

- White balance and exposure are linear multiplies, so buildPointCoeffs folds them, the input profile and the Colour RGB gains into one matrix (PointCoeffs::preMat). Exposure = a 2^EV scene-linear gain. White balance is ABSOLUTE (Kelvin + tint); see [11.27 White Balance (Absolute, Kelvin)](#1127-white-balance-absolute-kelvin).
- The tone curve (contrast + the four tone controls + the Curves panel's curves) is a pure 1-D function of a channel's white-normalised value, applied in a PERCEPTUAL (\~gamma 2.2) domain, NOT scene-linear: a linear-space curve about 0.18 explodes highlights, which sit several stops above the pivot, while encoding to gamma first puts mid-grey near 0.46 so tones shape evenly. buildPointCoeffs BAKES the whole chain into a per-render LUT (PointCoeffs::toneLut, indexed by s = (v/white)^(1/gamma), returning white-normalised linear), so the hot loop does ONE encode pow + one interpolated lookup per channel. The LUT spans \~3 stops above white (kToneLutMaxN) so highlight headroom is shaped, not clipped.
- Contrast = a gentle slope (1 + 0.4\*amount, [0.6, 1.4]) about mid-grey. The -100..100 slider is NORMALISED to amount -1..1 (without that the first slider unit already hits the extreme).
- Colour RGB (red / green / blue, -100..100) are per-channel scene-linear gains folded into the matrix (kRgbGain 0.5: full slider = +/-50% on a channel).
- Colour HSL (hue / saturation / vibrance / luminance, -100..100, under the Color header; vibrance and saturation also at the bottom of Basic) is a cross-channel block applied AFTER the tone curve (it mixes channels, so it cannot be a per-channel LUT). Hue = a Rodrigues rotation about the neutral (1,1,1) axis, so greys stay grey (kHueMaxRad = 60 deg at full); saturation = a chroma scale about the working space's luma (-100 -> grey, +100 -> 2x); vibrance = the same chroma scale weighted per pixel by (1 - HSV saturation), so muted pixels move more than already-saturated ones (protecting skies and skin from clipping); luminance = a uniform gain (-100 -> black, +100 -> 2x). hslActive gates the block, so identity sliders leave the pass untouched.

#### 11.11.2 Spatial Ops

Texture (#6), Clarity (#6.5), Dehaze (#7), Vignette (#8), Sharpen (#8.5), Grain (#9) and local Denoise run AFTER the fused point pass, each owning a full-image pass. They need a neighbourhood (or, for Vignette and Grain, pixel coordinates / a noise field). Every one except Sharpen scales its radius to the image's LONG EDGE, so the screen-resolution proxy and the full-res settle render shape the same relative band. Their cost lands on the settle render; the proxy filters \~3 MP.

One operation at four radii, the local-contrast family. Texture, Clarity and Dehaze's first stage are the SAME band operation (split a frequency band off a blurred base and scale it), differing only in radius and weighting; Sharpen is the same shape at \~1 px. On an 8640 px edge:

```
Sharpen  ~1px ABSOLUTE     edge-gated            acutance
Texture  0.0015 x edge     ungated               fine detail contrast
Clarity  0.007  x edge     midtone + halo        midtone punch / glow
Dehaze   0.02   x edge     ungated (+ pivot)     atmospheric veiling
```

An order of magnitude apart, so they STACK rather than compete. The scalar maths is header-only in Develop/localcontrast.h (applyBand / bandFactor / midtoneWeight / haloGuard); the shared perceptual-luma prep and ratio fold-back are develop.cpp's buildPerceptualLuma + shapeAndFoldLuma, TEMPLATED on the shape functor on purpose, so it inlines and each op still costs ONE parallel pass and no extra buffer. gaussianBase carries Texture's downscale-blur-upscale trick and is shared with Clarity; Dehaze keeps a box blur (at its far larger radius a running-sum blur is cheaper still). Grain borrows only midtoneWeight.

- Texture: mid-frequency local contrast, ratio-preserving on LUMINANCE (chroma untouched). A Gaussian base (kTextureSigmaFrac \~0.0015 x edge) splits a detail band that + amplifies (kTextureGain) and - smooths.
- Clarity is what stops the ladder having a 13x gap in the middle, and is more than "Texture with a bigger radius": the band is weighted by midtoneWeight (so it cannot crush blacks or flatten highlights) and rolled off by haloGuard where the high-pass excursion is large (strong edges, where a band this wide rings). The weights multiply the AMOUNT, not the result, so they only pull the band factor toward 1 and can never invert or overshoot. Measured on an M4 at 49.8 MP: clarity 61 ms, texture 83 ms, dehaze 141 ms.
- Dehaze is an APPROXIMATION, not the dark-channel prior (a user choice): a large-radius local-contrast boost (a box blur, kDehazeSigmaFrac \~0.02 x edge) + a contrast pull about a low pivot (kDehazePivot 0.3, deepening shadows) + a saturation lift (kDehazeSat); + clears haze, - adds it. Ratio-preserving on luminance.
- Vignette: a radial exposure falloff about the centre. mask = pow(rn, k), rn the elliptical radius (0 centre, 1 corner), k from the Feather slider (high feather -> low k -> gradual, reaching inward; low feather -> corner-hugging); corner gain = 2^Exposure (- darkens, + brightens), scaled by the mask. Off-centre or shaped vignettes use radial masks, so this global op is just Exposure + Feather.
- Grain: monochromatic film grain added to perceptual luminance (ratio-preserving): a fixed-seed noise field on a coarse grain-cell grid (Size sets the cell, scaled to the long edge so the proxy and full res match) is bilinearly upsampled, its amplitude modulated by a lower-frequency Roughness field (0 uniform, 1 patchy), weighted toward the midtones (fading to 0 at black/white) and scaled by Amount. The fixed seed keeps the pattern stable across re-renders (no shimmer).
- Local Denoise (Detail "Denoise", key "localDenoise"): two 0..100 sliders (mapped to 0..1) into Develop::Denoise. "Denoise" (localDenoiseLuma) = luminance NR via a perceptual bilateral (ratio-preserving: rgb' = rgb \* (Yd/Y), so only luminance changes); "Denoise Color" (localDenoiseChroma) = chroma NR via a downscaled opponent-chroma (R-Y, B-Y) blur that keeps luma exact. Luma runs first, then chroma. It is a maskable Develop op on the already-decoded WorkingImage, so it needs no second decode and is independent of the decode engine: a portable OpenCV pass on both platforms. It is distinct from the global, decode-time "Denoise raw" ([11.17 Raw Denoise](#1117-raw-denoise)).

The refactor that extracted the shared kernel rewrote three ops that already shape saved recipes, so tests/unit/tst_localcontrast.cpp is a CHARACTERIZATION test whose golden values were captured from the build immediately BEFORE the extraction. Texture, Sharpen and Grain came out bit-identical; Dehaze was re-expressed from yp + k\*(yp-base) to base + (1+k)\*(yp-base) (equal in exact arithmetic) and measured at most 6e-7 different over a full frame (25x below a 16-bit quantum). If one of those tests fails, a saved recipe now renders differently; do not re-bless the numbers without proving the change is intended.

#### 11.11.3 Sharpen

Sharpen is the ONE SCALE-DEPENDENT op. Acutance is a property of the PIXEL GRID, so sharpenRadius is an ABSOLUTE pixel radius (0.5..3 px at full res). WorkingImage::renderScale carries this render's long edge as a fraction of the full-res long edge (set in WorkingImageCache::downscaled, carried through assignReusing), and Sharpen::effectiveSigma multiplies the radius by it: the drag proxy shows a scale-honest approximation, the settle render shows the truth, and the panel tells the user to judge at 1:1. renderScale is deliberately NOT an EditParams field: EditParams is both the sidecar format and the per-scope render-cache key, so a render detail there would persist to every sidecar and make the proxy and settle renders miss each other's cache entries.

- The op is an unsharp mask on perceptual luminance, ratio-preserving like Texture: a small Gaussian base gives hp = yp - base, which Detail soft-thresholds (suppressing the smallest amplitudes as noise, sign preserved) and Masking gates by the gradient magnitude of the BLURRED luma (so noise does not read as an edge).
- The Masking knee is a CURVE (Sharpen::maskKnee, knee = m\*(0.10 + 0.40\*m^2), recalibrated 2026-08-21): a linear ramp topped out at 0.10/px, which still passed ordinary texture (\~0.05/px) at half strength, so the top of the slider could not quiet a noisy sky. It is linear at the bottom and cubic at the top, so the last third of the travel is where strong protection lives. The stored key and its 0..1 range are unchanged, but a sharpenMasking written before this protects more above the middle. The remaining limiter is the (1 - m) blend in edgeGate, which keeps flat areas at (1 - m) of full sharpening so intermediate settings soften rather than switch.
- Scalar maths is header-only in Develop/sharpen.h (tests/unit/tst_sharpen.cpp); develop.cpp owns only the OpenCV blur / Sobel and the parallelFor. The Sobel pair is skipped entirely at Masking 0.
- Placed after Vignette (darkened corners are not detail-boosted) and before Grain (grain is never itself sharpened). Distinct from Texture, which is resolution-proportional (\~13 px on an 8640 px edge) and ungated, so the two occupy disjoint bands.

Seeing the mask (Opt + drag Masking), Lightroom's Alt-drag: holding Opt while DRAGGING the Detail panel's Masking slider replaces the photo with the gate itself in GREYSCALE (white sharpened, black protected, greys the soft roll-off). It is momentary in two inputs (Opt down AND the slider's handle held), so releasing either, or the app deactivating, brings the photo back; the drag gate, rather than mere row focus, is what lets the preview be this loud.

- It is built from the DEVELOPED FRAME ON SCREEN (MW::updateSharpenMaskPreview keeps a copy in developFrame as each render is applied), NOT from inside the pipeline, where the true gate lives several stages deep in a worker-thread stack render. The same blur + 1/8-Sobel + Sharpen::edgeGate over that frame's luma reproduces the gate closely enough to set the slider by, and it is always in step with what is on screen. Two approximations, neither material: the frame carries sharpening (and grain) the real gate is measured before, and its perceptual luma is sRGB-encoded grey rather than the pipeline's own encode.
- It is the one Develop overlay that is NOT in mask space: its source is the displayed frame, already post-geometry and oriented, so ImageView (setSharpenMaskImage / drawForeground) stretches it straight over the pixmap. Putting it through maskNormToItem would put it in the wrong place on a cropped image.
- Wiring: DevelopProperties::sharpenMaskPreviewActive (live Opt state + SliderEditor::sliderIsDown) -> syncSharpenMaskPreview, called from MW's event filter on each Opt edge and, QUEUED, on each mouse press/release (the slider sets isSliderDown in its own handler, so reading it inline would be one event stale), and on app activate/deactivate -> sharpenMaskPreviewChanged -> MW::updateSharpenMaskPreview, which also re-runs after every applied render so the mask follows the drag.

#### 11.11.4 The Panel Sections and Their Ranges

Each scope maps onto one EditParams (DevelopProperties::editParams()); the sections are built with PropertyEditor::addItem. Every slider defaults to identity.

- Basic: Profile (a combo: the built-in "Winnow Standard", the synthesised "Camera Base", and every DNG camera profile installed for THIS camera), Tone mapping (a combo), WB (dropper + preset dropdown), Temp, Tint, Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance, Saturation. Integer -100..100 except Exposure (EV, -5.00..5.00), Temp (KELVIN, 2000..50000, log ramp) and Tint (-150..150). Vibrance and Saturation sit at the bottom of Basic (Lightroom's Presence group) and belong to EditParams::Group::Basic for Reset / Show changes; the pipeline is unchanged (they still run in the post-tone-curve HSL block), and their preset keys "vibrance" / "saturation" are unchanged.
- Color: Red, Green, Blue (per-channel gain); Hue, Luminance. Integer -100..100.
- Detail: Sharpening (sharpenAmount, 0..150 -> 0..1.5, default 0), Radius (sharpenRadius, 50..300 -> 0.50..3.00 PIXELS at full res, default 1.0), Detail (sharpenDetail, 0..100 -> 0..1, default 25), Masking (sharpenMasking, 0..100 -> 0..1, default 0). Radius / Detail / Masking are inert until Amount is non-zero. Also Denoise (localDenoiseLuma) and Denoise Color (localDenoiseChroma), 0..100 -> 0..1, default 0. The denoise pair MOVED here from Effects (2026-08-20): NR and sharpening are one decision, so they share a panel as in Lightroom.
- Effects: Vignette (vignetteExposure, EV -5.00..5.00, default 0) + Feather (vignetteFeather, 0..100 -> 0..1, default 50); Grain (grainAmount, 0..100 -> 0..1, default 0) + Size (grainSize, default 25) + Roughness (grainRoughness, default 50); size and roughness are inert until the amount is non-zero. The section opens with an effect dropdown (the "effectsChoice" spanned row, the Curves mode-row idiom, added 2026-10-20): only the chosen effect's rows are shown (DevelopProperties::applyEffectsChoice, setRowHidden over the effectDefs() table, which pairs each item with its row keys); the others stay in the model, so populate, presets and resets still reach them, and every effect renders whichever is shown. The choice is UI state, persisted in QSettings "Develop/effectsChoice" (effectsChoice). updateSectionHeaderCaptions puts " *" on the item of any effect off its defaults (effectEdited), like the combined Color panel's mode radios. Layout (2026-10-20): the combo row has no left inset, so it lines up with the slider captions, and every effect's rows are flush at that indent (no "   " sub-control captions); each effect's first slider is captioned "Amount" (vignetteExposure, grainAmount), and itemChange's kEffectsHistory gives History the full names ("Vignette", "Grain size", ...). Per-effect [eye] [reset] (2026-10-20) at the right of the dropdown row, laid out like BarBtnEditor (G::headerBtnGap, G::headerBtnRightInset) so they sit under the Effects header's [eye] [:]; both act on shownEffect() only. The eye toggles EditScope::showVignette / showGrain / showKaleido (default true, written to the sidecar only when false, carried by sameScopeState / copyScopeState, cleared by Reset all), INSIDE showEffects: effectiveScopeParams folds vignette / grain fields to their defaults, and effectiveScopeParams folds the kaleidoscope too (segments to 0; kaleidoToolWanted reads the same eyes, so the handles go). History "Hide Vignette" / "Show Grain". The reset (resetEffect) restores that effect's values only and leaves its eye; for the kaleidoscope it restores all five fields. The third entry, Kaleidoscope, is per scope like the others (EditParams kaleido*, Group::Effects), but a GEOMETRIC op folded after the crop, not by Develop::Apply; on a mask scope only the masked pixels are folded (see [11.22.8 Kaleidoscope](#11228-kaleidoscope)). A new effect = a row in effectDefs(), a case in effectEdited, and its addSlider calls in addEffects.
- Lens (Global scope only): see [11.24 Lens Profile (lensfun)](#1124-lens-profile-lensfun) and [11.23 Lens Corrections (Chromatic Aberration and Defringe)](#1123-lens-corrections-chromatic-aberration-and-defringe).
- Curves, Point Color, Calibrate and Color Grade have their own sections below.

### 11.12 Develop Performance

Develop is optimised aggressively: an interactive drag must stay well inside a frame on a 50-60 MP raw. The architecture that achieves it, then the rules every new op must follow. How each piece was found is in [11.41.2 Develop Render Latency (the Measurement Record)](#11412-develop-render-latency-the-measurement-record).

#### 11.12.1 Ops Are Split by Cost, and the Cheap Ones Are Fused

The masking model (one edit set per scope, combined masks as an alpha), rather than a Photoshop-style pixel-layer stack, is what keeps Develop fast.

- POINT ops (white balance, exposure, contrast, the tone regions, the tone curve, Colour RGB + HSL, point colour, colour grading) are pure per-pixel functions. All of a scope's point ops run in a SINGLE fused pass over the image (Develop::buildPointCoeffs + applyPointOps): one read, one write, no intermediate buffers. This is the slider-drag hot path.
- SPATIAL ops (denoise, texture, clarity, dehaze, vignette, sharpen, grain) need a neighbourhood (or, for vignette and grain, pixel coordinates / a noise field), so each owns a full-image pass after the point pass. They recompute every full-res render because they run AFTER the point pass (an exposure change alters their input); an untouched op early-returns at 0.
- Masks store GEOMETRY, never bitmaps: parametric masks (linear / radial) are evaluated analytically; brush masks are stored as the stroke list the user painted and rasterised to a cached alpha on load and after each edit (a tiny, resolution-independent sidecar). A scope's combined alpha is rasterised once and cached, recomputed only when mask geometry changes, never when sliders move.

Threading: the fused point pass is data-parallel WITHIN one render (row tiles), NOT spread across the ImageDecoder pool. The decoder pool is task-parallel ACROSS images (one decoder per image); an interactive edit is a SINGLE image, so only splitting its rows uses all cores. It is QtConcurrent::run over the global QThreadPool (the idiom FocusStack uses), not cv::parallel_for\_. The global pool is fixed-size, so a background decoder that also renders shares it and oversubscription is bounded. Rows split into &lt;= maxThreads chunks of >= 64 rows; small images run flat. The file-local parallelFor() in develop.cpp wraps it.

#### 11.12.2 The Two Renders

Every parameter change goes DevelopProperties::paramsChanged -> MW::developParamsChange -> MW::renderDevelopPreview. developParamsChange does no rendering itself:

- THE PROXY (interactive). A 0 ms single-shot (developProxyRenderTimer) collapses a burst of ticks into one proxy render. The proxy is a screen-resolution WorkingImage (WorkingImageCache::downscaled, INTER_AREA in scene-linear, \~1.5x the loupe viewport, cached per path in MW::developProxy), with raw orientation applied while it is still small: \~6-20x less pixel work per tick. renderDevelopPreview does only what MUST happen on the GUI thread (orientation, which reads dm->sf; ImageView::ensureAutoGuide, which reads the loupe pixmap; the ensure\*Mask builders; the proxy build), then hands the composite to developProxyPool, a DEDICATED 1-thread pool (not developRenderPool, where a settle render would block every tick behind it). The worker captures the source as a shared_ptr and the job/path by value.
- THE SETTLE (full resolution). developFullResTimer (\~160 ms, re-armed by every tick) runs MW::renderDevelopFullResAsync once the slider stops, on its own 1-thread pool (developRenderPool), and marshals the result back via QMetaObject::invokeMethod -> MW::onDevelopFullResReady.

Their guards:

- developParamsGen is bumped on every paramsChange; a settle render whose captured gen differs (or whose path is no longer current) is discarded, and onDevelopFullResReady re-arms the settle timer so the latest value still gets a crisp render.
- The settle job also carries the geometry it rendered (appliedGeom), and onDevelopFullResReady requires sameDevelopGeometry(appliedGeom, developRenderGeometry()), re-arming when it fails. Crop / warp / level commits re-render WITHOUT bumping developParamsGen, so a settle launched with the crop suppressed and landing after the commit used to paint the UNCROPPED frame over the cropped proxy (2026-09-30).
- developFullResInFlight and developProxyInFlight allow one render of each at a time. developProxyPending makes the proxy CORRECT rather than merely serialised: a request arriving mid-flight is remembered and re-armed on completion (relying on developParamsGen would lose the crop / warp / level callers).
- Superseded proxy frames ARE shown: they are tens of ms old and arrive in order, and discarding them (6 of 7 ticks, `applied 0`) meant the loupe did not update until the user paused. developProxyGeomGen bumps only when the geometry actually moves and discards exactly the case that must not flash: the crop tool alternating geometry-applied and geometry-suppressed renders.
- Orientation is computed on the GUI thread (MW::developOrientationDegrees) before launch; the worker touches only the const WorkingImage (held by a shared_ptr) and value-copied params. Compositing (render + rotate) is shared by both paths via developComposite().
- Still on the GUI thread, deliberately: the one-off proxy build (\~34 ms per image), the ensure\*Mask inference (200-400 ms, once per image), and updateMaskOverlayTint (the veil is gated off for most drags).

#### 11.12.3 The Caches

```
Tier  What                                  Recomputed when
1     the pre-develop WorkingImage          image, renderer (WorkingImageCache)
2     per-scope combined mask alpha         that scope's mask geometry (DevelopStackCache)
3     brush component rasters               that component's strokes (g_brushCache)
4     mask-fold prefix                      a component before the cut changes (g_maskFoldCache)
5     developed prefix / layer              the edited scope, or the base (DevelopStackCache::Hot)
6     the fused point pass                  every tick (cheap)
```

- DevelopStackCache (Develop/developstackcache.h): one mask entry per scope POSITION (so a dragged scope replaces its own entry), keyed on the components' signature; plus the developed intermediates (prefix / layer) for the ONE scope being edited. renderStack takes a StackResume and skips every scope below the edited one, and skips the develop pass for the edited scope itself when only its MASK moved, so a mask drag collapses to one blend + one OutputTransform. Proxy-only (the settle render passes nullptr). reset() keys on image / dims / orientation only; the base params are folded into the per-scope MASK KEY only for range-mask scopes (MW::scopeMaskDependsOnBase), since only the content-range tools' coverage depends on the base; Hot carries its own baseKey because the prefix IS the developed base. A scope whose reference (AI field, range reference, auto-mask guide) was not registered yet is NOT cached, or the unconfined placeholder would never be retired. Covered by tests/unit/tst_renderstack. It is MUTEX-GUARDED with private members (the proxy worker reads and writes it while the GUI calls reset()/clear()): never hand out a reference into `entries` or `hot`; copy the shared_ptr out under the lock (hotAt() does).
- g_brushCache is a byte-budgeted LRU (kBrushCacheBudget; entries are \~8 MB at a 2 MP proxy, so a COUNT cap either thrashes on a busy mask or hoards on a big one). It used to `clear()` itself past eight entries, so it could never hit on a busy mask.
- g_maskFoldCache: the component fold is SEQUENTIAL per pixel, so the running value after components [0..k) is a well-defined image (a prefix), and editing one submask leaves it exactly right. buildMaskBuffer resumes from the deepest still-valid prefix (keyed on path + dims + orientation; mutex-guarded, since the GUI render, the veil and the settle worker all call it). Components inside the prefix are not folded, rasterised or even JSON-parsed. The cut point is the first component whose signature changed; at least one component is always left out. Per-component signatures cover everything read out of a MaskComponent but NOT the references a component SAMPLES, so ensureRangeRef (base-dependent) calls maskFoldCacheClear(), and a component whose ref is not registered yet is refused entry to the prefix (prefixRefsReady).
- applySpots is serialised behind g_spotHealMutex: the LaMa / MI-GAN heal engines hold per-process state, and two pools can now overlap.
- The veil (updateMaskOverlayTint) builds at the PROXY's exact dimensions when one exists, so it shares the render's brush raster keys. It is coalesced with the render (paramsChanged does not connect to it; the proxy timer's slot calls it, then renderDevelopPreview: one veil rebuild, one render, one loupe repaint per event-loop turn), and it returns before building when ImageView::maskTintVisible() is false (see [11.15.5 Mask Tint](#11155-mask-tint)).

#### 11.12.4 Buffers Are Reused

On a 2175x1447 proxy a 121 ms tick was 87 ms of RELEASING MEMORY (three \~38 MB WorkingImages at \~29 ms each) against 1 ms for the develop pass and 7 ms for the blend. Writing 38 MB takes 2 ms (\~19 GB/s on an M4) and releasing it fifteen times longer, because every tick handed large blocks back to the OS and the next tick faulted them in again.

- assignReusing(dst, src) (Develop/workingimage.h) refills a WorkingImage through vector::assign, which keeps the allocation when capacity fits, and falls back to plain assignment when there is nothing to reuse. That fallback is load-bearing: forcing a fresh 24 MP destination down the grow path measured 631 ms against 49 ms.
- DevelopStackCache owns the scratch (accScratch / layScratch / outScratch, and an A/B prefixScratch pair), released by clear() but NOT by reset(), which fires on every tick of a Global drag (dropping them there was WORSE: four allocations per tick instead of three). outScratch() hands back whichever of an A/B pair hot.layer is not serving, so the render never writes a buffer the cache is still handing out as const. The prefix has its own pair because it is captured on a different schedule.
- WorkingImageCache::render takes the same scratch: an UNMASKED image takes developComposite, not renderStack, so fixing only the stack path left the commonest case untouched.
- The settle render passes NO scratch (it runs once and should give its memory back), but allocates ONE layer buffer for all scopes, not one per scope. Giving it a scratch would recover \~1.4 s more at 61 MP but pin \~1.5 GB; that option is written up, with its measured cost and footprint, under "FULL-RES SCRATCH" in Develop/workingimagecache.h. Deferred: the settle is background work nobody waits on.

#### 11.12.5 Output and Scopes

- OutputTransform::ToImage splits rows across the global pool (it used to be the only serial stage, \~420 ms of a 520 ms tick on a 50 MP raw).
- The transfer LUT: on the per-channel 1-D path a 16384-entry table plus interpolation replaces the pow (\~4.8x). NOT bit-exact, deliberately: \~0.001% of inputs land one level of 255 away, always by exactly 1; a denser table does not remove them (float rounding at the .5 boundary), and an exact-threshold formulation had the SAME residue at only 2.9x. Used for the preview AND 8-bit export so the two always agree; ToImage16 keeps the exact maths. Bound asserted by tests/unit/tst_outputtransform. (See [11.4.3 Two Paths, Neither With a Transcendental](#1143-two-paths-neither-with-a-transcendental).)
- ScaledPixmapItem (Views/scaledpixmapitem.h) keeps presenting the FULL image size to the scene while holding the proxy pixmap and stretching it at paint time, so there is no per-tick full-size upscale + QPixmap::fromImage (\~200 MB each on a 50 MP file). Item coordinates ARE image coordinates as before, so no overlay, hit test or zoom calculation moved; only code that READS PIXELS out of the pixmap needs ImageView::imageToPixmap (the sample loupe; copyImage stretches back for the clipboard). Exception: a non-identity geometry still upscales first, because crop is applied on the full-output-dimension image so its dims match the settle render's exactly.
- updateDevelopScopes samples the RGB888 frame ToImage emits directly (it used to convertToFormat(RGB32) the whole frame on the GUI thread), and skips the 4096-sample verification diff on an interactive tick (updateDevelopScopes(shown, verifyVsPreview)).

#### 11.12.6 Mask and Brush Costs

- One throttle for every live mask emit: ImageView::maskEmitLiveGeometry(LiveEmit) (kMaskStrokeLiveMs, trailing edge); brushEmitLiveGeometry is a thin caller. A brush stroke and a handle drag are mutually exclusive, so one clock covers both. The grab invalidates the clock so the first move emits at once; both releases emit unconditionally, so the settled geometry is never a throttled sample.
- Brush cost is (arc length / (radius \* kDabSpacing)) dab boxes. BrushStamp::segmentMax tracks the residual distance across segments (`carry`), so dabs land at a fixed arc-length spacing however the events arrive; ImageView threads the same carry through maskBrushDabCarry so the live preview and the render place dabs identically. Both stamp the final/cursor point unconditionally (a spaced walk can stop up to one step short). Anything that stamps per EVENT instead of per DISTANCE scales with mouse polling rate.
- BrushStamp::dabMax is row-parallel (bands own disjoint rows, so the MAX accumulation cannot race; serial below 64k px so ImageView's per-move dab does not pay a thread hop), and its outside / full-core tests use SQUARED distance, so the sqrt is paid only in the feather band.
- BrushStamp::dabStats() (two relaxed atomics per dab) feeds the [DevTime] mask field "(N scopes, D dabs, P Mpx)": the only way to tell "too many dabs" from "each dab is the whole image", which have different fixes.

Result: on a 1618x1214 proxy with a \~24-submask scope, a brush drag went from \~1450 ms per tick (mask 709 + tint 750) to 77 ms (mask 46 [raster 15 / setup 22 / fold 2, ONE component] + develop 3 + toImage 8, veil off), and with the prefix-fold cache the setup and raster cost of untouched components went too.

#### 11.12.7 Rules for New Develop Code

- Every per-pixel Develop loop uses parallelFor.
- Every large-kernel blur uses a downscaled base (or an O(1) box / integral approach): Texture's base is computed on a luminance image downscaled by kDown = clamp(sigma/3, 1, 4) (INTER_AREA down / INTER_LINEAR up), cost \~1/kDown^2.
- Develop runs on 512 KB pool stacks: never hold PointCoeffs (or any large struct) by value, and never name a large struct inside a [=] lambda (see [11.41.1 A Stack Overflow on a Pool Thread](#11411-a-stack-overflow-on-a-pool-thread)).
- An index chosen under one lock acquisition means nothing under the next; only the data copied out under the lock is safe to keep (see [11.41.2.4 A Stale Fold-Cache Slot](#114124-a-stale-fold-cache-slot)).
- Before optimising, split the [DevTime] number until the stages SUM to the wall clock, and read the whole line, not just the stage you changed; check allocation churn before reaching for per-pixel cleverness.

#### 11.12.8 Measuring

G::isReportDevelopTime (Main/global.cpp, a probe switch) prints [DevTime] per-stage timings on every render: WorkingImageCache::RenderTimings + Develop::StageTimings, the develop number split into copy / apply / blend / free, the mask number into raster / setup / fold with dab and component counts, plus worker (off-thread ms), applied (0 when a frame was dropped), cacheKept and resume.

tests/tsan/run_tsan_develop.sh (--devtest -> MW::runDevelopStressTest) races the Develop render: it simulates a brush drag on a multi-submask scope and adjustment nudges (DevelopProperties::selfTestNudgeAdjustment) while switching images, toggling the veil, re-rendering through the crop-style caller and re-selecting the folder, so the worker collides with the GUI thread on DevelopStackCache, g_brushCache, g_maskFoldCache and the pending / gen guards. Reading its output:

- WINNOW_DEVTEST_SERIAL=1 is the DEFAULT and load-bearing: it caps the global pool at one thread so every parallelFor runs serially. Homebrew Qt is not TSan-instrumented, so QFuture::waitForFinished()'s happens-before edge is invisible and every parallel-for lambda's by-reference capture of the caller's stack reports as a race (49 reports parallel, 5 serial; the 44 that vanish are that artefact, proved by A/B).
- The run FAILS only on races naming the Develop render; the folder-load / metadata-reader family is warned about, not failed, and crashes always fail.
- Read the render count and the `resume` distribution, never the PASS line alone. The nudge cadence decides which branches run (a render spans \~16 ticks): nudge in 30-tick bursts with 30-tick brush-only gaps, holding a scope for 120, so cold, prefix-resume and prefix+layer-resume renders all occur (a good run: 1,206 ticks, 77 renders, 56 cold / 10 prefix / 11 prefix+layer, no races). selfTestNudgeAdjustment must NOT call noteScopeEdit (marking the stack dirty persists it and the driver stacks scope after scope), and selfTestAddMaskScope must stay idempotent.

#### 11.12.9 Image-Switch Latency

Switching image in Develop blocks on a full unpack + demosaic + RawColor before anything can be developed (Develop trims read-ahead to the current image). The deliberate answer is progressive display at ZERO memory cost: keep showing the already-decoded 8-bit image while MW::ensureDevelopWork decodes the scene-linear WorkingImage off-thread, and LABEL it. MW::updateDevelopRenderingHint raises ImageView's top-right chip ("Decoding raw", "Rendering full size") for the two slow stages only, never for the sub-second proxy tick. It is drawn from paintEvent, not drawForeground, so it survives the crop/spot early returns, and it sits top-right because drawMaskLegend owns top-left.

Not done, on purpose: caching proxies or reading neighbours ahead. A scene-linear WorkingImage is 12 bytes/pixel (\~600 MB for 50 MP, against a 768 MB WorkingImageCache budget), and even a screen-resolution proxy is \~46 MB. A half-size demosaic (2x2 CFA quad -> 1 px) feeding a proxy read-ahead of +/-2 neighbours is the obvious next step if this is revisited; a disk cache was considered and rejected (it only helps revisits, the files are large, and mtime invalidation is surface area).

The [DevTime] fields, for reference: proxy / full / full(async), dims, proxyBuild / mask (+ scope count) / srcCopy / develop [copy apply blend free OTHER] / outFree / resume / cacheKept|cacheWiped / toImage / orient+scale / setHot / worker / COMPOSEOTHER / applied / superseded / preview / scopes / tint ms; the async line adds denoise / point / texture / dehaze. OTHER and COMPOSEOTHER are the REMAINDERS (develop minus its buckets, worker minus every reported stage), and they are the point: while either is large the stages do not sum to the wall clock, and a fix chosen from the named numbers is aimed at a fraction of the cost. Both were \~40-80 ms, which is how the allocator churn was found. The TINT count is the coalescing diagnostic: more than one veil rebuild per render means it has come uncoupled again.

### 11.13 The Develop Dock

The Develop panel is a dock (View > Develop Editor Panel, F9), built like the Embellish dock: MW::createDevelopDock() in initialize.cpp wraps a DevelopProperties widget (Develop/Properties/), a PropertyEditor subclass mirroring EmbelProperties. It tabs with the Embellish and History docks in the right dock area, and its visible / collapsed state persists like the other docks (settings isDevelopDockVisible + DevelopDock, plus WorkspaceData::isDevelopDockVisible).

#### 11.13.1 The Action Row

The dock's tool bar: the Scopes, Transform (crop), Spot, Screen Sampler, Preset and Export BarBtns in a centred QHBoxLayout (a stretch at each end) below the dock title bar. It sits INSIDE the dock body, not in the title bar, which keeps only the ? (how this works), collapse and X buttons so the title text is not squeezed. Collapsing the dock hides the row with the rest of the body (DockWidget::setCollapsed clamps the dock to the title-bar height). (The mask-tint swatch moved from here to the Mask band; see [11.15.8 The Submask List](#11158-the-submask-list).) The Scopes and Transform strips are toggled independently from the row.

Transform and Spot are mutually exclusive. Both drive the loupe (the crop / warp overlay vs the spot brush and pins), so arming either closes the other, whether from the action row, the Develop menu or R / S:

- toggleDevelopTransform disarms Spot (onSpotToolToggled(false)) BEFORE showing the panel, so the spot tool has released the canvas before enterDevelopCrop starts the overlay.
- toggleDevelopReplace calls toggleDevelopTransform when a Transform session is open, re-using its hide path, which means the crop COMMITS, as when the user closes the panel with R or the button. Esc (cancelDevelopTransform) is the only way to discard a crop session.

The buttons that toggle a panel or tool (Scopes, Transform, Spot, the mask tint swatch, Preset) carry a WHITE border while their panel is shown or the tool is armed, like a checked tool button (BarBtn::setActive). White rather than G::appleBlue, which was too quiet against the dark panel to read as "on" at a glance. MW keeps them as members and calls setActive from the toggle handlers (toggleDevelopScopes, toggleDevelopTransform + cancelDevelopTransform, spotActiveChanged), so the border tracks the real state even when toggled from the keyboard (R / Esc / S).

The Preset button is the awkward one: "its panel is up" means "the History dock is the front tab AND its Presets section is open", and a tabified dock keeps isVisible() == true when a sibling tab is selected, so visibilityChanged never fires on a tab switch. MW::updateDevelopPresetBtn is driven from four places: historyDockVisibilityChange, QMainWindow::tabifiedDockWidgetActivated (the only reliable signal for a tab click), showPresetsDock (raise() on an already "visible" dock emits nothing) and HistoryPanel::presetsExpandedChanged. Since 2026-09-26 the Preset button is HIDDEN (MW::createDevelopDock, the showDevelopPresetBtn flag in initialize.cpp); it is still constructed so this logic stays live, and Presets remain reachable via P and the View menu. Flip the flag to restore it. Export is still a stub with no border.

#### 11.13.2 Screen Sampler

2026-10-10. The pipette after Spot on the action row (also Develop > Screen Sampler; no shortcut; not gated on Develop mode) opens a small always-on-top readout and arms a dropper that reads a 5x5 PHYSICAL-pixel average from ANYWHERE on screen, another app's window included. Built for comparing renders across apps: sample a spot in Lightroom, then the same spot in Winnow, and both sit in its table, one row per sample (Sample | R G B in percent | H in degrees, S and L in percent, conventional HSL, rounded; the Sample cell carries a colour chip). Utilities/screensampler.{h,cpp}, MW::toggleScreenSampler.

- Copy puts the whole table on the clipboard as tab-separated text with a header row (no Cmd+C shortcut, by request). Esc closes the sampler, from the readout or while aiming; right-click cancels just the pick.
- Aiming: while armed, an overlay per screen (painted at alpha 1/255 so macOS delivers the clicks to it rather than the app underneath) takes the click, and a magnifier follows the cursor showing 11x11 physical pixels with the 5x5 block outlined and the live average. The overlay tints what it covers by up to one level, so the final grab happens 80 ms after the overlay and magnifier have closed.
- What it reads: the display's own 0..255 values, in the DISPLAY's colour space (Display P3 on most Macs), not sRGB. Two windows on one display compare exactly; a copied number is not an sRGB value. Grabs go through QScreen::grabWindow (Qt's Cocoa plugin uses CGDisplayCreateImageForRect), in the screen's logical coordinates, clipped to the screen; the cursor's physical pixel is found from the grab's actual device pixel ratio.
- macOS permission: reading other apps' windows needs Screen Recording. The sampler checks CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess first; without it, it calls CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess (the system prompt, once), refuses to arm, and says why INSIDE its window with an Open Settings button. Without permission macOS returns the wallpaper in place of other apps' windows, so it would otherwise report wrong numbers. A grant takes effect after Winnow restarts; launched from Qt Creator, the permission belongs to Qt Creator. Windows needs no permission.
- The button reuses DevelopProperties::dropperIcon (public), ghosted with a blue border while armed, like the WB dropper.

The dock body, from top to bottom: the action row, the Scopes strip (histogram / vectorscope), the Transform, Fill Replace and Raw panels, and then ONE scrolling block made of the Edits bar (ScopeHeader), the Mask panel and the adjustment tree. The action row, Scopes strip, Transform, Replace and Raw panels stay pinned above the block; the block scrolls in the dock's QScrollArea (MW::createDevelopDock always builds it).

#### 11.13.3 The Edits Bar (ScopeHeader)

Develop/Properties/scopeheader.cpp: ONE gradient-headed line carrying the whole scope control, "Scope: n [Global v] [+] [eye] [:]", with the Mask panel and the adjustment tree directly below it as its DETAILS (setRowDetail).

- The caption reads "Scope" in G::header2Color (2026-09-28), followed by ": n", the number of scopes on the image with Global included (2026-10-14), in the [+] glyph's own grey #b8b8b8 at G::iconOpacity (barCountLabel, refilled in updateScopeBar; a click on it folds like the caption).
- The gradient is painted by ScopeHeader::paintEvent, the same header gradient TransformPanel and RawPanel use.
- The combo carries every scope on the image, index 0 always Global, and only a USER pick selects one (QComboBox::activated; updateScopeBar refills with signals blocked) -> scopeSelected -> onScopeSelected: switch activeScopeIndex, open NO submask (selectedMaskIndex = -1) and latch the scope's COMBINED mask (red, no handles) when it has one. Its submasks are listed in the Mask panel below, and clicking one re-opens it.
- [+] -> addScopeRequested -> newScope (a name dialog at the cursor, default "Mask n"), promoted out of the menu because it is the primary action. On accept it immediately calls showMaskMenu: a new scope exists to carry a masked adjustment, so choosing the mask tool is the next step (Escape leaves an empty scope).
- [eye] -> scopeEnabledToggled(activeIndex, !on) -> onScopeEnabledToggled (EditScope::enabled; the compositor skips a disabled scope, so Global off renders with no develop adjustments).
