- [:] -> showScopeMenu, the ONLY menu in the panel, so it carries both the active scope's actions and the panel-wide ones: Global gets "New mask" + "Reset Global"; a mask scope gets "Modify &lt;mask> mask" (M) / Reset / Rename / Delete; then, always, a checkable "Hide global image" (any scope; its own connect -> hideGlobalImageToggled -> DevelopProperties::setGlobalImageHidden, ticked from refreshPreviewButtons via setGlobalImageHidden), "Reset all edits" (see [11.37 Reset All Edits](#1137-reset-all-edits)) and "Edits help".

"Hide global image" (2026-10-20) is EditScope::hideImage on the GLOBAL scope: a recipe setting like the eyes (written to the sidecar only when true, joins EditStack::isIdentity, cleared by "Reset all" on Global; one History row per toggle, no merge key; not propagated by multi-image editing). buildStackJob carries it as StackRenderJob::hideGlobal and, while it is on, KEEPS a mask scope with no visible adjustment (normally skipped as identity) unless that scope's own eye (showScope) is shut, because such a mask still decides what shows. MW::developCompositeStack applies it LAST, after the geometry and the kaleidoscopes: it keeps every mask scope's coverage buffer (foldMasks), carries each into the frame (kaleidoMaskInFrame), unions them (unionCoverage, a + b - ab; a scope with no placed mask covers everything) -- a folding scope contributes its FOLDED coverage, and Global's kaleidoscope folds the union -- and cuts the frame out to it (cutOutToCoverage: PREMULTIPLIED ARGB32 / RGBA64, so a format without alpha gets black, not the hidden photo). The masked pixels are the full render's, Global's adjustments included. It changes nothing before the cut, so no develop cache is invalidated. The choice is read as an int code while the menu is alive and fired on the NEXT TICK, after re-selecting the scope it was raised on. A select can be REFUSED (a pending submask prompts; Cancel keeps the old scope), so the code re-checks currentScopeName() before acting, or "Delete Mask 2" would delete Mask 1.
- Every emission from this widget is DEFERRED a tick, since each loops back through setScopeRows and refills the combo the click came from.
- The old dropdown header's eye/preview, collapse-arrow and mask-overlay setters survive as INERT state-holders (setPreviewShown / setGlobalActive / setMaskOverlayAvailable / setMaskOverlayShown / setCollapsed); the bar shows none of it.
- DevelopProperties::bindScopeHeader connects the signals.

Naming: index 0 is always "Global" (named "Base" before 2026-07-30; older sidecars are normalised on load in setCurrentImage). Every other scope is a MASK in the UI ("Mask 1", "Mask 2", ..., the number = its index), renameable ("Sky", "Subject") via [:] "Rename &lt;scope>" -> renameActiveScope (uniqueScopeName resolves clashes with a numeric suffix). Global cannot be removed or renamed (popups "Global cannot be removed." / "Global cannot be renamed."). Terminology: see [11.15 Scope and Mask Model](#1115-scope-and-mask-model).

#### 11.13.4 The Adjustment Tree

The tree (DevelopProperties, a PropertyEditor) is REBUILT for the active scope by buildTree() (on image change, scope switch and mask add/remove/select) and holds the ADJUSTMENT SECTIONS only: Basic / Curves / Color / Point Color / Calibrate / Color Grade / Detail / Effects. The raw-decode controls live in the Raw panel above the bar, and the mask in the Mask panel below it.

- buildTree close()s and removes all rows then re-adds them, preserving the sections' expand state within a session (read from the current rows). Across sessions the expand state persists in QSettings under "Develop/SectionExpanded/&lt;Header>": the first build seeds each header from sectionExpanded() (first-ever run: Basic open, others closed), and QTreeView::expanded/collapsed -> persistSectionExpanded() writes it.
- Section headers show their plain name only ("Basic", "Color"; updateSectionHeaderCaptions), since the active scope is named in the Edits bar. They are NOT indented (UR_ExtraIndent 0 on the header caption index, read by PropertyDelegate::paint: a bool there means one indentation() level, an int that many pixels). Child rows keep their own indentation, so the sliders keep their full width.
- Section bands (2026-09-05): each section header carries the standard Winnow header gradient (UR_isBackgroundGradient in PropertyDelegate::paint, backgroundShade +5 -> -15, caption pen G::header2Color), the same band the Preferences root categories and the Embellish tree draw. The UR_HeaderFlat role that once made Develop an exception is DELETED; do not reintroduce a per-tree header style without a reason the whole app can follow.
- The edited marker: a section header whose group holds any non-default value reads "Basic \*". The test is EditParams::groupIsDefault, which resetGroup's a COPY of the active scope's params and compares, so it can never drift from the group membership. It is driven by paramsChanged plus populateSlidersFromStack / refreshScopeList / buildTree, and caches each section's star state (hdrStar[], -1 = unknown after a rebuild) so a slider drag does not run five recursive findCaptionIndex searches per tick.
- No selection: the tree runs in QAbstractItemView::NoSelection. Its rows are adjustments, not a list to pick from, and a selected row showed only as an ARTIFACT: the app QSS "QTreeView::item:selected" background fills the row's INDENTATION strip, which QTreeView paints before the delegate runs, so a solid blue tab appeared left of the caption. Stripping State_Selected in a drawRow override does NOT cure it (QTreeView::drawRow re-derives the flag per cell from the selection model); the fix has to be an always-empty selection model. The CURRENT index is unaffected (still set on click, with NoUpdate), so keyboard navigation is unchanged.

The tree sits INSIDE the Edits bar's block: it is a DETAIL widget of ScopeHeader (slot EditsDetail follows slot MaskDetail, the Mask panel), so the bar, the Mask panel and the sections are one block. Details are never indented. Because it is inside that block the tree cannot scroll itself:

- DevelopProperties::setFitToContentHeight(true) turns off both scrollbars and makes sizeHint() = viewportSizeHint() (the bottom of the LAST VISIBLE row) plus the closing rule's band. scheduleContentFit() re-fits, deferred and coalesced, from buildTree, expand/collapse, the setRowHidden callers (applyScopeItemsCollapsed, which emits no model signal), resizeEvent and a paintEvent backstop.
- wheelEvent is IGNORED in fit mode so the wheel reaches the dock's QScrollArea.
- minimumSizeHint in fit mode is (0, sizeHint().height()). The HEIGHT floor is the point (QAbstractScrollArea's own minimum would hold the block open above its content when every section is collapsed), but the WIDTH must stay free: returning the content width floored the scroll body (which has no horizontal scrollbar) at its pre-scrollbar width, so raising the vertical scrollbar clipped the value column and the eye buttons instead of reflowing.

#### 11.13.5 Header Controls: Eye, Then Menu

Every header and row in the Scope / Edits panel ends with the SAME trailing pair (2026-08-19): an EYE (show or hide that thing's changes) and then a vertical-ellipsis MENU, always last. That covers the Edits bar, the Submasks band (its eye hides every submask at once; the [+] add button stays ahead of the pair), each submask row, and each section header (whose menu repeats the Preview + Reset items; Calibrate adds "Calibrate help"). Each band's menu ends with its "&lt;band> help" item (see [20.5 Develop Panel Help Pages](#205-develop-panel-help-pages)).

- The pair lines up down the whole panel: G::headerBtnGap (6) between the two buttons and G::headerBtnRightInset (6) from the panel's right edge, used by the bands, the rows AND the tree's section headers. The section pair is queued into the BarBtnEditor column in order (btns: eye, then menu), which right-aligns them; BarBtnEditor reads a btnsSpacing global set alongside btns (drained and reset to 0 with them), so only the rows that ask for spacing get it (the Embellish dock's pairs stay tight). The delegate gives the editor the whole value-column rect, so BarBtnEditor's right inset is measured from the same edge as the bands'.
- EVERY eye and menu emission is DEFERRED a tick (QTimer::singleShot(0)), because the handler rebuilds the rows or the tree and so destroys the very button the click is inside.
- eye.png / eye_off.png live in images/icon16.

Preview is NON-DESTRUCTIVE. Each section header's eye toggles that group's Preview flag on the active scope; the whole-scope eye lives in the Edits bar (EditScope::showBasic / showColor / showDetail / showEffects / showScope, default true, persisted in the sidecar only when false; Effects also has per-effect showVignette / showGrain / showKaleido on its dropdown row). effectiveScopeParams() returns a COPY of the scope's params with any previewed-off group folded to identity (EditParams::resetGroup), so stored values are kept and re-showing restores them; showScope folds all of them. The fold is applied at every render-capture site (EditStack::effectiveParams, DevelopProperties::editParams and stackJob). Reset is DESTRUCTIVE: EditParams::resetGroup on the STORED params, then repopulate.

Group -> keys mapping follows the UI: texture / dehaze are Basic; the tone splits are Basic for Reset only; the sharpen\* quartet and localDenoiseLuma / localDenoiseChroma (Detail "Sharpening" and "Denoise") are Detail (the denoise pair moved there from Effects on 2026-08-20, so a scope's showDetail, not showEffects, gates them; old sidecars carry no showDetail key and it defaults to true); denoiseLuma / denoiseChroma (the Global "Denoise raw") are in no group. The preset format did not change: presets store a flat map of EditParams field names, and section titles only group the checklist UI.

The tree's context menu (anywhere in the tree) also carries Expand all / Collapse all / Solo mode, mirroring the Embellish dock:

- Expand all / Collapse all go through DevelopProperties::setAllSectionsExpanded, which calls QTreeView expandAll/collapseAll AND drives the tree's own scope items (setTreeCollapsed) and the Raw panel (RawPanel::setCollapsed). A bulk guard (isBulkExpandCollapse) keeps Expand all from tripping the Solo handler.
- Solo mode is a checkable toggle (persisted as "Develop/isSolo") that collapses the other top-level sections whenever one is expanded (PropertyEditor::collapseAllExcept). The Edits bar and the Raw panel are Solo peers too, and the base class cannot reach them, so DevelopProperties::soloCollapseOthers(owner) folds every peer except the one just opened. It is called from onSectionExpanded, from setTreeCollapsed(false), and from the RawPanel::collapseToggled handler (bindRawPanel). RawPanel::setCollapsed is programmatic and emits nothing, so a fold cannot bounce back; the state persists as "Develop/rawCollapsed".
- For a raw being edited as raw (currentIsRaw() && G::useRaw) the menu also offers "Raw demosaic" ("Raw demosaic and denoise" under the Winnow engine), a navigation shortcut: DevelopProperties::showRawDemosaic un-collapses the Raw panel (and folds its peers away under Solo).

#### 11.13.6 One Block and Panel Separators

Every Develop dock PANEL draws a G::panelBorderHeight (2 px) rule in G::tabWidgetBorderColor across its bottom edge, so stacked panels read as distinct blocks (G::panelBorderHeight = 0 removes them all). Each panel reserves the space as its outer layout's bottom margin, so the rule never overlaps content. Carried by: the action row under the dock title (a QSS border-bottom on QWidget#developActionRow, ID-scoped so it misses the child buttons; the dock title bar's own 1 px rule is switched off there via DockTitleBar::setBottomBorderVisible(false), since two rules that close together read as a mistake); the Scopes strip (fixed height 160 + the rule); Raw, Mask, Transform and Fill Replace (each in its paintEvent); and the tree's closing rule under the last row (DevelopProperties::paintEvent).

The Edits bar deliberately has NONE: it, the Mask panel and the tree are ONE BLOCK, closed by the tree's own rule at the bottom. The seam between the bar and the tree is closed too: rowsLayout has no bottom margin, and DevelopProperties turns OFF the frame (setFrameShape + a widget-level "QTreeView { border: none; }", since the app QSS gives every QTreeView a 1 px border). In fit mode the viewport is exactly the rows plus the band reserved for the rule (kBlockCloseGap 0 px above it) and kBlockBottomGap (2 px) clear space under it, so the rule always draws, full width from x 0. (In the legacy scrolling tree it is drawn only when empty dock remains below, since a rule at the last visible row of an overflowing tree would be a false bottom.)

History: the Edits panel once had a run-time A/B/C layout picker (G::developEditsLayout: Flat = a scope list with the editor below it, Nested = the editor inserted under the selected row, Minimal = one scope bar and no list), so the candidates could be compared on real edits (2026-09-05). Minimal won; the other two, the flag, the "Edits layout" submenu, the ScopeHeaderBase / ScopeHeaderLab split, the in-tree Core and mask-tool rows, the containment rail (G::scopeRailX / scopeRailW) and the "developEditsLayout" QSettings key are all deleted (MW::removeDeprecatedSettings retires the key, and now actually removes the keys it lists; it used to build the list and drop it).

#### 11.13.7 The Delegate Draws a Header Caption in Both Passes

PropertyDelegate::paint spans EVERY header caption (UR_isHeader) across the full row. The delegate painter is not clipped to the cell (QPainter::hasClipping() is false during item paint), so a single column-0 pass draws the caption across both columns on a full repaint. Partial repaints are the catch: dragging the dock splitter resizes the (stretch) value column and marks ONLY the value-column cells dirty, so QTreeView repainted just their background, erasing the caption overflow, and a long header caption truncated back to the column boundary after a resize.

So the caption is drawn in BOTH passes: the value-column pass fills its own background (gradient, or the bottom separator for non-gradient headers) and then redraws the SAME elided caption at the SAME viewport rect. capLeft must be identical in both passes; for a decoration row it is the column-0 cell left (view->visualRect(capIndex).x()), reproducible without column 0's rect. The caption's right edge is pulled in and the text elided when the value field is occupied: before a delegate-drawn [-] glyph (UR_DeleteBtn), or before a value-column widget (the value sibling's UR_Editor geometry + childrenRect). setFirstColumnSpanned is not required for plain headers.

### 11.14 Develop Persistence

Per-image develop state is an EditStack (Develop/editstack.h) stored in the image's XMP sidecar, Lightroom-style (parametric geometry and brush strokes as numbers). It replaced an early global QSettings "Develop/Scopes/&lt;name>/..." store, which was per-machine, not per-image; those QSettings helpers (readLayerList / setCurrentLayer / layerRootPath / layerValue) are deleted. Presets use their own store.

- The data model: EditStack { version; QVector&lt;EditScope> }, each EditScope { name; components (the mask's tool list; empty = global); opacity; enabled; show\* preview flags; EditParams params }. Serialised to JSON, then base64 (raw JSON quotes are awkward in an XML attribute). VERSIONED and FORWARD-TOLERANT: unknown keys ignored, missing keys default to identity. Header-only and free of any render-hot-path include (develop.cpp does not include it).
- The sidecar: the winnow:Develop rdf:Description attribute (Xmp::initialize registers definedElements["develop"]; the winnow namespace already existed). Metadata::writeDevelopSidecar / readDevelopSidecar mirror writeOrientation. An identity stack writes "", which CLEARS the attribute: no sidecar is created just to store nothing.
- An all-identity stack is never persisted, so empty scopes added to an unedited image are not written. Exception: a scope that has any mask component counts as non-identity, so masks survive navigation.
- The dock reflects the CURRENT IMAGE's EditStack. setCurrentImage(fPath) flushes the previous image, then loads and caches this image's stack and pushes its params into the editors (populateSlidersFromStack, guarded by isPopulating so the programmatic setValue -> itemChanged does not re-mark dirty). itemChange writes into the current image's active-scope params, marks it dirty, drives the live preview, and arms the debounced write. editParams() returns the ACTIVE scope's params.
- The sidecar is written only where source files may be modified or a sidecar is allowed (see [9.4 Writing Metadata Into Image Files](#94-writing-metadata-into-image-files)), and every edit is also a History row (see [11.36 Develop History](#1136-develop-history)).
- Schema drift and recovery are in [11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)](#1139-stale-presets-and-history-schema-drift) and [11.40 Corrupted or Changed Develop Settings](#1140-corrupted-or-changed-develop-settings).

#### 11.14.1 When State Is Read and Written

- MW::fileSelectionChange calls setCurrentImage; after the loupe pixmap is shown (both the cache-hit path and MW::refreshViewsOnCacheChange), MW::applyDevelopPreviewIfEdited renders the saved edits over an edited image (a no-op for identity, so an unedited image stays the normal decode and is never written).
- Sidecars are flushed on navigate-away (setCurrentImage), quit (closeEvent), and before ingest/copy (MW::ingest / copyFiles); NEVER during a drag. Writes are synchronous (a few-KB text file). The optional debounced write while editing (\~2 s after edits settle) is gated by G::isDevelopDebounceWrite (default true); the other flushes always run.
- setCurrentImage reads the sidecar synchronously on first touch of each image (cheap: no sidecar is a fast empty read). Folding the develop blob into the existing metadata sidecar read is a fast-follow if navigating many edited images shows latency.

#### 11.14.2 Videos

The Develop module operates on decoded still frames, so it is gated off for video selections. MW::currentIsVideo() (the VideoColumn flag) guards every entry point: fileSelectionChange hands developProperties->setCurrentImage an EMPTY path for a video (still flushing the image being left), and the three render entries (applyDevelopPreviewIfEdited, renderDevelopPreview, renderDevelopFullResAsync) early-return, so armed proxy/settle timers or Transform refreshes never try to develop a video.

- The mode is not changed: selecting a video in Develop leaves G::operationMode alone. Preview/Develop is the user's deliberate choice, and auto-flipping it would churn G::useRaw and rebuild the image cache on every video/still crossing in a mixed folder. The video plays on the VideoTab as in Preview.
- The panel greys (syncDevelopPanelEnabled) and a RED show-stopper alert row says why (see [11.19 Develop Alerts and the Greyed Panel (Severity Rows, Disabled States)](#1119-develop-alerts-and-the-greyed-panel-severity-rows-disabled-states)).
- D still works on a video (operationModeAction is never disabled; disabling it would strand the user in Preview-only navigation). setOperationMode skips the forced re-decode / read-ahead re-target for a video current item, but NOT the useRaw flip, a mode-level setting the next still needs.

### 11.15 Scope and Mask Model

Terminology (renamed 2026-07-30; it was "layer" throughout). The dock band is captioned SCOPE and lists what each edit set applies to: row 0 is GLOBAL (the whole image) and every other row is a MASK ("Mask 1", or renamed "Sky" / "Subject"). Each mask is built from SUBMASKS, the building blocks folded into it. In code the unit is an EditScope (EditStack::scopes); its mask is EditScope::components, an ordered list of MaskComponents (a submask is a MaskComponent; Mask/Submask is UI and docs vocabulary, and the sidecar keys are unchanged). Do not confuse this "scope" with the Develop SCOPES panel (histogram + vectorscope), an unrelated feature sharing the word.

The goal: apply any edit globally or through masks, with the SAME edit set shared across a scope's masks, performance-critical. This is the Lightroom MASKING model (a mask group carrying one edit set), NOT a Photoshop pixel-layer stack; that distinction is what keeps it fast (see [11.12 Develop Performance](#1112-develop-performance)).

- A scope = one EditParams + an ordered collection of submasks combined into a single per-pixel alpha, plus an opacity. The edit set applies wherever that alpha > 0.
- A scope with NO components is global, so "globally OR on masks" needs no special case. Global (index 0) carries no mask.
- Each submask ADDS, SUBTRACTS or INTERSECTS; the first must Add (there is nothing to subtract from an empty mask). Components fold SEQUENTIALLY, so ORDER is the result (see [11.15.14 Submask Order](#111514-submask-order)).
- MaskComponent: tool / op / inverted / feather / enabled + an opaque paramsJson holding the per-tool geometry (the legacy combine field is unused).

#### 11.15.1 Compositing

Sequential on an accumulator. Each scope develops the result of the stack BELOW it, blended back by opacity x mask alpha:

```
acc = Develop(workingImage, global.params)               // the foundation
```

```
for each mask scope i (bottom -> top):
    a   = opacity_i * maskAlpha_i(x)                      // 0 where the scope does not act
    acc = lerp(acc, Develop(acc, params_i), a)            // per pixel
```

Edits are therefore sequentially ADDITIVE (each scope sees the result below it), while opacity and masks stay well defined per pixel. Scope ORDER matters and a reorder changes the result; that is correct. Global is always opacity 1, no mask. A disabled scope (its eye off) is skipped, and a disabled submask is dropped from its mask (stackJob skips it). Stage 0 runs once, on the base (see [11.6.4 Wiring](#1164-wiring)), and mask scopes adjust BEFORE the output look.

#### 11.15.2 The Mask Panel

Below the Edits bar: the Mask block (with its Edge / Halo rows), the Submasks band, and the selected submask's details (MaskPanel, SubmaskList, MaskEditor). The whole panel sits on G::panelContentBg; only the "Mask" band carries the header gradient. Its structure is in [11.15.8 The Submask List](#11158-the-submask-list) and [11.15.12 Mask-Level Edge and Halo](#111512-mask-level-edge-and-halo).

Adding a submask: a new scope offers its first tool at once (newScope -> showMaskMenu); further tools come from the bar's [:] ("Modify &lt;mask> mask", M) or the SubmaskList's own [+]. The menu lists "Add &lt;tool> Mask" (and, once a tool exists, "Subtract &lt;tool> Mask") for every tool: Linear / Radial Gradient, Brush, Color / Luminance Range, Subject / Sky / Background, Depth Range, Object, Segmenter, Refine Brush, ... (every name ends in "Mask"; the AI tools drop a "Select" prefix; DevelopProperties::maskToolName).

#### 11.15.3 Pending and Committed Submasks

Every submask, including the first, is PENDING from the moment its type is picked (beginMaskTool appends it and sets pendingIdx) until it is committed. Commit writes the op into the component, ends the pending session, names the History entry and makes the submask persistent.

Submasks commit THEMSELVES (2026-09-21); the commit button and the "Commit submask?" dialog are gone. A pending submask folds itself into the mask kMaskAutoCommitMs (2000 ms) after its last edit: DevelopProperties::maskCommitTimer, a singleShot restarted by armMaskAutoCommit() from every mutation that touches the pending submask (onMaskEditorSetting: feather / edge / invert / brush / range; setActiveMaskParams, through which EVERY canvas shape edit funnels: handle drag, brush stroke, pipette pick; toggleSubmaskInverted; and setPendingMaskOp, so changing what the submask DOES gives the user the full two seconds to look at the new op).

- Why the button went: it was a commit boundary with nothing buffered behind it. Every mask edit is written straight into the MaskComponent and rendered live, so the only thing the button decided was the combine op, and a committed submask's op is still changeable from its row's [:] menu: a modal ceremony guarding a revisable decision, paid for with a dialog on the way out of a scope and a SILENT DISCARD on the way out of an image.
- Mid-stroke is exempt: maskStrokeActive (ImageView::maskStrokeStateChanged, routed through MW's syncPendingMaskOp lambda) stops the timer while a brush/object stroke is down, and the stroke's END re-arms it. Handle drags arrive as setActiveMaskParams ticks, each restarting the window anyway.
- Untouched never lands: autoCommitPendingMask() bails on pendingMaskIsUntouched(), so picking a tool and never using it leaves nothing. EXCEPT one-click masks (fixed 2026-10-07): for Subject / Sky / Background, choosing the tool IS the edit, so pendingMaskIsUntouched() is false for them (a fresh Sky submask used to be flushed away by the next Add Submask, leaving the scope empty).
- The veil stays up: commitPendingMask(keepVeil) is set by every automatic path, because the automatic commit fires WHILE the user is still editing. closeSubmaskEditing() drops it when the session really ends.
- The History entry stays: History snapshots the EditStack, which does not carry pendingIdx, so without its own entry an undo past the commit would restore the submask with the wrong op.
- Leaving: flushMaskAutoCommit() (land it, or drop it if untouched, no prompt) runs at reopenSubmask, onScopeSelected and newScope, and in setCurrentImage BEFORE flushImage so the sidecar gets it. (setCurrentImage used to DISCARD the pending submask; that was defensible while committing was an explicit act, not when it happens on its own two seconds later.) The sites that still DISCARD are those whose scope or stack is being destroyed anyway (reset-all, deleteScope, applyHistoryEntry); each stops the timer so it cannot fire into a dead index.
- Keys: Return -> finishSubmaskEditing() (flush + close, so it lands the submask and puts its handles away; it also closes a RE-OPENED submask, "Done"). Esc discards while still pending. The Return branch deliberately has NO value-editor bail (only a QLineEdit keeps the key): while a submask is being defined the focus is almost always on the panel's own sliders.
- Changing your mind: the row's [:] > Delete (deleteMask fixes up pendingIdx and stops the timer), or Cmd+Z / the History panel.

#### 11.15.4 Combine Modifiers

Opt = SUBTRACT, Shift+Opt = INTERSECT, held while defining a submask. DevelopProperties::maskOpFromModifiers() reads the LIVE keyboard state, and the veil preview, the op chip and the commit all go through it, so they cannot disagree.

- The op LATCHES on action (latchMaskOp, 2026-08-08). A modifier PRESS previews momentarily, but starting to SHAPE the submask (a brush/object stroke or a handle drag; ImageView::maskOpActionStarted) freezes the op held at that instant into latchedMaskOp, and a later key release falls back to THAT, not to Add. So a subtract you painted stays a subtract with your hands off the keyboard. Paint or drag again with nothing held and the latch re-reads as Add. Reset per submask. (Re-reading the live modifiers at the instant of commit meant releasing Opt to reach for the button committed an Add: the user painted a subtract and nothing changed.)
- MW's filter tracks Key_Alt / Key_Shift press AND release (the veil must follow the key with the mouse stationary, and the dock usually holds focus) and calls MW::syncPendingMaskOp -> setPendingMaskOp, which re-composites. The Alt KeyPress is accepted so Windows cannot open the menu bar; ApplicationActivate re-syncs so a modifier released while the app was inactive cannot stick.
- The op drives the RENDER, not just the veil. The pending submask is stored with op = Add until commit, so stackJob() substitutes pendingOp into its component (a local copy; nothing is written into the stored stack), exactly as updateMaskOverlayTint does, and setPendingMaskOp emits paramsChanged. Without that the image kept showing an Opt submask being ADDED while the veil showed it subtracted, and over an already-masked area that is NO VISIBLE CHANGE ("subtract brush is broken").
- The FIRST submask has nothing to combine with, so it is pinned to Add and the hint is hidden.

Brush Opt = ERASE (restored 2026-10-14; G::useBrushEraseStroke = true). Opt takes away from the STROKE while painting a Brush or Object submask (maskBrushErase), and from the MASK otherwise, with one clause: a stroke with nothing to erase is not an erase. While the submask has no coverage yet (maskBrushStrokesJson empty) Opt still means Subtract and the stroke paints, otherwise the natural gesture for a subtract brush ("hold Opt, paint what to remove") would paint nothing, leaving an empty submask whose Subtract is a no-op (m \*= 1 - 0).

- Once the submask has strokes, Opt erases from it. Two guards came with the restore: an erase press does NOT emit maskOpActionStarted (latching the held Opt would also make the submask a Subtract), and MW::syncPendingMaskOp treats Opt as erase BETWEEN strokes too (ImageView::maskOptWouldErase), so the veil does not flip the submask to Subtract each time the mouse button comes up. Such a submask's op is set from SubmaskDialog or its row.
- Only an ERASE stroke owns Opt: ImageView::maskStrokeIsErase() (not merely maskStrokeInFlight) drops the previewed op back to Add for the stroke's duration, so an Opt paint on an empty submask keeps previewing the subtraction. ImageView emits maskStrokeStateChanged on both edges of a stroke (AFTER maskBrushErase is decided) and MW re-reads the modifiers there.
- History: Opt = Subtract everywhere replaced the erase stroke on 2026-08-08, on the reasoning that the effect now re-renders DURING the swipe so a mis-paint is visible as it happens. With it off, Opt+stroke on the first or a re-opened submask silently painted while the cursor showed a minus, and on a later pending submask it flipped the WHOLE submask to Subtract, never what a Lightroom user means by Alt-brush. The whole erase path (maskBrushErase, the per-stroke "erase" JSON flag, BrushStamp's erase composite, the pink cursor) stayed intact behind the flag.

The op indicator: while the overlay is shown, ImageView::drawMaskLegend paints a compact chip top-left naming what the commit will do ("Add: Brush Mask", "Subtract: Brush Mask", "Intersect: Brush Mask") over a dim reminder line "Opt subtract . Shift+Opt intersect" (suppressed on the first submask). MW pushes it via ImageView::setMaskLegend(submaskName, op, showHint). It replaced a colour-key legend naming a RED/GREEN/BLUE scheme that no longer exists.

#### 11.15.5 Mask Tint

One colour, outcome preview. The overlay does NOT colour-code Add / Subtract / Intersect. While a submask is being defined (selectedMaskIndex >= 0 on a non-Global scope), the loupe shows the ENTIRE mask (all the scope's submasks composited) as one flat coverage tint, the RESULT VEIL, in the ONE overlay colour; alpha is the composite coverage alone (up to 150), so Subtract holes stay holes and the veil answers "what does this scope affect?". The PENDING submask (pendingMaskIndex) is composited into it with the op the held modifier is previewing (pendingMaskOp), so the veil shows the RESULT of the commit: hold Opt and the veil retreats where that submask would be removed; hold Shift+Opt and it collapses to the overlap. That is strictly more informative than tinting the operand, which is why one colour suffices.

- MW::updateMaskOverlayTint (wired to maskEditBegin/End; coalesced with the render on parameter changes) reuses the render path's buildMaskBuffer (so the tint is pixel-consistent with the render) at the proxy's exact dimensions when one exists (else a \~1600 px cap), builds the AI/range refs it needs (cached), converts coverage to premultiplied overlay colour, rings the pending submask's footprint, orients it to the displayed pixmap, and hands it to ImageView::setScopeMaskTint (clearScopeMaskTint when nothing is being edited). drawForeground paints the veil UNDER the active submask's handles, not hover-gated; with a veil present the per-submask preview takes drawTint=false. The veil reflows live during a geometric drag.
- One ring is still drawn: a thin outline of the pending submask's footprint, painted ONLY where the result is absent (buf &lt;= \~0.12), because a Subtract whose footprint misses the mask would otherwise change nothing on screen. The veil winning everywhere it covers also keeps a noisy content submask (Color/Luminance Range), whose per-pixel "edges" are everywhere, from fogging the subject.
- Disabled submasks are not veiled: a submask whose row eye is off is dropped by the render, so updateMaskOverlayTint filters it out of the vector it hands buildMaskBuffer (which never reads the flag) and REMAPS the pending index onto the filtered vector. Before the fix the veil advertised coverage the image did not have. The filter also drives the ensure\*() reference builds, so an unchecked AI/range submask costs nothing. A hidden pending submask leaves the veil too (no ring, no chip); the tool's own live preview still draws.
- Visibility is explicit-only (2026-10-07): the overlay STARTS HIDDEN and is shown only by an explicit toggle: "O" or "M" (toggleMaskOverlayAction -> MW::toggleMaskOverlay -> ImageView::toggleMaskTint, which flips maskTintHidden, gating both the veil and the per-submask preview; handles and cursor keep drawing), the action-row tint button, the scope menu's "Show mask overlay" row, or the new-submask dialog. Changing an adjustment slider while shown hides it (maskTintHideRequested -> hideMaskTint) so the effect is visible; mask-only edits (Feather / Invert / Range / Brush) keep it. Committing a submask hides it (commitPendingMask emits maskTintHideRequested after paramsChanged) but leaves the overlay LATCHED (maskLatched -> maskOverlayActive), so it is only hidden. maskTintHidden is sticky. The automatic re-show on selecting another scope (onScopeSelected -> maskTintShowRequested -> ImageView::showMaskTint) was removed by request; the signal and showMaskTint are kept for when auto-show rules are decided.
- When hidden, MW skips building the veil entirely (ImageView::maskTintVisible()); see [11.41.2 Develop Render Latency (the Measurement Record)](#11412-develop-render-latency-the-measurement-record).

The overlay colour: G::maskOverlayColor (default 220,40,40) is the single colour of the veil, the per-submask live preview (ImageView::maskTintColor) and the pending footprint ring. The tint button's CONTEXT MENU picks it (red / green / blue / yellow / magenta / white; red reads badly over a red subject) via DevelopProperties::setMaskOverlayColour, which writes "Develop/maskOverlayColor" and asks for a veil rebuild; the DevelopProperties ctor seeds G:: from that key. The palette is MaskPanel::overlayColours(). (The Mask panel's own swatch row was removed on 2026-08-15: the overlay's appearance describes the veil, not a submask, so it belongs with the tint button.)

Overlay greyscale (same menu): no overlay colour reads well over every subject, so the other half of the answer is to take the colour out of the PICTURE. G::maskOverlayGrayscale (persisted as "Develop/maskOverlayGrayscale") makes the IMAGE ITEM paint itself grey (Qt has no saturation blend mode, so it cannot be laid over the top in drawForeground). ImageView::paintEvent evaluates maskGrayscaleActive() and pushes it to ScaledPixmapItem::setGrayscale (no update() from inside a paint pass); the item blits a grey copy cached by pixmap().cacheKey(), so a Develop tick pays one Grayscale8 conversion at PROXY resolution and pans/zooms pay none. The veil, handles and legend are drawn after it and keep their colour. A VIEW effect only: the render, the sidecar and the export are untouched. It follows the veil (hidden by "M"/"O", colour returns) and emits maskOverlayRepaintRequested, a repaint with NO veil rebuild. Submask row captions are not role-tinted: "Subtract Brush Mask" already says it, and a coloured caption would re-introduce the colour key this design removed.

#### 11.15.6 Linear and Radial Gradients

Edited directly on the loupe, not the dock. Geometry lives in MaskComponent.paramsJson in normalised coordinates: Linear {x1,y1,x2,y2}; Radial {cx,cy,rx,ry,angle} (cx/cy by W,H; rx by W, ry by H; angle in degrees). Resolution- and zoom-independent; survives proxy/full re-render. Overlays map through the geometry stage (see [11.25 Overlays Over a Transformed Image (Mask Space vs Displayed Space)](#1125-overlays-over-a-transformed-image-mask-space-vs-displayed-space)).

- Handshake (wired in MW, mirroring paramsChanged): selecting a spatial tool fires DevelopProperties::maskEditBegin(tool, op, inverted, paramsJson, feather) -> ImageView::beginMaskEdit; deselecting fires maskEditEnd. developDockVisibilityChange() ends / re-asserts it so the overlay never leaks into the plain loupe.
- ImageView::drawForeground dispatches by tool to drawLinearMask / drawRadialMask, shown only while the cursor is over the view (maskHover via enter/leaveEvent). Tints and handles draw in viewport coordinates for a constant on-screen size; a miss falls through to pan/zoom.
- Linear: tint ramp + centre line + 0% / 100% perpendicular guides + endpoint / centre handles. An endpoint drag rotates and scales about the fixed centre; a centre or line drag translates.
- Radial: an elliptical tint (a unit-circle QRadialGradient mapped through a brush transform to the rotated ellipse) + TWO outlines + centre + 4 axis handles. The solid outline is the nominal boundary (through the axis handles); a dashed ellipse marks the HALF-COVERAGE radius (hidden at feather 0). Coverage falls from the centre outward and runs a little PAST the solid outline (see [11.15.7 Mask Feather Profile](#11157-mask-feather-profile)), so the tint's gradient brush is stretched to the profile's tMax. The centre handle moves; axis handles resize each semi-axis (centre fixed); dragging the outline rotates.
- Shift + an axis-handle drag resizes PROPORTIONALLY: both semi-axes scale by the one factor the grabbed handle moved through, measured in frame pixels against the shape at grab time, so a circle stays a circle. Shift may be pressed or released mid-drag (the anchor is the shape at mouse-down).
- The wheel / two-finger scroll with the cursor inside the radial's CORE (within the dashed half-coverage ring; ImageView::maskRadialCoreContains -> adjustRadialSize) resizes it proportionally (one multiplicative factor, centre and angle fixed, clamped to a 2 px floor and four frame diagonals), emitting through the shared live-geometry throttle as LiveEmit::Wheel, whose trailing emit carries the settled geometry since a wheel gesture has no release. Over the rim or outside, the wheel zooms the image; Shift + wheel is the feather at any position; Space bypasses both.
- Drag emits maskGeometryChanged LIVE (and on release) -> DevelopProperties::setActiveMaskParams (stores into the component, debounce-persists, no tree rebuild).
- Feather and Invert live-update via maskFeatherChanged / maskInvertChanged. Feather is also Shift + wheel on the canvas (ImageView::adjustMaskFeather -> maskFeatherRequested -> setActiveMaskFeather, which syncs the panel slider, notes the edit and re-composites, sending no echo back). Invert flips (Radial: effect outside). The preview always shows the SELECTED tool, in the one overlay colour.

#### 11.15.7 Mask Feather Profile

Develop/maskfalloff.h is ONE feather curve for every mask tool. Every tool used to taper with a smootherstep, flat-ended by construction (exactly 1 across a core, a ramp, exactly 0). Measured against Lightroom on the same frame (white image, radial mask, feather 82, exposure -3.0), recovering coverage from both screenshots through Winnow's own perceptual blend:

```
Winnow  smootherstep from 0.180R (== feather 82)  fit rms 0.002
LR      GAUSSIAN, sigma 0.450R                    fit rms 0.024
        (best smootherstep fit to LR: k~0.02, still rms 0.086)
```

Winnow's render was exactly per spec; the SHAPE differed: Lightroom's coverage starts falling at the very centre (no flat core), still carries \~4% at the boundary, and dies by \~1.3R. Feeding a Gaussian through Winnow's blend reproduced Lightroom's whole profile to \~3/255, which also confirmed the blend space (kPerceptualMaskBlend). The family is a super-Gaussian in t, the normalised distance from full coverage (t=0) to the boundary (t=1):

```
m(t) = 2^-((t/h)^p)     h = half-coverage radius, p = roundness
h = 1 - 0.579f          p = (3.3 - 2.024f)/f       f = feather/100
```

p=2 is a true Gaussian, large p a near-hard edge, p&lt;2 peaks harder with a longer tail. Feather 82 gives (0.525, 2.0), the Lightroom measurement; the rest of the map makes the 10-90% transition width PROPORTIONAL to the feather (\~0.92f) through that anchor, so softness rises monotonically to 100. Feather 0 short-circuits to a hard step. Three entry points, because the tools are not all the same shape:

- Lut (distance to boundary: Radial, Brush): table-built once per component/dab, so the pow never enters a per-pixel loop.
- cdf (the Linear Gradient's two-sided S): a Gaussian CDF, sigma = 0.25f, matched to the old smootherstep's 10-90 width, so the ramp keeps its apparent width but gains tails past p1/p2.
- taper (the fixed-band tools: Luminance/Colour Range, Depth, Subject, Sky, Object), where feather is a TOLERANCE band the caller has already scaled, so only the curve's character is shared (same half-coverage at mid-band, no flat start). Not calibrated against Lightroom; there is no reference capture.

Consequence: a mask reaches slightly past its drawn outline, exactly as Lightroom's does, and overlay guides mark the HALF-COVERAGE radius, the only radius the profile makes a promise about. Changed in place, so existing sidecars re-render with the new curve (the feather key is unchanged, 0-100). Still open: Lightroom reads exposure -3.0 on white as only -1.95 EV (its scene-referred tone curve), where Winnow applies a literal linear gain, which is why the two frames still differ in DEPTH once the shape matches.

#### 11.15.8 The Submask List

The Mask panel is a DETAIL of the Edits bar (ScopeHeader::setRowDetail, slot MaskDetail, directly under the bar naming the mask it edits), up whenever a MASK scope is active (2026-08-13; it used to be a transient strip shown only while a submask was being built). Current layout (2026-10-14):

```
Scope: 3  [Mask 2 v] [+]        [eye] [:]    <- the Edits bar (ScopeHeader)
|  v Mask              [+] [swatch]  [:]     <- MASK band: add submask, overlay tint
|    Edge      -----o-----                     <- levelEditor (mask level)
|    Halo      -----o-----
|    -------------------------                 <- rule under Halo
|    v Linear Gradient Submask      [eye] [:]
|    v Brush Submask        [-]     [eye] [:]  <- open for editing; [-] = its op button
|      Attribute adjustment applies to next stroke
|      Feather   -----o-----                   <- embedded MaskEditor (the submask)
|      Invert    [ ]
|      Edge      -----o-----
```

- ScopeHeader::setRowDetail parks the Mask panel and the tree in wrapper widgets that outlive every refresh of the bar, so a scope switch never takes a detail down (setScopeRows refills the combo and nothing else). The wrappers are kept even when a slot is re-bound: re-parenting a QTreeView full of setIndexWidget editors would be the flicker-prone, expensive path. A detached detail is handed back to rowsContainer, NEVER to nullptr: a parentless QTreeView briefly becomes a top-level window and flashes on screen.
- The Mask band always shows on a mask scope, even an empty one, because its [+] (MaskPanel::levelAddBtn -> addSubmaskRequested -> DevelopProperties::showMaskMenu) makes the first submask. showMaskLevel only governs the Edge / Halo / Opacity rows. Its arrow folds the submask rows as well as those rows. Its [:] reads Add submask / Show all submasks / Hide all submasks (SubmaskList::setAllEnabled) / Reset mask Edge, Halo and Opacity / Mask help.
- The "Submasks" header band is GONE (2026-10-14): its [+] moved onto the Mask band, left of the overlay tint swatch, directly below the scope bar's own [+]; its eye became Show all / Hide all in the Mask band's [:]; "Submasks help" went with it (Mask help opens the same page). The submask rows' arrows sit in the Mask band's arrow column (G::headerLeftInset + G::subHeaderIndent). The rows are no longer collapsed by default, and MaskPanel::beginPending unfolds the mask.
- The tint swatch sits at the right end of the Mask band, beside its [:] (2026-09-21; it used to be in the action row at the top of the dock, among buttons with nothing to say it acted on the mask). Ownership is unchanged: MW builds developMaskTintBtn, wires it to toggleMaskOverlay and showDevelopMaskTintMenu, and repaints it (refreshDevelopMaskTintBtn) off maskTintVisibilityChanged / maskTintAvailabilityChanged / maskOverlayRefreshRequested, because the veil is application state. Only the placement moved: MaskPanel::setTintButton(QWidget\*) inserts the caller's widget at a slot recorded while the band is built (levelTintSlot, just after the stretch, ahead of levelMenuBtn), and DevelopProperties::placeMaskTintButton forwards to it. On the Global scope there is no Mask band, so the swatch is absent; "O" still pops the "no mask to tint" explanation. CAUTION: a plain method like setTintButton must be declared under public:, NOT inside the signals: block; moc generates a signal body for it there and the link fails with a duplicate symbol against mocs_compilation.o.
- Spacing (2026-10-14): every gap is the tree's DIVIDER spacing (caption -> rule \~18 px). The spacer under every tree section header ("&lt;name>TopSpacer") is HALF a group divider (G::groupSeparatorHeight / 2), the band playing the rule's part; levelBody's top margin above Edge is the same half divider; the Edge/Halo MaskEditor is fitted with no slack (PanelEditor::fitHeight(0)) so the rule under Halo sits at divider spacing; submask rows are shorter than tree rows, so SubmaskList pads above the first row by rowPad() = (G::propertyRowHeight() - row height) / 2, and MaskPanel::syncAttrVisible leaves G::groupSeparatorHeight / 2 + rowPad() under the last row (only when no submask is open) before the Basic band.

SubmaskList (Develop/Properties/submasklist.h) lists the mask's components IN FOLD ORDER, and is the only way back into one. A rows container is rebuilt wholesale by setSubmasks(rows, selected), and EVERY emission is DEFERRED a tick (QTimer::singleShot(0)), because the handler loops back through setSubmasks and deletes the very row the click is inside. Per row:

- the caption "&lt;tool> Submask" ("Brush Submask"), rewritten in syncMaskPanel (maskToolName itself still says "... Mask", for history, the canvas legend and the dialog), with " (null)" appended for an AI submask whose model found nothing (autoSubmaskIsNull, 2026-10-20): Subject / Background read SubjectRef::noSubject / noBackground, Sky reads SkyRef::noSky, each set ONCE by markEmpty when MW::ensureSubjectMask / ensureSkyMask builds the ref (under 0.05% of the map at >= 0.25 coverage, or for Background <= 0.75) -- the sky map can be 4096 px, too big to rescan per sync. A ref lands inside a render, so those two then queue DevelopProperties::autoMaskResultsChanged (-> syncMaskPanel). No ref yet (building, or the model missing) is not null. Read on the model's result, before the submask's own Invert;
- an OP BUTTON left of the eye (SubmaskList::opIcon paints +, - or an arch for Intersect at runtime, matching new.png's 2 px grey strokes); each click cycles Add -> Subtract -> Intersect. The FIRST submask has none (nothing to combine with; its tooltip says it always adds);
- an EYE (MaskComponent::enabled: the fold skips a disabled component, so it is a one-click A/B);
- a [:] menu: Edit / op / Invert / Move up / Move down / Duplicate / Delete.

DevelopProperties owns the model side: reopenSubmask, setSubmaskEnabled, setSubmaskOp, toggleSubmaskInverted, moveSubmask, duplicateSubmask and deleteMask; each mutates, fixes up selectedMaskIndex / pendingIdx, noteEdit()s, buildTree()s and emits paramsChanged(). syncMaskPanel() at the end of buildTree() is the single refresh point, so the list tracks image, scope and mask changes without any caller remembering to update it. SubmaskList::opGlyph() is public so the dialog and the row cannot drift.

- Deleting the last submask deletes the mask (2026-10-14): a mask with no submasks covers nothing, so deleteMask removes the scope too (as deleteScope would) and records ONE History step, "Delete &lt;mask name>", so a single undo restores the mask with its submask.
- Folding the mask closes what is open (2026-09-21): folding used to hide only the rows, while selectedMaskIndex and MaskPanel::attrShown survived, so the open submask's HANDLES stayed live on the canvas with no row on screen, and syncAttrVisible re-revealed its settings on the next expand (which read as though EXPANDING had selected a submask). MaskPanel::maskFoldedChanged -> DevelopProperties::onMaskFolded now flushes any unsettled submask and calls closeSubmaskEditing(). The fix belongs on COLLAPSE: expanding is then pure disclosure.
- The row is a TOGGLE (2026-08-24): clicking the row of the submask that is ALREADY open closes it (reopenSubmask's `if (index == selectedMaskIndex)` calls closeSubmaskEditing(): deselect, keep the mask latched, buildTree to take the handles off the canvas, hide the tint). A pending submask lands first, because closing it is the user saying they are done. The row [:]'s first item reads "Close &lt;tool> settings" when that row is the open one.

Committed submasks re-open (2026-08-13). commitPendingMask() used to set selectedMaskIndex = -1 ("committed submasks don't re-open"), making the mask a WRITE-ONLY PILE: a committed submask could not be reshaped, re-tuned, disabled, reordered, re-op'd or even deleted (deleteMask existed with no reachable caller). The data model always supported it (enabled / op / inverted / feather / paramsJson per component, order = array order, all in the sidecar); only the UI threw it away. Now commit ends the PENDING session and nothing else, and clicking a row calls reopenSubmask(): selectedMaskIndex moves, pendingIdx goes to -1, the settings load into the panel's MaskEditor, and buildTree()'s updateMaskEdit() re-arms the on-canvas overlay (maskEditBegin already fires for any selectedMaskIndex across all tools). Every mask mutator writes through selectedMaskIndex, so they work on a re-opened submask unchanged. Two states:

- PENDING (pendingIdx >= 0): auto-commits two seconds after its last edit; Esc discards it; its op follows the dialog's choice and the held modifier (latched).
- EXISTING (pendingIdx &lt; 0, selectedMaskIndex >= 0): its edits are already real, so Esc / Return / the row just close it, and MODIFIERS ARE INERT (setPendingMaskOp returns early; a stray Opt press rewriting a committed submask's op would be an invisible edit). Its op is changed on its own row.

#### 11.15.9 The Create Submask Dialog

Develop/Properties/submaskdialog.h, SubmaskDialog (2026-09-21), titled "Create submask" (2026-10-14). Adding a submask asks two questions TOGETHER: the ACTION ("Action:" section: Add / Subtract / Intersect radio buttons carrying the same glyph the row will wear, with a line each saying what it does to the mask), and the TYPE (the tool list in the old pop-up's order, its two separators promoted to headings: Drawn / Content / Automatic; names without maskToolName()'s " Mask" suffix). OK reads "Create".

- Why: the old bare QMenu of tool names could only ask half the question. The op came from a modifier held at some LATER instant, which is undiscoverable (nothing said Opt subtracts until you were already painting) and easy to lose (the bug latchMaskOp was added to paper over). Asking up front makes the op a written choice.
- First submask: an empty mask has nothing to combine with, so Subtract and Intersect are disabled AND the reason is on screen (three greyed radio buttons do not explain themselves). beginMaskTool(tool, op) forces Add there regardless.
- Nothing is preselected in the type list, and Create is disabled until a row is picked: the tool is the one thing the dialog cannot guess, and a default row would be added by a stray Return. Double-click a row to accept in one gesture.
- The modifiers stay as the shortcut, but their resting point moved: DevelopProperties::chosenMaskOp holds what the dialog picked, and latchMaskOp falls back to IT (not Add) when a shaping action happens with nothing held. beginMaskTool seeds pendingOp / latchedMaskOp / chosenMaskOp from the dialog, so the veil, the render and the op chip preview the chosen op from the first instant. The component still carries op = Add until the submask lands (commitPendingMask writes pendingOp).
- Removed with the menu: DevelopProperties::newMask() (which parsed the op back out of an action's TEXT: "Add Subject Mask".section(' ', 1)), maskToolFromName(), the maskMenu member and an unreachable Add/Subtract menu builder after showMaskMenu()'s early return.

#### 11.15.10 The Veil Follows Engagement

2026-09-21. The veil has a RULE instead of ten hand-written hides: DevelopProperties::maskVeilEngaged() = maskOverlayActive() && (maskPanelHovered || lastInteractionWasMask); syncMaskVeilEngagement() emits maskTintShowRequested / HideRequested ONLY on a change.

- It replaced ten `if (maskOverlayActive()) emit maskTintHideRequested();` calls in the adjustment handlers (the Basic/Color/Effects catch-all in itemChange, the WB temp/tint pair, gradeLum, calHue/calSat, the delegate's slider-caption click and four more), each of which could only HIDE the veil; once it went it stayed gone. Those sites now call noteNonMaskInteraction().
- Canvas editing counts as engagement: noteMaskInteraction() is called from setActiveMaskParams (every handle drag, brush stroke and pipette pick), onMaskEditorSetting, onMaskLevelSetting, the SubmaskList mutators, beginMaskTool, setPendingMaskOp and closeSubmaskEditing, which is what lets the user move the cursor off the panel onto the photo to paint without the veil dropping out.
- The hover source: MaskPanel installs itself as an event filter on qApp and answers only QEvent::Enter / Leave, recomputing `rect().contains(mapFromGlobal(QCursor::pos()))` and emitting hoverChanged(bool). Not enterEvent / leaveEvent: moving onto a CHILD sends the panel a Leave, and SubmaskList rebuilds its rows wholesale, so there is no stable set of children to watch. hideEvent syncs too (a panel disappearing under the cursor is a Leave that never arrives).
- "O" overrides with no override flag: MW::toggleMaskOverlay calls setMaskVeilOverride(imageView->maskTintVisible()), which records the veil's REAL state in maskVeilEngagedNow (the value engagement is compared against). Nothing is emitted until the user's attention actually moves, and that first genuine transition retires the override.
- A second submask no longer starts hidden (beginMaskTool): the veil now distinguishes the submask being built from the rest of the mask, which is what a second submask needs.
- This sits inside the explicit-only rule in [11.15.5 Mask Tint](#11155-mask-tint): engagement applies once the overlay has been shown (maskOverlayActive()).

Mask, submask and overlap in one hue (MW::updateMaskOverlayTint): with a submask open, the veil says which part of the mask IS that submask by varying the DENSITY of the one overlay colour: mask only at alpha 150, overlap at 215, and the submask where it falls OUTSIDE the mask at 55, plus a white contour with a dark halo along the submask's boundary, drawn over all of it.

- Written as a blend, a = 150\*m\*(1-s) + 215\*m\*s + 55\*(1-m)\*s, not three branches: coverage is FEATHERED, so m and s are weights in 0..1 and a gradient's ramp has to stay a ramp. With s == 0 it reduces exactly to the old single-term veil.
- One hue on purpose: the overlay colour is user-configurable across six values including white, and there is a greyscale backdrop, so any fixed contrast colour collides with at least two of them.
- The focus submask is DevelopProperties::focusSubmaskIndex() (pending if there is one, else selectedMaskIndex), so a committed submask reopened from the list gets the same treatment. Its coverage is buildMaskBuffer({c}, ...) with op forced to Add and the mask-level Edge withheld, so the buffer is the submask's own footprint rather than its signed contribution.
- The contour matters most for SUBTRACT: a Subtract submask contributes NOTHING to the folded mask, so no variation of the mask's own fill can show where it is. It is entirely in the 55 ghost, inside its outline.
- The ring it replaced was drawn only where the result was ABSENT (buf &lt;= 0.12), so the boundary vanished the moment the submask overlapped the mask, the common case. The density step now carries the overlap, so the line is drawn everywhere, with two safeguards against a Colour/Luminance Range submask fogging the subject: the boundary is taken from a 3x3 box average of the coverage (killing isolated speckle), and if the line still covers more than 8% of the buffer it is dropped and the densities carry the distinction alone.
- ImageView is unchanged: it is handed one finished premultiplied ARGB QImage via setScopeMaskTint.
- Cost: the second buildMaskBuffer runs whenever a submask is SELECTED, not only while one is pending; watch the [DevTime] tint line.

#### 11.15.11 Brush Attributes Have Three Scopes

Size, feather, flow and auto-mask are BAKED INTO EACH STROKE as it is drawn (ImageView writes them into the stroke object; BrushStamp reads them back per stroke), which is what lets one submask hold strokes of different sizes. So the same slider can mean three things, and a slider whose effect you cannot predict reads as broken:

- ADDING (pendingIdx >= 0): the NEXT stroke (brushWith).
- ADDING + Shift, with a stroke already painted: the LAST STROKE only (brushLastStrokeWith), "I just painted that, make it softer". The component's next-stroke default is deliberately NOT touched.
- SELECTED (pendingIdx &lt; 0, re-opened from the list): EVERY stroke (brushStrokesWith). Nothing is being painted, so there is no next stroke to arm; a slider that only armed would change nothing. Shift is deliberately inert here; it belongs to the act of painting.

The attribute scope header (MaskPanel::setAttributeScope, text from DevelopProperties::maskAttributeScopeText) is a dim caption just above the settings naming the state in force: "Attribute adjustment applies to 7 strokes" (singular at 1), "... to next stroke", "... to last stroke", or for a non-stroke tool "Attribute adjustment applies to this Linear Gradient submask". It is LIVE: MW's modifier filter calls syncAttributeScopeLabel() on every Shift press and release, so it names the scope the next drag will use BEFORE the drag. A stroke tool with nothing painted yet always reads "next stroke".

#### 11.15.12 Mask-Level Edge and Halo

Under the Mask band (MaskPanel::buildMaskLevel, 2026-08-24): a collapse arrow + caption + [:], the band painted by MaskPanel's paintEvent mapping the band rect with mapTo() (the band is a GRANDCHILD: levelWrap > levelBand; levelWrap, levelBand and levelBody are all WA_TranslucentBackground, or the app stylesheet's opaque QWidget fill would paint over the gradient). Edge appears TWICE in the panel (once for the folded mask, once in a selected submask's settings), and the band is what says which is which. It opens by default, and its collapse is view state only.

- No band eye, breaking the usual eye-then-[:] pair on purpose: Edge and Halo reshape the mask rather than contribute to it, so there is nothing to show or hide. "Reset mask Edge, Halo and Opacity" -> DevelopProperties::resetMaskLevel zeroes Edge and Halo and puts Opacity back to 1 on the active scope, leaving each submask's own Edge alone.
- The mask-level row is a SECOND MaskEditor (MaskPanel::levelEditor(), populated by showMaskLevel(), keys "scopeMaskEdge" / "scopeHalo" / "scopeOpacity", handled by onMaskLevelSetting), not a row inside the first editor, because that one is rebuilt per selected submask and hides when none is. History labels are "Edge" and "Mask edge", so the two levels are distinguishable.
- Opacity (2026-10-20): the long-reserved EditScope::opacity (0..1, always serialized, sanitized) made live -- the "Opacity" row under Halo, in percent, history "Mask opacity". Carried as StackRenderJob::Scope::opacity; MW::developCompositeStack scales the FOLDED coverage buffer by it right after buildMaskBuffer, so the blend, the scope's kaleidoscope (foldMasks) and "Hide global image" all read the scaled mask, and the Detail 1:1 patch samples it too. Below 1 it is appended to that scope's MASK cache key ("#op..."), not the params key: the scaled buffer is what is cached, and firstDirty then re-blends from this scope while the hot layer (its developed pixels) stays reusable -- so an opacity drag re-blends without re-developing, and a cached prefix can never keep an old opacity. A scope with no mask (whole image) has no coverage and ignores it. Carried by sameScopeState / copyScopeState (multi-image links). The mask tint overlay is NOT scaled: it shows the mask's shape.
- The footprint (updateMaskOverlayTint's second buildMaskBuffer call) is passed scopeEdge 0 on purpose: it tracks the submask, not the assembled mask.
- Known gap: the loupe's gradient / radial HANDLES draw from the stored geometry, so a Radial at Edge +40 renders larger than its drawn outline.

##### 11.15.12.1 Edge (Grow / Shrink)

2026-08-23. TWO sliders, both -100..100, both "1 unit = 1 pixel OF THE FULL-RESOLUTION IMAGE": MaskComponent::edge on each submask (MaskEditor::showTool, every case including default:, so all tools have it; handled by onMaskEditorSetting), and EditScope::maskEdge on the mask as a whole. Positive dilates, negative erodes. The two compose: submask +5 inside mask -3 nets +2.

Why it is not feather: feather SOFTENS an edge, it does not MOVE one, and it is not a pixel distance for any tool (a fraction of a radius on Radial, of the p1->p2 length on Linear, of a value band on the Range tools, of an alpha threshold band on Subject/Sky/Object). Edge is Photoshop's Select > Modify > Expand/Contract: "this AI cutout lands two pixels inside the subject, push it out two pixels". On the Range tools a small negative Edge is the cheapest way to kill thresholding speckle, and a small positive one closes pinholes.

Resolution independence is the whole contract. buildMaskBuffer takes a pixelScale (this render's long edge / the FULL-RES long edge) and converts before anything else: src.renderScale at the composite call, developProxy->renderScale at the veil (renderScale COMPOUNDS against the original full res, so deriving it from buffer widths would disagree whenever the cached WorkingImage is itself capped), and sc\*work->renderScale on the veil's 1600-cap branch. At a \~0.3 proxy a 1-unit nudge is a 0.3 px radius, which is why MaskEdge interpolates fractional radii instead of rounding them.

The mechanism (Develop/maskedge.h, header-only, tests/unit/tst_maskedge.cpp): grayscale morphology, because dilating by a flat structuring element TRANSLATES a soft edge rigidly (the feather profile rides along instead of being reshaped).

- The structuring element is an OCTAGON, square(a) (+) diamond(b) with a = r(sqrt2-1), b = r(2-sqrt2), decomposed into FOUR separable 1-D passes (horizontal, vertical, and the two diagonals at strides w+1 and w-1). A plain separable square would be half the cost and was rejected: it displaces a 45-degree boundary by r\*1.414, a 41% error against a "1 unit = 1 pixel" contract, and would put the analytic and buffer tools 41% apart on the same diagonal edge. The octagon is exact on the axes AND the diagonals and overshoots at most 8.2% at its vertices.
- Each pass is van Herk / Gil-Werman (forward prefix + backward suffix extremum over blocks of the window width), so cost is O(1) per pixel REGARDLESS of radius.
- Samples are uint16 (MaskFalloff::kCutoff is 1/512, so 16 bits is \~7 bits finer than the profile promises), and every pass is IN PLACE (a line is gathered into a per-thread scratch, processed and written back).

Two analytic tools, eight buffer tools:

- Linear and Radial Gradient fold Edge into their GEOMETRY in parseMaskComp and never touch a buffer. Linear precomputes tShift = edgePx \* |grad t|, EXACT (dilating a ramp monotone along its normal by a disc is precisely a translation). Radial adds edgePx to both semi-axes (exact for a circle, the standard ellipse approximation otherwise), and its feather rides the radius rather than translating, deliberately: Edge then behaves exactly like dragging the radius handle.
- The other eight (Brush, Luminance/Colour Range, Depth, Subject, Sky, Background, Object) are materialised and morphed. Brush deliberately does NOT grow each dab radius (dilation distributes over union, so it would be exact for grow): it would change the brushRasterCached key, re-rasterising every stroke every tick; it would grow INSIDE an auto-mask stroke's confinement when the user means to push past it; and dab feather is a fraction of dab radius, so +1 then -1 would not return. The AI tools morph their per-component w\*h buffer, never the ref: Subject/Sky/Depth refs are SHARED per path across components.
- A zero semi-axis: parseMaskComp used to return valid=false for one and the caller did `if (!g.valid) continue`, DROPPING the component. Dropping is not the same as empty (under Intersect an empty component must zero the mask; under Subtract it must be a no-op). Unreachable from the UI until Edge made shrinking a small radial to nothing an ordinary drag; now clamped to a 1e-3 px epsilon.

The fold is SEGMENTED, not restructured. buildMaskBuffer's fold is a per-pixel scalar loop with no neighbourhood access, so an Edge-bearing component cannot be evaluated inline. Maximal runs of edge==0 components keep the original interleaved fold (a mask nobody has run the slider on costs exactly what it did); each edge!=0 component becomes its own segment: materialise (its `inverted` applied, which puts invert BEFORE the morphology, so growing an inverted mask shrinks the original), morph, fold with its op. ONE uint16 scratch serves every such component AND the mask-level pass: at 45 MP that is 90 MB held once instead of 180 MB of float PER SUBMASK (on a 22-submask scope, the difference between a transient allocation and an OOM). One pass per component over the whole fold was rejected for the opposite reason: 22 read-modify-write passes over 45 MP is \~8 GB of traffic. The per-tool eval switch is hoisted into evalCompAt() so the inline fold and the materialiser cannot drift.

The mask-level pass runs AFTER the prefix snapshot, never before: the prefix is a PARTIAL fold, and morphing it would hand every later resume a shape that is not a prefix of anything. It also runs on the EMPTY-comps early return, because dragging that slider changes no component signature, so a fully resumed prefix is exactly the path it takes every tick. Cache keys: MaskComponent::edge is in maskComponentSignature (which keys both the fold-prefix cache and the per-scope mask cache), and EditScope::maskEdge is appended by maskComponentsSignature(components, scopeEdge); leaving it out would make the mask-level slider move nothing.

##### 11.15.12.2 Halo

2026-08-24. ONE slider, 0..100, at MASK level only (EditScope::maskHalo, panel key "scopeHalo"). It answers what Edge and Feather cannot: when a mask boundary does not land on the subject's real edge, a masked tone/colour adjustment lifts a RIM OF BACKGROUND and reads as a glow around the subject. Feather sets the WIDTH of the transition band, not its position; Edge slides the whole boundary a uniform distance, so wherever the mask's error is not uniform it trades a halo on one side for a bitten edge on the other. Halo FADES THE ADJUSTMENT OUT ACROSS the picture's edge, leaving the boundary where the user put it. Mask level only, because a halo is a property of the final folded boundary, and it then costs one pass per scope rather than per submask. Disabled, with the reason in the tooltip, on an all-gradient mask (maskHasRealEdge in developproperties.cpp): pure geometry has no relationship to anything in the image.

- It is an ALPHA operation, which is why it lives in buildMaskBuffer and not in the compositor. Compositing is a per-pixel lerp (acc = acc\*(1-m) + scope\*m, WorkingImageCache::renderStack), so "weaken the adjustment near the edge" is identical to "multiply the alpha near the edge", and doing it on the alpha keeps a mask a PURE FUNCTION OF ITS COMPONENTS, which the per-scope render cache assumes.
- The guide is the UNDEVELOPED working image (buildHaloGuide in mainwindow.cpp), perceptual luma (pow 1/2.2, the mask BLEND's encoding), built ONCE per render tick and shared by every scope. Not the developed result, which would move every time a slider moved (the mask reshaping itself in response to the adjustment it masks). Not RangeMask::RangeRef, which is fixed at \~1024 px, so the full-res settle and export would snap to a blurry guide. developCompositeStack already holds the WorkingImage it sizes the mask from, so the guide is on EXACTLY the mask's grid.
- The mechanism (Develop/maskhalo.h, header-only, tests/unit/tst_maskhalo.cpp): the mask's boundary NEIGHBOURHOOD is found by blurring the alpha and taking 4\*b\*(1-b) (1 where the blurred mask is halfway, 0 in the solid interior and clean exterior). ("Wherever 0 &lt; alpha &lt; 1" was tried first and does nothing on a crisp mask, where that band is one pixel wide.) The guide's Scharr gradient is spread over the reach radius by a LOCAL MAX, not a blur (Scharr responds over three pixels, so the raw magnitude is a hairline that cuts a two-pixel notch and leaves the rim beyond it fully adjusted; dilation answers "is there a committed edge within reach of this pixel" without attenuating the peak). Then alpha \*= 1 - amount\*edge\*band.
- The slider is REACH: how far out a halo can be and still be found, which is what varies between pictures. The damping BAND width is FIXED (kDampBandPx), because widening it would eat further into the subject.
- Order, cache, veil: Halo runs immediately AFTER applyScopeEdge on both of buildMaskBuffer's exit paths (Edge is a deliberate uniform offset, and Halo works from the picture's edges against that offset boundary), after the fold-prefix snapshot. maskComponentsSignature takes the amount alongside scopeEdge. The veil passes the same value (activeScopeMaskHalo) and builds its guide from developProxy; on the capped fallback path (no proxy yet) it draws the UNSUPPRESSED mask for that moment rather than a guide resampled off the wrong grid.

Refine was built, tested and REJECTED (2026-08-24), recorded because it is the obvious thing to reach for again: instead of fading the adjustment, MOVE the alpha (guided-filter the folded mask against the picture, SegRefine::guidedFilterGray, then pinch about 0.5 to kill the residual fringe). It passed its displacement tests (a boundary 6 px out pulled to within 2 px, monotonic in the slider, preview matching render across a 0.4 proxy), and IN THE LOUPE IT BLURRED THE HALO RATHER THAN REMOVING IT. A guided filter reconstructs the alpha as a local linear function of the guide, and a wide window over a soft, low-contrast boundary (fur, hair, foliage, exactly where masks miss) has no sharp answer to converge on, so it returns a smooth ramp. Damping never has to decide where the edge IS, only that one is near. The unit tests' synthetic step edge is precisely the case Refine was good at, which is why they passed and a photograph caught it. Do not re-add the guided-filter path without a real picture it beats damping on.

Retired sidecar key: both algorithms shipped briefly behind a method combo, so sidecars written on 2026-08-24 may carry "maskHaloMode" (0 = Refine, 1 = Damp, 2 = Both). It is no longer read or written, but the NAME must never be reused (see [11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)](#1139-stale-presets-and-history-schema-drift)). A maskHalo value dialled in while Refine was selected now renders as damping, a one-off break confined to that day's test images.

#### 11.15.13 The Mask Tint Button

The swatch on the Mask band toggles the mask overlay tint, the same thing O does (MW::toggleMaskOverlay -> ImageView::toggleMaskTint), and gives that otherwise invisible key a home in the UI. It carries NO glyph; it IS the swatch: MW::refreshDevelopMaskTintBtn paints a 12x12 rounded chip filled with G::maskOverlayColor into the 16x16 BarBtn (12, so the active border has room), dimmed to G::iconOpacity while the tint is off. It is repainted from ImageView's maskTintVisibilityChanged (the key, the scope menu, the slider auto-hide), maskTintAvailabilityChanged and DevelopProperties::maskOverlayRefreshRequested (the colour changed), so the swatch and the border stay true whatever changed the state.

Nothing to tint: the tint exists only while there is something to show. When there is not, the swatch paints HOLLOW (an outline in the overlay colour) at half G::iconOpacity, and a left-click (or O) says why in a message instead of doing nothing. The button stays ENABLED on purpose: its right-click menu must be reachable without a mask, and a disabled QToolButton would swallow that too. maskTintAvailabilityChanged is emitted from beginMaskEdit / endMaskEdit / setScopeMaskTint / clearScopeMaskTint, each guarded so only a real null &lt;-> non-null transition fires (setScopeMaskTint runs every drag tick). The scope menu omits its "Show mask overlay" row when unavailable (ScopeHeader::maskOverlayAvailable), so the two agree.

Availability is "has a mask", not "has a built veil" (fixed 2026-10-09). Once the tint started hidden, keying availability off scopeMaskTint became a deadlock: MW::updateMaskOverlayTint returns before building the veil while it is hidden, so on a mask scope with no submask open, scopeMaskTint stayed null, availability was false, and O / the button refused with the no-mask message on a scope that plainly had a working mask. Now maskTintAvailable() == maskEditMode || scopeHasMask || !scopeMaskTint.isNull(). updateMaskOverlayTint calls ImageView::setScopeHasMask(true) once it has an enabled component list, BEFORE the hidden early-out; every "nothing to tint" early-out goes through clearScopeMaskTint, which also clears scopeHasMask, as does endMaskEdit. toggleMaskTint / hideMaskTint gate on maskTintAvailable() rather than re-deriving it.

A new submask shows the tint (2026-10-09), the one automatic show: choosing a submask in SubmaskDialog emits maskOverlayShowRequested -> ImageView::showMaskTint, so the user sees the new submask build. It is a separate signal from maskTintShowRequested on purpose (that is the veil-engagement auto-show, which stays disconnected). The adjustment-slider auto-hide still applies afterwards.

Right-click (MW::showDevelopMaskTintMenu) is the ONLY place the overlay's two APPEARANCE settings live: the colour, and the grayscale background. The Mask panel's swatch + "Gray" row was removed on 2026-08-15, because those settings describe the veil rather than any submask, and in the submask editor they were unreachable without a mask open. Colours and names come from MaskPanel::overlayColours() / overlayColourNames(); both settings are applied through DevelopProperties::setMaskOverlayColour / setMaskOverlayGrayscale, which update the G:: flag, persist it (Develop/maskOverlayColor, Develop/maskOverlayGrayscale) and ask for the right redraw: a colour rebuilds the veil (maskOverlayRefreshRequested); grayscale is view-only, so it just repaints (maskOverlayRepaintRequested).

#### 11.15.14 Submask Order

Order is the result (moveSubmask): components fold sequentially, so a Subtract placed before the Add it was meant to cut into does nothing. The fold-prefix cache resumes at the longest matching prefix of per-component signatures, so a move / delete / toggle at index k invalidates [k..n) and keeps [0..k) with no cache work. No sidecar change was needed: enabled, op, inverted, feather, params and the array order were always written.

#### 11.15.15 The Mask Composite

The render composites the WHOLE stack in SCENE-LINEAR before the output transform, independent of which scope is active for editing, so a saved mask is visible the moment the image loads. DevelopProperties::stackJob() captures it as plain values (Global params + each enabled non-Global scope's params / masks), so it is safe for the off-thread renders. WorkingImageCache::renderStack starts from Global, then for each scope develops the RUNNING ACCUMULATOR with that scope's params (an identity scope aliases acc: no copy, no Develop) and blends back by its mask (acc = acc\*(1-m) + scope\*m); one final OutputTransform. developComposite remains the fast single-pass path when there are no masks.

- Where two scopes' masks OVERLAP, their adjustments COMPOUND (two overlapping +1-stop scopes give \~+2 stops in the overlap), because each develops the accumulated result. In scene-linear this per-op composition is natural (exposure multiplies). Scope order therefore matters for non-commuting ops.
- The mask blend space is a flag, kPerceptualMaskBlend in workingimagecache.cpp. A = lerp in scene-linear (physically faithful, but a STRONG masked adjustment's visible falloff is front-loaded: display gamma steepens it near m=1, so a linear feather reads abrupt at the edge). B, the current choice, = lerp in a PERCEPTUAL (gamma 2.2) space, so displayed brightness tracks m roughly linearly and a feather reads evenly (matching the coverage tint). Only feather pixels (0 &lt; m &lt; 1) pay the pow; m &lt;= 0 skip, m >= 1 copy.
- buildMaskBuffer (mainwindow.cpp) rasterises a scope's components at WorkingImage (pre-orientation) resolution; each pixel maps work-normalised -> output-normalised (output = work rotated CW by degrees), so geometry edited on the oriented loupe lines up after the EXIF rotation. parseMaskComp / evalMaskComp branch by tool: Linear = a projection ramp; Radial = distance in the ellipse's local frame, computed in OUTPUT-PIXEL space so the ellipse keeps its aspect and rotation, which IS the MaskFalloff t.
- Components combine in order: Add = union (max), Subtract = \*(1-c), Intersect = \*c, Invert flips (applied before the component's own morphology). A non-analytic component samples its own buffer.
- Every mask add / delete / geometry / feather / invert change and every brush stroke (live during the swipe, throttled, and again on release) emits paramsChanged() to re-render.

#### 11.15.16 Brush

Vector strokes in paramsJson: {size, flow, autoMask, strokes:[{pts, size, feather, flow, erase, autoMask}]}. Each stroke snapshots its settings; the current settings drive the next stroke. autoMaskMode ("lum" | "ai") is a RETIRED key: old sidecars still read, the value is ignored. Defaults: feather 0 (crisp), flow 100. Strokes are rasterised by Develop/brushstamp.h, shared with ImageView's preview so they match, into a work-space coverage buffer cached by brushRasterCached (paramsJson + dims + degrees + guide dims; mutex-guarded; only proxy-size buffers are cached, since full res is \~w\*h\*4 bytes and built once per settle).
