Painting on the loupe (ImageView): left-drag paints. Dabs accumulate per stroke by MAX, then are composited with flow (build-up across strokes). Cmd/Ctrl+Z removes the last stroke. ImageView needs focus (set on brush enter) and claims [ ] A from their global action shortcuts via QEvent::ShortcutOverride.

- Feather is Lightroom's model: it softens INWARD through the shared MaskFalloff profile and does not change the footprint (size = the outer extent, fixed). It pulls the half-coverage radius inward with a rounder falloff and no flat core (feather 0 = a hard edge at the size ring; 100 = fully soft). It pairs with the perceptual blend, so the displayed effect tracks coverage as Lightroom's does.
- The cursor is two rings: the OUTER ring is the brush SIZE (the total extent; the dab is clipped there), and when feather > 0 an INNER ring at the HALF-COVERAGE radius (MaskFalloff::Shape::h) marks the feather, matching Lightroom's cursor and the Radial's dashed ellipse. Each ring is drawn twice (a dark halo under the coloured line) so it is visible on light AND dark images. Colour: green = auto-mask, pink = erase, white = plain.
- A centre glyph says what the work will do: a plus in the ring colour when adding, a RED MINUS when subtracting, a RED CROSS when intersecting (skipped when the brush is smaller than the glyph). It polls the HELD MODIFIER (QGuiApplication::queryKeyboardModifiers, the same read maskOpFromModifiers uses) ORed with the legend op, so it answers "what does Opt do right now?" even on the first submask, and a LATCHED subtract keeps the minus after the key is released. With the erase stroke on, maskBrushErase is latched at mouse-press, so on hover the cursor PREDICTS it from the Opt key held. MW::eventFilter's Alt/Shift branch repaints the loupe, because it eats the Alt KeyPress and an unchanged op returns early.
- Size is a % of the long edge at 0.1 resolution (ImageView::kBrushSizeStep): the dock slider is a div-10 row (1..1000 = 0.1..100.0), and every path (canvas gesture, slider, sidecar) quantises to the same step through ImageView::setBrushSize / DevelopProperties::setActiveBrushSize. The floor is ImageView::maskBrushSizeMin(), a \~3 px diameter on the image (the spotSizeMin rule), never coarser than one step (the old whole-percent round made the smallest brush \~60 px on a 6000 px file).
- [ / ] and the wheel / two-finger drag (gated to brush + hover) resize RELATIVELY (ImageView::scaleBrushSize: x1.15 per key, \~x1.0075 per wheel pixel; a fixed delta crawls at 80% and jumps from 0.5 to 5), falling back to one step when the proportional move is below the quantum -> maskBrushSizeRequested -> setActiveBrushSize. Shift + wheel is the feather -> maskFeatherRequested -> setActiveMaskFeather. "A" toggles auto-mask (maskBrushAutoMaskRequested -> setActiveBrushAutoMask).
- The canvas size and feather gestures ALWAYS arm the next stroke and never rewrite strokes already painted (2026-10-14). They used to go retroactive once the submask landed, and since a submask lands on its own while the user is still painting, the wheel that sized the cursor a moment earlier suddenly grew or re-feathered the whole brush mask. Rewriting existing strokes is the panel slider's job (see [11.15.11 Brush Attributes Have Three Scopes](#111511-brush-attributes-have-three-scopes)); setActiveBrushAutoMask still takes the pending/existing split. Per-stroke VARIATION is lost the moment a selected brush's slider is touched (every stroke takes the new value); Cmd+Z restores it.
- MW's modifier/commit block is gated on isSubmaskOpen() (any open submask), not isMaskPanelOpen() (a pending one), so Return/Esc and the attribute header follow a re-opened submask too; syncPendingMaskOp keeps the op preview itself pending-only.

The develop effect follows the swipe. The in-progress stroke is handed to the dock mid-stroke (brushEmitLiveGeometry -> maskGeometryChanged -> setActiveMaskParams -> paramsChanged), THROTTLED to kMaskStrokeLiveMs (100 ms) because each tick costs a proxy render of the whole stroke set. The throttle has a TRAILING edge (one scheduled catch-up emit), so a stroke that pauses mid-swipe still settles as painted; the release emit is unconditional. brushParamsJson(withLiveStroke) is the single builder for the live, release and undo emits.

The veil during a stroke:

- While an ADD stroke is swiped, the whole-mask veil is SUPPRESSED (drawForeground's brushStroking guard, ImageView::maskBrushOwnsTint) so the per-brush live preview shows the stroke building up, and MW::updateMaskOverlayTint returns early while it is in flight (maskStrokeInFlight). The local preview is rebuilt only on the dirty segment bbox.
- The stand-in HOLDS PAST THE RELEASE: mouse-up sets maskBrushVeilStale, which setScopeMaskTint clears when MW pushes the veil rebuilt from the finished stroke. Without it the coverage blinked back to the PRE-stroke veil at mouse-up, exactly when the user reads the mask to place the next stroke. The hold is dropped when the local preview would not be drawn anyway (it is hover-gated), because off the image a stale veil beats no coverage.
- A SUBTRACT / INTERSECT stroke inverts both gates: the local preview paints the overlay colour exactly where the mask is being REMOVED (it reads as adding), so the real veil stays drawn and IS rebuilt on the live ticks, retreating under the brush. Whether a stroke is a subtract comes from DevelopProperties::focusSubmaskOp() (pending -> pendingOp; landed -> the component's own op; first or none -> Add). It used to ask pendingMaskOp(), which commitPendingMask resets to Add, so a stroke on a LANDED Subtract submask left the veil stale (fixed 2026-10-14).
- A stroke that PAUSES before the mouse comes up has its geometry carried by the throttled live emit, so the release emit arrives identical; setActiveMaskParams's identical branch emits maskOverlayRefreshRequested so the veil is still rebuilt after the stroke. setActiveMaskParams also refreshes the attribute header's "N strokes" count.

#### 11.15.17 Brush Auto-Mask

ONE checkbox and one algorithm ("A" toggles it). It attenuates each dab by an acceptance field evaluated in the SHARED rasteriser, so preview == render. Rewritten 2026-10-14 as a RELATIVE two-class model; tune it with several noise seeds.

The guide: a small YCbCr COLOUR map of the displayed image (BrushStamp::Guide, output-oriented), built from the loupe pixmap when the brush activates (ImageView::ensureAutoGuide) and registered by path (putGuide). The render samples the SAME guide (getGuide(fPath), threaded through developCompositeStack / buildMaskBuffer / brushRasterCached), so the confinement is identical in the overlay and the render. ensureAutoGuide sizes it so the brush DIAMETER spans at least kGuidePxPerDab (96) guide pixels, clamped to [1024, 3072], sized against the smallest brush it must serve (the loaded one AND every committed auto-masked stroke, so re-opening a submask re-rasterises its strokes on a guide at least as fine as the one they were painted with), rebuilding only ever finer. The guide dims are part of brushRasterCached's key.

Per DAB, in guide space (BrushStamp::buildDabField), the question is: does a pixel look more like the class under the crosshair or the OTHER class in the brush?

1. Search zone = the CORE. The fill runs only inside the core radius (the cursor's inner ring = MaskFalloff::Shape::h x radius; the whole dab at feather 0; dabMax passes it and the field cache keys on it). The FEATHER BAND never adds area: a band pixel takes the core value on its own radius just inside the rim, gated by its own class acceptance (with no other class learned, an ABSOLUTE gate: within the merge distance of a subject centre, fading to zero at twice it), then the dab's falloff fades it. Ungated, a rim meeting the edge at a slant projected past it and sawtoothed the stroke (one spike per dab).
2. Analysis scale. The box is blurred at a radius proportional to the core (kSmoothFrac, two box passes), with a TEXTURE plane: each pixel's distance from its own 3x3 mean, averaged over the window. (Fine scale on purpose: measured against the analysis blur, a plain step edge read as a band of texture and stopped the fill 10-30 px short of a light/dark wall edge.) A big dab is DECIMATED to \~kAnalysisDiameter pixels across (DabField carries `dec`). Features = Y, sqrt(2) x Cb/Cr, and texture on a LOG scale (kTexLogK x log2(1 + tex/kTexLogT)): texture contrast is a ratio, and over noise seeds every LINEAR texture weight that separated a fine texture from a smooth field also holed a uniform rough surface.
3. Classes. A deterministic k-means (kClusters = 5; farthest-point seeding from the median under the crosshair; no RNG, so it is a pure function for the render caches) over a subsample (&lt;= kKmSamples) of the disc's FLAT pixels: a pixel whose feature gradient exceeds kGradK x the disc median (floor kGradFloor) sits on a boundary and does not vote (skipped if that would drop over half the disc), because the blur turns a hard edge into in-between colours whose own clusters otherwise CHAINED the merge across a pure lightness edge. SUBJECT = every cluster holding kShareMin of the seed disc (kSeedFrac x core) plus the one nearest it, closed under a MERGE (closer than max(kMergeMin, kMergeSig x spread), kMergeSig 2.5, with Y down-weighted by kMergeYW: a surface's own light and shadow, pebbles or a sky gradient, is a lightness spread, while a silhouette still splits). Five clusters, not four: with four, gravel's three lightness modes left the background sharing a cluster with the ridge's transition pixels, which merged into the subject and painted one dab of sky. No OTHER class = one surface: the core paints whole (no holes in texture, unlike Lightroom's brush, which holes gravel on every pebble).
4. Likeness p = dO / (dS + dO) to the nearest subject / other centre; acceptance ramps over kPLo..kPHi.
5. A COST FILL from the seed disc (a monotone dial queue: Dijkstra in integer buckets, kCostLevels, 4-connected, core only). Each step onto a pixel with p &lt; 0.5 pays kStepK x (1-2p)^2 within a budget of 1.0, acceptance smoothstepping off as the budget runs out. Connectivity, so a look-alike patch beyond the edge is not painted. A 3x3 blur then softens the analysis-resolution staircase.

The dab's pixel loop bilinearly samples that 0..1 field (DabField::at) through an AFFINE target -> guide map solved once per dab (guideMapFor; degrees is the same rotation buildMaskBuffer uses), and the field is cached and reused while the centre has not moved a guide pixel. Per-dab cost \~0.4 ms at a 100-guide-px brush. Prototyped in Python on the user's screenshot plus synthetic cases (equal-lightness brown/grey, silhouette, texture vs smooth of one colour, blurred edge, sky gradient, uniform texture), the C++ diffed against it exactly; pinned by tests/unit/tst_brushstamp.cpp.

Known trade-off: a strong LIGHTNESS step inside one surface (a dark shadow streak in gravel, dY \~40) is the same signal as a light wall against a dark one (dY \~45), so it is respected as an edge, as Lightroom does. A looser merge that joined the streak leaked small soft dabs into the background at the gravel ridge, and a density-continuity test could not tell a defocused edge from a gradient.

##### 11.15.17.1 How It Got Here

- The first auto-mask compared each pixel's LUMINANCE against a single reference sampled at the STROKE START, within a fixed +-0.15 band, INDEPENDENTLY per pixel. All three parts failed on one photo (a brown cone on a grey background of the same lightness): equal luminance meant the background matched; a fixed band cannot cover a textured surface, so the object came out speckled; and a lone pixel needs no route back to the brush, so matching pixels beyond the edge were painted. Chroma answered the first, an adaptive tolerance the second, a flood fill the third. The guide was also a fixed 1024 px map of the whole frame, so a small brush on a big file decided everything from \~10 guide pixels of mush; hence the per-brush guide sizing.
- FUR (a squirrel's head on a soft brown background, 2026-09): the flood fill was a BINARY reachability test over a PER-PIXEL colour band, and fur's per-pixel spread is far wider than the step from fur to a background of the same family, so the tolerance opened to its ceiling, the background fell inside it, and the fill walked out through the hairy edge. The analysis SCALE (averaged over a few pixels the fur's noise collapses, making the boundary the largest thing in the box) and the COST fill (paying to cross it) fixed it, and a large brush got cheaper with decimation (a 600 px dab on a 1024 px guide went 5.7 ms -> 1.1 ms).
- A DEFOCUSED edge (textured gravel against smooth bokeh, 2026-10-14) then defeated the absolute model (median reference + a tolerance adapted to the centre window's spread + an edge term relative to the local texture): a dab on dark pebbles opened its tolerance to \~41 with the background \~38 away, and the soft edge's \~1.5/px gradient never cleared the edge term's floor of 4. Replaced by the relative class model above; kTolK / kEdgeK / kDrift and the tolerance are gone, while the analysis scale, decimation, guide sizing and cost fill carry over.
- An "AI edge (SAM)" auto-mask mode (confining a stroke to the SAM 2 object under its seed, \~1 s encode + 40 ms decode) was RETIRED in 2026-08: two auto-mask checkboxes is one too many ("just works" is the requirement), and on real edges it was no better than the colour algorithm at a far higher cost. Gone with it: the BrushStamp SAM-field store, MW::ensureBrushSamField(s) / onBrushSamFieldRequested / warmBrushSamEncoder, ObjectMaskPredictor::refinePoint and the maskAutoMaskAi row. The Object mask tool keeps the whole SAM 2 stack.

#### 11.15.18 Luminance Range and Color Range

Content-range masks: coverage depends on the pixel VALUE, not its position, so they need the image's pixels.

- Both measure on a SHARED display-referred reference (Develop/rangemask.h, RangeMask::RangeRef: interleaved RGB 0..1, output-oriented, capped \~1024), built and registered by path (putRef / getRef, mirroring BrushStamp's guide), so the loupe overlay and the render sample the IDENTICAL map.
- The reference is the developed GLOBAL scope only (Global params + OutputTransform + orientation; MW::ensureRangeRef via developComposite on a downscaled work), "what you see", so the selection tracks the base tones, and BASE-ONLY on purpose: measuring on the composite would let a range mask that shifts its own tones feed back on its own selection and oscillate.
- ensureRangeRef is cached (keyed on path + a base-params signature; run from renderDevelopPreview and renderDevelopFullResAsync only when a range mask exists), so a range-slider drag or a colour sample never rebuilds it, only re-thresholds. Because its coverage depends on the base, range-mask scopes fold the base signature into their mask key, and ensureRangeRef clears the fold-prefix cache (see [11.12.3 The Caches](#11123-the-caches)).
- buildMaskBuffer's range kind fetches getRef(fPath) once (absent -> the component yields 0) and per pixel calls RangeMask::lumCoverage / colorCoverage at the mapped output coordinates.

Luminance Range: paramsJson {lo, hi} (0..1 display luminance, Rec.601); coverage 1 inside [lo, hi] with a feathered band. Dock rows Range Min / Range Max / Feather / Invert; lo/hi changes emit maskRangeChanged -> ImageView::setMaskRangeParams (live tint). No canvas interaction.

Color Range: a HUE + SATURATION band selection in HSV (value ignored; brightness stays with Luminance Range). paramsJson {hueLo, hueHi (degrees 0..90), satLo, satHi (0..100 -> fractions), samples:[[r,g,b],...] 0..1 display}.

- Each sample fixes a centre (hue angle, sat radius; ColorSample via RangeMask::rgb2hs). Coverage is 1 where a pixel's hue lies in [centre-hueLo, centre+hueHi] AND its sat in [centre-satLo, centre+satHi] of ANY sample (a union), each edge feathered, with a small sat floor dropping near-neutral pixels. The four bounds widen the band INDEPENDENTLY in four directions (they replaced an earlier symmetric "refine" distance tolerance).
- The wheel: a spanned ColorRangeWheel index widget above the sliders (like the Color Grade wheel embed) paints the HSV disc, a dot per sample, the band SECTOR per sample, and four grab handles on the anchor (first) sample: two hue edges on the rim, each labelled with its ABSOLUTE hue in degrees, and inner/outer sat arcs. Dragging a handle changes the matching global bound; wheel and sliders stay in sync (onColorRangeWheelChanged writes params + guarded setSliderReal; slider drags call wheel->setBounds). The disc uses the SAME HSV as the coverage, so the wheel is a faithful picture of the selection.
- The eyedropper: with the tool active, a loupe click samples RangeRef under the cursor (the shared dropperCursor, as the WB pick), Shift-click ADDS another sample. Sampled colours draw as on-image swatches (bottom-left, viewport coordinates), and clicking a swatch removes it. The sampling loupe (ImageView::drawSampleLoupe, shared with the WB picker) follows the tip while hovering: a magnified 5x5 grid of the pixels under the tip with their RGB and HSL readout. Sample edits go through the existing geometry handshake (maskGeometryChanged -> setActiveMaskParams, which also refreshes the wheel dots).
- Dock rows: the wheel, then Hue Lo / Hue Hi / Sat Lo / Sat Hi / Feather / Invert.
- Deferred: a dual-handle luminance range slider, a per-scope "image below" reference for stacked range masks, an in-dock swatch strip.

The content tools' preview (ImageView::drawRangeMask / buildRangePreview, rebuildContentPreview) rebuilds on any dock param change or eyedropper edit and heals if the reference lands after the overlay began. Unlike the geometric tools (hover-gated, since their handles are pointer-relative), a content tool's coverage stays drawn as long as the tool is active (maskEditMode), even with the pointer off the view, so it is visible while adjusting Feather in the dock.

#### 11.15.19 Select Subject

An AI salient-object mask. Content-derived like the range masks, sharing their preview == render design, but its coverage is a FIXED saliency map produced once by the U^2-Net model rather than a per-tick threshold.

- The model runs through OpenCV DNN (cv::dnn::readNetFromONNX, the runtime FocusPredictor uses), wrapped in Utilities/subjectpredictor (SubjectPredictor): U^2-Net preprocessing (RGB, 320x320, /maxpixel, per-channel ImageNet mean/std). u2net.onnx (\~176 MB) is downloaded on demand by ModelStore (Model::U2Net), not shipped in git.
- GOTCHA: U^2-Net has 7 outputs (d0..d6), and OpenCV's forward() with no name returns the LAST-registered layer, a COARSE side output (d6, a fuzzy blob: the original "rough selection" bug). Outputs are fetched by name (getUnconnectedOutLayersNames) and outs[0] = d0, the fused full-res saliency, is used.
- The saliency is refined by the shared SegRefine::refine (Utilities/segrefine.h): upsampled to the reference size and guided-filtered against the developed base's luminance so the cutout snaps to the real subject boundary.
- MW::ensureSubjectMask (mirroring ensureRangeRef) develops the downscaled BASE scope (output-oriented), runs the model synchronously on the GUI thread with a busy cursor (\~200-400 ms, once per image), and registers the coverage by path (Develop/subjectmask.h, SubjectMask::SubjectRef). It is CACHED BY PATH ONLY: detection is independent of the develop sliders. It is called from renderDevelopPreview / renderDevelopFullResAsync only when a Subject mask exists (stackHasSubjectMask).
- buildMaskBuffer's isSubject kind fetches getRef(fPath) once (absent -> 0) and per pixel calls SubjectMask::coverage. paramsJson is empty; the dock shows Feather (a band around the 0.5 cutoff, softening the edge) and Invert (selects the background). The preview is ImageView::buildSubjectPreview.

Background, Depth Range, Object and Segmenter masks are in [11.16.1 More AI Masks](#11161-more-ai-masks). Still in development: when an AI mask model is replaced, the old one is replaced outright (no back-compatibility shims).

#### 11.15.20 Select Sky

A TWO-MODEL sky matte (rebuilt 2026-10-07). The wiring parallels Select Subject: Utilities/skypredictor SkyPredictor, Develop/skymask.h SkyMask store (separate from SubjectMask so both masks coexist on one image), MW::ensureSkyMask / stackHasSkyMask, an isSky component in buildMaskBuffer, ImageView::buildSkyPreview, tool == 6. Dock rows Feather + Invert.

The models, both through OpenCV DNN (so Select Sky works without ONNX Runtime; the Qt Creator Debug build has WINNOW_ENABLE_ORT=OFF), both downloaded on demand by ModelStore (Model::SkySeg, Model::SkySegFormer; onAiMaskEditBegin asks for both):

- skyseg.onnx: a U^2-Net sky net, 320x320 in, outs[0] = d0, a SIGMOID sky probability.
- sky_segformer.onnx: SegFormer-B4 trained on ADE20K, 512x512 in, 150-class logits at 128x128, sky = class 2 (softmax taken in skypredictor). A STATIC-SHAPE export: the stock HF export (Xenova/segformer-b4-finetuned-ade-512-512) has dynamic Shape nodes that OpenCV 4.13's importer rejects ("parseShape ... !isDynamicShape"); it was re-exported with the input pinned to 1x3x512x512 and simplified with onnxsim (ONNXSIM_FIXED_POINT_ITERS=500) until no Shape/Gather nodes remained, and verified against ONNX Runtime to 3e-5 logits with identical argmax. Its weights are NON-COMMERCIAL (see [2.11 Licenses and Third-Party Notices](#211-licenses-and-third-party-notices)).

Why two: measured offline on the user's library, skyseg draws crisp edges and handles sunset, grey, haze and night skies, but calls smooth BOKEH and calm WATER "sky" at full confidence (a wildlife library is full of both); SegFormer is semantically better on those but its edges are blobs. They fail on DIFFERENT pictures, so agreement removes most false sky while skyseg keeps the edges.

The matte (Utilities/skyrefine.h, header-only, OpenCV core + imgproc); each step fixes a failure seen on a real picture:

1. CALIBRATED probabilities. The old SegRefine path min-max stretched skyseg's output, turning no-sky pictures peaking at 0.005-0.016 into a full false sky.
2. Region gate. Each connected skyseg sky region (at quarter resolution) is kept or dropped WHOLE by SegFormer's mean agreement over it (smoothstep 0.2..0.3, near-binary, so there are no half masks). A per-pixel gate was tried first and FAILED: SegFormer's blob ate the sky between branches.
3. Small gaps (&lt; 1% of the frame) near a kept large region are kept regardless (below SegFormer's resolution); colour decides them.
4. Disputed pixels (skyseg > 0.5, SegFormer &lt; 0.2) fall back to min(skyseg, SegFormer) ONLY where the pixel is colour-distinct from the local sky; without that test uniform bokeh was punched full of blotches.
5. A colour matte in the uncertain band: local sky colour S and foreground colour F are filled in from the eroded confident pixels with a push-pull pyramid, and alpha = the pixel's projection on the F -> S line, trusted only where S and F are well separated AND the pixel lies near the line; elsewhere a colour (RGB) fast guided filter of the fused probability. 5a: the local sky and foreground are RANGES along the F -> S axis (measured by push-pull of t and t^2), and the residual is measured relative to the sky's own off-axis spread. 5b: the colour alpha snaps to 0/1 beyond HALF its own edge width (1 / steepest local slope).
6. Recovery: where SegFormer sees sky skyseg missed, next to kept sky, strong colour evidence may PROMOTE pixels (snowy branches, canopy), never demote.
7. The halo pass: the FINAL alpha snaps to 0/1 beyond HALF the PHOTO's edge width (contrast across the edge / steepest local colour gradient), everywhere. Sky just above a ridge is usually darker, paler or hazier than the sky further up, and a single local sky colour read it as "part ridge", leaving a band of half-darkened sky along the skyline. Colour alone cannot tell that sky from a real ridge/sky mix, but DISTANCE can: a real mix exists only within the edge's own width. A crisp ridge gets a crisp mask edge even where the colour test backed off, while a hazy ridge or a defocused branch keeps its soft edge. (Both snaps use HALF the measured width: a per-pixel profile across a ridge found sky-coloured pixels 1-4 px above it still at alpha 0.77-0.94 when the whole width was allowed, a 1-2 px bright line on the edge at -2 EV.)
8. Decontaminated alpha: where the foreground is about as bright as the DARKENED sky, a correctly mixed edge pixel still ends brighter than both sides, because blending an exposure change by alpha scales the WHOLE pixel. a' = a \* S / p (linear luminance; S = the nearest pure sky, alpha > 0.98, 2 px Gaussian reach) puts the change on the pixel's sky part alone: exact for exposure (darken or brighten), close for other adjustments, &lt;= 1 by construction, fractional pixels only.

Measured (Joffrey Lake / Dempster / Manning Park, against the first matte): halo pixels -79% / -77% / -65%, over-masking on Dempster -82%, bright-line overshoot on a fixed edge set -37% / -48% (Dempster / Joffrey), oak canopy error vs colour ground truth 0.177 -> 0.107; the cyan line on Dempster is the lens's colour fringe and now reads as a faint dark edge. Remaining: a dark cloud sitting ON a ridge stays slightly partial (it is within the ridge's edge width); semantic misses (glacier, moon, snow vs cloud) are for the Refine Brush. All radii scale with the long edge.

- Resolution: built at up to 4096 px (kSkyMatteLongEdge), stored as uint8 (11 MB at 4096x2730). The old 1024 px float map bilinear-sampled onto a 6000 px render was a \~6 px ramp, and that ramp WAS the halo.
- Feather: 0 = the matte as is (its fractional edge is the result, as for the Object mask); > 0 = the band around 0.5 every AI mask has. A NEW Sky submask starts at Feather 0 (DevelopProperties::beginMaskTool), because the old default 50 re-sharpened the matte toward 0/1 and partly undid the decontaminated alpha; saved sidecars keep their own value.
- Cost: \~0.7-0.9 s for the matte at 4096 plus \~1 s for SegFormer and \~0.3 s for skyseg on the CPU, once per image (cached by path), synchronous on the GUI thread behind a "Finding the sky..." popup, because the full-res render and export callers need the alpha before they composite.
- Proof: the C++ port was diffed against the Python prototype on six real pictures; tests/unit/tst_skyrefine.cpp pins the calibration / gate / agreement rules and the canopy matte on a real photograph (fixtures/sky/oak\*.png = photo + the two models' real outputs).
- Open (seen on the user's "Sky Mask Test Images" collection): a few sky holes stay inside a snow-laden tree; a small isolated sky strip far from the main sky is dropped (redwoods looking up); grey bokeh that BOTH models call sky stays selected (it may be overcast sky); a distant snowy mountain is a judgement call. Future: run both models through ORT/CoreML once ORT is on in every build; an async build would need renders and exports to wait for the alpha.

#### 11.15.21 Refine Brush

MaskTool::RefineBrush (2026-10-07): a submask that RE-MATTES THE MASK ABOVE IT inside a painted region, against the photo's own colours. It is the fix for what an automatic mask gets semantically wrong (a glacier, moon or foreground snow counted as sky; snow clumps in branches; sky holes in a treeline) and for an edge that still haloes. Untested in-app at the time of writing.

It works on ANY mask (Sky, Subject, Object, Brush, ...) because it is a FOLD STEP, not a coverage: buildMaskBuffer's foldSegments routes it to MaskRefine::apply (Develop/maskrefine.h, header-only, OpenCV) on the buffer holding every submask above it, and the result is blended in by the stroke's own coverage, so a soft brush edge fades it in. It is a pure function of strokes + mode + folded mask + guide, so the per-scope render cache and the fold-prefix cache hold unchanged.

Modes (Add / Remove ARE the op: Add = add, Subtract or Intersect = remove, so the Opt latch picks Remove for free; Fix Edge is "mode":"edge" in paramsJson and overrides the op, refineModeOf in mainwindow.cpp):

- ADD: the unmasked pixels under the stroke are split RELATIVELY. k-means (k = 4) in a chroma-weighted YCbCr space (chroma x3, because pale horizon sky and lit snow share lightness and differ only in chroma); the cluster nearest the mask colour is the mask's (clusters within 0.15 of it merge, so a sky gradient stays one class); each pixel goes to whichever side's nearest centre is closer; the clearly mask-like pixels seed a LOCAL S and the rest define F; and the matte between them adds the holes but not branches or snow. The mask colour comes from masked pixels in the stroke's context box or, when there are none, from the K nearest masked pixels anywhere (the search widens; NOT the mean of every masked pixel in reach, which was the deep zenith blue). k-means runs from a fixed RNG seed so the render caches see a pure function. An empty mask -> a plain add brush. Why relative (2026-10-08): a FIXED 0.08 "looks like S" distance failed because sky seen through branches is hazier and paler than the open sky (0.13-0.31 away), so the holes were classed as foreground, and with no masked pixel nearby it plain-added the branches. Known limit: over a stroke with NO sky under it, shaded bluish snow can be the cluster nearest the mask colour and gets added.
- REMOVE: the TRUE mask colour is learned from masked pixels OUTSIDE the stroke, and masked pixels under the stroke that are clearly unlike it are matted out, so painting over real sky changes nothing. "Clearly unlike" is ADAPTIVE (at least 0.08, twice the reference's own spread, and the Otsu split of the under-stroke distances, cut at the upper edge of Otsu's bin), because sky near a horizon is paler than the reference above the stroke and a fixed threshold removed it.
- FIX EDGE: the edge under the stroke is re-matted with local S and F, snapped beyond half the photo's edge width and decontaminated (the sky matte's halo steps, shared as SkyRefine::photoEdgeWidth / snapBeyondEdgeWidth / decontaminate).

- The dock's Mode row (MaskEditor, a PanelEditor::addCombo row) writes them: Add / Remove through setSubmaskOp, Fix Edge the key. The first submask cannot Remove (its op is pinned to Add), so its Mode row offers Add / Fix Edge only and says why, and the Create Submask dialog greys the Refine Brush for an empty mask with the reason. No Edge / Invert rows (a step, not a coverage).
- On the canvas it IS a brush: DevelopProperties::updateMaskEdit hands ImageView the Brush tool, so painting, size, flow, auto-mask, cursor, undo and shortcuts are the Brush's own; setActiveMaskParams carries the "mode" key across (ImageView's brush JSON has none); editrotate rotates its strokes; isBrushCanvasTool / isStrokeTool cover it.
- The guide: MW::buildRefineGuide, the UNDEVELOPED working image through toWorkingColor (as-shot WB + camera matrix), / white, display gamma, clamped 0..1, built once per render tick only when a scope carries a Refine Brush (componentsHaveRefine), on the proxy grid for the veil. Undeveloped for Halo's reason (a guide that moved with the sliders would make the mask chase the adjustment). With no guide (the veil before a proxy exists) it degrades to the plain brush it looks like; the veil's focus-submask footprint rasterises it as a Brush.
- Proof: prototyped in Python on the user's "Sky Mask Test Images" (foreground snow and snow clumps removed with the sky between untouched; a glacier removed without the paler sky above it; ridge halos under a Fix Edge stroke -66% Dempster / -36% Joffrey); the C++ diffed against the prototype on six real cases (exact); tests/unit/tst_maskrefine.cpp pins the rules on synthetic scenes (intruder out / sky kept; paler horizon sky kept, which caught an Otsu off-by-one; holes added / trees not; pale holes added far from any masked pixel with trees and snow left out; lit snow left out beside pale horizon sky; Add deterministic; a mis-registered edge snapped; outside the region bit-identical). Cost: \~20-40 ms per stroke region at 2048 px (crop-local).

### 11.16 Model Inference

Utilities/inference/ is the unified model-inference seam for NEW neural features. InferenceSession (the front door) owns an InferenceBackend; the only concrete backend is OrtBackend (ONNX Runtime). All ORT contact is confined to ortbackend.cpp behind a PIMPL, and the whole scope is guarded by WINNOW_HAVE_ORT: built without ORT (CMake option WINNOW_ENABLE_ORT=OFF) it compiles to a stub (IsLoaded() == false, Run() no-ops), so features degrade like a missing model.

- It deliberately supersedes cv::dnn for NEW models (it reaches the ANE / GPU and loads architectures cv::dnn cannot, e.g. attention / diffusion). The existing cv::dnn predictors (u2net, skyseg, SegFormer, MiDaS, focus, SAM 2) keep working and migrate opportunistically.
- InferenceBackend is an ESCAPE HATCH: a native CoreMLBackend can be added for a model that needs maximal ANE use (generative fill) without touching callers. A full native-per-platform solution (Core ML on the Mac, DirectML on Windows) remains an option if ORT's CoreML EP underuses the hardware.
- Models are downloaded on demand by ModelStore (Utilities/modelstore.\*) or bundled (pmrid.onnx in ReleaseExtras/, warn-if-absent).
- Consumers: PMRID "Denoise raw" ([11.17 Raw Denoise](#1117-raw-denoise)), the LaMa / MI-GAN fills (lamafill / miganfill), ImageEmbedder (SigLIP, [16.12 Audit Keywords (Finding Keywording Mistakes by How Images Look)](#1612-audit-keywords-finding-keywording-mistakes-by-how-images-look)).

Device selection (the InferenceDevice preference, ortbackend.cpp) biases WHICH compute units the CoreML EP targets:

- Auto / NPU: the CoreML EP with flags 0 = the full set (ANE -> GPU -> CPU), the older NeuralNetwork format.
- GPU: COREML_FLAG_USE_CPU_AND_GPU | COREML_FLAG_CREATE_MLPROGRAM, i.e. the Apple GPU (Metal / MPSGraph) with the ANE EXCLUDED, for graphs whose ops the ANE cannot service (e.g. FFT-based FFC blocks in LaMa-style fill). BackendName() then reports "CoreML/GPU".
- CPU forces the CPU EP.
- Caveat: this picks the target DEVICE only; ops the CoreML EP cannot map are still partitioned back to the CPU EP, so an end-to-end-GPU LaMa also depends on the ONNX export (FFT decomposed to matmul). There is NO ONNX Runtime "MPS execution provider"; MPS-as-a-backend is a PyTorch concept, and on ORT the GPU is reached through the CoreML EP's CPUAndGPU compute units.
- DirectML on Windows, CPU everywhere as the fallback.

Compile cache: OrtBackend / InferenceSession take an optional compileCacheDir; on macOS with GPU it appends the CoreML EP through the provider-options API with ModelCacheDirectory set, so a large graph's \~90 s ML Program compile happens once per model VERSION rather than every launch (the directory must be version-specific: ORT reuses a compiled graph by key, not by bytes). ImageEmbedder and PMRID pass one.

Fixed dims (2026-10-13): an optional FixedDims list ({{"H",512},{"W",512}}) is applied as ORT free-dimension overrides, turning a model exported with dynamic axes into a static graph at load (no re-export, so a bundled model's ModelStore hash is untouched). Every Run must then feed exactly those dims.

PMRID was the case. It shipped on Auto (NeuralNetwork) with dynamic H/W, and ORT logged "number of partitions supported by CoreML: 5 ... nodes supported: 145" of 149: the graph split with CPU hops between, 88-92 ms per 4x512x512 tile. Measured offline (Python ORT CoreML EP, same model): ML Program + dynamic dims 5.7 ms but \~2 s to re-specialise on each session's first Run; ML Program + dims pinned to 512 on the GPU 5.4 ms (40 ms first Run); ML Program on CPU + Neural Engine 66 ms; all within 2e-7 of the CPU EP. So PMRID asks for InferenceDevice::GPU with a pmrid-v&lt;version> compile cache and FixedDims 512x512, and its tiler pads every tile (including a sub-tile image) to exactly 512. LESSON: the default Auto / NeuralNetwork path is the slow one for convolutional nets here; measure ML Program on the GPU before assuming the ANE wins.

First run: even with a warm compile cache, CoreML spends \~1.8 s on a fresh session's first Run (measured in-app: first tile 1,843 ms, then \~7 ms). PMRID::WarmUpAsync() loads the session and runs one zero tile on a pool thread, once per process; MW::setOperationMode calls it on entering Develop with the Winnow engine (before its no-change return, so a launch that restores Develop warms too), and the renderer switch calls it when switching to Winnow inside Develop. Its timing is recorded for the Develop diagnostics ("warm-up run N ms"); nothing is printed to the console.

#### 11.16.1 More AI Masks

##### 11.16.1.1 Select Background

The INVERSE of Select Subject, with no new model or store. It reuses the SubjectMask saliency (ensureSubjectMask; stackHasSubjectMask, the subjRef fetch and onAiMaskEditBegin all treat Subject and Background the same) and selects 1 - subject. In buildMaskBuffer the subject CompDesc carries subjectBaseInvert (true for Background), and coverage is sampled with (inverted ^ subjectBaseInvert), so Background with Invert off = background, Invert on = subject; the loupe tint (buildSubjectPreview) XORs the same way (maskIsBackground, tool == 7). Dock rows Feather + Invert.

##### 11.16.1.2 Depth Range

A HYBRID: the MODEL produces a depth field (like Subject/Sky), but the SELECTION is a [near, far] BAND (like Luminance Range over depth).

- The model is MiDaS v2.1 small (midas.onnx, \~64 MB, convolutional, an official OpenCV DNN sample; ViT DPT / Depth-Anything will not load in cv::dnn), via Utilities/depthpredictor: input [1,3,256,256], /255 + ImageNet mean/std, a single output [1,256,256] of inverse depth. The map is min-max'd and INVERTED to 0 = near .. 1 = far, then guided-UPSAMPLED against the photo (SegRefine::guidedUpsample: a continuous field, joint upsampling, NO binary contrast).
- Stored in Develop/depthmask.h (DepthMask::DepthRef, its own path store), built by MW::ensureDepthMask (stackHasDepthMask + a depthRef fetch + onAiMaskEditBegin, all mirroring Sky).
- buildMaskBuffer's isDepth CompDesc carries the band [lo, hi] from paramsJson {lo, hi}; per pixel DepthMask::coverage is a feathered band over the sampled depth (the analogue of RangeMask::lumCoverage).
- Dock rows Near / Far / Feather / Invert (Near/Far reuse the maskRangeLo / maskRangeHi sources -> maskRangeChanged -> ImageView::setMaskRangeParams, which accepts Depth; live tint buildDepthPreview). paramsJson is non-empty, so it survives stackJob's empty-params skip.

##### 11.16.1.3 An Automatic Mask That Finds Nothing Says So

2026-10-09. An empty Subject / Sky mask looks identical to one still being built (the tint never appears), so after onAiMaskEditBegin builds the ref it calls MW::reportEmptyAiMask, which shows a 4 s popup when there is NO ref (the model failed to load, inference failed) or the ref selects essentially nothing (under 0.1% of pixels above half coverage): "Select Subject returned nothing: no subject was found in this image." (Sky likewise; Background says it found no subject, so the mask covers the whole image). Depth reports only a failed build (its field is continuous, and an empty selection is the user's Near/Far band). Object Mask is excluded: an open trace is "nothing yet", not a failure. Only the user's gesture (adding or selecting the mask) reports; the render paths that re-enter ensure\* on every slider tick never do.

##### 11.16.1.4 Object Mask (Perimeter Paint + SAM 2)

A PROMPTABLE mask. The user traces the object BOUNDARY with a solid brush (multiple strokes; Opt/Alt erases); when the traced perimeter forms a CLOSED loop the enclosed region is filled, and that silhouette is refined to the edge by a SAM 2 encoder + decoder pair via OpenCV DNN (no onnxruntime; cv::dnn 4.11 loads and runs both graphs). A matting network was considered and declined.

It is TWO-PHASE, matching SAM's heavy-encoder / light-decoder split (Utilities/objectmaskpredictor, ObjectMaskPredictor):

- setImage() encodes the developed base ONCE (\~1 s CPU), caching image_embed + high_res_feats + the guide.
- refine() runs the decoder PER brush edit (\~40 ms), feeding the painted silhouette as the dense mask_input prompt (has_mask_input = 1) plus the stroke bbox as a box (labels 2/3), picks the best of 3 candidates by predicted IoU, cleans it morphologically (open + keep-largest-CC + hole-fill, killing occluder specks), then shares SegRefine::refine for the edge matte.
- Preprocessing is SAM 2's reference: RGB, 1024^2, (px/255 - mean)/std with ImageNet stats; point_coords scaled to the 1024 space.
- The three-level dense prompt (2026-08-28): the silhouette is NOT prompted as uniform foreground. The traced perimeter straddles the true boundary, so the painted band is \~half background; prompting it at +8 logits baked the brush dabs into the mask (soft dab-shaped blobs spilling onto the background, SAM given no way to disagree). refine() takes fill and band SEPARATELY: interior +8, exterior -8, and the band FADED TO 0 ("no opinion, read the image"), continuous after the 256^2 downsample. ObjectMask::fillEnclosed's optional bandOut (the bridge-thickened wall) produces it; parseObjectBrush returns both.

Resolution: an ROI-cropped encode (2026-08-28). The encoder input is a fixed 1024^2 whatever it is fed, so encoding the WHOLE frame spent that budget mostly on background (an object covering a third of the frame got \~340 px, and SAM's 256^2 mask head resolved it at \~85: one mask pixel per \~23 image pixels). Fine structure (fur, hair, foliage) was never REPRESENTABLE. ensureObjectEncoder takes an output-normalised ROI: objectBrushRoi computes the trace's extent from the stroke JSON (points expanded by the brush radius, which is a % of the LONG edge and so a different normalised amount per axis), pads 12% of the ROI long side for context, and quantises OUTWARD to a 1/16 grid. The guide long edge is chosen so the ROI lands at \~1024 px (clamped to [1024, min(4096, native)]), and ONLY the crop is encoded. The cached embedding is reused whenever the requested ROI still FITS INSIDE it (developObjectRoi / GuideW / GuideH / Crop) and is not > 2.5x larger in area than needed; the outward quantisation is what makes a growing trace keep hitting that path. ObjectRef is stored CROP-LOCAL (x0,y0,x1,y1 = the crop's normalised extent, coverage 0 outside), so the higher resolution fits in the same \~4 MB.

The matte (SegRefine::Mode, 2026-08-28): Saliency (Subject/Sky, the default) min-max stretches the net's map and CONTRASTS it around 0.5 into a clean 1-2 px cutout. AlphaLogits (Object) takes the SIGMOID of the signed logits (their zero crossing IS the decision boundary; min-max put 0.5 wherever the extremes landed, systematically growing or shrinking the mask) and SKIPS the contrast, because on fur / hair / foliage the fractional alpha in the fringe IS the result. ObjectMask::coverage matches: feather 0 passes the stored alpha through UNCHANGED (a genuine matte, unlike the coarse saliency refs, which must be thresholded; a hard 0.5 threshold was the second half of the fur defect); feather > 0 softens via the MaskFalloff cdf band.

Wiring:

- MaskTool::Object; MW::ensureObjectMask (encode cached by path + ROI in objectMaskPredictor; decode the component's brush and putRef under objectRefKey = path + brushHash, so multiple object masks coexist); stackHasObjectMask; and the four triggers (onAiMaskEditBegin warms the encoder and decodes if a stroke exists; updateMaskOverlayTint per component; renderDevelopPreview and renderDevelopFullResAsync loop the job's object components). ObjectMask get/putRef are QMutex-guarded, since buildMaskBuffer runs off the GUI thread.
- paramsJson {"size":N, "strokes":[{"pts":[x,y,...], "size":N, "erase":bool},...]}, output-normalised boundary strokes (like the Brush). parseObjectBrush rasterises them with BrushStamp::rasterize, then ObjectMask::fillEnclosed (Develop/objectmask.h) does a morphological close + border flood-fill: it thickens the wall by bridgePx (a fraction of the long edge, so preview and render agree), floods the background inward from the border, and any unreached non-wall pixel is ENCLOSED. It returns the filled silhouette only for a closed loop; an open trace yields no coverage. buildMaskBuffer's CompDesc.isObject carries a PER-COMPONENT objRef (object refs are per brush, not shared by path).
- The canvas (ImageView): a solid BOUNDARY brush (not a lasso, not a fill brush) reusing the Brush buffers (maskBrushMain = the perimeter wall, maskBrushStroke the stroke in progress, maskBrushSize the diameter, maskBrushStrokesJson the committed list). A move stamps segments and runs objRecomputeFill (fillEnclosed) -> maskObjClosed + maskObjFill; objRebuildPreview tints the overlay AMBER while open, GREEN + a faint fill once closed. Release composites the stroke into the wall and emits via maskGeometryChanged -> setActiveMaskParams -> paramsChanged, which runs ensureObjectMask when closed. Size works as the Brush's (see [11.15.16 Brush](#111516-brush)); Cmd/Ctrl+Z = objUndoStroke. It is not a content tool (no content preview), and is NOT in stackJob's contentDerived list: an undrawn/open Object mask yields no coverage and is dropped like an unplaced gradient.
- The dock: Size + Feather + Invert; defaultMaskParams {"size":8,"strokes":[]}; selecting it fires onAiMaskEditBegin (warms the encoder).
- The hint (2026-10-09): a new Object submask starts empty and waits for a traced boundary, which is not self-evident, so beginMaskTool shows "Use the brush to outline the object(s)" as a 3000 ms popup the first 3 times (QSettings Develop/objectMaskHintCount) and in the status bar after that. It MUST be showPopupNow: the plain queued showPopup never appeared here.
- Models: sam2_encoder.onnx (as is) and sam2_decoder.onnx, which must be the FIXED-SHAPE export: cv::dnn's importer rejects the stock samexporter decoder's dynamic num_labels / num_points ("parseShape: dynamic 'zero' shapes"), so ReleaseExtras/tools/export_sam2.{py,sh} pins them (1 label / 2 points) and onnxsim constant-folds (prints Shape=0 on success); see ReleaseExtras/tools/README.md. Downloaded by ModelStore ("Object Mask / Segmenter"). Verified under cv::dnn (encoder \~1 s, decoder \~43 ms). Model quality was validated offline on a real photo: the brush dense-prompt path fixes the box-only occluder weakness (IoU 0.92 -> 0.99).

##### 11.16.1.5 Segmenter (Click to Select)

MaskTool::Segmenter (2026-10-14): a submask built by POINTING. SAM 2 cuts the photo into the objects it is made of; the object under the pointer is highlighted, a click adds it, a click on a selected one takes it out, and the submask is the union of what is selected. Picked from the Create Submask dialog's Automatic group (SubmaskDialog::addToolGroup takes an explicit tool list, because MaskTool is append-only and a group's members need not be contiguous). Untested in-app.

The engine (Utilities/segmenter.{h,cpp}) is SAM's own "automatic mask generation" recipe through the SAME encoder/decoder pair as the Object mask: no new model or runtime.

1. Encode the frame once (\~1.3 s CPU).
2. Prompt a 16 x 16 point grid, three candidates per point (the decoder's multimask output; one positive point, the second exported point slot padded with label -1, no dense prompt).
3. Keep candidates with predicted IoU >= 0.70 and stability >= 0.88 (logit offset 1.0); clean them (holes and specks under 0.05% of the frame, SAM's remove_small_regions, but never the island under the prompt); drop near-duplicates by MASK IoU > 0.7 (a box test would merge a whole object with its part).
4. Gap fill: up to 3 rounds of up to 16 prompts in the still-uncovered area (interior points, greedy farthest-point spacing, not near a point already tried; the distance transform runs on a padded copy, or a gap touching the frame edge puts its deepest point in the corner), with relaxed thresholds (IoU 0.5, stability 0.75), a candidate kept only if more than half lies IN the gap.
5. What is still uncovered (opened, components >= 0.3% of the frame) becomes REMAINDER segments, so every sizeable region can be clicked.
6. A containment HIERARCHY: a segment's parent is the smallest segment >= 1.1x its area holding >= 80% of it; depth 0 = a whole object, 1 = a part, 2+ finer.
7. Each segment's logits are upsampled to the LABEL GRID (the frame's aspect, long edge 1024), thresholded at SAM's zero crossing, cleaned again and traced into polygon rings (findContours RETR_CCOMP + approxPolyDP 0.75 px; holes are rings too, the path is even-odd).
8. One int16 label map per Detail level, painted largest first, so the SMALLEST segment offered at that level wins a cell.

The defaults are a notch looser than SAM 2's (32 points, 0.8 / 0.95): the decoder is the cost (\~110 ms per prompt per core), 16 x 16 is a quarter of the decodes, and on the six test photos 0.8/0.95 left a third of a car photo unsegmented where 0.7/0.88 found the same objects plus the foliage around them. Gap fill took the dark forest behind that car from 36% unsegmented to 11%; the remainder covers the rest.

Speed and memory (M1 Ultra, 3840x2160 JPEG): encode 1.3 s; grid decode 2.9 s on 10 threads / 2.2 s on 16; gap rounds \~0.5 s; post-processing \~0.25 s; total \~4-5 s. The decoder parallelises almost linearly over PRIVATE cv::dnn nets (1 thread 112 ms/prompt, 16 threads 8.5 ms/prompt); each net costs \~120 MB once it has run, so MW uses idealThreadCount - 2, clamped to [2, 16], and the nets are freed when the search ends. The worker loads its OWN encoder and frees it before the decoders load (its activations peak at \~2.4 GB), so nothing is shared with the GUI thread's ObjectMaskPredictor. A batched decoder export was considered and not done: per-prompt multi-net scaling already reaches \~13x on 16 cores.

What is saved (the design decision): paramsJson = {"segments":[{"rings":[[x,y,x,y,...],...]},...]}, the selected segments' OUTLINES, mask-normalised (oriented, uncropped frame), rounded to 1e-5 (a twentieth of a pixel at 4096 px). NOT the prompts. So the render needs NO MODEL: a cold open, an export, or a machine without the SAM download rasterises the same polygons, and a later model swap cannot silently move a saved mask. Persisting (point, candidate) and re-decoding would have tied every sidecar to these exact weights and to the exact pixels the encoder saw. Cost: a few KB per selected object (two large objects on the car photo: 9.8 KB). EditRotate::maskParams rotates every ring (tst_editrotate::segmenterOutlinesTurn).

The render: MW::ensureSegmenterMask -> Segmenter::matte rasterises the union of the selected outlines (QPainter, antialiased, even-odd per segment) at the snap guide's size and snaps it to the photo with SegRefine::refine in Mode::Alpha (coverage taken as is: no min-max, no sigmoid, no contrast; then the guided filter). The guide is the developed base at up to 2048 px (MW::segmenterGuideImage: downscaled + lens-corrected + developComposite, uncropped, oriented), built once per image + orientation and NOT rebuilt when the sliders move. The result is registered in the Object mask's store (ObjectMask::putRef under objectRefKey(path, paramsJson), whole-frame extent), so buildMaskBuffer samples it through the Object CompDesc unchanged; stackHasObjectMask and the four ensure loops (renderDevelopPreview, renderDevelopFullResAsync, developPixelSource, updateMaskOverlayTint) dispatch Segmenter components to ensureSegmenterMask. A Segmenter with NOTHING selected is skipped in buildMaskBuffer before the ref lookup; it is not "a ref still being built", so it must not mark the refs unready and keep the result out of the fold cache.

The search (MW): onAiMaskEditBegin offers the SAM download ONCE per tool session (buildTree re-emits maskEditBegin on every rebuild; maskEditEnd re-arms it), sets segmenterWanted and calls MW::startSegmenter, which is IDEMPOTENT and cheap once the objects are known (a cache hit -> ImageView::setSegmentation) or being found (the same key running -> nothing). That lets renderDevelopPreview call it on every tick while the tool is open, the only way to catch the working image landing AFTER the tool was opened.

- Key = path + orientation degrees (segmenterKey). Segmenter::Job runs Segmenter::segment on its own QThread; the result is posted back to a context QObject the Job owns (a Job that is gone drops the call) with a generation counter (a result queued before a shutdown is ignored).
- One search at a time: a request for another image cancels the run (it ends within a decode or two) and onSegmenterDone starts the wanted one; a run cancelled for an image the user came back to is restarted the same way; a real failure is reported, not retried.
- Results are cached for the last 3 images (segmenterCache); noteLensGeometry drops an image's cached objects and snap guide when its lens geometry changes; closeEvent shuts the job down (cancel + wait).
- Progress: a 150 ms timer pushes Job::progress into the canvas chip and the panel note (encode 0-20%, decodes 20-90%, post-processing 90-100%).

The canvas (ImageView): maskIsSegmenter() (maskTool == 11) is in maskToolUsesMouse, so developToolActive swallows click-zoom and pan (Space still borrows the pan). A CLICK is a press + release within 4 px (segPressed / segPressVp).

- segUpdateHover, on every move: a SELECTED outline under the pointer first (the smallest; QPainterPath::contains, even-odd), so a selection made at another Detail level can always be taken back; else Segmentation::at(n, level). A pointing-hand cursor over either, re-asserted on every move (busy cursor while the search runs).
- drawSegmenter draws in mask space through maskNormToItem, clipped to the photo, with cosmetic pens: selected = an overlay-colour outline, filled too unless the whole-mask veil is already painted; hover = a white outline on a dark halo + a light wash (click adds); hover over a selected one = a dashed outline on a dark wash (click removes). Selected outlines show whether or not the pointer is over the view.
- segToggleAt appends or removes a segment entry, rebuilds the path FROM the JSON (so the overlay shows exactly the rounded outline the render rasterises), emits maskOpActionStarted (a click latches the held op as a stroke does) and maskGeometryChanged(paramsWith(...)) -> setActiveMaskParams.
- drawSegmenterChip: "Finding objects... N%" + a bar, or a one-line failure, bottom centre (the legend owns top-left, the rendering hint top-right).
- [ / ] (claimed in ImageView::event; focus taken on enter): [ = smaller pieces (finer Detail), ] = bigger, the sense they have for a brush's size; emits segmenterDetailRequested.

The dock: maskToolName "Segmenter"; defaultMaskParams = an empty selection; MaskEditor rows = Detail (Objects / Parts / Details) + Feather + Edge + Invert. Detail is a TOOL PREFERENCE (QSettings Develop/segmenterDetail), not an edit: changing it re-renders nothing and leaves the selection as is, so it has no History entry ("maskSegDetail" -> segmenterDetailChanged -> ImageView::setSegmenterDetail; the canvas keys come back through setSegmenterDetail, which re-seeds the row). MaskPanel's tool-note line (setToolNote, under the attribute-scope line), filled from MW's setSegmenterNote, shows the progress, then "N objects found. Click one to add it to the mask, or a selected one to remove it. [ and ] give smaller or bigger pieces.", or why it cannot run (model not downloaded: a greyed reason in the panel + chip, never a popup after the fact). First 3 uses: a "Click the objects you want in the mask" popup, then the status bar only (Develop/segmenterHintCount). User help: Docs/developsubmaskshelp.html; [ ] in Help/shortcutsform.ui.

Tests: tests/unit/tst_segmenter.cpp drives Segmenter::assemble with a SYNTHETIC decoder (a disk holding a smaller disk, a rectangle, a ring with a hole, and background whose confidence is the knob): objects found once each, with whole at Objects and part at Parts; a label grid per level on a non-square grid; gap rounds pick up a half-confident region; an unsegmentable one becomes a remainder; a selection round-trips through JSON to the right area (holes included); empty selection; cancel. Validated offline first on six real photos with the real models (car in a park, ground squirrel, maple leaf, towhee on branches, elk, flying woodpecker): Objects gives the whole car / animal / tree, Parts its wheels, windows, plate, door.

### 11.17 Raw Denoise

"Denoise raw" is GLOBAL-ONLY, decode-time noise reduction: PMRID (MegVii, Apache-2.0), a PRE-demosaic (CFA / Bayer-domain) learned denoiser that runs on the raw mosaic BEFORE demosaic (ImageFormats/Raw/pmrid.{h,cpp}, PMRID::Apply) through the unified inference layer ([11.16 Model Inference](#1116-model-inference): ORT, the CoreML GPU on macOS, DirectML on Windows). It needs a WINNOW_ENABLE_ORT build (otherwise a no-op stub) plus pmrid.onnx (ReleaseExtras/, committed, warn-if-absent). Because it needs the CFA mosaic it is WINNOW-engine + BAYER only: inert on the Apple engine (no CFA) and on X-Trans. Conditioned by ISO (ImageMetadata::ISONum). (An earlier post-demosaic RawRefinery "TreeNet" path and an unwired NAFNet export were removed 2026-07-12 when PMRID superseded them; recover from git if a post-demosaic engine is ever wanted, e.g. to cover X-Trans or Apple.)

It is distinct from the maskable local Denoise in the Detail section ([11.11.2 Spatial Ops](#11112-spatial-ops)).

#### 11.17.1 The Controls (Raw Panel)

The controls live in the RawPanel (Develop/Properties/rawpanel.cpp), beneath its "Demosaic" / "Render using" row, shown only on the Winnow engine (the whole RawPanel is hidden for a non-raw file; DevelopProperties::syncRawPanel). Layout (2026-10-13): a "Noise Reduction:" caption, then one row ("Auto run" first, then "Run on this image", HIDDEN while Auto run is checked: RawPanel::updateRunOnImageVisible), then the Lum / Color sliders. Their captions use the tree's caption split (RawPanel::setCaptionWidth) so they align with the Basic sliders.

- Auto run persists to QSettings Develop/autoRunDenoise (mirrored in G::autoRunDenoise). It is the FALLBACK for images whose recipe says nothing (denoiseRaw == -1). AUTO RUN OVERRIDES (2026-10-13): wantsDenoiseRaw = autoRun || denoiseRaw > 0, so with Auto run ON every raw is denoised, including one whose recipe says 0 (the panel hides the per-image box while Auto run is on, and an explicit off winning would render clean with nothing on screen saying why). Turning it ON runs the denoise immediately (MW::onAutoRunDenoiseToggled -> runRawDenoiseNow); turning it OFF calls clearRawDenoiseNow unless the current image opted in (denoiseRaw == 1), so the now-visible box matches the loupe (PmridCache keeps the base, so re-ticking is instant).
- "Run on this image" shows the image's SAVED choice (EditParams::denoiseRaw == 1, pushed by syncRawPanel -> RawPanel::setRunOnImage), NOT completion, so a ticked image does not read unticked while its denoise is still running. Checking it emits runRawDenoiseRequested -> MW::runRawDenoiseNow (one ensureRawDenoise regardless of the flag); unchecking emits clearRawDenoiseRequested -> MW::clearRawDenoiseNow (drops both developDenoised and the full-strength developPmridFull base and re-renders clean).
- The checkbox WRITES THE RECIPE (DevelopProperties::setDenoiseRawFlag -> EditParams::denoiseRaw on the Global scope, with a History row). The amounts cannot carry the intent, since they default NON-ZERO, and before this a manual run existed only in the session caches, so it reached neither the exporter nor the devPreview builder: the loupe showed a denoised image while the stored preview stayed clean under a recipe hash claiming they matched.
- denoiseRaw is TRI-STATE: -1 unset (follow Auto run; the default, OMITTED from the JSON so an untouched raw keeps the recipe hash it always had, and browsing raws in Develop writes no sidecars), 0 off (unless Auto run is on), 1 on (denoised even with Auto run off). Every render site asks EditParams::wantsDenoiseRaw(G::autoRunDenoise) rather than testing the field. The checkbox writes 1/0 EXPLICITLY, never folding back to unset when it agrees with the preference, so an image that opted in stays denoised when Auto run is later turned off.
- The Lum / Color sliders (EditParams denoiseLuma / denoiseChroma, Global-scope 0..1, "Denoise Lum" / "Denoise Color") are HIDDEN until a denoised base exists for this image (RawPanel::setDenoiseRunState -> updateAmountsVisible, fed by MW::rawDenoiseReadyForCurrent, which tests developPmridFull, keyed path + ISO and so AMOUNT-INDEPENDENT); their appearing is the "denoise finished" cue. Because the base is amount-independent, an amount change is only a cheap re-blend. applyItemsEnabled re-asserts the disable when the panel is (re-)enabled. Signals (autoRunDenoiseToggled / runRawDenoiseRequested / clearRawDenoiseRequested) are wired in initialize.cpp.
- The render gate is the RECIPE alone: wantsDenoiseRaw(G::autoRunDenoise). It used to be "Auto run OR rawDenoiseReadyForCurrent", which would render a deliberately UN-denoised image denoised whenever a base happened to be cached for it.

Remembered amounts (2026-10-13): denoiseLuma / denoiseChroma are TRI-STATE like denoiseRaw. -1 = UNSET (the default; omitted from the JSON, counted as identity) means "use the remembered amounts", G::denoiseLumaDefault / G::denoiseChromaDefault, persisted as Develop/denoiseLumaDefault / denoiseChromaDefault and seeded from the factory EditParams::kDefaultDenoiseLuma 0.75 / kDefaultDenoiseChroma 1.0. Moving either slider (DevelopProperties::setGlobalDenoise) stores the value EXPLICITLY on that image AND updates the remembered amount, so every image the user never adjusted follows the last setting while adjusted ones keep their own.

- Every render site reads EditParams::denoiseLumaOr(G::denoiseLumaDefault) / denoiseChromaOr(...), never the raw field, whose -1 would read as "no denoise" in the "> 0" gates. Presets capture the EFFECTIVE amounts.
- Render identity: Metadata::denoiseAmountsKeyPart appends |dnL|dnC to devPreviewKey (always) and to defaultRenderKey (when Auto run is on), but only while the remembered amounts differ from the factory values, so no existing key changed.
- Legacy sidecars: paramsToJson used to write both amounts unconditionally, so every image edited before this stores them explicitly (usually 0.75 / 1.0) and keeps them. Reading a stored factory value as unset was rejected: it would have re-keyed every edited image's devPreview. sanitize keeps -1 legal and repairs any other negative to -1. Pinned by tst_denoiseraw::unsetAmountsFollowTheRememberedValues.

When denoise cannot run, it is said on the panel, not in a popup: the box keeps its saved state but is greyed, the sliders are hidden, and the reason line takes their place (MW::rawDenoiseAvailable -> DevelopProperties::updateDenoiseAvailability -> RawPanel::setDenoiseAvailable, refreshed on every syncRawPanel; sticky, so setDenoiseRunState cannot re-enable the amounts while it is false). The build-level case needs no decode to detect: PMRID::IsSupportedBuild() is a CHEAP check (InferenceSession::BackendCompiledIn() + pmrid.onnx beside the binary, no model load), so on a build without ONNX Runtime the group is dead from the moment the panel appears. The per-sensor case can only be learned by running (below).

#### 11.17.2 One Decode, Two Bases

"Denoise raw" is a BLEND scaled by the luma/chroma amounts, so the decode needs BOTH endpoints, both from demosaicing the SAME CFA mosaic:

- the clean base (outClean) = the mosaic demosaiced BEFORE PMRID: the noisy RGB, the 0% endpoint;
- the PMRID base (\*work) = the mosaic demosaiced AFTER PMRID: full-strength denoised RGB, the 100% endpoint.

Develop::BlendRawDenoise then shows clean + amount\*(pmrid - clean), luma by denoiseLuma, chroma by max(luma, chroma). Caching both bases is what lets an amount drag re-blend instantly; the model re-runs only on an image or ISO change.

- The cached pre-develop WorkingImage is kept CLEAN (RawFormat::Decode caches it BEFORE denoise). The interactive render derives the denoised base from it (MW::developRawDenoisedBase / ensureRawDenoise), cached and computed OFF the GUI thread (developRenderPool); both the proxy and the full-res render start from it.
- ensureRawDenoise is triggered on image SELECT (MW::fileSelectionChange) AND on entering Develop (MW::setOperationMode), not only on settle, so its progress row (progressRawDenoiseRow) appears immediately. Its single decode returns BOTH bases (one UnpackCfa, not two) and publishes the clean base to the cache; the ImageCache decode then REUSES it (ImageDecoder::load short-circuits UnpackCfa + Demosaic when a scene-linear entry is cached). Meanwhile the loupe shows the embedded JPG (ImageView::loadImageInterim on a develop-raw cache miss) and the developed image pops in when the decode lands.
- Staged progress: one 0..1000 bar spans the WHOLE decode: the clean demosaic [0, 25%], PMRID [25, 75%], the denoised demosaic [75, 100%] (Demosaic::Run's per-row progress callback), so the bar moves with no empty gap. Inert for a normal decode, which passes no progress sink.
- Demosaic progress with Auto run off: the plain Winnow sensor demosaic runs in the ImageCache decoder threads (ImageDecoder::load -> RawFormat::Decode), so its progress is a SIGNAL: Demosaic::Run's per-tile callback drives RawFormat::Decode's sink; ImageDecoder::load emits demosaicProgress(sfRow, fPath, done, total); ImageCache relays demosaicProgress(fPath, done, total); MW::onDemosaicProgress updates a blue "Demosaic" row (progressDemosaicRow), gated to the current file + Develop + useRaw + Winnow + Auto run off, and clears it on setCached for the current row. (The scene-linear fallback MW::ensureDevelopWork -> ImageDecoder::decodeIndependent passes its own decodeProgress callback to the same row.)
- The demosaic is parallel (2026-10-13): Demosaic::Bilinear3x3 and XTransWindow run their row loops through ParallelRows (cv::parallel_for\_, OpenCV's own pool, NOT the QThreadPool-based Develop parallelFor, because decodes run on decoder threads / developRenderPool and must not wait on a pool they may belong to). Output is identical to the serial loop; abort is polled per row; progress is reported every 32 rows. A 50 MP bilinear pass was \~550 ms single-threaded, and a denoise decode runs two. With the GPU ML Program, PmridCache and the parallel demosaic, a denoise decode went from \~8.7 s x2 to \~0.95 s.

No silent no-op. PMRID can return an UNCHANGED mosaic (no ORT in the build, pmrid.onnx missing, a non-Bayer CFA). RawFormat::Decode reports that through outDenoiseApplied (relayed by ImageDecoder::decodeRawWorking), so MW::ensureRawDenoise drops the result instead of publishing a denoised base pixel-identical to the clean one (the dock had shown "Denoised" over an unchanged image). MW::reportRawDenoiseUnavailable records WHY, via PMRID::IsAvailable(): the model cannot run (session-wide, rawDenoiseUnavailable) vs this sensor is unsupported (per path, rawDenoiseUnsupported). Both gate ensureRawDenoise, so a failed denoise is not retried as a full re-decode on every settle. The freshly decoded clean base is still published.

The clean base must be scene-linear, AND its colour state must match. The blend subtracts the clean base from the denoised re-decode, so the two must share geometry and space.

- MW::ensureDevelopWork -> ImageDecoder::decodeIndependent selects the in-house raw decoder off ImageMetadata::ext, and DataModel::imMetadata() populates m.type but NOT m.ext, so ensureDevelopWork sets m.ext from the file suffix; without it the raw decode is skipped, the base falls back to the display-referred embedded JPG, and the blend silently rejected the size mismatch (denoise appeared dead).
- Matching dims are not enough: the display-referred fallback is active-area sized, so it can be the SAME dimensions as the sensor image. Its pixels are working-space, white-balanced and display-referred, while the PMRID base is camera-native scene-linear, so blending them adds a camera-native difference to white-balanced pixels and casts the image (dominated by green). Preview mode and the display-referred paths (ImageDecoder::applyDevelop, MW::ensureWorkingImageNow) can put such an entry under a raw's path. MW::rawDenoiseCleanBaseOk is the single test (valid + sceneReferred + space == CameraNative): a clean base that fails it is DROPPED, not fixed up, so the decode produces its own (outClean) and that replaces the bad cache entry. Develop::BlendRawDenoise also refuses a space / sceneReferred mismatch outright (serving the clean image with a qWarning). This latent hazard is closed; it was NOT the cause of the 2026-08-30 magenta cast below.

#### 11.17.3 The View Across the Pop

- Zoom and pan are kept: MW::fileSelectionChange captures the outgoing zoom/pan (ImageView::captureDevelopView -> developCapture\*) BEFORE the pixmap is replaced, for every Develop navigation (loadImageInterim also captures if the caller did not); the developed image restores it via applyDevelopCapturedView (from both the clean-image loadImage and setDevelopPreview) instead of re-fitting. A crop still re-fits: setDevelopPreview keeps the view only when the aspect ratio is unchanged.
- Same area in the next image, as in Preview: in Preview the swap is synchronous, so navigating zoomed lands on the same area and a thumbnail click pans the loupe to the clicked point (IconView::thumbClick -> ImageView::panTo). In Develop the developed image arrives seconds later, so a capture frozen at navigation would undo any pan made meanwhile, and the thumbnail click always arrives afterwards (selection happens on press, thumbClick on release). ImageView::refreshDevelopCapture therefore keeps the capture in step with the live view (called from panTo, scale and scrollChange) until the developed image consumes it; developCaptureLocked suspends tracking while the view is being reframed. The interim JPG is a fraction of the sensor resolution, so loadImageInterim scales the carried zoom by the change in fit zoom (interimZoomScale), so the placeholder frames the same content (and stays scrollable); tracking divides the factor back out, so the capture is always in full-size terms. The first image in a new folder starts at fit.
- A re-render of the same image keeps the live view (2026-10-13): switching the raw renderer or the Apple decoder version re-decodes the image on screen, and the decoders crop the sensor a few pixels differently (D850: Winnow 8288 x 5520, Core Image 8256 x 5504), so setDevelopPreview saw a size change and re-fitted a 100% view. It records the frame it showed (developShownPath + the pixmap's cacheKey); a size change while the pixmap on screen is still that frame of the same image is a RE-RENDER, and with the aspect unchanged it keeps the live view (fit re-fits, a zoom keeps its number, the pan keeps its fraction). Any other pixmap replacement changes the cacheKey, so navigation still goes through the capture.

#### 11.17.4 The Noise Model (k, b)

PMRID's KSigma normalisation needs a per-frame Poisson-Gaussian model, var = k\*x + b on the white-normalised green plane, resolved by a priority chain (PMRID::resolveKB):

1. A DNG NoiseProfile (tag 51041) baked into the file, read by DngRaw::UnpackCfa: exact, no calibration.
2. A per-camera-model K(ISO) / B(ISO) table (pmrid_calib_tables.h), MEASURED by a photon-transfer sweep (calibrate_pmrid.py) or DERIVED from published sensor data (gen_pmrid_tables.py, photonstophotos / Bill Claff), ISO-interpolated.
3. Blind estimation from the CFA (PMRID::estimateKB): per 32x32 block, noise variance = var(G1 - G2) / 2 against the green mean; blocks touching the clip point (>= 0.95 white) skipped; a bin needs >= 32 blocks; a 10th-percentile floor per bin; a least-squares line. So an uncalibrated body still denoises with its own model.
4. A generic full-frame Sony table as a last-ditch guard.

Only DNG carries a NoiseProfile, so proprietary raws (ARW / NEF / CR2 / CR3 ...) use tier 2 if known, else tier 3. The chosen tier is reported in the Develop diagnostics.

A tier must be PLAUSIBLE, not merely present (PMRID::kbPlausible): k + b is a small fraction of 1 even for a very noisy frame, so a tier whose numbers fall outside deliberately loose bounds (k in (0, 0.5], b in [0, 0.1], both finite) FALLS THROUGH to the next one. Checked on the DNG NoiseProfile and the blind estimate, the two tiers read from the file. The blind estimate must ALSO pass PMRID::kbPlausibleForIso: k within [1/32, 32]x the generic A7R5 table at the frame's ISO (the span of all 410 calibrated bodies, 0.05x..32x, iPhones at the top).

Two magenta casts, the record of why:

- 2026-08-30, every DNG: TiffWalk::Reader::reals() had no case for TIFF type 12 (DOUBLE) and fell to its integer default, and NoiseProfile (51041) is DOUBLE, so every DNG returned the low 4 mantissa bytes of each value read as an integer: k \~ 3.8e9 instead of 6.9e-5. That gives cvt_k \~ 2.7e-13, so the KSigma forward multiplied the image to a constant (-0.82 everywhere) before the net saw it, and the inverse then divided by 2.7e-13, leaving +/-1e9 that clamped to a near-BLACK mosaic. The visible symptom was not black: Develop::BlendRawDenoise adds lum\*dY of the correction, so the render base came out flat achromatic (R=G=B \~ 0.011), and stage 0 then applied asShotMul (1.78/1.00/1.59) to a signal that was ALREADY neutral instead of one at R,B \~ 0.59G, over-boosting red and blue by exactly those factors: magenta. Reader::scalar() still has the same DOUBLE gap; no DOUBLE tag is read through it today, so it is left deliberately.
- 2026-10-16, a Panasonic DMC-LX3 RW2 at ISO 80, "sometimes" magenta under Winnow: the LX3 has no table, so tier 3 ran, and the old estimator used the plain variance of the green sites, which carries every gradient and texture in the block, not just noise. On a frame with blown sky through trees, the bright bins were filled by blocks straddling clipped sky and dark trunks (variance \~0.1); the fit gave k = 0.37 (a calibrated body of that class is \~1e-4), it passed kbPlausible's loose box, and cvt_k \~ 0.003 wrecked the mosaic. Same camera, same ISO, other frames fitted 5e-4..0.05: content-dependent, hence "sometimes". The G1 - G2 estimator brought that folder's ISO 80 frames to a consistent 2-3e-4; frames still fitted out of the ISO band (heavy fine texture) fall through to the generic table, which under-denoises a compact a little but cannot cast.

Two lessons: a colour cast can be a LEVELS failure wearing a colour disguise (chase the channel MEANS of each base, which the Develop diagnostics' k/b line and a means probe in the blend show at once), and the diagnostics report would have named the DNG case in one look (source = "DNG NoiseProfile" with k = 3.8e9 is self-evidently wrong). The headless calibration loop skips PMRID, so a cast seen only in-app may still be this.

#### 11.17.5 One Shared PMRID Base (PmridCache)

Added 2026-10-13. The full-strength PMRID base (the camera-native WorkingImage a raw decodes to with the denoiser run on its mosaic) is amount-independent, so one copy serves every consumer. Before this, three paths each made their own: the interactive denoise (ensureRawDenoise -> decodeRawWorking), the ImageCache decode of an image whose saved recipe wants Denoise raw (RawFormat::Decode's saved-edit block), and developPixelSource (export / devPreview). Selecting a denoised image in Develop started the first two AT ONCE, so the same image ran the \~7 s model twice concurrently (measured: two \~9 s decodes finishing 0.5 s apart).

PmridCache (ImageFormats/Raw/pmridcache.h) is a process-wide, byte-budgeted LRU (768 MB, the most recent entry never evicted) keyed by SOURCE file + ISO, with in-flight dedupe: CLAIM EARLY, WAIT LATE. RawFormat::Decode calls tryAcquire() (non-blocking) before UnpackCfa whenever it needs the base:

- Hit: cached, reuse it.
- Claimed: run PMRID here and publish() it.
- InFlight: another decode is making it. This one still unpacks and demosaics its own CLEAN base in parallel, and only then blocks in acquire() until the base is published (Waited), polling the decode's abort every 100 ms so an ImageCache stop() is not held up. Waiting before the unpack (the first version) put the waiter's \~0.7 s clean decode AFTER the producer's whole run.

Details:

- Inside Decode the denoised base always comes from one helper (makeDenoised: PMRID::Apply on a mosaic, then demosaic + RawColor) and the clean base is always the main demosaic, so the interactive and saved-edit passes differ only in which base the caller gets.
- A producer that fails or is aborted abandons the claim (RAII Claim) and a waiter takes over, so an aborted ImageCache decode cannot strand the interactive denoise.
- An interactive pass that reuses the base and needs no clean base skips the decode entirely; one that needs the clean base still decodes the mosaic but skips PMRID and the denoised demosaic. ensureRawDenoise and developPixelSource also check PmridCache before deciding to decode at all.
- developPmridFull stays as MW's handle on the CURRENT image's base (it drives "Denoised" and the diagnostics); it is a share of the cache entry, not a separate copy.
- Cleared with the other Develop caches in resetDevelopCachesForNewFolder. Winnow engine only.
- The Develop diagnostics DENOISE section shows the entry count / MB and whether this image is cached, and the denoise timing line reports "cache wait" and "PMRID (ran | reused, cached | reused, waited)".

### 11.18 Spot Removal (Fill Replace)

Heal a clicked spot parametrically and non-destructively. SHIPPED SCOPE (decision 2026-07-17): SPOT CLEANUP ONLY. The action-row spot button or S (a Develop mode-local key; Slideshow in Preview) arms a click-to-heal spot tool. The Fill (paint an area) and Object (remove an object) modes and the Fill Replace panel are SHELVED behind G::useReplaceFillModes = false (global.cpp); all their code is kept and working, and flipping the flag brings the panel and modes back.

The primary engine is an exemplar CLONE heal (real neighbouring pixels, Lightroom heal-brush style). Clone fallbacks (and Object-kind fills) use LaMa regenerative inpainting on the Apple GPU; MI-GAN is the G::useLamaSpotFill = false fallback.

#### 11.18.1 Data Model and Render

Per image, like Geometry: EditStack::spots is an ordered list of FillSpot{enabled, paramsJson}, serialised under the "fill" key (forward-tolerant). paramsJson is opaque brush geometry (FillSpotGeom: feather 0..100 + "kind" = the Replace mode, and EITHER the single-stroke form (size = diameter / long edge, pts = output-normalised stroke points; Spot click / Object drag / legacy spots) OR the painted-area form "strokes", an ordered add/erase stroke list each with its own brush size, from Fill mode). rasterize() composites strokes in paint order (add = max, erase = multiply by 1 - alpha, per segment so long strokes stay cheap). Only the strokes are stored; the heal is re-synthesised at render (the engines are deterministic) and is stable under later slider changes.

Heals run BEFORE the geometry stage, on the developed oriented full frame, so spots stay glued to content when it is later cropped or straightened: developCompositeStack (mainwindow.cpp) applies them just before CropTransform::applyGeometry (StackRenderJob.spots filled by DevelopProperties::stackJob; applySpots is serialised behind g_spotHealMutex, since the heal engines hold per-process state).
