Spots apply in order, each healing over prior ones. The shared FillSpotGeom rasteriser (Develop/fillspot.h) is used by BOTH the ImageView preview and the render, so preview == render.

Spot coverage is spot-LOCAL (2026-09-30). Every render re-runs every heal (they work on DEVELOPED pixels, so they cannot be cached across an edit), and each heal starts by rasterising the spot's coverage, which used to be a full-frame W\*H float buffer cleared and scanned PER SPOT PER RENDER: on a 68-spot 12 MP NEF, 817 of 925 ms per render in Debug and 55 of 105 ms optimised, on every slider tick. FillSpotGeom::Coverage now stores only the rect the strokes can touch (at() reads 0 outside, so the engines still address it in frame coordinates): 925 -> 70 ms Debug, 105 -> 52 ms optimised, output pixel-identical. tst_fillspot pins equality with a full-frame raster at every pixel, including paint/erase order and frame-edge clipping. A heal-result cache was considered and NOT built: what remains is mostly cv::seamlessClone's Poisson solve, which depends on the developed pixels; the pixel-independent setup a cache could hold is \~15-20% of the 52 ms.

#### 11.18.2 UI

- The spot BarBtn in the Develop action row (initialize.cpp, images/icon16/spot.png; dim off, bright armed) or S arms the tool via DevelopProperties::onSpotToolToggled. DevelopProperties owns the armed state (spotMode) and drives the button icon back via spotActiveChanged. The tool must NOT claim S back while armed, or S could arm it but never disarm it.
- Armed, ImageView shows a brush-size circle cursor ([ / ] resize); a click paints one spot on release. Escape disarms. Each spot drops an on-canvas PIN; click a pin to remove it. A stroke -> spotStrokeCommitted -> DevelopProperties appends a FillSpot -> re-render; pins come from spotPinCenters via spotPinsChanged.
- The brush has NO user-facing feather: the cursor is one ring (exactly what gets replaced), and rasterisation is HARD (a 1 px anti-alias edge). The seamless transition is the ENGINE's job: at composite time the alpha is feathered by a band sized from the stroke THICKNESS (featherFromHole = clamp(0.7 x max inscribed radius, 2..12 px), NOT the bbox: a thin diagonal stroke has a huge bbox, and a bbox-sized feather smeared content far outside the brushed area), and the clone extent is dilated by the same band so the ramp blends cloned content over its whole width. The stored per-spot "feather" JSON field is legacy metadata, no longer rasterised.
- Models: ReleaseExtras/lama.onnx and migan.onnx (gitignored, EXISTS-guarded mac bundling); warn-if-absent. Clone heals need no model, so a build without them still heals spots.

The shelved Fill Replace panel (Develop/Replace/replacepanel.\*), when G::useReplaceFillModes is true: a TransformPanel-style strip below the Transform panel ("Fill Replace" gradient header with [?] tips and an [E] preview eye that renders with/without every committed heal, a non-destructive bypass via DevelopProperties::spotsShown gating stackJob's spots), with three mode rows, each shortcut letter bold in G::header2Color:

- Spot (S): click a blemish, a single click; clone heal.
- Fill (F): PAINT the area to replace (a resizable brush; strokes accumulate as a teal tint; Opt/Alt strokes ERASE), then Enter commits the painted area as ONE heal; Esc clears the pending paint (a second Esc exits the tool). Uncommitted paint is discarded on mode switch / tool exit. Clone heal.
- Object (O): brush over an object to remove; regenerative model fill.

S/F/O select the mode while the panel has focus (ReplacePanel::eventFilter); the panel's visibility tracks the armed state. The mode is stored per stroke as "kind" (legacy spots parse as fill), so each heal re-renders with the engine it was made with; the mode persists to QSettings "Develop/Replace/mode". The loupe's old S/F/O mode keys, the "F" tool toggle, the "B" correction cycle and the "N" grain toggle were RETIRED when S became the Develop spot toggle; G::spotFillCorrectMode / G::spotFillGrain keep their defaults and are no longer keyboard-settable.

#### 11.18.3 Engine Selection

LamaFill::apply (lamafill.cpp), per spot by kind: spot and fill heal by the exemplar CLONE (cloneHealOne) and fall back to the model path when no clean source exists (e.g. the hole touches a frame edge); object goes straight to the model path (a removed object leaves no clean source to clone).

#### 11.18.4 The Clone Heal

cloneHealOne, Lightroom heal-brush style. A masked template match on the context ring finds the best source patch near the spot, coarse-to-fine (match at reduced resolution so the hole is \~&lt;= 48 px, refine +-q px at full res), with a search window 3x the hole so lighting agrees. Then cv::seamlessClone (NORMAL_CLONE) Poisson-blends the patch over the hole (texture AND gradients from the source, the level solved from the destination boundary), and the engine-feathered alpha blends it in.

- Why Poisson: ground-truth benchmarked (scratch heal_bench.py: heal strokes over CLEAN background, compare against the untouched original), it beat every alternative on every content type (trunk RMSE 5.8 vs 7.5 membrane-split / 5.9 xphoto SHIFTMAP / 7.0 pure membrane; bokeh 5.4 vs 10.3 / 8.7 / 7.4). Harmonic membranes obey the maximum principle and can NEVER reconstruct a local brightness maximum, so any membrane-based low frequency dims the bokeh blobs a stroke crosses (a visible "dark sausage"); SHIFTMAP shows graph-cut patch seams on defocused backgrounds; Poisson keeps the source's own blobs and only tilts them to fit the boundary. Copied pixels carry the surround's true texture at EVERY frequency (grain, mid-frequency mottle), which was the remaining visible tell of every generative fill.
- Holes reaching a FRAME EDGE still clone: seamlessClone needs its mask strictly inside the patch, so the tile is REFLECT-padded 8 px for the solve and cropped back. It returns false when no clean source exists, and the caller falls back to the model.
- Pinned sources: the match runs on DEVELOPED pixels, so re-matching every render could flip the chosen source mid-slider-drag (heal-content shimmer). The first successful match per (image path, render size, spot geometry, chunk) is pinned in a small mutex-guarded cache and reused; the Poisson blend still re-runs on the current pixels, so exposure/colour edits track while the heal GEOMETRY stays stable. "No source" is pinned too. Keyed by qHash(paramsJson), so editing a spot re-matches.
- Chunked clone (large or long painted regions): ONE source offset for a whole stroke leaves a stroke-shaped ghost when the background does not repeat at a single shift, so when the coverage bbox exceeds \~1.5x the chunk size the heal splits into a grid of chunks. Each chunk clones its windowed share of the coverage (ChunkWin: weight 1 on the core cell, a linear ramp over core/4 px; cores tile the bbox so every covered pixel is at full weight in exactly one chunk) from its own LOCAL source, and the ramps blend neighbouring chunks' sources into each other. The chunk core = 3x the painted THICKNESS (6 x max inscribed radius, clamped 96..384 px), NOT the brush diameter (640 px chunks from a big brush sit far from any boundary, and nothing matches a smoothly varying background at that scale). The coarse match carries a DISTANCE PENALTY (score x (1 + (d/R)^2)), so a source at the search edge must be \~2x better than a near one.
- Coverage-aware source rules, against the WHOLE blemish, not just the chunk's hole: (1) the template-match ring ignores all coverage (else it seeks sources that LOOK like the remaining blemish); (2) a candidate source is rejected if the pixels it would copy (the chunk's hole SHAPE, padded past the feather dilation) overlap ANY coverage. The overlap for every offset comes from ONE cross-correlation (cv::matchTemplate TM_CCORR) of the coverage with the hole shape. The shape matters: a bounding-RECT test rejected nearly every candidate for a diagonal stroke, silently sending all chunks to the model path, which WAS the visible stroke-shaped smudge. A chunk with no valid source falls back to the model for just that chunk.

#### 11.18.5 The Model Path (LaMa)

Utilities/inference/lamafill.\* (LamaFill::apply), used when G::useLamaSpotFill (default true), else MiganFill. It runs on the GPU (InferenceDevice::GPU -> CoreML CPUAndGPU) because the ANE cannot service LaMa's FFC blocks. Per spot it takes a square context tile (\~4x the spot), resizes to 512, and fills; the hole is DILATED a few px for the model (hard edges seam), and the ORIGINAL soft alpha composites the patch back, so the seam is feathered.

- I/O: image [1x3x512x512] RGB in [0,1] + mask [1x1x512x512] where 1 = inpaint; output [1x3x512x512] RGB in [0,255] (verified by probe). (MI-GAN packs [keep-0.5, im\*keep] instead.)
- The lama.onnx export MUST be the fixed-shape (1x3x512x512) + Einsum("ij,jk->ik") -> MatMul rewrite, which cut CoreML partitions 405 -> 76; a raw dynamic-batch export is far slower. The Windows deploy copy is not added (matching MI-GAN).
- Luminance match (applyFillCorrection, G::spotFillCorrectMode): large fills leave a low-frequency "patch" offset against a smooth surround, since the alpha composite feathers only the SEAM. Modes: 0 none; 1 Poisson (cv::seamlessClone NORMAL_CLONE, boundary-gradient match; no-op if the hole is empty or touches a frame edge), the DEFAULT, because the model path serves Object fills and clone fallbacks, which must keep the model's content; 2 membrane transfer, INERT for this lama.onnx (probe-verified 2026-07-16: the export composites the input over the keep region IN-GRAPH, so orig == model outside the hole and any correction anchored on their difference is dead); 3 pure harmonic (discard the model; only right for smooth surfaces). The surround is reconstructed by pushPull(), a Gaussian-pyramid push-pull (Gortler et al.) that fills the hole with a smooth harmonic membrane (it replaced a single-Gaussian normalised convolution that collapsed to a flat average deep in a large hole).
- Grain match (applyGrainMatch, G::spotFillGrain, default on; model path only, since clone heals carry real grain): the residual "patch" on smooth walls is NOT luminance (level corrections land within \~1/255) but MISSING sensor grain (a harmonic fill measured at 0.17x the surround's grain). Synthetic RNG noise measured WRONG in character (white, lag-1 autocorrelation \~0.05 vs the real grain's \~0.38; channel-independent \~0.04 vs \~0.92, so chroma confetti), so the grain is QUILTED: random high-frequency residual (sigma-4 highpass) blocks from the tile's kept surround, screened to near-median energy so structure is never copied, overlap-blended across the hole with random flips. Per channel the amplitude tops the fill's grain up to the surround's in quadrature; it falls back to channel- and spatially-correlated synthetic noise when the surround has too few clean blocks (a fixed RNG seed either way, so re-renders do not shimmer). Diagnosed instrument-first (the A/B outputs measured in Python) after level-only fixes kept failing.

#### 11.18.6 What Was Tried

The intent was a full Lightroom-class Fill Replace tool (Spot, Fill, Object), entirely offline. Results:

1. MI-GAN inpaint (27 MB, \~76 ms per 512 tile on the ANE): fine on tiny spots; on high-ISO, noisy or defocused content the fill is a coarse coloured mosaic that reads as a smudge. Kept only as the fallback. (It had beaten LaMa in the first bake-off, when LaMa seemed CPU-bound.)
2. LaMa inpaint (208 MB, \~272 ms per tile on the Apple GPU via CoreML CPUAndGPU, 4.2x faster than CPU; the ANE cannot run its FFC blocks): better than MI-GAN, but any 512-net fill upscaled to a large tile is soft and its low-frequency level drifts (a measured +5 luma dome). Corrections plus grain matching narrowed but never closed the gap; a ground-truth bench proved any generative fill leaves a visible patch on grainy or mottled surrounds.
3. The exemplar CLONE heal: EXCELLENT on spots and thin-stroke removals (branch tests healed invisibly, user-confirmed). On LARGE fills it hits an information limit: a 200 px-wide region's true content is not inferable from its surround (ground-truth RMSE \~15 for every method tried), and patch-scale colour drift remains perceptible; low-frequency harmonisation and smaller chunks benched WORSE.
4. Diffusion inpaint (DreamShaper-8-inpainting, SD1.5-class, \~2 GB fp16, \~15 s per 512 fill via torch/MPS on an M4): clearly the best large-area quality (fat-fill RMSE 9.1 vs 15.8 for clone; stalk + leaf removal visually superior), but only with ALL of: a complete object mask + margin (else it REGENERATES the object from leftover fragments), a background prompt plus a negative prompt (else worse than clone; the word "bokeh" literally paints bokeh discs), and the grain quilt. Integration would need a \~2 GB model, a new runtime (stable-diffusion.cpp or Core ML), heal-result caching (15 s cannot run per render) and prompt plumbing.

Conclusion (2026-07-17): spots are solved and shipped; large-area fill is not worth the model size, runtime and complexity for Winnow's scope. If revisited, the path is: SAM 2 click-select (a full-object mask) -> a diffusion tier with a negative prompt + grain quilt + cached results. A "Fill" pseudo-scope could also be promoted to a real EditScope (the format is forward-tolerant).

### 11.19 Develop Alerts and the Greyed Panel (Severity Rows, Disabled States)

Two halves of the same job: tell the user when Develop is not doing what the panel appears to promise (ALERT ROWS), and make the controls LOOK as dead as they are (the greyed panel). Both are driven from the selection, so both refresh on every selection change.

#### 11.19.1 Alert Rows

developAlertRows sits directly BELOW the Develop action row: coloured text on the panel background (no filled banner), one row per live condition, filled by MW::setDevelopAlerts from MW::updateDevelopSelectionWarning. Conditions STACK, each in its own row. Two severities (MW::DevelopAlert):

- AlertShowStopper: Develop cannot run on this selection at all (a video). RED #FF4040. The panel is greyed alongside, so the row is what explains the dead controls. Text: "First image selected is a video."
- AlertWarning: Develop runs, but not on what the user thinks. With a multi-image selection every edit and every Paste Settings lands on ALL of them (DevelopProperties::flushPropagation), off-screen. AMBER #FFB340: proceed, knowingly.

setDevelopAlerts stable-sorts show stoppers to the TOP, so severity reads from position as well as colour (colour alone fails a colour-blind user). It re-applies the colour to every REUSED row: the label pool means a row that held a show stopper last time may hold a warning now. The same text also goes to the STATUS BAR (for a video, the longer "Video selected - Develop applies to still images only"), because the dock may be tabbed away behind History or Presets.

A read-only volume is a WARNING, not a show stopper. A locked SD card or a read-only archive mount takes develop edits happily: the render is real and the user may be looking rather than keeping. What fails is the sidecar write that would make the work outlast the session, so the panel says "Read-only volume - edits cannot be saved." in amber and leaves the controls live, said BEFORE the editing. Metadata::writeDevelopSidecar used to fall through to open() and report a failed write per file, burying the one fact the user needs; it now declines once per path, silently. The recipe stays in the live EditStack for the session, so copying the images somewhere writable keeps the work.

- The warning is asked of the CURRENT IMAGE'S FOLDER (MW::currentImageFolderIsWritable, memoised per folder and dropped with the develop caches when a new set loads), not of the folder last clicked: a recursive load and a Catalog result set both span volumes, and a single flag from the last folder selection described the wrong one (it also latched true for the session once any writer hit a read-only path).
- The test is Utilities::folderIsWritable, which is access(W_OK) and NOT QStorageInfo::isReadOnly(). On macOS the system volume is a sealed read-only APFS snapshot and /Users is a firmlink into the writable Data volume, and QStorageInfo matches mount points by path prefix, so it answers "/" (read-only) for every folder in the user's home. That made the warning appear on the internal drive, and made writeDevelopSidecar decline every sidecar on it.

A mixed selection (a video CURRENT, stills selected) is its own case. MW empties developProperties' current path for a video, so selectedEditCount is 0 and the multi-image row would say nothing while a dozen JPGs are selected. DevelopProperties::selectedStillCount counts the developable stills WITHOUT going through the current path, and the alert block adds a second row: "N still images are also selected - make one of them current to develop the selection". Nothing can be edited from a video current item (Develop edits the current image and fans the change out from it), so the row says how to reach the stills. When the current item is a STILL, videos elsewhere in the selection need no special case: selectedEditCount goes through otherSelectedPaths, which already skips them.

#### 11.19.2 Greying the Panel

syncDevelopPanelEnabled() greys the panel for a video, so the sliders look dead instead of live-looking and inert. setDevelopPanelEnabled takes TWO flags: VISIBLE (developAction checked AND Develop mode) and USABLE (the selection can be developed). The dock itself is NOT disabled in the unusable case (a disabled parent greys every child, and a child cannot override a disabled ancestor), so each piece is greyed individually, leaving the alert rows readable:

- developProperties (setPanelEnabled also reaches its sibling ScopeHeader and RawPanel);
- the developActionRow;
- the pinned Transform and Fill Replace strips, siblings of the property panel and so NOT covered by setPanelEnabled (miss them and a video selection leaves a live crop/heal strip over a dead panel);
- History and Presets.

setDevelopPanelEnabled raises developDock only on a hidden -> visible TRANSITION; it runs on every selection change, and an unconditional raise() would yank Develop to the front tab whenever the user navigated with History or Presets selected.

#### 11.19.3 Every Item Must Have a Disabled State

setEnabled() only greys what the style paints, and a Develop panel overrides the style in four ways that each defeat it; all four carry a disabled form:

- Per-widget stylesheets. A widget stylesheet beats the app one, including its "QLabel:disabled" rule, so a hand-rolled "color: x" stays at full strength on a greyed panel. G::labelCss(colour, ptSize) emits the normal AND the :disabled rule; use it for every explicitly coloured label (scope header, scope and submask rows, Raw captions, Transform / Fill Replace titles and hints). Non-label rules spell out :disabled (and :checked:disabled) themselves: the Transform mode buttons, the Color Range hue chips.
- Inline HTML. An accented shortcut letter ("&lt;b>C&lt;/b>rop", "&lt;b>S&lt;/b>pot") colours the letter inside the text, where no pseudo-state reaches. G::setAccentCaption stores the two halves on the label and G::restyleAccentLabels re-renders them; the panel calls it from changeEvent on QEvent::EnabledChange.
- Custom painting. paintEvent and item delegates draw with literal colours. The Edits bar gradient (ScopeHeader::paintEvent) and the tree's closing rule (DevelopProperties::paintEvent) dim via isEnabled(). PropertyDelegate paints the tree from PENS, not from widget state: the leaf branch honours UR_isEnabled, and so does the HEADER branch (the section captions stayed teal over dead rows). It is tested only when the role IS SET, so trees that never set it (Preferences, Embellish) keep their normal colour.
- Shared or app-wide QSS that forgot :disabled, or greyed to the WRONG grey. BarBtn::setActive paints the armed tool's accent border white and adds a G::dimmed(white) ":disabled" border, so the armed tool stays legible on a greyed action row without looking live. SliderEditor's value field greyed to a literal "gray", brighter than every caption beside it; it uses G::disabledColor. WidgetCSS::radioButton set ":checked" (cadetblue) and ":unchecked" with no ":enabled" qualifier, so a disabled radio kept full-strength text (the Raw panel's source pair); its ":disabled" rule is added LAST (same specificity, later rule wins).

Colour that carries MEANING (selection band, rail, hue chip) dims via G::dimmed(), blended halfway into the panel background, so it stays identifiable but visibly dead. TEXT uses G::disabledColor.

### 11.20 Develop Scopes (Histogram and Vectorscope)

A live histogram (left) and vectorscope (right) sit above the property tree, in Develop/Scopes/: HistogramView (256-bin R/G/B with additive blend + a faint luma outline), VectorscopeView (YCbCr Cb/Cr 2-D accumulation on a circular graticule, log-scaled and hue-coloured), wrapped by ScopesView (a QHBoxLayout, the histogram given the larger stretch). A standalone widget above the tree was chosen over an in-tree spanned row so the scopes stay pinned rather than scrolling away.

They reflect the image CURRENTLY SHOWN in the loupe. MW::updateDevelopScopes(const QImage&) does ONE strided sample pass (\~180k-pixel budget, so a 50 MP raw costs the same as the proxy; constScanLine, so no detach; it samples the RGB888 frame directly) that fills both scopes. It is called after each develop preview render (both setDevelopPreview sites) and, for an unedited image, from the decoded image in applyDevelopPreviewIfEdited; the scopes are cleared at the imageView->clear() sites. No new timers: it piggybacks the coalesced render path, and it is a cheap no-op while the scopes are hidden.

#### 11.20.1 Showing and Laying Out the Strip

A button on the Develop action row (graphic.png) shows and hides the strip (MW::toggleDevelopScopes -> setDevelopScopesVisible), persisted as "Develop/scopesVisible".

The layout (both / histogram / vectorscope / hidden) is PICKED from two places showing the same four exclusive checkable actions (developScopesBoth/Hist/Vect/HideAction, one QActionGroup, no shortcut). (Until 2026-08-22 a "G" key cycled the four; the key and MW::cycleDevelopScopes are gone.)

- Right-click ANY scope in the strip. The layout section is built in ONE place and each scope contributes only its own items: the scope widget's contextMenuEvent builds a stack QMenu with its own items (HistogramView: none yet, where channel visibility, log scale or neutral-core opacity would go; VectorscopeView: 100/150/200% zoom + the skin-tone line; ScopesView: nothing, the fallback for right-clicks no scope claimed) and emits menuRequested(QMenu\*, QPoint), relayed by ScopesView to MW::showDevelopScopesMenu, which appends a separator (only if the scope added items) and the four layout actions, then execs. The QMenu is on the emitting scope's stack, so the receiver handles it synchronously and keeps no pointer to it; the actions belong to MW and outlive the menu.
- The Develop menu's "Scopes" submenu (developScopesMenu), Develop-mode gated like the rest of the menu and ticked from the strip's state on aboutToShow (MW::syncDevelopScopesMenu).

Both routes call MW::setDevelopScopesChoice(int), a ScopesView::ScopeLayout or MW::kDevelopScopesHidden (-1). ScopesView::setScopeLayout hides the scope(s) not wanted (a hidden widget is an empty layout item, and the stretches are re-set to 0), so the surviving scope fills the strip. The tone-region slider shares the histogram's x-axis and follows it. The layout persists as "Develop/scopesLayout" (the ScopeLayout values 0/1/2: do not renumber the enum) and is re-applied in createDevelopDock. Picking a layout while the strip is hidden also shows it, and showing it repopulates the scopes, which go stale while hidden.

The close button is ONE [X] for the whole strip, owned by ScopesView: a BarBtn (close.png, the dock title bars' chrome button) FLOATED over the top-right corner rather than placed in the layout (a layout slot would steal width from whichever scope is on the right). ScopesView::resizeEvent pins it and raise()s it (setScopeLayout raises it too, since the scope underneath changes). Its click -> closeRequested -> MW::closeDevelopScopes -> setDevelopScopesVisible(false): the strip hides and the LAYOUT IS LEFT ALONE, so the action-row button brings it back showing the same scope(s).

#### 11.20.2 Readouts

- Cursor readout: hovering the loupe marks the pixel under the cursor on both scopes (vertical R/G/B ticks on the histogram, a ring at its Cb/Cr on the vectorscope). ImageView (mouse tracking on) emits cursorImagePos (normalised) / cursorLeftImage; MW::onImageCursorPos samples that one pixel from developShownImage (the cached QImage last handed to updateDevelopScopes, implicitly shared, so O(1) per move) and calls ScopesView::setMarker / clearMarker. A no-op while the scopes are hidden.
- Vectorscope zoom: the right-click 100/150/200% magnifies the trace and marker outward from the centre to reveal low-saturation detail; the graticule circle stays the 100% reference and a small "%" label shows bottom right when zoomed. VectorscopeView::setZoom + zoomChanged -> ScopesView::vectorscopeZoomChanged -> "Develop/vectorscopeZoom".
- Skin-tone line: the same menu toggles a flesh-tone reference line, the YIQ I-axis, which from the BT.601 Cb/Cr coefficients is (Cr-128) = -1.946\*(Cb-128); skin of every ethnicity falls along it (hue is constant; only saturation and brightness vary). Drawn centre -> edge into the warm upper-left ray, independent of zoom. setSkinLine + skinLineChanged -> ScopesView::vectorscopeSkinLineChanged -> "Develop/vectorscopeSkinLine".

#### 11.20.3 The Tone-Region Slider

ToneRegionSlider, under the histogram and sharing its x-axis: a black -> white track with three draggable handles that place the tone regions (as Lightroom's tone-curve region splits). They map to three EditParams fields, toneShadowCenter / toneCrossover / toneHighlightCenter (perceptual 0..1, defaults 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75). In Develop::buildToneShape the two outer handles SLIDE the shadows and highlights regions (their offsets from 0.25 / 0.75), and the middle handle's offset from 0.50 stretches how far each reaches, so the fitted shapes keep their form while their placement moves; the defaults are an exact no-op. The shadows handle moves where the Shadows GAIN starts to fade (below it, the gain is at full strength). Blacks and Whites are endpoint moves, not regions, which is why only two bands have handles (see [11.8 The Tone Controls](#118-the-tone-controls)).

- A drag writes the active scope's params and emits paramsChanged() (a live, coalesced re-render). The splits only change pixels when a tone slider is non-zero, so they are NOT part of EditParams::isIdentity().
- DevelopProperties::bindToneSlider() connects the slider (drag -> onToneSplitsChanged), and populateSlidersFromStack() pushes the saved positions back on image switch.
- The same handles appear in the Curves panel, under its plot in Parametric mode: one set of params, two ToneRegionSlider instances. onToneSplitsChanged cross-pushes to the instance that did not originate the change (setPositions emits nothing, so it cannot loop). They stay here as well because this is where they align with real histogram data. See [11.28 Curves Panel (Tone Curve)](#1128-curves-panel-tone-curve).

### 11.21 Detail 1:1 Preview

Sharpening is the only Develop op with an ABSOLUTE pixel radius, which makes it the only op the interactive proxy renders wrongly BY DESIGN: at a typical proxy scale (\~0.3-0.4) Sharpen::effectiveSigma collapses to the kMinSigma 0.4 floor and the whole 0..1.5 amount range moves acutance by \~5%, against \~70% at renderScale 1.0 (measured with Develop::Apply on a synthetic detail field). A fit-to-window loupe hides it for a second, independent reason: the VIEW downsamples the settle render. So the Sharpening slider looked dead at every zoom except a 1:1 loupe on a landed settle render.

The Detail preview (Develop/Properties/detailpreview.h) is a square window at the head of the Detail section showing one patch of the image at one image pixel per LOGICAL pixel (the loupe's own definition of 100%). It is LIVE: the patch is re-rendered on every proxy tick, so it tracks a slider drag with no settle wait, independent of the loupe's zoom. Layout (2026-10-09): one spanned row (DevelopProperties::addDetailPreviewRow), "1:1" and the target button in a left column pinned to the top, and the preview as a FIXED square (side = G::propertyRowHeight() + 170, the ROI size it renders) whose top is level with the button, centred by a balancing spacer on the right. (It used to be a caption row plus a full-width well, showing the square patch with unused black either side.)

#### 11.21.1 The Render

MW::renderDetailRoiImage (mainwindow.cpp), carried as a DetailRoiJob into developCompositeStack, where this tick's per-scope mask buffers already exist. The patch is cut from the FULL-RES base (cutDetailRoi, renderScale forced to 1.0; copyMetadata would otherwise carry the base's own value; it also fills the frame's statistics samples from the full image before cutting, see [11.8.4.1 The Strength Is a Budget](#11841-the-strength-is-a-budget)) and run through WorkingImageCache::renderStack, the function the main composite uses, then EXIF-rotated. A few hundred px square against a 50 MP settle render, so it rides along with the proxy tick.

Two deliberate approximations, documented at their call sites:

- A masked scope's coverage is sampled BILINEARLY from the mask already rasterised at proxy resolution (sampleMaskRoi), not rebuilt at full res. Coverage is a smooth field, so the cost is a slightly softer mask EDGE inside the patch; rebuilding a 50 MP mask per tick for a 170 px window would cost orders of magnitude more than the render it feeds.
- Geometry (crop / warp) is NOT applied. Crop does not resample, so 1:1 pixels are identical either way; a warp does, but reproducing it for one patch buys less than it costs. The sample point is normalised over the geometry-INPUT (oriented) frame, the space ImageView::maskItemToNorm reports.

Coordinate mapping (Develop/detailroi.h, tests/unit/tst_detailroi.cpp): three spaces, source (the un-rotated WorkingImage), oriented (source turned by the EXIF degrees; where masks are normalised and where the pick arrives), and displayed (oriented, then geometry). The header maps an oriented normalised point to a SOURCE pixel rect, undoing the rotation. The rect inverse is where the sign errors live (at 90 the oriented rect's LEFT edge comes from the source's BOTTOM edge, and the axes swap), so the test checks every mapped corner against an independently written FORWARD mapping rather than copied numbers, and asserts the rect always lies inside the pixel buffer.

#### 11.21.2 The Picker

The target button beside "1:1" arms ImageView's detailPickMode, with the WB dropper's contract: ImageView reports a normalised point (detailPointPicked), the dock disarms, and MW stores it. It joins developToolActive() so an armed click cannot also toggle the loupe zoom, and it sets suppressClickZoom for the release (the dock disarms synchronously, so the gate is already false by then). Esc is handled in MW::developShortcutIntercept, not ImageView, because the tool is armed from the dock and focus is there. A marker is drawn on the image at the sample point, and dragging inside the preview slides it (resolved by MW, which owns developOrientationDegrees). The loupe-target picker also offers the loupe itself as a target.

The sample point is VIEW STATE, not an edit: not in EditParams, the sidecar or a preset. It is which patch you are looking at, not what the image looks like. It resets to unpicked on image change (MW::resetDetailPoint), so the preview opens on a "pick a location" prompt rather than a guess.

### 11.22 Transform Panel (Crop, Straighten, Perspective)

TransformPanel (Develop/Transform/) is a compact control strip below the scopes and above the property tree, the sibling of ScopesView. It is the UI for a non-destructive crop / straighten / perspective edit and carries NO geometry or pixel state itself: the crop rectangle, straighten angle and perspective quad live in the edit stack (EditStack::Geometry) and are applied LAST in the pipeline, after the develop ops, so they stay non-destructive and masks map through them (see [11.25 Overlays Over a Transformed Image (Mask Space vs Displayed Space)](#1125-overlays-over-a-transformed-image-mask-space-vs-displayed-space)).

#### 11.22.1 Layout

- A property-style gradient HEADER band ("Transform", an internal GradientHeader drawn with PropertyDelegate's backgroundShade +5 -> -15 gradient) with four trailing BarBtns: [?] tips ("Crop and transform tips"); [E] the preview eye (previewToggled, see Persistence below); [R] reset (crop, straighten and warp to identity, resetRequested; reset.png); and, at the extreme right, [X] close (closeRequested). [X] runs MW::toggleDevelopTransform's hide path, so closing from the header COMMITS exactly like the action-row button or R.
- A three-way MODE toggle down the left: Crop / Level / Warp (an exclusive QButtonGroup; the selected button gets a teal #1b8a83 background and border). Each mode row carries that mode's controls and its own [R] reset (resetModeRequested), all in the last grid column so they line up. (A fourth, Kaleido, lived here briefly on 2026-10-19; the kaleidoscope is now Effects > Kaleidoscope, see [11.22.8 Kaleidoscope](#11228-kaleidoscope). A persisted mode of 3 reads as Crop.)
  - Crop: an Aspect combo (As shot / Custom / 1x1 / 3x2 / 4x3 / 5x7 / 4x5 / 8.5x11 / 16x9 / 16x10 / the persisted custom aspects / "Add custom aspect..."; each item's userData is the w/h ratio, 0.0 = As shot, -1.0 = Custom (TransformPanel::kCustomRatio)), a padlock that locks the ratio, and a flip button (swap.png, F) that swaps the crop between landscape and portrait.
  - Level: a straighten-angle field (-45..45 deg; editingFinished -> levelAngleEntered, applied as an absolute straighten). Selecting Level also arms the draw-a-level-line tool.
  - Warp: selecting it seeds the 4-point quad (ImageView::beginWarp) for corner dragging. Commit the traced quad with Enter/Return or a double-click (ImageView claims those via ShortcutOverride while cropWarp is active and emits warpCommitRequested -> MW::rectifyDevelopCrop, which stores the warp + a suggested crop and returns the toggle to Crop). There is no separate Rectify button.

The Aspect combo / lock / flip are enabled only in Crop mode, the angle field only in Level mode. Custom aspects, the lock state and the selected mode persist under "Develop/Transform/".

MW wiring: modeChanged -> setDevelopTransformMode arms the matching ImageView tool (beginCropEdit / beginLevel / beginWarp); levelAngleEntered -> setDevelopLevelAngle; resetModeRequested -> resetDevelopTransformMode clears just that mode's contribution (the Warp row clears hasWarp, which is also how you re-warp: reset, then trace again). The CROP reset and the header reset call setAspectAsShot() first: beginCropEdit re-fits a full-frame crop to a LOCKED aspect, so without freeing the aspect a reset to the full frame would just re-inscribe the locked ratio and appear to do nothing.

#### 11.22.2 Aspect Lock and Flip

- Locking "As shot" constrains drags to the image's native aspect (ImageView::cropLockedAspect); flipping honours 1/aspect.
- Flip (ImageView::setCropAspectFlip) turns the crop box 90 deg by swapping its pixel width and height, keeping the centre and scaling down only if the rotated box would not fit. A locked crop already sits at the ratio, so the swap lands on the inverted ratio; a free crop just swaps its own dimensions.
- Custom (key "free", not "custom", which would collide with the "custom:" user aspects) is the crop's OWN ratio. Releasing a handle drag or a newly drawn frame with the aspect UNLOCKED that leaves the chosen ratio (more than 0.5% off cropTargetAspect) makes the view adopt the frame's ratio (cropAspect = it, flip cleared, flip stash dropped) and emit ImageView::cropAspectFreed; MW connects that to TransformPanel::setCustomAspect, which selects Custom and clears the flip with NO aspectChanged (the view is already there). A negative cropAspect, from picking Custom in the combo or restoring it at beginCropEdit, is resolved by cropResolveCustomAspect to the current frame's ratio (inverted when flipped), so locking or flipping Custom honours what is on screen.
- The flip STASH: a straight flip back must restore the exact pre-flip rect, or the scale-to-fit clamp shrinks the crop a little on every round trip. cropFlipPrevN holds the rect before the last flip and cropFlipResultN what that flip produced; if cropN still equals cropFlipResultN (epsilon compare), the next flip restores cropFlipPrevN verbatim instead of recomputing. Any manual edit moves cropN off cropFlipResultN, so the next flip recomputes. The stash is discarded in beginCropEdit (a new session) and setCropAspect (an aspect or lock change breaks the pairing).

#### 11.22.3 Shortcuts

R toggles the panel (MW::toggleDevelopTransform, developTransformAction, the editor-bar button rectangle.png; persisted as "Develop/transformVisible"). R is a Develop-mode local shortcut ([7.5 Develop Mode Local Shortcuts](#75-develop-mode-local-shortcuts)) with ONE Preview meaning: in Browse (Preview), MW::eventFilter sends a bare R to toggleDevelopTransform, which enters Develop the way D does and then OPENS the panel (always opens, never toggles shut, even if Develop restored a persisted Transform on entry). Where Develop is refused (the preview cache folder), setOperationMode shows its reason and the panel stays closed. It is skipped in a slide show (R = random order there), in dialogs and in text / value editors. The Develop menu item follows the same rule: syncDevelopMenuEnabled gates it like D rather than greying it in Preview.

Closing the panel has two OPPOSITE outcomes:

- R, Enter, [X] and the action-row button COMMIT (toggleDevelopTransform -> exitDevelopCrop: write the overlay crop into the edit stack and show the cropped result). While a WARP quad is being traced, Enter instead commits the quad (rectify) and does not close.
- Esc CANCELS (MW::cancelDevelopTransform): it restores the Geometry snapshot taken at enterDevelopCrop (developCropGeometryBackup), drops the overlay WITHOUT reading its rect, and hides the panel. The snapshot is needed because straighten and warp are written to geometry LIVE during a session (applyDevelopLevel / rectifyDevelopCrop), so a cancel must revert them, not merely skip the pending crop.

While Transform is active, single letters act: C Crop, L Level, W Warp, A toggles the aspect lock, F flips the aspect. They must beat the window-level shortcuts on the same keys (A Run Droplet, C Compare, F the spot/fill tool, which stays available outside a transform session). Because the crop overlay (ImageView), not the panel, usually holds focus, they are dispatched by MW::developShortcutIntercept, gated on developCropEditing: it accepts the key's ShortcutOverride (freeing it from the global QAction) and on the KeyPress calls TransformPanel::handleTransformShortcut(key). The arbiter's value-editor guard excludes text fields, so typing an aspect or angle still works. TransformPanel::eventFilter claims the same keys when the panel or one of its non-text controls has focus. A panel-scoped letter QAction is not used because it would be an ambiguous overload with the window-level shortcuts.

#### 11.22.4 The Crop Tool (ImageView)

Showing the panel calls ImageView::beginCropEdit; hiding it calls endCropEdit. KEY RULE (user-specified): the crop tool NEVER changes the view transform. No zoom, no auto-pan: begin/end only toggle the overlay and leave the image where it is. cropN (normalised image coords) is the source of truth; cropFrameVp (the on-screen frame, viewport px) is DERIVED from it (cropNToVpRect) and tracks the image under the current zoom/pan. All interaction is guarded by cropActive():

- Drag a HANDLE (cropHitTest 0..7: four corners + four edge mids) to resize the frame over the static canvas (cropResizeFromHandle anchors the opposite corner/edge and clamps to the image's on-screen rect); cropN := cropVpRectToN(frame).
- While the crop is still the WHOLE frame (cropIsFull) the cursor is a crop crosshair, and a drag on empty area rubber-bands a brand-new crop (cropDrawNewFrom, kCropDrawNew), so you draw the crop rather than shrinking the full frame by its handles. Over a handle it reverts to resizing.
- Once a sub-crop exists, dragging elsewhere is a NORMAL canvas pan: the frame stays fixed on screen and the image slides under it, and cropN is recomputed from the unchanged frame. You reposition a crop by moving the canvas, not the rectangle.
- Alt/Opt over a rectangle crop shows the "transform" rubber band (red border, circular corner handles, no side handles); an Alt-drag of a corner pulls a free perspective quad (see Warp below).
- The aspect lock (setCropAspect) constrains the ratio; ratio 0 / As shot unlocked is free.
- A crop-size chip ("2032 x 2415") is drawn centred under the frame (just inside its bottom edge when the frame reaches the viewport bottom) and updates live (ImageView::cropDrawSizeLabel). The numbers are FULL-RESOLUTION output pixels (ImageView::cropPixelSize): while the tool is open the render suppresses the crop but keeps straighten / warp, so cropN is scaled by the geometry stage's output size (developGeomOut) when there is geometry, else by the oriented full frame (developGeomSrc); pmItem's size is a last-resort fallback. Not shown while tracing a warp quad (its output size is unknown until rectified).
- When the user zooms or the window resizes, the frame is re-derived from cropN (cropSyncFrameFromN), so the crop stays on the same image content.
- The overlay (cropDrawOverlay, viewport coords in drawForeground): dimmed exterior, rule-of-thirds grid, frame border, handles. ImageView emits cropChanged(x,y,w,h) for persistence. The wheel is swallowed during a crop (the wheel is image navigation, which would strand the overlay).

#### 11.22.5 Warp (4-Point Perspective)

Holding Alt/Opt while dragging a crop CORNER, or choosing the Warp mode, breaks the rectangle into a free quadrilateral (cropWarp = true; cropEnterWarp seeds cropQuadN / cropQuadVp from the rectangle, corners TL, TR, BR, BL). In warp mode only the four corners are handles, each dragged independently and clamped to the image; cropHitTest / cropResizeFromHandle / cropDrawOverlay / cropSyncFrameFromN all branch on cropWarp. The overlay draws the quad with a bilinear 3x3 guide grid and dims outside the polygon. Panning still works (the pan clamp uses the quad's bounding box, cropFrameBBoxVp). Choosing an aspect, re-entering or rectifying leaves warp mode.

The pixel engine is Develop/Transform/croptransform.{h,cpp}, OpenCV only and portable. CropTransform::rectifyPerspective(src, quadPx[4], &outCropNorm) warps the image so the quad becomes an axis-aligned rectangle and returns the corrected image (transparent where the warp leaves the original) plus the largest inscribed axis-aligned rectangle (normalised) as the default crop:

```
cv::getPerspectiveTransform (quad -> WxH, sized by averaged opposite-edge lengths)
-> translate into a positive canvas bounded by the warped corners
-> cv::warpPerspective (BGRA, transparent border)
-> validity mask (alpha >= 250)
-> largest rectangle in a binary matrix (histogram + stack, on a downscaled mask)
```

It was validated offline against the same algorithm in cv2 (a keystone quad gives an exact axis-aligned rect; the inscribed rect avoids the transparent corners).

Known limit: re-warping an already-warped image is wrong if done in place (the new quad would be traced on the warped canvas, but applyGeometry warps the un-warped frame). Reset the Warp row first, then trace again on the original.

#### 11.22.6 Level (Straighten)

The Level mode arms ImageView::beginLevel: draw a line along something that should be horizontal or vertical. On release the line's tilt is reduced to the nearest H/V and emitted (levelAngleChanged). MW::applyDevelopLevel adds it to g.straighten (clamped +/-45), auto-fits the crop to the rotation wedges via CropTransform::straightenCropNorm (the analytic rotatedRectWithMaxArea, pixel-validated to sit inside the valid region), then re-renders the straightened canvas and restarts the crop overlay. applyGeometry's straighten converts to ARGB32 so the wedges are transparent.

#### 11.22.7 Persistence and Rendering

EditStack carries a per-image Geometry: cropX/Y/W/H, straighten, hasWarp + quad[8], fillCanvas, show (and the render-only renderFolds, see [11.22.8 Kaleidoscope](#11228-kaleidoscope)), serialised in the sidecar (toJson / fromJson) and folded into isIdentity. developCompositeStack applies it LAST, CropTransform::applyGeometry(out, job.geometry), after the develop ops and EXIF orientation, on the full-output-dimension image, in both the proxy and async full-res paths (StackRenderJob.geometry from DevelopProperties::stackJob).

The commit model is Lightroom's. MW::developCropEditing gates it: while the crop tool is being edited the render NEUTRALISES the crop so the FULL frame shows under the overlay, but KEEPS straighten and warp, so before rectify you trace on the full frame and after rectify you set the final crop on the corrected canvas.

- MW::enterDevelopCrop: set the flag -> render full -> ImageView::beginCropEdit(storedCrop), saving the Geometry snapshot Esc restores.
- MW::exitDevelopCrop: read cropRect -> endCropEdit -> DevelopProperties::setCurrentGeometry -> clear the flag -> render cropped. It keeps the stored warp and updates only the crop.
- Both are driven from toggleDevelopTransform and developDockVisibilityChange.
- MW::rectifyDevelopCrop stores g.hasWarp + g.quad (the traced corners, normalised in the developed + oriented frame, applyGeometry's input space) + g.crop (the suggested largest-inscribed rect from ImageView::computeRectifyCrop), re-renders the corrected canvas and restarts the overlay on it. The warp is a stored parameter, never baked pixels.
- ImageView::setDevelopPreview re-fits when the image dimensions change (a crop applied or removed); the same-size path (a slider drag) just swaps pixels.

The preview eye is a LIVE RESULT TOGGLE. The panel is only on screen while the crop tool is active, and that view deliberately shows the full frame + overlay, so a plain show/ignore flag would have nothing to toggle. Eye ON commits the overlay's crop, drops the overlay (endCropEdit) and renders with the geometry applied (MW::developCropShowResult gates the crop suppression in renderDevelopPreview and the async full-res path); eye OFF re-renders the full frame and re-arms the overlay. enter/exitDevelopCrop reset the flag + setPreviewShown. (Geometry::show remains in the model and sidecar for a persistent ignore, but it is not what the eye drives.) The header Reset writes an identity Geometry and returns to editing.

The Lens rows the panel briefly carried (Remove chromatic aberration + Defringe) moved to the Global scope's own Lens section on 2026-10-12; see [11.23 Lens Corrections (Chromatic Aberration and Defringe)](#1123-lens-corrections-chromatic-aberration-and-defringe).

#### 11.22.8 Kaleidoscope

Effects > Kaleidoscope, modelled on the mirror / kaleidoscope filters in Affinity Photo. History: a Transform mode (2026-10-19), then a Global-only Effect stored in Geometry, then (2026-10-20) a PER-SCOPE Effect in EditParams, so a mask scope can kaleidoscope just its masked pixels. It sits under Transform in this document because the fold runs in the geometry stage, after the crop. None of the earlier forms shipped, so nothing reads them.

The model (Develop/editparams.h, one per scope):

- kaleidoSegments: 0 = off, else EVEN 2..32. An odd count leaves the last wedge and the first both unreflected, so that one seam would not match; sanitizeParams rounds odd up to even and switches anything out of range off. 2 is a plain mirror across one line. The only field in isIdentity() (the rest are inert while it is off), so a kaleidoscope-only scope is still composited (buildStackJob's identity skip) and a kaleidoscope-only image counts as edited.
- kaleidoX / kaleidoY: the centre, normalized in the CROPPED frame (the fold's own input). kaleidoAngle (deg, -180..180, y-down so positive is clockwise): turns the mirror lines AND the sampled slice together. kaleidoSource (deg): turns only the sampled slice, so the pattern's orientation stays put while its content changes. kaleidoZoom (0.25..8, default 1; the "Zoom" slider is percent 25..800): magnifies the slice about the centre -- the source is sampled at radius r / zoom (KaleidoFold::inv), so the centre stays put and the pattern's middle grows; below 1 reaches further out. Written only when on AND off 1; in Group::Effects, presets (the "kaleido" leaf), kFloatFields; not positional, so EditRotate leaves it. kaleidoOpacity (0..1, default 1; "Opacity" slider in percent): applyKaleidoscope lerps each strip back toward the unfolded frame (cv::addWeighted); applyKaleidoscopeMasked scales the folded coverage by it. Under "Hide global image" a masked fold contributes its own mask plus its folded copies at that opacity (union(cov, lerp(cov, fold(cov), op))), and Global's fold lerps the cut-out's alpha the same way. Same bookkeeping as kaleidoZoom.
- Group::Effects (resetGroup), so Reset Effects, the Effects eye and groupIsDefault's " *" all include it. The per-effect eye is EditScope::showKaleido, folded in effectiveScopeParams (segments to 0, settings kept).
- paramsToJson writes the five keys only when on, so existing recipes keep their JSON and hash. paramsFromJson reads them; sanitizeParams clamps them.
- Presets / Paste Settings: the Effects leaf "kaleido" (kEffectsLeaves; leafChanged = hasKaleido), collected as the five raw fields even when off (a checked leaf with it off turns the target's off), assigned by DevelopPresets::assignParam. updatePresetFromCurrent restores kaleidoX / kaleidoY to 0.5 when the JSON omits them.
- Multi-image: kaleidoSegments in kIntFields, the other four in kFloatFields.
- EditRotate::kaleido turns every scope's centre like any point and adds the quarter turn to the angle (source is relative, so unchanged). Settings still at their defaults are left alone, or every untouched scope would come out with a 90 degree angle and read as edited; only an ON kaleidoscope reports "moved".

The fold (Develop/Transform/croptransform, CropTransform::Kaleido::from(params)): each output pixel goes to polar form about the centre, its angle minus kaleidoAngle is folded into one wedge of 360/N (reflected in odd wedges), and the source is sampled at the same radius along kaleidoAngle + kaleidoSource + the folded angle, bilinear via cv::remap. A ray that leaves the frame is reflected at the border IN THE MAP (reflectCoord), not by remap's border mode, because remap's fixed-point maps saturate at +/-32767, which a reflected ray on a big frame can exceed. Strips of 32 rows each build their own small maps (KaleidoFold::strip) inside cv::parallel_for_, so there is no full-frame map pair. 8-bit stays ARGB32, 16-bit export stays RGBA64. Measured on Quark: ~35 ms at 24 MP, ~5 ms at a 2.7 MP proxy. kaleidoSourceNorm is the point form (unit-tested against the pixels in tst_kaleidoscope).

- applyKaleidoscope: the whole frame (Global, or a scope with no placed mask -- which already means "everywhere" for a scope).
- applyKaleidoscopeMasked(frame, coverage, k): a mask scope. The unmasked part is TRANSPARENT: only the masked pixels are folded, and the result is laid over the frame. Colour and coverage are folded with the same map in one pass and blended out = lerp(frame, fold(frame), fold(mask)), which equals fold(frame x mask) over the frame except within one bilinear tap of a hard mask edge. A subject masked in the sampled slice is mirrored round the centre over the photo; masked content outside the sampled slice is never sampled, so it changes nothing.

Where it runs (MW::developCompositeStack): the develop never sees a kaleidoscope. The job is copied with every kaleidoscope switched off (stripKaleidos), so the develop, the per-scope cache keys (paramsToJson) and the hot prefix's baseKey (renderDevelopPreview strips it there too) are unchanged by a kaleidoscope edit -- a centre drag re-folds the cached frame instead of re-developing the stack. Each folding mask scope's coverage buffer is kept from the composite (foldMasks). After applyGeometry: each mask scope's kaleidoscope in stack order (its buffer carried into the frame by kaleidoMaskInFrame -- to 8-bit, oriented like the composite, through the same geometry, scaled to the frame; the geometry is resolution-independent), then Global's over everything, LAST. On an interactive tick whose geometry forced the full-size upscale, all folds run at proxy resolution and the result is stretched back, so the output keeps the settle render's dimensions.

Suppression (MW::developKaleidoSuppressed): the fold has no inverse, so any overlay drawn in the geometry stage's INPUT space (via developGeomFwd) would land on the wrong pixels. The render switches every kaleidoscope off (stripKaleidos), and the frame is not faithful (no devPreview caching), while:

- the crop overlay is editing (developCropEditing && !developCropShowResult): you crop the real photo;
- ImageView::needsUnfoldedFrame(): a mask tool is open, a committed mask's tint is shown, or the spot brush is armed. ImageView emits unfoldedFrameNeedChanged on each edge (syncUnfoldedFrameNeed, called from begin/endMaskEdit, begin/endSpotEdit, setScopeHasMask, clearScopeMaskTint and the three tint toggles), and MW re-renders (queued) when any scope has a kaleidoscope (DevelopProperties::stackHasKaleido).

Geometry::renderFolds is a RENDER-TIME-ONLY flag (never stored) set on each render job's geometry -- whether its kaleidoscopes are on after suppression -- and compared by sameDevelopGeometry, so a fold switching on or off counts as the frame changing shape exactly as a crop does: a late proxy (developProxyGeomGen) or full-res completion (developRenderGeometry) of the other state is dropped rather than flashed. Known gap: the one-shot WB dropper and the Detail picker sample through maskViewportToNorm, which does not fold, so over a kaleidoscope they sample the un-mirrored position; kaleidoSourceNorm is there for when that matters.

The UI (DevelopProperties::addEffects, every scope): the Effects dropdown's third entry (effectDefs() id 2). Rows "Segments" (0..32), "Angle" and "Source" (-180..180, whole degrees; a handle drag may store a fraction, shown rounded). itemChange handles the three keys itself: odd counts round UP to even (so leaving 0 turns it on at 2, and the slider is re-seeded), each writes the ACTIVE scope's params with its own history mergeKey (<scope>/kaleidoSegments, ...; "Kaleidoscope" / "Kaleidoscope off" / "Kaleidoscope angle" / "Kaleidoscope source"), then paramsChanged + kaleidoToolChanged. syncKaleidoSliders seeds them from the active scope (populateSlidersFromStack). The row's eye and reset are the per-effect ones (showKaleido; resetEffect restores all five).

The handles (ImageView, kaleidoActive() joins developToolActive()): the ACTIVE scope's centre and angle, shown AUTOMATICALLY by MW::syncDevelopKaleidoOverlay exactly while DevelopProperties::kaleidoToolWanted() (Kaleidoscope the shown effect, its row really on screen -- every section above it expanded and the dock visible -- and the active scope's showScope / showEffects / showKaleido eyes open) AND that scope's kaleidoscope is on, in Develop, with no Transform session and !developKaleidoSuppressed(). Re-evaluated on every edge: kaleidoToolChanged (queued; emitted by applyEffectsChoice, populateSlidersFromStack = image / scope / history change, section expand / collapse, the eyes, a Kaleidoscope slider), unfoldedFrameNeedChanged, historyApplied, enter / exit / cancel of the crop session, and entering Develop; leaving Develop ends them (setOperationMode). Not re-evaluated when only the dock is shown / hidden. A handle drag calls DevelopProperties::setKaleidoHandles (the active scope's x / y / angle; ONE history row per drag, mergeKey <scope>/kaleidoHandles; the Angle slider follows). Drawn: a white centre ring + crosshair, a yellow spoke to an angle handle a fixed 80 px out (grabbable at any zoom), dashed seams for every wedge clipped to the image. A press on the spoke drags the angle (Shift snaps to 15 deg); on the centre drags it with the grab offset kept; anywhere else on the image jumps the centre there and keeps dragging (so click-zoom and drag-pan are off while the handles are up; Space pans). The WB / Detail / Point Color pickers and the spot brush are tested before it in mousePressEvent, so they keep priority. Coordinates are the DISPLAYED image's (displayedNormAt), which is the fold's own space because the loupe shows the full geometry whenever the handles are up.

### 11.23 Lens Corrections (Chromatic Aberration and Defringe)

Why (2026-10-07): after the sky-mask halo work, a thin cyan line stayed along the Dempster ridge at -2 EV. The edge pixels were not a mix of sky and ridge (red too low, blue too high), so no mask could fix it: a mask decides HOW MUCH of an adjustment a pixel gets, never its colour. Two lens defects make that kind of edge colour, and Winnow corrects both on the whole image BEFORE any develop step, so every scope, mask (including the Refine Brush) and guide sees corrected edges, and export matches the screen.

#### 11.23.1 Lateral Chromatic Aberration ("Remove Chromatic Aberration")

Red and blue are imaged at slightly different sizes than green, so they are offset radially by an amount that grows toward the corners.

- LensCorrect::estimateCA (Develop/lenscorrect.h) measures it from the image itself, at FULL resolution because the shifts are sub-pixel. Strong-edge tiles away from the centre each give the radial shift of R and B against G that best aligns their radial derivatives (normalised correlation, a coarse grid then a parabolic refine); a weighted, outlier-rejecting fit gives shift = k \* r per channel. A fitted shift under 0.1 px at the corner counts as "no CA" (k = 0).
- LensCorrect::applyCA resamples R and B by (1 + k) about the centre. k is a ratio, so a proxy and a full-res render agree.
- Measured: Dempster (Nikon D810) R +1.11 px / B -0.41 px at the corners; Joffrey (Olympus) +0.22 px; an in-camera-corrected JPEG 0.04 px, correctly none. \~0.27 s at 36 MP in C++ (the prototype took 173 s).
- It ASSUMES the optical centre is the frame centre, so a file cropped before import is estimated poorly.

It was NOT the ridge line. Lateral CA was the first diagnosis and it was wrong for that line: the ridge is mid-frame, where the fit predicts only \~0.25 px. The line is EDGE FRINGING (axial CA / blooming), a coloured rim along high-contrast edges anywhere in the frame, which is what Defringe is for. Lateral CA is real but secondary.

#### 11.23.2 Defringe (Purple / Green)

An edge pixel's colour should be the mix of its two sides, in proportion to where its brightness sits between them. LensCorrect::defringe samples the two sides along the brightness gradient (r + 1.5 px out, r \~3 px at full res), predicts the mix in LINEAR light (t from linear luminance), and pulls the pixel's Lab chroma toward that prediction (lightness is never changed), but only where the DEVIATION's hue is in a fringe band:

- PURPLE group: cyan-blue (235 +/-40 deg), purple (305 +/-35) and magenta (350 +/-25, for the red-magenta rim on Joffrey's snow edges).
- GREEN group: green (140 +/-35), off unless asked for, as in Lightroom.

It is gated by edge strength and a meaningful deviation. Clipped highlights are never modified: their true colour is unknown, and writing the clamped value back would flatten raw headroom.

Two earlier designs failed and are recorded so they are not retried:

- Comparing chroma with the NEIGHBOURHOOD average: a bluish sky hid the fringe that spills onto the dark side of the edge.
- Predicting the mix in LAB: lightness is non-linear, so every vivid edge against shadow read as a fringe.

Measured: Dempster ridge deviation 0.065 -> 0.009 and 0.058 -> 0.008 (the cyan line gone in the plain view); synthetic clean edges (sky/trees, yellow/blue, green leaf/shadow, red/grey, white/navy) changed by &lt;= 0.6 dE, so no damage; synthetic axial and lateral fringes reduced 70-90% where their hue is in a band. Limit: a fringe outside the bands (yellow, red on grey) is deliberately left alone. Joffrey's light rim around the rocks is NOT a fringe (it is blue-on-blue brightness at a mask edge where the rock is about as bright as the darkened sky), and defringe correctly leaves it.

#### 11.23.3 Recipe

Three Global-scope EditParams fields (Develop/editparams.h), written to the sidecar ONLY when set (the JSON is also the devPreview key and the render-cache key, so writing defaults would re-key every image ever edited):

- removeCA: TRI-STATE like denoiseRaw (-1 unset = follow G::autoRemoveCA for a raw, off for anything else; 0 off; 1 on), read through wantsRemoveCA().
- defringePurple / defringeGreen: 0..1.

They are clamped by EditStack::sanitize, listed in kFloatFields / kIntFields for multi-image editing, and recorded in History by noteScopeEdit ("Remove chromatic aberration", "Defringe purple/green").

In Presets and Copy/Paste (2026-10-09) they are two "Global settings" leaves, Remove chromatic aberration and Defringe. buildPreset reads them from scope 0 into preset.globals; mergePreset writes them back to scope 0 through DevelopPresets::assignParam (removeCA with toInt, since "-1" from QSettings must stay unset); multi-image paste rides propagatePreset like every other global. Update with Current Settings refills omitted fields with their defaults (-1 for removeCA and denoiseRaw, 0 for the defringe amounts), because paramsToJson leaves a default out and an absent key would read back as 0, which for denoiseRaw had silently turned "unset" into "off". Pinned in tst_presetparams (lensKeysAreGlobalAndRaw).

#### 11.23.4 Preference

Preferences > Develop > "Remove chromatic aberration on raw files" (G::autoRemoveCA, QSettings Develop/autoRemoveCA, default OFF). An image the user ticked or unticked keeps that choice; JPEGs are never corrected automatically. It changes the default render, so Metadata::defaultRenderKey and devPreviewKey hash it, appended only when ON, so with the default every existing key is unchanged and nothing rebuilds.

#### 11.23.5 UI

The Global scope's LENS section (DevelopProperties::addLens, between Detail and Effects, Lightroom's order), below the lens-profile rows ([11.24 Lens Profile (lensfun)](#1124-lens-profile-lensfun)): a "Remove CA" checkbox showing the EFFECTIVE state, then "Purple fringe" and "Green fringe" sliders (0..100, addSlider). The section exists only while Global is the active scope; a mask scope cannot carry lens corrections.

- itemChange routes the three keys to setGlobalRemoveCA / setGlobalDefringe (always scope 0; removeCA written explicitly as 1 / 0). syncLensPanel loads them from populateSlidersFromStack (image switch, History, undo, scope change) and when the preference changes.
- They belong to EditParams::Group::Lens (with the profile fields), so the Lens header's Reset clears them, its "\*" marks them, and its eye (EditScope::showLens, sidecar key showLens) previews them off. An explicit removeCA / lensProfile folds to 0 under the eye; an unset one stays unset, so with the raw preferences on, an untouched raw keeps its automatic corrections.
- History of the rows: Transform panel (2026-10-07) -> Global Effects section (2026-10-09) -> the Lens section (2026-10-12, with the lens profile). The preset format did not change at any step: presets store field names, and sections only group the checklist.

#### 11.23.6 Pipeline

lensCorrectedSource (Main/mainwindow.cpp) is applied in all three render workers (the proxy, the settled full-res render, and the export / devPreview builder, developPixelSource) to the source they composite from, never on the GUI thread.

- CA coefficients are estimated once per path from full-resolution pixels (the proxy worker is handed the full base for this) and kept in a path store.
- Defringe runs in display terms: the working image goes through toWorkingColor (as-shot WB + camera matrix), / white and display gamma, and ONLY the pixels it changed (its `applied` map) are mapped back through the inverse transform.
- Results are cached per (source object, settings); at most ONE full-resolution result is held (\~430 MB at 36 MP) beside a couple of proxy-sized ones.

#### 11.23.7 Tests

tests/unit/tst_lenscorrect.cpp: a known radial R/B scale recovered and undone; an aligned image reported as none; clean colour edges untouched; an axial fringe removed; clipped highlights bit-identical; and the recipe fields (untouched serialises as before, round trip, sanitize, the wantsRemoveCA truth table). The C++ was also diffed against the Python prototype: CA kR 2.504e-4 vs 2.51e-4, kB -9.45e-5 vs -9.25e-5; defringe identical except clipped highlights (protected by design) and the prototype's own Lab round-trip noise (&lt;= 0.013). Untested in-app at the time of writing.

### 11.24 Lens Profile (lensfun)

Profile-based lens correction (distortion, transverse chromatic aberration (TCA) and vignetting) from the lensfun project's calibration database, in the Global scope's Lens section above Remove CA / defringe. Added 2026-10-12, with manual corrections on 2026-10-13.

#### 11.24.1 The Database Is Shipped, the Library Is Not Linked

liblensfun drags in glib (+ gettext, pcre2, libintl): one more stack to vendor under Lib/ on Windows and to bundle and notarise on macOS. Homebrew only has the old 0.3.4 API, and it is LGPL-3. The user chose to ship lensfun's XML database instead (CC BY-SA 3.0; attribution in the Lens row tooltip and the Lens help page) and implement the models natively.

- Develop/LensDb/db/\*.xml is upstream data/db verbatim (the commit and the update procedure are in Develop/LensDb/README.md), compiled into the binary through Develop/LensDb/lensfun.qrc (:/lensfun), so there is no packaging step on either platform.
- \*.xml files in &lt;AppDataLocation>/lensfun (macOS \~/Library/Application Support/Winnow/lensfun) are read on top and replace a bundled lens / camera with the same identity. That is how a user adds a lens or takes a newer database without a rebuild.
- Note: the devPreview / render keys do not hash the database, so an updated profile does not invalidate previews built with the old one.

#### 11.24.2 Database and Lookup (Develop/lensdb.h/.cpp)

- Parsed once with QXmlStreamReader under std::call_once (\~125 ms in a debug build; 1057 cameras / 1571 lenses, the same counts liblensfun loads), preloaded on a pool thread at startup (LensDb::preload, Main/initialize.cpp), and immutable afterwards, so every query is lock-free.
- A lens's identity (Lens::id, the EditParams::lensProfileId value) is "maker|model|crop": the database calibrates some lenses twice under one name (full frame and APS-C), and maker|model alone silently dropped 99 of them.
- LensDb::resolve(shot, overrideId) is the one call the render and the panel make: camera lookup, lens match (or the user's pick), then interpolation. It returns the coefficients or a short reason for the panel ("no lens in EXIF", "no profile found", "profiled on a smaller sensor", "no focal length in EXIF", "no calibration at N mm"). It is memoised (render workers ask every tick).

Matching follows lensfun's own rules:

- Camera: maker + model equal ignoring case and spacing, also with the maker's first word in front (Winnow's models are maker-prefixed via canonicalCameraModel; lensfun's sometimes are).
- Lens: lensfun's WORD split (runs of digits / punctuation / other; single punctuation and a lone "f" dropped; order and case ignored), scored by Dice overlap with the maker's words removed from both sides, requiring recall >= 0.75 and Dice >= 0.6. The NUMBER words must match exactly both ways (or a 24-70 f/4 would match a 24-70 f/2.8).
- Candidates must fit the camera's mount (lensfun's mount compat lists), cover the shot's focal length (2% + 0.5 mm slack: the datamodel stores focal length as WHOLE mm, which puts a compact's 4.3 mm at 4), and be calibrated on a sensor no smaller than the camera's (lensfun's crop ratio >= 0.96).
- A FIXED-LENS camera (its mount is not a declared &lt;mount>) takes the one lens carrying that mount, whatever the EXIF lens name says.

Interpolation is lensfun's scheme:

- Distortion / TCA: a Hermite spline over focal length through the calibrations either side (Catmull-Rom tangents, chord at the ends). Terms that follow 1/f (all distortion terms; TCA's terms other than kr/kb/vr/vb) are multiplied by their calibration's focal before the spline and divided by the shot's after. Outside the calibrated range the nearest end is used.
- Vignetting: inverse-distance weighting, power 3.5, in (focal normalised to the zoom range, 4/aperture, 0.1/distance). No vignetting when the nearest calibration is further than 1 in that space or the aperture is unknown. Distance is not read from EXIF: 1000 m (lensfun's infinity).

#### 11.24.3 The Models (Develop/lensprofile.h)

Header-only, OpenCV core. Every model maps the UNDISTORTED radius to the distorted one, so correction is a direct lookup per output pixel and nothing is inverted:

```
output pixel -> / auto-scale
-> distortion   ptlens a r^3 + b r^2 + c r + 1-a-b-c | poly3 1-k1+k1 r^2 | poly5 1+k1 r^2+k2 r^4
-> per-channel TCA (linear k, poly3 b r^2 + c r + v; green is the reference)
-> photo position, bilinear-sampled per channel
-> devignette AT THAT PHOTO POSITION   C / (1 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4 + k3 r^6)
```

(The vignetting radius is a photo radius: lensfun devignettes the photo first.)

- Units: distortion / TCA r = 1 at half the SHORT side of the calibration frame (43.27 / lensCrop / hypot(aspect, 1) / 2 mm); vignetting r = 1 at the calibration frame's corner (43.27 / lensCrop / 2 mm); photo mm per pixel = 43.27 / cameraCrop / hypot(W-1, H-1). W and H are the frame's own, so proxy and full resolution agree.
- Winnow follows lensfun 0.3.x, not master, in two places, because 0.3.x is what lensfunpy (the oracle) and the raw developers ship: NO centre normalisation of ptlens / poly3 (master divides out the 1/d magnification; it does not survive the auto-scale anyway), and the W-1 pixel-centre span.
- Amounts: distortion scales D toward 1 (D_a = 1 + a(D - 1)); vignetting raises the gain to the power a. Range 0..2 (panel 0..200), 1 = as calibrated. The profile's TCA follows the Remove CA checkbox.

Auto-scale: the corrected frame is zoomed (about the optical centre) by the smallest factor at which every BORDER pixel samples inside the photo, so there are no empty corners and no more of the photo is discarded than that takes (it can be &lt; 1 for pincushion). Bisection over 64 samples per edge. Lensfun's own GetAutoScale is looser: on the FE 70-300 at 135 mm its corner still samples 4 px outside the frame.

#### 11.24.4 Manual Corrections

Lightroom's Manual tab (2026-10-13): EditParams lensManualDistortion / lensManualVignetting (-1..1, panel -100..100, default 0) and lensManualMidpoint (0..1, panel 0..100, default 0.5), carried in LensProfile::Amounts::manual\*. They need NO profile. The motivating case was a Sony FE 600mm F4 GM, which lensfun 0.3.x has never calibrated, so the profile amount sliders (which only scale the profile) were rightly greyed and nothing could be corrected.

- Defined on the FRAME, not a calibration sensor: rn = 1 at the frame's corner (half its diagonal), about the same centre as the profile (Frame::pxToManual).
- Distortion: the output position is scaled by M = 1 - kManualDistK \* m \* rn^2 BEFORE the profile lookup, so manual is a correction on top of the profile in the same resample; + corrects barrel.
- Vignetting: gain 2^(v \* kManualVigEV \* rn^p), p = 2^(3 \* midpoint), evaluated at the photo position and multiplied with the profile's (totalVignettingGain); + brightens corners.
- kManualDistK = 0.10 and kManualVigEV = 2.0 are tuning constants. Recipes store the slider, so changing them re-renders every saved manual correction.
- Manual distortion is in geometryActive, so the auto-scale fills the frame for it too (a barrel fix at +100 zooms 0.966, a pincushion fix at -100 1.084, on a 3:2 frame).
- lensProfileState no longer returns early when the profile is off or unresolved: the coeffs stay empty and the manual terms alone can make it active. Its lens id is then "manual", and geomKey / key carry the manual values (Midpoint only while Vignetting is non-zero).
- Unlike Effects > Vignette (post-crop, creative, display-referred), this is applied to the BASE before any crop, where the lens's falloff actually lives.

#### 11.24.5 Pipeline

lensCorrectedSource (Main/mainwindow.cpp) applies the profile FIRST, resampling the source straight into the new buffer (applyLensProfile; no copy-then-overwrite), then the image-measured CA, which is SKIPPED when the profile has TCA and Remove CA is on (two corrections of one aberration), then defringe ([11.23 Lens Corrections (Chromatic Aberration and Defringe)](#1123-lens-corrections-chromatic-aberration-and-defringe)).

- LensProfileState (lensProfileState(shot, recipe, isRaw)) is the resolved correction with two keys: key (everything; the source cache and the proxy stack cache's baseKey, which would otherwise miss an unset recipe following the preference) and geomKey (only what MOVES pixels: distortion amount + TCA).
- The shot (LensDb::Shot: camera make/model, lens, focal, aperture) comes from the datamodel row on the GUI thread (MW::lensShotFor) for the loupe paths, and from the job's ImageMetadata (lensShotFromMetadata) for export / devPreview.
- Cost: \~225 ms at 36 MP, \~25 ms on a 3.8 MP proxy (-O2); cached per source object, so only lens-slider ticks pay it.

Everything built from the base must see the same geometry. The AI mask guides (subject, sky, depth, SAM object) and the range reference are downscaled from the UNCORRECTED base and developed; with the profile moving pixels they would select the subject where it was before correction.

- MW::correctGuideForLens applies the same profile to each guide image before it is developed.
- MW::noteLensGeometry, the first call in every ensure\* builder, drops the image's cached references when its geomKey changes (developLensGeomKeys: path -> the geometry they were built under; object refs are keyed by path + brush, so that whole small store goes). A vignetting tick does not change geomKey, so it never re-runs a two-second sky model. The range reference's key also carries the full lens key.
- The Detail 1:1 patch is RESAMPLED from the full frame through the same mapping (cutDetailRoi with the job's LensProfileState; the corrected frame has the same dimensions, so the patch rectangle means the same place).
- User-drawn masks need nothing: they live in output-normalised coordinates, which are the corrected frame's.

#### 11.24.6 UI

DevelopProperties::addLens / addLensProfileRow / repopulateLensCombo:

- "Lens profile" checkbox, showing the EFFECTIVE state like Remove CA.
- "Lens" row: a combo owning its value cell (the camera-profile row's idiom). Its first entry is the automatic match WITH its result: "Auto: &lt;lens>", "Auto (&lt;reason>)", or, when a lens IS matched but has nothing for this shot, "Auto: &lt;lens>  (&lt;reason>)". The reason sits where the user looks ([11.19 Develop Alerts and the Greyed Panel (Severity Rows, Disabled States)](#1119-develop-alerts-and-the-greyed-panel-severity-rows-disabled-states)). Then every profiled lens that fits the camera's mount (names the database uses twice get "(crop N)"). A picked lens the camera cannot take is shown, marked and selected, never swapped for Auto. Picking a lens turns the profile on. The combo elides (AdjustToMinimumContentsLengthWithIcon) so long names cannot widen the dock; its tooltip lists what the profile corrects for this shot, the EXIF lens and the lensfun credit.
- "Distortion" / "Vignetting" sliders 0..200 (default 100), greyed when the profile is off or has no such data for the shot.
- A "Manual" caption row, then "Distortion" / "Vignetting" (-100..100) and "Midpoint" (0..100, default 50), always live.
- Setters setGlobalLensProfile / setGlobalLensAmount / setGlobalLensManual / setGlobalLensProfileId (scope 0, noteScopeEdit -> History + multi-image).

Greyed rows survive a panel enable. setPanelEnabled(true) -> applyItemsEnabled(true) used to set EVERY caption's UR_isEnabled, un-greying the captions of rows whose own gate (setItemEnabled) had disabled their editor: a black "Distortion" over a dead slider. applyItemsEnabled now leaves a row's caption grey when its editor has WA_ForceDisabled (set only by that editor's own setEnabled(false), never inherited from the tree). This applies to every such gate (lens amounts, Point Color, raw denoise amounts).

#### 11.24.7 Recipe and Presets

- EditParams lensProfile (tri-state like removeCA: -1 follows G::autoLensProfile for a raw), lensDistortion, lensVignetting (0..2, default 1) and lensProfileId ("" = automatic), all in Group::Lens; written to the sidecar only when off their defaults.
- Preferences > Develop > "Apply lens profile on raw files" (G::autoLensProfile, QSettings Develop/autoLensProfile, default OFF), hashed into defaultRenderKey / devPreviewKey only when ON.
- Presets / Copy-Paste: a "Lens profile" leaf under Global settings carrying all four (lensProfileId empty = each target matches its own EXIF), and a separate "Lens manual corrections" leaf carrying the three lensManual\* keys. updatePresetFromCurrent restores the absent-key defaults explicitly (-1 / 1.0 / "" / Midpoint 0.5), since an absent key would otherwise read back as 0 = "no correction".
- The diff/copy tables carry lensDistortion / lensVignetting / lensManual\* / lensProfile and a lensProfileId pseudo-field, so multi-image edits propagate them.

#### 11.24.8 Tests

tests/unit/tst_lensprofile.cpp tests against liblensfun ITSELF. tests/fixtures/lensfun_oracle.py runs lensfunpy (lensfun 0.3.4) over the same database (version header lowered and real-focal stripped: 0.3.4 rejects both and neither matters for rectilinear) for five shots (ptlens / poly3 / poly5 distortion, poly3 TCA, pa vignetting, an FX lens on a DX body, a portrait frame, a fixed-lens compact at 4:3) and writes unit/lensprofile_oracle.h.

- Pinned: the load counts, lensfun's word split, the same camera crop and lens chosen, interpolated terms (1e-6), every sampled output pixel's photo position per channel (worst 0.0013 px), devignetting gains (0.1%), auto-scale leaves no border pixel outside, a region equals the same window of the whole-frame render, identity is bit-exact, linear TCA, amounts, the no-match cases and the smaller-sensor refusal.
- manualWithoutProfile pins the manual terms with an EMPTY Coeffs: identity at zero, the corner's documented scale, the auto-scale direction for barrel vs pincushion, and the vignetting gain at centre / corner and its midpoint ordering.
- tst_presetparams pins the four preset keys and the three manual ones.

### 11.25 Overlays Over a Transformed Image (Mask Space vs Displayed Space)
