Everything [11.33 Develop Presets](#1133-develop-presets) says therefore holds unchanged: only the ticked settings are written, the target is the ACTIVE scope, the per-image items (raw engine, raw NR, lens, tone splits, crop / level / warp) go to scope 0 / the geometry whatever is active, spots APPEND rather than replace, and the mask does not travel. Pasting is one history step ("Sky: Paste settings"), undone by clicking the row above it in History.

#### 11.34.1 The Buffer

A single slot that every Copy overwrites, held by the SAME store class (DevelopPresets) under its own QSettings root, "Develop Clipboard/buffer". read / write / migrate are shared with presets via readGroup / writeGroup, so the copy buffer gets the schema version and forward tolerance for free, and cannot appear in names() or collide with a preset the user names "clipboard". DevelopPreset also carries sourceImage (display only), which is what lets the UI say WHAT would be pasted.

The buffer is SESSION SCOPED, unlike Lightroom's: the DevelopPresets constructor calls clearClipboard(), which removes the whole "Develop Clipboard" group, so every run starts with nothing copied and Paste reports nothing until the first Copy. QSettings holds the buffer only because that is where the preset store already reads and writes; persistence would be an accident of sharing the store, not a feature, and pasting adjustments copied in an earlier session, from an image long out of view, is far more often a slip than an intent.

#### 11.34.2 UI

- Dialog: SaveDevelopPresetDlg::Mode::CopySettings: the same groups, Scope combo, pre-checked "differs from default" and All / None, minus the name field and its overwrite check. Title "Copy Develop Settings", button "Copy". One dialog class, because "pick a set of develop settings, from a scope" is the same question either way.
- Menu: Utilities > Develop, above Save Develop Preset. Paste RENAMES itself to "Paste Develop Settings from IMG_1234.NEF" in syncDevelopMenuEnabled, so the menu answers "have I copied anything?" without being opened twice. The Develop dock context menu carries the same three items.
- Shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+Opt/Alt+C and +V, real QKeySequences (like Save Preset's Cmd+Shift+N; the bare-key arbiter only handles UNMODIFIED keys), enabled only in Develop mode by setOperationMode. Lightroom's own keys are Shift+Cmd+C/V, but Shift+Cmd+C is already "Copy images" in Winnow, and two enabled actions on one sequence is an ambiguous shortcut.

Gotcha: Paste is NOT disabled on an empty clipboard. syncDevelopMenuEnabled runs on aboutToShow, and a disabled QAction's shortcut does not fire, so greying it there would leave Cmd+Opt+V dead until the menu happened to be opened again after a copy. The slot reports "No develop settings have been copied yet" instead.

Paste lands on the WHOLE selection ([11.35 Multi-Image Editing](#1135-multi-image-editing)). Paste is the whole-object path: every other selected image gets the same mergePreset onto its scope 0, so the copied crop, straighten, warp and spot heals travel with it exactly as on the current image. The confirmation says how many images were written ("Pasted develop settings from IMG_1234.NEF onto 12 images"), since silence about a bulk overwrite is how a user loses forty recipes.

### 11.35 Multi-Image Editing

With more than one image selected, EVERY develop edit made on the current image is copied to every other selected image (Lightroom's Auto Sync, always on); Paste Settings and Apply Preset do the same. The Develop dock carries an AMBER warning row ("Multiple images will have edits applied.") whenever the selection is larger than one, because the images being changed are off screen and the change is otherwise invisible until the user navigates to them. Amber, not red: the edit does work, it just works on more than the visible image; red is reserved for a show stopper ([11.19 Develop Alerts and the Greyed Panel (Severity Rows, Disabled States)](#1119-develop-alerts-and-the-greyed-panel-severity-rows-disabled-states)). Videos in the selection are skipped: they have no develop recipe, and writing one would leave a sidecar the pipeline never reads.

#### 11.35.1 The Rules

The "Multi-image editing" block in DevelopProperties' header:

- ABSOLUTE, not relative. The target gets the same VALUE, not the same delta: Temp lands as the same Kelvin everywhere (temp / tint are absolute), and Exposure +0.5 means +0.5 EV on every image, whatever each started from. A delta rule would be unpredictable on a mixed selection where some images are already edited.
- WHAT CHANGED, not the whole recipe. Each commit is diffed against propagateBase (the current image's scope-0 params as of the previous commit), and only the fields that actually moved are written, so syncing Exposure onto twelve images leaves each one's own Temp alone.
- The GLOBAL SCOPE travels. A drawn mask scope's params describe pixels chosen from THIS image's content, so an edit made inside a brush, gradient, range, depth or object mask scope stays on the current image, the same rule presets follow. Mask geometry and spot heals are per-image for the same reason and are never propagated by an adjustment. (A pasted preset is different: it carries its own per-image items and applies them, because the user explicitly asked for that recipe.)
- CROP / STRAIGHTEN / WARP travel (2026-09-30). Geometry is per-stack, outside EditParams, but cropping with several images selected is a sync the user expects; the original "per-image" rule left the warning row claiming every edit applied while the crop silently stayed on one image. Each Transform control is its own pseudo-field ("crop", "straighten", "warp"; diffGeometryFields / copyGeometryFields beside kFloatFields), diffed against propagateGeomBase, so a crop does not drag the current image's straighten onto images that have their own. Coordinates are normalised, so the same rect lands proportionally on every image (on a mixed portrait/landscape selection the crop's aspect therefore differs between orientations). Geometry::show (Transform Preview) is a view toggle and stays per-image.
- AI MASK SCOPES travel (2026-10-13), described next.

#### 11.35.2 AI Mask Scopes Travel

A mask scope built ONLY from Subject / Sky / Background submasks (DevelopProperties::isPortableScope) is the exception to the mask rule: the model redraws that selection from each image's own pixels, so "the sky" means the same thing on every image. Add a Sky mask with 12 images selected and all 12 get a Sky mask scope, each masked by its own sky; the adjustments made in it apply to all 12.

- Such a scope carries EditScope::link (a UUID; sidecar key "link", written only when set, so additive).
- noteScopeEdit runs diffLinkedScopes BEFORE recording the History step. It diffs every linked or AI-only scope against propagateScopesBase (the current image's scopes at the last commit, matched by link, or by position for a scope with no link yet) into a ScopeSync {params fields that moved, submask list changed, scope state changed (combine / edge / halo / enabled / preview eyes), deleted}.
- An AI-only scope that changed gets its link there, but only when other images are selected, so a mask made on one image alone never appears elsewhere until it is edited with others selected. The link is assigned before the step is recorded, so a revert cannot strip it (a stripped link would make the next edit mint a second one and add a second copy to every target).
- The changes ride the normal batch (pendingScopes beside pendingFields, the same syncId and 400 ms timer). flushPropagation calls applyLinkedScopes on each target: no scope with that link -> a whole copy is appended (name made unique on that image); one with it -> the moved params, the state and (while still AI-only) the submask list are copied; deleted here -> deleted there. Scope NAMES do not sync.
- A linked scope that gains a geometry submask (a Refine Brush stroke) stops sending its submasks (the stroke was drawn on this image) but still sends its params.
- The target's mask is computed when its preview renders (the devPreview builder's ensureSubjectMask / ensureSkyMask, one model run per image on the GUI thread), so a large selection takes a model run per image.
- Tested: tst_historystore::scopeLinkSurvivesSidecarRoundTrip. The in-app fan-out is untested.

Still open: the other CONTENT masks (Depth, Luminance / Color Range) also compute their coverage from each image's own pixels and could travel the same way, but isPortableScope admits only Subject / Sky / Background today. Brush, gradient and Object (SAM) masks are drawn in one image's coordinates and stay per-image. If they are added: inference is GUI-thread (\~200-400 ms per image), so a large selection needs visible progress, and the ensure\* early-outs that key on the LAST path only should test the per-path ref instead, so moving between images does not re-run the model.

#### 11.35.3 Where It Hooks

queuePropagation() is called from noteScopeEdit(), the single commit point every develop action already goes through. That is deliberate: any future edit path gets multi-image behaviour by construction rather than by remembering to add a call. The field-by-field diff and copy share ONE table of member pointers (kFloatFields / kIntFields, above diffParamFields), so they cannot drift apart; see [11.38 Adding or Changing a Develop Adjustment (Checklist)](#1138-adding-or-changing-a-develop-adjustment-checklist).

Batching: a slider drag commits continuously and each target may need a sidecar read, so commits accumulate in pendingFields and land once edits settle (kPropagateMs, 400 ms). propagateTargets is captured when a batch OPENS, so changing the selection mid-drag cannot redirect edits already made, and the drag reads the selection once instead of once per tick. flushPropagation() forces the batch out early: MW::updateDevelopSelectionWarning calls it on every selection change, and it also runs before an image switch, a history revert, a preset / paste, and flushAll.

Thumbnails: a propagated image has no render in memory, so its flush writes no preview; MW::devPreviewUpdated then queues it for the devPreview builder (src "sync"), which renders it in the background even inside Develop ([12.1 Original and Developed Previews](#121-original-and-developed-previews)).

Persistence: propagated images are marked dirty like any edited image and written by the ordinary flush path. The debounced write was widened from flushImage(current) to flushAll() for this: a crash should lose no more of the other selected images than of the one being edited.

#### 11.35.4 History Follows the Link

Every image an edit lands on gets the step, and the steps are linked (2026-09-30). This used to be recorded only on images the user had already opened (to spare DevelopHistory's then-40-image LRU store), so after a multi-image crop the other images had no step and a History revert could only undo the current one.

- flushPropagation seeds any target with no history (its state BEFORE the edit) and records the step on every target. kMaxImages went to 200 so a big selection does not evict what it just edited, and the image on screen is touched last so its own history is never the one evicted.
- Each batch gets a syncId (HistoryEntry::syncId), stamped on the current image's step (DevelopHistory::stampTop, since the source records before the batch exists) and on every target's step; Paste Settings / Apply Preset (propagatePreset) do the same.
- A batch is ONE history step: a commit with a different mergeKey (or none) flushes the open batch first, so two steps on the current image never map onto one step elsewhere. Propagated entries still coalesce on the field set, so a long Exposure drag reads as one "Exposure" step on every image.

Reverting follows the link, on the selection. A click in History moves the current image to that entry; then revertSelectionToMatch moves every OTHER selected image that shares linked steps with it to the matching point in its own history: just before its first linked step that is no longer in force (DevelopHistory::syncedPos), or its newest step when all are (so a forward click is a redo). An image sharing no linked step is untouched, and so is every image outside the selection: a revert follows the same rule as an edit. Reverted images are marked dirty, so the flush writes them and the devPreview builder rebuilds their thumbnails. Hover still previews only the current image.

### 11.36 Develop History

A Lightroom-style list of every develop action on the current image. Hovering an entry previews that state in the loupe; clicking it reverts the image to it.

#### 11.36.1 The Panel

The dock is called History and holds TWO sections, each under a gradient band: History (this list) and Presets ([11.33 Develop Presets](#1133-develop-presets)). Its body is HistoryPanel (Develop/History/historypanel.{h,cpp}), which creates both QListWidgets and hands them to MW to bind; it knows nothing about develop state itself.

- The bands are PanelSectionHeader, painting the same G::backgroundShade a -> b ramp PropertyDelegate paints behind the Develop editor's section rows, so a section header reads the same everywhere. Each carries a 9 px branch arrow (the ScopeHeader pattern), a caption that toggles on click, and a trailing [:] menu with that section's help. A collapsed section hides its LIST, never its band. Expand state persists per section under Develop/SectionExpanded/&lt;name> and defaults to expanded.
- The panel's own title bar is just "History" and an X; there is no [?], because the help lives in the section menus.

A drag divider between the sections: they sit in a vertical QSplitter (HistoryPanel::splitter), each pane being its band plus its list, so the handle sits on the Presets band's top edge and the user drags it to share the dock (the Keywords dock's tags / tree idiom).

- The panes are NOT collapsible (setChildrenCollapsible(false)): a pane dragged to nothing would take its band with it, and folding is the arrow's job.
- HistoryPanel::applySplit runs after every expand / collapse. A FOLDED pane is capped at its band's height so the open section takes the rest of the dock; with both folded, the splitter itself is capped, so the panel's trailing stretch takes the leftover and the bands stay stacked at the top; with both open, the caps come off and the remembered split is re-applied (lifting a cap does not grow the pane back by itself, so without setSizes a re-opened section would stay squeezed to its band).
- The split persists under Develop/SectionSplit as the two expanded pane heights, written only on a user drag with both sections open; setSizes treats them as proportions, and the first-run split is 3:2 in History's favour. This replaced an earlier fit-to-content sizing that left the user no say in the split.

Right-click anywhere in the panel for Expand all / Collapse all / Solo mode (HistoryPanel::contextMenuEvent). The bands and the History list do not consume the right-click, so it reaches the panel; the Presets list keeps its own preset menu (Qt::CustomContextMenu). SOLO MODE is Lightroom's: at most one section open, so opening one folds the other (persisted under Develop/SectionSolo). Two asymmetries are deliberate:

- Solo folds the other section only on an OPEN; closing one in solo mode leaves nothing open, which is a legitimate state.
- Turning solo ON with both sections open resolves the contradiction immediately in History's favour, it being the primary list.
- "Expand all" stays live while solo is on and turns solo OFF on its way: asking for every section open has already said which half of the contradiction the user meant. The restore path re-checks the pair as well, since the two expand keys are written independently and a half-written settings file must not open the panel in a state solo mode forbids.

#### 11.36.2 The Copy / Paste Button Row

Pinned to the bottom of the panel: the two actions most used while carrying a look from one image to the next, where the lists they work with already are, reachable without the menu or the modified combo ([11.34 Copy and Paste Develop Settings](#1134-copy-and-paste-develop-settings)). They TRIGGER developCopySettingsAction / developPasteSettingsAction rather than duplicating anything, so they grey with those menu items outside Develop mode. The labels are the literals "Copy" and "Paste": the Paste action's own text is rewritten at runtime to "Paste Develop Settings from &lt;image>", which no button should grow to fit. The row is built in createUtilActions beside the two actions, NOT in createHistoryDock, because createDocks() runs BEFORE createActions().

The row itself is general: PanelButtonBar (Utilities/panelbuttonbar.h) adds a row of push buttons to the TOP or BOTTOM edge of any panel with a vertical layout, each stretched to an equal share of the width (Add(panel, buttons, edge); MakeButton(action, label) for a button that follows a QAction's enabled state). Header-only with no Q_OBJECT, the shape of Utilities/gradientheader.h. A BOTTOM row is APPENDED after the trailing addStretch(1) a packed panel ends with, so the stretch eats the slack and the row lands on the bottom edge as the dock resizes; a TOP row is inserted at index 0. It handles three things every hand-rolled row before it (CatalogView's Load/Add, MaskPanel's commit row) had to rediscover:

- The app sheet's "QPushButton { min-width: 100px }" is a REAL minimum, so a row of buttons becomes a hard floor on how narrow the dock can be dragged; each button gets min-width: 0.
- A plain QWidget under the app sheet fills opaquely and would paint a slab over the panel; the bar's background is explicitly transparent, with the ID selector #panelButtonBar keeping the rule off the buttons.
- NO setFixedHeight or minimum height anywhere in it: DockWidget::setCollapsed folds the dock by zeroing the body's minimum height, and a hard floor inside the body propagates back up and blocks it.

The bar carries the usual panel separator (G::panelBorderHeight in G::panelSeparatorColor) on the side facing the panel contents. That colour tracks backgroundShade, and a per-widget stylesheet is not regenerated by the app-sheet rebuild, so MW::setBackgroundShade and MW::setFontSize call PanelButtonBar::Restyle(this).

#### 11.36.3 Showing the Dock

The dock is tabbed with the Develop dock in the right area and shown / hidden with it; the two are one tool. Develop is always raised as the front tab of the group (History is shown first, then Develop, then raised), so History is reached by clicking its tab, or with H (View > History Panel). H is a Develop MODE LOCAL key (developShortcuts / developShortcutIntercept), not a QKeySequence, since the dock is Develop-only; the F-key series the other docks use ran out at F10 (F11 is taken by macOS). Like F3-F9 it shows / raises rather than toggles. In FULL SCREEN it is independent of the group: Preferences > Full screen defaults > "Show history panel" (fullScreenDocks.isHistory, persisted as isFullScreenHistory), one toggle for both sections.

- Startup: Winnow always opens in Preview mode, so MW::showEvent hides the Develop tool after restoreState() through closeDevelopDock(), which takes the History panel with it and unchecks both dock actions. Hiding developDock alone was not enough: restoreState() re-shows every dock the last session had visible, so quitting from Develop reopened with History on screen, visible but disabled.
- Gotcha (cost an afternoon): a TABIFIED dock keeps isVisible() == true even when a sibling tab is selected; that is why isSelectedDockTab tests the visible REGION. developDockVisibilityChange used to raise() developDock on any visibilityChanged where isVisible() was true, which yanked Develop back to the front the moment a sibling tab was clicked, so the History tab appeared dead. It now raises only when Develop really is the front tab. Any future dock tabbed with Develop needs the same care.

#### 11.36.4 The Sidecar Does Not Record Actions

winnow:Develop holds ONE base64 blob: the current EditStack, i.e. the RESULT state (Metadata::readDevelopSidecar / writeDevelopSidecar, DevelopProperties::flushImage). There is no action log to read, so History builds its own timeline of labelled EditStack SNAPSHOTS. It stays in sync with the sidecar by sharing the same object: an entry IS an EditStack, so restoring one just writes it back into stackCache and marks the image dirty, and the ordinary flush persists it. The sidecar remains the single source of truth for the current state.

#### 11.36.5 Persisted in the Local Index

Since 2026-09-30 (it used to be session scoped). Nothing new is written to the sidecar. flushImage saves the image's whole history to index.db, in the same pass as the sidecar write: HistoryStore (Develop/History/historystore.\*), table develop_history (schema 18): pathkey, pos, recipe stamp, and the entries as qCompress'd JSON.

- DevelopHistory::seed restores it through its loader hook on the image's first touch in a session, but ONLY if the row's stamp (HistoryEntry::recipeStamp, the SHA-1 of the recipe written in that flush) matches the recipe the sidecar holds now. Otherwise (edited on another machine, a restored sidecar, a reset elsewhere) the history starts afresh as Original + "Saved settings": a history that does not lead to the image on screen would revert to states the user never saw.
- The stamp is of the RECIPE, not of the current step's snapshot: some changes reach the recipe without recording a step and must not make a good history look stale (tst_historystore pins both, and that the stamp survives the sidecar round trip).
- FileOps moves / deletes carry the rows, versions included; forget() (reset, a deleted version) removes the row; the table is pruned to HistoryStore::kMaxImages (5000) by last save.
- Multi-image link ids (HistoryEntry::syncId) are saved too, so nextSyncId starts from the clock rather than 0.
- Cost measured on a 69-step, 68-spot history: save \~6-7 ms, load \~4 ms, 5 KB stored.
- In memory DevelopHistory caps at kMaxEntries (100) steps per image, dropping the oldest EDITS after Original and counting them in Original's `trimmed` (persisted in the entry JSON), which the dock shows as a dimmed, unclickable "N earlier steps trimmed" row above Original; and at kMaxImages (200) images LRU. An evicted image's history is still in the store.

Entry 0 is always the TRUE ORIGINAL (2026-10-03): the image with no develop edits, DevelopHistory::originalStack (one default Global scope), never advanced, relabelled or replaced. An image whose sidecar already carried edits when first seen gets a second step, "Saved settings". Previously the cap ADVANCED "Original" to the dropped step's state, so once history persisted, a truncated history showed a mid-edit state labelled "Original" in every later session. Trimming strands nothing, because every step is a whole EditStack. Histories saved before the change are fixed on load (DevelopHistory::normalizeOriginal): an entry 0 that is not identity is kept as an ordinary step ("Original" relabelled "Earlier edits"; "Saved settings" kept) and the real original is inserted under it, pos shifted by one. tst_historystore::capKeepsTrueOriginal / legacyBaselineGetsOriginal pin both. Multi-image steps are LINKED across images ([11.35.4 History Follows the Link](#11354-history-follows-the-link)).

#### 11.36.6 Recording (One Seam)

Every develop action already ended with the same three lines (dirty.insert(currentImagePath) / emit paramsChanged() / debounceWriteTimer->start()). That dirty.insert was the exact commit point, and every one of them (\~30) is now DevelopProperties::noteEdit(action, value, mergeKey): mark dirty, record the snapshot, arm the debounced write. Use noteScopeEdit(scope, ...) where the prefix is not the active scope: "Global" for the raw rows (they always write scope 0) and "" for whole-image actions (crop, spot heals) that belong to no scope.

- Labels: the scope prefix is the active EditScope's name, except that an unrenamed "Mask N" carrying tools reads as its first tool (maskToolName), so an edit on a Subject mask logs as "Subject Mask: Hue  -18". Slider captions come from the row's own caption cell; values are formatted exactly as the slider shows them (integer when UR_Div is 0, else 2 dp) with a + on positives (historyValueText).
- Coalescing: a non-empty mergeKey that matches the top entry REPLACES it, so a whole slider or colour-wheel drag is ONE entry. Structural actions (add / delete mask, reset, crop) pass no mergeKey.
- Guards: isPopulating (pushing saved values into the editors) and isRestoringHistory (a revert repopulating the panel) suppress recording.

#### 11.36.7 Reverting and Previewing

The revert model is Lightroom's. pos is the entry currently applied. Recording a new action while pos is not the last entry DISCARDS everything after pos: editing from an earlier state truncates, like an undo stack. Rows after pos are painted dimmed meanwhile.

- Hover preview = PROXY RENDER ONLY. previewHistoryEntry sets previewStack / previewActive (read at the top of stackJob and editParams, so nothing else in the render path knows) and emits historyPreviewChanged, which createDevelopDock connects to renderDevelopPreview(false). It deliberately does NOT go through developParamsChange, which also arms the full-res settle render: a cursor passing down the list must not queue one heavy render per row. The view debounces the hover (kHoverDelayMs 120) and ends the preview on leave; preview is skipped while a mask tool or the spot tool is armed (they own the canvas overlay).
- The click (applyHistoryEntry) takes the full path: retire any half-built mask tool, write the snapshot into stackCache, mark dirty, refreshScopeList + buildTree (scope / mask structure may differ), emit paramsChanged.
- A chosen row RE-SEEDS THE CROP OVERLAY. While the crop tool is open the overlay owns its own rectangle (ImageView::cropN) and exitDevelopCrop commits it on close, so a revert that only replaced stackCache left the old crop on screen and wrote it straight back (entering with R and choosing Original did nothing). applyHistoryEntry emits historyApplied (before paramsChanged); MW restarts the overlay from the restored geometry exactly as Transform Reset does, clearing the aspect lock / flip (TransformPanel::resetCropState) when the restored state has no crop, else beginCropEdit re-inscribes the full frame to the old ratio. The Level field follows the restored straighten. In result preview (Transform eye on) there is no overlay to re-seed.

#### 11.36.8 Before / After

"\\" (Develop menu > Before / After) flips the loupe between BEFORE (the image with no develop edits, DevelopHistory::originalStack, the same state as History's "Original" row) and AFTER (the entry currently applied, which is just the stored stack). DevelopProperties::toggleBeforeAfter owns it; MW::toggleDevelopBeforeAfter is only the mode gate. It rides the SAME previewStack / previewActive override the hover uses, so the stored stack, the sliders and the history are never touched, and renderMatchesStoredRecipe keeps the Before frame out of the devPreview cache. Two things set it apart from a hover:

- It LATCHES. Before stays until the user presses "\\" again, EDITS (noteScopeEdit: an edit while comparing means the comparing is over, and the edit has to be what is on screen), NAVIGATES (setCurrentImage), or opens a MASK or SPOT tool (those take the canvas; toggleBeforeAfter likewise declines to go up while one is open, saying so). Every one of those routes through DevelopProperties::clearBeforeAfterLatch, so beforeAfterActive can never describe an override that is no longer up. The other preview sources (a Presets hover, a Profile-dropdown hover, a History hover) call it too, since they replace previewStack with their own.
- It renders the FULL path (emit paramsChanged: proxy now, crisp full-res on settle), not the hover's proxy-only path. A comparison the user holds on screen and zooms into has to be crisp on BOTH sides.

The state is reported through DevelopProperties::beforeAfterChanged(bool), which ticks the checkable developBeforeAfterAction (the latch comes down on routes the user did not press a key for, so the menu follows the signal). A popup names the side that just came up ("Before  (Original)" / "After"), and declines with a reason when Before and After are the same (pos == 0, nothing edited yet) or a tool owns the canvas.

#### 11.36.9 Files

Develop/History/develophistory.h (HistoryEntry + DevelopHistory, header-only, owned by DevelopProperties) and Develop/History/historyview.{h,cpp} (HistoryView, a QListWidget themed by WidgetCSS::listWidget, plus HistoryDelegate painting the action left and the value right). MW::createHistoryDock runs AFTER createDevelopDock (it binds to developProperties). Adding the dock required the full new-dock checklist ([2.5.3 Every Tabbable Dock Needs a Glyph](#253-every-tabbable-dock-needs-a-glyph)), including the history_white.png glyph and a winnowStateVersion bump.

### 11.37 Reset All Edits

"Reset all edits" wipes one image's recipe. It sits in the Edits bar's [:] menu directly under "New mask" (ScopeHeader::showScopeMenu -> resetAllEditsRequested, connected once in bindScopeHeader) and runs DevelopProperties::resetAllEdits.

- What it deletes: everything the EditStack holds, meaning every scope and its masks, the crop / straighten / warp geometry, and the spot heals. The stack is replaced with a fresh identity stack (one "Global" scope), not reset field by field, which is what makes the geometry and the spots go too.
- The whole selection: like a preset apply or a settings paste (and unlike Reset / Remove on a scope), it lands on every selected image: the current one, then each of otherSelectedPaths() (which skips videos). The per-image work lives in resetImageEdits(fPath); resetAllEdits adds only what the DOCK needs for the image on screen (mask-tool teardown, refreshScopeList + buildTree, spot pins, propagate base, paramsChanged) and the "Reset all edits on N images." popup. A multi-image batch already queued is flushed first (flushPropagation): its targets were captured when the batch opened and need not be the current selection, so it cannot just be dropped.
- History and sidecar (per image, resetImageEdits): the image's whole timeline goes, history->forget(path) then seed(path, identity), so the dock shows one fresh "Original", but only for an image that HAS a timeline (count > 0, visited this session); seeding an unvisited image would fill the LRU with images the user never opened. The sidecar is written IMMEDIATELY (dirty.insert + flushImage) rather than left to the debounce: an identity stack makes flushImage write an empty blob, which clears the winnow:Develop attribute (Metadata::writeDevelopSidecar will not create a sidecar just to store nothing), so the settings are gone even if the app never gets a clean shutdown.
- Confirmed, not undoable: history is wiped with the edits, so there is nothing to revert to. A QMessageBox with a destructive "Reset" button (Cancel default) asks first, naming the image or the number of selected images.
- Teardown, in applyHistoryEntry's order: retire a half-built mask tool (no commit prompt; the scope it would land in is being deleted), clear selectedMaskIndex, hide the mask panel, drop any hover preview, then rebuild under isRestoringHistory (so the repopulation records nothing), re-seed the propagate base and emit paramsChanged.

### 11.38 Adding or Changing a Develop Adjustment (Checklist)

A new slider, or a change to an existing one, is NOT a one-file edit: the value has to reach the pipeline, survive a round trip through the sidecar, repopulate the panel on the next image, and be capturable by a preset. Thirteen touch points, in dependency order. Working example: grainAmount (the Effects "Grain" slider); grep it to see every site at once.

1. Develop/editparams.h: THREE edits, not one.
   - The field + its identity default + a block comment giving meaning and range.
   - EditParams::resetGroup(): add it to its Group case. Miss this and the section Reset button and the Preview eye silently skip it.
   - EditParams::isIdentity(): add it ONLY if it is a primary control. Sub-modifiers (vignetteFeather, grainSize, grainRoughness, the tone splits) are deliberately left out: they are inert until their amount is non-zero, so counting them would make an untouched image non-identity and write a sidecar.
2. Develop/develop.h + develop.cpp: the op itself.
   - Tuning constants in the constexpr block at the top of develop.cpp.
   - The function, declared in develop.h and implemented in develop.cpp.
   - The call in Develop::Apply(), at the right place in the fixed pipeline order ([11.1.1 Operation Order](#1111-operation-order)). A POINT op costs nothing extra if folded into buildPointCoeffs / applyPointOps; a SPATIAL op owns its own pass.
   - parallelFor every per-pixel loop; downscale for large-radius blurs.
   - A LOCAL-CONTRAST op does NOT hand-roll its luma prep or fold-back: use buildPerceptualLuma + shapeAndFoldLuma (and gaussianBase if the radius is a fraction of the long edge), with the scalar maths in Develop/localcontrast.h. Adding one should be \~15 lines in develop.cpp; if it is more, it is duplicating something that already exists.
3. Develop/editstack.h: paramsToJson() AND paramsFromJson(). paramsFromJson is forward tolerant (an absent key keeps its default), so ADDING a field needs no version bump and old sidecars stay valid. Add the range clamp to EditStack::sanitizeParams() in the same pass: a field with no clamp line is one a hand-edited sidecar can feed to the pipeline unchecked. paramsToJson is ALSO the per-scope render cache's invalidation key (MW::developCompositeStack), so a field added to the pipeline but not here renders stale from cache AND never persists. Write a new key only when it is off its default, so existing recipe hashes do not change.
4. developproperties.cpp, the section's add&lt;Section>() (addBasic / addCurves / addColor / addPointColor / addCalibrate / addColorGrade / addDetail / addEffects / addLens): the addSlider call, with dock key, caption, tooltip, section header, min, max, divisor, colours and default. A sub-control of the slider above it uses a "   "-indented caption ("   Feather", "   Size").
5. developproperties.cpp, applyKeyToParams(): dock key -> EditParams field, applying the DIVISOR scaling (a 0..100 slider backing a 0..1 field writes f / 100.0f).
6. developproperties.cpp, populateSlidersFromStack(): the setSliderReal() call, the exact inverse of 5 (p.field \* 100.0). If 5 and 6 disagree, the value drifts a little further every time the user navigates away and back.
7-9. Presets: four functions, and NOTE THE KEY NAMESPACE CHANGE.
   - kBasicLeaves / kCurvesLeaves / kColorLeaves / kPointColorLeaves / kCalibrateLeaves / kColorGradeLeaves / kDetailLeaves / kEffectsLeaves in developproperties.cpp: the checklist row's key + label. Params the panel treats as one control fold into ONE leaf (Grain = amount + size + roughness).
   - leafChanged(): is this leaf non-default? Tests the PRIMARY param(s) only, matching isIdentity().
   - collectScopeLeaves(): writes the values under their EditStack JSON FIELD names (raw, unscaled), not the dock slider keys.
   - DevelopPresets::assignParam() in Develop/Presets/developpresets.cpp: the other half, JSON field name -> field, raw, NO divisor scaling. applyKeyToParams (dock keys, scaled) and assignParam (JSON names, raw) are the two key namespaces, and the easiest thing in Develop to get wrong.
   - If an absent key must not read back as 0 (a tri-state, a non-zero default), updatePresetFromCurrent must restore its default explicitly.
10. Multi-image editing: kFloatFields (or kIntFields) in the anonymous namespace above DevelopProperties::diffParamFields. ONE row: the EditParams field name and a pointer to the member. The diff and the copy both walk that table, so a field missing from it silently does NOT propagate to the rest of the selection while every other slider does: the worst kind of bug to notice. A NON-SCALAR field (the tone curve's arrays) cannot use a member pointer: give it a named pseudo-field plus a differs / copy pair beside the table, wired into diffParamFields AND copyParamFields (see curvesDiffer / copyCurves).
11. History: FREE for a normal slider (the generic tree-edit handler calls noteEdit with the caption and value, and noteEdit snapshots the whole EditStack). NOT free for a custom editor (the colour wheel, the WB row, the tone-region slider): those need their own noteEdit(action, value, mergeKey) call, and the mergeKey is what collapses a drag into one history row instead of forty.
12. This document: the op under [11.11 The Adjustments](#1111-the-adjustments) (and [11.1.1 Operation Order](#1111-operation-order) if it adds a stage), the slider in [11.11.4 The Panel Sections and Their Ranges](#11114-the-panel-sections-and-their-ranges), and any leaf folding under [11.33.5 The Save Dialog](#11335-the-save-dialog).
13. The in-app help: the section's page, Docs/develop&lt;section>help.html (e.g. developeffectshelp.html, which carries Vignette and Grain).

Preset keys are a published format: add freely, never rename or rescale in place ([11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)](#1139-stale-presets-and-history-schema-drift)).

#### 11.38.1 Changing an Existing Op's Math

A different job from adding a slider, and a riskier one: the ops shape recipes users have already saved, so a "harmless" rewrite silently re-renders their pictures. tests/unit/tst_localcontrast.cpp is the worked example: capture golden values from the CURRENT build FIRST, confirm they pass before touching anything, then refactor and require them still to pass. Mutation-check the gate too (a 0.1% change in any tuning constant should fail it); a characterisation test whose goldens match its own inputs proves nothing.

#### 11.38.2 A Whole New Section

A new section (rather than a slider in an existing one) adds a fixed set of bookkeeping on top of the thirteen, and every item fails SILENTLY if missed. Working examples: the Curves panel (grep PV_Curves) and the Detail panel (grep PV_Detail), which also shows what MOVING an existing control between sections costs (see [11.13.4 The Adjustment Tree](#11134-the-adjustment-tree)).

- DevelopProperties::PreviewGroup gains PV\_&lt;Name>, and hdrStar[] grows by one.
- paramsGroup() / groupLabel() / previewFlag(): three switches, plus a new EditParams::Group and its resetGroup() case.
- EditScope gains show&lt;Name>; effectiveScopeParams() folds it, EditStack::isIdentity tests it, and toJson / fromJson read + write its key.
- updateSectionHeaderCaptions()'s hdrs[] table (the " \*" edited marker), and GROW hdrStar[] with it: it is indexed by POSITION in hdrs[], so a new row with a too-short array walks off the end.
- buildTree(): the add&lt;Name>() call in pipeline order, the &lt;name>EyeBtn nulling, and the expand-state capture / restore pair; addHeader()'s eye-assignment chain; persistSectionExpanded()'s name list.
- refreshPreviewButtons and resetSection(PV_Scope) ("Reset all"); see [11.29.4 A New Section Must Join Every Per-Group Sweep](#11294-a-new-section-must-join-every-per-group-sweep).
- kSections gains the section's leaf table.
- sectionHelp()'s switch + a Docs/develop&lt;name>help.html page + its winnow.qrc entry.

#### 11.38.3 Maskable or Global-Only?

A per-scope adjustment belongs to a Group and is edited on whichever scope is active. A Global-only one (denoiseLuma / denoiseChroma, the tone splits, the lens corrections) belongs to NO Group (or to Group::Lens, shown only on Global), cannot be previewed or reset per mask scope, and must be read from scopes[0] in buildPreset() and written to scopes[0] in mergePreset() whatever scope is active.

### 11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)

What happens to a user's saved presets and their History when an adjustment is later renamed, rescaled or removed. The two behave quite differently.

#### 11.39.1 Presets Are the Exposure Point

They live in QSettings indefinitely, key by key, and are applied by assigning the stored value straight into an EditParams field. Three ways a key goes stale, in increasing order of harm:

- REMOVED key: harmless. read() returns it and mergePreset() hands it to assignParam(), an if / else-if chain with no final else, so an unknown key is silently ignored. The preset applies minus that one setting.
- RENAMED key: silent data loss. The same mechanism as removed: the user's preset quietly stops carrying that adjustment, with no warning and nothing in the UI to show it happened.
- RESCALED or REDEFINED key: silent CORRUPTION, the case that actually matters. assignParam writes the stored float straight into the field, so if a 0..1 field becomes 0..100 (or an EV becomes a percentage, or the op's maths is retuned), every old preset applies a wildly wrong value and reads to the user as broken.

THE RULE: treat a preset key as a published format. ADD keys freely (an absent key is a no-op both in a preset, where childKeys() reports only what was written, and in a sidecar, where paramsFromJson defaults it). NEVER rename or rescale one in place.

#### 11.39.2 The Migration Hook

For when a change is genuinely unavoidable. Every preset carries a schema stamp: DevelopPresets::write() stores `version = kVersion` at the preset root (beside sourceScope, so it never lands in the Global/Edits key sweeps), and read() calls migrate() before returning, i.e. before any value reaches assignParam. To change an existing key, bump kVersion and append ONE ordered step to migrate():

```
if (p.version < N) { ...rewrite the affected keys in p.params / p.globals...; }
```

so an old preset falls through every intervening step in turn. A preset stamped NEWER than kVersion (a downgraded build) is passed through untouched: assignParam already ignores keys it does not recognise, which degrades better than guessing backwards.

Presets written before the stamp existed have no version key and read back as 1, which is correct by definition (v1 is the schema they were written against), so the default in read() must stay 1 forever. They are NOT rewritten on startup: they get their stamp the next time that preset is saved or renamed, and until then behave identically. Sidecars have the same hook available via EditParams::version, which is persisted and round-tripped but not yet branched on.

Export presets have the same exposure and the same contract (Export/exportpresets.h): they live in QSettings indefinitely and are applied by assigning stored values into an ExportSettings, so add keys freely and never rename or rescale one in place. They are less fragile in one respect: read() starts from a default-constructed ExportSettings and overwrites field by field, so a key added after a preset was saved keeps its struct default instead of reading back as 0. When a key genuinely must change meaning, bump kVersion and convert in migrate(), which runs inside read() before any value reaches the struct.

#### 11.39.3 History Is No Longer Immune

Since 2026-09-30 history persists in index.db ([11.36.5 Persisted in the Local Index](#11365-persisted-in-the-local-index)), so a snapshot CAN be written by an older build. It is safe for the same reason a sidecar is: every snapshot is EditStack JSON read back through EditStack::fromJson, the sidecar's own forward-tolerant path, so a stale snapshot gets exactly the treatment a stale sidecar gets, and the "never rename or rescale in place" rule protects both. Two drifts remain, both cosmetic:

- An entry's action label is the slider caption FROZEN as a string at record time, so a renamed caption leaves older rows reading the old name, now across launches.
- A history whose stamp no longer matches the sidecar is set aside, never migrated.

#### 11.39.4 Retired Sidecar Key: "cameraProfileLook"

The camera-profile feature shipped for one day (2026-09-13) with a Look checkbox on the Profile row, storing 0 or 1 under that key. It was removed on 2026-09-14 in favour of applying a profile WHOLE and offering its bare characterisation as a separate "Camera Base" entry. paramsFromJson ignores the key, so an image edited during that day with the look switched OFF now renders WITH its look. Not migrated, deliberately: the key can only appear in that day's test images, and a migration would have to reach the profile store from the sidecar loader. The NAME must never be reused for anything else.

### 11.40 Corrupted or Changed Develop Settings

Develop state is read back from three stores the app does not fully control: the per-image XMP sidecar (a user file that a crash, a sync client or a hand edit can damage), the preset store in QSettings, and the general settings.ini. Forward tolerance handles values that are ABSENT. This section is about values that are PRESENT but wrong: unreadable, out of range, or naming something this build has no code for, like an unknown demosaic engine.

The old failure mode was uniform and silent: every read path fell back to a default without telling anyone. A corrupt sidecar came back as "this image has no edits" (indistinguishable from an untouched image), and the user's next edit overwrote what was still on disk.

#### 11.40.1 What Is Validated

- Sidecar: EditStack::fromBase64 returns a Status (Ok / Absent / Corrupt), so callers can tell "unedited" from "unreadable", plus a list of repairs. A stack stamped newer than EditStack::kVersion is reported.
- EditStack::sanitize / sanitizeParams range-check every value that reaches the render pipeline, against the SAME limits the panel sliders enforce, so a repaired value is always one the user could have dialled in. They reject NaN and infinity (one NaN turns the whole image black), order the three tone splits, repair a degenerate crop (a zero or negative width divides by zero downstream), and drop a warp whose quad did not survive (geometryFromJson only fills quad when the array is exactly 8 long, so a truncated one would otherwise warp through the DEFAULTS).
- Mask components whose tool or op is outside its enum are DROPPED, not rendered: both enums are append-only, so an out-of-range value is either corruption or a tool from a newer build, and neither has geometry this build can interpret. The bound is kLastMaskTool beside the enum, pinned by tests/unit/tst_masktools (see below for why).
- Presets are range-checked too, in mergePreset: their values come from QSettings as bare QVariants and reach EditParams through a plain toFloat().

The demosaic engine was the worst of the silent cases. G::DecodeRawEngine has two enumerators and three code paths tested against them, so a value that is NEITHER does not merely pick the wrong decoder: it fails every test. RawFormat skips the Apple branch AND the Winnow-only PMRID raw denoise, and the user gets un-denoised raws with no indication why. Three ways in, all now closed:

- settings.ini: MW::loadSettings cast the stored int straight to the enum; it is now range-checked before the cast.
- A preset: applyPreset tested `== "apple"` and treated everything else as Winnow; it now matches both tokens explicitly and warns on anything else.
- Cross-platform: the Apple engine is macOS-only and its branch is compiled out elsewhere, but MW's demosaicEngineChanged handler set it unconditionally, so a preset built on a Mac silently disabled raw denoise on Windows. Now clamped.

#### 11.40.2 When to Notify (and When Not To)

Notify when the user would otherwise discover the loss themselves: settings that could not be read, a mask that will not be drawn, values that had to be limited, a store written by a newer Winnow. Do NOT notify for the cases forward tolerance exists to absorb: an absent sidecar (the normal state of an unedited image) or an unknown KEY in an otherwise valid record.

Anti-spam is the hard part. Sidecars are read on EVERY image the user visits, so a damaged folder could fire one popup per file. DevelopProperties::warnOnce reports each KIND of problem at most once per session (warnedIssues holds the kinds already shown) while still logging every occurrence, and the message says other images may be affected. Startup settings use a second channel: MW::loadSettings runs long before G::newPopUp exists, so those messages queue in G::startupWarnings and MW::whenActivated shows them as ONE popup once the window is up.

#### 11.40.3 A Damaged or Repaired Sidecar Is Never Rewritten Behind the User

- A CORRUPT sidecar stays on disk: it may be recoverable, and a silent overwrite is the exact failure this path exists to prevent. It is replaced only when the user edits that image, an explicit act, and the popup says so.
- Nor is a REPAIRED one (2026-10-16). The two preview writers, DevelopProperties::topUpDevPreviews (on a Develop view) and MW's devPreview builder (background), rewrite the sidecar with developBlobFor, i.e. the IN-MEMORY stack, which is the SANITISED one, so any repair (a dropped mask, a clamped value, a newer-format stack's unknown settings) became permanent on a mere view. DevelopProperties::repairedStacks records paths whose load produced issues; sidecarRecipeRewritable(fPath) gates both writers' sidecar write (the loupe tier, cache-only, is still written); flushImage, a real edit, clears the flag.
- Found because the sanitize bound was a literal MaskTool::RefineBrush that was not moved when Segmenter was appended: every Segmenter mask was dropped on load (the "uses a tool this version does not have" popup), and a top-up then wrote the stripped stack over the sidecar. One image lost its mask; its develop_history row in index.db still held it.

#### 11.40.4 Winnow No Longer Creates One

Xmp::writeSidecar used to truncate the open handle with resize(0) and write the document in place, so a crash, a power loss or a full volume between the two left an empty or half-written sidecar, and the sidecar is the only copy of the develop recipe, the rating, the label, the title and the copyright. It is now a QSaveFile: a temporary is written and renamed over the original, so what is on disk is either the whole old document or the whole new one. It also treats a SHORT write as a failure (only a return of zero was tested before, so a partial write on a full disk was reported as success).

Develop previews are why this stopped being theoretical. The 256 px tier puts a base64 JPEG in the sidecar, roughly ten times the bytes the file used to carry, so the write window is ten times longer, and topUpDevPreviews rewrites sidecars for images the user merely VIEWED, so the window is entered far more often than an edit session would suggest. The caller's QFile is closed inside writeSidecar, because on Windows the rename fails while another handle to the target is open, and every caller opens the sidecar ReadWrite to construct the Xmp.

### 11.41 Investigations and Fixes

#### 11.41.1 A Stack Overflow on a Pool Thread

2026-10-11, fixed the same day. Developing the forest raw in-app died with SIGBUS / "Thread stack size exceeded" in \_\_\_chkstk_darwin under Develop::applyPointOps, on a QThreadPool thread (512 KB stack on macOS). PointCoeffs carries its tone tables inline (\~150 KB once the frame-relative Highlights tables were added), and it was (1) held BY VALUE in Develop::Apply, which nests (the frame's StatSample is developed through Apply first), and (2) COPIED into the fused pass's row lambda, which captures [=] and named c.hiBackLut[...]. Two Apply frames plus the lambda's copy exceeded the stack.

Fix: buildPointCoeffs returns std::shared_ptr&lt;const PointCoeffs> built on the heap, Apply holds a reference (and shares the sample's coefficients without a copy), and the row lambda reads plain table pointers (hiBackR/G/B), never c. Verified with -Wframe-larger-than=32768: no frame in develop.cpp or workingimagecache.cpp is over 32 KB (MW::updateDevelopScopes is 70 KB, on the GUI thread's 8 MB stack, untouched).

Why no test saw it: every unit test and developrender run Apply on the main thread's 8 MB stack. tst_toneregions::highlightsDevelopsOnAPoolThread now develops on the global pool; with the fix reverted it dies at the same instruction as the user's crash report.

RULE: Develop runs on 512 KB pool stacks. Never hold PointCoeffs by value, and never name a large struct inside a [=] lambda: hoist the fields or pointers first.

#### 11.41.2 Develop Render Latency (the Measurement Record)

The rules in [11.12 Develop Performance](#1112-develop-performance) came out of four rounds of measurement, each of which overturned a plan reasoned from the code.

##### 11.41.2.1 Slider Drag (2026-06)

The naive path re-rendered the full image synchronously on the GUI thread every tick: \~520 ms/tick for a 50 MP raw, dominated by OutputTransform::ToImage (\~420 ms), the only serial stage. Fixes: the proxy, a parallel ToImage, coalesce + settle. [DevTime] then showed proxy ticks \~45 ms (render 25 / rotate+scale 18 / preview 2), but interleaved `full 8640x5760 render 1300-1440 ms`: the settle ran synchronously and froze the drag, and the freeze drained queued slider events in bursts whose gaps re-fired the settle timer, so the 1.3 s render ran REPEATEDLY mid-drag. Fix: renderDevelopFullResAsync.

With texture/dehaze left non-zero the async settle was still \~1.45 s: point 64 / texture 899 / dehaze 399 ms. The per-pixel loops in Develop::Denoise / Texture / Dehaze were single-threaded (now parallelFor, bit-identical), and Texture's large-sigma cv::GaussianBlur dominated what remained (now a downscaled base). Net \~1.45 s -> \~360 ms (texture 899 -> 72, dehaze 399 -> 120) on an M4.

##### 11.41.2.2 Mask Drag (2026-08)

With masked scopes the proxy tick still did all of the work every time: paramsChanged fanned out to developParamsChange (coalesced) AND updateMaskOverlayTint (NOT coalesced, one or two full buildMaskBuffer passes at a 1600 px cap on every mouse-move); developCompositeStack re-rasterised EVERY scope's mask and renderStack redid the base and every scope even when one mask had moved; and Linear/Radial handle drags emitted on every mouse-move while brush strokes went through a 10 Hz throttle. Fixed by the coalesced veil, the shared throttle, and the per-scope mask and layer cache.

Then the dominant cost, found by the probe: with the develop stages down to \~3 ms, a brush drag on a 2 MP mask still measured `mask 900 ms` per tick and `tint` the same again.

1. Dab spacing: BrushStamp::segmentMax computed its spacing PER SEGMENT (n = max(1, len/step)), so ANY mouse-move, even 3 px, stamped two full-radius dab boxes (\~105k pixel evaluations each at a 20% brush), and the render replays every dab of the stroke every tick, so cost grew with the number of mouse EVENTS. Fixed with the carried residual. It bought only \~1.4x, because a fast drag already delivers events roughly a step apart.
2. Dab area: a dab box is (2\*radius)^2, so a large brush touches most of the image per dab, and dabMax was single-threaded. Now row-parallel with squared-distance tests.
3. Splitting the mask number into raster / setup / fold settled it: on a scope with 21 submasks a tick read raster 275 / setup 308 / fold 51, and 185 dabs = 4 Mpx against a 700 ms build. The cost was PER COMPONENT: all \~19 brush submasks re-rasterised every tick, each re-parsing its JSON and allocating + zeroing its own w\*h\*4 buffer, because g_brushCache cleared itself past eight entries. Now a byte-budgeted LRU.
4. The veil built at its own 1600 px cap, missing every cache entry the render had just filled. It now builds at the proxy's dimensions.
5. What was left (setup 22 ms, mostly signature hashing twice per tick plus the 8 MB prefix copy) went with the prefix-fold cache.

Lesson: three fixes were aimed at this before the split existed (dab spacing, dab parallelism, the scope layer cache), all reasoned from the code, and only the first was even a real bug. Sub-timings and COUNTS (dabs, components, strokes) found it. Split a number before optimising anything behind it.

Veil gating (2026-08): (a) maskTintHidden lived entirely in ImageView and was read only by drawForeground, so pressing "O" hid the veil while MW kept compositing it at full proxy resolution every tick (\~87 ms for something nothing drew). MW::updateMaskOverlayTint now asks ImageView::maskTintVisible() first; the stored QImage is left in place and maskTintVisibilityChanged rebuilds on the way back up, so re-showing cannot flash a stale overlay. (b) It mattered beyond the veil: with veil \~87 + render \~47 ms against a 100 ms live-emit throttle, the GUI thread was over 100% occupied, mouse-moves queued, and the brush CURSOR RING (painted by ImageView on the GUI thread) visibly lagged. A saturation problem, not a hot loop; the structural fix was moving the proxy render off the GUI thread.

##### 11.41.2.3 Adjustment Drag (2026-08)

Dragging a slider was slow even with NO edits and NO masks, and the cause was not pixel maths: 87 ms of a 121 ms tick was releasing memory (the tell: `copy 2` next to `free 29`). Fixes, each exposing the next allocation down:

1. Buffer reuse (assignReusing + DevelopStackCache scratch): 121 -> 35 ms.
2. Showing superseded frames (`applied 0` on 6 of 7 ticks was the lag itself).
3. The transfer LUT: toImage had become \~90% of the tick (35 of 38 ms).
4. Scopes sampling in place: newly urgent once every frame was shown.
5. The cache wiped under the worker: developStackCache.reset() ran BEFORE the developProxyInFlight early-return, so every mouse-move arriving mid-render (one per \~8 ms against a \~120 ms render) wiped the per-scope masks out from under the worker and returned, and no mask ever survived. The symptom was contradictory on purpose: [DevTime] said `cacheKept` while `maskScopes 1` rebuilt the mask anyway, and the orphaned buffer's last reference died in the compositor (all COMPOSEOTHER ever was). Fixed by moving the in-flight check above the reset.
6. Base params no longer invalidating masks: a Global drag changes the base signature every render, which was part of reset()'s key, so every mask still died every tick, for a dependency only the range tools have.
7. Prefix snapshot scratch: with the mask cached, setHot was 62 ms of a 108 ms tick, a fresh snapshot per tick whose predecessor setHot released.

The settle render had the same disease at full size: a 9600x6376 file with 2 mask scopes took 5,207 ms, of which free 1,735 + outFree 572 = 2,307 ms (44%) was releasing memory, because layLocal was declared INSIDE the scope loop. Hoisted out. WARNING: an ISOLATED benchmark frees the same 735 MB in \~0 ms and says there is nothing here. The cost is memory PRESSURE, not size: it appears only with the image cache, the source image and the 245 MB mask buffers all resident, and a micro-benchmark nearly argued the fix away.

Lesson: the plan going in was to bound the develop pass and the blend to the mask's BOUNDING BOX, worked out down to the guard list. Measured, those two stages were 1 ms and 7 ms; the design would have saved 8 ms of 121 while the allocator ate 87.

##### 11.41.2.4 A Stale Fold-Cache Slot

Found by the TSan driver on its first run, a real crash. buildMaskBuffer picked foldSlot while holding g_maskFoldMutex during the LOOKUP, then re-acquired the mutex to store. Between the two the cache could be cleared (maskFoldCacheClear() from the GUI thread's ensureRangeRef, the key cap, or another render), leaving entries[] shorter than foldSlot: QVector::operator[] out of range, a SEGV. foldSlot is now a HINT, re-validated against the vector under the store lock. An index chosen under one lock acquisition means nothing under the next.

## 12 Previews

### 12.1 Original and Developed Previews

Two pictures, two words. Every image Winnow shows has an origPreview (the camera's embedded JPEG, or the plain decode of a JPG / TIFF / PNG: the picture as shot) and, once it has been developed, a devPreview: the render of its develop recipe. The original Winnow design predates the Develop module and had only one word, "preview", for both; once developed thumbnails started appearing in the icon grid, the two began to disagree in a way the user could see. The code now says which one it means: devPreview / DevPreviewCache / loadDevThumb for the developed picture, origPreview (G::WidthOrigPreviewColumn, ImageMetadata::widthOrigPreview) for the camera's. Not everything called "preview" is either of these: previewActive is a History hover, previewShown is a section eye, maskRangePreview is a tool overlay, renderDevelopPreview is the live interactive render, and those keep their names.

The on-disk names do NOT change. The XMP attributes winnow:Develop, winnow:DevelopPreview and winnow:DevelopPreviewKey (Metadata/xmp.cpp) and the devPreview index's column names are a published format: sidecars written by shipped builds must keep loading. The two TableView header strings "WidthPreview" / "HeightPreview" stay too: column visibility is persisted in QSettings under the header string, so renaming them would silently reset the user's show / hide choice.

Why any of this exists: the develop recipe lives in each image's sidecar and had no visual counterpart anywhere. The icon grid showed the camera's JPG, so a developed image looked exactly like an untouched one, and entering Develop on a raw spent 2-3 seconds displaying the UNDEVELOPED picture while the scene-linear decode ran. devPreviews close both gaps, and they travel with the image (tier 1 is in the sidecar) rather than depending on the catalog.

### 12.2 Which Picture Is Shown

#### 12.2.1 Three Pictures, Two Controls

Every image has up to three pictures, and the UI uses one word for each:

- Developed: the render of its develop recipe (a devPreview, or Develop's live render). An unedited raw Winnow can demosaic may also have one, its DEFAULT RENDER (identity recipe), which is still Winnow's rendering and so reads Developed.
- Original: the file with no edits: Winnow's neutral raw render (Develop's Before), or the JPG / TIFF / PNG itself.
- Camera: the camera's embedded JPEG. Raws only; for any other file it IS the Original. The user-facing word was "Preview" until 2026-10-18; it collided with Preview mode and with devPreview, so the status bar now says Camera. Code names (G::PreviewSource, togglePreviewSourceAction) are unchanged.

Browse never decodes a raw (that is the point of Preview mode), so the unedited picture of a raw in Browse is the Camera picture, and the label says so rather than calling it Original.

Which picture is shown is decided by TWO CONTROLS WITH TWO SCOPES, never mixed:

- Y, View > Show Edits (All Images) (togglePreviewSourceAction, checkable): a persistent lens over the whole collection, every thumbnail and the loupe, in every workflow except Develop. It sets G::previewSource (persisted) through MW::setPreviewSource, which rebuilds the icons and the image cache ([12.2.4 Changing It Rebuilds Both Caches](#1224-changing-it-rebuilds-both-caches)), so it is a deliberate switch. Default: edits shown. It pops "Edits shown for all images" / "Edits hidden for all images", naming the scope as well as the state.
- "\\", View > Compare Original / Developed (browseCompareAction, MW::toggleBrowseCompare): the CURRENT image only, in the loupe only, never persisted. See [12.2.5 The Browse Compare](#1225-the-browse-compare).

Why the scope of Show Edits is ALL images and not the current image, the selection or the visible rows: it is a way of looking at the collection, not a property of an image. Per-row state would produce a grid mixing developed and unedited thumbnails that nobody can explain afterwards, would need its own persistence, and "visible" changes under the user on every scroll. The per-image question ("what did this one look like before?") is the compare, which is momentary and so needs no state.

"\\" was Show image count until 2026-10-12, then the Original / Developed toggle (sharing it with Y). Since 2026-10-18 it is the per-image compare in every mode: the Browse compare outside Develop, Before / After in Develop (the arbiter's table claims it there). Y alone is the all-images switch, so the cheap action and the expensive one are on different keys. The radio pair View > Show Original / Show Developed was removed with that change.

THE PICTURE CHIP (MW::pictureChip, a QToolButton at the left end of the status bar, built in MW::createStatusBar) names the picture of the current image on the loupe AND is its control, so the state and its options are in one place. Its menu (filled in MW::createMenus, after the actions exist) holds the SAME QActions as View: Show Edits (All Images), Compare Original / Developed, Compare Camera / Developed, then "About Developed, Original and Camera...". One QAction each means the chip, the menu and the keys can never disagree. MW::syncPictureChip sets its text (MW::getPictureShown plus a menu glyph), tooltip and a chipState property that WidgetCSS styles (QToolButton#pictureChip):

- normal: a quiet outline, the picture's word.
- compare: an Apple-blue outline, the compared picture's word; momentary.
- hidden: amber (the has-edits badge colour), "<picture> · edits hidden". The exception-only indicator: a switch flipped yesterday cannot silently persist.

It is hidden when there is no picture to name (no image, a video). updateStatus calls syncPictureChip on every status refresh, and syncPreviewSourceEnabled calls it on mode and Show Edits changes. In Develop the items stay in the menu with the reason in their TEXT ("Show Edits (not in Develop)"; "\\" reads "Before / After"), since a greyed menu item gives no other hint why.

It replaced two earlier controls: the "Picked: ## Developed" word at the end of the status text, and the status-bar Original / Developed dropdown (previewSourceCombo, built hidden since the Module dock arrived), which only offered a choice, not the state, the second scope or the help. A separate "Edits hidden" pill existed briefly; it was folded into the chip's amber state.

The help page is Docs/pictureshelp.html (qrc), opened by MW::helpPictures in an HtmlWindow like the other tips pages. It is reachable from the chip menu, View and Help.

Develop mode is deliberately NOT an item in it. It was, briefly, on the reasoning that Original and Developed are both Preview mode. That is true of the plumbing and false of the control: Develop is an editing MODE, a different kind of thing from a choice of picture, and as a third peer item it read as one of three pictures. It is also redundant (D enters Develop, and E / G / T leave it).

What each workflow shows:

- Browse (Library / Folders): loupe and thumbnails show Developed when a devPreview exists and edits are shown, otherwise Camera (raw) / Original. "\\" and Opt+"\\" both compare the current image.
- Develop: the live Developed render, thumbnails forced to Developed. "\\" is Before / After, Opt+"\\" the camera latch. Y is disabled with a reason.
- Keywords: follows the Browse setting and keys.
- Embellish: renders from the developed image; the Show Edits setting still governs the thumbnails.

#### 12.2.2 The Choice Does Not Exist in Develop

Develop shows the developed image in the loupe (a live render of the recipe being edited), and the thumbnails must agree with it, so offering Original would let the user ask for a picture Develop cannot show.

- MW::syncPreviewSourceEnabled greys the combo (which then reads Developed) and disables the two menu items with a reason; a disabled QAction greys its menu item AND stops its shortcut firing, so one gate covers the menu and the key, and the reason surfaces through [7.2 Disabled Shortcut Feedback](#72-disabled-shortcut-feedback).
- G::previewSource ITSELF is not changed by the mode: entering Develop must not silently rewrite a Preview-mode preference the user gets back the moment they leave. syncPreviewSourceEnabled is called by both setOperationMode and setPreviewSource, so the control can never drift from the pair (mode, previewSource).
- Y does nothing in Develop: the action is disabled there (the reason surfaces through Disabled Shortcut Feedback). Y is deliberately NOT in developShortcuts; the arbiter passes it to the global QAction ([7.5 Develop Mode Local Shortcuts](#75-develop-mode-local-shortcuts)).
- Both read paths test the mode first (Thumb::loadDevThumb and ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview): Develop always shows Developed, whatever G::previewSource says.

The effective thumbnail source is the PAIR, not the setting:

```
(G::operationMode == Develop) ? Developed : G::previewSource
```

which is exactly the test Thumb::loadDevThumb makes. So a MODE change moves it too, and MW::refreshDevelopThumbs runs on entering AND leaving Develop, not only on setPreviewSource; otherwise entering Develop with Original chosen leaves the camera thumbnails on screen while the loupe shows the developed image. setOperationMode skips the re-read when Developed is chosen (the effective source is Developed in both modes), which matters, since Developed is the default and every D press would otherwise re-read every developed thumbnail.

#### 12.2.3 Camera Preview / Developed

Opt/Alt + "\\" (toggleCameraPreviewAction, View and Develop menus): the camera's own picture vs the developed one, available in every mode and never disabled. MW::toggleCameraPreview dispatches on the mode:

- Outside Develop it is the Browse compare (MW::toggleBrowseCompare): Preview mode never decodes a raw, so the unedited picture already IS the camera's embedded preview and the two keys agree.
- In Develop it is MW::toggleDevelopCameraPreview, a LATCH. Pixmap::load reads the embedded JPEG of a raw (the file itself otherwise, oriented and colour managed as Preview shows it), and it goes on the loupe with an identity geometry, sized to the frame's oriented width at the camera's aspect so the zoom survives. While developCameraShown is set for developCameraPath, both render completions (the proxy hand-off in renderDevelopPreview and onDevelopFullResReady) still retain their frame but leave the loupe alone, so a settle render in flight cannot paint over it.
- ANY NEW RENDER REQUEST takes it down: clearDevelopCameraPreview runs at the top of renderDevelopPreview, so an edit, a History step, navigation or a tool all return to the develop, and setOperationMode clears it too. Pressing it again re-renders via developParamsChange. It is declined (popup) while a mask, spot or Transform tool owns the canvas, as Before / After is. If Before is latched it is taken down first and the queued After proxy render is stopped (it would clear the camera latch the moment it ran).

The picture chip names the picture with MW::getPictureShown: "Camera" (the camera's embedded preview: a raw browsed with edits hidden or compared, or the Develop camera latch), "Original" (a non-raw browsed with edits hidden or compared, or Develop's Before) or "Developed" (Develop's render, or a browsed image that has a devPreview while edits are shown; one without reads Camera / Original). A Browse compare reports its own label (ImageView::compareLabel). setPreviewSource, setOperationMode, the compare, the camera latch (set and clear) and DevelopProperties::beforeAfterChanged each call updateStatus, which calls syncPictureChip, so the word follows.

#### 12.2.4 Changing It Rebuilds Both Caches

That is why it is a deliberate user action rather than something that fires on selection. MW::setPreviewSource is modelled on toggleUseRaw: the setting changes what a CACHED DECODE MEANS, so a repaint is not enough.

- The icons (MW::refreshDevelopThumbs), because the developed thumbnail OVERWRITES the row's icon (DataModel::setDevelopIcon); the camera thumb is not kept alongside it, so getting it back means re-reading it. The rows that carry a devPreview key are cleared, both delegates' per-row pixmap caches are dropped, and reloadIconChunk re-dispatches MetaRead, which loads the visible rows first. Rows with no devPreview key are left alone: they have one picture.
- Clearing an icon is NOT enough to get it re-read. MetaRead remembers every row a reader has returned for the current folder (readSuccessThisCycle) and needToRead short-circuits on it. It re-arms rows whose icon is missing only when the icon chunk is a WINDOW (G::useJitIconCache); in the default mode it assumes a loaded icon stays loaded. MW::setPreviewSource and MW::devPreviewUpdated therefore call MetaRead::invalidateLoadedIcons (queued, ahead of reloadIconChunk's own queued call), which makes the next setStartRow re-arm once. Symptom when this is missed: the thumbnails clear and never come back. See [5.6 Icon Loading Rules](#56-icon-loading-rules).
- The full-size image cache, because ImageDecoder consults the flag to decide whether to serve the devPreview or decode the file.

Only images that HAVE a devPreview change appearance; the rest re-read to the same pixels. That is the price of not keeping two icons per row in memory for a folder of thousands.

The amber "has edits" badge is driven by the RECIPE (G::DevelopColumn), never by whether a preview exists, so an edited image whose preview could not be rendered still reads as edited, and so does one shown as Original.

#### 12.2.5 The Browse Compare

"\\" outside Develop (MW::toggleBrowseCompare) puts the current image's OTHER picture on the loupe, and a second press takes it down:

- Loupe shows Developed: the compare is Camera (raw) or Original (anything else), read with Pixmap::load, oriented and colour managed exactly as Preview mode shows it.
- Loupe shows the unedited picture: the compare is the devPreview, read straight from DevPreviewCache and colour managed as sRGB (an empty profile), the way ImageDecoder::colorManage treats a served devPreview.

"Developed" means a devPreview EXISTS under the row's current key, the same lookup ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview makes; the key is built by the shared ImageDecoder::devPreviewKeyFor, so the two cannot drift. An edited image with no devPreview yet says so (open it in Develop, or Build Developed Previews) rather than decoding a raw.

It rebuilds nothing. ImageView::showCompare keeps the displayed pixmap, swaps in the other picture through setDevelopPreview at the WIDTH of the picture it replaces (in its own aspect, so a small embedded JPEG does not refit the loupe and lose the zoom), and ImageView::endCompare puts the kept pixmap back. Any real load (ImageView::loadImage, loadImageInterim) drops the compare, since those pixels supersede it: that is how navigation ends it. MW::endBrowseCompare is also called on a view change (grid, table, compare), a mode change and a Show Edits change.

In grid or table "\\" explains that compare works in the loupe and that Y switches all images.

### 12.3 The Two Tiers

- TIER 1, THE THUMBNAIL (256 px, matching G::maxIconSize), lives IN THE XMP SIDECAR as winnow:DevelopPreview, base64, roughly 15-20 KB. It is in the sidecar so it travels with the image: a move, a rename, a copy to the other machine all carry it for free, and Winnow already trashes the sidecar with the file. It needs no cache, no index and no orphan handling.
- TIER 2, THE devPreview, lives in AppDataLocation/PreviewCache as &lt;id>.jpg, indexed by the devpreview table in index.db beside it (Cache/devpreviewcache.h, Cache/cachedb.h). It is out of band because several MB per image in every sidecar is not a trade worth making, and because losing it costs only a re-render.

#### 12.3.1 Size and Quality

Full sensor resolution is the default, and it is what makes the devPreview more than a placeholder: at full size the loupe can show AND ZOOM the developed picture with no raw decode at all. The cost is real (an entry is several MB rather than a few hundred KB), so it is a preference (G::devPreviewMaxEdge: Full / 4096 / 2560, "Developed preview size") beside a cache limit that defaults to 20 GB. The LRU byte cap is load-bearing.

"Developed preview quality" (G::devPreviewQuality) is the JPEG quality the devPreview tier is written at, TYPED AS A NUMBER from 40 to 100, default 90. A number rather than a few named steps because there is no quality a preview is too poor to be worth offering: this is a cache of pictures to look at, not masters, and q50 looks fine on plenty of material. The floor of 40 is where JPEG starts showing blocking on smooth tone at any zoom; a stored value outside 40-100 is treated as damaged and ignored (Main/settings.cpp), not clamped.

- One non-linearity at the top of the range: Qt's JPEG handler disables chroma subsampling only ABOVE 90 (qjpeghandler.cpp), so 91 writes 4:4:4 and roughly doubles the file over 90, the best quality that still subsamples 4:2:0. The jump in size between 90 and 91 is far larger than the jump in appearance.
- The thumbnail tier is NOT covered and stays at a fixed 85. Measured on a 61 MP source, dropping it from 85 to 50 saves 13 KB per image (0.12% of what that image's full-res devPreview costs, and it comes out of sidecars, not the capped cache). The quality side is asymmetric: a full-res preview is almost always viewed DOWNSCALED (61 MP into a screen is a 4-8x reduction, which averages JPEG artifacts away), which is why q50 is sound there, while a 256 px thumbnail is viewed at \~1:1, where an 8x8 JPEG block is \~3% of the icon's width.
- Neither setting rewrites what is already cached: the staleness test is the recipe hash, not the dimensions or the encoding, so only NEW previews are written the new way. Develop > Clear Developed Preview Cache is the immediate route.
- A devPreview and an export at the same quality are the same encode: QImage::save(&buf, "JPG", q) and ImageExporter's QImageWriter::setQuality(q) both reach Qt's one JPEG handler, neither sets optimize or progressive. What still differs is upstream: an export can render 16-bit, can target Adobe RGB or Display P3 where a devPreview is always sRGB, sizes by its own rules, and can carry copied EXIF. At 8-bit sRGB, full size, no metadata copy, the compressed pixels match.

### 12.4 Writing Previews From the Render

#### 12.4.1 The Pixels Are Free for the Image on Screen

Full size does not mean a new render: MW::onDevelopFullResReady already produces a crisp full-resolution frame for the loupe (the settle render, \~1.3 s on a 50 MP raw) and RETAINS it as developFullFrame. The provider prefers it and falls back to developFrame, the screen-resolution proxy, when the settle render has not landed. Either way a preview is a scale plus a JPEG encode off a buffer that existed anyway.

It writes BOTH tiers and gates on both. The thumbnail and the devPreview must never come from different recipes (a grid showing one picture while the loupe shows another is worse than neither), so if EITHER tier is missing or stale, both are rewritten. Accepted consequence: visiting an edited image in Develop can rewrite its sidecar. Only the preview attributes and modifydate move; the recipe is passed through unchanged (but see [11.40.3 A Damaged or Repaired Sidecar Is Never Rewritten Behind the User](#11403-a-damaged-or-repaired-sidecar-is-never-rewritten-behind-the-user)).

#### 12.4.2 Only a Faithful Frame May Be Cached

stackJob() applies view overrides that make the rendered frame diverge from the STORED recipe: a hovered History row (previewActive) renders a different stack entirely; the Transform preview eye off bypasses geometry, so the frame is uncropped and unstraightened; the Replace eye off bypasses the heals; and in the full-res path an interactive crop drag suppresses the crop, making the frame the wrong SHAPE. Caching any of those against the stored recipe's hash would key a preview to a picture it does not depict.
