DevelopProperties::renderMatchesStoredRecipe answers this; both render paths capture it WITH the job (the eyes can change while a render is in flight), and the provider declines when it is false.

#### 12.4.3 And Only a Current One

Faithful says the frame depicts the STORED recipe; it does not say WHICH stored recipe. A retained frame is replaced only when a render completes and is still current, never by the edit itself, so after an edit inside the settle window (leave Develop, switch image or quit within \~1.5 s of the last change) the frame on hand is the PREVIOUS recipe's, with the same path and the same faithful flag. Writing it out is worse than writing nothing: it stamps old pixels with the new recipe's hash, and since that hash is what every staleness check compares, the wrong picture then looks correct forever. Both render paths therefore capture developRecipeKey(fPath) WITH the job (developFrameRecipe / developFullFrameRecipe), and the provider declines unless it equals the recipe being flushed. The hash is computed only for a faithful render, so an unfaithful tick pays nothing.

Geometry edits arm the settle render too. Crop, warp, level and the mask tools re-render through renderDevelopPreview WITHOUT going through developParamsChange, so nothing used to re-run the full-resolution render for them: developFullFrame stayed at the pre-crop recipe forever. A faithful proxy render now (re)arms developFullResTimer itself, which is also why developParamsGen cannot stand in for the recipe hash: those callers change the recipe without bumping it.

#### 12.4.4 The Proxy May Not Serve the devPreview Tier

Only the full-res frame (or a proxy that already meets a finite size cap) may. The interactive proxy is sized to the VIEW (\~1600 px), so an image flushed before its settle render landed was cached at proxy size, and the loupe then showed a visibly soft picture where the preference said "Full size". It looked current forever, since staleness is keyed on the RECIPE HASH, which says nothing about resolution. It was the common case: any edit inside the settle window failed the full-frame test and fell through to the proxy. The provider now DECLINES the devPreview tier there (the 256 px thumbnail tier still takes the proxy); flushImage drops any older entry, the loupe decodes the raw, and the image is queued into the builder for a proper preview shortly after.

To check a suspect preview: the Develop diagnostics' CURRENT IMAGE section names this image's cache payload and reports its pixel size beside the sensor's, flagging one far smaller. DevPreviewCache::payloadPath is the lookup behind it (the mapping only, with no recipe hash and no LRU touch, because payloads are named by index row id in hex, "537.jpg"). A winnow:DevelopPreviewFileName sidecar attribute was prototyped and DROPPED: the cache and the sidecar have independent lifetimes, so an eviction or a cleared cache silently falsifies the name. Failing that, the cache files are plain JPEGs, so `sips -g pixelWidth` says the same thing.

#### 12.4.5 Neither May the Embedded Preview

The builder's version of the same failure (2026-08-30, finally closed 2026-10-06). The builder renders through MW::developPixelSource, and whenever it swept while the user was in Preview mode the raw demosaic was skipped and developPixelSource fell through to a WorkingImage built from the 8-bit EMBEDDED PREVIEW (1024x683 for an Adobe DNG's SubIFD1), stored as the "full resolution" preview. The fix is that every independent caller decodes the sensor in any mode ([14.2.2 Every Caller Gets the Sensor Image, in Any Mode](#1422-every-caller-gets-the-sensor-image-in-any-mode)), and developPixelSource refuses a cached base that is not sceneReferred (WorkingImageCache is keyed by path alone, and Preview mode fills it from that same embedded JPEG).

- Symptom to recognise: a preview whose pixel width equals the file's embedded preview width (exiftool -a -G1 -s -ImageWidth lists every IFD).
- Existing bad entries are NOT self-healing (staleness is the recipe hash): Develop > Clear Developed Preview Cache forces a rebuild.

#### 12.4.6 A Decline Queues a Build

Declining makes flushImage DROP the old devPreview, so if nothing replaced it the image would show undeveloped outside Develop for good (ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview misses and the file is decoded as shot). The provider therefore queues the builder (buildDevPreviews, src "flush") whenever it has no faithful, current frame, not only when the proxy is too small. The case that exposed it: pressing E with the crop tool open. The Transform session commits the crop and re-renders asynchronously, but every frame on hand was rendered with the crop suppressed, so the flush declined and a version came back to Browse uncropped. When the build lands for the image ON SCREEN outside Develop (Developed preview source), devPreviewStore re-caches it (removeCachedImage + setImageCachePosition), so the loupe swaps to the developed preview immediately. A decode of that image still IN FLIGHT at that moment is superseded: removeCachedImage marks the key (supersededDecodes) and okToCache discards the result and re-queues the row, otherwise the stale decode (a large TIFF takes seconds) lands after the swap and the loupe shows the previous crop. The flush that asks for the build usually runs while still IN Develop (the crop commit flushes before the mode changes), so startDevPreviewBuild defers it and setOperationMode builds it on the way out; see 12.9.4.

#### 12.4.7 Visiting Writes Previews Too

- A byproduct of rendering, not only of editing: flushImage runs only for DIRTY images, so an image whose recipe came from an earlier session and which the user merely VISITS never reaches it. DevelopProperties::topUpDevPreviews closes that gap: on leaving an image, leaving Develop or quitting, if a faithful frame exists and no preview matches the recipe in force, it caches one. The frame was rendered anyway, so this never causes a decode or a render.
- Re-entry is free: flushAll runs before EVERY file operation (FileOps::flushPendingEdits), so a multi-image paste or ingest would call topUpDevPreviews once per file. It remembers the last (path, recipe) it brought up to date and returns immediately for a repeat.
- Cleared, not left behind: when flushImage cannot obtain a preview for a new recipe it CLEARS both tiers. A preview that no longer matches its recipe would show a picture the user has already changed; the camera thumbnail is at least honest.

### 12.5 Staleness Keys

Every preview is stamped with a 12-char hash of the develop blob it was rendered from, PLUS the two renderer facts that change the pixels without touching the recipe: the raw engine and G::autoRunDenoise (Metadata::devPreviewKey). They are in the key for the same reason defaultRenderKey hashes them: on the recipe alone, toggling either left every EDITED image serving pixels built under the old setting while the unedited half of the folder correctly re-rendered. Auto run matters even to a recipe that pins denoiseRaw, because unset means "follow the preference"; hashing it unconditionally costs one extra rebuild for images that pinned it and never shows the wrong picture.

Tier 1 stores the key as winnow:DevelopPreviewKey beside the pixels, written in the SAME sidecar pass as the recipe, so the three can never disagree; tier 2 keeps it in the index. A reader serves a preview only when the key matches the recipe in force, so an edit made by another Winnow instance, another machine or another application can never show stale pixels: it just misses and falls back.

#### 12.5.1 Decoder Fixes: Per-Format Revision

ImageFormats/Raw/decoderrevision.h. Neither the recipe nor the renderer facts change when a sensor decoder is FIXED, so the previews it rendered kept being served. Found 2026-10-10: the CR2/CR3 black level averaged lit border columns (7D Mark II black 2130 vs 2047), turning images green; after the fix the Develop render was right but the browse thumbnail and loupe still showed the green pixels.

- RawDecoder::revision(ext) is a per-format number, folded in by Metadata::renderKey(baseKey, fPath) (via devPreviewKey(blob, fPath) and defaultRenderKey(fPath)) at every point that READS OR WRITES a cached preview: the sidecar thumbnail and its winnow:DevelopPreviewKey, a version's previewKey, and DevPreviewCache get / put.
- Bump a format's number when a decoder change alters its pixels; only that format's previews miss and rebuild. Revision 0 is the identity, so a never-bumped format keeps its keys exactly.
- The one-argument devPreviewKey(blob) remains the BASE key, and that is what G::DevPreviewKeyColumn, the catalog and VersionSummary hold: those outlive a build (rows restored from the catalog without a sidecar re-read), so a revision baked in there would keep the old key alive. ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview applies renderKey to the column value at lookup time.

#### 12.5.2 Denoiser Fixes: kDenoiserRevision

RawDecoder::kDenoiserRevision (same header). PMRID changes the pixels without touching the recipe or the decoder, so a denoiser fix left its old previews in place. Found 2026-10-16: after the LX3 blind-noise-estimate fix the Develop render was right but the grid thumbnail stayed magenta.

- Metadata::denoiserKeyPart appends "|denoiser=N" inside the BASE key hash (devPreviewKey(blob) and defaultRenderKey) only when the render runs PMRID: the Winnow engine AND EditParams::wantsDenoiseRaw (G::autoRunDenoise, or the recipe's denoiseRaw = 1, probed by substring before parsing). Apple-engine and un-denoised previews keep their keys.
- Bump it when a PMRID change alters output. With Auto run on, that misses every Winnow-engine raw preview once, rebuilt as each image is viewed (the stale sidecar thumbnail falls back to the camera thumbnail in the grid until topUpDevPreviews rewrites it on the next Develop view).
- Unlike the decoder revision it IS in the base key (it depends on the recipe, which renderKey does not see), so it lands in G::DevPreviewKeyColumn and the catalog. Consequence: a row restored from the catalog WITHOUT a sidecar re-read keeps the pre-bump base key and can go on serving the old loupe preview until the image is viewed in Develop (topUpDevPreviews -> MW::devPreviewUpdated rewrites the column) or its sidecar is re-read. The autoDenoise / engine parts of the base key share that limitation.

### 12.6 Read Paths

#### 12.6.1 The Icon Grid

Thumb::loadDevThumb runs FIRST in loadThumb, ahead of the embedded JPG and every other source, and returns early: the preview comes out of developCompositeStack already EXIF-rotated and cropped, so it must not go through the scale-and-checkOrientation tail that follows. It declines outright when the user has asked for Original.

#### 12.6.2 The Image Cache

Outside Develop mode, ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview serves the devPreview INSTEAD OF DECODING THE FILE (Cache/imagedecoder.cpp), before the file is even opened. This is what makes browsing a folder of developed raws as fast as browsing JPEGs: no demosaic, no develop pipeline, no float buffer, just a JPEG decode. The decoder has to honour four consequences:

- decode() must skip rotate() AND applyDevelop(): the pixels arrive oriented, cropped and developed. loadedFromDevPreview says so.
- colorManage() must treat the source as sRGB, not as the image file's embedded profile. The devPreview left the pipeline through OutputTransform in sRGB, so using the raw file's profile would be a WRONG transform, not merely a redundant one. An empty buffer makes ICC::transform assume sRGB, which is exactly right.
- The recipe hash has to be reachable from a decoder thread, which cannot call DevelopProperties on the GUI thread. G::DevPreviewKeyColumn carries it, filled by Metadata::parseSidecar in the same pass that sets the develop badge (no extra I/O) and refreshed by MW::devPreviewUpdated when an edit is flushed. That function also drops the path from the image cache, because the QImage cached there was decoded from the old recipe.
- An EMPTY key column does not mean "no preview": it means the image has no recipe, and for a raw with a sensor decoder there may still be a cached DEFAULT RENDER, so loadDevPreview SYNTHESISES Metadata::defaultRenderKey and looks that up instead. It is synthesised because an unedited image has no sidecar to fill the column from. Any other format returns false: its file already is the default render.

#### 12.6.3 In Develop: The Preview as a Placeholder

In Develop the loupe must show the live render, so the devPreview is used only as the interim placeholder during the sensor decode: MW::devPreview feeds ImageView::loadImageInterim's `substitute` argument, replacing the camera JPG while the raw decodes, and the rendering-hint chip says "Cached preview - decoding raw", so the later swap to the real render does not read as an unexplained flicker.

Entering Develop is a separate hook from selecting an image. MW::fileSelectionChange only reaches its placeholder branch on an image-cache MISS, but a Preview -> Develop switch is a cache HIT, so the loupe would sit on the untouched camera render for the whole re-decode. MW::setOperationMode therefore paints the cached preview itself, through the SAME loadImageInterim path. Not setDevelopPreview: that one is for the drag case, where only the pixels change and the displayed dimensions stay the current image's, which is precisely wrong on a mode switch, because a CROPPED preview has a different shape from the uncropped image on screen. loadImageInterim fits from the pixmap's own bounding rect, so the crop's aspect ratio survives, and it captures and restores zoom/pan across the swap.

Every path that paints a decode in Develop substitutes the preview. ImageView::loadImage paints the decode WITHOUT the saved recipe, and applyDevelopPreviewIfEdited only SCHEDULES the render, so wherever an edited image's decode reaches the loupe, the cached preview is painted over it in the same call (gated on MW::currentDevelopEditsVisible). There are four such places:

- the cache-MISS branch of MW::fileSelectionChange (no decode yet, so the preview replaces the camera JPG);
- the cache-HIT branch of MW::fileSelectionChange (e.g. returning to an image before read-ahead trimmed it);
- MW::setOperationMode on entering Develop;
- MW::refreshViewsOnCacheChange when the decode lands.

A new path that calls loadImage in Develop needs the same substitution, or a cropped recipe flashes back to the original aspect before snapping to the crop.

#### 12.6.4 A Monitor or Display-Scale Change

The third hook, and the one that used to BLANK the loupe. MW::setDisplayResolution (driven by moveEvent, so it fires while the window is dragged between screens) reloads the loupe on a device-pixel-ratio change, and that reload was an unconditional ImageView::loadImage from the image cache. In Develop that is wrong twice over: the loupe is showing a rendered develop frame the image cache knows nothing about, so at best the reload replaced the developed image with the undeveloped decode; and on a cache MISS (routine in Develop: read-ahead is suspended and the raw is re-decoded to scene-linear) loadImage set a NULL pixmap, which cleared ScaledPixmapItem's logical size and left an EMPTY scene that nothing repaired until the next selection change. Now an edited image in Develop re-renders instead, via developParamsChange (the usual coalesced proxy + settle path, so the geometry pairing and zoom/pan survive), and the plain reload runs only when the image is actually cached.

### 12.7 The devPreview Index

#### 12.7.1 Design

Tier 2 files are named by an OPAQUE ID. Lookup is by path, but the file on disk is named by a counter, never by a hash of the path. That makes file-operation sync cheap: a rename or a move rewrites one row's path column (no file to rename, nothing to re-encode, O(1) per image), and deleting an image unlinks one file.

The index is SQLite, sized for 250,000 images. It began as a JSON array held entirely in memory and rewritten in full on every put: cheaper than a dependency at a few hundred entries and indefensible at a quarter of a million (tens of MB of JSON, \~50 MB of paths in memory, and a background preview build rewriting the whole file once per image). It is now the devpreview table in AppDataLocation/PreviewCache/index.db: an indexed lookup, an O(1) write, real transactions, and a file format that survives being extended.

That last point is why it is called CacheDb and not "the preview database" (Cache/cachedb.h). It is Winnow's local index database: one file for every derived, rebuildable index the app keeps about images it has seen (today the devpreview, thumb, image, keyword, image_keyword, keyword_context and vocab tables, plus History's develop_history), with a versioned, ADDITIVE schema (PRAGMA user_version) and one connection per thread. Nothing irreplaceable goes in it (everything is derived from the images and their sidecars), which is what lets the failure policy be "move it aside and rebuild". User-authored data lives in userdata.db instead (Datamodel/userdb.h).

- A connection is released when its thread ends, but NOT when the application is already gone, which for thread-pool threads is when they usually end: Qt's SQL registry is being torn down by then, so touching it warns once per thread on every quit and achieves nothing.
- WAL, and synchronous=NORMAL: a preview read on a decoder thread never blocks the write on the GUI thread. Full fsync-per-commit durability would buy nothing here (the worst a lost commit costs is a re-render) at a price paid on every develop flush. MW::closeEvent and the startup sweep still call save(), which folds the write-ahead log back into the database.
- Existing caches were carried over: the first open of a database with no rows imports any index.json beside it and renames it index.json.migrated (renamed, not deleted, so a bad import is recoverable). Without that, every upgrading user's cache would have read as empty and reconcile() would have deleted every payload (tst_devpreview::legacyJsonIndexIsImported).

#### 12.7.2 A Locked Index Is Left in Place; Only a Broken One Is Moved Aside

CacheDb::db() used to move the file aside (.corrupt) and start a new one on ANY failure to open or migrate, and "database is locked" was one of them, made likelier because busy_timeout was the LAST pragma, so journal_mode = WAL took its lock with no timeout at all. Several Winnow processes on one profile (the parallel smoke tests do exactly that) could discard a healthy index; it surfaced as a one-off catalog_capture failure in a parallel ctest run (2026-10-03). Now:

- busy_timeout is set first.
- A failed open is followed by probeFile on a fresh connection. SQLITE_BUSY / SQLITE_LOCKED (and their extended codes) mean LOCKED: the file is left alone, the issue is logged, and db() answers "no index" for 30 s before trying again (each try waits out the timeout twice, and callers ask constantly).
- A file that reads at a schema this build can migrate is retried once in place.
- Anything else (not a database, unreadable, a newer schema, or a readable file that fails again) is moved aside as before (index.db.corrupt.&lt;timestamp>, with its WAL sidecars) and recreated, because the alternative is a user who can never cache anything again. If SQLite is unavailable altogether, every get simply misses.
- tst_catalog::aLockedIndexIsLeftInPlace holds an EXCLUSIVE lock in rollback-journal mode across the call (\~10 s, both timeouts) and checks the same file opens once the lock goes; anUnreadableIndexIsStillMovedAside pins the other half. userdata.db never moves its file aside at all, and also sets busy_timeout first.

A corrupt index is not recoverable by scanning, and does not need to be: the id in a filename says nothing about which image it belonged to, so an unreferenced &lt;id>.jpg is dead weight.

#### 12.7.3 The Index Is Opened Lazily, and That Is the Only Load Path

Nothing calls load() or setCacheDir() in the app, and setCacheDir deliberately opens nothing. An explicit init call is a thing a caller can forget, and forgetting it fails silently and destructively: the cache reads as empty every session, so every prior-session preview misses, and nextId restarts at 1, so the first new preview OVERWRITES the cache file of an unrelated image. That is exactly what happened when the load was tied to an init call MW did not make. nextId now comes from MAX(id) in the table rather than a stored counter (tst_devpreview::lazyLoadPreservesIdsAcrossSessions). setMaxBytes is safe before any load, which is why MW::loadSettings applies the preference there.

#### 12.7.4 Every Mutation Is Committed When It Happens

The index used to be written only by closeEvent, so an abnormal exit did not merely forget the previews written that session: reconcile() deletes files the index does not name, so the next launch DELETED them, while the tier-1 thumbnails written to the sidecars in the same flush survived. The result was the one state this design exists to prevent: the grid showing the developed picture and the loupe showing the camera's. tst_devpreview::putCommitsIndexWithoutAnExplicitSave pins it. With SQLite this is simply what a commit is.

Moves and deletes count as mutations. onMoved used to change only the in-memory index, so a crash after a rename left an index still naming the SOURCE path. Let something else take that path later and the row describes a different image, and if the two share a recipe (which a preset makes normal) the hash agrees. The source stamp (below) is the backstop for a rename Winnow never saw; committing the move is the fix for the ones it did.

#### 12.7.5 Identity: The Recipe Hash Is Not Enough

The recipe hash identifies a RECIPE, not an image. Presets, Paste Settings and multi-image edits give whole folders a BYTE-IDENTICAL recipe, so the hash cannot tell two images apart. If a path is reused by a different image behind Winnow's back (renamed in Finder while Winnow was closed, restored from a backup, renumbered by the camera), the path matches, the hash matches, and the previous occupant's picture is served as though it were correct. Each row therefore also records the SOURCE IMAGE's length and modification time, and a hit needs those to agree too (tst_devpreview::reusedPathDoesNotServeThePreviousImage).

- Nothing on disk at all is deliberately NOT a mismatch: a missing source is the sweep's demote case (the file is in the trash, or its volume is ejected), and the preview is still the right picture of it. Only a file that is present and DIFFERENT drops the entry.
- Rows imported from the JSON index carry no stamp; they were grandfathered rather than discarded, and the first sweep (which stats every source image anyway) stamps them.

Lookup is by a NORMALISED KEY, not the raw path. The same file reaches Winnow spelled several ways: DataModel stores QFileInfo::filePath() (the path AS CONSTRUCTED: not cleaned, not absolutised); drop and paste build destinations by concatenation (doubling the separator when the folder already ends in one); Finder and Explorer drags arrive through QUrl::toLocalFile(); Windows mixes '\\' and '/' and varies the drive letter's case; and the same folder can be reached through a symlink, a share mounted under another name, or as /Volumes/X and /System/Volumes/Data/X. A mismatch never showed the wrong picture, but a put under a second spelling INSERTED A SECOND ROW (the same image cached twice at several MB each), a get under a second spelling silently re-decoded the raw, and the FileOps hooks found nothing to update.

- Every row carries both: path as the filesystem spelled it (what gets stat'd and reported) and pathkey for every WHERE clause. Cache/pathkey.h is shared, because the key must be computed identically by the code that stores a row, the code that looks one up, and the migration that backfilled the column, and the catalog and keyword tables key on the same thing (tst_devpreview::pathSpellingDoesNotSplitTheEntry).
- CASE IS FOLDED, following the codebase's existing decision (DevPreviewCache::isCachePath and DataModel compare paths case-insensitively, since both supported platforms are case-insensitive by default). The edge case left is a case-SENSITIVE volume holding two files whose names differ only in case: they fold to one key, but the source stamp disagrees, so the two take turns MISSING rather than lying.
- Unicode is normalised to NFC on macOS, where the filesystem returns decomposed forms and QUrl does not.

#### 12.7.6 Orphans and the Sweep

Previews are disposable, so the design makes orphans harmless rather than trying to prevent them. Four layers:

1. An LRU byte cap, the load-bearing bound: the dominant growth case is thousands of images that all still exist, which no sweep would ever reclaim.
2. A one-shot sweep at the first folder load, off the GUI thread, which DEMOTES entries whose source file is missing rather than deleting them (so a file restored from the trash finds its preview intact) and REAPS the ones that have stayed demoted past the grace period.
3. reconcile(), immediately after the sweep in the same pass, for orphans that are not rows at all.
4. The FileOps hooks, for operations Winnow performs itself.

The sweep must NEVER touch an unmounted volume. Winnow browses memory cards and external drives constantly. Each entry records the mount point it was created under, and the sweep skips any entry whose volume is not currently mounted; otherwise ejecting a drive and restarting would demote, then evict, every preview on it. This is the single most important behaviour in the cache, pinned by tst_devpreview::sweepSkipsUnmountedVolume.

It runs at the first folder load, never at shutdown: a force-quit or a crash skips shutdown work entirely, and closeEvent is already doing a synchronous flushAll plus thread teardown.

Demotion needed an end (fixed 2026-09-12). A demoted row kept its multi-MB payload until the LRU cap was breached, so on a cache comfortably under its cap "demoted" meant "kept forever": one real cache was 6,468 previews / 9.65 GB, of which 3,404 rows / 5.05 GB were dead entries from a single camera card, against a 20 GB cap they would never reach. The devpreview table carries a `demoted` column (schema 13, epoch seconds, 0 for a live row): sweep() stamps it on demotion, every path that sets live = 1 clears it, and a row still missing kDemotedGraceSecs (30 days) later is deleted, row and payload together. Thirty days is comfortably longer than anyone takes to notice a deletion they did not mean, and it is a constant, not a preference. A row demoted BEFORE the column existed reads 0 ("we do not know when"): the sweep dates it and reaps it a grace period from there.

The reap clock runs whether or not the volume is mounted, and that is not a hole in the rule above. The mount check guards the VERDICT (deciding that a file is gone requires being able to look), so a LIVE row on an unmounted volume is left strictly alone. A row ALREADY demoted had that verdict reached while the volume was mounted and the file was missing, and ejecting the card afterwards does not make it less true. Gating the reap on the volume would mean a card never reinserted keeps its previews forever, which is precisely the population the reap exists to collect (tst_devpreview::demotedRowIsReapedEvenOnAnUnmountedVolume).

reconcile() was never called, which made layer 3 a comment (fixed 2026-09-12): its only caller was its own unit test. Strays are not rows, so the byte cap cannot see them and no eviction reclaims them. Two paths create them deliberately: the schema-2 pathkey dedupe, and CacheDb::moveAside, which turns the ENTIRE payload folder into strays at a stroke. It now runs immediately after sweep() in the same once-per-session pool task (MW::folderChangeCompleted); sweep first, because its reap deletes rows and their files together.

- Reconcile is one directory listing and one table scan, matched through a set of ids, rather than a stat per row (a quarter of a million stat calls at launch).
- It re-checks every deletion under the lock. It used to hold the cache mutex across the whole walk, scan and every unlink (a multi-second block on every decoder thread's get() at 250,000 entries). The listing and unlinks now run unlocked and the table is read a page at a time, which exposes a race: put() writes its payload with the mutex DROPPED and takes it again to insert the row, so a put() straddling the pass can leave a file the listing missed and a row the scan missed. The snapshots therefore only nominate CANDIDATES: before a row goes its payload is stat'd again, and before a file goes the table is asked again for its id. An id watermark was tried first and is WRONG: after a moveAside the fresh table starts at id 1, so every stray outranks it (tst_devpreview::reconcileKeepsARowWhosePayloadIsThere).

ThumbCache has the same layers minus one, and its sweep was not wired up either (fixed in the same pass, same call site). It needs no reconcile: its thumbnails are BLOBs in the table, so it has no payload files to go stray. Until its sweep ran, thumb.live was never 0 in a real session, and its ORDER BY live, used eviction degenerated to plain LRU.

What the housekeeping did is reported: Help > Diagnostics > Develop prints a housekeeping line (demoted rows reaped, stray files removed, rows with no file dropped), and the per-folder lines flag a folder whose volume is NOT CURRENTLY MOUNTED (those rows read live by design, so the "missing source images" note understates them).

#### 12.7.7 Locking: No Payload I/O Under the Cache Mutex

A full-resolution entry is several MB. get() used to hold the one cache mutex across the read, which serialised all of ImageCache's decoder threads on one disk read at a time (undoing the parallel read-ahead), and put() held it across a multi-MB QSaveFile write plus commit. Both now take the lock, decide, drop it, do the I/O, and take it again to record the result. The serialisation had been entirely self-imposed: WAL was chosen precisely so a decoder-thread read would not block the GUI-thread write.

Releasing the lock opens one window, and both outcomes are safe. Between the lookup and the read the row can be evicted or replaced. An evicted payload fails to open and answers with a miss. A replaced one is caught by re-checking the id before anything destructive: get() only drops a row whose payload is missing if it is still the row it looked at; put() re-reads the row after writing and removes the earlier payload if the id moved underneath it.

The long passes do not hold the lock. sweep() stats one source image per row, which on a network volume is slow, so it works in pages of 512 rows, taking the lock to read a page and again to apply the verdicts, and stats in between. Rows are taken in id order so the cursor survives deletions, and the pass is idempotent. The mount table is walked ONCE per sweep (a statfs per volume), not once per row.

LRU has one-second resolution: entries last used in the same second are tied, and evictLocked falls back to insertion order (id). Harmless in use, but it is why tst_devpreview::lruEvictsLeastRecentlyUsedAtFullSize has to let the clock move before asserting an order.

#### 12.7.8 Clearing

Develop > Clear Developed Preview Cache empties the on-disk tier after a confirmation that reports how much is being deleted. It does NOT touch the 256 px thumbnails: those live in the sidecars and are the image's own property, so deleting them would be an edit to the user's files rather than a cache operation.

### 12.8 The Preview Cache Folder Is Read-Only

The folder is browsable, and that is the problem. The tier-2 cache lives in AppDataLocation/PreviewCache and holds nothing but JPEGs, so the folder panel will happily open it: the user gets a grid of their developed images with no hint that these are not their photographs. Everything Winnow does to an image folder is destructive here:

- A cache file is named by an opaque id that ONLY the index can attribute to an image, so renaming or moving one detaches a preview from its image permanently.
- reconcile() DELETES any file the index does not name, so a file copied in (and any sidecar Winnow writes beside a preview when it is rated, labelled, rotated or developed) is silently deleted at the next launch.
- A preview trashed by hand leaves an index entry pointing at nothing.

So it is READ-ONLY, announced up front. Selecting the folder shows a popup saying the images here can be viewed but not edited, renamed, rated, deleted or developed, and drops out of Develop mode if it was active. Everything that writes is then GREYED with that reason while the folder is loaded (MW::isPreviewCacheFolderLoaded, applied in enableSelectionDependentMenus): rename, delete, paste, the ratings and labels menus, rotate, and Develop mode itself. A disabled QAction greys the menu item AND makes its shortcut inert, so the reason reaches the user through [7.2 Disabled Shortcut Feedback](#72-disabled-shortcut-feedback) rather than as a popup after the fact.

The UI gate is not the protection; it is the explanation. The protection is the refusals below it, so no future caller (a drag-and-drop onto the folder, a script, a context menu that forgets to ask) can get through:

- FileOps::copyFile / moveFile / trashFile refuse on either side of the path.
- The three sidecar writers (Metadata::writeOrientation / writeDevelopSidecar / writeXMP) refuse to write into it.
- MW::setOperationMode refuses to ENTER Develop there.
- MW::deleteFolder and MW::pasteFiles refuse at the folder level, one step above what FileOps can see.

Each refusal logs a G::issue warning and changes nothing on disk. The one predicate they all share is DevPreviewCache::isCachePath (case-insensitive; matches the folder itself and anything under it), pinned by tst_devpreview::isCachePathIdentifiesTheProtectedFolder and tst_fileops::refusesToWriteInThePreviewCacheFolder.

Reading is unaffected, deliberately: browsing the cache is how a user answers "what is in here, and is it worth the disk?" Emptying it is supported through Develop > Clear Developed Preview Cache, which drops the index with the files; deleting the JPEGs by hand would leave the index describing a cache that is not there.

### 12.9 Building devPreviews (Edited Images and Unedited Raws)

A devPreview is a byproduct of a render that happened anyway, which covers the image on screen and nothing else. Every image edited in an earlier session, and every target of a multi-image paste (which has no proxy in memory and correctly CLEARS its preview), has a recipe but no render: no preview, so the grid shows the camera thumbnail and the loupe has to decode the raw.

Closing that gap means DECODING AND RENDERING an image purely to cache it, which is exactly what the byproduct rule exists to avoid, so it never happens unasked. Either the user runs Develop > Build Developed Previews, or they turn on "Build developed previews in background" (G::buildDevPreviewsInBackground, off by default) and accept the cost. Main/devpreviewbuilder.cpp.

#### 12.9.1 Two Populations

- EDITED images are keyed on the hash of their recipe (Metadata::devPreviewKey): the gap above, usually a handful per folder.
- UNEDITED RAWS (any raw with a sensor decoder, RawFormat::HasSensorDecoder) are keyed on the RENDERER instead (Metadata::defaultRenderKey), and what gets cached is the DEFAULT RENDER: the pipeline run with identity adjustments, what the user would see on entering Develop without touching a slider. This population is much the larger.
- MW::devPreviewBuildKey decides which key an image gets, or empty for a file that should have no preview at all (a JPEG, or a raw with no sensor decoder: the file on disk already IS the default render, so a preview would be a re-encode of it).

The second population exists purely for BROWSING SPEED. With it cached, ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview serves a raw from a JPEG decode instead of a demosaic, so an unedited raw folder browses like a folder of JPEGs, and shows WINNOW's rendering of the sensor data rather than the camera's embedded JPEG. The cost is paid once, up front, and it is steep: a thousand-raw folder is a thousand full decodes and composites, one at a time, so hours rather than seconds, and several GB of cache. That trade is the whole point of the feature, and why the preference is off by default.

- The default-render key hashes the RENDERER, not a recipe, because there is no recipe to hash (devPreviewKey returns empty for an unedited image, and an empty key is what loadDevPreview reads as "no preview"). defaultRenderKey hashes everything OUTSIDE the recipe that changes the pixels (the raw engine, G::autoRunDenoise, the opt-in raw preferences when ON) plus a version to bump when a pipeline change makes existing default renders wrong. Changing any of those makes every previously built default render MISS; the stranded entries age out through the LRU. The key is prefixed 'R', not a hex digit, so the recipe and renderer key spaces are provably disjoint.
- Only the LARGE tier for an unedited raw. The 256 px grid thumbnail lives in the image's XMP sidecar, and an image the user never edited must not GAIN a sidecar as a side effect of a cache fill. The grid keeps the camera-embedded thumbnail, already read during the metadata pass.

#### 12.9.2 Only Where the User Said Their Library Is

A devPreview is keyed on the image's PATH and stored away from the image, so building one for a folder the user is passing through is work thrown away. The case that makes this a bug rather than an inefficiency is a CAMERA CARD: selecting one used to queue a full sensor decode of every raw on it (hours), then ingest copies those files to a different path and the card is erased, so every preview built is orphaned at the moment it could first have been used, having evicted real library entries from the LRU on the way out. A network share is the same read cost without the orphaning. DevPreviewPolicy::folderEligible (Main/devpreviewpolicy.h) decides, per FOLDER rather than per volume, because a recursive load routinely spans both kinds:

- With a catalog scope table, the test is catalogScopeIncludes && !catalogScopeExcludes: "did the user nominate this folder", the same statement as "is this part of my library". It is a PREFIX test, so a subfolder created a minute ago under a recursive include qualifies at once (scope MEMBERSHIP is tested rather than catalog ROWS, which a new folder does not have yet). A card is never under it.
- With no scope table (promptForCatalogScope asks once and can be dismissed), the fallback is the volume itself: build on fixed local drives, never on removable or network media.

VolumeInfo (Utilities/volumeinfo.h) is the volume half. UsbUtil::isRemovable could not be reused: on macOS it answers "is the path under /Volumes", which is true of a permanently attached external library drive as well as an SD card (right for offering Eject, wrong for deciding whether a volume is worth a cache). The real signals are statfs's MNT_REMOVABLE and MNT_LOCAL on macOS (an exFAT card reads local=1 removable=1, an APFS data volume local=1 removable=0, so neither flag alone separates them) and GetDriveTypeW on Windows. Any failure, and any other platform, answers Unknown, and Unknown counts as LOCAL FIXED: the callers use this to withhold work, so a failed query must fall back to the behaviour that existed before the rule. A wrong "skip" is a feature that silently stopped working; a wrong "build" is a cache fill nobody asked for.

None of this governs Develop > Build Developed Previews, the escape hatch (asking explicitly, on a card, means it), nor the byproduct paths (flushImage, topUpDevPreviews, the provider's flush fallback), which are consequences of editing an image on purpose wherever it lives.

In the Library the background build covers the WHOLE Library. queueBackgroundDevPreviewBuild is called from MW::metadataComplete, which runs for a Library load as well as a folder load, and it walks every DataModel row. Every Library folder is in the catalog scope by definition, so every raw plus every edited image without a current preview is queued: tens of thousands of full renders on a large Library. Leaving the Library (MW::stop -> cancelDevPreviewBuild) abandons the queue and the next Library load rebuilds it; finished rows are filtered out downstream, so progress is not lost. The preference tooltip says so ("In the Library this covers the whole Library and can take many hours"). Whether the Library case should be narrowed (e.g. to folders actually visited) is an open question.

#### 12.9.3 How It Runs

- The "does this need building?" filter runs OFF the GUI thread. Which key an image should carry needs model reads (plus a sidecar read for the few edited images) and has to be on the GUI thread; whether the cache already holds that key (DevPreviewCache::contains: one SQLite query AND one stat() per path) used to be too, which is a thousand queries and stats arriving exactly when a 1000-image folder finishes loading. buildDevPreviews now derives the keys on the GUI thread, hands the (path, key) pairs to a pool thread for the cache test, and resumes in startDevPreviewBuild with the filtered list, guarded by dm->instance in case the folder changed meanwhile.
- It runs on the exporter's engine, MW::developPixelSource ([14.2 The Pixel Sources and Their Callers](#142-the-pixel-sources-and-their-callers)), so a built preview cannot drift from what an export or a real develop render produces.
- ONE AT A TIME: the next image starts when the previous one's render returns. That keeps the builder inside the raw-decoder concurrency budget ([5.7 Memory Governor (Process Footprint, Decode Concurrency)](#57-memory-governor-process-footprint-decode-concurrency)) whatever the folder size, and a long build never competes with the image the user is looking at.
- The key is RE-DERIVED when the render lands and compared with the one captured at dispatch. A render takes seconds, and in between the user may have edited that image or switched raw engine; on a mismatch the write is dropped and the image simply misses again, to be rebuilt correctly next time.
- The queue is disposable: changing folders (MW::stop) abandons it, and it is rebuilt from what is actually missing every time, so re-running after a partial build is free and a stale queue can never be wrong.

#### 12.9.4 Inside Develop It Renders Only Multi-Image Edit Targets

A develop edit made with several images selected (or a Paste Settings / Apply Preset onto a selection) lands on images with no render in memory, so flushImage has no preview to write and clears it, and the grid fell back to the camera thumbnail until the user left Develop. MW::devPreviewUpdated queues each such target with src "sync" (devPreviewBuildSyncPaths), and devPreviewBuildNext, in Develop, drops every queued path that is NOT a sync path or IS the image being edited, then renders the rest. Everything else (a background folder build, a menu build) still yields to Develop: developRenderPool has ONE thread, so each of those renders would sit in front of the user's own settle render. Accepted cost for sync targets: while they render, the edited image's settle render (and a navigation decode) can wait up to one target render.

- The edited image is PINNED. A builder decode puts the target's WorkingImage into WorkingImageCache, and on a large raw one decode alone exceeds the \~768 MB budget, so the LRU rule (never evict the most recent put) would protect the TARGET and evict the image being edited, costing its next slider tick a full re-decode. renderDevelopPreview pins the current image (WorkingImageCache::setPinned), setOperationMode clears the pin on leaving Develop, and evictLocked skips the pinned entry. An export run from Develop benefits the same way.
- A sync re-queue of the in-flight path is allowed: a further edit while a target renders changes its recipe, the in-flight render is then dropped by the key check, so the path is queued again behind it. startDevPreviewBuild no longer dispatches when a run is already going (it used to call devPreviewBuildNext unconditionally, which would have started a second render beside the one in flight).
- Flush builds are DEFERRED, not dropped. When flushImage's provider cannot write the loupe tier (with the cap at Full: whenever the settle render has not landed, i.e. most edits, and always when Develop is left with the crop tool open), it queues the image with src "flush". Inside Develop, startDevPreviewBuild parks those in devPreviewBuildDeferred instead of queueing them, and setOperationMode builds them when Develop is left. They used to be discarded by the gate above, and nothing asked again (topUpDevPreviews had already marked the image handled), so the image kept its thumbnail but had no devPreview, and Browse showed the file undeveloped: a cropped version looked uncropped in the loupe. MW::stop clears the deferred set, since its paths belong to the folder being left.

#### 12.9.5 Progress

A status-bar row ("Dev Previews", progressDevPreviewRow), alongside Metadata, Raw Denoise and Demosaicing, not a popup: a build is minutes of work the user is not waiting on, and a popup parked over the image would be in the way of the very pictures being rebuilt. The row appears when a run starts and collapses when it ends. Only a run the user ASKED for (Develop > Build Developed Previews) reports its result in a popup ("nothing to do" up front, "Built N" or the Develop-mode pause at the end); a background build says nothing, because the row already said it was happening and the grid shows the result.

## 13 Versions (Virtual Copies)

Lightroom's virtual copy: a second (third, ...) Develop recipe for the same source file. Each version is its own row in the grid, grouped after its master and collapsed behind it by default (a collapsed master shows a count badge). Rating, colour label and pick belong to each version; keywords, title and the other IPTC fields belong to the file and are shared.

Status (2026-09-28): all six phases are done. The row key split from the source path, sidecar storage, version rows in the grid (collapse and badge), Develop per version (New / Rename / Delete Version, Set Version as Master, per-version recipes, previews, export naming), per-version rating / label / pick with the file's fields shared across the group, the file operations (rename, delete, ingest, find duplicates, stacking, copy / drag / share), and the catalog (schema 17). Not built: a Versions band in the Develop panel; the operations are in Develop > Versions and the thumbnail context menu.

### 13.1 The Row Key

A DataModel row's identity is its KEY (G::KeyRole, which replaced G::PathRole): the file path for a master, byte for byte what it always was, and path + "/#v" + id for a version, e.g. /Photos/IMG_1.CR3/#v2 (Utilities/versionkey.h). G::SourcePathRole is derived from the same field and is always the file on disk; it is read-only (RowStore::setValue ignores it). fPathRow, the proxy snapshot, IconStore, ImageCache, the selection and DataModel::currentKey are all keyed by the key; everything that opens, stats, reads or writes a file must use the source path (G::SourcePathRole, DataModel::currentSourcePath(), sourcePathFromProxyRow).

The rename WAS the audit. G::PathRole was deleted rather than aliased, and rowFromPath / proxyRowFromPath / indexFromPath / proxyIndexFromPath / pathFromProxyRow / currentFilePath became rowFromKey / proxyRowFromKey / indexFromKey / proxyIndexFromKey / keyFromProxyRow / currentKey, so every call site had to be looked at. The split: identity (datamodel, image cache, views, status, slideshow, selection) takes the key; file I/O (metadata reads, rename, ingest, find duplicates, reveal, drag and copy-to-clipboard, video load, the catalog builder) takes the source path; the version-aware writers take the KEY, so a version row reaching a file write fails loudly at the guard below instead of silently writing the master's file.

Why "/#v": the key must fail loudly if it ever reaches file I/O. IMG_1.CR3 is a regular file, so nothing can exist beneath it, and any open or stat of IMG_1.CR3/#v2 fails (ENOTDIR on macOS and Windows alike). "|" and "::" were rejected: both are legal in APFS names, and FileOps::sidecarPath's legacy stem logic would have turned IMG_1.CR3|v2 into IMG_1.xmp, the master's sidecar. A folder literally named "#v2" is not mistaken for a key: the id must be all digits and end the string.

The guard: FileOps::refuseVersionKey(path, src) raises G::issue("Error", "A version key reached file I/O; refused.") and returns true for a version key. It is called by FileOps::sidecarPath / existingSidecar / prepareSidecarForWrite / companions / copyFile / moveFile / trashFiles, Metadata::writeXMP / writeKeywordsToSidecar / writeOrientation / writeDevelopSidecar / loadImageMetadata, ImageDecoder::load and Thumb::loadThumb. Seeing that issue in the log means a call site still passes a key where it needs the source path. A version KEY handed to any FileOps entry point is refused rather than acted on as the master (tst_fileops::versionKeysAreRefused): deleting a version must never trash the image.

Sort order: DataModel::sortKey sorts a key on its source path's key plus VersionKey::sortSuffix(id) (U+0001 and a zero-padded id), so a version lands immediately after its master and before any other file. Raw keys would not do: "img_1.cr3-edit.jpg" sorts between "img_1.cr3" and "img_1.cr3/#v1" because '-' is below '/'. DataModel::insertFiles orders by the key but decides folder membership on the source path. Pinned by tests/unit/tst_versionkey.cpp and tst_imagerow::sourcePathIsDerivedFromTheKey (the three version roles).

### 13.2 Storage

Metadata/versions.h. Versions live in ONE sidecar attribute, winnow:Versions, beside the master's winnow:Develop: base64 of compact JSON

```
{"schema":1,"nextId":N,"versions":[{id, name, created, rating, label, pick, develop, previewKey, preview}]}
```

develop is the version's EditStack::toBase64(); preview is its 256 px JPEG and previewKey the devPreviewKey of the recipe it was rendered from, the same pairing the master keeps in DevelopPreview / DevelopPreviewKey. The master is NOT in the set, so an older Winnow, or anything else reading winnow:Develop, still sees the master exactly as before, and an older Winnow rewriting the sidecar keeps winnow:Versions because Xmp edits the parsed document in place (tst_versions::anotherWriterKeepsTheVersions).

- IDs are never reused. The id is part of the row key, and every key-keyed cache (devPreview, history, icon) would hand a reused id the deleted version's state. nextId only rises; fromBase64 repairs a nextId behind its ids; update() overrules an edit that lowers it; and deleting the LAST version keeps the attribute as {"nextId":N,"versions":[]} rather than removing it (the first cut removed it, and tst_versions caught the next version coming back as v1).
- Nothing is overwritten that cannot be read. Versions::update is the only writer: one read-modify-write under FileOps::sidecarLock. It refuses, and writes nothing, when the stored set is corrupt or from a newer schema, when the sidecar is a symlink, the folder is read-only or is the preview-cache folder, or src is a version key. Fields this build does not know, on a version or on the document, are carried through untouched (ImageVersion::extra, VersionSet::extra).
- File operations need nothing new: versions ride in the sidecar, and FileOps already carries it on copy, move, rename and trash (tst_fileops::versionsTravelWithTheImage).

The sidecar lock: FileOps::sidecarLock(path) is a per-image QRecursiveMutex (keyed by cachePathKey of the source path) held by every whole-document sidecar writer: writeXMP (GUI thread), writeKeywordsToSidecar, writeOrientation (QtConcurrent) and writeDevelopSidecar. They used to run unlocked, so two concurrent writers could lose one another's changes; versions add more read-modify-writes of the same document. Recursive because writeXMP and writeKeywordsToSidecar call markSidecarEmbedded while holding it.

### 13.3 Version Rows in the Model

Metadata::parseSidecar reads winnow:Versions from the document it has already parsed and fills ImageMetadata::versions with VersionSummary rows (id, name, rating, label, pick, developed, devPreviewKey): no recipe or preview bytes. Versions::read / readVersion / readRecipe serve everything else.

A version is its own DataModel row, keyed path + "/#v" + id, placed right after its master by DataModel::sortKey. It has no file, so its values come from its MASTER: addMetadataForItem keeps a copy of each master's ImageMetadata whose sidecar lists versions (DataModel::versionMasters), and DataModel::fillVersionRow replays it into the version's row through addMetadataForItem (the same writer every row uses) with the version's name (G::VersionNameRole), rating, label, pick and develop state laid over it. A master carries its count (G::VersionCountRole); G::VersionIdRole is derived from the key. fillVersionRow resets the row's search text first, because addMetadataForItem APPENDS to it and a refill would double every field.

#### 13.3.1 Rows Are Added Only Through applyModelChange, and Never Mid-Load

MetaRead and the ImageCache address the model by row number; an insert while they are reading would land reads on the wrong image. So MW::reconcileVersionRows (Main/mwversions.cpp) runs once when a load completes (synchronously at the TOP of MW::metadataComplete, ahead of the filter build) and, coalesced, whenever a master is re-read afterwards (DataModel::versionsChanged). It asks DataModel::versionRowChanges for the rows to add (a master lists a version the model lacks) and remove (a version row its master no longer lists), applies both in one applyModelChange, and refills the version rows that stayed. applyModelChange's synchronous load step fills a version row with fillVersionRow rather than reading a file. See [4.3 On-the-Fly Insert and Delete (One Pipeline)](#43-on-the-fly-insert-and-delete-one-pipeline).

- versionsChanged is POSTED, not emitted: addMetadataForItem holds a QSignalBlocker on the model for its whole body, and the first cut's direct emit was swallowed without a trace (the model_mutation self-test caught it).
- What "never mid-load" is tested on (2026-09-28): the first cut guarded on G::isModifyingDatamodel, which is FALSE for the whole fill (MW::loadCatalogScope and MW::folderSelectionChange both set it and then call MW::stop(), which clears it). Opening the Library with one version in it ran applyModelChange at row \~120,000 of 155,000 (an 812 ms filterChange and a 1.75 s GUI stall mid-fill), bumped the instance and restarted the readers while DataModel::loadingModel was still refusing their icons, and those thumbnails never painted. reconcileVersionRows now also returns while dm->loadingModel or G::isLoadRunning ([4.7.3 "Is a Load Running" Is Not "Has Every Row Been Read"](#473-is-a-load-running-is-not-has-every-row-been-read)).
- MW::metadataComplete's own call passes atLoadEnd and runs FIRST, before its filter build: the first cut queued it after, and applyModelChange's filter rebuild then cut the load's build short (the Filters panel came up greyed with 23 tree items instead of \~17,800).

#### 13.3.2 The Parts That Must Never Treat a Key as a File

- Reader::read drops the metadata read for a version (its metadata is the master's).
- Reader::readIcon and applyModelChange take the icon from Thumb::loadVersionThumb: the version's own 256 px preview when its key matches the recipe, else the SOURCE file's original camera thumbnail (never the master's developed one, and never written to the path-keyed ThumbCache).
- ImageDecoder decodes the source file (fPath) and caches and reports the result under the key (rowKey), looking up the devPreview by key.
- DataModel::refresh / sourceModified skip version keys in the "removed" and "modified" diffs (a key is never in a folder listing; it follows its master's sidecar); removeFiles takes a master's version rows with it; rawJpgPairing never pairs a version; catalogRowFor skips version rows (the file-level facts are the master's).
- verifyIntegrity also checks every version has its master in the model, ahead of it.

### 13.4 Collapse, Sorting and the UI

#### 13.4.1 Collapse

Groups start collapsed. SortFilter::filterAcceptsRow hides a version whose group is collapsed, with or without a filter, as long as its MASTER is shown. A version that matches a filter its master does not still shows on its own, because a matching version hidden behind a master that is not there would be a wrong answer. The master is tested with the same compiled predicate. (Until 2026-09-28 a set filter disabled collapse outright; in the Library, where a LibTree folder is itself a filter, that made collapse do nothing.) A master whose values change so that it stops matching re-shows its versions at the next filterChange, not instantly: dynamic filtering re-tests only the row that changed.

The state lives on the proxy (setVersionsExpanded per master key, setShowAllVersions global) and changes only through MW::setVersionsExpanded / toggleVersionsExpanded / setShowAllVersions, which re-filter through MW::filterChange; collapsing a group whose version is current selects the master first. Filter counts include version rows: they are what a filter would show.

The open groups persist (2026-10-18). MW::writeSettings saves SortFilter::expandedVersions as "expandedVersions" (dropping a master that is loaded but has no version left; one outside the loaded model is kept), and createModuleDock puts them back next to versionMastersOnly. Groups no longer always start collapsed: a new session opens the ones that were open. The selection restore backs this up: MW::applySelectionRestore opens the group of any saved key that is a version in the model but not in the proxy (a crash skips writeSettings), then re-filters before selecting. Under Masters it selects the version's master instead.

#### 13.4.2 Sorting

Column sorts keep a group together: SortFilter::prepareSortKeys gives each version its master's value (only when the model holds version rows, DataModel::versionRowCount), and the proxy's ordering keeps the source order (master, then its versions) among equals. That holds in BOTH directions: SortFilter::lessThan breaks ties on source row, and because a descending sort calls lessThan(right, left) the tie-break flips with the order (fixed 2026-10-18 -- a plain l < r put every version ahead of its master under any descending sort).

Every sort tie breaks on source order (2026-10-01). SortFilter::lessThan gives the proxy a TOTAL order in all three of its paths (cached ranks, stored keys, and Qt's own lessThan): equal keys compare by source row. A full sort never needed this, because Qt's sort is stable; a SINGLE-ROW RE-PLACEMENT does. When one row's data changes, the dynamic sort removes the row and binary-searches it back in, and with no tie-break it landed at either end of its block of equal keys. Sorting a catalog by Created puts thousands of images with a blank date in one block; an edit to one of them, such as a Develop flush, could move it, and code holding its old proxy row (dm->currentSfRow) then selected a neighbour. The same bug surfaced with versions: a renamed master sorted after its version, which still carried the old name for a moment, and equal names never moved it back. The source-row tie-break is exactly the order a stable full sort produces, so a re-placed row goes back to its own slot. Ties keep source order under descending sorts too (the tie-break flips with the order, 2026-10-18; it used to reverse them, which put versions ahead of their masters).

#### 13.4.3 The Badges

A master with versions shows a count and an arrow ("2 ▸" / "2 ▾") in amber text on a tag tucked into the top-right corner of its cell frame, mirroring the icon number in the top-left (bold, one point above the UI font; the tag is G::backgroundColor with a 1 px G::borderColor border, the text carrying the amber / blue). A plain click on it opens or closes the group (IconView::mousePressEvent -> IconViewDelegate::versionsBadgeHit -> MW::toggleVersionsExpanded). A version shows its name ("v2" until named) in blue text on the same tag in the same corner. Both have tooltips.

File > Show All Versions (also in the thumbnail context menu, persisted as "showAllVersions") opens every group; clicking one badge while it is on turns it off and leaves that group open.

#### 13.4.4 Masters | Versions

The Module dock's MASTERS | VERSIONS pair (right side, mirroring Library | Folders on the left; added 2026-10-14).

- MASTERS is the outermost scope: SortFilter::mastersOnly (persisted "versionMastersOnly") rejects every version row in acceptsRow, above the load test and the user's filters (like the raw+jpg hide), so no version appears under any filter, open group or Show All Versions. versionsExpanded() answers false under it (badge arrow, self-test, rescue pass), and BuildFilters folds version rows into FilterSnapshotRow::hiddenRaw so the unfiltered counts leave them out too (cache keyed on cachedValuesMastersOnly). An image with no versions is its own master.
- VERSIONS lifts it and turns Show All Versions on (every row).
- Things that lift Masters (MW::setVersionMastersOnly(false) or inline): Versions, checking Show All Versions, a badge click (opens just that group), and New Version (opens just the new groups, or the new row would be hidden).
- Toggling Masters re-filters AND recounts (filterChange alone refreshes only the filtered side). MW::syncVersionModeButtons pushes the state to the buttons.

### 13.5 Develop per Version

The recipe I/O dispatches on the key, so every caller (DevelopProperties' stackFor, flushImage, topUpDevPreviews; the devPreview builder; Thumb::loadDevThumb; export) is version-correct without knowing versions exist: Metadata::readDevelopSidecar / writeDevelopSidecar / readDevThumb, given a version key, read or write that version's record in winnow:Versions (develop, preview, previewKey in one Versions::update) instead of winnow:Develop. A write to a version deleted meanwhile is refused, not recreated. DevelopProperties' stackCache, dirty set and History were already keyed by the string they were given, which is now the row key.

What is shared and what is not:

- Pixels are the FILE's: WorkingImageCache maps a key to its source (switching between versions of one raw is a re-render, not a re-decode), as do DataModel::imMetadata's m.fPath (what decodeIndependent opens), fPathRawInfoGet and MW::isFileRaw.
- Everything recipe-derived is the KEY's: DevPreviewCache entries (a version's loupe preview is its own), the develop frame / proxy paths, developRecipeKey.
- The raw DEFAULT render is the KEY's as well: an unedited version gets its own default-render entry, built by the devPreview builder (MW::devPreviewBuildKey) and read by ImageDecoder::loadDevPreview under the version's key. It used to borrow the source's entry, but DevPreviewCache holds ONE entry per path, so once the master was edited that slot held the master's recipe and every unedited version missed (Browse showed the camera's embedded JPEG while Develop showed the default render). A recipe reset to identity (MW::devPreviewUpdated with an empty blob) queues its default render at once.
- The segmentation references (Subject / Sky / Depth) and the develop proxy are compared by key, so switching versions recomputes them: correct, and a candidate for sharing by source if it proves slow.

DevPreviewCache and versions: a version's row is keyed by its version key, but stamped, foldered and volumed by its SOURCE (SrcStamp::of maps a key to its file; a stamp of the key itself would read as a vanished image on every get and every sweep). onDeleted(image) also removes its versions' entries and onMoved(image) re-keys them onto the new path (versionKeysLocked: pathkey LIKE key + "/#v%", with % and \_ escaped); removeEntry removes exactly one. Pinned by tst_devpreview::versionsHaveTheirOwnEntries / versionsFollowTheirImage.

### 13.6 The Operations

Main/mwversions.cpp; Develop > Versions, also the thumbnail context menu, in both modes, synced per current image on aboutToShow. Every one flushes pending Develop edits first and writes only the master's sidecar, never the image file.

- New Version (Cmd/Ctrl + ', Lightroom's key): a version of every selected image, copying its recipe, 256 px preview, loupe preview, rating, label and pick. The group opens and the current image's new version is selected (queued, because filterChange recovers the previous selection as it finishes). When any image getting a version is in collections, a checklist of those collections (all ticked) asks which the version should join too; Cancel makes no version. A version is a collection member in its own right, never by way of its master ([17.5.6 Versions Are Members in Their Own Right](#1756-versions-are-members-in-their-own-right)).
- Rename Version...: "v&lt;id>" typed back means unnamed.
- Delete Version...: a destructive-button confirmation that says the image file is not affected; lands on the master, removes the record, its loupe preview and its History (DevelopProperties::forgetImage).
- Set Version as Master: swaps the two RECIPES (and both preview tiers), so the chosen edit is the one in winnow:Develop that other applications see. Name, rating, label and pick stay with their rows. The selection moves to the master, following the edit: staying on the version row put the user on the OLD master's settings, so the next adjustment edited the wrong recipe (reported 2026-09-28).

After a sidecar change the masters are re-read (MW::rereadVersionMasters: applyModelChange + an immediate reconcile). A version's recipe saved by DevelopProperties updates the captured summary in place (DataModel::noteVersionDevelop), so a later refill does not revert the badge. applyModelChange resets a re-read row's search text first, as fillVersionRow does.

Export: ImageExporter names a version from its source file plus its name (IMG_1-B&W.jpg, IMG_1-v2.jpg until named, characters a file name cannot hold replaced by "\_"), so a master and its versions export as separate files; the folder is the source's. The {VERSION} token (Utilities/tokenfilename.h) places the name in a template instead, and then no suffix is added; Rename and Ingest expand it to "".

### 13.7 Per-Version and Shared Fields

#### 13.7.1 Rating, Label and Pick Are the Version's

They live in the version's record, Winnow-private, always in winnow:Versions whatever "Permit image file modification" says; the master's stay in xmp:Rating / xmp:Label. Thirteen places write those three columns (the menus and keys, the mouse-over pick, pick undo, crash-log recovery, Ingest's mark) and all of them go through DataModel::setValDm / setValSf, so that is where a version row is caught:

- DataModel::noteVersionValueWrite queues the row's KEY (not its row number, which can move) and posts one versionValuesEdited per event-loop turn.
- MW::writeVersionValues writes the row's current rating, label and pick to the record (Versions::update) and brings the captured summary in line (noteVersionValues), so a refill keeps them.
- The two writers that ALSO write the file (MW::setRating and MW::setColorClass / setColorClassForRow) skip writeXMP for a version row.
- Pinned by model_mutation "version values", which also checks the master's rating and xmp:Rating are untouched.

setColorClassForRow had a WRONG-FILE bug, independent of versions: it asked keyFromProxyRow(sfRow) for the file to write AFTER filterChange had re-filtered and re-sorted the proxy, so with a label filter active the label could be written into a different image. The key and dm row are now taken before anything moves, and \_Label is still set after writeXMP (its change detection compares against that shadow; setting it first would skip the write). The lesson is general: audit every caller before anything writes into an original.

#### 13.7.2 Shared Fields Are the File's

Title, creator, copyright, email, url, keywords and orientation. An edit made with a version row selected is retargeted to its master's row and file, written once per file however many of the group were selected (InfoView::dataChanged, MW::applyKeywordsToSelection), and DataModel::syncSharedToVersions copies the master row's values onto its version rows and into the captured master metadata, so a later refill keeps them; MW::publishKeywordWrite (retag) does the same.

Rotation (MW::setRotation) walks DATAMODEL rows, expanding the selection to whole groups (a collapsed version is not in the proxy), so rotating any row turns the file once (writeOrientation on the source) and every row of the group, each row's recipe re-expressed in the new frame by rotateImageEdits ([11.26 Rotating a Developed Image (the Recipe Follows the Photo)](#1126-rotating-a-developed-image-the-recipe-follows-the-photo)). Pinned by model_mutation "shared keywords", "rotate group" and "refill keeps edits".

### 13.8 File Operations With Versions

The rule throughout: a version is its master's FILE, so anything that acts on files acts on each source file once, and nothing ever trashes a file to delete a version.

- Rename (RenameFileDlg::renameDatamodel, the in-place update): after the master's row is re-keyed, DataModel::rekeyVersions re-keys its version rows (key, fPathRow, name, captured metadata, collapse state) and returns the (old, new) pairs so the ImageCache entries follow. The records ride in the renamed sidecar, the loupe previews in FileOps::onMoved. The collapse state moves FIRST, because each key write makes the proxy re-test that row on the spot.
- Delete (MW::deleteSelectedFiles): the selection is split. Masters go to the trash and take their versions with them; the confirmation says how many, and is shown whenever versions would go, even with the delete warning turned off (turning it off agreed to trashing images, not to losing versions the user may not know are there). A selected version whose master is not also selected is removed as a RECORD (MW::deleteVersionRecords: one sidecar write per master, previews and History dropped); with only versions selected, no file is touched and the version confirmation replaces the trash one.
- DataModel::getSelectionOrPicks returns each selected / picked SOURCE FILE once: all its callers (rename, external app, focus and mean stack, embellish export) act on files.
- Ingest (Ingest::getPicks, IngestDlg's copy): each file once however many of its group are picked; a version hidden only by a collapsed group counts as in view when its master is.
- Find Duplicates skips version rows (each would be a duplicate of its master every time).
- Copy, Share, Drag Out and Copy Path hand each file over once.

Pinned by model_mutation "rename master" and "delete version".

### 13.9 Versions in the Catalog

Phase 6, schema 17. A row served from the INDEX never parses its sidecar: a catalog scope, and also a FOLDER load's fresh rows (Catalog::fetchFresh), which is why this was needed for versions to appear at all with a catalog defined. So the index holds each image's version list in image_version (image_id, vid, name, rating, label, pick, developed, devpreviewkey; ON DELETE CASCADE from image): what DataModel::fillVersionRow needs, never the recipe or preview bytes.

- CatalogRow::versions carries it: filled by CatalogScanner::parseInto and DataModel::catalogRowFor (from the captured master metadata), written whole by Catalog::commit (writeVersionsLocked, whenever the image row is, i.e. when its sidecar stamp changed), read back by fetchFresh and searchRows (readVersionsLocked scans the whole table, which holds only images WITH versions, rather than binding a 43,000-row scope's ids past SQLite's parameter limit), and copied into ImageMetadata::versions by IndexMetadata::fill.
- A CATALOG FILL inserts the version rows itself, straight after each master in the same batch (DataModel::insertCatalogBatch, catalogVersionIds), so a Library load never pays an applyModelChange over the whole model for them (a new instance, a filter pass and a filter rebuild, measured at \~1-2 s on 155,000 rows for ONE version).
- One catch, found in-app: insertRows makes the rows before their keys are written, so the proxy tested each version row as a keyless master and accepted it, and the batch's dataChanged came while dynamic filtering was off: a collapsed group showed its versions in the Library, and the badge's first click "expanded" them. finishCatalogFill re-emits dataChanged for just the version rows once restoreProxySortAfterLoad has dynamic filtering back on.
- A FOLDER load still gets them from MW::metadataComplete's reconcile: its rows arrive MetaNotAttempted and the versions are known only once MetaRead has read the masters. The end-of-load reconcile finds the version rows from the path hash (DataModel::versionRowKeys), not by walking every row.
- In-app version changes re-commit the master's row (updateCatalogForRow from rereadVersionMasters, writeVersionValues and devPreviewUpdated). Filtering a catalog scope happens in the proxy, so version rows are judged on their own rating and label there too.
- No backfill: an index row written before schema 17 with versions already in its sidecar shows none until the sidecar changes (possible only for a row written by a development build). Pinned by tst_catalog::versionsRoundTripThroughTheIndex.

### 13.10 Tests

The model_mutation self-test (Main/selftestmutation.cpp) writes versions into a master's sidecar and re-reads it: versions appear as a collapsed group filled from the master with their own name / rating / label / pick; expanding shows them after the master; collapsing with a version current lands on the master; a version deleted from the sidecar leaves the model; Refresh leaves version rows alone; removing the master takes its versions; New Version adds a selected copy of the current image; Set Version as Master swaps the recipes and the develop badges; plus the "version values", "shared keywords", "rotate group", "refill keeps edits", "rename master" and "delete version" steps above. Its budget is WINNOW_SELFTEST_MS=120000 (ctest TIMEOUT 240), because the mutation steps start at half the budget and the generic self-test's own timer fires at the whole of it (at 20 s it fired mid-run).

## 14 Export

Getting developed images out. X in Develop mode exports the SELECTED images with each image's own develop recipe applied. The same export is File > Export Developed Images... and the thumbnail context-menu item of that name (exportDevelopedAction): enabled in BOTH modes and keyless, since X means Reject outside Develop and developExportAction is greyed there. It works outside Develop because the export renders each image's stored recipe (stackJobFor), not the live session.

Everything about writing an image out of Winnow lives in one place; the only thing that varies between callers is where the pixels come from.

### 14.1 One Engine

Winnow had two unrelated export loops, and neither could do the job:

- MW::saveAsFile / SaveAsDlg rendered through Pixmap::load (the BROWSE decode), so it applied no develop recipe, embedded no ICC profile and copied no EXIF. Three formats, one quality spin, no naming or resizing.
- EmbelExport::exportImages had the mature batch (progress, Esc abort, subfolder destination, suffix, overwrite policy, ExifTool tag / ICC / thumbnail copy) but read each file FROM DISK, so it could not see a develop edit either, and its quality was hardcoded at 100.

A third copy was the wrong end state, so Export/ owns the shared engine. SaveAsDlg has been retired onto it (File > Save Preview as opens the same dialog with the plain pixel source and its develop-only rows hidden). EmbelExport's batch is not migrated yet, but its pixels now come from Develop ([14.2.3 Embellish Export](#1423-embellish-export)).

```
Export/exportsettings.h      ExportSettings (destination, naming, format, sizing) + the curated format table
Export/exportpresets.*       Named presets in QSettings; the DevelopPresets contract
Export/imageexporter.*       ImageExporter: the batch engine
Dialogs/exportdlg.*          The dialog (hand-built, no .ui)
Utilities/tokenfilename.*    The shared {TOKEN} filename parser
```

#### 14.1.1 The Pixel Source Is Asynchronous

ImageExporter owns destination resolution, naming, uniquify / skip / overwrite, resizing, saving, colour-space tagging, the ExifTool copy, progress and abort. It does NOT generate pixels: a PixelSource callback does, and it is ASYNCHRONOUS BY CONTRACT,

```
using Done = std::function<void(bool ok, const QImage &img)>;
using PixelSource = std::function<void(const QString &fPath, Done done)>;
```

because one full-resolution raw render is \~1 s and a synchronous batch would freeze the GUI for minutes. The batch is a CHAIN, not a loop: startNext() asks the source for one image and returns; onImageReady() saves it and queues the next through the event loop. That is what keeps progress painting and Cancel responsive throughout.

#### 14.1.2 Per-Image Recipes

DevelopProperties::stackJobFor(fPath) is the export twin of stackJob(): it reads the image's OWN stored EditStack (stackFor loads the sidecar on first touch), ignores the History hover override (a hovered row must never reach a file) and ignores the Transform / Replace preview eyes (VIEW toggles: an export always renders the stored recipe in full). Both share buildStackJob().

prepareExport() calls flushPropagation() + flushAll() FIRST. A develop edit across a multi-image selection is batched (kPropagateMs), and the exporter reads stored stacks, so without the flush an export fired straight after a slider drag would write the pre-edit recipe for every image except the current one.

### 14.2 The Pixel Sources and Their Callers

MW::developPixelSource is the develop provider. It reuses renderDevelopFullResAsync's staging exactly: the GUI thread captures the recipe and the metadata; developRenderPool decodes; the GUI thread runs the mask prerequisites (ensureRangeRef / Subject / Sky / Depth / Object / BrushSam, which are synchronous and keep path-keyed caches the live edit session also uses, so they must not race it); then developRenderPool composites. An image the exporter decoded ITSELF is dropped from WorkingImageCache afterwards, so a long batch does not evict the image the user is editing. Its callers are Develop export, the devPreview builder ([12.1 Original and Developed Previews](#121-original-and-developed-previews)), Embellish export and the focus stacker.

#### 14.2.1 Raw Denoise Is Part of the Base

"Denoise raw" (PMRID) is not a stage in developCompositeStack: it is pre-demosaic, so it changes the WorkingImage the composite starts FROM. The interactive render reaches it through developRawDenoisedBase / ensureRawDenoise, and neither is usable here (both are keyed to the image on screen, and a batch must not disturb the live session's caches). So developPixelSource re-decodes the mosaic with the denoiser on (ImageDecoder::decodeRawWorking) and blends toward the clean base by the stored amounts (Develop::BlendRawDenoise): the same two steps, without the caching. It first checks PmridCache ([11.17.5 One Shared PMRID Base (PmridCache)](#11175-one-shared-pmrid-base-pmridcache)), so exporting the image you are editing does not re-run the model.
