- It is GATED ON THE RECIPE (EditParams::denoiseRaw via wantsDenoiseRaw), not on the amounts: EditParams defaults denoiseLuma to 0.75 and denoiseChroma to 1.0, NON-ZERO, so "amounts > 0" is true for every raw including an unedited one, and testing only that would run PMRID on every image the exporter and the preview builder touch. The flag falls back to G::autoRunDenoise when the image says nothing, so this reads exactly the answer the interactive render reads. It is a global rather than an MW member because Metadata::defaultRenderKey has to hash it from decoder threads.
- Gated on the GUI thread (rawDenoiseAvailable reads session state); the decode goes to developRenderPool.
- Only the COMPOSITE gets the denoised base: orientation and the mask prerequisites stay on the clean one, exactly as renderDevelopFullResAsync splits src from work, so a mask selects the same pixels either way.
- Before this, an image the user had denoised exported clean, and the devPreview builder, which shares this provider, wrote that clean render under a recipe key asserting it matched the loupe.

#### 14.2.2 Every Caller Gets the Sensor Image, in Any Mode

Fixed 2026-10-06. G::useRaw follows the operation mode (MW::setOperationMode turns it off in Preview), so gating the decode on it rendered every independent caller from the EMBEDDED PREVIEW whenever it ran outside Develop: Develop export, the devPreview builder, Embellish export and the focus stacker (an OM-1 ORF came out 3200x2400 instead of 5184x3888).

- developPixelSource now decodes a raw with a sensor decoder from the sensor regardless of mode (ImageDecoder::forceSensorDecode, which ImageDecoder::load honours for independent decodes), and refuses a cached base that is not sceneReferred.
- The one exception is deliberate: useRaw off WHILE IN DEVELOP is the "Edit: Embedded Preview" selector, and the render honours it, except for requireSensor (the focus stacker), which never takes a preview.
- Cost: a devPreview or export started from Browse now pays the full raw decode (\~1 s per image), which is what it always should have paid. devPreviews already built from a preview are not self-healing (their key is the recipe, not the resolution): Develop > Clear Developed Preview Cache rebuilds them.

#### 14.2.3 Embellish Export

Since 2026-10-06 it renders through Develop too. EmbelExport::loadImage used the image-cache copy (the embedded preview of a raw while browsing, and never the develop recipe) or QImage(fPath). MW::exportEmbel and MW::exportEmbelFromAction now give it MW::setEmbelPixelSource -> developPixelSource (8-bit sRGB; pending edits flushed first), and the asynchronous render is one step of the export's event-loop chain (see [6.4.1.4 Embellish Export Runs From the Event Loop](#6414-embellish-export-runs-from-the-event-loop-2026-10-18)). Until 2026-10-18 the cached-image fallback in Embel quietly replaced the render with the image cache's copy whenever there was one. A remote (winnet / Lightroom) Embellish export keeps the old path: its sources are temporary TIFFs that are not in the DataModel. If the develop render fails, the old path is the fallback.

#### 14.2.4 The Focus Stacker

The third caller (2026-09-27). A focus stack is built from each slice's develop rendering, not from the browse decode or the file on disk: the stack should look like what the user sees in Develop.

- MW::generateFocusStack (FocusStack/generateFocusStack.cpp) picks the slices: every raw (and any format OpenCV cannot read), every version, and any other image with a stored recipe (developBlobFor non-empty); an image never developed renders with default settings. An unedited JPEG / TIFF / PNG is still read straight from disk by FSLoader::load, because its file already is its develop render and the direct read keeps a 16-bit TIFF at full depth.
- The choice is PER GROUP, all or nothing, so every slice in a stack has the same bit depth and rendering (fusion takes its output depth from slice 0). Renders are 16-bit sRGB, so the fused TIFF keeps develop precision.
- Previously raw slices went through ImageDecoder::decodeIndependent via MW::matFromQImage: 8-bit, global adjustments only, no masks, spots or geometry; edited JPEGs / TIFFs got no develop at all. That route (FS::requestImage, MW::matFromQImage, FSLoader::load's externalDecoder) was REMOVED 2026-10-05.

The stacker reads only files (2026-10-05). FS::prepareSources (FocusStack/fs.cpp) runs per group before alignment: each develop slice is rendered through FS::developDecoder and written as a 16-bit TIFF to grpFolder/source/NNN\_&lt;name>.tif (encoded on the FS thread, never in the GUI callback); any other slice is its own file. FS::sourcePaths runs parallel to FS::inputPaths: sourcePaths is what FSLoader::load and fusion read; inputPaths stays the identity list for grouping, naming the result and copying its metadata (VersionKey::sourceOf for a version). The source folder is removed with the group's other working folders unless removeTemp is off, which makes it easy to inspect what was actually stacked. The group aborts, naming the file, when a slice fails to develop or the developed slices differ in size (a different crop on one slice).

A raw must render from the SENSOR. The stacker calls developPixelSource with requireSensor = true: for a raw with a sensor decoder (RawFormat::HasSensorDecoder), a base that is not sceneReferred after the decode is a FAILURE, not a reason to build from the embedded preview. Found on an OM-1 stack started in the Library that came out 3200x2400 (the ORF's embedded preview): a half-long-edge guard let a preview-built cache entry through, since an Olympus preview is 62% of the sensor, not under half. The exporter leaves requireSensor off and keeps the preview as a last resort. With G::FSLog on, developPixelSource logs each base's size, sceneReferred and decodedHere, and prepareSources logs each written slice's size and depth.

Threading: the stacker waits for the render on ITS OWN worker thread (FS::developDecoder: a std::promise completed by the render's GUI-thread callback, polled every 100 ms against the abort flag), not through a BlockingQueuedConnection, which would park the GUI thread the render's own staging needs. The abort poll is what keeps Esc and quit (closeEvent aborts, then waits on fsThread) from hanging on a render in flight. Like metaSnapshot, the metadata and EXIF rotation are captured on the GUI thread before the stack starts and handed to developPixelSource (its mSnap / degreesSnap parameters), so the user can leave the folder while it runs; the recipe itself comes from the sidecar via stackJobFor. Memory: the aligned slices are held until fusion, so a 16-bit BGR slice costs 6 bytes/pixel against the 4 of the old 8-bit BGRA decode.

### 14.3 Output

#### 14.3.1 Formats

jpg, png, tif, heic and bmp, resolved at runtime against QImageWriter::supportedImageFormats(), so a missing plugin DROPS the entry rather than failing at save time: HEIC writes on macOS via the bundled qmacheif plugin and is simply absent on a stock Windows build. The table says which controls each format supports (depth, quality, TIFF compression), and the dialog HIDES the rest, caption and control both (ExportDlg::updateEnabledStates). A setting the format does not have is not one that could be switched on, so greying it would only invite the user to look for the switch. (Greying is kept for controls whose row IS live but currently irrelevant: the destination folder field, the sizing spin boxes.) Nothing in the dialog hard-codes a format name.

#### 14.3.2 Destination

Three choices, widest scope first in the dialog: Source folder (beside the originals), Source subfolder (a named subfolder of each image's own folder, created on demand) and Folder (one chosen folder for the whole batch). ExportSettings::Dest numbers them 0 SubfolderOfSource, 1 ChosenFolder, 2 SourceFolder. SourceFolder is APPENDED rather than inserted in reading order because "dest" is a published preset key, and renumbering would silently reinterpret every stored preset.

Overwriting the originals: Source folder + no suffix + no template + a format whose extension matches the source resolves to the source path itself. Only exists == Overwrite actually destroys anything (Unique name and Skip already handle it), so ExportDlg::onExportClicked counts those collisions and requires a confirmation naming the count, defaulting to Cancel.

#### 14.3.3 After the Batch

MW::onExportFinished. Nothing on screen changes unless the export landed in a folder the datamodel has loaded. When it did, "Insert exported images without rescanning the folder" picks HOW they appear: ticked inserts the written files into the open model in place (insertFiles); unticked rescans the folders (refresh). Both show the new files: the checkbox is insert-vs-rescan, not show-vs-hide, which is what its old label ("Add exported images to the folder view") got wrong. The setting key stays addToFolderView.

- The checkbox is DISABLED unless a destination folder is loaded, since it can have no effect otherwise (ImageExporter::willTouchLoadedFolder, re-evaluated on every edit; for a subfolder-of-source destination it tests one folder per distinct SOURCE folder). Its checked state is left alone while disabled, so pointing the export back at an open folder restores the user's choice.
- DataModel::isFolderLoaded is the single definition of "is this folder loaded": the dialog's enable test and onExportFinished's act-on test must not disagree about a folder spelled with a trailing slash. folderSet answers the common case in O(1), with a QDir::cleanPath comparison as the fallback.

#### 14.3.4 16-Bit

OutputTransform::ToImage16 is the 16-bit twin of ToImage: the same tone curve and transfer function, packed to Format_RGBX64. The develop pipeline is float throughout, so the 8-bit pack was the only place precision was lost. The depth is threaded through WorkingImageCache::render / renderStack (OutDepth, defaulting to Eight so every interactive caller is untouched) and developComposite / developCompositeStack. Three later stages had to be taught 16 bits or they would have silently flattened the whole frame:

- Straighten (CropTransform::applyGeometry) converted to ARGB32 for the transparent corner wedges; it now picks RGBA64 for a deep image.
- Warp (rectifyPerspective) round-tripped through 8-bit BGRA OpenCV; it now warps CV_16UC4 when the source is deep, with the opacity cut-off scaled to match.
- Spot heals are 8-bit by nature (LaMa / MI-GAN are 8-bit models, and the clone path works in ARGB32). applySpots() heals an 8-bit COPY and writes back only the pixels that actually CHANGED, promoted 257x. Healed pixels are synthesised, so 8-bit precision there costs nothing, and every untouched pixel keeps its 16 bits.

#### 14.3.5 Colour Space

sRGB, Display P3 or Adobe RGB, chosen in the dialog and carried in the preset (OutputSpace). Every export is TAGGED; exports used to be untagged, which left every viewer guessing. ImageExporter::renderSpace() maps the export layer's published OutputSpace onto OutputTransform::Space (the two enums stay separate because Develop must not depend on Export). The two pixel sources reach the same place from opposite directions:

- Develop: developPixelSource passes the space down through developCompositeStack -> WorkingImageCache::renderStack -> OutputTransform, which ENCODES in it, and tags the finished image with OutputTransform::ColorSpaceOf; save() sees a tag that already matches and writes it untouched. The tag is set at the export boundary, NOT inside the composite: the spot and geometry stages round-trip through OpenCV and fresh QImages, which drop it.
- Preview: File > Save Preview as hands over the plain browse decode, so save() CONVERTS it to the target with Qt (an untagged decode is taken as sRGB, which is what untagged means in practice). Qt's conversion was verified to work in place for RGB888, RGBX64, ARGB32 and RGB32.

Wide-gamut output at 8 bits can band in smooth gradients; the dialog's tooltip says so and points at 16-bit.

#### 14.3.6 Metadata Copy: Two Traps

- ICC: copySourceMetadata used to copy the source's ICC profile onto the export. A raw's profile describes the CAMERA space and a JPEG's what it was shot in, neither of which survives the develop pipeline, and with a selectable output space it would flatly mislabel the file. The copy now excludes it (ExifTool::copyAllTags gained excludeIcc, which adds --icc_profile:all, rather than trusting -all:all's block-tag behaviour); the profile the writer embedded is the one that describes the pixels.
- Orientation (fixed 2026-10-11): the tag copy also brought the source's Orientation, but every pixel source hands the exporter UPRIGHT pixels (a raw is rotated inside the develop render, a non-raw comes from the already-rotated decode, and Save Preview's Pixmap::load applies the orientation itself). A portrait OM-1 raw therefore exported as a portrait 16-bit TIFF still tagged Orientation 8, and any reader that honours the tag rotated it a second time (OpenCV refused to open it at all). copySourceMetadata now passes upright = true to ExifTool::copyAllTags, which adds -orientation#=1 to the COPY command itself (an assignment there overrides the copied value, and it also updates an existing XMP tiff:Orientation, verified); EmbelExport::exportImages does the same. It MUST be the same write: the first version issued writeOrientation as a separate command afterwards, and ExifTool refused it on an OM-1 export because the MakerNote the copy had just brought over contains sub-IFDs it cannot parse ("MakerNotes tag 0x2010 IFD format not handled", a minor error, and minor errors block a rewrite without -m). The same trap awaits any later single-tag ExifTool write to such a file. Image/stack.cpp still copies the first source's tags unchanged (not audited). Lightroom's own exports carry no Orientation tag.

### 14.4 The Export Dialog

#### 14.4.1 Fixed Size and Layout

The dialog is not resizable: ExportDlg::fitToContents pins it to the design width (kDialogWidth, 820) and to whatever height the layout asks for. The fields are sized to their content rather than their grid column (template 290, suffix 165, Type and Space 130, since they hold "Display P3", Depth and Compression 100), so a wider window would show nothing more and a taller one would pool space under the last section. fitToContents re-runs only when setBusy adds or removes the progress bar: changing FORMAT never changes the height.

- Every hideable control shares a row with one that never hides (Depth and Quality with Type, Compression with Space), so no row can empty out and leave a gap, and the group is the same height for every format. Both caption COLUMNS keep the width measured at build time, so nothing shifts sideways as the format changes.
- Quality sits on the Type row in the same cells as Depth, because no format has both: quality belongs to the lossy formats (JPEG, HEIC), depth to the lossless ones (PNG, TIFF). The slider gets the width Depth's combo would have wasted (it runs through the slack column, with its value at the right edge). A 16-bit lossy format would draw them on top of each other and need its own row back.
- The Name and Format grids are two layouts in two group boxes, so buildUi lines them up by hand: same margins, same column gap, both caption columns pinned to the widest caption in EITHER grid, each field column pinned to its own field, and the captions RIGHT-aligned so each sits hard against the control it names.

Which column takes the slack is the part that is easy to get wrong, and it must not be one of the four. Stretch on the FIELD columns does not work, because the fields are fixed-width: a stretchy field column cannot use its space, and QGridLayout passes the leftover to whatever can grow, i.e. the caption columns. The two grids have different field widths (290 + 165 vs 130 + 100), so their leftovers differed and their caption columns came out different widths. Stretching the middle caption column fails the other way, opening a chasm between the pairs. So the slack sits in a FIFTH, empty column past the last field:

- Columns 0-3 hold their pinned widths: column 0 is shared, so Type and Space start on the same x as Template, and each second pair follows its OWN first field (Suffix after the 290 px template combo; Depth and Compression after the 130 px type combo plus a 50 px gap, kFormatPairGap, added to that grid's caption column).
- The rows meant to use the whole width (the exists radios, and the example + Template editor button) span into the slack column.
- The Format group's two checkboxes are in the grid too, on the field column, so they line up with the combos; they go in AFTER the row-height pass, so they keep their natural height.
- The Size group has no captions and borrows the same geometry: a column 0 of the caption width, held open by a stand-in WIDGET, not by a column minimum alone (QGridLayout only puts its column spacing between columns that hold something, so a merely-wide column 0 starts column 1 a whole gap left of the other groups).

Two measurement rules make that arithmetic safe. The captions are ensurePolished() BEFORE being measured (a size hint is not final until the style and stylesheet are applied, which otherwise happens on the first layout pass). And every caption is then FIXED at the measured width rather than the column merely floored at it, so column 0 is exactly capW0 in every grid. A fixed-width label no longer fills its cell, and an item that cannot fill its cell sits at the LEFT of it, so the caption ITEMS are aligned right as well.

#### 14.4.2 Watch the Global Stylesheet

G::css sets "min-width: 6em" on every QComboBox and "min-width: 100px" on every QPushButton (Main/widgetcss.cpp), and Qt applies a stylesheet min-width by writing it onto the widget's minimumWidth when the widget is POLISHED. That write ALWAYS LANDS LAST (after setFixedWidth in buildUi, and after an ensurePolished() meant to get ahead of it: tried, it does not work), so an unguarded control silently takes the global width: \~130 px for a combo, 112 for a button (100 content + 5+5 padding + 1+1 border, since a stylesheet width is the CONTENT box).

A per-widget sheet is the only thing the re-polish cannot overrule, because it is what the re-polish applies. Two shapes, both in use here:

- Say the width IN the sheet, min-width AND max-width, converted to content units (sizeButton, minus kButtonChrome). Works anywhere; the cost is that kButtonChrome has to agree with widgetcss.cpp's QPushButton padding and border.
- Clear the floor with "min-width: 0px" and let a pinned GRID COLUMN supply the width, the control being Expanding with setFixedWidth as its cap (the Format combos). A maximum is safe; the global rules set no max-width.

Clearing the floor WITHOUT something to hold the control open leaves it at its own text width: that is how the preset buttons came out New 41 px, Update 55, Rename 65, Delete 52, all asked for 75.

#### 14.4.3 Sections and the Preset Bar

Formatted like IngestDlg: QGroupBox sections whose title is two points up on the body text, and 32 px-high buttons. ExportDlg::addSection makes the box, so every section (Preset included) is dressed the same way. The group-box title font is set on the BOX, and a widget's font propagates to its children, so addSection puts the controls in an inner widget whose font is reset to the dialog's; otherwise every control inherits the enlarged title size. (A compact alternative formatting was carried behind G::useExportDlgIngestStyle to compare; the Ingest style won and the flag was deleted 2026-08-07.)

The preset bar is ONE row: the combo and New / Update / Rename / Delete, with the combo Expanding so the preset NAME takes whatever the buttons and the "modified" label leave. It keeps its selection while you edit:

- Changing a setting marks the preset "modified" (the label beside the combo) and ENABLES Update, which writes the form back to the still-selected preset; Update is disabled while the form matches.
- The combo must NOT be reset to "(none)" on an edit: it is the only record of which preset Update targets, and you can only want Update after editing.
- Rename and Delete act on the STORED preset, so they stay enabled whether or not the form has been edited, and a Rename leaves an edited form still modified.

#### 14.4.4 Export Presets Are Complete

Unlike develop presets. A develop preset is partial on purpose (an absent key means "don't touch that adjustment"); an export preset is a whole ExportSettings INCLUDING the destination, which is what lets Develop > Export with preset > &lt;name> run with no dialog at all. An absent key falls back to the ExportSettings default, so an old preset survives a new field. The same versioning contract as develop presets applies: add keys freely, never rename or rescale one in place ([11.39 Stale Presets and History (Schema Drift)](#1139-stale-presets-and-history-schema-drift)).

#### 14.4.5 File Naming: One Token Parser, One Template Editor

{TOKEN} filename templates were parsed by two identical private copies (IngestDlg::parseTokenString and RenameFileDlg::parseTokenString); adding a third for Export would have been three. The language now lives in Utilities/tokenfilename.h (one ordered table driving the token list, the example map and the parser), and Ingest and Rename delegate to it, so a token added there appears in all three at once.

The template editor is likewise the one editor (Dialogs/tokendlg.h). File naming's Template editor button, right of the Example row, opens TokenDlg on MW::filenameTemplates, the same map Ingest and Rename edit, held by REFERENCE and persisted by MW, so a template created while exporting is offered by the other two immediately (which is why ExportDlg takes it non-const).

- Afterwards the combo is rebuilt and lands back on the template it was on: by key, then (a RENAME moves the key while the token string stays put) by token string, then the first template there is, where a DELETED one has to end up. The rebuild is signal-blocked (it is not a user edit), so the preset is marked modified only when the token string the export would use has changed.
- The combo lists EXACTLY the templates, in the editor's order. It offers no synthetic "no template" entry: keeping the original name IS a template ("{ORIGINAL FILENAME}"). The entry ExportDlg used to prepend, "Original file name", sat one space away from the real "Original filename" template. Like the other two dialogs, ExportDlg seeds the map with the stock pair if it is empty.
- ExportSettings::tokenTemplate may still be EMPTY: it is a published preset key, older presets hold it, and the engine reads it as "keep the original base name". Loading one selects the template that keeps the original name, or the first one.

## 15 Colour Management

Embedded profiles in browsed images. The Develop pipeline's own colour architecture (input profile, working space, view transforms) is under [11 Develop](#11-develop) and [11.6 Camera Profiles (DCP)](#116-camera-profiles-dcp).

### 15.1 HEIC and the colr Box

HEIC stores its colour space in a `colr` BOX inside the item properties (meta > iprp > ipco), not in a JPEG-style APP2 segment, which is why the segment-based ICC read copied from the JPEG parser could never have worked for HEIC (it sat commented out in Heic.cpp). Heic::colrBox already PARSED the box, but did all of it inside `if (isDebug)` and stored nothing, and "heic" / "hif" were missing from Metadata::iccFormats, so HEIC opted out of colour management entirely.

The symptom was iPhone photos rendering visibly UNDERSATURATED in ordinary browsing, not just in Develop: iPhone HEICs are Display P3, iccBuf stayed null, and "null means sRGB" applied. Verified against a real file: IMG_0375.HEIC carries colour_type 'prof' with a 548-byte ICC whose description is literally "Display P3".

Two forms, per ISO 23008-12:

- `prof` / `rICC` is a full ICC profile, taken verbatim. Its payload is length-12: the 8-byte box header plus the 4-byte colour_type (the old debug code read length-8 and would have over-read by four; the profile's own internal size field confirms 12).
- `nclx` is numeric ITU-T H.273 codes with no profile attached, so one is synthesised from QColorSpace rather than hand-built with lcms. Primaries 11 or 12 with an SDR transfer (1 or 13) gives Display P3; primaries 1 is sRGB and stores NOTHING, since null already means sRGB and keeping the bytes would put a redundant profile on every datamodel row (the same reasoning as the JPEG reader).

SDR only, deliberately: PQ (transfer 16) and HLG (18) are HDR and need tone mapping to an SDR display. Treating their code values as SDR would be far worse than the status quo, so they fall through untouched (still assumed sRGB) and remain separate work.

The chain from here is generic: Heic::colrBox fills m->iccBuf, DataModel writes it to G::ICCBufColumn, and ImageDecoder::colorManage reads it back (gated on Metadata::iccFormats, which the missing "heic" / "hif" entries had defeated). (An unrelated quirk: "hif" is listed in noMetadataFormats, but that list only feeds a display string in Views/infostring.cpp and does not gate parsing.)

## 16 Keywords

### 16.1 Reading Keywords (dc:subject and lr:hierarchicalSubject)

Two XMP properties carry keywords: dc:subject, the flat list of leaf names every application writes, and lr:hierarchicalSubject, Lightroom's parallel list of full keyword paths with '|' separators, e.g. "Location|Canada|BC|Vancouver Island".

Winnow used to lose almost every keyword it was shown. It read dc:subject in exactly two places (Jpeg::parse and PNG::parse) and lr:hierarchicalSubject nowhere at all (it was not even in Xmp::definedElements, so getItemList would have refused the name). The consequence was worst for RAW, which is most of a photographer's library: Nikon, Canon CR2, DNG, TIFF and Panasonic all built a valid Xmp from IFD tag 700 and read rating, label, title and creator out of it, then simply did not ask for the keywords. And Metadata::parseSidecar is the ONLY route by which a raw file's keywords can arrive at all (Lightroom does not write into a NEF, CR2, CR3 or ARW; it writes a .xmp beside it), and parseSidecar skipped dc:subject. A raw library keyworded over years showed an empty Filters > Keywords category, with nothing hinting why.

- ONE DEFINITION, in Metadata/xmpapply.h. The seven parsers each carried a byte-identical twelve-line copy of the same XMP block, which is how they came to disagree: the keyword line was added to the JPEG copies and to no others. applyXmp() is that block, once, and each parser calls it, so the next field added arrives everywhere at once.
- It is a FREE FUNCTION in its own header, not a Metadata member, because Metadata/metadata.h includes every parser header: a parser including it back would compile only while its own header happened to be first, and would drag QtWidgets into seven more translation units. xmpapply.h depends only on xmp.h and imagemetadata.h (the same reasoning as Cache/pathkey.h).
- PNG deliberately keeps its own copy. It guards several fields on isEmpty() and mirrors the exif: / tiff: namespaces into the camera fields, because Lightroom and Photoshop drop the eXIf chunk when they write a PNG and put the camera data in the XMP instead.
- The sidecar read is NOT guarded on isEmpty(), unlike the scalars beside it. An empty keyword list in a sidecar that is otherwise newer means the keywords were REMOVED, and honouring that is the point of parseSidecar's newer-wins rule. Guarding it would make keyword deletion impossible to sync.

#### 16.1.1 Three Columns

- G::KeywordsColumn holds the LITERAL dc:subject list, and G::KeywordPathsColumn the lr:hierarchicalSubject paths; both are folded into G::SearchTextColumn.
- G::KeywordsAllColumn holds what Winnow actually filters and searches on: every path the image carries plus every ANCESTOR PREFIX of each, so "Location|Canada|BC" contributes "Location", "Location|Canada" and the whole path. Metadata/keywordpaths.h is the one definition (keywordEffectivePaths, then keywordPrefixExpand), shared by the datamodel and the index, because if the two split a path differently the category and the search would disagree about the same picture.
- All three are appended before TotalColumns and marked GeekRole, like DevelopColumn and DevPreviewKeyColumn, because saved table column widths are keyed by index.

KeywordsColumn deliberately keeps the LITERAL list rather than being replaced by the flattened one, and DataModel::imMetadata still reads it. The two are different facts and only one may ever be written back: emitting the flattened column as dc:subject would put every ancestor into a property that never held them. dc:subject is written from KeywordsColumn and lr:hierarchicalSubject from KeywordPathsColumn, never from KeywordsAllColumn.

### 16.2 Keyword Identity Is the Full Path

Catalog schema 10, reversing schema 4. The flat model keyed a keyword on its bare leaf name; its three arguments are answered:

- The Lightroom double (the same tag written twice, leaf into dc:subject and path into lr:hierarchicalSubject) is resolved by LEAF CONSUMPTION: keywordEffectivePaths drops a dc:subject entry whose name matches the leaf of one of the SAME image's paths, because the path is the richer statement of the same fact. It never becomes two keywords with a split count.
- The hierarchy not being universal is not a problem: a flat list is a tree of depth one, so a phone image or an IPTC-only file simply produces root nodes.
- Ancestor search is still free, through prefix expansion.

What flat identity cost, and why it was reversed: a name used under two parents ("Location|Canada|BC|Vancouver" and "Location|USA|Washington|Vancouver") became ONE keyword meaning two places, with the counts merged and nothing able to tell them apart. A real vocabulary of 3,975 Lightroom keywords had 59 names under more than one parent, including a Bear Lake in BC and another in Colorado. Rendering a flat index as a tree also gave wrong parent counts in a MIXED library (a phone image tagged flat "Heron" sits under Heron but carries no "Fauna", so Fauna's count silently excluded it), and a write-back would have re-parented files to match our vocabulary rather than their own.

Ambiguity marking is gone, with the machinery that served it (keyword_context, Catalog::ambiguousKeywords(), G::AmbiguousKeywordRole, Filters::refreshAmbiguousKeywords and the amber colouring in both docks): the two Vancouvers are now two rows with two counts. Filter EXCLUSION stays, because subtracting a BRANCH ("everything under Location except the American one") is a question a tree raises rather than answers ([18.9 Filter Exclusion (Include This, Not That)](#189-filter-exclusion-include-this-not-that)).

Nested wins on display too (2026-10-09). When a file carries both flat and nested keywords, only the nested ones are shown, plus any flat keyword that no path names. The Info panel's Keywords row, the Table view's Keywords column (KeywordsItemDelegate::initStyleOption) and that column's tooltip (DataModel::data, ToolTipRole) all show keywordEffectivePaths(KeywordsColumn, KeywordPathsColumn), the same set Filters, search and the catalog use. The column still stores the literal list, and sorting that column still sorts on it.

### 16.3 Writing Keywords

#### 16.3.1 The List Writer

Xmp::setItemList writes a List property (dc:subject or lr:hierarchicalSubject) as an rdf:Bag of rdf:li, the shape Lightroom writes and Xmp::getItemList reads. It takes a QStringList rather than the QByteArray setItem takes, because keyword text is the user's (accents, CJK, dashes) and every setItem caller reaches it through toLatin1(), which would mangle all three.

- AN EMPTY LIST REMOVES THE PROPERTY rather than writing an empty Bag: parseSidecar reads keywords unguarded precisely so that clearing every keyword syncs, and a present-but-empty Bag would defeat that.
- Nothing escapes & or &lt; anywhere in Xmp, and nothing needs to: docToQString prints through rapidxml::print, whose copy_and_expand_chars expands them, and parse&lt;0> translates them back on read. That is a property of the PRINTER, so tst_xmpkeywords pins it.
- setItem now REFUSES a list property, a bug fix rather than tidiness. setItem removes the existing element before deciding what to write and has only an Attribute branch and a Node branch, so setItem("subject", ...) deleted every keyword in the file and put nothing back, silently, leaving a valid document. The guard returns false BEFORE the removal.

A bug the first keyword write found, unrelated to keywords: Xmp's backing stores a (names) and v (values) were read as a PAIR, every writer appending one of each and then indexing BOTH with "a.count() - 1". setItemList broke that unwritten invariant (one property write appends three names, the property, rdf:Bag and rdf:li, and N values), so the NEXT writer's a.count()-1 indexed v out of range and the app ABORTED on a QList assert. Nothing indexes those lists by position any more: keepName / keepValue return the pointer directly and are the only things that may append.

#### 16.3.2 What a Keyword Edit Writes

Metadata::writeXMP emits BOTH properties whenever EITHER has changed, because they are one fact in two places and writing half leaves a file that contradicts itself.

- dc:subject gets the LEAF of every assigned path, de-duplicated (two keywords can share a leaf, and "Vancouver" twice is a duplicate tag anywhere else the file is opened).
- lr:hierarchicalSubject gets every assigned path of depth 2 or more, whole.
- A depth-1 path goes to dc:subject ONLY: it carries no hierarchy, and it is what an application that has never heard of lr: writes.

Reading that back is IDEMPOTENT, the property the whole scheme rests on: keywordEffectivePaths consumes exactly the dc:subject leaves that match a path's leaf (precisely the set that was emitted), leaving the depth-1 entries as roots, so the assigned set is reconstructed exactly and a second write of an unchanged image is a no-op. tests/unit/tst_keywordwrite.cpp pins the round trip, the byte-identical rewrite, the two-Vancouvers case and the clearing case.

The change detection is ORDER-INSENSITIVE AND CASE-FOLDED, and has to be: applyXmp reads the two properties in FILE order and the writer emits them sorted, so a plain list compare would report a change on every Lightroom-written file, and since writeXMP writes every changed field in one pass, a RATING edit would then silently rewrite the user's keyword block on files Winnow was never asked to retag.

The shadows are not columns. Every other edited field carries one (G::\_RatingColumn beside G::RatingColumn); ImageMetadata::\_keywords and \_keywordPaths are filled by DataModel::imMetadata from the model's own values instead, because two more QStringList columns at 250k rows is real memory spent to re-derive what the model already holds. THE PRICE IS AN ORDERING RULE: a keyword edit writes the FILE first and the MODEL second, the opposite of MW::setRating. Updating the model first would make the shadow equal the new value, and writeXMP would conclude nothing had changed and write nothing, silently. It is stated at both ends (Main/keywordedit.cpp and the assignment in DataModel::imMetadata), because anyone "making it consistent with setRating" breaks keyword writing without breaking a build. Where the edit lands (the file or the sidecar) follows [9.4 Writing Metadata Into Image Files](#94-writing-metadata-into-image-files).

#### 16.3.3 The Batch: MW::applyKeywordsToSelection

Modelled on MW::setRating:

- Snapshot the selection rows BEFORE touching the model (the proxy re-filters underneath an iteration otherwise).
- Add and remove in ONE pass (re-parenting is both, and two passes would write every sidecar twice); skip a row whose set is unchanged; mirror onto the hidden half of a raw+jpg pair.
- Call MW::updateCatalogForRow per row (scope-gated, so an edit cannot put an out-of-scope image into the index).
- Only then suspend the proxy, rebuild the Keywords category through BuildFilters::KeywordEdit, and let filterChange lift the suspension.
- REMOVING A PATH REMOVES ITS SUBTREE: taking "Fauna|Bird" off an image cannot leave "Fauna|Bird|Heron" naming a parent the image no longer claims. keywordIsDescendant is shared with the vocabulary tree's drop rejection, so the two cannot disagree about what "beneath" means.
- An edit with a version row selected is retargeted to its master's file ([13.7.2 Shared Fields Are the File's](#1372-shared-fields-are-the-files)).

BuildFilters::KeywordEdit has NO SNAPSHOT SLOT. Keywords are the one category counted from a row's LIST rather than a single column, so the handler appends its own ops from countKeywords instead of going through countSlot; and Filters::updateKeywordItems REBUILDS the tree rather than patching it, preserving check and EXPANSION state by path. Patching a tree means removing a node whose children may still be wanted, re-parenting what is left and pruning emptied branches: three chances to leave it malformed, on a path that runs after every keyword edit, to save rebuilding a few thousand nodes.

#### 16.3.4 Writing an Image That Is Not Loaded

Metadata::writeKeywordsToSidecar exists for the retag (below) and is deliberately narrower than writeXMP. writeXMP decides what to write by comparing the shared ImageMetadata against its shadows, so it can only be used for an image the datamodel has loaded; reconstructing a whole ImageMetadata for each unloaded image, to write two properties, would mean getting every OTHER field right as well. This opens the sidecar and replaces the two keyword properties in place, leaving every other property exactly as found, because rapidxml re-serialises the document it parsed.

tests/unit/tst_xmpkeywords.cpp pins it all: both properties off a Lightroom-shaped fixture; an absent-keyword document staying quiet; applyXmp filling both lists and still taking the underscore snapshot writeXMP needs; and on the write side an rdf:Bag that survives a re-parse in order, ampersands and CJK round-tripping, an empty list removing the property while leaving the other alone, setItem refusing a list property WITHOUT having eaten the Bag first, an attribute-form dc:subject being replaced rather than duplicated, and lr: being declared when the hierarchy is written into a file that never had it.

### 16.4 The Vocabulary (the Keyword List)

The vocabulary is a second table and a second model (Datamodel/keywordvocab.h). The index's keyword table (Cache/catalog.cpp) is OBSERVED: rows appear as a side effect of indexing and cascade away with their images, keyed on pathfold. vocab is AUTHORED: rows are user intent, only an explicit delete removes one, it holds branches no image uses yet, and its identity is an id that SURVIVES a rename, which it must, because a node's synonyms and export flag attach to the node rather than its spelling.

- They join on pathfold: a vocab row with no keyword match is an empty branch; a keyword row with no vocab match is a tag found in a file the user has not filed ("unfiled", drawn red).
- KeywordVocab loads the whole tree in memory on the GUI thread (thousands of nodes, not the 250k the datamodel is sized for), and every mutator writes SQL and the tree together, so the two cannot drift within a session.
- The table lives in userdata.db (Datamodel/userdb.h), NOT the index, because it is user-authored ([17.5.8 The Store Is Not index.db](#1758-the-store-is-not-indexdb)), so the join with the observed keyword table is made in memory (Catalog::keywords() against KeywordVocab's byPathFold), never in SQL.
- Rename and re-parent rewrite every DESCENDANT's path in one pass, the other half of why the id is the identity.
- Measured against a real 43,070-image index: 1,971 nodes, 528 roots, 8 levels deep, loaded in 47 ms. Its completer offers FOUR different "Vancouver Island" keywords, carrying 509, 2, 1,223 and 6,163 images, which flat identity merged into one entry with a summed count.
- Every vocabulary mutation is a full model reset, which invalidates every QModelIndex taken before it ([16.13.3 Six Gotchas Found Reviewing the Keyword Path](#16133-six-gotchas-found-reviewing-the-keyword-path)).

#### 16.4.1 Rename and Re-Parent Ask Before Touching a File

The model changes the vocabulary immediately and emits pathChanged. MW::keywordPathChanged counts what each scope would rewrite (Catalog::imagesUnderKeyword, the ONLY prefix range in the codebase, since a subtree COUNT is the one keyword question plain equality cannot answer), and Dialogs/keywordretagdlg offers This folder (N) / Everywhere (M) / Not now, with Not now as the default so a user who has stopped reading takes the safe branch.

- Declining needs no pending-work table: those images keep a path that matches no node, and the dock shows them as unfiled, visible in the panel the user is already looking at.
- The dialog says the rename has ALREADY happened, because the obvious misreading of a confirmation is that cancelling undoes it.

The retag executes from the CATALOG rather than the model (MW::retagKeywordPath), because a rename near the root reaches folders the datamodel has never loaded. Catalog::searchRows on the old path returns every affected image with the two verbatim keyword lists it was indexed with, and needs no subtree walk (every image is linked to every ancestor prefix, so equality already reaches everything beneath).

- A descendant is rewritten AT ITS PREFIX and keeps its tail: renaming "Fauna|Bird" to "Fauna|Birds" turns "Fauna|Bird|Heron" into "Fauna|Birds|Heron", using mid() rather than replace(), because a path can contain the old text further along.
- A loaded row is updated in the model as well as on disk, or the panel would show the old keyword until the folder was reopened; an unloaded one is written with writeKeywordsToSidecar and has its index row committed from what was just written.
- Delete keyword uses the same pass to REMOVE. KeywordTree::deleteSelected offers Cancel (default) / Remove from list / Remove everywhere, plus a "Remove all children" checkbox (unchecked) when the node has children. Checked, or no children: KeywordVocab::remove (cascade) and, for Remove everywhere, MW::removeKeywordEverywhere runs retagKeywordPath in RetagMode::Remove, which drops the path and its subtree from every catalogued image. Unchecked: the node STAYS in the list (it is still its children's parent, and a branch cannot leave a tree its children stay in), so Remove from list is disabled while the box is off and the dialog says why; Remove everywhere runs RetagMode::RemoveOwn, which drops only images' own exact path and keeps everything beneath it. A redundant "People" beside "People|Harry" is not a case for it: the read path already prunes it (next bullet). Remove everywhere is disabled when the node's count is 0, since the catalog-driven pass would find nothing (the dialog says so inline).
- REDUNDANT ANCESTORS ARE PRUNED ON READ (2026-10-19). keywordEffectivePaths ends with keywordPruneAncestors, so an image whose lr:hierarchicalSubject lists "People" beside "People|Harry" carries ONE keyword everywhere (tag zone, info/table views, flat-keyword scan, audit, applied marking). This reverses the earlier rule that only Tidy keywords pruned and reading kept what the file said. Nothing downstream of the catalog changes: everything indexed is keywordPrefixExpand of the effective paths, which puts "People" back as an ancestor, so links, counts and filters are identical and no data repair was needed. The writers (applyKeywordsToSelection, retagKeywordPath) prune their result too, so Winnow's next write of an image drops the redundant entry from the file, and adding an ancestor of a keyword the image already carries is a no-op that rewrites nothing.

#### 16.4.2 Import and Export: The Lightroom Keyword Files

There are TWO formats, both taken from REAL exports rather than documentation, and reading only one was a bug: for a year the reader accepted only the CSV, so importing the .txt every Lightroom user actually has added NOTHING and reported success.

- The five-column CSV: Include On Export, Export Containing Keywords, Export Synonyms, Person Type Keyword, then the keyword. UTF-8 with a BOM, with THE HIERARCHY AS TAB INDENTATION INSIDE THE LAST FIELD; ordinary CSV quoting applies, so "Vancouver, BC" arrives as one field. Verified against a 3,975-keyword export (tests/fixtures/lightroom_keywords.csv is a trimmed copy preserving every shape).
- The PLAIN INDENTED .TXT that "Metadata > Export Keywords" writes: one keyword per line, no columns, no quoting, no BOM; the hierarchy IS the indentation. Verified against a 4,050-line export (tests/fixtures/lightroom_keywords.txt), which parses to 4,022 keywords, 28 synonyms and 7 levels.

The format is SNIFFED, not taken from the extension (a CSV export saved as .txt exists, and the indented export is a .txt with no columns). The first record decides: five or more fields whose first four are each blank, Y or N is the CSV; anything else is indented text. The FLAG COLUMNS decide rather than the field count, because a plain-text keyword may contain commas, and a row of five comma-separated words would otherwise be read as a CSV row and silently truncated.

Depth is counted from the indent, row by row, and lrPaths turns depths into paths with an ancestor stack: a deeper row pushes, a shallower row pops back to its own level however many levels that is. Both readers hand it the same depth and neither builds a path itself. The failure that guards against is silent: a reader that pops one level per row files the root following a four-deep branch as a leaf of it, and the rest of the file inherits the mistake. Tabs are the indent; a file indented with SPACES is read too, with the unit inferred as the file's SMALLEST indent (depth cannot be read off one row: "    Animal" is depth 1 in a four-space file and depth 2 in a two-space one).

- A SYNONYM is a row whose keyword is in {braces}, one level deeper than the keyword it belongs to; in the CSV its four flag columns are also BLANK. It attaches to the nearest preceding NON-SYNONYM row at depth minus one, which is not "the previous row": consecutive synonyms share a parent. The brace rule and the flag defaults live in ONE shared appender (lrAppendRow).
- What is not verified is treated as unknown: square brackets are widely said to mark a keyword that is not exported, and there is not one bracket in 3,975 rows, nor a single "N" in Include On Export. A bracketed name is read as a name. A flag that IS present is honoured.

Import MERGES, never replaces. A branch built here that the file has never heard of survives; a path that already exists is left exactly as it is, synonyms included. Matching is by FOLDED PATH, so re-importing after a small edit in Lightroom adds the few new keywords and touches nothing else (measured: 1,971 nodes plus a 3,975-keyword export gave 2,781 additions in 342 ms, and a second import added NOTHING). Synonyms are applied only to nodes the import created. A path that could not be created is REPORTED rather than rounded up to success. Export sorts by folded path, which is also depth-first order (a path is a prefix of its children), and writes through a QSaveFile so a failure cannot leave a truncated vocabulary behind.

### 16.5 The Keywords Dock

Views/keywordtree.h, Views/keywordtags.cpp. Two zones by design: the TAG ZONE on top, for the keywords on the current selection, and the vocabulary TREE (the "Keyword list") below it with its own Find field, because curating the keyword LIST and tagging PHOTOGRAPHS are different jobs with different consequences.

- Each zone carries a header band ("Selected image tags" / "Selected images tags", tracking the count, and "Keyword list"), drawn by Utilities/gradientheader.h. The tag zone sits ABOVE the tree because it is what the user reads on every selection change; the Find field travels with the tree, so a search box never appears to be searching the tags.
- The split between the zones persists: the two sit in a vertical QSplitter (MW::createKeywordsDock), its state written to "KeywordsDockSplitter" on every splitterMoved (not at quit, so a crash or a Dock/logout quit cannot lose it) and restored over the default 120/420 split.
- The dock ships OFF, like the Catalog panel: the left group is already four tabs deep. Window > Keywords Panel turns it on. It has NO SHORTCUT (F3-F9 are taken by the other docks and F10-F12 are spoken for). Adding it bumped winnowStateVersion 4 -> 5 with a MW::placeDocksAddedSince row, and followed the full dock checklist, glyph included (images/icon16/keywords_white.png, a luggage tag).
- Entering the Keywords workflow focuses the Keywords filters: switching to Keywords (K, the status-bar switcher, a workspace menu, all via MW::invokeWorkflowLayout) or launching into it calls MW::focusKeywordsFilters, which a tick later runs Filters::focusKeywordsCategory (collapse every category, expand Keywords and its group heading, scroll it to the TOP). A launch also sets focusKeywordsFiltersAfterBuild, so MW::filterBuildCompleted does it once more when the first build fills the category.

#### 16.5.1 The Keyword List (Tree)

The tree has NO CHECKBOXES and never tags anything on its own: reorganising a vocabulary is cheap and reversible, retagging a thousand files is neither, and a checkbox that did both would put every reorganising gesture one mis-click from a mass edit. A keyword the current image carries is drawn in DULL YELLOW (G::appliedKeywordColor, via AppliedKeywordDelegate): a hint, not a control. Double-click, Enter or the context menu ADDS a keyword to the selected images. Keywords are CREATED in the Keyword list and nowhere else.

Drag and drop is all at the VIEW, not the model: two different things can be dropped on the tree (a keyword node, to re-parent it; a set of images, to tag them), and only the first is the model's business. A dragged keyword carries its PATH rather than its row or id, because a row is meaningless once the tree re-sorts.

- The model still has to ADVERTISE the drag, and forgetting that is why keyword dragging did nothing for its first release. QAbstractItemView never CALLS startDrag unless the pressed index carries Qt::ItemIsDragEnabled, and the default QAbstractItemModel::flags() returns Selectable|Enabled only (measured: a QTreeView with setDragEnabled(true) over a model whose flags lack the bit starts 0 drags). KeywordVocab::flags() supplies Drag|Drop on a node, and Drop alone on the INVALID root: dropping on blank space below the tree is the only gesture that moves a keyword back to the top level.
- The REJECTION happens in dragMoveEvent, not at the drop: a drop that silently does nothing reads as a broken widget, and dragging a parent onto its own child, the case users actually hit, is exactly the one that must be refused. keywordIsDescendant decides.
- IMAGES dropped on a keyword are tagged by SELECTING them and calling MW::applyKeywordsToSelection, then restoring the previous selection. Indirect, deliberately: the whole edit path lives in that one function, and a second implementation taking a path list would be a second place for the pairing and ordering rule to be got wrong. With keywords CHECKED in Filters > Keywords the same drop becomes a MOVE ([16.8 Filing Keywords by Drag (Filters Beside the Keyword List)](#168-filing-keywords-by-drag-filters-beside-the-keyword-list)).

#### 16.5.2 The Tag Zone

The only place a keyword goes onto a photograph by typing or clicking. One tag per keyword the SELECTION carries, marked by what it is:

- Plain: every selected image has it.
- "\*": only some have it; right-click > "Add to all selected images" promotes it to all, while the x removes it from all. Without the marker a tag would be a lie the moment more than one image is selected. (Promoting used to be the click; it moved to the menu because it WRITES FILES, and a click that only meant "where is this?" must not rewrite a hundred sidecars.)
- RED (G::unfiledKeywordColor): the keyword is on the image but NOT in the vocabulary (written by another application, or left behind when a rename was declined).

The tags read the ASSIGNED paths, never the expansion: MW::keywordsInSelection builds them from KeywordsColumn and KeywordPathsColumn through keywordEffectivePaths, not from KeywordsAllColumn, which would put a "Fauna" tag on an image tagged only "Fauna|Bird|Heron" (and removing that tag would have no good meaning).

What a tag is called: the rule is about STABILITY before brevity.

- An UNFILED (red) tag shows its whole path: it is the tag the user is deciding about, and "Buoy|Thing" drawn as "Thing" is a different keyword.
- A FILED tag shows its leaf: the user put it where it is ("Category|Aspect|16x10" is "16x10" to the person who filed it).
- The label depends only on the tag, never on its neighbours, and that took two attempts: a version that showed a full path only where two leaves COLLIDED in the selection relabelled "Buoy|Thing" back to "Thing" when "Dinghy|Thing" was deleted, and the user went looking for a chip that had been on screen the whole time under another name.
- The one exception is two FILED tags sharing a leaf (the two Vancouvers): there the collision rule survives, instability and all, because the alternative is two identical chips each carrying a destructive x.

The tag zone follows the SELECTION SET, not only the current index. refreshKeywordsDock was called from MW::fileSelectionChange alone, which fires when the CURRENT image changes, and extending a selection does not change it. So Select All left the zone showing one image's tags, and a keyword every selected image carried had no chip to remove. It is now also connected to QItemSelectionModel::selectionChanged, COALESCED on a 50 ms timer (a rubber band emits per row it crosses, and a rebuild is up to sixty QFrames): KeywordTags::rebuild caps the tags, and MW::scheduleKeywordsDockRefresh caps the rebuilds.

#### 16.5.3 Clicking a Keyword Filters on It

Clicking a white tag, or single-clicking a keyword in the Keyword list, runs MW::filterOnKeyword: every other filter is cleared (uncheckAllFilters, the pick / rating / colour actions, the search text), the keyword's Filters item is included and scrolled into view (Filters::checkKeywordItem), and ONE filterChange runs. A keyword nothing loaded carries has no Filters item: a popup says so, and the user's filters are left alone.

- Clicking a WHITE (filed) tag also shows it in the Keyword list: KeywordTags::showRequested -> KeywordTree::revealPath expands to, selects and centres the node, clearing the Find filter first if it is hiding it.
- The tag path is DEFERRED a tick (the filter change can rebuild the tag zone and delete the clicked Tag inside its own mouseReleaseEvent).
- The keyword-list path WAITS OUT THE DOUBLE-CLICK INTERVAL, and a double-click cancels it (KeywordTree::clickTimer): a double-click ASSIGNS the keyword, and filtering on its first click would hide the very images about to be tagged. Modifier clicks in the list are selection gestures and never filter.
- RED tags filter too, and then open the replace list: KeywordTags emits redTagClicked and MW runs filterOnKeyword THEN KeywordTags::startReplace. The replace survives the filter's selection change because setSelection only cancels a replace when the new selection no longer carries the red keyword, and the filter keeps exactly the images that do.

#### 16.5.4 Correcting a Red Tag

- CLICK it: KeywordTags::startReplace puts the Add field into REPLACE mode, filling its completer with the list keywords that resemble the red one (name or synonym equal, or one containing the other, judged on the leaf and then on each ancestor from the deepest; equal first, then shallowest) and showing it with an empty prefix so every candidate is visible. Picking one emits replaceRequested. The legend says what is being replaced; emptying the field or changing the selection cancels. Nothing resembling it: a popup says so and points at dropping or creating one in the Keyword list.
- DROP a keyword from the Keyword list on it: it is taken to be the correct version. KeywordTags emits replaceRequested and MW::applyKeywordsToSelection(add, {red}, true, replace=true) swaps it in ONE pass per image, adding only to the selected images that actually carried the red keyword. The red tag under the mouse is outlined while dragging. Released anywhere else in the tag zone, a drop adds to the whole selection.
- DRAG it onto the Keyword list: it is FILED there. Only RED tags are draggable (mime application/x-winnow-keyword-tag, kKeywordTagMime, carrying the path). KeywordTree::dropEvent files the tag's LEAF under the drop target (or at the root on blank space), creating the node with insertChild unless that name is already there: a red "Buoy|Thing" dropped on "Marine" becomes "Marine|Thing", because the stray's own branches are what is being corrected. This is keyword creation IN the Keyword list, so the rule holds. It then emits tagFiled(tag, newPath) and the dock swaps the tag for the filed path on the selected images that carry it. A drop that would name the tag itself is refused while dragging.
- The tagFiled connection is QUEUED, and the QDrag is parented on the tag area: the drop runs inside the dragged Tag's QDrag::exec(), and refreshKeywordsDock rebuilds the tag zone, which would delete that Tag under its own stack frame.
- After the swap, MW::rebuildKeywordFilters rebuilds the Keywords filter category (filter, icons, unfiled marking), the catalog rows are updated, and the keyword list's counts refreshed. It also restores the Filters panel's scroll position after ANY keyword edit (the rebuild empties the category, which clamped the scroll bar and threw the panel toward the top).

#### 16.5.5 The Add Field

The fast path, because a tree is the wrong instrument for the twentieth image. It HEADS the tag zone (at its foot it would land against the tree's Find box: two text fields in a row doing opposite things). Its completer is rebuilt per keystroke from KeywordVocab::completions (shallowest-first, searching synonyms as well as leaves) and draws each row as the leaf followed by its branch dimmed, so the four different "Vancouver Island" keywords are four choices that differ visibly.

THE FIELD NEVER CREATES A KEYWORD. Return with nothing chosen from the popup (KeywordTags::commitTyped) resolves the text against the vocabulary (a full path first, then a name or synonym that names exactly ONE node) and adds that node's path. Two nodes sharing the name are refused as ambiguous (pick from the popup, which shows each branch); no match is refused with a popup pointing at the Keyword list, and the text is left for correction. It used to take the text literally and put a new root keyword on the images, which is how stray red keywords were born.

#### 16.5.6 Keyword List Help and Tools > Keywords

The list's context menu ends with "Keyword list help...", which opens Docs/keywordlisthelp.html through MW::helpKeywordList (KeywordTree::helpRequested). It is a separate page from the panel's ? (Docs/keywordshelp.html), and written for a different reader: someone who does not yet know what a keyword is. It explains keywords, the list-versus-photographs distinction and branches, then takes every context-menu command in turn as what it does, why you would use it and how, and which ones touch files. Keep it in step with the menu: a command added to KeywordTree::contextMenuEvent gets a section there.

The list-wide commands (Tidy keywords, Audit keywords, Build vocabulary from catalog, Import Lightroom keywords, Export keywords, and the help) are also in Tools > Keywords (MW::createUtilMenu), because nobody finds a context menu they do not think to open. They use the same names as the context menu. Audit reuses the Edit menu's auditKeywordsAction. Build, Import and Export are KeywordTree methods made public for this. They call ensureKeywordVocabLoaded first (the dock may never have been opened, and an unloaded list would export as empty), and they take a dlgParent so their dialogs sit on the main window rather than on a tree that may be in a hidden dock.

The context menu also has Expand all / Collapse all (QTreeView::expandAll / collapseAll), between the per-keyword commands and the list-wide ones. They act on the whole list whatever row was clicked, and are not in Tools > Keywords because they are about the view, not the vocabulary.

Clearing the Find keyword filter with a keyword selected (KeywordTree::setFilterText, filtered -> empty, current index selected) runs expandAll and scrolls that keyword to the centre: the filter was how it was found, and without this it vanished among the rows that came back. No selection, no change to the expansion state.

The menu now acts on the row under the mouse. KeywordTree::contextMenuEvent makes the clicked row current, and a mouse right-click on empty space clears it. Before, the menu read whatever had been current, so right-clicking below the list offered "New keyword inside" the last keyword touched rather than the top-level "New keyword..." its label promises.

### 16.6 Node Consumption (the Phantom Top-Level Keyword)

A keyword filter that appeared to do nothing. Reported as "I tagged the image, the tag is on the file, and filtering on it finds nothing." Traced with five temporary probes down the whole path (the edit, the snapshot, the category rebuild, the compiled predicate, the row test), every stage was right. The compiled predicate read

```
col 31 include[2026]  /  col 94 include[Squirrel]
```

Two facts, neither a filter bug: a year filter was still checked from an earlier catalog-year scope, and the item checked was a TOP-LEVEL "Squirrel" (9 images, none of them 2026), not the "Fauna|Animal|Squirrel" (5) inside the tree. The panel drew both as the single word "Squirrel".

The phantom was manufactured by keywordEffectivePaths, and that WAS a bug. It built its consumed set from the LEAF of each hierarchical path only, so a dc:subject entry naming an ANCESTOR of a path the same image carries survived as a separate depth-1 keyword. That is what Lightroom writes with "export containing keywords" on. One real row:

```
dc:subject              Animal, BC, Canada, Chipmunk, Fauna,
                        Kettle River Recreation Area, Location, Southern BC, Squirrel
lr:hierarchicalSubject  Fauna|Animal|Squirrel|Chipmunk
                        Location|Canada|BC|Southern BC|Kettle River Recreation Area
```

Chipmunk and Kettle River Recreation Area were consumed as leaves. The other SEVEN survived, every one an ancestor name from those same two paths, each becoming a top-level keyword with its own count (Squirrel = 9 beside Fauna|Animal|Squirrel = 5, Gray Squirrel = 18 beside Fauna|Animal|Gray Squirrel = 8, and so on).

- CONSUME EVERY NODE, NOT JUST THE LEAF. A node name is dropped from dc:subject wherever it sits in a path the image carries, because keywordPrefixExpand already emits every ancestor as a keyword in its own right: "Fauna|Animal" is searchable, and a bare "Animal" beside it is the same fact spelled without its parents. A subject naming something NO path mentions is still kept: that is a genuinely unfiled keyword.
- SCHEMA 11 RE-DERIVES, and reads no files. The links already in the index were derived under the old rule, and no file changed, so nothing would re-read them (the freshness stamp is still correct, which is exactly why this needed a migration). The keyword tables are rebuilt from image.keywordpaths and image.keywords_literal, which the rows hold verbatim. No DDL: the derivation changed, not the shape.
- The duplicate is still possible, and is MARKED. A library where some images were tagged flat and others hierarchically genuinely holds both, and no rule can merge them without deciding for the user that they mean the same thing. Filters::addKeywordItems draws a top-level keyword whose name also appears inside the tree in ITALIC, with a tooltip naming the other paths and saying plainly that they are different keywords. Only the top-level copy is marked. The fix is the tidy, below.

### 16.7 Tidying Keywords

Filing a legacy vocabulary. A library tagged over years by more than one application holds the same tag both ways: a bare "Nanaimo" from whatever wrote dc:subject alone, and "Location|Canada|BC|Vancouver Island|Nanaimo" from Lightroom. Node consumption removes the ones that are the same image's own ancestors; it cannot touch the ones that are genuinely only flat, because nothing on that image says where they belong. Deciding that is the user's: Keywords panel context menu > "Tidy keywords..." (also Tools > Keywords) does it for the whole library in one pass.

UNFILED BRANCHES TOO (2026-10-19). The same review covers hierarchical paths images carry that the authored vocabulary does not hold: "Birds|Robin" from another application where the list has "Fauna|Bird|Robin". Catalog::tidyKeywords / tidyKeywordRows take the folded vocabulary and add those paths to the flat ones (one shared per-image test, tidyOf, so counts and rows agree); flatKeywords / flatKeywordRows are the same scans with an empty vocabulary. In KeywordTidyDlg a branch row is matched on its LEAF like a flat name, may also land on a ROOT of that name, and ranks candidates by shared parent names (compared with a trailing "s" dropped, so Birds matches Bird) before depth. A branch that matched nothing defaults to Leave alone, not Remove: a bare container name carries nothing, a path like "Birds|Robin|Juvenile" carries detail. The apply replaces EXACT paths only, never by prefix, so filing a flat "Canada" still leaves "Canada|BC|Nanaimo" alone unless that path is its own row. KeywordTidyAction.flat became .from.

APPEND TO (2026-10-19) is a fourth action beside Move to / Remove / Leave alone: the row's WHOLE keyword goes under "Goes to" ("Nanaimo" + Location|Canada|BC = Location|Canada|BC|Nanaimo; the branch "Birds|Robin" + Fauna = Fauna|Birds|Robin, its structure kept). plan() emits it as an ordinary move to the joined path, so applyKeywordTidyPlan has no third case. Switching a row to Append when its target ends in the keyword's own name (the pre-selected leaf match) swaps the target for its parent, since appending to Fauna|Bird|Robin would say Robin twice; the target's tooltip shows the result. Typing a target no longer forces an Append row back to Move. No bulk button: an append target is per-row by nature. After the apply, tidyKeywords inserts every target the vocabulary lacks (KeywordVocab::insertPaths, one reset, ancestors included) -- an Append always makes one, and so can a hand-typed Move -- or the freshly filed images would show the keyword as unfiled; the completion message reports how many were added.

#### 16.7.1 What "Flat" Means

A flat keyword is one an image carries AS A ROOT, not a keyword row without a separator. That distinction is the whole reason Catalog::flatKeywords is a scan over image.keywords_literal and image.keywordpaths rather than a query on the keyword table: prefix expansion puts a row in that table for every ANCESTOR of every path, so "Location" is there as the parent of Location|Canada whether or not any file ever said it alone. A tidy that read the table and called every separator-less path flat would offer to delete the entire top level of the vocabulary. The scan asks keywordEffectivePaths (the indexer's own function) and keeps what comes back with no '|'. On the author's library: 1,018 names across 10,781 of 43,000 images.

#### 16.7.2 A Review List, Not a Button

Matching is by LEAF against the authored vocabulary, and on that library 807 names matched exactly one branch, 181 matched several ("BC" is under both Canada|BC and Location|Canada|BC) and 30 matched nothing. Applying a guess to a fifth of a library's keywords, in the photographs themselves, is not something to do silently, so Dialogs/keywordtidydlg.\* shows every row with what it matched, pre-selects a target, and lets the target be edited or the row skipped.

- The pre-selection is the DEEPEST match, because where a name sits under both a stray branch and a filed one, the longer path is where it ends up anyway once the stray branch is itself filed.
- With one exception that matters: a candidate whose leaf repeats one of its own ancestors is ranked LAST. "Build vocabulary from catalog" records every path any file ever carried, and a mixed library carries nonsense (Fauna|Bird|Gyrefalcon|Bird, Category|Moire|Category) where a flat keyword was written into a hierarchical field. Those are the deepest matches for exactly the names most in need of filing, so ranking on depth alone pre-selected rubbish for the biggest rows. They are offered, never chosen for the user.
- Each row's tooltip lists every candidate WITH ITS IMAGE COUNT, which is what actually decides them: "Animal" under Fauna|Animal (257 images) or under Fauna|Bird|Arctic Ground Squirrel|Animal (1) is not a coin toss once the numbers are on screen.
- A name that matches nothing defaults to REMOVE. Those are the container names (Location, 8,908 images; Fauna, Flora, Scape, Category, Thing) that Lightroom writes with "export containing keywords" on. Under prefix expansion an image tagged Location|Canada is already found by a search for "Location", so a bare "Location" beside it is the same fact. Keep is one click away per row.

The Show list and the selection were added after the first version was tried. Two questions came straight back from use ("I want to move everything that matched one branch: how?" and "does Apply only do the selected rows?"), and both were the same defect: the only filter was "needs review", the inverse of the interesting set, and the bulk buttons acted on the FILTERED rows while the selection did nothing at all, silently. Now:

- A Show list (all / matched one branch / matched several / matched nothing / will move / will be removed / left alone), so a class of rows can be isolated and dealt with in one press.
- The buttons act on the SELECTED rows when there is a selection and on everything shown otherwise, with a live hint beside them naming which.
- Apply's own label carries the count it is about to carry out, and the opening paragraph says Apply carries out every row's action, not the selection.
- A selected row that the filter has hidden is NOT acted on: Qt keeps a selection alive across a filter change, so without that rule a button could reach rows that scrolled out of the question three filters ago.

#### 16.7.3 Applying the Plan

One pass over the images, with the whole plan in hand. MW::applyKeywordTidyPlan is deliberately not a loop of MW::retagKeywordPath calls: images overlap heavily between keywords (one photograph carries Nanaimo and Heron and 16x9), so a call per keyword would open, rewrite and re-index the same sidecar once per keyword, moving its ModifyDate that many times. The set it walks is Catalog::flatKeywordRows, the same scan and test that produced the counts the dialog showed, so it cannot touch an image the user was not told about.

- Only DEPTH-1 paths are rewritten, even when a hierarchical path's ROOT is a flat keyword being filed: "Canada|BC|Nanaimo" is a hierarchy the user has, and moving it is a RE-PARENT, which the vocabulary tree offers with its own count and confirmation.
- Redundant ancestors are pruned (the read path now prunes them too; see [16.4.1 Rename and Re-Parent Ask Before Touching a File](#1641-rename-and-re-parent-ask-before-touching-a-file)), and this is the operation that creates them: moving a flat "Canada" onto an image that already carries Location|Canada|BC would otherwise leave the image claiming both. keywordPruneAncestors (Metadata/keywordpaths.h) drops a path that is a proper ancestor of another path on the same image, which is safe because prefix expansion still answers a search for the ancestor. It is scoped to the rows the tidy rewrites. The pruned write round-trips exactly (tst_keywordpaths).
- The cleanup afterwards is two tables, meaning different things. Catalog::pruneUnusedKeywords deletes OBSERVED keyword rows nothing links to any more (a name no file says, which would otherwise offer a filter that matches nothing) and drops the path-to-id memo with them, or the next commit would link an image to a deleted id. KeywordVocab::removeUnusedRoots deletes AUTHORED nodes only where all three hold: depth 1, no children, and a count of zero after a refresh. An empty branch the user made room for stays.

#### 16.7.4 The Popup That Outlived the Work by Hours

Reported from the first real run. The tidy itself was fine (1,018 flat keywords over 10,781 images finished in about five minutes and left 4 on 7 images), but the popup announcing it was still on screen two hours later, so there was no way to tell a finished job from a hung one. Popup::showPopup shows nothing: it posts a QTimer::singleShot(0) and returns, and MW::applyKeywordTidyPlan then holds the GUI thread for the whole run. The show was still QUEUED when the loop ended, reset() hid a window that had never been shown, and the queued show finally fired inside the completion QMessageBox's own event loop, appearing AFTER the work was over with msDuration 0 (no hide timer) and nothing left to hide it.

The first fix was two application pumps (processEvents once after showPopup, and every 25 rows). That was replaced: every such pump repaints the WHOLE main window, measured at 112-577 ms apiece on a keyword move, so a tidy over ten thousand images spent longer painting than writing. Now:

- Popup::showPopupNow shows the popup synchronously, with no application pump.
- Popup::pulse moves the progress bar, repainting the popup ALONE and throttling itself on TIME rather than row count (ten a second whether rows take a microsecond or a second each). It also closes a re-entrancy hole rather than managing one: with no application pump, no click can start a folder change mid-rewrite.
- The general rule: any long synchronous loop that shows progress uses showPopupNow + pulse; showPopup from a loop that owns the GUI thread is at best late and at worst permanent.

The bar still never appeared on macOS (reported 2026-10-19, "show the progress when Apply runs"). repaint() is not enough there: Qt 6.11's QCALayerBackingStore::flush only assigns layer.contents and marks the window as needing display, and Core Animation commits that implicit transaction when the run loop next turns, which a synchronous loop never does. Every pulse painted into a back buffer nobody saw. Popup::paintNow (used by showPopupNow and pulse) follows the repaint with [CATransaction flush], which commits the pending layer change without delivering any queued event, so it keeps the no-pump property. On Windows the flush is a synchronous blit and repaint() alone suffices.

The tidy also now covers the whole Apply, not only the writes. One popup goes up straight after the confirmation, before Catalog::tidyKeywordRows scans the index. It shows a running count ("Tidying keywords: 1,234 of 10,781 images", via Popup::pulse(text), which only touches the label when the throttle lets a paint through). It then names each later phase: rebuilding the keyword filters, removing unused keywords from the catalog, updating the keyword list counts. MW::tidyFlatKeywords resets it LAST, just before the summary.

#### 16.7.5 A Bug This Found in the Retag Path

Catalog::commit skips a row whose (srcSize, srcMtime, sidecarMtime) still match the index: the skip that makes revisiting a folder free. MW::retagKeywordPath committed back the CatalogRow it had fetched FROM the index, so the stamps matched by construction and the commit was silently discarded: the keywords were written correctly into the sidecar, and the index went on serving the old ones to Catalog-scope searches until the folder was next opened. Both writers now go through MW::publishKeywordWrite, which re-stats the file and its sidecar before committing.

### 16.8 Filing Keywords by Drag (Filters Beside the Keyword List)

The tidy dialog is the bulk pass; this is the one that keeps up. The problem does not end when the review table does: a new camera, an imported folder or a keyword typed into another application puts a stray back into the library the same week. That wants the strays visible where the user already is, and one gesture to file each. So the Filters panel MARKS the keywords that match no node in the keyword list, and images dropped on the Keywords dock FILE them. Filters on the left, Keywords on the right, and the whole loop (see the strays, click one, look at its pictures, drag them home) happens without a dialog until the moment files are about to be written.

#### 16.8.1 Marking Unfiled Keywords in Filters

- Unfiled is decided by the one test that already existed: a keyword is unfiled when its full path is not in the AUTHORED vocabulary (KeywordVocab::indexForPath invalid), exactly what the Keywords dock uses to mark an unfiled tag. Sharing it, and the colour (G::unfiledKeywordColor), means the chip on the picture and the row in the panel can never disagree.
- The Filters items are drawn in a DULL red, deliberately unlike the red of an EXCLUDED item: "not in your keyword list" and "excluded from this filter" are different facts. Exclusion keeps the strikeout, which lets the two compose on the same row.
- The count is on the category header, because the strays are not visible from it: "Keywords (63 unfiled)" on the collapsed row is the only thing that says there is anything to look for in a tree a thousand nodes deep. It counts TOP-MOST unfiled items only (2026-10-19: an unfiled item whose parent is filed or is the category; Filters::unfiledKeywordCount). Counting every unfiled item made one stray branch with five keywords inside read as six, and nested strays under collapsed filed branches made the number disagree with the red rows in view. It is also what gives a reason to open the context menu and find "Show unfiled only", which hides the filed keywords while keeping the ANCESTORS of an unfiled one on screen (a stray shown with no branch above it cannot be read). Turning it on EXPANDS every item with a visible child (Filters::expandToUnfiled), so every stray is on screen; it used to expand only the category, leaving strays inside collapsed filed branches counted but unseen. It re-expands after a keyword rebuild while on, and turning it off restores the expansion the user had (expandedBeforeUnfiled, keyed on folded path because a rebuild remakes every item). The toggle is session-only, deliberately not saved: a filter that hid most of a category and came back after a restart would look like a panel that had lost its keywords. It changes only what is SHOWN; hidden items keep their check state.
- Making the header say anything cost a bug first: Filters::save keyed its saved item states on the top-level category's DISPLAY TEXT, so a header that changed with a count would have silently dropped every restored keyword filter. Categories now carry their name in Filters::CategoryNameRole, set once by createFilter, and save and restore key on that. The same lesson twice in one panel: the ITALIC marking a duplicated top-level keyword was written straight onto the item's font, and Filters::styleFilterItem rebuilds the font on every check, rebuild and restore, so the italic vanished the first time the user clicked it. Both marks are data roles now (DuplicateRole, UnfiledRole), and styleFilterItem is the single place appearance is written.
- The marking follows the vocabulary through the MODEL, not the gestures.
