Add, delete, rename, re-parent, "Build vocabulary from catalog" and a Lightroom import all change the keyword list, and three are done by the view without telling anyone. MW::refreshFilterVocabMarking is connected to KeywordVocab's own modelReset, rowsInserted, rowsRemoved and pathChanged, and to BuildFilters::finishedBuildFilters (the build runs on a thread, and the Keywords category has no items to mark until its Done op has run). The vocabulary reaches Filters as a VALUE (a set of folded paths), not a KeywordVocab pointer, which would be null exactly when wanted and stale the rest of the time. An EMPTY set turns the marking off: a fresh install has no authored vocabulary, and a panel in which every keyword read as an error would say the opposite of the truth.

#### 16.8.2 The Checked Keyword Makes a Drop a Move

Dragging thumbnails onto a node of the Keywords dock tags them with it, and with nothing checked in Filters > Keywords it still does. With one or more keywords CHECKED, the same drop becomes a MOVE: each checked keyword is removed from those images and its resolved target added. The check is the missing half of the sentence: an image can carry several strays, and nothing in a bag of thumbnails says which one the drag was about. Naming the source is also what makes the REMOVE possible, and without the remove a drop is additive and grows the mess it was meant to tidy.

#### 16.8.3 A Keyword and a Branch Are Different Drop Targets

That is the rule (keywordDropTarget in Metadata/keywordpaths.h, pinned in tst_keywordpaths). Dropping "Animals" on Fauna|Bird|Ferruginous Hawk says THESE ARE THAT BIRD: the drop is the user identifying a stray, so the images move into that keyword and nothing is created. Dropping the same stray on Fauna|Bird says FILE IT UNDER HERE, and the branch gains a child. A node with no children is a keyword; a node with children is a branch. The first version matched on the NAME instead (merge when the leaves agreed, append otherwise), which turned the commonest gesture into Fauna|Bird|Ferruginous Hawk|Animals.

The name still decides FIRST, in the two cases where it is unambiguous (a target whose own leaf IS the keyword, and a target that already HAS a child of that name); both are merges and must beat the branch rule, or "Squirrel" dropped on a Fauna|Animal|Squirrel with a Chipmunk under it would become Fauna|Animal|Squirrel|Squirrel. So there are four outcomes, and only the last creates anything:

1. the target, because it is named for the keyword;
2. an existing child named for it;
3. the target, because it is a keyword rather than a branch;
4. otherwise a new child of the branch.

- A library holds the same bird spelled three ways, and checking all three and dropping them together on the one real keyword is the shortest path to a tidy vocabulary. Several checked keywords dropped on a BRANCH still each get their own child.
- Only the LEAF of the checked keyword moves: filing "Trip|Kenya" under Location gives Location|Kenya, because "Trip" is the spelling being abandoned.
- A branch that does not exist yet is made in the Keywords dock first and then dropped onto: Winnow does not invent structure.
- The one thing the rule cannot say is "merge this into that BRANCH": a stray dropped on a node with children is always filed under it, so that case is handled by renaming in the dock. Deliberately: the alternative is a modifier key on a drag whose consequence is a mass file rewrite, and the confirmation names the outcome before anything is written.

#### 16.8.4 MW::applyKeywordMoves: One Pass per Checked Keyword

Several checked keywords are OR-ed by the filter, so what was dragged is a mixed bag (one image carries only "Bunny", the next only "Vole"). applyKeywordsToSelection applies one add list and one remove list to every row, so a single call would tag every dropped image with every target. Each keyword therefore gets its own pass over the subset of dropped images that actually carry it, reusing MW::applyKeywordToPaths' trick of selecting a subset and delegating, so there is still exactly one write path. The filter rebuild is hoisted out of that loop into MW::rebuildKeywordFilters: it recreates the entire keyword tree, and filing five keywords is one user action.

Nothing is created before the user agrees. The targets are resolved first (only computing paths); Dialogs/keyworddropdlg.\* then shows every move, which targets are NEW, and how many images each will rewrite; the vocabulary nodes are inserted afterwards. Cancelling leaves the keyword list exactly as it was. Keywords that resolved to where they already are, or that none of the dropped images carry, are LISTED with their reason rather than dropped silently.

- The button reads "Update image file(s) keywords" rather than "File 62": the count is two lines above it, and what is worth having under the cursor is that this rewrites the keywords inside the user's own image files. The table's columns are INTERACTIVE rather than stretched (keyword paths vary wildly in length, and stretch mode refuses to be dragged at all). Widths start from the content.
- The scope line is the one nobody would otherwise see. A drop can only rewrite images the datamodel has loaded (applyKeywordToPaths skips a path it cannot find a row for), so in Folders scope the keyword survives in every other folder in the library, silently. Catalog scope loads the catalog and has no such limit, which is why the dialog names the scope it is running in and says what Folders scope leaves behind.
- The cleanup afterwards is the tidy's: prune the observed keyword rows, refresh the counts, and only THEN removeUnusedRoots (a keyword only partly filed, because the rest of its images live in a folder this scope cannot reach, still has a count and correctly survives).

The operation is slow and SAYS SO. A drop rewrites every affected sidecar synchronously and then rebuilds the whole keyword tree, which on a real library can be minutes. It shows "Busy updating the image file keywords and refreshing this filter" with showPopupNow and pulses it, as the tidy does. Feedback must outlast the WORK, not the writing: the popup used to be reset once the sidecars were written, leaving the filter rebuild, the vocabulary re-count and the verification running behind a window that looked finished. It is reset LAST now, and each phase names itself ("Rebuilding the keyword filters", "Updating the keyword list counts").

The filters are refreshed, not repointed, and not cleared. rebuildKeywordFilters remakes the keyword tree, and Filters::updateKeywordItems carries check state across the rebuild keyed on the PATH, so a keyword moved in FULL loses its item and its tick with it, and a keyword moved in PART keeps both and goes on showing what is left to file. Both obvious alternatives were tried and are wrong: ticking the TARGET answered a question nobody asked (one image moved into Location|New Zealand|Castlepoint came back showing four, the three filed there all along included), and CLEARING the keyword filters discards the rating, year or other keyword that are still the user's.

Three places count a keyword, and the drop checks that they agree (MW::verifyKeywordMoveCounts): the datamodel's G::KeywordsAllColumn (what BuildFilters counts), the Filters item (what the user reads), and the catalog (where the dock's own count comes from). A move that succeeded everywhere except the Filters panel was a real report, and reading the write path did not settle which was wrong. Any disagreement is LOGGED with all three; it reports rather than repairs, deliberately, because papering over a mismatch would hide a write path that is genuinely losing an edit. It compares the panel against the CATALOG (one indexed query per keyword), and only in Catalog scope: in Folders scope the two legitimately differ. (It used to walk all 41,444 datamodel rows converting a QStringList per row per moved keyword, which was the "several seconds" the user reported as a slow count update, and was asking a tautology anyway.)

#### 16.8.5 The Drag Must Not Delete the Photographs

Tagging is not a file move, and a drop target that forgets to say so DELETES PHOTOGRAPHS. IconView::startDrag ran a no-modifier thumbnail drag as drag->exec(Qt::MoveAction) and, when that returned anything other than Qt::IgnoreAction, called deleteFiles() on the dragged paths (on macOS, an AppleScript putting them in the Trash). KeywordTree accepted the images with acceptProposedAction(), which returns MoveAction, so every drag of a thumbnail onto a keyword tagged the image AND trashed the file. Six of the author's photographs went that way before the pattern was seen, and cancelling the confirmation made no difference: the deletion happens in the drag SOURCE after exec() returns.

- The fix: the drag offers BOTH actions and only a move deletes. IconView::startDrag runs exec(CopyAction | MoveAction, MoveAction) and deletes only when the result is MoveAction. A file destination (FSTree, BookMarks, the Finder) takes the proposed MoveAction and the originals go exactly as before. A target that merely reads the paths declares CopyAction on dragEnter, dragMove AND drop.
- Qt::IgnoreAction was the first fix and it shipped BROKEN: it prevents the delete, but it also tells Qt the target REFUSES, so dropEvent is never delivered and the drag does nothing at all. In Qt, "do not treat this as a move" and "do not accept this" are the same value only if the drag supports one action; the fix is to widen the supported actions rather than to refuse. It goes on all three handlers because the action is re-proposed as the pointer moves and exec() returns whatever the last handler said; the drop sets it BEFORE emitting assignToPaths, so an early return or a cancelled dialog cannot leave the source believing otherwise.
- What made it hard to see, a lesson about diagnosis: the missing files showed up as a datamodel shrinking by a row per drag, which looked like index hygiene (rows naming files no longer on disk). Checking that the file was absent CONFIRMED the innocent reading, twice. The file was absent because Winnow had just deleted it. The check that would have settled it in one step was looking in the Trash. A disappearance is not evidence of staleness until you have looked where the deleter would have put it.

The drag says where it will land, in the grey Folders and Bookmarks already use (AppliedKeywordDelegate in Views/keywordtree.cpp, the colour from File/hoverdelegate.cpp: backgroundShade + 20). Qt's own drop indicator is a one-pixel rule BETWEEN rows, which answers the wrong question: dropping between two keywords has no meaning. The highlight is cleared on every refusal as well as set on every acceptance, and the delegate is the tree's own because a view has one delegate and this one also draws the applied colour.

### 16.9 Merging Two Branches

The same place filed twice is what a library keyworded by two applications actually holds: "Canada|BC|Vancouver Island" beside "Location|Canada|BC|Vancouver Island", "Costa Rica|Monte Verde" beside "Location|Costa Rica". The fix in every case is to put one branch inside the other. Dragging the node onto its destination used to warn and stop (reparent refuses a name already taken under the new parent, because merging "has to decide what happens to both nodes' images"). That reasoning is right, and the answer is to ASK rather than refuse: the drop now offers the merge, and the ordinary retag dialog then asks about the photographs.

- Name by name, all the way down (KeywordVocab::reparentMerging, mergeNodes). Each child of the source either has a counterpart under the destination, in which case the two are merged in turn, or it does not, in which case it simply moves. That recursion is the whole feature: filing "Canada" under "Location" must leave "Canada|BC|Nanaimo" as "Location|Canada|BC|Nanaimo", which the drag-filing tool cannot do (a dropped keyword contributes only its LEAF). A moved child's new path is free by construction.
- ONE pathChanged for the whole merge: MW::retagKeywordPath rewrites every descendant at its PREFIX, so the top-level move already describes the subtree; emitting per node would raise the file-rewriting dialog once per keyword in the branch.
- Synonyms are UNIONED rather than one side winning: two nodes that turn out to be the same keyword have between them every spelling the user recorded.
- A merge is also what makes the retag produce DUPLICATES, which it guards against: an image filed under both branches has them rewritten to the SAME path, and dc:subject de-duplicates on the way out while lr:hierarchicalSubject does not, so without the fold-keyed pass in retagKeywordPath the keyword would be written twice.

The bug the merge found, unrelated to merging: vocab.synonyms is "NOT NULL DEFAULT ''". QStringList::join returns a default-constructed (NULL) QString for an empty list, Qt binds a null QString as SQL NULL, and SQLite refuses the UPDATE. So EVERY write of a node with no synonyms failed, which is very nearly every node in a real vocabulary. It was invisible in a running session because the tree on screen is the in-memory one: rename checked the result and returned false, having already changed the name and without emitting pathChanged, so the photographs were never offered the retag; reparent and rewritePaths did not check at all, so a moved branch stayed moved until the next reload put it back. writeNode now binds a non-null empty string, rewritePaths returns whether it succeeded, and rename and reparent reload and report. The regression test asserts against a SECOND KeywordVocab that re-reads the database, because checking the model in memory passes against the broken code.

### 16.10 Merging an Unfiled Branch Into the Keyword List

The third route, and the only tail-preserving one. Right-click an unfiled keyword in Filters > Keywords and merge it, with everything under it, into the branch it belongs to. Filters::mergeUnfiledKeyword (the signal) -> MW::mergeUnfiledKeyword (Main/keywordedit.cpp) + Dialogs/keywordmergedlg.\* + KeywordVocab::insertPaths.

The gap it fills: a keyword the catalog holds and the vocabulary does not is drawn unfiled in the Filters panel and nowhere else, so that panel is the only place the user can point at the problem, and neither existing route could move a BRANCH:

- Filing by drag (MW::applyKeywordMoves) carries only the dropped keyword's LEAF, so "New Zealand|North Island|Wellington" dropped onto Location arrives as "Wellington" and two levels of the user's own structure are gone. Worse, ticking the PARENT and dropping it removes the path AND ITS SUBTREE from every image and adds back a single node, so the tails are destroyed in the files.
- KeywordVocab::reparentMerging keeps tails at any depth, but needs a vocabulary node on BOTH sides, which is precisely what an unfiled branch does not have.

It is a RETAG, not a vocabulary move, and that is what makes the tails survive. Nothing is dragged and nothing is re-parented: the whole thing is MW::retagKeywordPath rewriting a PREFIX (newPath + p.mid(oldPath.size())) over every image the catalog says carries the old path or anything beneath it. Depth is irrelevant to a prefix rewrite, and it reaches images the datamodel has never loaded, which the drag cannot.

- The keyword list gains the tails, or the problem has only moved: after the rewrite those photographs carry Location|New Zealand|Castlepoint, and if the list has no Castlepoint under Location|New Zealand, Filters marks the result unfiled again. So every observed tail is rebuilt under the chosen parent, and only the missing ones. KeywordVocab::insertPaths exists for this: insertChild resets the model per node, right for a hand gesture and wrong for filing a branch (dozens of resets, rebuilds of the Filters marking and passes over the tree's expansion state). One reset and one transaction, and a failure rolls the rows back and reloads.
- The choice is offered only when there is one. A vocabulary grown from two applications routinely holds the same leaf under two parents, so a single candidate is STATED and several are ASKED, in a list carrying the image count each already holds ("Location|New Zealand, 812 images" beside "Trips|New Zealand, 4"). It is the one keyword operation that refreshes the vocabulary counts on ENTRY: everywhere else they are output; here they are input.
- What each choice would add is computed PER TARGET and follows the selection. Nothing is created before the user agrees (the KeywordDropDlg contract): targets and their node lists are computed, shown, and inserted only on Apply.
- Disabled with the reason when there is nowhere to merge to. The panel already holds the authored vocabulary as a set of folded paths, so Filters::vocabHasLeaf answers "is there any branch of this name?"; when there is not, the menu entry reads "Merge into keyword list - no branch of that name" and its tooltip names the remaining routes.

The dialog's three numbers are three different things, and saying so is the whole of its wording. Photographs to rewrite, keywords moving, and keyword-list entries to create all appeared on one small dialog, and on first use two were read as the third: the scope buttons' bare "(124)" was taken for a keyword count, and a list of six under a heading saying nineteen were moving read as thirteen missing branches. Nothing was wrong with the arithmetic. So the buttons say "(124 images)", the created entries are called "keyword branches (nodes)", and the list is introduced by what the destination ALREADY holds, so the numbers reconcile with the opening sentence. It no longer OPENS with "USA is not in your keyword list" (the user right-clicked a keyword drawn unfiled; they know); it opens with the one fact the panel cannot give: the whole BRANCH travels with the node that was clicked.

retagKeywordPath now calls rebuildKeywordFilters instead of a copy of it. It carried its own suspend / updateCategory / filterChange sequence, minus refreshFilterVocabMarking, so a retag left the freshly recreated keyword items unmarked until some later build ran.

### 16.11 The Keywords Diagnostic Report

Four stores hold the same fact, and every keyword bug so far has been two of them disagreeing:

- the FILES carry dc:subject and lr:hierarchicalSubject;
- the DATAMODEL carries them as G::KeywordsColumn / KeywordPathsColumn plus the expansion in KeywordsAllColumn, which is what the Filters panel counts;
- the CATALOG carries `keyword` + `image_keyword`, the observed vocabulary, which the Keywords dock and every cross-folder search count;
- `vocab` (in userdata.db) carries the tree the user curates, which decides whether a keyword reads as filed or unfiled.

Schemas 11, 12 and 15 are all repairs of a drift between the second and the third; the rename that never persisted was a drift between the fourth and its own database. None announced itself. Help > Diagnostics > Keywords diagnostics asks all of those questions at once, on demand, in one read-only report (MW::keywordDiagnostics).

- It leads with the COMPARISONS, not the inventory. The DRIFT AUDIT (Catalog::keywordAudit), for each sampled image, recomputes keywordPrefixExpand(keywordEffectivePaths(keywords_literal, keywordpaths)), the same two functions Catalog::writeKeywordsLocked calls, and compares it, folded, against the paths the image's links actually name. Deliberately the writer's expression rather than a second one: an independent re-derivation could drift from the writer and report a fault that was its own. It reports images that disagree, links missing, links present that the text does not carry, and spells out up to five with the paths on both sides.
- Then the two counts of one keyword, side by side: Filters::keywordItemCount against the catalog's own count, per keyword (what MW::verifyKeywordMoveCounts does after a move, over the whole vocabulary). In CATALOG SCOPE ONLY: in Folders scope the two SHOULD differ, and a report that flagged every keyword would teach the reader to ignore it. The section says so rather than showing meaningless deltas.
- Then the CURRENT IMAGE at all four levels: its dc:subject, its lr:hierarchicalSubject, the effective paths after node consumption, their prefix expansion, what KeywordsAllColumn actually holds, whether the two agree, and which of its keywords have no node in the authored vocabulary. The whole keyword pipeline for one picture on one screen.
- The INVENTORY: schema version against what the code expects; live images, images with keyword text, images with links; row counts for keyword / vocab / image_keyword; keywords nothing links to (prunable); links naming a keyword or an image that is gone; and images with links and NO text (the population a rebuild cannot derive from the file). The vocabulary side reports nodes, roots, leaves, depth, synonyms, non-exportable nodes, empty branches (legitimate in `vocab`, impossible in `keyword`), and names living under more than one parent. Unfiled keywords are listed biggest-first.
- It ENDS with the keyword list itself, indented: last because it is the only section whose length is the size of the vocabulary rather than the problem. It is drawn by walking the MODEL, so its order and shape are the dock's own. Each row carries the node's image count (a subtree total by construction) and three markers: synonyms, not exportable, no images. With no authored vocabulary loaded, the OBSERVED keywords stand in (Catalog::keywords() returns them ordered by pathfold, which IS depth-first order for a tree).

Sampled, and on the GUI thread, which is why it is a menu item: the drift audit caps at 20,000 images (the summary counts are whole-table and cheap) and the report puts up a busy cursor. Nothing here writes: a diagnostic that could change what it measures would be the wrong tool for stores that have twice needed repairing.

### 16.12 Audit Keywords (Finding Keywording Mistakes by How Images Look)

Edit > Audit Keywords... (also the Keywords panel's context menu) lists images whose keywords do not match how they look: SUSPECT keywords ("tagged Egret, but looks like your Heron images") and MISSING ones ("not tagged Heron, but looks like your Heron images"). Every finding is a question for the user, never an automatic edit. It began from the observation that most disagreements between an image model and a hand-kept keyword list are keywording mistakes, and a Phase 0 prototype confirmed it on an 87k-image catalog before any C++ was written.

The question is NOT "what is in this picture?" but "does this picture look like the OTHER pictures you gave this keyword?". A general model's idea of "Heron" is irrelevant, and useless for most of a real vocabulary (places, people, projects). Each keyword in the user's list (userdata.db vocab) is learned from the images that carry it, against the keyworded images that do not. That is what makes "Location|Canada|BC|Nanaimo|&lt;a street address>" auditable at all: it is learned from the user's own pictures of that place. (The prototype's zero-shot text scores came out near a coin toss, AUC \~0.55, even on Fauna and Flora, which may be a tokenizer problem in the prototype; unresolved, and not needed by the method below.)

#### 16.12.1 Image Vectors

Every keyworded catalog image is reduced to one 768-d SigLIP 2 vector (base/16 image tower at 256 px, Utilities/inference/imageembedder.h) computed from its cached browsing thumbnail: 256 px is what the model sees, so decoding the full image would cost a hundred times more for no better vector. An image never browsed falls back to its file's embedded preview.

- Stored as float16 in index.db table image_embedding (schema 22, Cache/embeddingstore.h), stamped with the source's size / mtime and tagged with the model, so an edited file is re-embedded and another model's vectors are never mixed in.
- Computed ON DEMAND when the user presses Run, not in the background, and only for images whose vector is missing or stale; the first run over 100k images takes \~8 minutes on an M1 Ultra.

#### 16.12.2 Scoring

Cross-fitted, or a wrong tag vouches for itself. Every score for (image, keyword) comes from a model that never saw that image labelled (Utilities/visualaudit.h): kNN (a similarity-weighted vote of the 20 nearest images) and a 5-fold one-vs-rest ridge regression. Both must agree before anything is reported. Ridge replaced the prototype's logistic probe: it found 96-98% of the same top findings at 1/130th of the cost (2 s vs 273 s), closed form, with the Gram matrices summed once and each fold solved with the totals minus its own share. The whole audit scores 87k images against 1,757 keywords in \~25 s.

- BURSTS ARE ONE UNIT. Adjacent near-duplicate frames of a folder (cosine >= 0.95, within 60 s) are grouped. A burst tagged together and wrongly would otherwise confirm itself (each frame's nearest neighbours are its siblings, carrying the same wrong tag), and the review would list one mistake twelve times. kNN excludes an image's own burst from its neighbours, the ridge folds are grouped by burst, and a finding covers the whole burst; a decision applies to every frame.
- SCORES BECOME RANKS, so a rare keyword and a common one share one threshold. A Suspect is an EXPLICITLY carried keyword (ancestors are implied and never reported) beaten by more than 10% of the images that do not carry it; the best-scoring sibling it does not carry is offered as the alternative. A Missing keyword is one where the image outscores 60% of the images that carry it, deepest keyword only ("Fauna|Bird|Heron" is reported, not also "Fauna|Bird"). "Tagged Heron, looks like Egret" and "missing Egret" on the same image are ONE mistake, reported once as the former.
- kNN votes are quantised to 1e-4: most carriers of a well-kept keyword score \~1, and without it float rounding decided whether a lookalike "outscored" them.
- NOT EVERY KEYWORD IS VISUAL. A keyword whose cross-validated AUC (either method) is under 0.80 (a person across shoots, a rating-like tag, a client) is skipped, and the Keywords tab says so ("Not visual"). Some non-visual keywords still score high because they cluster by SHOOT; "Don't audit" excludes a keyword permanently (userdata.db audit_skip).

#### 16.12.3 The Review

Dialogs/keywordauditdlg.h. Non-modal, so the user can Show an image in Winnow and come back. Each finding shows the image beside three of the user's own best examples of the keyword and of the suggested alternative: the question is answered by looking, not by trusting a score.

- Decisions are keys: R replace, D remove, A add, C keywords are right, U undecide, S show; the list advances to the next undecided finding.
- Replace / Remove / Add wait for Apply and are then written in one pass (MW::applyKeywordAuditFixes, the retag's shape: catalog rows, composeKeywordWrite, writeKeywordsToSidecar respecting G::modifySourceFiles, publishKeywordWrite).
- "Keywords are right" is saved at once (userdata.db audit_verdict, schema 3) and is what stops the next audit asking again.

#### 16.12.4 The Model and the Mac

siglip2_image.onnx (ModelStore::Model::SigLipImage, 185 MB, downloaded on first Run; exported and parity-checked by tools/export_siglip.py) is float16 with float32 I/O and a FIXED batch of 16. Measured on an M1 Ultra: CPU 16 img/s; CoreML ML Program on the GPU 203-223 img/s; the Neural Engine only 46 img/s, so it runs on the GPU. Windows runs the same model through DirectML. Three export details are load-bearing:

- A dynamic batch dimension makes the CoreML EP fail at run time.
- The exporter's auto_pad="VALID" on the patch Conv makes ORT's ML Program builder omit CoreML's required 'pad' ("Unable to parse ML Program ... Required param 'pad' is missing"), so the export writes explicit zero pads.
- The compiled ML Program takes \~90 s to build, so OrtBackend accepts a compile-cache directory (CoreML EP ModelCacheDirectory, through the provider-options API). ImageEmbedder keeps it in Caches/CoreML/siglip2_image-v&lt;version> (\~1 GB; a later load takes 0.2 s) and removes directories left by older versions. The dialog says "Preparing the image model for this computer (once...)" during that first compile rather than looking hung.

#### 16.12.5 Headless and Tests

Winnow --keywordaudit [keyword substring] runs exactly what Run does against the real index and keyword list, stores any vectors it computes, and prints the totals, findings by branch and the top findings (Main/keywordauditprobe.h). tools/keyword_audit_proto.py is the Phase 0 prototype (Python, reads index.db read-only, writes an HTML report with a precision tally); its rules are the ones VisualAudit implements. Pinned by tests/unit/tst_visualaudit.cpp, each over eight seeds: a planted mislabel is caught with the right alternative; a mislabelled burst is one finding with no duplicate Missing; ancestors are never reported missing; a random keyword is skipped as not visual; dismissed and excluded findings stay hidden.

Not yet: zero-shot text scoring (for keywords with too few images to learn, and "suggest keywords" for unkeyworded images) needs the SigLIP text tower, a C++ SentencePiece tokenizer and int64 tensors in the inference layer; the prototype's text scores were not useful as measured, so it waits for a reason and a fixed measurement.

#### 16.12.6 Report Scope (Current Filter)

The dialog's "Report on" choice (Whole catalog / Current filter) limits what is REPORTED, never what is LEARNED (2026-10-19). A keyword learned from a filtered handful would be learned badly, so every keyworded catalog image still trains; the scope only gates which images get Suspect, Missing and Suggested findings.

- MW captures the filter when Run is pressed: every proxy row's path (a version mapped to its master's file, de-duplicated), so a filter change during a run does not move the goalposts. An empty filter is refused in the dialog's status line.
- KeywordAuditJob::run takes the paths, keys them with cachePathKey, and passes VisualAudit::run an inScope flag per image. The `add` lambda drops a finding member that is out of scope, so the Keywords tab's per-keyword counts follow the scope too.
- Unkeyworded catalog rows are read (and embedded) only when in scope: embedding a whole unkeyworded catalog to report on a filtered handful would be minutes of GPU for nothing. In Whole-catalog scope that means every unkeyworded image is embedded on the first run, which can be long and is shown in the progress line.
- Filtered images the catalog does not hold cannot be audited; the result line says how many (KeywordAuditOutcome::scopeUncatalogued) rather than letting them read as "nothing to report".

#### 16.12.7 Suggested Keywords

Keyword suggestions for ANY image, keyworded or not, reusing what the audit learned (2026-10-19). Two signals, both pure functions in Utilities/visualaudit.h:

- Visual. VisualAudit::run now also solves the ridge model on ALL training rows (one extra solve with the Gram totals it already summed; no fold held out, because an image being suggested for was never a label) and returns it as Result::model, a SuggestModel: the visual columns' full-fit weights plus each column's sorted CROSS-FITTED carrier scores. SuggestModel::score ranks a new vector's full-fit score against those carriers and suggests when it beats missingTpr of them, the Missing rule. Ridge only: a kNN vote needs every vector in memory, and the panel asks one image at a time.
- Session. sessionSuggestions: other images in the same folder within Params::sessionSecs (3 h) of the capture time; a keyword-list keyword carried (on EXPANDED paths, so Ceremony/Reception agree on Wedding) by at least sessionShare (0.5) of at least sessionMinImages (2) keyworded neighbours. This is how non-visual keywords (an event, a client, a name) get suggested.
- mergeSuggestions joins the two (one suggestion with both reasons), drops a suggestion that is an ancestor of another (deepest wins), ranks both-reasons first, and caps at maxSuggestions (5). Carried keywords (with ancestors) and dismissed ones are never suggested.

Two surfaces, one engine:

- Audit dialog: a third finding kind, Finding::Suggested, from VisualAudit::suggest over the in-scope images (training images first, then the unkeyworded ones; run() learns only from [0, trainCount)). Grouped by burst like the other kinds, and a keyword already reported as Missing for an image is not suggested again. A = Add; C = "Not This Keyword", stored as an audit_verdict with kind "suggested" (no schema change: the kind column is free text). "Don't Audit" is hidden for suggestions.
- Keywords panel: a "Suggested" band under the tags (KeywordTags::setSuggestions), chips "+ Leaf" with the reason in the tooltip. Click = MW::applyKeywordsToSelection on the selection, like every other add in the panel; x = dismiss for this image. The status line says when the model was learned and links to Audit keywords.
- KeywordSuggester (Main/keywordsuggester.h) runs on its own thread: the catalog row by path (Catalog::rowsForPaths), the image's vector from EmbeddingStore::get (new: one row, stamp-checked) or embedded from its cached thumbnail and stored, then SuggestModel::score; the session from a folder + capture-window CatalogQuery. Requests are numbered (nextGeneration) and an overtaken one is dropped. It never triggers the ~90 s first CoreML compile (ImageEmbedder::NeedsFirstCompile): without a stored vector, such an image gets session suggestions only.
- MW::requestKeywordSuggestions re-asks only when the current image or its keywords changed (or forced: an accepted or dismissed suggestion, a vocabulary change, a new model). It clears the chips immediately, so the previous image's suggestions are never on screen to be clicked. The vocabulary reaches the suggester from MW::refreshFilterVocabMarking, which every vocabulary change already reaches.
- The model is saved after every audit (KeywordAuditJob::suggestModelPath: keywordsuggest.bin beside index.db; QSaveFile, versioned, all-or-nothing load) and reloaded on KeywordAuditJob::modelSaved. A model whose modelTag differs from the current ImageEmbedder::ModelTag is ignored.
- Tests: tst_visualaudit covers an unkeyworded lookalike being suggested its leaf only, the model's save/load round trip (and a truncated file loading as nothing), the session rule (folder, window, share, minimum, carried, dismissed), and the scope gate.

### 16.13 Investigations and Fixes

#### 16.13.1 Schema 12: The Links Drifted From the Text (Third Data Repair)

Two places count a keyword, and they stopped agreeing. The Filters panel counts the datamodel, built from image.keywordpaths and image.keywords_literal (the verbatim text each row holds). The Keywords dock, and every catalog keyword search, counts image_keyword, which is DERIVED from that same text by keywordPrefixExpand(keywordEffectivePaths(...)). On a 43,000-image library a keyword read 574 images in one panel and 1 in the other. A 300-image sample found 179 rows whose links did not match their own text: 1,285 links missing and 689 present that the image does not carry. One image's text read "Buoy|Thing", "Location|Canada|BC|Southern BC|Kettle River Recreation Area" and "Thing|Rain" while its links read "People" and "Thing|Rain": not expanded, most of them absent, and one belonging to some other picture entirely.

A rescan is precisely the thing that CANNOT fix it, and the report said so ("I did a new scan - no change"). The text columns are correct and no file has changed, so every freshness stamp still matches and Catalog::commit skips the row: the property that makes revisiting a folder free is what makes a drift in the derived tables permanent. That is what a migration is for. Schema 12 rebuilt keyword and image_keyword from the two verbatim columns without reading a file or touching a stamp.

seedVocab = FALSE, and it is the half that matters. rebuildPathKeyedKeywords also SEEDS the authored vocabulary from what it observed, so a first-ever index opens the Keywords dock on the user's own hierarchy. That is right once and wrong every time after: run again as a repair, it would push every path the library contains back into the list the user curates, including the mis-parented ones they have just spent an afternoon filing away. The links are DERIVED and may be rebuilt at will; the vocabulary is AUTHORED and may not. tst_catalog pins it. (Since userdata schema 2 the seed lands in index.db's RETIRED vocab table, which UserDb copies into userdata.db once, UserDb::importIndexVocab, and never reads again.)

First root cause: two sources for one fact. A CatalogRow carries the keywords three ways: keywordsLiteral and keywordPaths, stored verbatim on the image row, and keywords, their prefix expansion. Catalog::writeKeywordsLocked built image_keyword from the THIRD while the same commit wrote the image row from the first two, and r.keywords is read out of the datamodel's G::KeywordsAllColumn, so a row committed while that column was stale or half-written stored text saying one thing and links another. The links are now derived from the text the same commit is storing, by the same two functions the migration uses: the disagreement becomes impossible rather than rare. Two fixtures had to change with it: both simulated a keyword edit by moving r.keywords ALONE, a row the application never produces.

Second root cause, and schema 15 (2026-09-25). Fixing the two sources did not stop the drift, and after schema 14 re-committed the whole library it was nearly total: on a 155k-image index, 99% of the images with keywords carried links that disagreed with their own text (about 457,000 missing, 47,000 pointing at the wrong keyword). Found chasing a Library filter on two keywords; the signature was unmistakable once the raw links were listed: image N was linked to keyword id N-1, image after image. Catalog::keywordIdLocked inserts with ON CONFLICT(pathfold) DO NOTHING and read the new id from lastInsertId(). When the keyword already exists, that is a successful exec() that inserted nothing, and sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() still holds the connection's previous insert: the previous image's FTS row, whose rowid IS that image's id. The "if (!id) look it up" fallback never ran, and the per-session memo kept the wrong id, so this hit the first use of every existing keyword in every session. The same trap KeywordVocab::insertChild fell into ([16.13.3 Six Gotchas Found Reviewing the Keyword Path](#16133-six-gotchas-found-reviewing-the-keyword-path)), in the writer this time. The fix tests numRowsAffected() before trusting lastInsertId(), in keywordIdLocked and both of rebuildPathKeyedKeywords' inserts. Schema 15 re-ran schema 12's rebuild, again with seedVocab = false. Pinned by tst_catalog::existingKeywordLinksToItsOwnRow, which pre-seeds the keyword rows the way a previous session would have.

What the report turned out NOT to be, the more common confusion: "Buoy" showing 574 images when no file carries a keyword called Buoy is CORRECT. 574 images carry "Buoy|Thing" in lr:hierarchicalSubject, prefix expansion links each to the ancestor "Buoy", and a branch's own count is its subtree total. The keyword is genuine Lightroom data (a 2014 JPEG Winnow has never written carries "Buoy|Thing" and "Dinghy|Thing" embedded), so "Thing" is mis-parented under two other keywords in that vocabulary. A count that is the subtree total, on a vocabulary with a mis-parented node, looks exactly like a bug and is not one.

#### 16.13.2 What a Keyword Move Actually Costs (Measured, and the Feedback That Cost More Than the Work)

A keyword move had been reported as taking seconds to minutes, and three rounds of reading the code produced three wrong answers (the per-image sidecar writes, the keyword tree rebuild, the catalog queries). It was settled by sampling the running application through a real drop (macOS `sample`, 240 s at 1 ms). The drop took 2,734 ms:

```
QDialog::exec (the confirmation, waiting for the user)   1,011 ms
widget repainting                                          984 ms
  QTreeView::paintEvent                                    681 ms  (678 through QStyleSheetStyle::drawControl
                                                                    into an AppKit NSAppearance block per item)
sqlite                                                     368 ms
BuildFilters::makeSnapshot                                 224 ms
Filters::updateKeywordItems                                 41 ms
MW::refreshFilterVocabMarking                               20 ms
accessibility                                               12 ms
Metadata::writeXMP (writing keywords into the files)         4 ms
```

THE FEEDBACK COST 230 TIMES WHAT THE WORK COST. MW::applyKeywordMoves called qApp->processEvents() three times (577, 234 and 112 ms) purely to get a progress popup onto the screen, because Popup::showPopup defers through a zero timer. A pump does not deliver only that timer: it also flushes every update request the write loop, the filter rebuild and refreshIcons have posted, so the main window was fully repainted three times MID-OPERATION instead of once at the end, at macOS tree-view prices.

Popup::showPopupNow and Popup::pulse are the answer, and the distinction they draw is the point. showPopupNow does on the GUI thread what showPopup defers: it delivers the popup's OWN posted events (QCoreApplication::sendPostedEvents aimed at the popup object, so nothing else in the queue moves), shows, raises and repaints. The popup is its own top-level window, so painting it costs none of the main window's work, and the view updates coalesce and are painted once by the ordinary event loop after the drop returns. pulse is the same trick inside a loop, throttled on TIME (ten repaints a second whether a row takes a microsecond or a second). Off the GUI thread showPopupNow falls back to the queued route rather than asserting.

- The progress bar had NEVER been drawn by the loops that set it: setProgress writes a value and returns, and with nothing turning the event loop the widget is never asked to paint, so a rewrite of thousands of sidecars showed a bar frozen at zero, indistinguishable from a hang. MW::applyKeywordsToSelection, MW::retagKeywordPath and MW::applyKeywordTidyPlan all pulse now.
- Dropping the pumps also closed a re-entrancy hole that was being MANAGED rather than avoided: every processEvents passed ExcludeUserInputEvents with a comment explaining that a click starting a folder change would re-enter everything the loop was walking. Nothing is delivered now, so there is nothing to exclude.
- KeywordVocab::refreshCounts ran TWICE per drop: applyKeywordMoves called ensureKeywordVocabLoaded() on entry, which refreshed the counts (106 ms) that the move then invalidated and recomputed (152 ms). ensureKeywordVocabLoaded takes a withCounts flag now: "make sure the tree is loaded" and "recount every node" are two jobs.
- MW::verifyKeywordMoveCounts cost 111 ms per drop; it is gated behind G::isPerfProbe or G::isVerboseIssues now, because the drift it was written to catch is prevented at the writer (Catalog::writeKeywordsLocked derives the links from the text the same commit stores).
- And FOUR TIMES PER WORKSPACE SWITCH (2026-10-01): leaving Develop for the Library ran refreshCounts (\~240 ms at 155k images) four times inside one switch (visibilityChanged fired twice during setVisible and once during restoreState, and MW::setKeywordsDockVisibility asked again on its own): \~950 ms of a 1.25 s switch, measured by WFPROBE. The visibility routes now load the tree with withCounts = false and call MW::scheduleKeywordCountsRefresh: ONE refresh, coalesced, 50 ms later, so the new layout paints first, skipped if the dock has been hidden again. Callers whose counts are an input (the merge dialog) still load synchronously with counts.

What is NOT slow, so nobody measures it again. Filters::updateKeywordItems (the "deletes and recreates the entire keyword tree" three source comments warn about) is 41 ms. The catalog side is milliseconds throughout, checked against a real 669 MB index (41,440 images, 1,665 keywords, 134,740 links): Catalog::keywords() 65 ms, categoryItems 41 ms, imagesUnderKeyword 55 ms, pruneUnusedKeywords 3 ms, and a single-row Catalog::commit (its own transaction, WAL, the FTS delete-and-insert and the link rewrite) 0.40 ms. MountSnapshot::take(), which that commit calls once per row, is 0.41 ms. Batching the commits into one transaction would be 0.043 ms a row: an optimisation, not a bug.

The minutes are still unnamed, and the instrument is in place rather than a guess. The sampled drop wrote almost nothing, so the per-image half never showed itself; a move that files thousands of images is a different regime. MW::applyKeywordMoves carries a phase stopwatch (MovePhases, WritePhases in Main/keywordedit.cpp) that prints one [PERF] KWMOVE line whenever a move takes over a second, always, not only under --perfprobe: a move that took a minute is a bug report the user is already holding.

The method generalises: sample the running app before fixing GUI latency; do not reason about where the time goes.

#### 16.13.3 Six Gotchas Found Reviewing the Keyword Path

A deliberate read of the whole keyword surface, done after the move was profiled rather than instead of profiling it. Six defects, none of which the performance work would have found, each verified rather than inferred.

1. A multi-keyword drag in the tree was a USE-AFTER-FREE. KeywordTree::dropEvent captured its target QModelIndex once and then looped over the dragged paths calling reparent or reparentMerging, both of which wrap their work in beginResetModel / endResetModel, and both of which call reload() when a write fails. A reset invalidates every index taken before it; reload() runs clearTree(), which DELETES every node. From the second keyword onward the target's internalPointer was dangling. (The tree is ExtendedSelection and startDrag joins every selected path, so a two-keyword drag is a supported gesture.) The target is carried as a PATH now and re-resolved each pass, re-checking validity (an earlier pass can legitimately have merged it away). An INVALID target is the root, so that case is a flag rather than an empty path.
2. mergeNodes threw away the one result the file had been repaired for. rewritePaths' writes used to be issued and their results discarded, which is how the null-synonyms bug in writeNode stayed hidden; every caller was fixed except this one, the worst place for it: reparentMerging wraps the merge in a transaction precisely so that a half-merged vocabulary cannot be read back, and a discarded failure returned success and let that transaction COMMIT the half-rewritten branch.
3. insertChild's conflict guard NEVER FIRED. The insert is ON CONFLICT(pathfold) DO NOTHING and the guard was "if (!id)" on lastInsertId(). sqlite3_last_insert_rowid() keeps the rowid of the last SUCCESSFUL insert on the connection, so a refused row leaves it reporting somebody else's id (verified: two inserts then a conflicting one leaves it at 2 with changes() == 0). The node built from that id would alias a live row, go into byId over the real node, and have every later writeNode update the wrong row. numRowsAffected() is the test that answers the question. (The catalog writer had the same bug: [16.13.1 Schema 12: The Links Drifted From the Text (Third Data Repair)](#16131-schema-12-the-links-drifted-from-the-text-third-data-repair).)
4. Every vocabulary mutation COLLAPSED THE TREE. rename, reparent, merge, insertChild, remove and reload all call beginResetModel, and QTreeView collapses on a reset; one drop can reset the model several times. The principle was already written at MW::ensureKeywordVocabLoaded (which declines to reload a populated vocabulary so being raised as a tab does not collapse the branch being read); it had not been applied to the mutators. KeywordTree::rememberOpenBranches / restoreOpenBranches now hang off the model's own modelAboutToBeReset and modelReset (hooked to the MODEL, since three of the six routes are taken by the view without telling anyone), keyed on the FOLDED PATH. A renamed branch reappears collapsed, which is honest: it is a different branch now.
5. A multi-keyword drop on the TAG ZONE rewrote every sidecar once per keyword. KeywordTags::dropEvent emitted addRequested per path, each calling MW::applyKeywordsToSelection with rebuildFilters defaulting to true: five keywords on a 200-image selection was 1,000 sidecar writes instead of 200, five ModifyDate bumps per file and five rebuilds of the keyword tree, for ONE gesture. A new addManyRequested signal carries the whole drop.
6. The progress bar was set up wrong in two of the three loops (it only mattered once Popup::pulse made it paint at all). MW::retagKeywordPath made the bar visible but never called setProgressMax, so it pinned at full on any run longer than the last operation's maximum; the move path never made it visible or set a maximum, so the one operation that can take minutes had no bar. The RANGE is set where the rows are counted now, in applyKeywordsToSelection itself; VISIBILITY stays with the caller, which knows whether this is a long rewrite or a single-image tag that would flicker one for nothing.

## 17 Catalog and Library

Terms: the CATALOG is one index of the folders the user designated; the LIBRARY is the browsing scope that shows everything the catalog holds, through the Library tree ([17.3 The Library Tree (LibTree)](#173-the-library-tree-libtree)).

### 17.1 The Catalog (Cross-Folder Search)

A local index of what Winnow has learned about images it has seen, so a keyword or title search answers ACROSS FOLDERS instead of only inside the one loaded. Tables image / keyword / image_keyword (plus image_version and image_embedding) and the image_fts full-text index, in the shared local index database (Cache/cachedb.h, [12.7.1 Design](#1271-design)). Cache/catalog.h is the class.

It is an INDEX, not a library in the Lightroom sense, and that distinction is the whole design. The XMP sidecar (or the image's own embedded XMP) remains the source of truth, every column is re-readable from the image and its sidecar, and the catalog itself never writes into anyone's photographs (keyword and metadata edits are written to the files by their own paths, then re-committed here). That is what lets the catalog share the preview cache's move-it-aside-and-rebuild failure policy: losing this file costs a rescan, never data.

The one thing that is not derived lives somewhere else. The folders the user nominates (the scope table, include / exclude rows with a recurse flag) are user intent, not rebuildable, and CacheDb::moveAside discards index.db without asking, so the scope table is in QSettings (Main/settings.cpp, catalogScope). Putting it in the database would mean a corrupt index silently forgot what the user asked to be indexed. The authored keyword vocabulary is likewise not in the index: it lives in userdata.db ([16.4 The Vocabulary (the Keyword List)](#164-the-vocabulary-the-keyword-list)).

#### 17.1.1 How Rows Arrive

- Opportunistically, from MW::folderChangeCompleted, alongside the devPreview sweep and for the same reasons: metadata is complete by then, the user is no longer waiting, and the work runs off the GUI thread. DataModel::catalogRows() reads the model ON THE GUI THREAD into plain values (QStandardItemModel is not thread-safe), and only those values cross to the pool thread that inserts them. Commit is deliberately NOT called per image from addMetadataForItem: that fires once per image on a Reader thread whose backpressure is already tuned, and a database write there is the per-row signal fan-out that has twice been the cause of folder-load lag.
- From the background scanner, for the designated folders ([17.15 Cataloguing Designated Folders](#1715-cataloguing-designated-folders)).
- Rows that are not MetaLoaded are SKIPPED. Cataloguing a half-read row is worse than cataloguing nothing: it would be stored with empty keywords, its freshness stamp would then MATCH on the next visit, and the blank entry would look current until its file changed on disk.

Freshness is (srcsize, srcmtime, sidecarmtime). The sidecar stamp is the load-bearing one for a raw library: Lightroom edits keywords by rewriting the .xmp and never touches the NEF, so a check that looked only at the image would never notice. Unchanged rows are skipped before any write, which matters because the opportunistic capture runs on EVERY folder change: without the skip, a user pacing between two folders would rewrite both indefinitely.

#### 17.1.2 Keywords in the Index

- NORMALISED into keyword + image_keyword rather than kept as text on the image row, so the category list ("every keyword, with counts") is an index scan rather than a quarter of a million string splits. Links are REPLACED on re-index, not added to, so a keyword deleted in Lightroom disappears here too.
- Keyed on the FULL PATH (schema 10). Each commit links an image to keywordPrefixExpand(keywordEffectivePaths(...)) of the text it stores, so an ancestor is an ordinary keyword row linked directly to every image beneath it. Querying a keyword is plain equality on pathfold, with no subtree walk, no LIKE and no recursive CTE, and a parent's count is already its subtree total. (Schema 4 keyed on namefold alone and merged two places into one keyword; schema 3 kept BOTH the leaf and the path as separate rows, listing the same keyword twice with its count split. Leaf consumption is what lets schema 10 have the hierarchy without that duplication.) See [16.2 Keyword Identity Is the Full Path](#162-keyword-identity-is-the-full-path).
- image.keywordpaths and image.keywords_literal (schema 7) hold the verbatim strings, which is what lets every keyword migration (10, 11, 12, 15) rebuild the links without re-reading a file. It is done in C++ rather than SQL because a recursive CTE would have to reimplement keywordFold, and SQLite's lower() is not QString::toCaseFolded() (they disagree on anything non-ASCII, and a pathfold that disagreed with the writer's would produce duplicates ON CONFLICT cannot see).

The stamp reset is NARROW, and getting that wrong was instructive. Schemas 6 and 7 cleared (srcsize, srcmtime, sidecarmtime) on EVERY row because they widened what every row means. Schema 10 does not: only a CARRIED-FORWARD row (indexed before schema 7, so its old keyword names were kept as depth-1 paths) gains anything from a re-read, and kw_carry names exactly that set. Resetting every row produced three symptoms that looked unrelated: a stamp of -1 never matches the file, so MW::refreshStaleRows (the scroll-in verification) treated a whole 43,000-image library as out of date; it CLEARS THE ICON of a stale row before queuing the re-read, so thumbnails blanked as they scrolled into view; and clearing a row back to MetaNotAttempted DECREMENTS metadataAttemptedCount, so G::allMetadataAttempted flapped false, which silently disabled the entire filter panel. The lesson is not about keywords: a migration's stamp reset is a library-wide re-read, and it should name the rows that need it.

#### 17.1.3 Full-Text Search

The full-text table is a PLAIN fts5, not contentless and not external-content: contentless needs the original text handed back on every delete, so a second copy is kept anyway; external-content cannot span the image_keyword join. The duplicated text costs \~200 bytes an image and buys prefix search, AND / OR / NOT, phrase queries and BM25 ranking with no query code of Winnow's own. What the user typed becomes a MATCH expression through the SHARED grammar ([18.3 Searching Folders and Catalog (One Grammar)](#183-searching-folders-and-catalog-one-grammar)).

- Quoting every term is not cosmetic: an unquoted term containing punctuation is a MATCH syntax error, and a syntax error fails the whole query, so an apostrophe or a hyphen mid-word would break the search rather than narrow it.
- Negated text is a separate NOT EXISTS, not FTS5's NOT operator, which is binary: "-heron" has no left-hand side to subtract from. Excluded KEYWORDS are a NOT EXISTS too, over image_keyword: joining would multiply the rows and then need a DISTINCT to undo it.
- Every value is BOUND, never interpolated, including the FTS expression. The search box is user text and the catalog shares its file with the preview index (tst_catalog::searchTextIsNotInjectable).
- Text columns are NOT NULL and bind through a helper: a default-constructed QString is SQL NULL to QSqlQuery, not '', and an image with no title, lens or GPS is the ORDINARY case, so binding QString() directly aborted the whole folder's transaction on the first such row ("NOT NULL constraint failed: image.label"). Catalog's text() supplies the empty string.

#### 17.1.4 Sharing a File With the Previews

- Neither tenant may override the other's database location. Both open lazily and either may be first, so Catalog::ensureLoadedLocked only supplies the DEFAULT path when nothing has been set. An unconditional setPath would close every open connection, bump the generation and silently drag a relocated database (a test's temp dir) back to AppDataLocation.
- Clearing one tenant does not clear the other: "Clear preview cache" deletes devpreview rows and payloads only; clearing the catalog leaves the previews alone. They share a file, not a lifetime (tst_catalog::clearingPreviewsLeavesTheCatalog pins both directions).
- The sweep DEMOTES, never deletes, and skips unmounted volumes, the devPreview sweep's rule for the same reason: an ejected drive must not read as a mass deletion. A demoted row stops appearing in searches but survives, and the next commit that sees the file promotes it. A delete Winnow performs ITSELF is certain, so FileOps::onDeleted removes the row outright, including its image_fts row (which has no foreign key and would otherwise keep matching text for an image that no longer exists).
- MountSnapshot and SrcStamp live in Cache/mountsnapshot.h, shared, because both tenants index paths across removable media and must answer "which volumes are mounted" and "is this still the same file" identically.

### 17.2 Loading Catalog Results Into the Model

Catalog results are LOADED into the ordinary datamodel rather than shown in a second kind of model: the images then appear in the ordinary views, where the loupe, Develop, ratings and filtering all work on them exactly as on a folder.

- Loading results is the same reset as a folder change. MW::loadCatalogResults does what folderSelectionChange does (stop(), drop the develop caches, refill, let folderChangeCompleted run), because everything downstream of the model (MetaRead, the icon chunks, the image cache, Develop) assumes that when the model's contents are replaced it was told to stop first. The develop-cache reset is MW::resetDevelopCachesForNewFolder, shared by both, so a cache added in future cannot be dropped on one path and forgotten on the other.
- DataModel::addPaths is the model half. Every other load path starts from a directory, but a result set is a list of files from any number of folders. It reuses addFolder's BATCHED insert (one setRowCount, signals blocked, one wide dataChanged), because a result set is routinely thousands of rows, the exact shape that made per-row signals the folder-load bottleneck. It takes the same proxy-sort bracket as scheduleProcessing, or the one wide dataChanged would make the sorted proxy re-sort the inserted block Z-A. It registers EVERY distinct parent folder in folderList / folderSet / folderImageCount (what the Folders filter category, removeFolder and isFolderLoaded read). It ends by emitting folderChange, so nothing downstream needs to know where the images came from. A set the catalog resolved is filled from the index rather than re-read ([17.11 Loading a Catalog Scope](#1711-loading-a-catalog-scope)).
- It checks that the files are still there. A row can name a file since deleted or on an unmounted volume; the sweep demotes those, but only when it has run since, so addPaths stats each path as well: fewer results are better than one that cannot be opened.
- The Folders panel deliberately does not follow: the results span many folders, and highlighting an arbitrary one would misrepresent what is loaded.

#### 17.2.1 The Legacy Catalog Dock

Superseded by the Filter dock ([18.1 The Filter Dock (Folders and Catalog)](#181-the-filter-dock-folders-and-catalog)) when G::useFilterPanel is true, the default: the Catalog panel's search box, Keywords category and Load button became the Catalog scope of one panel, and the separate dock (Views/catalogview.cpp) is not built at all. The flag still restores it. In that dock:

- It searches the INDEX, where Filters searches the DATAMODEL, and it shows no thumbnails (a picture list in a narrow dock would be a worse version of the grid): it reports how many images matched and offers to LOAD them.
- Searching is debounced (250 ms), and an empty query deliberately does nothing (offering to load a quarter of a million images is not an answer to having typed nothing).
- Its Keywords category is a FLAT list of paths, labelled with the leaf, the full path in the tooltip; click includes, Opt+click excludes, clicking an item already in that state clears it. The selection lives in the view and survives a rebuild.
- LOAD replaces, ADD appends (DataModel::addPaths was already additive and skips paths already in the model), which is what makes two searches combinable.
- With no catalog (the index will not open, or is empty) the panel says so inline and the controls are disabled.
- The dock's registration followed the full new-dock checklist (catalog_white.png glyph, graphicFor / dockFor / dockForTabText, dockTextNames, dockTabToolTip, winnowStateVersion 4 and a MW::placeDocksAddedSince row). It ships off by default.

There is ONE search key: F2 opens the search row in whichever scope is current. It used to be two (F2 "search the folders", Shift+F2 "search the catalog"), and each forced its scope on the way in, so the key you had learnt threw away the scope you were working in.

### 17.3 The Library Tree (LibTree)

#### 17.3.1 Library and Catalog Are Two Levels, Not Two Names

The LIBRARY is everything Winnow browses: every catalog, seen together. A CATALOG is one index with its folder rules (Manage Catalog...). There is one catalog today, but more than one per Library is intended, so user-visible words are chosen by meaning: what is browsed says Library (the toggle, the tree's top row, File > Open Library, "Filters (Library)"); what configures an index says Catalog (Manage Catalog..., Scan, "Nothing is catalogued yet"). Code identifiers keep Catalog\* (G::Scope::Catalog is the Library scope). Do not "fix" the split by renaming one side to the other. The UI never says "forget" for the catalog: it is "Remove from Catalog".

#### 17.3.2 The Source Panel Is Folders or Library, One at a Time

Its title bar carries an exclusive pair of buttons beside "Source" (MW::createFolderDock; sourceFoldersBtn / sourceLibraryBtn), and the body is a QStackedWidget holding FSTree and LibTree (Views/libtree.h). QToolButtons, not QPushButtons (the global QPushButton min-width in widgetcss.cpp would widen the dock). MW::styleSourceToggle colours the lit half with G::selectionColor, the colour a selected folder is lit with in the tree beneath.

- The toggle is a VIEW of G::scope, not a second copy of it. G::scope is the one fact, and MW::setScope is the only thing that changes it. The buttons act on clicked (never toggled): Library calls setCatalogScopeWhole, Folders calls MW::showFoldersSource, and MW::setScope pushes the scope back into the buttons and the stack with their signals blocked, RE-ASSERTED even when the scope did not change, so a refused switch leaves the toggle honest.
- A folder click switches to Folders the ordinary way (MW::folderSelectionChange calls setScope, which early-returns when nothing changed, so an ordinary folder click costs nothing).
- Folders goes back to what was loaded. setScope records the folder and its recurse flag from dm->scopeRequest() at the moment the Library replaces a folder load (lastFolderPath / lastFolderRecurse), and showFoldersSource replays it through FSTree::select (the normal folder load, with the un-ingested-picks guard; a refusal pushes the toggle back to Library). With nothing to go back to it asks okToDiscardPicks, stops the load and shows "Select a folder.": the Library's rows must not stay on screen under a toggle that says Folders. Known limit: a multi-folder Cmd selection comes back as its primary folder only.

#### 17.3.3 A LibTree Click Filters; It Does Not Load

The whole Library is already loaded ([17.19.1 What Selecting the Catalog Actually Cost (14.2 s to 1.7 s, and the Three Bugs Underneath)](#17191-what-selecting-the-catalog-actually-cost-142-s-to-17-s-and-the-three-bugs-underneath)), so reloading a folder's worth would only add cost. A click CHECKS THE FOLDER in the Filters panel's Folders category, and that category is the ONE folder filter: LibTree holds no filter state of its own.

- It asks (LibTree::folderFilterRequested -> MW::applyLibraryFolderFilter -> Filters::setFolderFilter, which sets every folder item and emits ONE filterChange), and MW pushes the result back (MW::syncLibTreeFromFilters -> LibTree::syncFromFilters) after every filter change and every build. So a folder checked in Filters lights up in LibTree, Clear All clears both, and neither can disagree. Selection by the mouse is disabled (NoSelection): what is selected is what Filters includes.
- A click during the load WAITS: BuildFilters::build runs on a thread, so the Folders category is empty until its Done op runs on the GUI thread. The request is kept in pendingLibraryFolderFilter and applied on BuildFilters::finishedBuildFilters (MW::applyPendingLibraryFolderFilter). (Applying it at the click, or where the build is ASKED for, checks an item about to be deleted or not yet made: the retired year rows taught that, and appeared to do nothing at all.) A folder the Library lists but no loaded row is in (all its raws hidden behind JPGs, say) says so in a popup rather than being a dead click.

The clicks, in FSTree's vocabulary:

```
click         the folder AND every folder in it ("2020-2029" is the decade)
Opt+click     this folder only = include it, exclude each folder directly in it
Cmd+click     add or remove the folder, keeping the others
Shift+click   every visible folder from the last one clicked to this one
Library row   no folder filter; the other categories are left alone
Return/Space  the current row, as a click
```

"This folder only" is deliberately NOT a new kind of filter: include-plus-exclude-children is what the Filters panel can already say, so it shows there truthfully. The default is the subtree, not FSTree's folder-only, because a folder holding no images of its own (2020-2029) would otherwise be a click that shows nothing.

#### 17.3.4 Bookmarks Follow the Source

Bookmarks is a list of folders, so it means what the Source panel means: in Folders a bookmark LOADS its folder (FSTree::select); in the Library it FILTERS the Library to it (MW::bookmarkClicked sends BookMarks::libraryFolders(path) to MW::requestLibraryFolderFilter, the request a LibTree click on that folder makes). Before this, a bookmark click in the Library silently switched back to Folders and reloaded from disk.

- A bookmark click CLEARS EVERY OTHER FILTER FIRST (2026-10-01, user decision), as a Collections or Queries click does: all Filters categories, the search text and the pick / rating / colour actions, then the folder is set, in one filterChange (requestLibraryFolderFilter(includes, excludes, clearOthers = true); a LibTree click passes false and only narrows). The clear rides in pendingLibraryFolderFilter with the folders. If none of the bookmark's folders has a Filters item, the clear is applied with its own filterChange.
- The count is the LIBRARY's in the Library (images at or beneath the folder: FolderTree::expandCounts over Catalog::liveFolderCounts, pushed by MW::updateLibraryTree through BookMarks::setLibraryFolders); in Folders it is the disk count. Blank in the Library until the first read lands.
- A bookmark ABOVE the Library's include folders asks for the include folders beneath it (the Filters Folders tree starts at the include folders, so the bookmark's own path would have no row to check).
- A bookmark the Library holds nothing in is DIMMED with the reason in its tooltip ("Not in the Library. Click to open it in Folders.") and still works: the click falls through to the Folders load. A dead row would strand a bookmark the user put there on purpose.
- The highlight is the Library folder filter's (BookMarks::syncFromLibraryFilter): the bookmark whose request equals the current includes, with no excludes, is lit. MW::setScope sets the mode (BookMarks::setLibraryMode), which clears the other source's highlight.
- The path moved out of the tooltip into BookMarks::PathRole (read with BookMarks::pathOf), so the tooltip can carry the reason; every reader goes through pathOf. BookMarks::select matches by path, not folder name, so two bookmarks named "2024" on different drives no longer select each other.

#### 17.3.5 A Folder's Identity Is Its Path

The Folders filter matched G::FolderNameColumn (the folder's NAME), and the user's library held 22 names shared by 1,599 folders ("DxO" eight times), so ticking one ticked all of them. It now filters on G::FolderPathsAllColumn: the row's folder and every folder above it (FolderTree::ancestry), so "this folder and everything in it" is QStringList::contains, exactly the move G::KeywordsAllColumn makes for keyword paths; FilterPredicate did not change.

- The row stores ONE interned id (G::FolderPathColumn, folderPathId); RowStore keeps one ancestry list per distinct folder (mFolderAncestry, filled on write under the write lock) and every row in the folder shares it, so the column costs a row 2 bytes (tst_imagerow::folderAncestryCostsARowOneId). FolderPathsAll is read-only (RowStore::setValue refuses it). G::FolderNameColumn is unchanged; TableView and keywordedit still read the name.
- Counts arrive per folder and are rolled up by Filters. The snapshot slot is FilterCat::FolderPath (the raw path, NOT trimmed: a folder called "Trip " is a different folder), counted like any single-valued slot. Filters rolls every map for the folders category up to the ancestors (FolderTree::expandCounts) on receipt, an exact sum because an image is in exactly one folder. (Keywords cannot do this, since an image can sit under a parent twice, which is why they expand at write time.)
- The catalog side matches a subtree too: Catalog::buildQueryLocked turns a FolderPathsAll include or exclude into (folder = p OR (folder >= 'p/' AND folder &lt; 'p0')), a half-open range rather than LIKE, because '\_' is a LIKE wildcard and folder names are full of underscores ('0' is one past '/'). Pinned by tst_catalog::folderQueryTakesTheSubtreeAndNothingBeside. (The older cq.folder clause still uses LIKE and has the underscore problem; it is not on this path.)

#### 17.3.6 One Set of Hierarchy Rules

Utilities/foldertree.h, used by both trees so they cannot disagree about a parent, a top row or a label.

- Top-level rows are ANCHORS. In the Library: the catalog's include folders (MW::catalogScopeEffective(true)), pushed into Filters by setScope (Filters::setFolderAnchors), so both trees start at "Photos" rather than "/". In Folders scope: the folders SELECTED in the Folders tree (FolderTree::outermost of FSTree::selectedFolderPaths), pushed by buildFiltersWhenModelReady just before each build, because a Cmd- or Shift-click adds to the selection without changing the scope. (The first version used the deepest folder the rows share instead, so two folders picked side by side in Pictures became ONE row, and the panel greys a category with a single item, so Folders looked disabled.) With no anchors at all, the common-ancestor rule is the fallback.
- Folders between an anchor and the folders holding images are synthesised (they are what selects a branch). An anchor inside another is just a folder; a folder under no anchor becomes its own; two anchors with the same name each add their parent's name; siblings sort naturally ("2" before "10", case-insensitive, QCollator).
- FolderTree::normalize is the one spelling (forward slashes, no trailing slash except a root); Main/catalogscope.h's catalogScopeNormalize delegates to it. Pinned by tst_foldertree.
- A NESTED category is counted at every depth: Filters::setEachCatTextColor, isCatFiltering and disableEmptyCat used childCount(), which greyed a Library under one catalogued root and never lit the header of a category whose checked item sat below the top level (a deep keyword included). They count Filters::itemsInCategory now.

#### 17.3.7 Built From the Index

LibTree is built from the INDEX, not the model, so it is ready the moment the toggle is pressed. MW::updateLibraryTree reads Catalog::liveFolderCounts (live = 1; folderCounts counts demoted rows too, which reconciling needs and a tree must not offer) and stats each anchor (a stat that can stall on a dead network mount) OFF THE GUI THREAD, one read at a time with a single follow-up pass if asked again meanwhile. The Library row's total is the sum of what is shown, not Catalog::count(). It is refreshed at startup, on entering the Library, after a scan, a reconcile, a folder-load commit, a delete (refreshAfterRemoval) and the panel's Refresh button. Anchors whose volume is missing grey their whole subtree, with the reason in the tooltip and on the disabled context-menu items.

- LibrarySource is the multi-catalog seam, and the only one. LibTree::setSources takes a list of {id, name, anchors, folderCounts, offlineAnchors}; MW builds one today. With more than one, each gets a row under Library whose click includes its anchors; with one, that level is not created. The folder filter is keyed on path alone, which stays correct as long as two catalogs do not index the same folder.
- READ-ONLY. The context menu offers Reveal in Folders (switches to Folders and selects it through FSTree::select), Show in Finder / Explorer (MW::revealInFileBrowser) and Manage Catalog.... There is no rename, move or drop, and LibTree refuses drops outright: a MoveAction a target accepts makes IconView::startDrag trash the dragged files ([16.8.5 The Drag Must Not Delete the Photographs](#1685-the-drag-must-not-delete-the-photographs)).
- Expansion persists in the "LibTreeExpanded" setting (paths), written on every expand / collapse, and survives a rebuild along with the scroll position.

### 17.4 The Retired Catalog Scope Tree (Design Record)

Retired 2026-09-24. Before LibTree, the Source panel held a small Catalog tree (Views/catalogscopetree.\*, a Catalog row with a row per year) above the Folders tree, under a "Catalog" band and a "Folders" band. It replaced a checkable QToolButton and was itself replaced by the Folders | Library toggle. Its reasoning that still holds where the code moved:

- G::scope as the one fact, with every entry point routed through MW::setScope and the result pushed back to every view; and re-asserting the view even when the scope does not change, so a click on the current scope leaves it selected rather than cleared.
- A pending filter check waits for BuildFilters::finishedBuildFilters (emitted by the build's Done op, on the GUI thread), not for the click or the build request; and when the filters are ALREADY built there is no rebuild to wait for (build() returns early on filtersBuilt and would never emit), so it applies immediately.
- A MAXIMUM height, never a fixed one. setFixedHeight also sets the minimum, and a minimum on a docked widget propagates out through the dock to QMainWindow's minimumSizeHint, so Qt resized the WINDOW to satisfy it: expanding a twenty-year catalog in a short dock grew the whole application, in a runaway (the cap was measured against the parent's height, which the minimum had just made taller). A maximum plus a sizeHint, the minimum pinned at one row and QSizePolicy::Maximum, is the safe shape.
- Size columns from the VIEWPORT, not from width(): the stretched last section ends where the viewport ends, which is already short by the scrollbar and any margin.
- Counts are written without a thousands separator and the column grows rather than eliding ("43,050" in a narrow column came out "43,0..."), measured with the widget's own font.
- FSTree::folderSelectionChange, not QAbstractItemView::clicked, is the hook that covers every click: FSTree::mousePressEvent chains to the base class on only one branch, so clicked() never fires for a Cmd, Opt or Shift click.
- The panel is called "Source" (what both halves answer: where the images come from), and help is Docs/sourcecatalogfoldershelp.html.
- Verified by driving it, not by reading it: a temporary probe at the --selftest exit flipped the scope both ways and reported the state.

### 17.5 Collections

A set of Library images the user put together by hand: Lightroom's collection. Each is a row in the Collections panel (Window > Collections Panel; off by default, like Keywords; tabbed with Bookmarks). A QUERY is Lightroom's smart collection ([17.6 Queries and the Query Builder](#176-queries-and-the-query-builder)); both share one store and one widget.

#### 17.5.1 Nesting and Reordering

Collections nest. Dragging collection A onto the middle of collection B makes A B's last child; dragging it onto the blank space below the rows puts it last at the top level. Drag reordering (2026-10-13): dropping A on the top or bottom quarter of a row puts it BEFORE or AFTER that row as its sibling, at any level, so one drag both reorders and re-parents; a highlight-coloured line marks the insertion point (after an expanded branch means its first child). A drop into itself, its own subtree or where it already is shows the no-drop cursor. CollectionTree::nodeDropSpot works out the spot from the pointer, and CollectionStore::move(id, parent, beforeId) writes it, renumbering the new siblings' node.position 0..n-1 in one transaction (tst_collections::moveReordersAndRenumbersSiblings). The Queries panel gets the same, since it is the same widget. Expansion persists in "CollectionTreeExpanded" (node ids).

#### 17.5.2 A Collection Is a Filter, Not a Dataset

User decision 2026-09-29, replacing a first build in which a click reloaded the Library as a new dataset holding the collection. The whole Library stays loaded; each collection is an item in the Filters panel's COLLECTIONS category (under Folders), and a click in the Collections panel checks it there. So a collection combines with every other filter exactly as a folder does (OR within the category, AND across categories, Opt+click in the Filters panel to EXCLUDE a collection), and no click ever reloads anything or asks about picks.

The Collections panel is a SECOND VIEW of the category, as LibTree is of Folders: the panel ASKS (CollectionTree::filterRequested -> MW::applyCollectionFilter -> Filters::setCollectionFilter, which sets the whole category and emits ONE filterChange), and MW pushes back what the category holds (MW::syncCollectionTreeFromFilters, called from syncLibTreeFromFilters after every filter change and every build). A collection checked in the Filters panel, Clear All, or a restored Library filter all show in the panel; the two cannot disagree.

Library only.
