In Folders the panel stays on screen greyed, with the reason above it, and the Filters category is hidden and UNCHECKED (Filters::setCollectionsAvailable, from MW::updateCollectionsAvailability, which MW::setScope calls on every scope change): a hidden check would go on filtering where nobody could see it. The menu items follow (2026-10-03, user decision): in Folders, Window > Collections Panel and Window > Queries Panel are DISABLED, each with "Library only: choose Library at the top left of the window." as its tooltip (MW::updateLibraryOnlyActions, from createActions and setScope). A panel already open stays on screen, greyed with its own reason. (File > Manage Catalog... was disabled in Folders too until 2026-10-16, when it was re-enabled in both sources: it configures the index, which is set up from Folders as often as from the Library.)

#### 17.5.3 The Clicks

The Folders panel's (FSTree), as asked: click = filter to this collection; Opt+click = it and every collection inside it; Cmd+click = add or remove it; Shift+click = every visible collection from the last one clicked.

- A click CLEARS EVERY OTHER FILTER FIRST (2026-09-30, user decision): all Filters categories, the search text and the pick / rating / colour actions are cleared, as Clear All does, and then the category is set, in one filterChange (MW::applySetFilter). A click means "show me this collection", not "narrow what I am looking at". Cmd+click off the last checked collection is Cancel.
- The tree acts on the RELEASE, not the press, so pressing on a row to drag it does not filter first. Return / Space act on the current row; F2 renames. NoSelection: what is selected is what the category includes.
- A click during a load is refused with a popup: the load's build clears the category's checks when it lands, so the click would be swept away unseen.
- DIRECT membership: checking a parent collection in the Filters panel matches the images directly in it, not its children's. The Collections panel's Opt+click is what adds every collection inside.
- CANCEL clears the Collections category (includes and excludes) and nothing else. It is the title bar's reset button (disabled, with the reason in its tooltip, while no collection is filtering; MW::syncCollectionsCancel) and the context menu's last item (MW::cancelCollectionFilter).

#### 17.5.4 The Column and the Category

The category filters on G::CollectionsColumn: the ids, as text, of the collections a row is DIRECTLY in. It is NOT in the row store (collections change without the row changing, and they are the user's, not the image's), so DataModel::data answers it from a side table, row KEY -> ids (DataModel::setCollectionMembership, under a read-write lock; G::KeyRole, so a version is its own row). MW::refreshCollectionMembership builds that table in two statements whatever the Library's size: CollectionStore::membershipByKey (pathkey -> ids) and Catalog::pathsForKeys (pathkey -> image.path, one json_each statement per page). image.path is the exact string every Library row was loaded with, so a filter pass is one hash lookup per row. It is rebuilt on every membership change (CollectionStore::membersChanged: adds, removes, and FileOps moves and deletes), and a refilter follows when a collection is filtering, so an image removed from the collection being looked at leaves the grid at once.

The category is MW's, not BuildFilters'. Every other category is built from the loaded rows; this one's items are the user's collections, which exist whether or not anything loaded is in them.

- removeChildrenDynamicFilters never touches it. MW fills it from the store (MW::refreshCollectionNodes -> Filters::setCollectionNodes, which keeps each item's check, expansion and count by ID across a rename or re-parent, and emits a filterChange only when a checked collection was deleted), and pushes the LOADED counts after every build (MW::updateCollectionCounts on BuildFilters::finishedBuildFilters; clearAll and uncheckAllFilters blank every item's counts).
- Because its items survive a build, the Library's saved filters restore into it (save / restore key a nested category on data(1), the id).
- setEachCatTextColor and isCatFiltering exempt it from "a category of one item is not filtering": one collection is still a subset.
- It is not in Filters::fillQuery, so a CAPPED catalog search (G::maxSearchResults) does not narrow the loaded set by collection; the proxy filter still applies.

#### 17.5.5 Adding and Removing

- Thumbnails dropped on a collection (MW::addPathsToCollection) are filtered to Library images: rows in the loaded model, or, for a Finder drag, paths Catalog::availabilityOf knows.
- Sidecars riding along with a thumbnail drag are skipped, and so is their share of the drag cursor's COUNT BADGE on macOS: AppKit badges a multi-file drag with one per URL, sidecars included, so while the drag is over the Collections panel the badge is set to the images alone (CollectionTree showImageCountBadge -> Mac::setDragBadgeCount, applied through NSDraggingInfo.numberOfValidItemsForDrop by a wrapper round QNSView's draggingEntered: / draggingUpdated:, Mac::installDragBadgeHook in Utilities/mac.mm; AppKit's own count is put back when the drag moves on). Windows drags carry no count.
- The drop is ALWAYS a CopyAction, on enter, move and drop: a MoveAction accepted here would make IconView::startDrag trash the files.
- The context menu offers "Add Selected Images to" and "Remove Selected Images from" as the discoverable path; Remove is enabled only for a collection the grid is filtered to (anywhere else "the selection" is images from some other set).

#### 17.5.6 Versions Are Members in Their Own Right

A version is stored by its row key, path + "/#v" + id; cachePathKey of that is the file's pathkey plus the same suffix, so the member table needs no second scheme. refreshCollectionMembership looks a version member up in the catalog by its file's pathkey and puts the suffix back (VersionKey::make).

- A version does NOT inherit its master's collections: Add to / Remove from act on the selected rows' KEYS (selectedKeys in Main/mwcollections.cpp), so a selected version is added or removed alone. (A thumbnail DRAG onto a collection carries file URLs, so a dragged version adds its file.)
- A move of the file carries its versions' memberships, suffix kept (CollectionStore::onMoved); a delete of the file takes them too (onDeleted); deleting a version record takes only its own (MW::deleteVersionRecords -> onDeleted(versionKey)). Versions made before this change are in no collection.
- New Version asks: when it is made for an image that is in collections, VersionCollectionsDlg (Dialogs/versioncollectionsdlg.h) lists those collections by tree path, all ticked; Cancel makes no version. With several images selected the list is the union, each collection showing how many of the selected images it holds, and each new version joins only the ticked collections its OWN origin is in. The memberships are added BEFORE the version rows are inserted (MW::newVersion), so with the grid filtered to a collection the new rows pass the filter as they arrive. CollectionStore::collectionsOf(key) is the lookup (tree order).
- A collection OPENS its version groups: choosing a collection expands every master that has a VERSION in the chosen collections, so the grid shows every member rather than a master with a "1 >" badge (the panel's count includes version rows). MW::expandVersionsForCollectionFilter, called from filterChange before the proxy invalidates, acts only when the set of collections filtered on CHANGES (lastCollectionIncludes), so collapsing a group while looking at a collection sticks; it waits until the membership table is built. Clearing the collection leaves the groups open. DataModel::keysInCollections is the lookup.

#### 17.5.7 Identity Is the Path

As everywhere in the index (Cache/pathkey.h): member.pathkey matches image.pathkey; member.path is kept so the file is readable and a move can be followed. A move or delete Winnow performs goes through FileOps::onMoved / onDeleted, which tell CollectionStore as well as the preview caches and the catalog: a moved image stays in its collections (a collection already holding the destination keeps one membership), a deleted one leaves them all. A file moved OUTSIDE Winnow stays a member and simply matches nothing until it is back. Known limit: there is no folder-rename hook (the catalog has none either).

#### 17.5.8 The Store Is Not index.db

Datamodel/userdb.h (UserDb) owns the file, userdata.db in AppDataLocation, with its schema and connection; Datamodel/collectionstore.h (CollectionStore) is the collections / queries / places API over it, and Datamodel/keywordvocab.h keeps the keyword vocabulary in it. The local index holds only what can be rebuilt and is moved aside when it cannot be migrated; a collection, a query, a place and a curated keyword list are the user's own work, so they live in their own file, and UserDb NEVER moves it aside. A file it cannot open, or one written by a newer Winnow, leaves Collections, Queries, Places and the Keywords dock's list unavailable with the reason in each panel and the file untouched (tst_collections::aNewerFileIsLeftUntouched). The Keywords dock greys its list with UserDb's reason; its tag zone still works, because tags are written to the images.

- Schema (PRAGMA user_version, additive only): 1 = node(id, parent, kind, name, position, definition, created, modified) with ON DELETE CASCADE on parent, and member(node, pathkey, path, added) keyed (node, pathkey); 2 = vocab, column for column as index.db had it; 3 = audit_verdict (and audit_skip) for [16.12 Audit Keywords (Finding Keywording Mistakes by How Images Look)](#1612-audit-keywords-finding-keywording-mistakes-by-how-images-look).
- node.kind: 0 collection, 1 query, a published value never renumbered. A Query's saved query is in node.definition.
- Foreign keys are switched on per connection, so a delete takes its subtree and every membership in it in one statement. GUI thread; one connection, with busy_timeout set before any other pragma so two instances opening the file at once wait rather than fail. The CollectionStore singleton moves itself to the GUI thread whichever thread touches it first.

It was collections.db until the keyword vocabulary joined it. The vocabulary had lived in index.db: user work in the one file whose failure policy is to throw itself away. Two one-time steps carry an existing install across, both in UserDb::db():

1. An existing collections.db, with its -wal and -shm files, is RENAMED to userdata.db before it is opened, sidecars first and the main file last, so a second Winnow starting at the same moment never sees a userdata.db whose WAL has not followed it. A failed rename puts the sidecars back and opens collections.db where it is (tst_collections::anOldCollectionsDbIsRenamedNotLost).
2. The schema 2 step ATTACHes index.db and copies its vocab table, ids and all so parents stay parents, shallowest first with foreign keys off for the copy so an orphan row cannot abort it (UserDb::importIndexVocab). It runs once per file because it IS the migration: a vocabulary the user later empties is never refilled from the old index (tst_collections::theVocabularyIsImportedFromTheIndexOnce). index.db keeps its vocab table (its schema is additive only), but nothing reads it after the copy.

#### 17.5.9 One Widget for Both Kinds

CollectionTree is constructed with a Kind; a Queries tree refuses thumbnail drops, hides Add / Remove, and sends New and Edit to the Query Builder. Both panels are built by MW::buildLibrarySetDock, and the Filters functions take the category as a parameter (Filters::setSetNodes / setSetCounts / setFilterState / setSetFilter / setLibrarySetsAvailable).

Registered as a dock in every place the dock checklist names: collections_white.png (a stack of photographs), graphicFor / dockFor, dockForTabText, dockTextNames, dockTabToolTip (no F-key, as Keywords), dockVisibleAction, placeDocksAddedSince (v9, tabbed with favDock), winnowStateVersion 9, workspaces (isCollectionsDockVisible; absent = off), full screen (Preferences "Show collections"), collapse state, diagnostics.

### 17.6 Queries and the Query Builder

A saved search over the Library: Lightroom's smart collection. Each is a row in the Queries panel (Window > Queries Panel; off by default; tabbed with Collections; Library only) and an item in the Filters panel's QUERIES category, directly under Collections. Like a collection it is a FILTER over the loaded Library, not a dataset: a click clears every other filter and checks it, checked queries OR together, the category ANDs with every other, Opt+click in the Filters panel excludes, and Cancel clears only the category. A query can sit inside another in the tree; that is organisation only (each matches by its own query).

#### 17.6.1 One Grammar, Three Places

Utilities/queryexpr.h. The Filters Search row, the Query Builder and a saved Query are three views of one expression: groups that match ALL / ANY / NONE of their children, holding rules (field + operator + values) and further groups. Query::Expr::parse and toText round-trip (text built by hand opens in the builder and comes back unchanged), and toJson is how a Query is stored. Both are PUBLISHED FORMATS: field keys and operator names are added, never renamed (Query::fields(), Query::opName). Pinned by tst_queryexpr (textRoundTrips, builderTreeSurvivesText, jsonRoundTrips).

The text grammar extends the Search row's, and everything it accepted means what it did: bare words AND-ed and matched as substrings of G::SearchTextColumn, "phrases", OR (binding looser than AND), -word and NOT word, (brackets). A word may be qualified by a field:

```
rating:>=3   rating:3..5   -rating:5       numbers: = < <= > >= a..b; -x is "is not"
label:red,yellow   -label:red              any of / none of
keyword:Fauna|Bird   -keyword:*            has it (or one beneath it) / has none
collection:"Trip 2024"                     in the collection of that name
title:heron  title:=Heron  title:her*  title:*ron  title:*  -title:*
captured:2024-05   captured:<2024-05-01   captured:2024-05-01..2024-06-30
shutter:1/250   iso:>3200   aperture:<=4   focal:400
gps:yes   developed:no   pick:rejected
```

- A QUOTED value is literal: no wildcard, no comparison prefix. OR, AND and NOT are operators in capitals only. A value is quoted by the printer only when it must be.
- An unknown field name made of letters ("colour:red") is reported by Expr::error (shown under the builder's text box) and searched as a plain word meanwhile; anything else with a colon ("10:30") is simply a word.
- Negation is no longer LIFTED. SearchTerms moved every negative to the top of the query because FTS5 cannot nest a NOT, so "(heron OR -eagle)" meant "heron AND NOT eagle". The query evaluator honours nesting. The catalog's FTS compilation still lifts, and is used only by a CAPPED catalog search (G::maxSearchResults > 0), and FilterPanel::currentQuery sends it the Search text only when the text is plain words (FTS would read "rating:>=3" as a word and match nothing). With field rules the capped set is the newest N, and the proxy applies the whole query to it.

#### 17.6.2 The Fields and How Each Type Compares

The main list (the builder's first block), then, after a separator, the REST OF THE DATAMODEL: every user-facing column the main list does not cover (folder name, ingested, video, has sidecar, exposure compensation, duration, focus point X/Y, GPS coordinates, file size (typed in MB, held in bytes: Field::scale), dimensions, aspect ratio, cropped dimensions and aspect, orientation, rotation, email, url, and the keywords as written in the file). Left out: the icon, row number, the macOS thumbnail handles, the Search flag, load timing and the icon aspect (bookkeeping, not facts about a photograph). Extras are Field::extra and sort by label. Each type compares as the column stores its value (Query::fields() names the column):

- Text: case-insensitive over the column's string.
- Number: parses the LEADING number of the value (a fraction such as 1/250 included, units ignored, so exposure compensation's "+0.7 EV" is 0.7) and compares with a small tolerance. A blank rating is 0, so rating:&lt;2 finds unrated images; any other blank matches no comparison.
- Date: compares the same-length PREFIX of "yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss.zzz", so 2024-05 is all of May and captured:&lt;2024-05 is before May began.
- Enum: folds case and yes/no to the stored true/false; honours is empty / is not empty, so "no label" can be said (-label:\*).
- List: QStringList::contains; because G::KeywordsAllColumn and G::FolderPathsAllColumn hold every ancestor, keyword:Fauna|Bird reaches everything beneath it.
- collection: values are NAMES, turned into ids by the Query::Resolver MW installs (MW::collectionIdsByName), once per compile, never per row. A renamed collection therefore stops matching a query that names it.
- An EMPTY group restricts nothing, so a group just added in the builder does not empty the grid.

#### 17.6.3 Evaluated Live

Not precomputed. FilterCategory gained includeExprs / excludeExprs (Datamodel/filterpredicate.h): SortFilter::compileFilters parses each checked query item once per compile (Filters::queryTextFor gives the Search row's text for searchTrue, negated as a NONE group for searchFalse, or a Query item's QueryTextRole), prepares it, and FilterPredicate::accepts evaluates it per row with the same valueFor as everything else. exprColumns makes readsColumn true for every column a query reads, so MW::editNeedsRefilter refilters after a rating or keyword edit (the old G::SearchColumn was precomputed per keystroke and went stale after an edit). DataModel::searchStringChange still writes G::SearchColumn, with the new evaluator, because the Search category's COUNTS are built from it. Pinned by tst_filterpredicate::queryExpressionsCombineLikeItems.

The Queries category is MW's, like Collections: MW::refreshQueryNodes gives Filters::setSetNodes each Query's text (Query::Expr::fromJsonText(definition).toText()) and the Search row's "Load query" list (Filters::setSavedQueries). setSetNodes emits a filterChange when a CHECKED query's text changed, so editing a query refilters at once. Its column is -1 (it reads none of its own). Counts (loaded images each query matches, for the category and the panel, CollectionTree::setCounts) are MW::updateQueryCounts after every build: queries x rows on the GUI thread, timed under G::isPerfProbe ("[PERF] updateQueryCounts"); not yet measured on a large Library.

#### 17.6.4 The Query Builder

Dialogs/querybuilder.h. QueryBuilderWidget shows the expression as rows:

- A group header "Match [all|any|none] of the following:" with "+ Rule" and "+ Group" (and - to remove a nested group, which is outlined and indented).
- A rule row: [field] [operator] [value] [and value] [-] [+], where Alt/Opt+click on + adds a group (Lightroom's gesture, layered on the visible "+ Group" button). The operator list and the value boxes follow the field's type (a second box for "is between", none for "is empty"); several values for "is any of" are separated by commas. A rule left blank is dropped.
- Value boxes offer TYPEAHEAD from what the loaded Library holds (MW::querySuggestions: distinct values of the field's column, capped at 5,000; collection names; an enum's own choices). A value the Library does not hold is RED: for a field with typeahead, a value box turns red (with the reason in its tooltip) when nothing offered CONTAINS what was typed, as the typeahead filters, so a half-typed name is not flagged; each value of an "any of" is checked.
- Below the rows, the SAME QUERY AS TEXT in a four-line scrolling box (a QPlainTextEdit), rewritten on every change; editing it and pressing Return (or leaving the box) rebuilds the rows, with any parse problem shown beneath. Shift+Return is a line break, read as a space.
- TEST, at the left of the button row, counts the loaded rows the query matches, out of all loaded rows (MW::countQueryMatches, through QueryBuilderDialog::setCounter; the other filters are not applied), and the count is cleared the moment the query changes.

QueryBuilderDialog wraps it two ways: AdHoc (the Search row: Apply writes the canonical text back through Filters::setSearchText, and "Save as Query..." adds it to the Queries panel without closing) and SavedQuery (a Name field; OK disabled until named).

Where it is reached:

- Search row right-click: "Build query...", "Save search as Query..." (renamed so it is not confused with the next), "Load query" (lists the Queries).
- Queries panel: + on the title bar, New Query..., Edit Query... (or double-click), Duplicate, Rename (F2), Delete, Move to Top Level, Cancel.
- Filters signals queryBuilderRequested / saveAsQueryRequested; MW::openQueryBuilderForSearch, saveQueryAs, newQuery, editQuery answer them.

#### 17.6.5 Save the Filters as a Query

Every Filters context menu (after "Filter on...") has "Save as a query...": it asks for a name (QInputDialog, through MW::saveQueryAs) and adds ONE query to the Queries panel that means what the panel's checks mean now. Filters::activeFiltersAsQuery walks the same checks SortFilter::compileFilters does:

- Each filtering category is ANDed; its includes are ORed ("Match all checked keywords" ANDs them); its excludes reject (a NONE group).
- A value becomes Query::matchValues(field, values): an any-of rule for an enum or list field (label:Red,Blue, keyword:"Fauna|Bird"), an exact match per value otherwise (title:="Great Blue Heron", iso:800, the item's value trimmed of the sort padding ISO and focal length carry). A BLANK value is "is empty" (rating:0 for a rating).
- Collections are written by NAME (collection:"Trip 2024"), the resolver mapping them back to ids. The Search row's query and checked Queries are copied in as sub-expressions (Not matching = NONE).
- A category the grammar has no field for (Map pins, Places, Availability, Compare, a "Filter on..." column outside the field list) is LEFT OUT, and the name dialog says which before anything is saved; the menu item's tooltip says so too. The item is greyed with the reason when nothing a query can hold is filtering ("- no filters set" / "- no filters a query can hold").
- The query is saved from its TEXT (parse(toText())), because that is what a saved Query is evaluated from; tst_queryexpr::filterValuesSurviveText pins each matchValues shape through that round trip. Signal: Filters::saveFiltersAsQueryRequested(text, notSaved).

#### 17.6.6 Store, Migration, Registration

- CollectionStore::create takes a definition; setDefinition changes one; duplicate copies a Query's definition (or a collection's members) as "&lt;name> copy". No schema change: node.definition was reserved at version 1.
- Saved searches migrated once. The Search row's saved text queries lived in QSettings ("SavedSearchQueries"); MW::migrateSavedSearchQueries turns each into a Query on the first launch of this build (flag "SavedSearchQueriesMigrated"), leaving the settings array in place so a rollback loses nothing. Filters::legacySavedSearchQueries is the reader.
- Registered as a dock at every checklist site: queries_white.png (a magnifier over a list), graphicFor / dockFor, dockForTabText, dockTextNames, dockTabToolTip (no F-key), dockVisibleAction, placeDocksAddedSince (v10, tabbed with collectionsDock), winnowStateVersion 10, workspaces (isQueriesDockVisible; absent = off), full screen (Preferences "Show queries"), collapse state, diagnostics. Expansion persists in "QueryTreeExpanded".

Not yet: relative dates ("in the last 30 days", "on this day"), a live match count inside the builder, a query that refers to another query (a cycle needs guarding), star / colour-chip / date-picker value editors, and the catalog SQL compilation (counts without a load, capped searches with field rules).

### 17.7 Index Schema and Migrations

The index (index.db, opened through CacheDb in Cache/cachedb.cpp) is shared by several tenants: the catalog's image, keyword and image_keyword tables, devpreview, thumb, develop history and more. CacheDb::schemaVersion() is the current version (kSchemaVersion, 23 as of 2026-10-17). Migrations are ADDITIVE: each version block runs once, in order, on PRAGMA user_version.

#### 17.7.1 Rules

- A version block that has already run must not be edited. Schema 7 was extended twice during development, and each time the local database had already recorded user_version = 7, so the new ALTER never ran, the table lacked the column, every INSERT failed, and the catalog silently wrote nothing ("the capture is broken again"). For an unreleased version, delete the development database; once a version has shipped, the only correct move is a new version number.
- A migration that adds columns a row needs must also invalidate the rows that lack them (schema 6 set every freshness stamp to -1; see [5.9.3 What the Catalog Must Store to Fill a Row](#593-what-the-catalog-must-store-to-fill-a-row)). Otherwise every existing row is incomplete while its stamp says it is current, and nothing re-reads it.
- tst_catalog's version literal is a tripwire, deliberately. Bumping kSchemaVersion fails it on purpose, so whoever bumps it has to confirm that every tenant of the shared file still coexists at the new version and add the new tenant's tables to the list. The migration case beside it compares against CacheDb::schemaVersion() instead, because it is about a version 3 file migrating all the way UP, not which number it stops at.
- The migration test uses the real file. Every existing user has an older index, so a test against a fresh database proves nothing about them. Rather than hand-write old DDL into the test (one more copy of the schema, the thing rowfields.h exists to avoid), it takes the real migrated file, puts it BACK to the older shape (drop the newer table, set user_version) and reopens. It then checks that image, keyword, image_keyword and devpreview are all still there: an additive migration that quietly dropped the catalog is a catastrophe a "does the new table exist" check would not notice.

#### 17.7.2 Data Repairs

Most versions add tables or columns. A few repair data:

- Schema 8: doubled path separators. The scanner walked roots spelled WITH a trailing separator (the folder tree spells them that way, and the old catalogRoots setting stored what it was handed), and Utilities::subFolderTree builds a subfolder by concatenation, so every row below such a root carried a doubled separator: /Users/x/Pictures//1980/03/img.jpg. On the library it was found on, 5,059 of 6,200 image rows and 172 of 1,400 devpreview rows. It never showed the wrong picture, which is why it survived a whole library: pathkey runs through QDir::cleanPath (Cache/pathkey.h), so every lookup matched and no duplicate row was inserted. Only the stored `path` carried the doubled form, and that is what searches hand back to the DataModel, availability checks and file operations. The scope table now normalises at every door. The repair deletes colliding image rows (a doubled row whose cleaned path already exists), FTS row first since image_fts has no foreign key onto image, and rewrites the rest in place. devpreview is repaired more cautiously: its path index is UNIQUE and every row names a JPEG on disk, so a colliding row is LEFT ALONE (deleting it would orphan a file nothing would collect) and the cache evicts those few normally. Dry-run on the library that produced it: 5,059 + 172 rows rewritten, none deleted, FTS intact, all 6,200 paths resolving on disk, integrity_check ok, one pass.
- Schema 12: keyword links drifted from the text (see [16.13.1 Schema 12: The Links Drifted From the Text (Third Data Repair)](#16131-schema-12-the-links-drifted-from-the-text-third-data-repair)).
- Schema 23: deletes the thumb rows of every image with develop_history, which could have had a developed thumbnail cached as the camera's (see [5.8.2 Writing Thumbnails as They Load](#582-writing-thumbnails-as-they-load)).

### 17.8 Availability (Offline Is Not Missing)

The catalog outlives the files it indexes, and the two ways that happens are not the same thing:

```
  Present   the file is where the catalog says it is
  Offline   its VOLUME is not mounted: an ejected card, an unplugged drive,
            a share that is not up. The image is fine; the disk is absent.
  Missing   the volume IS mounted and the file is not there. Deleted or moved
            by something other than Winnow.
```

The sweep has always depended on that distinction: it demotes a row only when the volume is mounted and the file is still gone, so ejecting a card is not read as a mass deletion. For BROWSING the whole catalog, "that disk isn't plugged in" is information the user wants, not a row to hide (CatalogQuery::includeMissing, which drops such rows, is never set by the app). Catalog::availabilityOf answers it for a list of paths in one pass.

- Offline is COMPUTED, not stored. A volume's presence changes without anything telling the catalog, so a stored answer would be wrong the moment a drive is plugged in. Missing is the stored `live` flag, which the sweep maintains: one is a fact about the past that had to be observed, the other a fact about now that can be asked.
- The volume is asked FIRST. A row can be marked not live by a sweep taken while the drive WAS mounted, and then the drive is unplugged, so the file is missing AND the volume is absent. "That disk isn't plugged in" is the useful answer then, because the user can act on it and because until the disk is back there is no way to know whether the file is still gone. Reversing the two tests makes an ejected drive report every row on it as deleted; the unit case catches it.
- A path the catalog does not know is ABSENT from the result, not reported Missing. "Not indexed" is a different statement from "indexed and gone".
- One mount-table walk per call (Cache/mountsnapshot.h), taken before the lock: it is a syscall per volume, and a folder's worth of rows should not pay it per row.

G::AvailabilityColumn carries the state per row, and the icon delegate paints a dot beside the develop badge: slate blue for Offline, dull red for Missing. Offline is the calmer one deliberately: an ejected drive is a normal state a user creates dozens of times a day, while a file that is genuinely gone is worth alarming about. The reason is inline, never a popup: hovering the dot says "Offline: this image is on a volume that is not mounted. Reconnect the drive to open it." or "Missing: this file was not found where the catalog expects it. It may have been moved or deleted outside Winnow."

- Present is 0 and unset reads as 0. The delegate reads the column once per paint and draws nothing for Present (every folder-scope row and most catalog rows), so the common case costs one int. A row nobody has asked about is openable until something says otherwise; tst_imagerow pins that.
- The column is APPENDED, not inserted, like DevelopColumn: saved table column order and widths are keyed by index, so an insertion would silently shift every user's layout.
- Only the catalog load asks. A folder load never calls availabilityOf and its rows stay Present (the filesystem has just listed them). The catalog path asks once for the whole result set, off the GUI thread, and the answers come back queued to be written, because the model is not thread-safe.

Availability is also a Filters category and is re-verified as rows scroll in; see [18.5.1 Availability as a Filter (One Spelling, Two Places)](#1851-availability-as-a-filter-one-spelling-two-places) and [17.12 Verifying a Hydrated Row (Scroll-In Stat)](#1712-verifying-a-hydrated-row-scroll-in-stat).

The category is ALWAYS SHOWN, disabled when there is nothing to choose. It used to be HIDDEN while every loaded row was Present, which answered a question the user never got to ask ("can Winnow tell me which of these files it cannot open?"), and a category that appears and disappears with the data is one nobody learns is there. Greyed with its items still visible says the same thing in the place the user is already looking. The enable test: any value that is not Present, so a scope in which every row is offline still counts.

A fourth value, UNREADABLE, marks a catalogued file the parser could not read (a stub row): Catalog::availabilityOf asks the volume first, then live, then the flag, ordered by what the user can act on ("cannot be parsed" only means something once the file is known to be there). Checking it shows exactly which files they are ([17.19.8 Twenty Images the Scan Could Never Catalogue](#17198-twenty-images-the-scan-could-never-catalogue)).

### 17.9 Edits Write Back to the Catalog

Rating and colour edits write back to the catalog. The sidecar is still the source of truth and is written exactly as before; the index row is brought into step at the same time.

In Folders scope this was never needed: an edit moves the sidecar's mtime, the freshness stamp stops matching, and the folder is re-indexed on the next visit, which always comes before the stale value can be seen. In Catalog scope the user works from search results and may never open the containing folder again: rate an image, search for that rating, and the catalog would not find it.

- The WHOLE ROW goes, not the field that changed, through DataModel::catalogRowFor, the same builder the bulk capture uses (extracted from catalogRows for this reason). Two builders would drift. Pushing only the changed field would leave the freshness stamp saying "current" over whatever else had drifted, so the row would look authoritative while being partly wrong.
- It costs nothing when the catalog is already right: commit() skips a row whose stamp already matches, and the write is off the GUI thread. The unit case pins that a re-commit REPLACES the values and restores freshness rather than being skipped, that the pre-edit stamp stops reading as fresh, and that committing the same row twice is a no-op.

#### 17.9.1 Picks Are Session-Only

Pick is deliberately NOT written back. It is a Winnow concept kept in the pick log, not written to XMP, so there is no sidecar edit to be in step with, and picks are SESSION-ONLY, so the catalog does not hold them:

- DataModel::catalogRowFor commits pick = false.
- DataModel::addFileDataForRow starts every row Unpicked, catalog-backed or not.
- A library-snapshot restore (DataModel::readLibrarySnapshot) unpicks every non-version row.
- The exception is a version row, whose pick lives in the master's sidecar (Metadata/versions.h).

The bug this replaced (2026-10-08): the catalog used to store the pick at commit and a catalog fill restored it, but an unpick writes no sidecar, so Catalog::commit's stamp check skipped the row and the index kept saying Picked. The pick came back on every launch, and so did the "picks not ingested" warning at quit. Index schema 21 is the data repair: it sets image.pick = 0 on every row. The column stays (the schema is additive only) and is never read for a model row.

### 17.10 What Limits a Large Scope

Measured on \~/Pictures recursively, 43,070 images, once the row work was done:

```
  rows in the model              43,070      loads fine
  icon, in memory               ~178 KB      256 px ARGB QPixmap
  icons if all were cached         7.7 GB
  resident, 26,000 icons in       6.5 GB     and the load had not finished
```

The icons are the constraint, and always were; the row work removed the larger number in front of them. An icon is two orders of magnitude bigger than its row (\~178 KB against \~600 bytes), so at any scale where "browse the whole catalog" is the point, thumbnails are the entire memory story.

The icon window is always bounded. setIconRange, MetaRead::needToRead and clearIconsOutsideChunkRange all key off iconChunkSize &lt; rowCount(), and resolveIconChunkSize computes a budget from free memory. That used to happen only under G::useJitIconCache (off by default); the default branch cached an icon for every row. Now:

- The default branch is bounded by the same memory budget. The JIT flag chooses a preference rather than safety: with it off the whole set is still cached whenever it fits.
- iconChunkSize honours G::maxIconChunk, which is a preference: Preferences > "Thumbnails held in memory", offering 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 / 50,000 / No limit, default 10,000. It is the user's call because it is a trade: memory against how far you can scroll before a thumbnail is re-read. (The number used to exist only for DataModel::okManyImagesWarning's "more than 10,000 images ... sluggish responses or system hangs" dialog, which nothing calls.)
- The memory budget derives from FREE memory, so the same code takes a different branch on different machines: on a 128 GB machine the budget did not bind at 43,070 icons, while on a 24 GB laptop it would have. A memory measurement is only meaningful with the machine attached to it.

Measured with the cap:

```
  50 images          chunk 50        8 MB      unchanged
  1,048 images       chunk 1,048   196 MB      unchanged
  43,070 images      chunk 10,000  ~1.8 GB cap (was 43,070 and 6.5 GB resident)
```

An ordinary thousand-image folder holds nearly 200 MB of thumbnails, which is worth knowing before raising the setting.

At large scope the binding cost is TIME, not memory: after seven minutes only 26,420 of 43,070 rows had metadata read. That is what G::useIndexMetadata addresses (see [5.9 Metadata From the Index](#59-metadata-from-the-index)). Bounding the icons makes a large scope fit; serving metadata from the index makes it arrive.

#### 17.10.1 Maximum Search Results

G::maxSearchResults is one setting, Preferences > Library > "Maximum search results", offering the same steps as the thumbnail ceiling, default 5,000. It replaced kResultLimit and kAutoLoadMax, two static constexpr values in two panels, fixed because a row used to cost 20 KB.

- The two questions they answered stay separate even though one setting drives both: how much may be SHOWN (FilterPanel::resultLimit), and how much may be REPLACED UNASKED (FilterPanel::autoLoadMax). If an automatic load ever feels heavy, the second is the one to lower.
- The reported match count is still the TRUE total, so a user seeing a subset is told so. The cap governs what is brought in, never what is found.
- The whole-Library scope is not capped (see [17.11.3 No Cap on the Library](#17113-no-cap-on-the-library)).

### 17.11 Loading a Catalog Scope

A catalog scope (the whole Library, or a search over it) loads ROWS from the index, not paths: no image is opened and no file is stat'd on the way in.

```
FilterPanel::runSearch            // pool thread: Catalog::searchRows
FilterPanel::applySearchResult    // GUI thread; newest searchGen only
MW::loadCatalogRows               // builds a ScopeRequest with rows
MW::loadCatalogScope              // teardown, cover, queued fill, availability
DataModel::addCatalogRows         // batched, posted fill
DataModel::finishCatalogFill      // folders, allMetadataAttempted, endLoad, folderChange
Catalog::availabilityOf           // once, off the GUI thread, after folderChange
```

MW::loadCatalogResults (paths) and MW::loadCatalogRows (rows) differ only in the ScopeRequest they build; both hand it to MW::loadCatalogScope, which owns the teardown a replace needs, the queued fill and the availability pass, so there is one copy of the reasoning about what an append must not reset. The old paths shape (search + loadCatalogResults + addPaths) remains for the separate Catalog panel, which is not built when G::useFilterPanel is on.

#### 17.11.1 Catalog::searchRows

Catalog::searchRows runs the query once and returns whole rows. The cost of hydrating a catalog scope was measured, not estimated, with Winnow --catalogprobe (Cache/catalogprobe.h), which runs its stages against the REAL index (an isolated test-mode settings dir would open an empty database and report that browsing a catalog is free). On 43,050 images in 176 folders, all local, debug build:

```
  A  SQL pass (Catalog::search)                 67 ms      1.6 us/row
  B  stat sweep (IndexMetadata::candidate)     509 ms     11.8 us/row
  C  bulk Catalog::fetchFresh                1,710 ms     39.7 us/row
  E  Catalog::searchRows                       308 ms      7.1 us/row
  D  full file read, serial                     67 s    1,616 us/row
  D  full file read, 18 threads                8.7 s      147 us/row
  F  result sort, QFileInfo comparator       1,517 ms
  F  result sort, key built once per row        75 ms
```

- fetchFresh is the wrong question for a browse: finding the rows took 67 ms, looking each up afterwards 1,710 ms. fetchFresh is one indexed seek per path plus one keyword query per image, right when the caller has a list of files and needs to know which are current, wrong when the caller has just run a query. searchRows is 5.8x faster than search + fetchFresh; the keywords come back in ONE join whose subquery reuses the predicate.
- searchRows deliberately does not check freshness. Freshness needs each file's size and mtime, so every candidate would have to be stat'd first; a browse does not need it, because a row's stamps are checked when the row is actually looked at (see [17.12 Verifying a Hydrated Row (Scroll-In Stat)](#1712-verifying-a-hydrated-row-scroll-in-stat)). Callers that must know a row is current still use fetchFresh.
- A stat is \~137x cheaper than a read, which makes verification affordable as a background activity: stat-ing the whole 43,000-row catalog costs half a second where re-reading it costs a minute, and the scroll-in stat of a 10,000-row icon window is 118 ms against 16 s to re-read it.
- The index answers for essentially everything: 42,996 of 43,050 rows fresh, 54 stale or unindexed (0.1%).
- Raw is not the expensive case. A raw-only folder (1,046 ARW) read at 690 us/row, well under the whole-catalog average of 1,616 us; this library is 89% JPEG (38,226 jpg, 2,733 tif, 1,825 raw) and the slow rows are the big JPEG and TIFF ones. The "\~20 ms per raw" quoted elsewhere and an older "1 ms" were both true measurements of different file mixes, which is why the probe reports the mix it measured.
- Caveats: a debug build, so the file-read figures are pessimistic and the SQL and stat figures much less so. Every volume was local; the network case is unmeasured (--catalogprobe takes a path substring so a mounted share can be timed on its own). The 18-thread read is wall clock against a serial stat sweep, which is not like-for-like, and the probe says so.

One predicate, shared. Catalog::buildQueryLocked compiles a CatalogQuery for both search and searchRows, because "which images does this query match" must mean exactly one thing; otherwise the count beside the results could describe a different set from the rows on screen. tst_catalog::searchRowsMatchesSearchExactly holds them to the same paths in the same order with the same total across five query shapes, and searchRowsReturnsWhatFetchFreshWouldHave compares the two row-fillers field by field; the probe repeats that over the real library (42,996 rows, 0 mismatched). The column list and row mapping are shared too (kRowColumns and readRow in catalog.cpp): a second place that spells a row is a second place for a shutter speed to come back different.

#### 17.11.2 Filling the Model (addCatalogRows)

Two things a row displays are not in the image table:

```
  permissions   assumed read-write, the ordinary case, and corrected when the row is
                verified or written. Assuming the opposite would grey out ratings and
                renames across a whole catalog on a value nobody had looked up.
  birth time    the Created column takes the CAPTURE date instead, which is what that
                column ends up holding anyway once metadata arrives.
```

Everything else (size, modified time, whether there is a sidecar) comes from the freshness stamp the index keeps. addFileDataForRow takes an optional CatalogRow and reads those from it instead of from QFileInfo; it is one function rather than two so that a row means the same thing whichever way it arrived.

- The rows are marked MetaLoaded and allMetadataAttempted is set. MetaRead::needToRead keys on metaAttemptedAt() and iconLoadedAt(), so a hydrated row is never read for metadata but is still collected for its ICON, the one thing the table cannot serve. Nothing else would ever set allMetadataAttempted for rows no reader will visit, and the filters and the sort wait on it.
- Nothing proves the file exists, deliberately. A catalog row can name a file on an unplugged drive, and the useful thing is to show it marked rather than drop it (see [17.8 Availability (Offline Is Not Missing)](#178-availability-offline-is-not-missing)). MW asks Catalog::availabilityOf for the whole set once, off the GUI thread.
- The fill is BATCHED, 2,000 rows at a time, and each batch is POSTED to the event loop rather than looped over. Each batch is one structural insert and one wide dataChanged, which keeps the proxy and the three views off the per-row signal path; between batches the event loop runs, so thumbnails paint, the scrollbar works and Esc is heard. The first version looped and called processEvents, and G::useProcessEvents is FALSE by default, so the pump was skipped and 43,000 rows filled in one blocking pass: a spinning beachball with no thumbnails. Posting is not a tuning of that, so it does not hang off a flag.
- The completion tail (folder registration, allMetadataAttempted, endLoad, folderChange) is DataModel::finishCatalogFill, because addCatalogRows returns long before the set is in.
- The availability pass waits for the fill: it hangs off a single-shot connection to DataModel::folderChange, which both fill shapes emit when they are actually done. Launched straight after setScope (correct while the fill was synchronous), it would look up paths that were not rows yet and mark none.
- The result is ordered by a key built once per row (the lower-cased path, with a jpg or jpeg rewritten to ".zzz" so it sorts after its raw), reproducing lessThan and lessThanCombineRawJpg exactly; this is DataModel::sortKey. The QFileInfo comparator addFolder used builds two QFileInfos per comparison, over a million at 43,000 rows (stage F above).

The count is true from the first batch. DataModel::expectedRows is set before any row is inserted and cleared in endLoad, and MW::getPosition reports it while a fill is running, so a 43,050-image catalog reads "1 of 43,050" from the first thumbnail instead of counting up as batches land. It applies only while loading AND only while the proxy shows everything the model holds; once a filter is applied, the proxy's own count is the honest answer.

ctest catalog_load drives the live path: searchRows + loadCatalogRows (see [17.11.4 The catalog_load Test](#17114-the-catalog_load-test)).

#### 17.11.3 No Cap on the Library

G::maxSearchResults defaults to 0, no limit: picking the catalog shows the whole catalog, the way picking a folder shows the whole folder. The old 5,000 cap existed because a row cost \~19,900 bytes and every row had to be read from its own file; neither is true now. The preference remains for anyone who wants a cap.

- The old saved 5,000 is retired once rather than honoured. It had been written to settings for every existing user, and a default nobody chose is not a preference. Settings::loadSettings removes the key when it reads exactly 5,000; every other value is kept. A user who deliberately picked 5,000 loses that choice, the price of not being able to tell it from the default.
- resultLimit and autoLoadMax differ in kind: resultLimit is the SQL limit and returns 0 for "no LIMIT clause"; autoLoadMax returns INT_MAX. Returning INT_MAX from both would have put "LIMIT 2147483647" on every query.
- The footer no longer says "N images catalogued. Showing the M most recent" when M is everything; claiming a window onto a larger set when there is none describes a limit the user does not have.

#### 17.11.4 The catalog_load Test

There are two ways rows get into the model, and for a long time only the folder load was tested; the catalog path was reachable only by a person typing in the Filter dock. WINNOW_SELFTEST_CATALOG_QUERY runs it: the folder load happens first, deliberately (it puts rows in the catalog for the query to find), and then a catalog search replaces the model exactly as the Filter dock would. An empty query is legal and means the whole Library.

It had to be made discriminating. The first run loaded the four-image fixture folder and then catalog-loaded four images: the numbers matched and proved nothing, because the same four images were on both sides. Cataloguing a fifty-image folder first and then loading the four-image one showed the model going from 4 rows to 43, from a folder the run had never opened. A test whose passing number equals its starting number is not testing the step in between.

ctest catalog_load fails if the search matches nothing (exit 4) or the model is empty after the load (exit 5). It is self-contained: the fixture folder is catalogued by the same run, with a wait on the thread pool so the capture has landed before the query. Verified to fail by making the catalog load return early ("catalogLoaded rows=0"). The wait lives in this mode alone, not on the default selftest path (see [17.19.2 The Catalog Capture Was Silently Not Running](#17192-the-catalog-capture-was-silently-not-running)).

### 17.12 Verifying a Hydrated Row (Scroll-In Stat)

A row filled from the index is not checked against the file it names (43,000 images cannot be opened), so without this it was trusted until something else revisited it, and in Catalog scope nothing does. Edit an image's keywords in Lightroom (which rewrites the .xmp and never touches the raw) and Winnow would go on showing what the catalog remembers. In Folders scope the correction always arrived anyway, because the sidecar's mtime broke the freshness stamp and the next visit re-read it.

Preferences > "Verify images as they scroll into view" (G::useScrollInVerify) DEFAULTS ON, unlike G::useIndexMetadata beside it, which is off because it changes the loader/decoder contract. This one corrects wrong data on screen and its cost was measured before it was written.

#### 17.12.1 The Cost Decides Where It Runs

Freshness is (srcsize, srcmtime, sidecarmtime), so asking costs a stat of the image and a stat of its sidecar, \~137x cheaper than a read (11.8 us against 1,616 us per row, --catalogprobe stages B and D over the real 43,050-image library). Stat-ing the whole catalog costs half a second where re-reading it costs a minute; the scroll-in stat of a 10,000-row icon window is 118 ms against 16 s to re-read it. So verification is affordable as a BACKGROUND activity over what is on screen, not at load time over the whole set.

- It asks about the VISIBLE WINDOW, not the icon chunk. The chunk is a memory budget and can be tens of thousands of rows; a row scrolled past unseen is not worth a syscall.
- Coalesced: MW::updateIconRange fires on every scroll and selection change, so ScrollVerify::viewChanged restarts a 400 ms single-shot timer and the pass runs when the view settles. Dragging a scrollbar the length of a catalog costs one pass.
- Once per row, then again after a minute. Verifying on every settle would re-stat the same window each time the user rocks the scrollbar; verifying once per scope would leave a file edited AFTER the user scrolled past it stale for the session. The answers are remembered with a timestamp and expire, KEYED BY PATH (rows shift under sorting and filtering).

#### 17.12.2 Catalog::outOfDate Is Not staleOf

Catalog::outOfDate is staleOf asked by a browser rather than by an indexer, and the difference is a path the catalog has never seen. staleOf calls it stale, correctly: its caller is about to read every file it names, and an unindexed image is one that must be read. outOfDate's caller holds rows that were FILLED FROM the index and asks which of them the index can no longer vouch for, so a path it does not know was never filled from it and cannot be out of date; reporting it would clear and re-read every uncatalogued row in the window on every scroll, forever. tst_catalog::outOfDateIgnoresWhatWasNeverIndexed asserts BOTH answers on the same path, so neither function can quietly adopt the other's.

staleOf is paged (as availabilityOf's comment had already claimed it was): the queries run off the GUI thread, but a lock held for one query per row is what every GUI-thread call into the catalog then waits on.

#### 17.12.3 A Failed Row Is Re-read, Not Patched

What changed is not knowable from the stamps (a rating, a title, the whole keyword set, the capture time), so MW::refreshStaleRows clears the row back to MetaNotAttempted and the loader reads it exactly as a row it has never seen. That path already prefers the index and falls through to the file when the index is out of date.

- The icon goes too, because an embedded thumbnail can change with the file, and a row that keeps its old icon while its metadata is re-read is half-corrected in the way that is hardest to see. Clearing it is not enough on its own: MetaRead is told through invalidateLoadedIcons, the same announcement setPreviewSource and devPreviewUpdated make (see [5.6 Icon Loading Rules](#56-icon-loading-rules)).
- The catalog is corrected, which closes the loop. MW::folderChangeCompleted skips committing a hydrated catalog scope (every row came FROM the index), and commits exactly the rows this pass re-read, the only rows the index has anything to learn from, built by DataModel::catalogRowFor. A row that has not come back MetaLoaded stays pending rather than being committed, because writing what is still on it would put the stale values back as though current.

#### 17.12.4 What It Does Not Verify

Only rows filled from the index are worth asking about; a folder scope read every row from its file. The gate is a Catalog scope whose rows came back in the query that found them (ScopeRequest::isHydrated()), or any load while G::useIndexMetadata is on. It is the same condition MW::folderChangeCompleted uses to decide there is nothing to commit, and the two must not drift: what one skips committing, the other is responsible for. Rows already marked Offline or Missing are skipped: the availability pass has said the file is unreachable, and on an absent network volume the stat is not cheap.

The whole-set sweep (see [17.19.6 Is What We Loaded Still True? (the Whole-Set Sweep, and the Three Bugs That Stopped It Repairing Anything)](#17196-is-what-we-loaded-still-true-the-whole-set-sweep-and-the-three-bugs-that-stopped-it-repairing-anything)) covers what scrolling never reaches.

### 17.13 Start-up Source and State Restore

#### 17.13.1 Start in the Source Left Showing

Winnow always starts in the source that was active at the last close (2026-09-29; "Open library at start" is retired). One preference, Preferences > General > "Reopen as it was left" (variable and settings key still restoreLibraryState, default off), decides whether what was loaded comes back.

- MW::closeEvent, before any teardown, calls saveLibraryState and saveFoldersState and records lastScopeWasLibrary (written by writeSettings).
- MW::showEvent, Library last: chooseSource(true), which loads the whole Library (the Library cannot be shown without loading it; setScope drives the load through the Filters panel), with queueLibraryStateRestore first when the preference is on.
- MW::showEvent, Folders last: Folders. With the preference on (and no Shift at launch), MW::restoreFoldersState reloads the saved folders and queues their filters; off, it waits for a folder.
- Never in an automated run, a stress test, or a launch with startup arguments.
- Migration: a missing lastScopeWasLibrary defaults to the old openLibraryAtStart value, which is then removed from settings.ini.

#### 17.13.2 What Catalog Order Is

Without a restored sort, the Library opens in the order Catalog::searchRows returns rows: ORDER BY captured DESC, id DESC, newest capture first. restoreProxySortAfterLoad leaves the proxy unsorted (sort(-1)) after a load even though the sort menu names File Name; the first filter change then sorts into the menu's column.

#### 17.13.3 Library State

MW::saveLibraryState writes the LibraryState settings group: sortColumn, isReverseSort, the selection, and Filters::persistableState (each checked item as {top-level category, filter value, include/exclude}, joined by the ASCII unit separator; the search text; the keyword any/all mode). It saves on leaving the Library for Folders (MW::setScope, before G::scope changes) and in MW::closeEvent before any teardown, both only while the Library is loaded, so quitting from Folders keeps the state the Library was last left in. It refuses an empty model: a second save after closeEvent's teardown had cleared the model used to write File Name / ascending / nothing checked.

MW::queueLibraryStateRestore (from showEvent, just before the Library loads) restores it:

- The sort. The saved column and direction are held and applied by MW::applyRestoredLibrarySort from metadataComplete, AFTER that function's updateSortColumn(G::NameColumn), the reset that puts the sort menu back to File Name on every completed load. (The first cut applied the sort before it, so the grid was sorted by the saved column while the menu and sortColumn said File Name, and the next filter change re-sorted by name.)
- The filters, through Filters::setStateToRestore into the same after-build path a folder change uses (restoreFiltersPending -> MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange -> Filters::restore + one filterChange). That path runs when the filter BUILD finishes, and the build only runs while the Filters panel is showing, so a restored filter is never applied where it cannot be seen; with the panel hidden it lands when the panel is opened. (The first cut tested filterDock->isVisible() in showEvent, where dock visibility is not settled yet, and restored nothing.)
- libraryFilterRestorePending marks the pending restore as the Library's. Leaving the Library before it lands cancels it; otherwise the folder-change code, which does not save while a restore is pending, would put the Library's filters on a folder. It also exempts that restore from MW::reset, which clears restoreFiltersPending at the start of every new load (in the second cut, that cleared the Library's restore at the start of the very load it was queued for).
- A saved item whose value is no longer in the catalog is simply not restored (Filters::restore finds no match).
- Filters::restore writes the saved search text back only when it differs, and writes the placeholder back for "". It used to write it unconditionally, and an unsearched row saves as "", so every restore replaced the "Enter search query" placeholder with an empty row: an edit, which ran a search and two \~300 ms whole-proxy filterChanges at 148,567 rows. This also removed that cost from every folder add/remove restore.

Pinned by tst_filters::persistedStateSurvivesSettingsAndARebuild (through a real QSettings file, include and exclude, nested keywords by path). Filters::persistableState / setStateToRestore are declared in the class's FIRST public: section on purpose: the section right above the slots is signals:, and a method declared there links as a duplicate symbol.

QSettings must be synced at quit. The end-to-end test (launch, quick-filter, reverse the sort, quit, relaunch) found that nothing closeEvent wrote to `settings` reached the disk: a --perfprobe line showed saveLibraryState saving the right state while settings.ini kept the old one, and hasCrashed=true survived a clean quit. QSettings flushes on sync(), on a deferred UpdateRequest the event loop processes, or when destroyed; `settings` is never destroyed and the event loop ends right after closeEvent, so every quit-time write (writeSettings' geometry and dock state, hasCrashed=false, the Library state) was lost unless the deferred flush happened to win the race. closeEvent now calls settings->sync() after writeSettings. This was pre-existing, and also explains window/dock state not always persisting and the crash-recovery check seeing hasCrashed=true after clean quits.

#### 17.13.4 Folders State

MW::folderRoots holds the roots the user chose, each with its recurse flag (dm->folderList cannot, since a recursive load lists every subfolder). It is maintained in MW::folderSelectionChange after its refusal check: reset clears, Add appends or updates, Remove drops, Toggle flips.

- saveFoldersState writes the FoldersState group: roots as "path&lt;US>0|1", the selection, and Filters::persistableState (empty when nothing is loaded, so the next start waits for a folder).
- restoreFoldersState skips roots that no longer exist, selects the first through FSTree::select (the Recent Folders route; "Recurse" for a recursive root), adds the rest through FSTree::addFolderToSelection (FolderOp::Add, resetDataModel false: a Cmd-click from code), then calls FSTree::scrollToCurrentWhenLoaded.
- Filters go through Filters::setStateToRestore + restoreFiltersPending. foldersFilterRestorePending exempts that from the MW::reset the first load begins with (as libraryFilterRestorePending does for the Library); the later adds see restoreFiltersPending already set and so do not overwrite it; entering the Library cancels it (MW::setScope).
- No FoldersState group (a profile from before this) falls back to lastDir, non-recursive. The folder sort is not restored.
- The tree scroll: a reopened folder loaded but the Folders tree stayed at the top, because QFileSystemModel lists directories asynchronously and siblings inserted after a one-time scroll pushed the selection back out of view. FSTree::scrollToCurrentWhenLoaded re-centres (scrollToCurrent) after each directoryLoaded on the folder's path for 5 s, then disconnects so later browsing is never dragged back.

#### 17.13.5 The Selection Comes Back Too

2026-10-13; untested in-app. saveLibraryState and saveFoldersState write "selection" in their groups: MW::selectionKeysToSave, the current image FIRST, then the other selected keys. A selection over 5,000 saves the current image only.

queueLibraryStateRestore and restoreFoldersState (before its first FSTree::select) hand it to MW::queueSelectionRestore, the mechanism restoreParkedLibrary already used for its current image, now shared:

- folderAndFileChangePath makes the current image the load's START row (MW::folderChanged).
- MW::applySelectionRestore re-selects BY KEY on metadataLoaded, emitted at the end of metadataComplete after the Library's restored sort, so a proxy row taken earlier cannot name another image.
- The current image is selected through Selection::select(key) and the rest added with Selection::selectRows(rows, add = true). If the current image is gone, the first surviving one becomes current. A later filter restore keeps the selection (filterChange saves and recovers it).
- Folders may span several loads (the first root plus one add per further root), so the restore waits for up to one metadataLoaded per root, applying what is present each time, and ends when everything is found.
- A second queue for the same current image keeps the LONGER list: at start-up the snapshot path (restoreParkedLibrary) queues the snapshot's current image after the LibraryState selection and must not shrink it.
- A scope change cancels a pending restore of the other scope (MW::setScope), as with the filter restore.

### 17.14 The Library Load Cover

Every replacing Library load is covered, from the click to the finished, filtered, sorted view (2026-09-30). Without it the whole unfiltered Library showed (loupe, grid, filmstrip) for the seconds the filter build took, then jumped to the filtered set; the user asked not to see the rows stream in, re-sort, then shrink to the restored filter.

The cover is a LoadCurtain (Views/loadcurtain.h), an opaque CHILD raised over the central widget and over thumbView, not a hide(). A hidden view has no visible cells, so the icon range, scroll sync and every isVisible() gate would change their answers during the wait; covered, the views load exactly as usual underneath and lifting the cover simply reveals them. While it is up:

- setCentralMessage and setCentralProgressMessage write to the cover, so "Building filters: ..." stays visible for the whole wait.
- The status bar mirrors it: setCentralMessage / setCentralProgressMessage (cover branch) and raiseLoadCurtain call MW::mirrorLoadMessageToStatus (one line, the Esc hint dropped), and MW::updateStatus defers to it, so "Pos: 241 of 155098" no longer shows for a set still loading. lowerLoadCurtain calls updateStatus(true) so Pos / Selected / Picked return with the finished view.
- sortChange does not set its message, and showCentralMessageIfNoImages does not replace the message (the Browse view switch used to put "Select from the Source or Bookmarks panels." over "Loading the library.").
- Known leak: the Metadata panel shows the unfiltered current image while the cover is up.

#### 17.14.1 Raised From the Click

The catalog search runs on a pool thread for seconds (\~2.9 s at 155,000 rows) before MW::loadCatalogScope tears anything down, and until then the screen used to keep what it had: at start the "Select from the Source or Bookmarks panels." prompt, and from Folders the folder's image, as if nothing had been asked. The cover is now raised, with "Loading the library.", at every entry point:

- MW::setCatalogScopeWhole (the Library button, File > Open Library, open at start), whenever it will start a load (the scope is not already the Library, and not initializing). The picks question is asked there, AHEAD of clearing the view, since okToDiscardPicks must come before anything that cannot be undone; a refusal pushes the toggle back and touches nothing. pendingWholeLibrary carries the answer to loadCatalogScope, which then neither asks again nor replaces the message with "Loading search results."; it is consumed there and cleared on leaving the Library.
- MW::chooseSource (lifted if the Library is refused).
- MW::setScope on entering the Library.
- MW::loadCatalogScope after its stop(), for every replacing load. MW::stop does not lift it when called from loadCatalogScope (its own teardown).

#### 17.14.2 Lowered When the Model Is Ready

MW::lowerLoadCurtain is called on every path that ends the wait, because a cover left up reads as a hang:

- The end of MW::metadataComplete, after applyRestoredLibrarySort / applyDeferredSort, when no filter restore is pending ("model ready").
- restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange, after its filterChange, when one is. A filter that matches nothing leaves nullFiltration's "No images in filter result." showing; MW::filterBuildCompleted, which otherwise ends every load with "N images loaded. Loading images ...", leaves it alone when the proxy is empty.
- buildFiltersWhenModelReady when the Filters panel is hidden (no build, so the restore waits for the panel) or the filters were already built (recount only, no finishedBuildFilters). These two lifts are QUEUED and instance-guarded: they run inside metadataComplete BEFORE its sort, so an immediate lift showed the unsorted set, and a late one must not drop a newer load's cover.
- MW::setScope leaving the Library, and MW::stop (Esc or another load).
- Nothing-to-load paths: loadCatalogRows / loadCatalogResults empty, and FilterPanel::searchNotLoaded from applySearchResult, which says "No images to show." over an empty model.

lowerLoadCurtain(src, revealView) switches to prevCentralView BEFORE hiding for the "ready" lifts, so a stale "Collating folders ..." message pane is never shown for the \~140 ms before the grid.

#### 17.14.3 QStackedLayout Raises the Page It Switches To

QStackedLayout::setCurrentIndex RAISES the page it switches to (Qt source: next->raise(); next->show()), and the cover is that page's sibling. So any page switch during the load (the restored sort switching to the grid) put the view in front of the cover until something re-raised it: 17 ms, one frame at 60 fps, invisible to a "covered = isVisible()" probe and found only by a screen recording. The cover re-raises itself on centralLayout::currentChanged, which is emitted inside setCurrentIndex before anything can paint.

#### 17.14.4 Start-up Waits for an Exposed Window

showEvent used to run the whole Library start (Browse layout switch, scope change, query dispatch) before the window had painted, so the first message ever seen was loadCatalogScope's, after the query: \~2.2 s of empty central area. showEvent now only puts up "Loading the library." and the cover. MW::startLibraryWhenExposed polls (0/20 ms, bounded \~2 s) until windowHandle()->isExposed(), repaints the cover, then queues the restore and calls chooseSource.

#### 17.14.5 Probes

- --catalogload runs a headless Library load. WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_GRAB=&lt;dir> grabs window frames, \_RESTORESTATE=1 queues the saved LibraryState, \_WAITCURTAIN=1 runs until the cover drops. Verified: the message holds through fill, sort and filter build, and the first frame after it is the filtered set (14 of 14).
- WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_TIMELINE=1 logs every change in page / covered / top (the frontmost visible child of the central widget) / message / rows at 20 ms. WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_FROMFOLDER=&lt;folder> loads a folder first and then presses Library through chooseSource. WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_STARTUP=1 runs the start-up path in the harness.
- A normal launch with WINNOW_STARTUP_TIMELINE=1 prints the timeline from MW construction. The harness runs are single-instance-exempt; a normal launch is not, so it cannot run while another Winnow is open.
- "[PERF] CURTAIN raise/lower src=..." names every lift.

The timeline probe found, before the fixes: the folder's 14 thumbnails uncovered for 3.2 s after "Loading the library." (the query ran before loadCatalogScope raised the cover, and something switched the page back to the grid); 1.1 s of the old folder while chooseSource switched the Browse layout; "Sorting images" interrupting the message (the layout switch re-sorted the folder being left); 2.9 s of an EMPTY grid with no message when the Library was entered through setScope directly; and the stale "Collating folders ..." flash. All are covered by the rules above: Folders -> Library is covered from the first 20 ms sample to the finished grid with one message sequence.

### 17.15 Cataloguing Designated Folders

The scope table defines the catalog; the background scanner fills it.

#### 17.15.1 The Scope Table Is Definitive

Browsing a folder used to catalogue it unconditionally (free, since the metadata had just been read), which made browsing a second, INVISIBLE way into the index: it filled with folders the user never asked to index and could not see listed anywhere, and it made the editor's two counts incomparable. MW::isCatalogScopeFolder is now the only door: dm->catalogRows() is filtered through it before the commit, the folder reconcile is filtered the same way, and so is the single-row write-back after a rating or label edit (an edit must not be what puts an out-of-scope image into the index). A folder the table does not include is read, displayed and forgotten.

It is ONE scope table, not a root list. Each row names a folder, says whether it is INCLUDED or EXCLUDED, and whether it reaches into subfolders (Main/catalogscope.h). Include and exclude are the same kind of statement, so they belong in one place read top to bottom: a library with one branch carved out is two rows.

- An EXCLUDE ALWAYS WINS over an include, wherever it sits: order-as-precedence is a rule the table cannot show, and would change meaning the moment a user sorted it.
- RECURSE is per row and means the same thing on both sides: an include row with it off catalogues that folder alone; an exclude row with it off skips that folder while still cataloguing everything beneath it.
- Exclusions exist because recursion is all-or-nothing without them: subfolder reach is what makes a folder worth nominating, and without exclusions a single unwanted branch (renders, exports, backups) had no way out short of abandoning recursion.
- Every rule is a PREFIX TEST, so the path has ONE SPELLING (catalogScopeNormalize, delegating to FolderTree::normalize: no trailing separator except a volume root). "/Users/x/Pictures/" never prefixes "/Users/x/Pictures/Zenfolio" once the separator is appended, so a single trailing slash made an exclusion silently do nothing AND made the editor announce that a folder plainly inside the library was not inside it (the failure this feature shipped with). Paths arrive from a file dialog, from migrated settings and from the folder tree (which spells them WITH the slash), so normalisation is applied at every door.
- Prefix matches compare with a TRAILING SEPARATOR: a plain startsWith would make "/Photos/2024" exclude "/Photos/2024 raw" as well.

The table lives in QSettings, not the index: it is USER INTENT, and CacheDb::moveAside discards the index without asking ([17.1 The Catalog (Cross-Folder Search)](#171-the-catalog-cross-folder-search)). It is written as a QSettings ARRAY (group CatalogScope: path, include, recurse) rather than an encoded string list, because a row holds a path and any delimiter is one folder name away from corrupting the setting; the group is cleared before writing, or a table that shrank would keep the tail of the longer one. The old keys (catalogRoots + the global catalogRootsRecurse + catalogExcludes) are migrated when the array is empty and left in place, so a downgrade still finds them.

The table governs more than the index: it also decides where the BACKGROUND devPreview build may run (DevPreviewPolicy::folderEligible, [12.9.2 Only Where the User Said Their Library Is](#1292-only-where-the-user-said-their-library-is)). The two questions are the same one: "is this folder part of my library, or am I just passing through it?"

#### 17.15.2 An Empty Table Means Nothing Is in Scope

The honest reading, and a trap: on a new install nothing would ever be catalogued, and no part of the UI would reveal that the choice was the user's. So the first folder of images opened with an empty scope says "Nothing is catalogued yet." and explains the two sources: Folders browses any folder on disk with nothing to set up; the Library browses every catalogued image at once and searches and filters across them (Collections and Queries live there), and it holds only what the catalog holds, so to use the Library the user chooses its folders in File > Manage Catalog. Buttons: Manage Catalog... and Not Now, plus "Don't show this message again".

- It is asked ONCE PER SESSION (catalogScopePrompted, not persisted) until that box is ticked (skipCatalogScopePrompt, persisted; it replaced an older once-per-install key, which writeSettings removes). A prompt that returns on every folder is one the user learns to dismiss without reading.
- Whoever says Not Now can still get there: File > Manage Catalog is enabled in both sources, and choosing Library while the catalog is empty opens it too (catalogEmptyOpenManage).
- It is asked only where the question is concrete: the catalog must be available, and the folder must actually hold images.

#### 17.15.3 The Table Is the Catalog: Shrinking It Forgets

Removing a root used NOT to un-catalogue what it contributed, which left a catalog that could disagree with the table indefinitely with nothing on screen to say so (rows from removed roots, or from the opportunistic capture before the scope table existed, stayed findable in an Everywhere search). Two statements of intent, one made by adding a row and one by removing it, were honoured unequally. So MW::reconcileCatalogToScope runs on every scope edit (a row removed, an exclusion added, a reach turned off, a path retargeted) and forgets every catalogued folder the table no longer admits.

- Folder by folder, not by prefix: an included branch may sit inside an excluded tree, so only MW::isCatalogScopeFolder can answer, asked of each catalogued folder in turn. Catalog::folderCounts is one GROUP BY that returns the folders and their costs together; Catalog::forgetFolders deletes exactly the folders named.
- The count is CONFIRMED FIRST, and Cancel PUTS THE EDIT BACK (Warning icon, Cancel the default and escape button). Accepting an edit while refusing its consequence would leave the table naming folders the catalog still held. setScope repopulates under its populating flag and does not signal back, so putting the rows back cannot recurse.
- Emptying the table empties the catalog, and says so in its own words ("This will empty the catalog.").
- FORGET is a DELETE, where the sweep DEMOTES: the sweep infers that a file is gone and can be wrong (an ejected card), so its rows must be able to come back; a forget is the user saying they do not want the folder indexed, and a demoted row would sit in the database forever, neither findable nor reclaimable. Un-excluding indexes nothing; the next scan picks the folder up.
- What a forget does not reach: the image files and their sidecars (it deletes an index a Scan rebuilds); the devpreview and thumb tables (BROWSE CACHES keyed by file, evicted on their own terms); and the KEYWORD VOCABULARY (the authored list is in userdata.db, out of reach; image_keyword links go by cascade with the images, and an observed keyword left with no images reads as a count of 0, because Catalog::keywords LEFT JOINs through image_keyword). That is why the whole-catalog path goes through forgetFolders and NOT through Catalog::clear().
- The scan reconciles too, silently: a catalog can hold folders no edit ever passed over, and Scan is the other moment the user has asked for the index to be brought in line. No confirmation there: the scope was confirmed when it was edited.

#### 17.15.4 The Background Scanner

Opening a folder catalogues it (free, when it is in scope), but that only covers folders the user has visited, so search on a fresh install would find nothing. Main/catalogscanner.cpp walks the designated folders in the background.

- It reads METADATA and nothing else: no icon, no decode, no preview (a catalog row is text). isLoadXmp is passed TRUE, because the keywords are the entire point.
- It owns its own Metadata instance, created on the scanner thread rather than in the constructor (which runs on the GUI thread before moveToThread): Metadata holds one reusable ImageMetadata and parser set and is not safe to share, which is why Cache/reader.cpp does the same.
- ONE LOW-PRIORITY THREAD, not a pool, and that is the point: browsing must not get slower because an index is being built, so the scan pauses whenever the datamodel is being modified and resumes when the load finishes.
- G::stop is a PAUSE here, not an abort, and getting that wrong is the subtle failure. G::stop is a TRANSIENT teardown latch (MW::stop sets and clears it around every folder change; the memory-overrun path sets it while it drains). A scanner that treated it as an abort would die the first time the user clicked a folder. Only an explicit Stop, or the object being destroyed, ends a scan.
- It skips work already done, which makes Scan cheap enough to offer as a button: each folder is stat'd into bare CatalogRows (path, size, mtime, sidecar mtime, no parsing) and handed to Catalog::staleOf; only what comes back is opened. A rescan of an unchanged root is one stat per file (tst_catalog::staleOfSkipsUnchangedOnRescan).
