- The recursive exclusions PRUNE THE WALK rather than filtering its result: Utilities::subFolderTree takes them and never descends into an excluded folder, so carving out a hierarchy of a hundred thousand folders costs nothing (a big branch is exactly what a user excludes). A NON-RECURSIVE exclude cannot prune (the folders below it are still wanted), so those are applied to what comes back (catalogScopeExcludes).
- Commits are CHUNKED (200 rows) rather than one transaction per folder, bounding what a quit costs to a few hundred files re-stat'd; the scan resumes from staleOf.
- Files the scanner cannot parse are catalogued as STUB rows ([17.19.8 Twenty Images the Scan Could Never Catalogue](#17198-twenty-images-the-scan-could-never-catalogue)).

It reconciles every folder it walks, which is where orphans go. Indexing alone only GROWS the catalog, so a library the user had been deleting from left every removed image findable until the once-per-session sweep. The scanner has already read each folder's directory, and a complete listing is precisely Catalog::reconcileFolder's precondition, so the walk answers "what is gone" for free.

- dir.exists() is the load-bearing guard: an unmounted volume and an empty folder both enumerate to nothing, and reconciling against the first would demote a whole drive.
- PRESENT is what the folder holds, not what the scan would index: the set handed to reconcileFolder is built from EVERY file in the listing, ahead of the extension and zero-byte filters.
- Folders that vanish ENTIRELY are handled after the walk (a folder that no longer exists is never walked): only after a COMPLETE pass, only for folders the scope still claims (what the scope has disowned is reconcileCatalogToScope's business), and only on a mounted volume (the MountSnapshot guard sweep() takes).

#### 17.15.5 Progress and the Automatic Scan

Progress is a STATUS-BAR ROW (progressCatalogRow) beside Metadata, Dev Previews and Raw Denoise, counting FILES in two phases (Checking folders, then Indexing the files that need a parse) with the time left ([17.18 Long Scans: Progress, Time Left, Resume, and Catalog Diagnostics](#1718-long-scans-progress-time-left-resume-and-catalog-diagnostics)). It is labelled "Scanning for changes" (renamed 2026-09-29 from "Catalog", which did not say what it was doing); the internal row name passed to Progress::addRow is still "Catalog". A scan the user PRESSED A BUTTON FOR finishes silently: the row already said it was happening and the panel shows the result.

Selecting the Library scans it, THROTTLED. A catalog is an index of a filesystem that keeps changing underneath it, and the moment the user selects the Library is the moment a stale index matters most. MW::setScope calls MW::maybeAutoScanCatalog, hooked AHEAD of setScope's "scope did not change" return (selecting the Library again after browsing is exactly when a recheck is wanted).

- A throttle, not a schedule: an automatic run is allowed once per G::autoScanCatalogMinutes (default 60), timed from the START of the last automatic run (a big scan can outlast its interval). The Scan button ignores all of this. One preference (Preferences > Library), default on.
- Deferred by a moment, which is not cosmetic: MW::startCatalogScan reconciles the scope on the GUI thread before queueing anything, and the selection that triggered it has just started an asynchronous catalog load; in front of that load the reconcile is a stall. So the run is armed on a short timer, every guard is re-asked when it fires, and it waits again if the datamodel is still being replaced. The delay also coalesces a flurry of selections into one run.
- The automatic scan REPORTS, because a run nobody asked for produces the Library changing under the user, which reads as a bug unexplained. It ends with one transient popup ("Catalog updated: 3 new folders, 412 images added, 120 no longer on disk."), listing only the NON-ZERO parts; when no clause earns its place there is no popup at all, and a stopped run never reports. Rows dropped by the pre-scan scope reconcile are said in the scope's words ("N outside the catalog scope"), not filed under "no longer on disk". Counts, not names; newFolders counts only folders that yielded images.
- The Library view redraws itself from the same handler: FilterPanel::refresh re-runs the query and emits loadResults only when the result actually moved, so a scan that found nothing costs one query and no reload. updateLibraryTree re-reads the Library tree's folders and counts.

#### 17.15.6 The Manage Catalog Dialog

Dialogs/catalogrootsdlg.h: its own dialog, opened from File > Manage Catalog (and the legacy Catalog panel's Manage button). Editing the scope is CONFIGURATION, done once and revisited rarely. It is a Qt::Tool window and NOT MODAL: a scan runs for minutes to hours and this is where its state is shown. It is created on first use and kept, so it survives a scan and can be raised again. (A variable-length folder table is not a PropertyEditor property, which is why Preferences no longer holds an entry point; it was removed 2026-10-13.)

A four-column table (Action, Folder path, Include Subfolders, Images) with Append, Remove, Scan and Close beneath it. APPEND, not Add: it puts a row at the bottom of a table read top to bottom. Everything a row says is visible without selecting it. The mode is a combo (it names both states without a click); the reach is a CHECKABLE ITEM rather than a QCheckBox widget, because a widget in the cell swallows the click that selects the row. Adding a folder already in the table selects that row instead of adding a second rule.

The Images column counts the DISK, not the index, which is what makes it worth a column: a count read out of the catalog agrees with the catalog by construction and could never say whether a scan is owed. The status line puts both numbers side by side ("Catalog: 43,050 images in 176 folders.   Scope: 47,188 images on disk. 4,138 not catalogued yet: press Scan.").

- The column uses the SCANNER'S OWN RULE for what counts (a supported extension, .photoslibrary skipped), so the two numbers count the same thing. It reads NAMES ONLY (QDir::entryList, no stat): entryInfoList over a library is minutes rather than seconds.
- The walk is OFF THE GUI THREAD (QtConcurrent, a generation counter to drop a result whose table has since been edited, the watcher deleting itself). Three appearances: an ellipsis while counting, an em dash for a folder that is not there or whose volume is unmounted, the number otherwise; never a stale figure.
- The TOTAL is the scanner's own walk (catalogScopeFileCount, Main/catalogenumerate.h, the same catalogScopeFolders walk and file-name rule), not arithmetic over the table: the old includes-minus-excludes sum was a second definition of the scope that could disagree with the folders actually walked, and every disagreement showed as images "not catalogued yet" that no scan would ever catalogue.
- The outstanding clause is RED, and nothing else in the window is: it is the one sentence that asks for an action.
- The Images column is sized ONCE for the widest number it will ever hold (9,999,999): a ResizeToContents column jumps every time a count lands, and a settled table then looks like it is still working.
- A row that cannot achieve anything SAYS SO, in place, in the note under the table: nothing included yet, or an exclude outside every included tree ("... is not inside any included folder, so excluding it changes nothing"). The note states the rule the table carries: these folders ARE the catalog, and removing a row forgets what it contributed. (There is no pending-deletion count any more: the reconcile is immediate, so that number would always be zero.)
- While a scan runs, the dialog's button becomes Stop and its scope table is frozen (and the legacy Catalog panel's Manage button is disabled): editing the scope under a running scan would leave the user unsure whether a folder just added is being scanned. File > Manage Catalog is NOT disabled during a scan; the dialog is where scan state is shown.
- The Manage entry stays enabled when the catalog is empty: it is how the user FILLS it. It is disabled only when the database will not open at all.

### 17.16 The Parked Library

The use case: in the Library, hop to Folders to do something in a folder that is not in the Library, then hop back. Every return used to be a full Library load: the catalog query (2.9 s on a pool thread) and the streamed fill (3.8 s of per-row cell work, 78 batches of 2,000), 7.15 s click to cover down at 155,216 rows (Release build). Icons were not the cost: 513 came from the index in 6 ms.

#### 17.16.1 Park and Restore

Leaving a SETTLED Library (MW::libraryParkable: every row in, metadataCompleteDone, nothing writing to the model) MOVES the model aside instead of clearing it, and returning MOVES it back.

- DataModel::parkScope swaps out every store a row is made of (the row store, the scratch store, the icons, the path index, the raw-info cache, the folder list and counts, the issue lists, version masters, the keyword memo, the load-flag counters and the ScopeRequest) inside one model reset, leaving the model empty.
- DataModel::restoreScope swaps them back inside one reset and ends exactly as finishCatalogFill does (current row, setAllMetadataAttempted, endLoad, folderChange), so MW::folderChanged, metadataComplete and the filter build run as after any Library load.
- The swaps are O(1). The stores with locks (RowStore, ScratchStore) exchange under both locks, in address order, and move every generation counter forward on both sides (field generations included), because no setData will announce the new rows.

Leaving:

1. MW::prepareLibraryPark decides (libraryParkable), captures how the Library looked (sort column and direction, Filters::persistableState, the current image), sets parkLibraryOnReset, and asks FilterPanel::parkResults to keep the result paths it would otherwise clear.
2. The folder load's MW::stop -> MW::reset calls parkScope where it would have cleared, and turns on Catalog::trackChangedPaths.

prepareLibraryPark has two callers, and the second is the trap: MW::setScope (every folder load calls it before its stop) and MW::showFoldersSource's nothing-to-go-back-to branch, which stops (clearing the model) BEFORE it sets the scope. That branch is what a Library opened at start-up takes on its first Folders click, so with only the setScope call the first round trip of every session reloaded and later ones were fast ("after a while the switch became much faster"). prepareLibraryPark only ever SETS the flag, so the setScope call that follows that stop, finding no rows, cannot cancel it.

Returning:

1. MW::setScope takes the changed paths, tells the panel to resume (resumeParkedOnEntry) and queues MW::restoreParkedLibrary: loadCatalogScope's teardown and cover, with DataModel::restoreScope in place of the query and fill. MW::stop does not lower the cover for this caller.
2. The view as it was left goes back through the same pending-restore path start-up uses (libraryRestoreSort\*, Filters::setStateToRestore, restoreFiltersPending), and the current image through folderAndFileChangePath. The parked view re-asserts its current image by key on MW::metadataLoaded, past every load-end sort.
3. The FILTER restore is queued only when Filters::isAnyFilter was true at parking. A queued restore holds the cover until the filter build finishes (1.8 s at 155k rows), and persistableState also lists checks that narrow nothing (the search row's placeholder, a collection matching everything), which made the first cut wait 3 s for a view identical to the one it already had.

#### 17.16.2 What Changed While Parked

It is corrected AFTER the restore, never before, so nobody waits for it. Three things can change:

- Row VALUES. Catalog::commit and commitUnreadable are the only writers of a row's values, so while tracking is on they record each path they actually rewrite. commit already skips unchanged rows, so revisiting a catalogued folder records nothing; commitUnreadable now skips an identical stub the same way (the scanner retries every stub on every scan by design, and the first measurement had all 2,488 of them reported changed and re-read on each return). Those rows go through MW::refreshStaleRows, the scroll-in verification's repair, once the load has SETTLED (MW::repairRowsWhenSettled: metadataComplete run, nothing loading, cover down). Called straight after the restore, MetaRead was mid-pass, the re-read never happened and G::allMetadataAttempted stayed false for good. The pending repair is dropped only when the model is REPLACED (modelResetGen), not on dm->instance, which every sort bumps.
- Rows GAINED or LOST (a scan, reconcile, removal, sweep). FilterPanel re-runs the search UNFORCED with the parked path list restored, so its ordinary run-to-run comparison emits resultsDelta and MW::applyCatalogDelta splices them, or reloads above kMaxSpliceDelta.
- AVAILABILITY. The pass is queued again, and its write-back writes Present over a row that was Offline/Missing, since a parked row comes back holding its last answer.

#### 17.16.3 When It Falls Back to a Full Load

- More than Catalog::kMaxTrackedChanges (20,000) value changes, or a Catalog::clear, while parked (overflow).
- The Filters panel's own scope selector switching to the Library (it has already asked for a forced load).
- A restore refused because the model was not empty.
- A Library that had not finished loading is never parked. A row caught mid re-read parks as not attempted and is read after the restore (libraryParkable tests metadataCompleteDone, not G::allMetadataAttempted, which flaps false during such a re-read).

Picks are asked about exactly as for a load.

#### 17.16.4 Cost and Measurements

Measured (WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_ROUNDTRIP=1, three runs): Folders -> Library, click to cover down, 7.15 s -> 1.29-1.34 s at 155,216 rows. restoreParkedLibrary is \~0.57 s of that, entry to folderChange (most of it the proxy taking a 155k-row model reset); the rest is the post-load path every Library load runs (sort, current row, metadataComplete).

The parked model is held while browsing Folders: on the order of 100 MB for the row store at 155k rows, plus the icons that were loaded. It is not yet given back under memory pressure.

#### 17.16.5 The Library Snapshot (First Library of a Session)

The parked set is also written to disk at quit as library.snapshot beside index.db (MW::librarySnapshotPath). MW::saveLibrarySnapshot runs from closeEvent before any teardown: the parked set if the user quits from Folders, else the loaded Library if libraryParkable.

The first Library entry of a session with nothing parked (the start-up reopen, or a session that began in Folders) reads it on a pool thread (MW::startLibrarySnapshotRestore, DataModel::readLibrarySnapshot) while the cover is up, adopts it as the parked set (DataModel::adoptParkedScope, FilterPanel::adoptParkedResults) and takes exactly the parked restore path (MW::enterLibraryPanel -> restoreParkedLibrary). The Filters panel's switch WAITS for the read, because its search must compare against the snapshot's result paths, or it would ask for a full load. librarySnapshotGen voids a read the user has left the Library before.

What is in it (Datamodel/librarysnapshot.cpp):

- The row store, through RowStore::save/load: every ImageRow field through ONE X-macro list that both directions use (WINNOW_IMAGEROW_FIELDS in imagerow.cpp), guarded by a static_assert on sizeof(ImageRow) (496, macOS only), so a new field fails the build until it is added to the list and kRowFormat is bumped.
- The path index, the folder list and counts, the version row count, the memory estimate, and FilterPanel's result paths.
- NOT in it (a fresh fill leaves them too): icons and their geometry bits, the scratch store, the issue lists, the raw-info cache, the keyword memo.
- The version masters' metadata (DataModel::versionMasters) is REBUILT from the index (Catalog::rowsForPaths + IndexMetadata::fill); without it the load-end version reconcile would see version rows no master lists, and remove them.
- The scope comes back with ScopeRequest::hydrated set, since it has no rows vector. Every "rows came from the index" test goes through ScopeRequest::isHydrated() (four in MW, one in ScrollVerify), not !rows.isEmpty().

Validity. The reader refuses:

- another format;
- another BUILD (the executable's size and mtime): a rebuild may change what a row means, and a misread row would be shown as fact. The cost is one ordinary load after each update or rebuild. The fingerprint is pinned at START (DataModel::librarySnapshotFingerprint, called from MW's constructor); it used to read the executable at the moment of saving, so a Winnow left running across a rebuild stamped its snapshot with the NEW binary and the new build trusted rows the old code wrote;
- another INDEX (Catalog::catalogId, a random identity in catalog_meta, replaced by Catalog::clear).

Then the change sequence, the index's half. Schema 20 adds image.change_seq, stamped by Catalog::commit and commitUnreadable with a counter in catalog_meta advanced once per writing transaction. The snapshot records the counter its rows were READ at (FilterPanel captures Catalog::changeSeq before searchRows and keeps it as loadedSeq through parking and restores), and Catalog::pathsChangedSince(that) names the rows to re-read. More than kMaxSnapshotChanges (20,000), or a counter that went backwards, means a full load. Rows gained or lost while Winnow was closed are handled by the FilterPanel delta re-run, as for a parked restore. The base sequence deliberately does not advance on a restore: the repair is asynchronous, so advancing it could hide a row that was never re-read; the cost is that changes accumulate until a full load resets it.

Compression (format 2). The magic and format are a raw header; everything after goes through Utilities/zchunkdevice.h, a QIODevice that writes [length][qCompress level 1] chunks of 4 MB and a 0 end mark, so the QDataStream code on top is unchanged and memory stays at a few chunks. Writing, up to four chunks compress on worker threads while rows are still being serialised, written in order; reading, the next chunk inflates while this one is parsed. A missing end mark or a damaged chunk FAILS the stream (ZChunkDevice::streamError) rather than ending it quietly, so a cut-short file is a full load, never a partial Library. Why compress: the file is rewritten at every quit and lives in Application Support, which backups copy.

Measured at 155,216 rows (Release, real index):

- Start-up, exposed to cover down: 9.51 s -> 3.69-3.71 s. Of that, snapshot read 0.76 s (pool thread), restore 0.49 s, and \~1.9 s of filter build plus the saved filter landing, which the cover rightly waits for when a filter narrows the view.
- Size: 275 MB uncompressed (\~1.8 KB a row, mostly the per-row strings) -> 26 MB. Command-line zstd would give 18 MB but is a new dependency on both platforms; zlib comes with Qt.
- Read 0.76 s -> 0.78-0.80 s, the inflate almost entirely hidden behind parsing.
- Write 0.41 s uncompressed -> 0.28 s with four chunks in flight: smaller AND faster than writing it raw.

Not done: the snapshot is written only at quit (a crash keeps the previous one, which is still checked and still valid), and the Folders side is not parked, which the same mechanism could do.

#### 17.16.6 Tests and Probes

- ctest park_restore (WINNOW_SELFTEST_PARK=1, Main/selftestpark.cpp): Library -> Folders with nothing to go back to -> a folder picked -> Library on the fixture folder, asserting the model was parked, then restored (libraryRestoreCount, so a reload cannot pass), with the same keys and current image, verifyIntegrity clean and the worker row view rebuilt, under the model-contract tester.
- ctest library_snapshot (WINNOW_SELFTEST_SNAPSHOT=1): Library -> snapshot written -> Folders -> parked copy dropped -> one index row rewritten -> Library, asserting a counted restore, exactly one row reported changed, that row re-read and the load settled again, and the same rows and current image.
- Both self-tests catalogue the fixture themselves (MW::selfTestCatalogueFolder); they had passed only on an index earlier runs left behind. The smoke tests share one test-mode index: run them serially.
- tst_imagerow::snapshotRoundTripsEveryCell compares every covered cell through RowStore::save/load; tst_catalog::changeSequenceStampsWrittenRows covers the sequence, the identity and rowsForPaths; tst_zchunkdevice covers the round trip across many chunks, the empty stream, truncation and corruption.
- Measure with --catalogload: WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD_SAVESNAPSHOT=1 writes a snapshot at settle (the harness exits without closeEvent), then \_STARTUP=1 uses it.
- Probe lines (WINNOW_PERF_PROBE=1 or --perfprobe): "[PERF] leaving the Library (&lt;caller>): parkable = ... (&lt;first failed condition>)", "[PERF] Library NOT parked at reset", "[PERF] entering the Library: restore parked = ...", "[PERF] Library parked", "[PERF] restoreParkedLibrary ... rows restored in ... ms", "[PERF] parked Library dropped: &lt;why>".

#### 17.16.7 Older Defects the Snapshot Test Found

1. MW::folderChanged made folderAndFileChangePath current with MW::instance, a member NEVER ASSIGNED, so DataModel::setCurrent always failed its instance check: the image asked for (by a Finder open, or a restore) was never made current. It uses dm->instance now, and its start row is the PROXY row.
2. MetaRead's first selection crossed threads as a proxy row from its own snapshot, so a sort on the GUI thread before it landed (a restored Library's, at load end) made it select a neighbouring image. MetaRead::selectRow now carries the DataModel row too, mapped through the live proxy at the connect site (Main/initialize.cpp).
3. Popup::showPopup1 messages a native window, and under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen there is none: the first self-test to reach a popup (an auto-scan's "Catalog updated") SIGSEGV'd. It prints instead, headless.

### 17.17 New and Deleted Files Follow the Catalog

Export, ingest, stacks, copies, deletes. An image Winnow makes INSIDE the catalog scope is catalogued at once. Before this, an export into a library folder, an ingest onto the library drive or a focus stack written beside its sources sat outside search until the next scan, which with the throttled auto-scan could be a long way off. The rule is unchanged (the scope table is definitive, and a new file is catalogued exactly when the next scan would have catalogued it); only the timing moved.

#### 17.17.1 One Notification: FileOps::onCreated(paths)

Every producer calls it once the file is COMPLETE (metadata copied, sidecar written), because what it reports may be parsed within the second:

- Export (ImageExporter::onImageReady), which also carries Develop export and File > Save Preview as.
- Embellish export (EmbelExport::exportImages, after ExifTool has copied tags, ICC and thumbnail).
- Ingest, both the background Ingest::run and IngestDlg::ingest, primary and backup destinations, reported after the loop so every sidecar is already beside its image.
- Focus stack results (FS, where G::fsFusedPaths is recorded) and the mean stack (Stack::mean).
- Utilities::backup: a backup inside the scope is an image in the scope.
- FileOps::onCopied and FileOps::onMoved call it for their destination, so copy / paste, drag-copy onto a folder or bookmark, rename and moves are covered without their callers doing anything. A move whose row Catalog::onMoved already carried costs one stat and no parse: its stamps still match.

Deliberately NOT reported: focus-stack intermediates and debug dumps, and the transient embellish thumbnails. They are working files, not results (if they land inside the scope a scan will still find them; that is a question about where they are written).

The hook is MW's, because MW owns catalogScope. FileOps::setCreatedHook is set in MW::createCatalogScanner and cleared in closeEvent. onCreated may run on any thread (Ingest::run is a QThread), so the hook only posts to the GUI thread, and it is called under a mutex so that once the clear returns nothing can still be reaching into MW. Unset (unit tests), onCreated is a no-op.

Batched, filtered, then handed to the scanner thread. MW::catalogCreatedFiles collects paths for 500 ms, so an export of 300 files is one batch and one Library refresh. MW::flushCatalogCreatedFiles keeps a path when its extension passes catalogCandidateName and its folder passes MW::isCatalogScopeFolder (the scan's two rules), and queues CatalogScanner::indexFiles: the scan's Indexing phase over a given list (stamp, Catalog::staleOf, parse what is stale, commit; an unparseable file gets the usual unreadable stub). It is NOT a scan (it does not set isRunning() or report progress), and it waits behind a running scan on the same thread rather than racing it. It gives way to folder loads like the scan does, and stops for shutdown on its own closing flag (the scan's abort flag stays raised after a user Stop and would wrongly cancel it).

#### 17.17.2 The Library Redraws by Splicing

CatalogScanner::filesIndexed drives the same refresh a finished scan does (Filter panel re-query, LibTree counts, Manage Catalog status if open). Nothing pops up: the user just made these files.

The re-query SPLICES, it does not reload. It used to emit loadResults whenever the result paths changed, which is a full model reset: an export into a Library folder cleared the filters, selection and place about a second after it finished. FilterPanel::applySearchResult now diffs an UNASKED re-run (not forced, uncapped, over a result it had loaded) against the previous result and emits resultsDelta(added, removed) when the difference is at most kMaxSpliceDelta (200) paths. MW::applyCatalogDelta drops paths the model already has (onExportFinished inserts an export into a registered folder first) and removals already made, then runs the rest through MW::applyModelChange, which saves and restores the filters. A model that is not a settled Library load (Folders scope, a load running, empty) falls back to the full load, and so does a larger delta, because the splice reads each added file on the GUI thread. A finished background scan takes the same path.

#### 17.17.3 Deletions Leave the Catalog at Once Too

Deleting images was already covered: MW::deleteFiles goes through FileOps::trashFiles, whose FileOps::onDeleted calls Catalog::onDeleted, and that DELETES the row rather than demoting it, because a removal Winnow made is certain. What was missing was FOLDERS and two direct removes:

- FileOps::onFolderDeleted(folder) calls Catalog::forgetUnder(folder, recurse) and returns the rows removed. Callers: MW::deleteFolder (only once moveToTrash succeeds), MW::deleteAllImageMemCard (the DCIM folder), and FS::cleanup's work and input folders.
- FS::cleanup's temporary input images and EmbelExport::exportRemoteFiles' temporary sources call FileOps::onDeleted when the remove succeeds.
- The GUI callers redraw through MW::refreshLibraryAfterCatalogChange, which the filesIndexed handler also uses. FS::cleanup runs on the stack thread and does not redraw; the Library catches up on its next refresh.

A folder delete clears every store onDeleted clears. Besides the catalog, onFolderDeleted is called on ThumbCache (thumbnail rows), DevPreviewCache (index rows AND their payload files, through removeLocked so the byte total stays right), CollectionStore (membership; it hops to its own thread like onDeleted, and emits membersChanged when anything went) and HistoryStore (Develop undo history). Each matches by PATH-KEY PREFIX, substr(pathkey, 1, n) = cachePathKey(folder) + "/", so subfolders and version keys ("&lt;path>/#v&lt;id>") go too, and the trailing separator keeps a sibling such as "2024 raw" safe when "2024" is deleted. substr rather than LIKE so an underscore or percent in a folder name needs no escaping. Pinned by tst_fileops::folderDeleteClearsPreviewsUnderItOnly.

The mirror case is NOT immediate: a catalogued image MOVED OUT of the scope keeps its row, because Catalog::onMoved rewrites the path wherever it lands. It leaves at the next scan, when MW::reconcileCatalogToScope forgets folders the table does not admit.

### 17.18 Long Scans: Progress, Time Left, Resume, and Catalog Diagnostics

A library scan is a BACKGROUND JOB, not a "come back later". Adding 100,000 images takes hours, and it always ran on its own low-priority thread, giving way to folder loads and committing every 200 rows. What it lacked was an account of itself: progress moved once per folder (a folder of 10,000 images sat still for an hour), there was no estimate, and a quit part way through was lost until somebody pressed Scan again.

#### 17.18.1 Two Phases, Because Only the Second Has an Honest Total

CHECKING walks every folder, reconciles it, stats every candidate and asks Catalog::staleOf which need reading, keeping only their PATHS (a whole CatalogRow per file would be hundreds of MB at 100k). INDEXING then parses exactly those. done / total in Indexing is therefore a count of parses, and the rate is a parse rate: files skipped as unchanged cost microseconds and would otherwise make any estimate meaningless. The split costs one extra stat per stale file.

Progress is a struct, throttled. CatalogScanner::progress(CatalogScanProgress) carries phase, done, total, files/s, seconds left and paused, at most four times a second. The rate is measured over the last 60 s of ACTIVE time (time paused for a folder load is left out, or browsing during a scan would make the estimate climb), and no estimate is shown ("estimating...") until 50 files or 10 s of data. catalogFormatEta words it: "about 2 h 10 m", "about 4 min", "less than a minute". Checking has its own estimate (folders per second, "left to check"): it is usually seconds, but the first measured rescan spent 268 s there.

#### 17.18.2 Where It Is Shown

- The status-bar row's LABEL never changes ("Scanning for changes"); the counts and time left are the row's TOOLTIP (Progress::setRowToolTip). The first version put them in the label, which failed twice: Progress sizes one shared text column to the widest label and clips it to the container (\~100-200 px), so the estimate was cut off; and every setRowText rebuilds EVERY row's bar pixmap, so four label changes a second wiped the Image Cache and Metadata bars.
- Manage Catalog, when open, shows a bar and two lines ("Indexing 12,345 of 98,765 images · 14 per second · about 1 h 23 m left", then in grey that the window can be closed).
- Loading a catalog result has a status-bar row too ("Loading", blue). The streamed fill (DataModel::insertCatalogBatch) put "x of y images loading..." in the central message, which the grid covers as soon as it paints, and at 150k rows the fill runs for seconds. DataModel::catalogFillProgress(done, total) is emitted per batch, and finishCatalogFill emits (0, 0), which clears the row whether the fill finished or was stopped.
- Filter count columns fit the total: they were sized for "-99999-", so a 154,933-image catalog drew its count clipped. MW::folderChangeCompleted calls Filters::setCountCeiling(dm->rowCount()), and both count columns widen to fit that number as the delegate draws it (locale-grouped), never narrower than before.

#### 17.18.3 The Manage Catalog Window Fits Its Contents

- The scope table is exactly as tall as its rows (header + rows, scrolling beyond 12), and CatalogRootsDlg::fitToContents resizes the window's height whenever rows, the note, the status or the scan progress change, deferred a tick and coalesced.
- The status label is deliberately NOT word-wrapped: it holds an HTML table, and a word-wrapped rich-text QLabel under-reports its height, which clipped a line.
- The info section is a TABLE (2026-09-25), 850 px wide, set off by a rule: Catalogued, On disk, Status (the red "press Scan" value and "See which"), Cannot catalogue, Unreadable, Disk space. It had been one run-on sentence.
- DISK SPACE comes from CacheDb::storageUsage, measured with the scope counts off the GUI thread: index.db (+ -wal, -shm), the thumbnail JPEGs inside it, the develop preview files beside it, and the folder that holds them. The split inside index.db is exact only with SQLite's dbstat table, which Qt's bundled SQLite does NOT have; without it the thumbnail figure is the JPEG data (SUM(bytes)) and the remainder is labelled "Catalog and overhead ≈" (measured: 334 MB against an exact 228 MB on a 1.28 GB index).

#### 17.18.4 A Scan That Did Not Finish Resumes at the Next Launch

MW::startCatalogScan writes catalogScanIncomplete = true to settings AT ONCE (a crash or a forced quit is exactly the case it exists for); the finished handler clears it on a complete pass, and also when the user pressed Stop (a Stop is final). MW::resumeIncompleteCatalogScan runs once at start-up: five seconds in, then retrying every 1.5 s for about a minute while a load is running, it starts the scan as an automatic one. Nothing is redone: staleOf skips everything already indexed. Automated harnesses (G::isAutomatedRun) never resume.

#### 17.18.5 "13 Images Not Catalogued Yet: Press Scan" That No Scan Closed

Two causes, both fixed, and a report for anything else:

- The count and the scanner walked different definitions of the scope. Both now use catalogScopeFolders ([17.15.6 The Manage Catalog Dialog](#17156-the-manage-catalog-dialog)).
- Some files can never be catalogued: zero-byte files (the scanner skips them; a names-only count cannot see size) and NAME TWINS ("IMG_1.JPG" beside "img_1.jpg" on a case-sensitive volume, or one name in two Unicode forms). The index keys on cachePathKey (NFC, case-folded), so twins shared one row, each overwriting the other and each looking stale to every scan. The scanner now keeps the first and counts the rest. A complete scan saves zeroByte + collisions as catalogUncatalogable, and the status line takes that many out of the red clause and names them instead: "N files cannot be catalogued (empty, or a name that differs only in case from another). See which."

#### 17.18.6 Catalog Diagnostics

Help > Diagnostics > Catalog diagnostics; the Diagnostics... button in Manage Catalog; the status line's "See which" link. Built off the GUI thread (a popup says so), it walks and stats the whole scope with catalogScopeFiles, reads every index row with Catalog::allPaths (paged by id, the lock taken per page), and classifies the difference with catalogAnalyzeGap, a pure function, so tst_catalog drives it with synthetic case twins. Sections:

- Summary, with the identity disk - rows = not catalogued - not on disk - outside scope, so every image the status line counts is accounted for.
- The scope table, with unmounted / missing roots flagged.
- On disk, not catalogued (zero-byte / name twin of &lt;path> / not in the index).
- Catalogued, not found on disk (volume not mounted / on disk but the walk does not reach it / file gone, live or demoted).
- Catalogued outside the scope; Changed since indexed; Unreadable stubs; Last scan.

Lists are grouped by reason and capped at 500 paths with the count of the rest.

#### 17.18.7 Where the Time Went

Every scan records CatalogScanStats (CatalogScanner::lastStats): walk, directory listing, reconcile, stat / stamp, staleOf, parse and commit, each as active milliseconds and per-file cost, plus time paused. The report prints them. This is the measurement the parallel-parsing decision waited on.

The first measurement settled it (2026-09-25). A rescan of 155k files in 8,842 folders took 290 s, and 268 s of it was "reconcile"; parsing was 2.2 s. Catalog::reconcileFolder's "WHERE folder = ? AND live = 1" was planned on image_live rather than image_folder (the index has no ANALYZE statistics), and since nearly every row is live, each folder read the whole table: 39 ms per folder against 0.08 ms. The query now says "+live = 1", which keeps the planner off image_live; tst_catalog pins the plan (reconcileQueryUsesTheFolderIndex). Parallel parsing is not needed on this evidence.

### 17.19 Investigations and Fixes

#### 17.19.1 What Selecting the Catalog Actually Cost (14.2 s to 1.7 s, and the Three Bugs Underneath)

The complaint was the Filters. Selecting the Catalog on a 41,464-image library put the images on screen in about two seconds and then left the Filters panel stale for another twelve, with the central widget still showing the last message the fill had written. The obvious reading (building the filter tree over 41,000 rows is expensive) was wrong, and no amount of reading the code would have said so. A temporary probe (one stopwatch, laps at every stage, the whole span from the click to "images shown AND filters built") said it in one run: the filter build was 290 ms of a 14,111 ms load, about 2%. The 11,734 ms was a single segment ending BEFORE the build began.

- What that segment was: MW::folderChangeCompleted is reached only from MetaRead::done, and a hydrated catalog scope arrives with every row already MetaLoaded from the index and NOT ONE icon, so MetaRead is started for thumbnails alone, ten thousand of them, and everything hanging off folderChangeCompleted waited for it. Nothing in the filter build reads an icon. The wait was structural, not computational.
- So the tail was SPLIT by what it depends on. MW::metadataComplete holds everything the load can finish without an icon (the filter build, the sort and filter controls, the column widths, the catalog commit), and folderChangeCompleted keeps only what depends on the READ having finished (the progress row and the thread light). A folder load reaches the same code at the same moment as before, because there metadata and icons arrive together; a hydrated scope calls metadataComplete directly, after the readers have been set going. One guard makes the early call safe rather than a second execution.
- The drain that was the icon wait in disguise: buildFiltersWhenModelReady waits for dm->queuedReaderEvents to reach zero, and that counter is bumped for ICON deliveries as well as metadata ones, so on a hydrated scope the drain WAS the icon wait, one 10 ms poll at a time. The condition it guards is already true there by a stronger route (the fill is synchronous and setAllMetadataAttempted has run before folderChange is emitted), so it is skipped.
- The icons themselves: ThumbCache::get is shaped for the Reader (one path, a stat to learn the stamps, a SELECT, a decode, and a dispatch round trip), right when the icon is wanted because the user scrolled to it and wrong at ten thousand. ThumbCache::getBatch takes the stamps IN the request (a catalog row's size and mtime came out of the image table, so nothing is stat'd), prepares one statement for the whole batch, and MW::prefetchIconsFromIndex runs it over the chunk on a pool thread, decodes there, and hands the results back through setIcon1, so every piece of per-icon bookkeeping happens exactly as for a Reader icon. It is a PRE-PASS: whatever it cannot find is left to MetaRead. Reading all 32,552 stored thumbnails out of SQLite takes 134 ms.
- Pure duplication: FilterPanel::applyScope ran the whole 41,464-row catalog query TWICE per scope switch (once as runSearch(true), then again through the trailing refresh(), which for a Catalog scope IS runSearch), 346 ms of the critical path asking the same question twice.

What was measured and thrown away: RowStore::setValue takes a write lock per CELL (about 1.87 million acquisitions for the load), and batching that per row is an obvious-looking win. It is 13% of the insert in a debug build and ESSENTIALLY ZERO in release; the per-row lock hold was designed and then not written. Anything measured in a debug build is measuring the wrong program: the same load is 3,730 ms there and 800 ms in release, and the proportions do not survive the difference.

What the insert actually cost (release, per row): addMeta 9.8 us, fileData 4.1, indexFill 1.4, insertRows 0.8. Inside addMetadataForItem the keyword expansion was 2.8 us (28% of it), and keywordEffectivePaths / keywordPrefixExpand are pure functions of the two keyword lists. A library reuses those lists heavily (18,325 rows carry hierarchical paths but only 2,935 DISTINCT values, and 23,653 rows carry none), so memoised on the two lists (with their counts in the key, because joining lists is ambiguous on its own) and given a branch for the empty case, the insert went 800 ms to 730.

#### 17.19.2 The Catalog Capture Was Silently Not Running

A real bug, not a test artefact. It looked at first like the headless test could not reach it: a folder loaded, MW::folderChangeCompleted ran, and the catalog stayed empty.

MW::folderChangeCompleted read DataModel::catalogRows() INLINE. catalogRows() skips any row that is not yet G::MetaLoaded, and the writes that set that status arrive from the Reader and Thumb threads as QUEUED setValDm events. MetaRead::done, which calls folderChangeCompleted, can fire while those events are still in the GUI thread's event queue, so catalogRows() returned an EMPTY list, the `if (!rows.isEmpty())` guard skipped the commit, and the folder was never indexed. Nothing reported it: the capture is opportunistic, and silently doing nothing looks exactly like silently succeeding.

It depended on nothing but timing, which is why the catalog had entries for some folders and not others, and why a headless run indexed nothing (the app exits before the queue drains). Probes confirmed each link: folderChangeCompleted reached (twice), the catalog available, catalogRows() returning 12 at the selftest exit and 0 at the moment it was called.

Fix: the capture is POSTED rather than run inline. A queued invocation runs after every event already posted, which is exactly the set of status writes being waited for. A headless run now catalogues 12 of 12 in a raw+jpg folder and 47 of 50 in the mixed one (the other three are videos, which catalogRows skips by design).

catalog_capture is the ctest that was missing: it loads the fixture folder and fails if nothing reached the catalog. Verified to fail by restoring the inline capture ("catalogued=0 rows=4"). The wait it needs lives in that mode alone and NOT on the default selftest path, because waiting lets pool tasks complete and queue GUI callbacks that then run around the model_contract test's own row removal, which made that gate flaky.

#### 17.19.3 The Filter Tree Recompiled Once per Item (56 Seconds of Dead GUI)

A person clicked Catalog and waited several minutes for thumbnails, twice, after two earlier fixes had each made the headless numbers look fine. Every automated check ran on a \~1,000-row fixture, and this whole class of bug only appears at 43,000. Winnow --catalogload (MW::runCatalogLoadTest) exists for that: the real index, the real load path, headless, printing the time to the first batch and the last, then sampling the event loop every second until icons stop arriving.

It showed the fill finishing at 11.2 s and the first one-second tick not firing until 67 s: the GUI thread blocked solid for 56 seconds AFTER every row was in the model. A sample said where: BuildFilters::applyOps -> Filters::updateFilteredCountPerItem -> SortFilter::compileFilters -> QTreeWidgetItem::checkState -> qvariant_cast.

SortFilter recompiled the whole predicate on every tree mutation. It connects to itemChanged plus the tree model's rowsInserted/rowsRemoved so that no path mutating the tree can forget to say so, which is right, and the comment beside it claimed the cost "lands once rather than once per item" because filtering is suspended during a rebuild. That was wrong: suspension stops FILTERING, not COMPILING. BuildFilters adds items and updates counts thousands of times per rebuild and each compile walks every item, so a rebuild was O(items^2): invisible at 500 rows, 56 seconds at 43,050.

The fix is coalescing, not disconnecting. scheduleCompileFilters sets a pending flag and posts one compile to the next turn of the event loop. compileFilters clears the flag, so the synchronous compile SortFilter::filterChange does before it invalidates cannot leave the predicate a turn behind the tree the user just clicked. The predicate is derived wholly from the tree, so compiling once gives the same answer as compiling n times.

Measured, 43,050 rows, debug build:

```
  first batch inserted        5,900 ms  ->  1,403 ms
  fill complete              11,219 ms  ->  7,033 ms
  event loop responsive      67,026 ms  ->  8,004 ms
```

The compile storm also delayed the START (tree mutations during teardown and setup recompiled too). It is a Filters fix that a catalog scope was the first thing big enough to expose; every folder load paid a smaller version of the same bill.

A hydrated catalog scope also stopped committing itself back. MW::folderChangeCompleted builds the commit payload with dm->catalogRows(), which reads \~40 columns of every row on the GUI thread, and wrote them to the index for rows that had just come OUT of the index, unchanged. It is skipped when the scope is hydrated (ScopeRequest::isHydrated()). A folder scope still commits, because its rows were read from files and the index may never have seen them.

#### 17.19.4 Metadata Done Is Not Work Done (Why No Thumbnail Ever Appeared)

Filters appeared instantly and thumbnails never appeared at all: not slowly, never. MW::folderChanged has an early return that means "nothing was added, so there is nothing to read":

```
  if (dm->isMetaReadFinished()) { ...; folderChangeCompleted(); return; }
```

It was correct for the only two cases it had ever seen: a load that only removed rows, and an empty folder. isMetaReadFinished() asks ONLY about metadata (metadataAttemptedCount >= rowCount()). A hydrated catalog scope satisfies it on arrival, because every row came out of the index already MetaLoaded, and NOT ONE ICON is loaded. So metaRead->initialize and setStartRow were both skipped and nothing ever asked for a thumbnail.

Fix: the early return also requires isIconRangeLoaded(), and dm->setIconRange(startRow) moved above it (the range has to exist before it can be asked about). Measured after, 43,050 rows, debug, headless: fill complete 5,105 ms, 3,917 icons at the first tick (6,184 ms), 5,171 by 13,370 ms.

What this cost: three fixes in a row each looked complete on the headless numbers and each left a person waiting (a pump that never pumped, a filter tree that recompiled per item, and this). icons=0 sat in --catalogload's output for two rounds before it was read as the signal it was; it was explained away as an artefact of running offscreen. The icon range is chunk-based, not visibility-based, so it never was one.

#### 17.19.5 The Redo Loop That Could Never Finish

The catalog beachball was not the filters, and the numbers said so once a person clicked with the stall watchdog armed:

```
  [PERF] FilterPanel::applyScope       602 ms
  REDO MAXED OUT  (x12)
  [PERF] GUI STALL 31029 ms  ending at t = 32577 ms  dmRows = 42979
  [PERF] BuildFilters::applyOps      0 ms  ops = 0
  [PERF] BuildFilters::applyOps      0 ms  ops = 32
  [PERF] GUI STALL 10946 ms  ending at t = 43523 ms
  [PERF] BuildFilters::applyOps     78 ms  ops = 35
```

MetaRead::allMetaIconLoaded is G::allMetadataAttempted && G::iconChunkLoaded, and a hydrated catalog scope makes the first true on arrival, so the question is whether the icon chunk is COMPLETE. When every reader has been dispatched, none is pending, and that is still false, MetaRead concludes a read FAILED and calls redo(), which resets to startRow and re-dispatches across the whole model, up to redoMax (5) times per arm. That retry was written for a folder of a few hundred.

Two causes:

1. G::iconChunkLoaded could never become true. DataModel::updateIconChunkLoaded required every row in the 10,000-row chunk to carry an icon, discounting only videos. A catalog scope holds rows whose file is on an unplugged drive or deleted, and such a row can never produce an icon. Unloadable rows now come off the requirement: DataModel::iconUnloadableCount is maintained on AvailabilityColumn writes in setData and resynced by recountLoadFlags like the other counters, and isAllIconChunkLoaded skips a row whose availability is not Present. A folder load, which never writes that column, is unaffected.
2. Redo was retrying a queue, not a failure. The breakdown read "iconRange 0 - 10000 noIcon = 8918 (notAttempted = 0 attemptedButNoIcon = 8918) video = 210", identical across all twelve warnings, and notAttempted = 0 was guaranteed rather than informative (a hydrated row is MetaLoaded at fill time). The icon writes come back from the Reader and Thumb threads as QUEUED events, so while the GUI thread is busy applying them, iconLoadedAt still reads false for icons that have already arrived. Redo took that for a failed read, re-dispatched readers for those same rows, and queued more events onto the thread that was already behind. Redo is now bounded by PROGRESS: it counts the icons present in the range and only repeats if the last pass gained some. redoMax still caps the rest.

Measured after both, headless, 43,050 rows:

```
  worst GUI stall     41,596 ms  ->  2,817 ms
  icons in chunk      stuck      ->  10,000 (complete)
  settled             never      ->  21.6 s
```

REDO MAXED OUT still appears, now legitimately: each pass gains icons, so the guard lets it run to the cap, and it reports a real shortfall rather than a spin.

What this cost: four rounds of "fixed it" that were not, three because a headless run reported healthy numbers for code that stalled in the GUI, and twice because a number in the probe's own output (icons=0, treeItems=17) was explained away instead of checked. The stall watchdog exists because it measures the SYMPTOM (how late a 250 ms timer fired) rather than a function somebody suspected.

#### 17.19.6 Is What We Loaded Still True? (the Whole-Set Sweep, and the Three Bugs That Stopped It Repairing Anything)

The gap: ScrollVerify checks the rows a person is LOOKING AT, leaving the other forty thousand unverified until they scroll to them ([17.12 Verifying a Hydrated Row (Scroll-In Stat)](#1712-verifying-a-hydrated-row-scroll-in-stat)); CatalogScanner checks the scope tree ON DISK, a different set reached by a folder walk. Neither answers "is the set I just loaded still true". ScrollVerify::verifyWholeSet does: the same stat, the same Catalog::outOfDate question and the same repair, paged 2,000 rows at a time over every loaded row, three seconds after the load settles. It is affordable for the reason the scroll pass is (a stat is \~137x cheaper than a read), and the scroll pass outranks it for the single in-flight slot, because the rows on screen are the ones whose staleness can be seen.

It found two stale rows and could NOT fix either. The chain is: detect, clear the row, let the loader re-read it, commit the corrected row back. It reported "committed 0 of 2 pending" five times and gave up. Three bugs, each hiding the next, and only the first was reachable by reasoning:

1. A NULL pixmap is a REMOVE, and setIcon treated it as "already have one". DataModel::setIcon is idempotent on a row that already carries a decoration (the guard exists so that replacing a live QIcon cannot run \~QPixmapIconEngine under memory pressure), and it fired for a NULL pixmap too, setting IconLoadedColumn back to TRUE and returning without clearing anything. Both callers that pass a null pixmap meant remove. MetaRead::needToRead returns false on iconLoadedAt() BEFORE it looks at the metadata status, so a row whose icon survives can never be re-read: the clear was restoring the flag that made the row ineligible ([5.6 Icon Loading Rules](#56-icon-loading-rules)).
2. The repair committed the stamps that had just FAILED. catalogRowFor takes srcSize and srcMtime from the model's ByteSize and Modified columns, which is correct for the bulk capture (they were filled from the same enumeration about to be committed). A re-read refreshes the metadata columns through addMetadataForItem and never touches those two, because addFileDataForRow runs only when a row is first added. So the row still carried the values that had just been declared stale.
3. The two freshness paths disagreed about SIDECARS. catalogRowFor stats the .xmp only when the model's SidecarColumn says there is one, and for a hydrated row that column was derived from the stored sidecarMtime, which is 0 for precisely the rows whose sidecar appeared AFTER they were catalogued; IndexMetadata::candidate stats it unconditionally. One side committed 0, the other found a real mtime, for ever. Both fixes are in MW::catalogRowsForStale rather than catalogRowFor, so the bulk capture keeps its deliberately stat-free gate and the repair path pays one stat for a row already known to have changed.

The test of a repair loop is that it SETTLES: stale = 2, repair, then stale = 0 on the next load. Before the fixes the content was corrected on every load and the freshness never converged, which is indistinguishable from working unless you run it twice.

And a retry that could not stop: catalogRowsForStale leaves a row pending until it comes back MetaLoaded (so a half-read row is never committed over a good index entry), which means the drain's stopping condition is somebody else's work finishing. When the re-read never landed it re-armed every three seconds for the rest of the session. The allowance is now bounded the way MW::rebuildAbortedFilters bounds its own: giving up is cheap, because the verification passes forget an answer after kReverifySecs and ask again.

#### 17.19.7 Why Raw Thumbnails Were Never Cached (the Stale Struct on the Icon-Only Read)

The shape of the evidence: after the bulk prefetch landed, a catalog load served 8,437 of 9,789 icons from the index and read 1,352 from files, and the SAME 1,352 on every load, with the thumbnail count never moving. A cache that never fills is a cache with a bug in it, not a cold one. 1,241 of them were raw (1,190 arw and 46 cr2), against every jpg and tif in the chunk caching on first sight.

Two hypotheses died first. Not the develop gate (ThumbCache stands aside for an edited image in a developed-showing mode, but all 1,241 had no recipe, and 112 developed rows WERE cached). Not the sidecar path truncating dotted filenames (self-consistent then; sidecar naming has since been rewritten, [9.2 Sidecar Naming](#92-sidecar-naming)).

The cause is that `m` describes the PREVIOUS ROW. On an icon-only read Reader::readMetadata is skipped, so m still holds the last row's metadata, or a default-constructed struct on the reader's first task. readIcon gated its header re-read on m->fromIndex, which is therefore that row's answer, and false by default. The walk was skipped for exactly the rows needing it: a hydrated catalog row, whose offsets were preset from the model and are 0, because the decode geometry is deliberately not stored (an offset of 0 is a legal offset, so leaving the fields unset is what makes the gap detectable). A JPEG survives (loadThumb finds an embedded thumbnail unaided); a RAW cannot (the preview's location is only in the header). So it produced no image, fell back to the error icon, never reached putImage, and missed the cache again next time.

The gate now asks what it can answer LOCALLY (do I have usable offsets?) rather than interrogating a struct that may belong to another row. The cache then fills itself through ordinary loads: 8,437 to 9,675 of 9,789 over six of them, the residual being 112 develop-edited rows (correctly excluded), two PNGs with no embedded preview and a video. (The same stale-struct trap later turned rotated icons the wrong way; Reader::read now fills orientation, rotation, develop state and size from the model on an icon-only read, [11.26.4 The Grid Thumbnail](#11264-the-grid-thumbnail).)

No backfill scanner was built, and the plan had called for one. The premise (coverage was a gap to be filled by indexing more eagerly) was wrong: ordinary browsing already writes every thumbnail it decodes, and coverage was not growing because of a defect in the path that decodes them. A scanner-side thumbnailer would have hidden it.

#### 17.19.8 Twenty Images the Scan Could Never Catalogue

Unreadable stubs, and three HEIC parser defects. The first library the scope table shipped against settled at 20 images on disk and not in the index, and pressing Scan could never close the gap: Metadata::loadImageMetadata failed on them (18 HEIC and 2 JPG), so parseInto dropped them and no row was written. A file that is on disk, absent from the index and invisible to every part of the UI is not something a user can act on; the only evidence was a difference between two counts.

##### 17.19.8.1 Unreadable Files Are Catalogued as Stubs

The scan writes a STUB ROW for each such file (Catalog::commitUnreadable): path, folder, filename, extension and the freshness stamp, and nothing else, because everything else in a catalog row comes from the parse that failed, and writing zeros into those columns would be inventing a photograph's metadata.

- The stamp is the point of storing them: staleOf compares it like any other row, so a rescan does not re-attempt an unchanged file; a file that IS changed goes stale and is tried again, and the ordinary commit CLEARS the flag when the parse succeeds (image.unreadable = 0 on every normal write).
- They surface as a fourth AVAILABILITY, Unreadable ([17.8 Availability (Offline Is Not Missing)](#178-availability-offline-is-not-missing)), which makes them a list rather than a number. The editor's status line points at it by name.
- The old bookkeeping went with it: a persisted MW::catalogUnreadable, reset whenever the scope changed, was two sources of truth for one fact; the count comes from Catalog::unreadableCount(). Because a stub IS a catalogued row, the scope and catalog totals reconcile again rather than being permanently 20 apart.

##### 17.19.8.2 And None of Them Was Unreadable at All

Reviewed one by one, all 20 were HEIC (including two that call themselves .JPG and are ftypheic inside), and Winnow renders every one of them in the loupe. Three separate defects lay behind one symptom, and the first two hid the third:

1. A 64-bit LARGESIZE read as "rest of file". An ISO base media box whose size field is 1 carries its real length in a 64-bit largesize AFTER the type, and Apple writes mdat that way in every iPhone HEIC. Heic::nextHeifBox treated any size below 2 as "extends to end of file", so on a file that puts mdat FIRST (which a phone does) the walk swallowed everything behind it: meta, iinf, iloc and iprp were never visited, no Exif item was found, and the file was declared unreadable while the platform decoder rendered it perfectly. Now only size == 0 means to EOF, which is what the spec says.
2. The property container was only walked when REPORTING: Heic::iprpBox descended into ipco inside `if (isDebug)`, so in normal use ispe and irot were stepped straight over. The debug OUTPUT is still conditional; the parse is not.
3. A HEIC with NO Exif is not a broken file. A converted image or a screenshot carries no Exif item, which is legal. ispe carries the pixel dimensions of every item and irot the rotation, so those are used: the largest ispe is taken (a HEIC holds several: master, thumbnail, sometimes a depth map), and a file with no usable Exif gets dimensions and orientation and NOTHING ELSE. The date, camera and lens stay empty rather than being invented from the file's timestamps (a made-up capture date would put it in the wrong year in every filter). A MALFORMED Exif takes the same path. Windows reaches the same conclusion through libheif (heif_image_handle_get_width / height, already display dimensions).

A HEIC with the wrong extension is still a HEIC: Metadata::parseJPG already sniffed for ftypheic and rerouted, but Thumb did not, so the two .JPG files ended up with the error icon. Thumb::loadThumb now sniffs the twelve-byte ISO base media header, ONCE, and only after the extension's own decode path has failed, so a folder of real JPEGs pays nothing.

Proved against the 20 real files, not reasoned about: the parser was linked into a standalone harness against the app's own object files and run over every path the catalog had flagged. All 20 parse (the iPhone files with full Exif, 4032x3024, "iPhone 11", orientation 6/3/1; the two Exif-less ones with dimensions from ispe). tst_heicboxes pins both box defects with fixtures built byte by byte.

##### 17.19.8.3 The Stub Rows Themselves Hid the Fix

Rescanning after the parser was corrected changed nothing, twice over, because a stub records the file's freshness STAMP like any other row, and THREE functions compare those stamps: staleOf (so the scan re-attempts the file instead of skipping it), fetchFresh (so the loader is not handed an empty row INSTEAD of reading the file), and commit itself, which skips a row whose stamps match, so a file just parsed successfully looked unchanged, the write was skipped, and the flag stayed set. The first two were fixed and the symptom did not move, because the third still swallowed the result.

The stamp answers "has the file changed", which is not the question for these rows: what changes for an unreadable row is WINNOW (a parser gains a format, and last month's unreadable file reads perfectly today). So an unreadable row is NEVER FRESH, anywhere; staleOf and fetchFresh must already agree, or an image can be both skipped by the loader and unindexed by the scanner (invisible, permanently), and commit is held to the same rule. The cost is one re-attempt per unreadable file per scan, a population that is by definition tiny.

Proved on a COPY OF THE REAL INDEX, after two rounds of "this should fix it" that did not: the scanner's path (staleOf, loadImageMetadata, commit) was linked into a standalone harness and run against a copy of the 38,904-row database over the exact 20 paths. staleOf returned all 20 as stale, all 20 parsed, and commit cleared every flag it wrote: the whole chain, end to end, before anyone rebuilt the app.

#### 17.19.9 The Catalog Scanner Had Never Once Run

Everything written about the scanner had been written about a feature that crashed on its first line. MW::startCatalogScan begins by telling the views a scan has started, and its very first such line is `if (catalogView) catalogView->setScanning(true);`. CatalogView \*catalogView was declared in mainwindow.h WITHOUT an initialiser, the one member of its group missing one (catalogDock, catalogScanner, catalogRootsDlg, filterPanel and their siblings all had `= nullptr`). MW::createCatalogDock returns early when G::useFilterPanel is set (the default) and its own comment says "catalogDock and catalogView stay NULL"; only catalogDock actually did. An uninitialised pointer passes `if (p)`, so the guard was decorative and the call jumped into whatever happened to be mapped (in the reported crash, libre2's \_\_TEXT segment, which is why it arrived as SIGBUS at a mapped address rather than the usual SIGSEGV near zero).

The crash is three lines before the scan is queued, so the invokeMethod that starts the work never ran. Scan Now had therefore never worked for anybody: a user with \~/Pictures nominated and its subfolders included had 1,140 images in 3 folders indexed, and every one came from the OPPORTUNISTIC capture in MW::folderChangeCompleted (folders they had browsed). The two symptoms, "Scan Now crashes" and "almost nothing is catalogued", were one defect.

Why it survived: CatalogScanner appeared in tests/ only inside a comment, MW::startCatalogScan had exactly one call site, and that call site was a button in a preferences sub-dialog, so no headless run ever reached it, and a person only reaches it by deciding to index a library. Everything about the scanner had been reasoned about carefully and none of it had been executed. The lesson is not about initialisers: a feature whose only entry point is a button nobody automated is a feature with no evidence behind it, however well its parts are understood.

The guard is the catalog_scan SMOKE TEST, which DRIVES the scanner rather than checking the pointer: WINNOW_SELFTEST_CATALOG_SCAN=&lt;folder> sets the scope to that one included folder and calls startCatalogScan, and the settle exit fails (code 6) unless CatalogScanner::finished arrived un-aborted with scanned > 0. It asserts `scanned`, NOT `indexed`: the scanner skips work already done, and the fixture folder has just been catalogued by the folder load in the same run, so a correct scan legitimately indexes nothing. Proved by reverting the one-line fix and watching it fail (SEGFAULT, 17 s), then restoring it.

## 18 Filters

### 18.1 The Filter Dock (Folders and Catalog)

One panel, two scopes. Filters searched the datamodel and the Catalog panel searched the index, and they looked alike because they are the SAME QUESTION asked of different sets. Keeping them apart produced exactly the problems that split predicts: two keyword lists that disagreed, two search boxes with different grammars under deliberately paired shortcuts, and a Catalog panel that could not reach most of what CatalogQuery supported while Filters had those categories with counts and checkboxes all along. The Filter dock (Views/filterpanel.h) makes the difference a SCOPE the panel is showing rather than two panels. In both scopes the panel FILTERS what is loaded; only the set underneath differs (a folder, or the whole catalog, [17.11.3 No Cap on the Library](#17113-no-cap-on-the-library)).

- It is the SAME DOCK OBJECT as the Filters dock, deliberately: same DockWidget, same "FilterDock" objectName, same tab text, "Filters". Everything that reaches for filterDock (the full-screen dock set, workspaces, solo mode, the view-mode enables, the collapsed-state restore, MW::showFilterDock) keeps working, and a saved WindowState still restores, which is also why winnowStateVersion did NOT need bumping.
- The code names match the UI: the panel was called Find while it was being built (FindPanel, G::useFindDock), because it was conceived as a search surface over the catalog. What shipped is a FILTER with a scope, so everything is FilterPanel / Views/filterpanel.\* / G::useFilterPanel / "the Filter dock".
- The category tree IS the Filters widget itself, re-parented into the panel, not a copy: both scopes render the same categories, checkboxes, include / exclude gestures and colours. A second category renderer is precisely what the two panels had, and it is what drifted.
- Which scope is showing is said in the DOCK TITLE: "Filters (Folders)" or "Filters (Library)", written by MW::setScope (the one place G::scope changes, which re-asserts its state even when nothing changed). The panel used to say it in the search box's placeholder, which vanished the moment anything was typed. The TAB text stays "Filters" in both scopes: a tab that changes width moves every tab beside it.
- G::useFilterPanel is an ESCAPE HATCH, not a shelved feature: false rebuilds both original panels exactly as they were ([17.2.1 The Legacy Catalog Dock](#1721-the-legacy-catalog-dock)). It is read at dock-creation time, so changing it takes a restart. Under it catalogDock and catalogView stay null (both initialised to nullptr in the header, because createDocks and placeDocksAddedSince reach for them before that is decided; see [17.19.9 The Catalog Scanner Had Never Once Run](#17199-the-catalog-scanner-had-never-once-run)).

#### 18.1.1 The Scope Is Not Set From the Panel

The Folders | Catalog buttons at the top and the "84,102 images catalogued ... Manage..." row at the bottom were both REMOVED. Neither was a search control: choosing what to browse is the Source panel's toggle and File > Open Library (Shift+O, MW::showCatalogDock), and choosing which folders are indexed is configuration (File > Manage Catalog..., MW::manageCatalogRoots). In the panel they were findable only by someone who had already opened it.

- Open Library GREYS OUT WITH ITS REASON (tooltip) when the index will not open; Manage Catalog... stays enabled, because editing the roots and rescanning is what a user would do about it. MW::updateLibraryTree sets both, from the same places that refresh the Library tree, so the menu item and the tree cannot disagree.
- Asking for an EMPTY catalog opens the place it is filled. Empty is not unavailable and must not be greyed: every user door (File > Open Library / Shift+O, the Library toggle) calls MW::catalogEmptyOpenManage first, and when the index is open and holds nothing it opens Manage Catalog instead of switching scope. No popup explains the window that appears: Manage Catalog already states the case ("Catalog: 0 images in 0 folders" and what to do). This does not touch the FIRST-RUN PROMPT, which is asked when the user has NOT asked for the catalog.
- The catalog is FILTERED, NOT SEARCHED INTO. The panel's old footer (a line of prose over Load and Add buttons) is gone with the paradigm it belonged to: there is no found SET to load. Functionality over what is loaded (Collections, Queries) goes in the main menu and the context menus; the filter panel does not grow buttons.
- Nothing to report is nothing shown: one hidden label under the tree (FilterPanel::updateStatus) covers the case the panel genuinely cannot answer (the index will not open, or there is nothing in it), and hides again the moment that stops being true. FilterPanel::refresh calls updateStatus directly when the catalog is unavailable, because runSearch returns early then. A running scan is NOT reported here; it has its own progress row.

#### 18.1.2 Search Is a Filter Category

The query is typed into the editable searchTrue tree item, where it sits among the other things that narrow the view, with its counts in the same two columns and its "No match" row beside it. A QLineEdit above the tree, briefly, was wrong three ways: it made the query look like a different kind of thing from the ticks an inch below, it cost the Search category its two rows, and it put a second ? in the dock. F2 opens the row in whichever scope is current (Filters::editSearchText expands the category, scrolls to it and opens the editor). The grammar is [18.3 Searching Folders and Catalog (One Grammar)](#183-searching-folders-and-catalog-one-grammar) and [17.6 Queries and the Query Builder](#176-queries-and-the-query-builder).

RETURN RUNS THE QUERY; TYPING DOES NOT, which the tree item gives for nothing: a QTreeWidget editor writes on Return or on losing focus, never per keystroke, so there is no debounce and no committed-versus-typed bookkeeping. That matters at library size: Catalog scope once searched on a 250 ms debounce, where a single letter is a PREFIX to FTS5 ("a" compiles to "a"\*), so it matched most of the index and the result was then auto-loaded; one letter beachballed the application. Deleting the text and pressing Return removes the query; the row goes back to "Enter search query", which is also what the predicate reads as no search (Filters::ignoreSearchStrings).

An edit to the Search row NARROWS THE PROXY in both scopes (Filters::dataChanged emits searchStringChange, then filterChange: the same predicate over the same rows, and no reload). The index is asked only to LOAD the scope, on entry. The one case that still reloads is a CAPPED scope (G::maxSearchResults > 0: the model holds only the newest N rows, so the proxy cannot answer for the rest, and FilterPanel::searchTextChanged runs the query); at the default of 0 there is no cap and no reload.

The Search row has its own CONTEXT MENU, because the query is typed, can outgrow its row, and is worth keeping. Right-clicking "Enter search query" prepends Build query..., Save search as Query... and a Load query submenu (Filters::showSearchQueryMenu; see the Query Builder), greying an item with its reason IN the item rather than opening a dialog that says there is nothing to do. The panel's ordinary filter actions stay on the menu beneath a separator: taking them away on the one row a user is most likely to right-click would make the menu unpredictable.

- The menu could not appear at all until the policy changed, and the same was quietly true of the Include / Exclude / Clear menu beside it. The tree was Qt::ActionsContextMenu, which QWidget::event handles ITSELF, so contextMenuEvent was never called (with that policy, a contextMenuEvent override is dead code). The policy is Qt::DefaultContextMenu now (MW::createFilterViewContextMenu), and Filters::addFilterActions appends the same actions, under a separator, to every menu the class builds.
- The ? in the Filters title bar is where the grammar is written down: the query syntax is a set of sections in :/Docs/filtershelp.html (Filters::howThisWorks, 720x640), not a second help window behind a second ?. The tooltips carry the short form.

#### 18.1.3 Leaving and Entering a Scope

- LEAVING the Library CARRIES THE QUERY back to Folders: what was asked of everything can then be narrowed to what is in front of you. It has to be carried deliberately: BuildFilters::reset clears that row with every other item (Filters::clearAll -> setSearchNewFolder), so the rebuildFolderCategoriesRequested lambda in MW::createFilterDock reads the query before the reset and writes it back after with Filters::setSearchText.
- Going the other way it does NOT carry, and the row says so rather than showing text that is no longer filtering: entering the Library LOADS it, and a load resets the filters like any folder change.
- Every scope switch clears the CHECKS, because the two scopes are different VOCABULARIES: a folder offers the three camera models in it, the library forty, and re-applying checks that merely share a name would silently build a different query. Returning to Folders asks MW to rebuild the tree from the datamodel (buildFilters->reset() then build()), since only MW knows whether the model is ready.
- runSearch takes a FORCE: it loads only when the result set CHANGED, right for a re-run and wrong for a scope ENTRY (coming back, the model holds a folder while results still names last time's catalog rows, so the guard would compare equal and load nothing). applyScope forces it.

### 18.2 Categories

#### 18.2.1 The Catalog's Categories Come From One SQL Map

Where categories are read from the index (a capped scope, the legacy panel, Filters::categorySource), Catalog::categorySql keys the expression for a category on the DATAMODEL COLUMN the Filters panel maps that category to, and both categoryItems() and search() use it, so a value the user checks cannot mean something different from the value offered. The strings must match what DataModel writes into the same column, because the user sees one list and does not know which scope produced it:

- Type is the suffix UPPER-cased; Year is "yyyy"; Day is the unpadded day of the month ("1".."31"; the SQL casts strftime('%d') through INTEGER to drop the zero); Pick is "Picked" / "Unpicked"; Rating is the digit as text; focal length carries no trailing ".0" (or "400" and "400.0" would look like two lenses); Folders is the folder PATH ([17.3.5 A Folder's Identity Is Its Path](#1735-a-folders-identity-is-its-path)).
- tst_catalog::categoryItemsMatchWhatTheDatamodelWrites pins every one.

In the Library scope itself the panel shows the DATAMODEL's categories with live counts, because the whole catalog is loaded. Counts from catalog-sourced categories are library TOTALS: per-item counts under a live query would be one GROUP BY per category over a quarter of a million rows on every run.

A category the index cannot answer is HIDDEN, not shown empty: Duplicates compares what is loaded, and the Search category is the panel's own row. categoryItems() returns nothing for those columns: an empty category reads as "you have no camera models", which would be a lie.

#### 18.2.2 Capture Times Are the Camera's Wall Clock, Not an Instant

Schema 16, 2026-09-26. EXIF DateTimeOriginal carries no timezone: 21:40 in the file is 21:40, and that is the day the user expects it filed under. The datamodel has always worked on those fields (QDateTime::fromString gives a local time with exactly them). The catalog did not: commit bound captured.toSecsSinceEpoch() (the fields converted to an instant with the INDEXING Mac's zone) and categorySql read it back with strftime(..., 'unixepoch'), which is UTC. So in the Library an evening photo west of Greenwich was filed under the NEXT day (after 17:00 at UTC-7), while the same folder browsed from disk filed it correctly.

- Adding 'localtime' to the SQL was rejected: it converts with the zone at QUERY time, so a laptop set to another zone while travelling would split the two scopes again.
- Instead image.captured stores the wall-clock fields encoded as if UTC: Catalog::wallClockSecs(dt) = QDateTime(dt.date(), dt.time(), UTC).toSecsSinceEpoch(), and Catalog::fromWallClockSecs reverses it to a LOCAL QDateTime with the same fields (what a file read yields), so a catalog row and its file compare equal. Plain 'unixepoch' then gives the recorded Year / Month / Day on any Mac in any zone.
- EVERY read, write and bind of captured goes through the pair: commit, the row read-back, CatalogQuery::from / to in buildQueryLocked, mostRecentCaptureDate. ORDER BY captured is unaffected except for rows inside a DST fall-back hour.
- CacheDb::migrate's version &lt; 16 block converts existing rows in one UPDATE: strftime('%s', captured, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') is the local wall clock read as UTC, using this Mac's zone and each row's own date's DST rules (the conversion Qt made when the row was indexed), so it is exact wherever the catalog was built in the zone it is opened in. It is a DATA conversion, and not idempotent (rewind fixtures in tst_catalog re-run it harmlessly, since none asserts on captured). Pinned by tst_catalog::migrationStoresCaptureAsTheWallClock (a 23:30 shot, run under TZ=America/Vancouver, Pacific/Auckland and UTC).
- OPEN: video creation dates (QuickTime) ARE true UTC by specification, unlike EXIF; MOV::createDate has not been checked for whether it converts, so a clip may file under a different day from stills shot beside it, in both scopes alike.

#### 18.2.3 Every Category Adds Up, and the Shortfall Is a Blank Row

If 43,064 images are indexed and 3,000 carry a rating, the Ratings category lists the rated values and then a BLANK one counting 40,064, not counts that quietly fall short with nothing to explain the gap. Checking the blank row means "the ones with nothing here", and Opt+clicking it excludes them. BuildFilters has always counted the empty string like any other key in a folder; the catalog side matches:

- categorySql wraps every expression in IFNULL(..., '') so a NULL title or an image with no capture date groups into the blank instead of vanishing.
- search() binds category values through text(), so a null QString does not go to SQLite as NULL ("NULL IN (NULL)" is NULL, and the blank row would select nothing).
- A category whose ONLY value is blank is still hidden: offering "" as the sole thing to check would filter to everything.
- KEYWORDS are the exception and get no blank row in either scope: an image carries many keywords, so the counts overlap and cannot sum to the total however they are presented. tst_catalog::blankCategoryItemAccountsForEveryImage pins the rest.

#### 18.2.4 Nested Categories: Keywords (and Folders)

Keywords are a nested category, because a keyword's identity is its full path ([16.2 Keyword Identity Is the Full Path](#162-keyword-identity-is-the-full-path)).
