Filters::addKeywordItems builds the tree from a map keyed on paths; each item is LABELLED with its leaf and carries the full path as its filter value in data(1, Qt::EditRole), with the path in its tooltip, so the tree stays readable at depth while what is filtered is unambiguous. NO SUMMING is needed: every image is linked to every ANCESTOR PREFIX of its keywords, so BuildFilters::countKeywords has already produced a count for a branch as well as a leaf. (Folders are nested the other way: counted per folder and rolled up on receipt.)

- One level was an assumption written into a dozen loops, all spelled "for i &lt; category->childCount()". On a tree each of those sees the roots and misses the leaves, silently. Filters::itemsInCategory is the single definition of "every filterable item beneath a category", and the count updaters, fillQuery and the catalog count loop all go through it. Filters::itemMapKey is the matching definition of what an itemMap is keyed on (the label everywhere, the path for keywords). SortFilter::compileFilters needed no change: it already walked with a QTreeWidgetItemIterator and read data(1).
- Filters::save / restore are keyed on {TOP-LEVEL CATEGORY, FILTER VALUE}, not {parent text, item label}. Those were the same thing while every category was one level deep. With Keywords nested, an item's parent is another KEYWORD, so a saved state recorded "Heron" under "Bird" and restore(), which looks under the category name, matched nothing and restored nothing, SILENTLY: the user's filter quietly came back empty after a folder change. Keying on the value also distinguishes the two Vancouvers. tests/unit/tst_filters.cpp pins it, and each of its cases was confirmed to FAIL against the old key before the new one was written.
- Category identity is Filters::CategoryNameRole, set once by createFilter, not the header's display text (which can carry a count): [16.8.1 Marking Unfiled Keywords in Filters](#1681-marking-unfiled-keywords-in-filters).

### 18.3 Searching Folders and Catalog (One Grammar)

The Search row is now parsed by the query grammar (Utilities/queryexpr.h), which reads everything described here the same way and adds field rules and true nested NOT ([17.6 Queries and the Query Builder](#176-queries-and-the-query-builder)). Utilities/searchterms.h remains the catalog's FTS compilation. What follows is the history of the shared grammar, and still describes plain words exactly.

Two search scopes used to disagree. The Folders scope searched the DATAMODEL with QString::contains; the Catalog scope searched the INDEX with FTS5. One box, one key (F2) and one pair of labels promised the same words meant the same thing, and they did not: "heron OR eagle" found images in one and nothing in the other, because to contains() it was a single literal string containing the word OR. Utilities/searchterms.h parses the text ONCE and each engine compiles the result its own way, so a term type added there reaches both at once.

#### 18.3.1 The Grammar

What a search box is expected to do: bare words AND-ed, OR between alternatives, (brackets) to group, quoted phrases, and -term or NOT term to exclude. AND is accepted and ignored. OR and NOT are recognised in UPPER CASE only, so a caption reading "black or white" is searched for as written. The user-facing statement is the query sections of :/Docs/filtershelp.html, behind the ? in the Filters title bar.

- The parse is an EXPRESSION TREE (SearchTerms::Node: a Term, an All or an Any), where it used to be a flat list of groups. That flat list is why the old precedence was odd: OR bound to the term BEFORE it, so "heron OR eagle nanaimo" meant (heron OR eagle) AND nanaimo. With brackets, AND binds tighter than OR as in every other search box, and the old meaning is spelled with the brackets it needs. This CHANGED what an existing un-bracketed query mixing the two operators finds; tst_searchterms::andBindsTighterThanOr pins the new reading with the old one written out beside it.
- A bracket is syntax wherever it is unquoted, mid-word included, so the tokenizer emits ( and ) as their own tokens, and a filename that really contains one is searched for by quoting it ("DSC(2)"). Quoting is the one general escape hatch: the tokenizer records WHETHER a token was quoted, so "OR" between quotes is the word and "(" between quotes is the character.
- UNBALANCED is TOLERATED, not rejected: a missing ')' closes at the end of the text, a stray one is dropped, because the box is read while it is being typed. The parser carries a bracket DEPTH for that: at depth 0 a ')' has no group to end, and without the depth ")heron" would close a group never opened and silently discard the rest of the query.
- A quote never survives into a term: the tokenizer treats every one as a phrase delimiter, opening or closing, and flushes whatever was accumulating. Without the closing flush '""' would merge the words either side of it; without the opening one 'say"what more"' would glue 'say' onto the phrase. The quote-doubling in the FTS compilation is therefore defensive, and tst_searchterms pins that.
- Whitespace-only text parses to no terms, which would match every row and light the Search filter up for a query that asked for nothing, so it is treated as no search.

#### 18.3.2 Negation

In the FTS compilation, negation is LIFTED out of the expression at parse time, wherever it was written: "-heron", "(a OR -heron)" and "-(heron OR eagle)" all mean "and not that", every negated node going into SearchTerms::negatives. That is deliberate: FTS5 has no "everything" token for a NOT to subtract from, so the index MUST apply negatives as a separate NOT EXISTS against image_fts (which works whether or not there is anything positive; SearchTerms::hasPositive is how Catalog::search knows), and several negatives are OR-ed into that one subquery. The query evaluator used for the loaded model honours nesting; the FTS compilation is used only by a CAPPED catalog search.

#### 18.3.3 What Each Engine Matches

- The datamodel matches a SUBSTRING and the index a PREFIX, because that is what each engine is good at: contains() over loaded rows is cheap, while an infix search over a quarter of a million FTS rows cannot use the index. "eron" finds Heron in a loaded set and not in a capped catalog search.
- The two surfaces do not cover the same FIELDS. searchText is NOT a catalog column: it is REBUILT at load time (IndexMetadata::fill copies the CatalogRow into an ImageMetadata, and DataModel::addMetadataForItem composes the string, seeded with the full path by addFileDataForRow, then label, dimensions, make, model, lens, keywords, keywordPaths, shootingInfo, title, creator, copyright, email and url). image_fts holds strictly less: keywords, title, creator, copyright, gear (make + model + lens) and filename. So the datamodel string is a SUPERSET: the proxy cannot find less than the index would have. It finds MORE, and the extra worth knowing is the PATH: a word in a user name or a drive name is in every image's text. The filters help page says so.
- That makes addMetadataForItem LOAD-BEARING for catalog rows: a future path that filled rows from the index without it would leave searchText empty, and those rows would silently match nothing.
- A photographer's own name is stamped by the camera into nearly everything they have ever shot (creator and copyright), so their own name is the least selective word they can type ([18.11.1 Two Names OR-ed: One Return Beachballed the App](#18111-two-names-or-ed-one-return-beachballed-the-app)).

### 18.4 A Filter Is a Filter in Either Scope

The query (or the folder) defines the SET; the Filters tree narrows it. A category check behaves identically in Folders and Catalog scope: the proxy is re-filtered, every item stays in the tree, and the category head turns yellow with the counts moving.

- FilterPanel::applyScope keeps the DataModel's categories (showAllCategories); it does not query the index for them.
- MW::filterChange filters the proxy in both scopes.
- FilterPanel::currentQuery carries the search TEXT only. fillQuery's checked items are a filter over what is loaded; putting them in the query as well would narrow the SET by the same values, filtering twice and rebuilding the tree from the remainder.

What stays scope-specific, deliberately: typing in the search box re-queries the index and reloads, because that is what changes the set. The categories then rebuild from the new set, which is correct for a search and would be wrong for a filter.

History: a catalog scope used to load a 5,000-row slice of the library, so the loaded rows could not answer for the library. FilterPanel::applyScope filled the tree from SQL aggregates over the whole index (Filters::loadCatalogCategories) and hid the DataModel's own categories, MW::filterChange declined to run the proxy in that scope, and a checked item went into the CatalogQuery, so checking it re-ran the search, reloaded the model and rebuilt the tree from the survivors: filtering on one day left only that day in the tree. With the whole catalog loaded, the DataModel's categories ARE the library's, with live counts BuildFilters already maintains. Filters::loadCatalogCategories and isAnyCatalogFilter remain for the separate Catalog panel (not built under G::useFilterPanel).

### 18.5 Special Filter Categories

How an ordinary category is declared is in [4.4.4.1 Adding a Filter Category](#4441-adding-a-filter-category). These three differ from "the column's text is the item".

#### 18.5.1 Availability as a Filter (One Spelling, Two Places)

G::AvailabilityColumn carries Present / Offline / Missing per row (see [17.8 Availability (Offline Is Not Missing)](#178-availability-offline-is-not-missing)). The badge answers "why can I not open THIS one"; the category answers "show me everything that is offline".

- It is counted from the DataModel like every other category, not from the catalog. Offline is computed at call time and never stored, so the index has no column to answer it from. It is one FilterCat slot, one BuildFilters::sinks() entry and one snapshot column.
- The column holds a CODE (0, 1, 2) and the category shows a WORD. The snapshot translates code to label when it is taken (FilterCat::Availability is the label), and Filters::filterValueFor puts the code back on the item's compare value, because SortFilter::compileFilters reads data(1, EditRole) and FilterPredicate compares it with the model's Qt::EditRole value; an item carrying "Offline" would never match a cell holding 1. Catalog::availabilityLabel and availabilityCode are that mapping, stated once; tst_catalog::availabilityLabelAndCodeAreOneSpelling holds them to exact inverses, including that anything unrecognised is Present (the same answer an unset cell gives).
- The category hides itself while every row is Present (every folder scope and most catalog scopes): offering "Present" alone would filter to everything. The test is "any value that is not Present" rather than "more than one item", because a scope in which EVERY row is offline is exactly the case worth showing.
- It is refreshed where the values come into existence: at the end of the availability pass, which runs after the fill. No user edit, folder change or metadata arrival would ever tell the tree.
- It adds the items DIRECTLY, not through BuildFilters::updateCategory. That path suspends proxy filtering and leaves MW::filterChange to lift it, and filterChange bumps dm->instance, saves and restores the selection and re-sorts the model, none of which may happen to a scope that has just finished loading. No counting pass is needed either: nothing is filtered yet, so both count columns hold the same number, which the availability pass has just counted. A new item is Unchecked and contributes nothing to the compiled predicate, which is what makes adding it here safe without recompiling.
- The table column shows the word through AvailabilityItemDelegate, and nothing for Present.

#### 18.5.2 GPS as a Filter (a Derived Column)

The question is "which of these have coordinates", not "which coordinate". G::GPSCoordColumn holds a DMS string per row, so a category built on it would offer one item per distinct location. The GPS category offers True and False.

- G::HasGPSColumn (Main/global.h; rowfields.h as WF_DERIVED) is computed by RowStore from the interned GPSCoord string: "True" when it is non-empty after trimming, else "False". It shares GPSCoord's field bit (RowStore::fieldBit), so it is UNSET (not "False") until the coordinate has been written, it moves the snapshot's watched-change tracking whenever the coordinate does, and it costs a row nothing. RowStore::setValue refuses a direct write to it.
- It is TEXT rather than bool so the item label and the value it matches are the same string: the snapshot counts the column's own string and Filters::filterValueFor needs no exception.
- Wiring, one row each: FilterCat::Gps in filtersnapshot.h, its column in BuildFilters::makeSnapshot, one BuildFilters::sinks() entry, and Filters::gps / catGps ("GPS") in the usual create / background / takeChildren / collapse lists. It sits after Creators. The catalog-query path (Filters::loadCatalogCategories / fillQuery) is not extended: it has no production caller.
- Pinned by tst_imagerow::hasGpsIsDerivedFromTheCoordinate.

The coordinate itself: GPS::decode reads the GPS IFD's rationals at their tag offsets PLUS the TIFF header's file position, which the caller passes. Jpeg::parse, Jpeg2 and Png passed a fixed 12 until 2026-10-02 (right only when Exif is the first segment after SOI), while every other Exif value in those parsers used startOffset. A JPEG with a JFIF APP0 before its Exif (an exported or converted iPhone image) decoded garbage: 48°28'7.72" N 123°22'13.88" W became 0°5'0.000" N 47°0'48.545" W. All three now pass startOffset. Index schema 19 is the data repair: it zeroes srcmtime on every JPEG/PNG row holding a coordinate, so Catalog::staleOf calls it stale and the next scan or folder load re-reads it (the file's own stamp never changed, so nothing else would).

#### 18.5.3 Filter On... (Session Categories From Any Column)

Right-click anywhere in the Filters panel > Filter on... lists every DataModel column that has no category (Aspect Ratio, Aperture, Make, Shutter, Orientation ...) and appends the chosen one to the BOTTOM of the tree. It is built from the data like any other category, filters like any other (include, Opt+click exclude, Shift-click ranges, save/restore across a folder change), and lasts until Winnow quits. Right-click the category (header or item) > Remove "X" category takes it out and clears any filter it applied. Built; untested in-app.

Who does what: Filters owns the menu item (Filters::filterOnAction, added by addFilterActions so it is on every menu) and only ASKS: filterOnRequested -> MW::filterOnColumn (Main/sortandfilter.cpp), which knows the model's columns, shows the picker, then calls Filters::addSessionCategory and BuildFilters::updateSessionCategory to fill it. The header carries G::ColumnRole, CategoryNameRole (the header name, which save()/restore() key on) and Filters::SessionRole.

Which columns are offered: every column whose value is text or a number and that is not already a category, ordinary columns first, then the geek columns marked "(diagnostic)". Left out, and only these: column 0 (the icon), the LIST columns (Keywords, KeywordPaths, All Keywords, Folder Paths All; a row carries several values and a one-value-per-row category cannot count them) and the ICC profile bytes.

- A header name that collides with a category's gets " column" appended (the search-text column is also called "Search"), because save()/restore() key on the name.
- A column with more than 1,000 distinct values (file name, size, created) asks first: its category would list about one item per image.
- The first version also hid geek columns, off-store columns and a hand-picked "unique per image" list. The user asked why the list was so short; those exclusions were a judgement the user should make.

Counting: BuildFilters' fixed slots (FilterCat::Slot) cannot name a column chosen at run time, so makeSnapshot captures the session categories on the GUI thread into FilterSnapshot::extraColumns / extraItems and each row's values into FilterSnapshotRow::extra; sinks(snap) appends them as slots FilterCat::SlotCount + i, and countSlot reads extra past the fixed slots. The worker never touches Filters::sessionCats, which the GUI thread changes. A change to the set changes the watched cells, which RowStore reports as structural, so the value table is rebuilt (cachedExtraColumns says the same explicitly).

- Columns RowStore does not hold (the scratch columns: cache state, decoder status, preview offsets) cannot be read inside RowStore::forEachRow, and RowStore cannot say when they change. makeSnapshot reads them through DataModel::data after the store pass, and their presence forces a full value-table rebuild on every snapshot.
- Numbers sort as numbers: a value that parses as a non-negative number is left-padded on its INTEGER PART to ten, so "1.25" sorts before "1.5" and "9" before "10". Padding the whole string, as ISO and focal length do, would put "1.5" before "1.25".
- Matching is text. The column may hold a double or an int while the item holds the padded string, and a Qt 6 QVariant compare of the two is not one to rely on. SortFilter::compileFilters sets FilterCategory::compareAsText from SessionRole, and FilterPredicate::accepts compares both sides as trimmed text. Pinned by tst_filterpredicate::sessionCategoryComparesAsPaddedText.

Adding does not rebuild. A full build clears every check in the panel, so a new category is filled by BuildFilters::updateSessionCategory: updateCategory(SessionEdit) with runSync, then it lifts the proxy suspension itself (nothing in a new category is checked, so no filterChange follows: the MW::togglePick pattern). When the filters are not built, or are building, it does nothing and the build in hand fills it through sinks().

Removed categories are retired, not deleted. FilterOps carry raw QTreeWidgetItem pointers and a BuildFilters run in flight may hold some naming the category; an op on a detached item is harmless, one on a freed item is a crash. Filters::removeSessionCategory takes the item out of the tree into retiredSessionCats, which lives as long as the panel. The remove item is disabled, with the reason, while the filters are building.

Scope and persistence:

- Filter on... is disabled ("Filter on... - Folders scope only") only when the tree is filled from the index (categoriesFrom != FromDatamodel, i.e. Filters::loadCatalogCategories, which only the separate Catalog panel uses). The Filters panel fills from the DataModel in both scopes, where it is enabled.
- Folder changes keep the headers and refill the items (removeChildrenDynamicFilters clears only children).
- persistableState skips their checks, so nothing written to settings names a category the next launch will not have.

### 18.6 Grouped Filter Categories (and the Lit Title)

Groups are a VIEW of the same categories (2026-09-30). The groups button in the Filters title bar (images/icon16/groups.png, beside expand / collapse) and "Group categories" on the panel's right-click menu toggle filterGroupsAction; MW::setFilterGroups calls Filters::setGrouped, syncs the button (BarBtn::setActive) and saves settings key isGroupedFilters (default off). Grouped, the top level is Adhoc search, then six group headers:

```
Folders and files   Folders, Collections, Queries, File types
Time                Years, Months, Days
Selection           Picks, Ratings, Color classes
Camera              Camera models, Lenses, Focal lengths, ISO
Metadata            Titles, Creators, GPS, Keywords
Status              Availability, Duplicates found
```

- FLAT USES THE SAME ORDER: Filters::createGroups declares the groups and their members once, and categoryOrder() is those member lists concatenated, so the two arrangements cannot drift. Session categories ("Filter on...") stay top-level at the bottom in both.
- The Search category's text is "Adhoc search" (Filters::catSearchLabel); catSearch stays "Search" as the key, and the Search header has no CategoryNameRole, so saved and persisted filter state is unchanged.
- The items are MOVED, not rebuilt: setGrouped takes every top-level item except Search and re-inserts it flat or under its group item, so checks, counts, values and roles travel with it and nothing refilters (the compiled predicate never depended on where a category sits). What does NOT survive a take / insert is the view's state (expansion, hidden rows, including what "Show unfiled only" hides), so it is recorded first and put back. Groups open the first time they appear. A group whose every category is hidden (the Library scope hides several) is hidden too (updateGroupVisibility).

Categories are no longer always top-level, and that was the real work: about thirty sites read "parent() == nullptr" as "is a category", "has a parent" as "is a filter item", or walked to the root to find an item's category, including SortFilter::compileFilters (which would have compiled a grouped category header as a filter item) and save() / restore() (which would have keyed a keyword on "Metadata"). They all ask Filters::isCategoryHeader (structural: top-level, or directly under a group), isGroupHeader (GroupRole present), isFilterItem, or categoryOf. setRowHidden(indexOfTopLevelItem(...)) became item->setHidden. compileFilters skips group rows.

- GroupRole is Qt::UserRole + 100 ON PURPOSE: Filters' roles share Qt::UserRole + n with G::UserRoles, and the next free number in sequence (+7) is G::ColumnRole, which every category carries. The first cut made every category read as a group, and tst_filters caught it.

#### 18.6.1 Expansion and the Arrows

Solo mode applies at BOTH levels (revised 2026-09-30 at the user's request): opening a group collapses the other groups, and opening a category collapses the other categories wherever they are (Filters::collapseCategories: collapseAll, then re-open the groups that were open) without touching the groups. Closing a group closes only that one; Cmd/Ctrl opts out of solo at either level; BuildFilters::reset uses collapseCategories for the same reason, or every folder load would close the groups. The header arrows (icons) follow itemExpanded / itemCollapsed and syncHeaderIcons, so expand-all or collapse-all no longer leaves stale arrows.

- A nested category would draw the stylesheet's branch arrow beside its own icon, so Filters::drawBranches draws nothing for a header row. NOT QTreeWidgetItem::DontShowIndicator: the first cut used it, and it makes QTreeModel::hasChildren return FALSE, so the view refused to expand any header. A header press is also not passed to the base class: nested, its branch area is the expand control, and the base press would toggle it straight back.
- First-level arrows sit UNDER the header's. A header's arrow is its icon, at the start of its cell, while an item's arrow is the branch glyph centred in the last indent slot, a few pixels left, so first-level arrows did not line up with the header arrows above them. drawBranches translates the glyph so its centre is the header icon's centre (style SE_ItemViewItemDecoration on the header's visualRect); deeper levels keep Qt's placement. (The member Filters::indentation shadows QTreeView::indentation(): same value.)
- The shift broke the click, fixed 2026-10-12: Qt's expand hit-test is the UNSHIFTED slot, so the right half of the drawn arrow lay in the item's cell and a click there toggled the CHECKBOX instead of expanding. Now: (1) Filters::branchShift computes the shift once for both drawing and hit-testing; (2) Filters::expanderHitRect is the drawn arrow's slot, padded 3 px left and the full row height but CUT OFF before the checkbox, and mousePressEvent tests it FIRST (a hit toggles expansion and swallows the release, so itemClickedSignal cannot toggle the box; a fast second click arrives as a double-click, and mouseDoubleClickEvent treats it as one more arrow click); (3) FiltersDelegate moves every checkable item right by Filters::checkGap (8 px), and paint, editorEvent (the box's own click test) and updateEditorGeometry (the Search row's editor) all take the same shifted rect, or the box drawn and the box clicked would part; (4) the viewport tracks the mouse and shows a POINTING HAND over an arrow.

#### 18.6.2 The Lit Title

A group header is drawn in the filtering yellow while any category in it is filtering, so a closed group still says where the filter is. Branch items are lit the same way: a collection folder, folder or keyword with a checked item anywhere beneath it is drawn in the filtering yellow (Filters::DescendantFilteringRole, set by setEachCatTextColor and read by applyItemStyle, where the unfiled and excluded colours still win), so a collapsed branch says where its filter is.

The Filters TITLE BAR (DockTitleBar::setTitleColor) turns the same yellow whenever ANY visible category header is lit: Filters::notifyFilteringState emits filteringChanged only when that answer changes, from setEachCatTextColor, clearAll, uncheckAllFilters, restore and a Search text edit. It follows the headers' rule rather than isAnyFilter's: a category of one item does not light its header, so it does not light the title either.

Pinned by tst_filters::flatOrderIsTheGroupOrder, groupsHoldTheirCategories, checksSurviveRegroupingAndSaveRestore (a grouped persistableState equals the flat one; view state survives) and filteringLightsTheGroupAndSignals.

### 18.7 Filter History (Back and Forward)

Back and forward through filter states (2026-10-06), like a browser's history. Previous re-applies the filter state before the one showing, Next the one after it. Each is greyed while there is nowhere to go, and its tooltip says how many states lie that way.

- What is recorded: MW::filterChange calls MW::recordFilterHistory just after its early-return gate, so every filter change actually applied is a candidate. The state is Filters::persistableState (checked items as {category, value, include / exclude}, the search text and the keyword any / all mode), the same map the Library and Folders restores save. It is appended only if it differs from the entry showing, so a refilter after a rating edit, a restore that lands on the same checks, or the step itself records nothing. A new state after a Back drops the forward entries. Capped at 100.
- The first entry is "NOTHING FILTERED": by the time filterChange runs the tree already holds the new checks, so the state before the first change cannot be read. After MW::reset it can only have been unfiltered, so the first record pushes an empty state ahead of the new one.
- Stepping: MW::stepFilterHistory applies an entry through the path a folder change's restore uses (Filters::setStateToRestore, Filters::restore(keepMissing false), one filterChange). filterHistoryStepping stops that filterChange (and the nested one restore triggers when the search text changes) from recording. A step is REFUSED, with a popup, while a load runs or a restore is pending (restoreFiltersPending): filterChange would apply nothing, and setStateToRestore would overwrite the states the pending restore is waiting for.
- Scope of a history: MW::reset clears it, so it covers one loaded set (a folder, a recursive tree, the Library): another set's checks mostly name values not in this one. Session categories (Filter on..., Map pin) are not in persistableState, so changing only one of them records nothing, and a step leaves them as they are.

The same controls under every Browse panel (2026-10-13). A PanelButtonBar ([11.36.2 The Copy / Paste Button Row](#11362-the-copy--paste-button-row)) is pinned to the bottom of the Filters, Bookmarks, Collections and Queries panels: Previous, Clear filters, Next. Those four are one tab group in the left area, and Qt has nowhere to put a widget UNDER a QDockWidget tab group, so each panel carries its own copy and whichever tab is raised shows the row in the same place.

- MW::createFilterNavBars builds them, called from the end of createFilterActions (createDocks runs before createActions, and the Clear button follows clearAllFiltersAction via PanelButtonBar::MakeButton). The row goes in each dock's FrameLineBox (DockWidget::widget()), after the content, so a dock whose content is a bare view needs no wrapper.
- Previous / Next call filterHistoryBack / filterHistoryForward; syncFilterHistoryButtons sets the enabled state and tooltips of every copy (MW::filterNavBackBtns / filterNavForwardBtns). They REPLACED the Filters title bar's own arrows, so the filter history has one control, reachable from every panel in the group. The arrows are drawn as a vector at 22 px (filterNavArrowIcon in Main/sortandfilter.cpp) from the old bitmap's outline.
- To give another panel in the group the row, add its dock to the list in createFilterNavBars.

### 18.8 Rebuild Filters Is an Escape Hatch

In the Filter menu only (2026-10-13). The Filters title bar had a refresh button ("Update filters") and the Filter menu a "Force update" item, both calling MW::updateAllFilters, which called BuildFilters::build(), and build() returns at once when the filters are already built, which they always are by the time anyone can click. Both did nothing. Nothing needs them either: every edit updates its own category (updateCategory for picks, ratings, labels, compare, keywords, title / creator; recount for geotags and file operations; updateSessionCategory for Filter on...).

The title-bar button is gone; the menu item is Filter > Rebuild filters and does a REAL rebuild: BuildFilters::rebuild() (reset + build) through the path applyModelChange uses (Filters::save, restoreFiltersPending and restoreKeepsMissing set, then MW::restoreFiltersAfterFolderChange restores the checks on finishedBuildFilters and re-runs filterChange). keepMissing because the set is the same one, so a checked value with no images left stays checked (showing nothing) rather than silently widening the view. Refused with a popup while a load runs or a build is already in progress. If the user ever NEEDS it, a category's incremental update is missing somewhere, and that is the bug to fix.

### 18.9 Filter Exclusion (Include This, Not That)

Subtracting is a question a filter has to be able to ask: "everything under Location except the American branch", "every camera but the phone", "this folder minus its exports". Exclusion was first built to take apart a keyword name used under two parents, when keywords were flat; path identity has since made the two Vancouvers two items ([16.2 Keyword Identity Is the Full Path](#162-keyword-identity-is-the-full-path)), but exclusion stayed, because subtracting a BRANCH is a question a tree raises rather than answers. It applies to EVERY filter category, not just keywords.

Three states on one checkbox: Qt::Checked includes, Qt::PartiallyChecked excludes, Qt::Unchecked is "don't care". PartiallyChecked was chosen over a parallel data role because the \~29 existing checkState call sites overwhelmingly test == Qt::Checked and were therefore already correct; only four treated the state as a bool or as != Qt::Unchecked and needed fixing (Filters::isOnlyMostRecentDayChecked, both halves of invertFilters, and the predicate itself).

The predicate: includes are OR-ed within a category and AND-ed between categories, as always. An exclusion is an outright rejection evaluated ACROSS categories: if the row carries an excluded value it is out, whatever else matches. An exclusion must NOT clear isCategoryUnchecked: a category holding only exclusions is subtracting, not narrowing, and were it to count as "this category is filtering", every row lacking any of its items would be rejected, which is the whole set. (The predicate is a compiled FilterPredicate, Datamodel/filterpredicate.h, built by SortFilter::compileFilters.)

#### 18.9.1 The Gestures

- OPT+CLICK EXCLUDES, and a plain click on something already excluded clears it. Both are handled in mousePressEvent BEFORE the base class runs, because the base class would toggle the checkbox as well, and Qt's own two-state toggle turns PartiallyChecked into Checked, silently inverting what the user asked for. Opt is the modifier the mask combine tools already use for "subtract".
- A right-click menu (Include / Exclude / Clear) is the discoverable path: a modifier nobody is told about is not a feature.
- SHIFT+CLICK CHECKS A RANGE, from the item last CHECKED to the one clicked, and only within the SAME category (a range spanning Ratings into Color classes would cross the AND boundary). The whole range is INCLUDED unless it is already all included, in which case the same gesture clears it, so the gesture is its own undo; an EXCLUDED item inside the range counts as not included, so the range is completed rather than emptied.
- The range anchor is remembered as CATEGORY + TEXT, not as a pointer (Filters::rangeAnchorCategory / rangeAnchorItem, set by noteRangeAnchor from every route that leaves an item checked): a category's items are destroyed and rebuilt on every filter rebuild, so a pointer would be a crash rather than a stale range, and an anchor whose text is gone makes the Shift+click an ordinary click. clearAll and uncheckAllFilters forget it.
- Filters::applyRangeCheck emits ONE filterChange for the whole range: a fifty-item range would otherwise re-run the predicate fifty times to arrive where it was always going.

#### 18.9.2 Where Exclusion Must Be Left Alone

- invertFilters leaves exclusions alone: "everything except this" has no meaningful inverse, and turning it into an inclusion would silently reverse what the user asked for.
- updateZeroCountCheckedItems unchecks only INCLUSIONS: an exclusion of something with a zero count excludes nothing, so it cannot produce the null result that guard exists for, and clearing it would discard the user's intent the moment the value came back.
- State travels through save / restore AND through a rename: Filters::ItemState carries the Qt::CheckState, not just "was it checked", and updateCategoryItems carries the state of a disappearing item onto its replacement (an exclusion restored as an inclusion would reverse the filter on every rebuild).
- Clearing must RESTYLE: exclusion is drawn on the FONT (strikethrough) as well as the checkbox, so uncheckAllFilters and clearAll call styleFilterItem rather than only setting Qt::Unchecked.
- The pick / rating / label MENU ACTIONS are binary and have no exclude representation: an excluded item leaves its action unchecked, and the panel stays the source of truth.

### 18.10 Any or All Keywords (AND Within One Category)

Within a category checked items are OR-ed, and for every category but one that is the only reading that means anything (a row has one rating, one camera, one folder). Keywords are the exception: a row carries a LIST, and "Family AND Beach" is as ordinary a question as "Family OR Beach". Before this the only way to ask it was the Search row, a substring match over every searchable field ("Beach" also found a title "Beach Road" and a filename).

- The mode is a property of the KEYWORDS HEADER ITEM (Filters::MatchAllRole), not a member of Filters, because SortFilter::compileFilters already walks the tree and reads each header's G::ColumnRole: reading MatchAllRole beside it puts the mode into FilterCategory::matchAll with the very checks it combines, so the two cannot be compiled from different moments. FilterPredicate::accepts then requires every include to hit; excludes reject in either mode. Prefix expansion still makes a parent match everything beneath it, so "Location AND Beach" is "some Location keyword, and Beach".
- The control is the header row's filter cell, which headers leave empty: "any" or "all", clicked to switch (Filters::mousePressEvent intercepts column 2 of the Keywords header before the expand / collapse handling, and swallows the release), plus "Match all checked keywords" on the Keywords context menu. ALWAYS SHOWN, so it can be found; DIMMED (hdrIsEmptyColor) while fewer than two keywords are included, because it changes nothing until then; lit in hdrIsFilteringColor when "all" is actually narrowing. Filters::updateKeywordModeLabel repaints it from setEachCatTextColor. setKeywordsMatchAll emits filterChange only when it changes the result (two or more included).
- It RESETS TO ANY with the categories (Filters::reset): a lasting "all" would quietly empty the next folder the first time two keywords were checked. It is NOT reset by the rebuild around a folder add / remove: save() records it beside the checks and restore() puts it back.
- The index agrees (CatalogQuery::keywordsMatchAll, set by Filters::fillQuery): Catalog::buildQueryLocked emits one EXISTS per keyword on pathfold instead of the OR join (still indexed equality, and no GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT, which would also multiply rows). Pinned by tst_filterpredicate::matchAllNeedsEveryKeyword, tst_catalog::keywordsMatchAllNeedsEveryOne and tst_filters::keywordMatchModeTravelsAndResets.

### 18.11 Investigations and Fixes

#### 18.11.1 Two Names OR-ed: One Return Beachballed the App

Waiting for Return was not the fix, only the first half of it. Asked for "&lt;a family member> OR &lt;the photographer's own name>" on a 43,070-image catalog, one deliberate Return still beachballed the application for the ten minutes before it was force-quit. What the measurement said, against the user's own 569 MB index:

- THE QUERY IS NOT THE COST. The three statements searchRows issues (the row SELECT, the keyword join and the COUNT) take 0.4 s TOGETHER.
- THE MATCH COUNT IS HONEST, AND ENORMOUS. The photographer's own name alone matched 40,540 of 43,070 rows. Not the file path, which is not indexed: image_fts holds keywords, title, creator, copyright, gear and filename, and CREATOR matched 37,585 rows while COPYRIGHT matched 40,068. A photographer's own name is stamped by the camera into nearly everything they have ever shot, so their own name is the least selective word they can type. The filters help page says so.
- SO THE PANEL RELOADED THE LIBRARY. 40,667 matching rows went to MW::loadCatalogScope, the same teardown a folder change is: MW::stop, dm->clearDataModel over the 43,070 rows already loaded, addCatalogRows for 40,667 of the SAME rows, BuildFilters over every one, the availability pass, and an icon read for the lot. Everything after the 0.4 s was that.

It never needed to load anything: the Library holds the WHOLE catalog in the model, so every row a query could match is loaded before it is typed, and the question is a FILTER. An edit to the Search row now narrows the proxy in both scopes ([18.1.2 Search Is a Filter Category](#1812-search-is-a-filter-category)); the index is asked only to LOAD the scope, on entry.

And the filter itself had the same defect waiting in it. DataModel::searchStringChange writes G::SearchColumn for EVERY row, and DataModel::setData emits dataChanged(idx, idx) on every write, so routing the query through the proxy would have emitted 43,070 separate notifications, each answered by the proxy, three views and the Cocoa accessibility bridge rebuilding its element array for the whole model. At \~27 ms a rebuild that is twenty minutes, worse than the reload it replaced. The loop now runs under a QSignalBlocker and a G::A11ySuspend and emits ONE dataChanged spanning the column at the end, with the model mutex released first. Nothing is lost: what re-filters the proxy is the filterChange Filters::setSearchText emits immediately afterwards, and invalidateFilter re-asks the predicate for every row regardless. MW::filterChange's own A11ySuspend does NOT cover this, because searchStringChange is emitted BEFORE filterChange. The same shape a fourth time ([4.14.16 The Accessibility Bridge Rebuilds the Whole Table, per Write](#41416-the-accessibility-bridge-rebuilds-the-whole-table-per-write)).

- filters->searchTrue->setText was inside that loop, restoring the "Enter search query" placeholder once per image (43,000 QTreeWidgetItem writes of the same string, each a view update). It is hoisted out.
- Filters::setSearchText was running the whole pass TWICE: setText on the searchTrue item reaches Filters::dataChanged with Qt::EditRole among its roles (the inline-edit path), which emits searchStringChange, and filterChange when the item is checked; then setSearchText emitted both again itself. Two passes over every row, and up to two dm->newInstance() bumps, the second landing on work the first had already dispatched. A settingSearchText guard makes the programmatic write distinguishable from a user edit.

#### 18.11.2 A Filtered Catalog Blanked the Loupe on Raw Files

The cause was an EMPTY if block. Reported as: Library scope, filtered to four images, the one CR3 among them shows its thumbnail but an empty loupe, while the SAME file opened from its folder, or from an UNFILTERED Library, is fine. The chain, from the session issue log:

1. A raw file's pixels live at an OFFSET inside it, and an index-hydrated row does not have that offset: addMetadataForItem deliberately writes nothing rather than zero, so the gap stays detectable, and ImageDecoder::ensureDecodeGeometry reads the header on the decoder thread to recover it.
2. ImageDecoder::load ALREADY TESTED for the gap ("// embedded image type but no offset"), and the block was EMPTY. So a decode that reached it with offsetFull == 0 carried on and read the file HEADER as though it were the embedded JPEG, produced a null image, and ended Status::Failed.
3. Failed is TERMINAL and keyed by path: ImageCache::okToDecode refuses to retry a path whose last decode ended Failed ("Prior terminal decode failure"), so ONE attempt made before the geometry was available blanked that image for the rest of the session ([4.14.5 The Terminal-Failure Check That Never Fired](#4145-the-terminal-failure-check-that-never-fired) is why that refusal works at all).
4. What made the attempt happen at the wrong moment was the FILTER: MW::filterChange calls dm->newInstance(), and 40 "Instance clash from ensureDecodeGeometry" entries said every geometry publish was rejected as a stale write, so the offset was never cached and each decode had to find it again (with two "Invalid sfIdx. Src: ImageDecoder::load" for decodes addressing proxy rows the filter had removed).

The guard now does what its comment says: it makes one last attempt at the geometry and, failing that, does NOT decode. The status it sets is Undefined, not Failed, deliberately: okToDecode treats Undefined, Abort and InstanceClash as transient and keeps the row retry-eligible, which is the honest state. A terminal status must mean the image CANNOT be decoded, never that it could not be decoded YET.

This latch is older than the filter change that exposed it. What was new was a Library that FILTERS a live 43,070-row model with the image cache running, where before it tore the model down and rebuilt it, resetting the per-path decode state every time and hiding the latch.

#### 18.11.3 Filter Clicks Swallowed: the Wrong Readiness Gate

Filters::itemClickedSignal and MW::filterChange both used G::allMetadataAttempted, which does not mean what they needed: DataModel::addMetadataForItem republishes it on EVERY metadata read as isMetaReadFinished() (metadataAttemptedCount >= rowCount()), and any path that clears a row back to MetaNotAttempted decrements that counter. MW::refreshStaleRows does exactly that for every row the scroll-in verifier finds stale, so one stale row flipped the flag false and swallowed every filter click. The checkbox toggled (QTreeWidget does that itself before the handler runs) and nothing else happened. In a catalog scope it never recovered, because each filter change moves the visible window and the verifier then finds more stale rows. The gates test whether a LOAD IS RUNNING now ([4.7.3 "Is a Load Running" Is Not "Has Every Row Been Read"](#473-is-a-load-running-is-not-has-every-row-been-read)): a model fully populated while a few rows are re-read is perfectly filterable, since an unread row does not match an active filter and BuildFilters re-runs when it lands.

- Catalog-sourced category items (the legacy panel, Filters::categorySource) are answerable whether or not the loaded folder has finished reading, so the readiness guards in itemClickedSignal, mousePressEvent and contextMenuEvent exempt them. Getting that wrong had the same confusing shape: the tick appeared and only the NOTIFICATION was swallowed.
- An early return must RELEASE THE LATCH. MW::filterChange lifts the proxy suspension its callers take before rebuilding a category (BuildFilters::updateCategory, MW::setRating, setColorClass, togglePick, applyKeywordsToSelection), and that lift was at the BOTTOM of the function, so its early returns left suspendFiltering true for the rest of the session and every later filter change was compiled and then ignored. G::stop makes the window wide (a transient teardown latch around every folder change). The returns now release it. Lifting is safe because filterAcceptsRow evaluates a compiled FilterPredicate and no longer walks the tree items the suspension protected it from.

#### 18.11.4 Categories Emptied and Greyed (an Aborted Build, an Empty Snapshot, a Teardown)

Reported more than once as "the Filters panel came back with categories empty and greyed", which reads as "disabled". Three causes, each a way a category tree is cleared and not refilled. (An intermittent "all dynamic categories empty in the Library" report is still open; if it recurs, capture the diagnostics below at the moment it happens.)

##### 18.11.4.1 An Aborted Full Build Must Run Again

BuildFilters::build calls Filters::startBuildFilters, which calls removeChildrenDynamicFilters: every dynamic category is emptied BEFORE the refill starts. The refill then walks the categories in creation order checking `abort` as it goes, and abortProcessing() is called at the top of every updateCategory, so anything asking for a category update while a full build is in flight stops it partway, and every category after that point stays empty. Nothing put them back, because the update that did the aborting fills only its OWN category.

- The evidence was the SHAPE OF THE DAMAGE, not the reasoning about it. Three rounds of plausible theories (a teardown latch, an empty snapshot, a stale metadata pass) were all wrong. What settled it was a probe reporting what each category actually held whenever the greyed set changed: healthy at 1,772 keyword items, then, immediately after two rows were removed for files that no longer existed, ISO, Titles, Keywords, Creators, Availability and Duplicates all at zero with everything up to Focal lengths intact. That is exactly the tail of createDynamicFilters, and a contiguous tail is a loop that stopped, not a category that was recounted.
- The action a run was asked for is captured ONCE, at the top, and the first attempt at this recovery is why. `action` is a plain member written on the GUI thread and read on the worker: updateCategory sets it to UpdateCategory immediately after calling abortProcessing(), so a full Reset already in flight had the value describing it replaced underneath it. The recovery check at the end of run() found UpdateCategory, and the Reset that had just cleared the tree never reported itself: the fix shipped and changed nothing. run() now reads the action once into a local and uses that for the switch as well: a run should carry out the request it started on.
- The abort itself is correct (a newer request supersedes an older one); what was wrong was treating a half-cleared tree as a resting place. run() reports it (abortedAfterClearing), and MW::rebuildAbortedFilters re-runs the build, delayed a quarter of a second and coalesced to one pending restart: the delay because whatever aborted it may still be arriving, the coalescing because that stops a ping-pong. It may abort again; each abort means a newer request took over.

##### 18.11.4.2 An Empty Snapshot Must Not Empty the Categories

A category is rebuilt FROM the counts a run produces: updateCategoryItems removes every item the count map does not mention, and updateKeywordItems deletes the whole keyword subtree and remakes it from the map. So a snapshot with no rows does not mean "nothing to update", it means "delete everything", and the panel came back with Titles, Keywords and Creators empty and greyed (the categories whose values require a FILE READ; Ratings, Years, Camera models and the rest arrive on the catalog row itself and survived).

A snapshot can be empty while the model is not: BuildFilters::makeSnapshot returns an empty one when dm is null, and otherwise reads dm->rowCount() at the instant it runs, and DataModel::addCatalogRows fills the model in BATCHES, so there is a window in every catalog load where the model holds few rows or none. BuildFilters::run now skips the rebuild when the snapshot claims zero rows and the datamodel holds some, finishing through the ordinary Done op so nothing downstream waits. The test is the MODEL rather than the snapshot, because a folder that genuinely holds no images must still clear the tree. A stale tree is the right failure: recoverable and self-correcting, where an empty one is neither.

It is DIAGNOSED at the moment it happens (MW::reportEmptyKeywordCategory), because this was reported three times and reasoned about twice without being reproduced. The category can only be empty for a few reasons, trivially distinguishable while it is happening: an empty datamodel; a model with rows but no keywords (metadata unread, or cleared and the re-read aborted); or rows and keywords both present, which would put the fault in the counting or the tree build. All are transient, so the state is captured rather than argued about later. The walk runs only once the category is already known to be empty.

##### 18.11.4.3 The Keyword Category Is Not Demolished During a Teardown

Filters::updateKeywordItems rebuilds rather than patches: it deletes every child and calls addKeywordItems to remake them. addKeywordItems ABORTS on G::stop, so a latch landing between the two left the category permanently EMPTY (no keywords under it, the header greyed by setEachCatTextColor's empty test, nothing to repair it). That is exactly the window MW::filterChange warns about (a transient teardown latch that MW::stop sets and clears around EVERY folder change), and a keyword edit was among the likeliest things to be sitting in it, because the edit path then PUMPED THE EVENT LOOP to keep its progress popup alive, and a pump is where a queued teardown gets its turn. updateKeywordItems now returns before touching anything when the latch is set, and the abort inside addKeywordItems updates the header on its way out, so a half-built tree cannot leave "Keywords (282 unfiled)" sitting above nothing. (The pumps have since gone too: [16.13.2 What a Keyword Move Actually Costs (Measured, and the Feedback That Cost More Than the Work)](#16132-what-a-keyword-move-actually-costs-measured-and-the-feedback-that-cost-more-than-the-work).)

## 19 Focus Predictor

Focus Predictor uses a machine-learning model to predict where in an image the user will want to check focus, such as the subject's eye. When it is enabled (Toggle Pan to Focus) and the loupe is zoomed, each image the user advances to is panned to the predicted point.

### 19.1 Architecture

```
Data              The training images and a CSV that records each one's focus point,
                  type and path (developer machine, outside the repo:
                  ~/Documents/Documents - Quark/FocusPointTrainer/focuspoint.csv).
Python            The training code, in a separate project (~/Projects/FocusPointTrainer):
                    config.py
                    model.py
                    train_focus_model.py      (creates the model)
                    validate_focus_model.py
Model             focus_point_model, in two forms: .pth (native PyTorch) and .onnx
                  (what OpenCV loads). The shipped copy is
                  DetectionModels/focus_point_model.onnx.
FocusPointTrainer A C++ class that writes the labelling data: it appends the focus
                  point, type and path for each training image to focuspoint.csv.
FocusPredictor    A C++ class that runs the model to predict the focus point for the
                  current image.
```

### 19.2 Training a New Model

1. Create the training data with FocusPointTrainer, which appends each training image's focus point, type and path to focuspoint.csv.
2. Run train_focus_model.py (Python, in a terminal). It writes focus_point_model.pth and converts it to focus_point_model.onnx, the format OpenCV can load from C++.
3. Copy focus_point_model.onnx to Winnow64/DetectionModels.
4. FocusPredictor::predict returns the predicted focus location in normalised image coordinates.

### 19.3 Panning the Loupe

When focus prediction is enabled and the loupe is zoomed, ImageView pans to the predicted point at the end of ImageView::loadImage, via ImageView::predictPanToFocus (get the focus coordinate and pan).

The viewport's position within the scene is then shown on the thumbnail: ImageView::predictPanToFocus emits the rectangle and image aspect, IconView::loupeRect receives them, and IconViewDelegate::setNormVpRect / setVpRectVisibility draw a rectangle on the thumbView thumbnail matching the loupe viewport.

## 20 Help System

All in-app help pages are HTML files loaded by HtmlWindow (Utilities/htmlwindow.cpp). Every page shares one stylesheet, Docs/help.css, applied automatically via QTextDocument::setDefaultStyleSheet. To restyle every help page at once, edit help.css.

### 20.1 Architecture

```
Utilities/htmlwindow.cpp   HtmlWindow (a QScrollArea hosting a QTextBrowser). Loads the
                           HTML, applies Docs/help.css as the default stylesheet, and
                           sets a qrc base URL so relative <img src="images/..."> resolves.
Docs/help.css              Shared dark-theme stylesheet: body, h1-h3, a, code, pre,
                           .highlight, .warn. Some values are fallbacks that HtmlWindow
                           overrides at load time (below); the static values apply only
                           when viewing the file outside the app.
Docs/_template.html        Reference template demonstrating every supported element
                           (headings, paragraphs, span colours, link, image, lists, code
                           block, table). Copy it for a new page.
Docs/<topic>.html          One file per topic. The <head> needs only
                             <link rel="stylesheet" href="help.css">
                           Qt ignores the <link> (it already loaded help.css); VS Code's
                           Live Preview honours it, so the editor view matches Winnow.
Docs/images/               Images used by help pages, referenced relatively:
                           <img src="images/Foo.png">.
winnow.qrc                 Every .html and image referenced from help must be listed here,
                           or the window opens empty.
```

HtmlWindow lifecycle: the constructor sets Qt::Window (top-level with a title bar) and Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose. Callers pass a parent (window() for embedded widgets, this for top-level dialogs) so the help window is destroyed with its owner; MW::closeEvent also sweeps findChildren&lt;HtmlWindow\*>() as a safety net. Do not store the returned pointer or delete it manually.

#### 20.1.1 Spacing (No Crowded Pages)

Help pages must not read as one dense block (reviewed across every page 2026-10-19).

- One &lt;p> per point. Never join lines with &lt;br> inside a paragraph ("What it does: ... &lt;br>Why: ... &lt;br>How: ..."). Qt gives &lt;p> 12px above and below and &lt;br> nothing, so br-joined lines run together. That was the complaint that started the review.
- Split a paragraph past roughly 80 words at its natural break.
- Text that continues a list item after a nested list goes in its own &lt;p> inside the &lt;li>. Bare text there gets no space before the next item.
- The spacing itself is global, in help.css: line-height 1.25 on p and li, 0.7em between list items, 1em above h1/h2, and padding on table cells. In Qt's rich text an em in a margin is the element's line height (qcssparser.cpp lengthValueFromData), and a bare-number line-height is a proportional multiplier. Do not tighten any of it per page.
- To check a page without building the app, render it with QTextDocument using help.css plus HtmlWindow::applyStyle's overrides, at 700px width.

### 20.2 Adding a Help Page

1. Copy Docs/\_template.html to Docs/&lt;yourpage>.html.
2. Edit it in a plain-text editor (see [20.3.1 Editing Tools](#2031-editing-tools)). Keep the &lt;link rel="stylesheet" href="help.css">; add a &lt;style> block only for per-page overrides.
3. Put any images in Docs/images/ and reference them relatively, e.g. &lt;img src="images/MyDiagram.png">.
4. Register the files in winnow.qrc under the /Docs prefix:

```
   <file>Docs/<yourpage>.html</file>
   <file>Docs/images/<YourImage>.png</file>
```

5. Open it from C++ (the pattern Filters::howThisWorks uses, Datamodel/filters.cpp):

```
   #include "Utilities/htmlwindow.h"
```

```
   void MyWidget::someHelp()
   {
       QRect r = QRect(mapToGlobal(geometry().topLeft()), geometry().size());
       new HtmlWindow("Winnow - My Topic",
                      ":/Docs/yourpage.html",
                      QSize(700, 600), r, window());
   }
```

6. Build. No other wiring is required.

### 20.3 Formatting

Edit Docs/help.css; every help page picks it up the next time one opens.

HtmlWindow::applyStyle() appends rules on top of help.css so help text tracks the app's font and theme. They win over help.css (later rule, equal specificity), so editing these in help.css alone has no effect in the app:

- body font-size -> the app font size (G::strFontSize)
- h1/h2/h3 font-size -> help.css's design size scaled by G::fontSize / 12
- h1/h2/h3 colour -> G::header1/2/3Color (theme-tied; set in WidgetCSS::styleGlobals)

applyStyle() re-runs on every font or theme change (HtmlWindow::refreshOpenWindows, called from MW), so open help windows update live. To change these, edit applyStyle() or the header colours in WidgetCSS::styleGlobals.

QTextBrowser supports only Qt's HTML 4 / CSS 2.1 subset (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/richtext-html-subset.html). Avoid flexbox, grid, CSS custom properties and HTML5 semantic tags; Qt silently ignores them.

#### 20.3.1 Editing Tools

VS Code with Microsoft's "Live Preview" extension (or BBEdit on the Mac): plain-text HTML editing that will not silently inject CSS3 Qt ignores (which is why WYSIWYG editors such as Typora and Pinegrow are not recommended), with a side-by-side preview that refreshes on save.

Expected differences between the preview and Winnow:

- Font sizes will not match pixel for pixel (Chromium vs QTextBrowser defaults), and the preview shows help.css's static fallback sizes, not Winnow's runtime sizes.
- Heading colours differ: the preview shows help.css's static colours; Winnow uses the theme-tied header colours.
- Anything outside the CSS 2.1 subset renders in the preview but not in Winnow. When in doubt, check in Winnow.

#### 20.4.1 The Winnow Overview Page

Docs/winnowhelp.html (Help > Winnow Overview, window "Winnow - Overview") was rewritten from scratch on 2026-10-03; the old "Winnow Help" content (file types, a reset-workspace tip, annotated loupe and grid screenshots) had gone stale and was removed, with the two screenshots' qrc entries.

It is written for users, not developers: keep it NON-TECHNICAL, with no class names, file names or database terms beyond what the UI itself shows (Manage Catalog...). Its one section so far, Overview, explains the two ways of looking at photos: FOLDERS (one folder at a time, nothing to set up) and LIBRARY (every catalogued photo as one set, narrowed with filters; Collections and Queries live here). It covers how photos get into the Library (ONLY the folders listed in Manage Catalog...; browsing another folder does not add it), what works the same in both (filters and search, keywords/ratings/labels, Places), and how to switch. When the Library/Folders switch or Manage Catalog changes, update this page.

Every header band in the Develop dock ends its [:] menu with a "&lt;band> help" item, after a separator, opening that band's own page. One page per panel, not one long module page: each panel has its own grammar, and the help a user wants is for the band they are standing on. develophelp.html remains the module-wide page (Raw panel "?" and PV_Scope).

Submasks                Submasks help        developsubmaskshelp.html

Wiring:

A new section needs only a case in sectionHelp (PV_Scope falls back to howThisWorks) plus the page and its qrc entry.
- The two BAND widgets own no Docs knowledge: ScopeHeader::helpRequested and SubmaskList::helpRequested are emitted from their menus and connected in bindScopeHeader / the SubmaskList block of DevelopProperties to editsHelp / submasksHelp.
