## 21 Check for Updates

Winnow checks GitHub for a newer release and, when the user agrees, downloads it, installs it over the running copy and relaunches. Releases are GitHub Releases on towhee/Winnow64, published by the deploy scripts' menu G (see packaging/README.md). Until 3.0 the check read a version.json on winnow.ca and only opened the downloaded installer; copies older than 3.0 still do that, so the server's version.json must stay current until they have upgraded.

Two entry points, both calling MW::checkForUpdate(bool silent) (`Main/mainwindow.cpp`):

- Help > "Check for updates": silent == false (loud). Also reports "up to date", "released but not yet for this computer", rate limiting and network errors via popups, and ignores the skip-version setting.
- Startup, from MW::showEvent: a deferred QTimer::singleShot fires checkForUpdate(true) 4 s after the window shows, gated by the checkIfUpdate preference ("Check for program updates at startup", default true) and skipped when G::isTest (no network during headless or soak runs). Silent: it speaks only when an update is available and has not been skipped. showEvent also warms Qt's TLS configuration on a pool thread first, so the first request does not load the system certificates on the GUI thread (see [4.14.10 The Two Post-Load Stalls](#41410-the-two-post-load-stalls)).

Code: Utilities/appupdate.h (header-only, pure: release parsing and version ordering, pinned by tests/unit/tst_appupdate.cpp), Utilities/appinstaller.\* (platform install), MW::checkForUpdate / onUpdateCheckReply / downloadUpdate / installUpdate, Dialogs/updateAppDlg.\*.

### 21.1 Detecting a Release

checkForUpdate() does an async GET of https://api.github.com/repos/towhee/Winnow64/releases/latest (with a User-Agent, which GitHub requires). That endpoint returns the newest FULL release; drafts and pre-releases are never offered, so a release reaches users the moment it is published as a full release. Unauthenticated, GitHub allows 60 requests an hour per IP address; a 403/429 is reported as "GitHub is limiting update checks" on a loud check and ignored on a silent one.

AppUpdate::parseLatestRelease reads:

- tag_name "v&lt;WINNOW_VERSION>" (e.g. "v3_beta", "v3.1"): the offered version, leading "v" dropped.
- html_url: the "release notes" link in the dialog.
- The asset for this platform, by name (\*.dmg on macOS, WinnowSetup\*.exe on Windows): browser_download_url, size, and digest ("sha256:&lt;hex>", which GitHub computes for every uploaded asset).

A release with no asset for this platform is NOT an error: one machine runs menu G first and the other attaches its file later, so in between the check stays quiet (silent) or says "released, but not yet for this computer" (loud).

Version ordering (AppUpdate::compareVersions) is neither a string compare nor a bare QVersionNumber compare, because labels carry pre-release suffixes:

- The numeric part first, trailing zeros insignificant (3 == 3.0).
- With equal numbers, a pre-release sorts before the release (3_beta &lt; 3.0).
- Two pre-releases compare their alphabetic stage (alpha &lt; beta &lt; rc), then its number (beta2 &lt; beta10).

The running version is WINNOW_VERSION (WINNOW_VERSION_LABEL in CMakeLists.txt, exposed as MW::versionNumber).

If the release is newer it shows UpdateAppDlg, worded by UpdateAppDlg::setInstallMode for the install that will happen:

- Install / Download: MW::downloadUpdate.
- Don't ask again for this version: sets updateSkipVersion, so the silent startup check no longer prompts for it (a loud manual check still does).
- Not now: no state change; offered again next launch.

Testing:

- WINNOW_UPDATE_AS_VERSION=&lt;older label> (e.g. 2.0) makes the check treat the running copy as that version, so the whole download -> install -> relaunch path can be exercised with a release of the same version.
- WINNOW_UPDATE_TAG=&lt;tag> checks that one release (GitHub /releases/tags/&lt;tag>) instead of the latest, and accepts a PRE-RELEASE, so a test build published as a pre-release (invisible to /releases/latest, the README link and every user) can be installed. Typical: publish the build as pre-release v3_beta-test, then run WINNOW_UPDATE_TAG=v3_beta-test WINNOW_UPDATE_AS_VERSION=2.0.

### 21.2 Download and Verify

MW::downloadUpdate streams the asset (GitHub redirects the download URL to its CDN; Qt 6 follows redirects) into a QSaveFile while hashing it, with progress in G::popup. Before the file is committed it must match the asset's published size and SHA-256 digest; a mismatch abandons it ("checksum mismatch"). isUpdatingApp blocks a second check or download while one is in flight.

AppInstaller::canInstallInPlace decides where it goes and what happens next:

- In place (the normal case): &lt;CacheLocation>/Update, then MW::installUpdate.
- Not in place: the Downloads folder, then opened (macOS mounts the DMG, Windows runs the installer) for the user to install by hand; the dialog says why. On macOS, Winnow must be a .app inside a folder named Applications that the user can write to, and not running from a disk image or from App Translocation. On Windows, unins000.exe must sit beside Winnow.exe (installed by our Inno Setup installer). So a development build from Qt Creator never replaces itself.

### 21.3 Installing

MW::installUpdate runs AppInstaller::prepare on a pool thread ("Preparing the Winnow update..."), then AppInstaller::launchFinisher on the GUI thread, then close(). Everything that can fail runs BEFORE Winnow quits, so an error is shown in a message box and the running copy is untouched. If the quit is declined (unsaved picks, a background ingest), the finisher keeps waiting and the update installs whenever Winnow does quit ("The Winnow update will be installed when you quit Winnow.").

The relaunched copy inherits Winnow's environment (`open` and the Windows installer both pass it on), so launchFinisher first unsets WINNOW_UPDATE_TAG / WINNOW_UPDATE_AS_VERSION; otherwise a test install re-offers the same test release at the next startup.

#### 21.3.1 macOS

- prepare: hdiutil attach the DMG (read-only, hidden), find the .app in it, and verify it with `codesign --verify --deep --strict -R=<requirement>`, where the requirement is identifier "com.winnow.Winnow" + an Apple-anchored Developer ID + Winnow's team ID. A DMG that is not ours is refused. Then `ditto` it to &lt;Applications>/.WinnowUpdate.app (the same volume as the destination, so the final move is an atomic rename) and detach.
- finisher: a /bin/sh script written to &lt;cache>/Update/install.sh and started detached, logging to &lt;cache>/Update/install.log. It waits for Winnow's pid to exit, then moves the staged bundle to the DMG's bundle name (Winnow&lt;ver>.app; the bundle names are version-stamped, so the new one lands BESIDE the old) and moves the old bundle to the Trash. Nothing is deleted: if the Trash cannot be written (privacy protection) the old version is left in place. When the old and new names are the same, the old one must go to the Trash first; if it cannot, or the move fails, the old version is restored and relaunched and the DMG opened for a manual install. On success it opens the new bundle and removes the DMG.
- Verified 2026-10-15 (3_beta over 3_beta, the same-name case, via WINNOW_UPDATE_TAG): the detached script moved the bundle in /Applications without a privacy prompt and wrote to \~/.Trash; quit -> relaunch took \~3 s.

#### 21.3.2 Windows

- prepare: nothing.
- finisher: the downloaded Inno Setup installer itself, started with /SILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /WAITPID=&lt;pid> /RELAUNCH=1. winnow.iss's InitializeSetup waits on that pid (OpenProcess + WaitForSingleObject) before installing, and a [Run] entry with Check: ShouldRelaunch restarts Winnow as the original, non-elevated user after the silent install. UAC asks for elevation as the installer starts (it installs to Program Files).
- Integrity is the SHA-256 digest check; there is no Authenticode check, because release signing is optional.
- Untested as of 2026-10-17.

## 22 Diagnostics and Probes

A probe is diagnostic tracing left in the code after the investigation that needed it. The tracing is kept because reproducing an intermittent symptom costs a session; the switch must never be left on.

### 22.1 Probe Switches

Every probe's on/off flag is defined in Main/global.cpp, in ONE block (PROBE SWITCHES), and declared together in Main/global.h. They used to be file-statics scattered across mainwindow.cpp, menusandactions.cpp, fileoperations.cpp and iconview.cpp, so "is anything instrumenting this build?" had no single answer, and a probe could ship on because its switch was three directories away (probeCopyPath had been left true).

```
G::isPerfProbe          [PERF] Phase 1/2 load timing, the scroll lines, filterChange
                        phases, GUI STALL watchdog (--perfprobe, WINNOW_PERF_PROBE=1,
                        --catalogload)
G::isIngestProbe        [INGEST] the cull path (Help > Diagnostics, --ingestprobe); an
                        atomic, since the hook sites are on worker threads
G::isPanelProbe         the dock geometry negotiation: panels that open narrow, a
                        thumbDock cut through an icon (Help > Diagnostics, PERSISTED;
                        --panelprobe). See [[Panel Probe]]
G::isReportDevelopTime  [DevTime] per-stage Develop re-render timings on a slider drag
G::isCopyPathProbe      [COPYPATH] the context-menu Copy path tracing (event filter,
                        action hovered/changed, the slot)
G::isWheelProbe         [WHEEL] IconView wheel/trackpad events (phase, both deltas, the
                        scroll engine that handled it)
```

All default false, and they stay separate flags: each answers a different question (a load, a cull, a context menu, a wheel), and arming everything at once buries the thing being looked for. The ones with no UI are armed by editing the default and rebuilding; the rest by Help > Diagnostics or a --flag (main.cpp). The counters the probes accumulate (probeThumbRetryCount, probeIndexMetaHits/Misses, the icon decomposition timers) follow the block.

MW::diagnostics has a PROBES section listing all six, so a build running with tracing on is visible in the report a user pastes rather than inferred from the noise in it.

When you add a probe:

1. Put its flag in the block in global.cpp (default false).
2. Declare it in the PROBE SWITCHES block in global.h.
3. Gate every hook site with `if (G::isXxxProbe)`, so a disarmed probe costs one load.
4. Add it to the PROBES section in diagnostics.cpp.

#### 22.1.1 The Row Trail Has No Switch

Utilities/rowtrail.h is the one deliberate exception. It exists for the intermittent "blank, unselectable thumbnail at startup" (an icon seen for an instant, then gone, and never re-read), which nobody can reproduce on demand, so it must already be recording when it happens.

- It records only TRANSITIONS of a row (metadata status, IconLoaded, icon stored/REMOVED/re-keyed, setIcon/setIcon1 drops with their reason, MetaRead dispatch/return, and a returning reader IGNORED because the proxy was suspended or MetaRead aborted) into a 262,144-event ring, with the thread and a caller tag (RowTrail::Tag in refreshStaleRows, applyModelChange, evictHiddenIcons, clearIconsOutsideChunkRange, clearDevelopIcon).
- MW::checkBlankRows runs 15 s after metadataComplete, 20 s after refreshStaleRows, 15 s after the last of a burst of filter changes, and when the stale re-commit gives up (a check that lands while a load flag is still up retries every 10 s rather than being dropped). Any row in the icon range still without an icon 5 s later (videos and offline files excepted) is written once per session to &lt;AppData>/Log/blank_rows.txt (model state, load flags, the row's whole trail, then MetaRead's own view from its thread), and an issue is logged pointing at the file. On macOS that is \~/Library/Application Support/Winnow/Log, beside WinnowIssueLog.txt.
- Self-heal: MetaRead::setStartRow re-arms the VISIBLE rows on every call in both modes (brute force used to skip re-arming entirely), so a row whose icon was lost after a successful read is re-read on the next selection or scroll. Each heal is a RowTrail event ("MetaRead visible re-arm") and an issue-log Warning naming the files, so the underlying cause is still recorded.
- Help > Diagnostics > Blank thumbnail report writes the same report on demand for every row blank right now (a blank cell cannot be selected, so Current Row Diagnostics cannot reach it).
- Remove it with the bug.

### 22.2 Measuring a Live Session (--perfprobe)

`Winnow --perfprobe` starts an ORDINARY session (the user's own settings, catalog and caches) with G::isPerfProbe on. The environment knobs below apply only in test mode and --catalogload is headless, so between them they can measure a LOAD and nothing else; scrolling a catalog is a person dragging a scrollbar over 43,000 rows, which no headless run reproduces. --perfprobe found two defects on its first run, and neither was the one code reading had predicted (see [5.10.5 Why a Catalog Scope Would Not Scroll (Nine Defects, One Policy, and Where It Ends)](#5105-why-a-catalog-scope-would-not-scroll-nine-defects-one-policy-and-where-it-ends)).

While scrolling, DataModel::reportScrollProbe prints one line a second (nothing when the view is still) for the per-scroll work that is not O(1), because which of it costs what is not decidable by reading the code (this file records two occasions where static analysis named the wrong culprit on exactly this path):

```
  scan   isAllIconChunkLoaded, reached from setIconRange (which runs twice per scroll
         event: MW::updateIconRange and MW::updateChange). It walks the whole icon chunk.
  evict  clearIconsOutsideChunkRange, queued from MetaRead::dispatchFinished onto the
         GUI thread, walking rows OUTSIDE the chunk. Reports walked as well as cleared:
         what the sweep looked at against what it found.
  rearm  MetaRead::setStartRow's re-arm loop on the metaReadThread. It decides which
         icons are eligible to be read, so a thumbnail that never appears is diagnosed
         from its counts.
  icons  set / redundant / dispatched / redos. REDUNDANT is the one to read: an icon
         delivered for a row that already had one is a read for nothing, and a newly
         visible row waits behind it. The redo count sits beside it.
  paint  repaint flushes / worstWait / readerQueue. worstWait is how long a visible row
         sat with its icon already in the model before the view was told: the only
         figure that measures what the USER experiences.
```

Read it alongside the [PERF] GUI STALL lines the watchdog prints in the same run (MW::armGuiStallWatchdog): the stall line says how long the event loop was gone (how late a 250 ms timer fired), and the scroll lines either side say what was being spent during it.

### 22.3 A/B Knobs (Test Mode)

So a measurement can be reproduced without editing a default and rebuilding. Test mode only (--selftest and friends, which set QStandardPaths::setTestModeEnabled): in an ordinary session these are preferences, and an environment variable that silently changed how metadata is read would be a trap. Applied in Main/settings.cpp AFTER the preference is read, so the environment wins.

```
  WINNOW_PERF_PROBE=1        emit the [PERF] lines
  WINNOW_INDEX_METADATA=0|1  force G::useIndexMetadata either way
  WINNOW_MAX_ICON_CHUNK=<n>  the icon ceiling, which decides how much of a load is
                             icon work
```

The --catalogload harness has its own set (WINNOW_CATALOGLOAD\_\*), listed with the features they test: [17.14.5 Probes](#17145-probes) under the Library load cover, and [4.14.18 Sort the Catalog and Every Other Cell Is Blank (a Position Is Not an Image)](#41418-sort-the-catalog-and-every-other-cell-is-blank-a-position-is-not-an-image).

### 22.4 Ingest Probe

Ingest (culling) is the workload every other probe misses. Reviewing thousands of frames off a card runs MetaRead's readers, the ImageCache decoders, three views, a sidecar write per classification and a copy at the end, all against the slowest storage the app ever sees. Its complaints ("the loupe sometimes doesn't show the selected image", "rapid progression stutters") are not load problems: --perfprobe's scroll lines are about a view being dragged, the GUI stall watchdog says a stall happened but not what was running, and ImageCache::diagnostics() is a SNAPSHOT. A blank loupe is an EVENT (the image was not there when it was needed, and arrived, or did not, later), and a snapshot taken afterwards shows a healthy cache.

Utilities/ingestprobe.h records events on the two paths a person drives during a cull:

```
SELECTION   arrow key or click -> MW::fileSelectionChange -> the loupe. Was the image
            in the cache when ImageView::loadImage asked? If not, did
            MW::refreshViewsOnCacheChange ever arrive to repair it, and how long was
            the user looking at nothing? Same phase marks as the [PERF] select line.
EDIT        1-5, 0-5, P. Split into model+sidecar / refreshIcons / buildFilters /
            filterChange: whether a slow keypress was the card or the filter panel.
```

plus counters for the ways finished work is silently discarded:

```
dropped setCached     DataModel::setCached refused the notification on an instance
                      clash. The image IS in the cache (cacheImage inserted it before
                      the guard), but refreshViewsOnCacheChange is below that return,
                      so a selection waiting on the row stays blank.
discarded decodes     ImageCache::okToCache refused a finished decode on an instance
                      clash; the row goes back on the queue.
hollow cache hits     icd->contains() said yes and the image came back null.
instance bumps        DataModel::newInstance, tallied BY CALLER. During a cull they come
                      from filter changes provoked by the classification keys, which is
                      the connection between "I pressed 3" and "the next four images
                      were slow".
cache status paints   MW::updateImageCacheStatus repaints the whole target range, a
                      QPainter per cell, once per image entering or leaving the cache.
gui stalls            the watchdog, tightened while armed: 50 ms ticks with 100 ms of
                      slack, so it reports ~150 ms stalls rather than 750 ms. The figure
                      is the whole interval, so the threshold must clear the tick.
```

#### 22.4.1 Is the Pause Periodic, and in What?

The report answers "a short pause approximately every 35 images" directly, which a percentile cannot (p90 is the same whether the slow ones are evenly spaced or clumped). It finds the run's median gap (the held-key rate), calls anything 2.5x that a long gap, and prints the distance from one to the next TWICE, in SELECTIONS and in MILLISECONDS. At a steady key-repeat rate those are one observation with opposite causes: a steady number of selections means something driven by ROW POSITION (a screenful of thumbnails, a cache range, a chunk boundary); a steady number of milliseconds means a TIMER, which no reading of the navigation code would find.

The gap, not the phase timer, is what makes this work. A pause the user sees while fileSelectionChange stays fast is time spent OUTSIDE it (a queued slot, a deferred layout, a repaint), and every phase timer is blind to it by construction.

#### 22.4.2 What Held the Event Loop

QtSingleApplication::notify brackets every delivery and reports the ones over 25 ms, named by receiver class and event type. Nesting takes care of itself: an inner delivery is timed too, so the innermost long-running leaf is charged as well as its caller. They are tallied and printed live as "[INGEST] event held the loop", and each long gap in the periodicity list carries the ones that landed inside it, the line that names a cause rather than a symptom.

- An event filter is not good enough, and the first version was one. A filter on qApp runs BEFORE delivery, so it can only measure from one filter call to the next, which equals the delivery only while the loop is busy; let the loop go idle and the wait is charged to whatever was delivered last (the first run reported the 50 ms memory watchdog as a 50 ms stall on every tick). notify() measures the delivery itself.
- GUI thread only, for correctness: notify() runs on whichever thread is delivering, so decoder threads' queued events come through it too (ImageDecoder/MetaCall measured a 1,596 ms mean: a raw decode doing its job). The tallies are plain QMaps, so recording from several threads would be a data race inside the diagnostic.
- Which slot: a queued call arrives as QEvent::MetaCall and Qt does not expose which method it carries, so "MW(MW)/MetaCall took 290 ms" names the object and stops. IngestProbe::Scope closes that gap: the MW entry points a worker can invoke each declare their own name (updateChange, updateIconRange, updateImageCacheStatus, refreshViewsOnCacheChange, folderChangeCompleted, filterChange, refreshStaleRows, setCentralMessage, updateSidecarStatus, reloadIconChunk, and the two thread-run-status slots). One over 25 ms prints "[INGEST] slot" beside the event line. The ABSENCE of that line is also an answer: a slow MetaCall on MW with no slot line is a queued entry point that is not in the list. When even that is not enough, `sample` the process (see [5.10.3 A Full-Sensor JPEG Encode on the GUI Thread (the Pause Every 35 Images)](#5103-a-full-sensor-jpeg-encode-on-the-gui-thread-the-pause-every-35-images)).

#### 22.4.3 Running It

Help > Diagnostics > "Ingest probe (record cull session)" arms it (and the GUI stall watchdog with it); work normally; Help > Diagnostics > "Ingest probe report" reads it. `Winnow --ingestprobe` starts a session already recording. Arming CLEARS the buffers, disarming KEEPS them. A report from a probe that was never armed says so rather than showing an empty run as a clean one.

Live output, prefixed [INGEST] beside the watchdog's [PERF] lines: nothing for an ordinary selection; a line for one whose loupe did not come from the cache or cost more than 120 ms; a line when a miss is repaired, with the wait; a line when a miss is ABANDONED (the user moved on before the image arrived); and a line for a classification key over 150 ms.

Disarmed, the cost is one relaxed atomic load per hook site, each written `if (G::isIngestProbe) ...`. Nothing is allocated and no timer runs until armed. The event buffers are GUI-thread only; the three counters reached from the ImageCache and decoder threads are plain atomics.

### 22.5 Panel Probe

Two intermittent complaints about geometry Winnow never asked for: panels that open NARROW at startup (the left dock group a fraction of its saved width, the folder tree a sliver), and a thumbView HALF HIDDEN after the window is resized or a dock dragged (the strip shorter than one icon cell, the thumbnails cut through the middle).

Neither can be read off the code. The final geometry is not set in one place; it is NEGOTIATED, within the first few event-loop turns after MW::showEvent, between restoreGeometry, MW::restoreWindowState, MW::placeDocksAddedSince, MW::applyDockCollapseState, MW::invokeWorkflowWorkspace, the resizeDocks calls in MW::setThumbDockFeatures and MW::builtInDefaultWorkspace, the min/max pin in DockWidget::setCollapsed, and QDockAreaLayout's own redistribution, all writing to the same numbers. A trace in any one of them shows a plausible value that something later overwrites, which is why "it looks right when I print it" and "it is wrong on screen" have both been true. So Utilities/panelprobe.h records the negotiation rather than any one step:

```
MARK      a labelled milestone in the startup or workspace sequence, with a snapshot of
          every watched panel. MW::showEvent marks every step above by name, plus two
          LATE marks (the first idle after show, and 1.5 s after), because the size the
          user sees is not the size at the end of showEvent.
SNAP      one panel's geometry AND its constraints: min/max, sizeHint, minimumSizeHint,
          the body widget's size, the area, floating and visible. A panel PINNED narrow
          and one merely ALLOCATED narrow look identical on screen and are different bugs.
RESIZE    every resize / move / show / hide the layout actually delivers, old -> new,
          from an event filter on each dock: the only record of WHICH step overwrote a
          good value.
REQUEST   an explicit sizing call Winnow made (resizeDocks, setMinimumHeight, the
          collapse/expand pins). resizeDocks is a REQUEST, not a result: QDockAreaLayout
          can refuse it outright when the area has no room, so a request with no
          matching resize after it is a refused request.
AUDIT     a verdict MW supplies (MW::panelProbeThumbAudit): does the thumbView viewport
          still hold a whole icon cell? Re-evaluated at every mark and after every
          settled resize, recorded only when it CHANGES.
```

- Settled marks, not immediate ones, for every gesture. A drop, a float, a window resize and a resizeDocks all return before the dock area has redistributed, so those hooks schedule the snapshot on the next event-loop turn (PanelProbe::MarkSettled) and coalesce a gesture's burst into one. Marking immediately would record the value about to be overwritten.
- Suspects are flagged as they are recorded and listed FIRST in the report: a docked, visible panel allocated less than its own minimumSizeHint width (minimumSizeHint rather than sizeHint, because sizeHint is a preference the layout may fairly ignore), and a thumb cell more than 2 px taller than the thumbView viewport (two pixels of rounding nobody can see is not the complaint).
- Watched: every dock (Folders, Bookmarks, Filters, Catalog, Keywords, Metadata, Thumb, Embellish, Develop, History, Presets), plus thumbView, centralWidget and MW. thumbView is watched ALONGSIDE thumbDock because the dock can be exactly the height asked for while the view inside it is short by a scroll bar, which is precisely the "thumbnails cut in half" report.

Running it: Help > Diagnostics > "Panel probe (record panel sizing)" arms it; Help > Diagnostics > "Panel probe report" reads it. `Winnow --panelprobe` arms exactly one run.

- The tick is PERSISTED (QSettings "PanelProbe"), unlike the ingest probe's. The startup sizing happens in showEvent, before any menu can be reached, so a session-only toggle could never record what it was ticked for; ticking it arms the NEXT launch as well. MW::setupPanelProbe reads the flag and registers the docks from the MW CONSTRUCTOR, because everything worth recording is still ahead of that point.
- Arming CLEARS the buffers, disarming KEEPS them. A report from a probe that was never armed says so. The report also goes to the console on the way out (MW::closeEvent), so a --panelprobe session leaves its timeline in console.txt.
- Disarmed, the cost is one relaxed atomic load per hook site (`if (G::isPanelProbe) ...`), and NO EVENT FILTER is installed (PanelProbe::Watch only remembers the widget). GUI thread only.
